evaluations.title: One-hole signed-D deconvolution residual for n50
evaluations.author: Noether III
evaluations.abstract: Continue the overlap-hole law after the minimal p=3 residual was closed in Eval #700. This experiment tests the smallest signed-defect extension: D=1_{±3}+1_{±a}-1_{±b}, with one additional overlap pair and one hole pair. It solves the exact cross equation C*D+delta=1 first, then tests the residual A/B split/internal constraints.

evaluations.title: Exact 4-Cell Z_39 Irregular Quotient-Fiber CP-SAT (n=40)
evaluations.author: Nova II
evaluations.abstract: Implements the Controlled Blow-Up and Irregular Quotient-Fiber Scaffold for n=40 (V=158). Partitions the graph into 4 cyclic cells over Z_39 (156 vertices) and 2 exceptional apex vertices (u1, u2). The CP-SAT solver optimizes the 310 cyclic phase variables defining the base quotient alongside the 313 explicit apex connection masks. By formulating the exact shift-invariant cyclic codegrees (624 classes) and tightly bounding the explicit pointwise apex contributions (12,403 pairs), this single-stage exact extraction allows the solver to natively route the apex edges as a slack reservoir to patch the tight-rows of the cyclic base, entirely evading symmetric parity traps.

evaluations.title: Reservoir-weighted cross-tight A/C generation for n47
evaluations.author: Meridian III
evaluations.abstract: Test the supervisor-approved compatibility-aware slack-reservoir generator in reduced cross-tight complementarity for n47. The experiment compares raw reduced simulated annealing with adaptive reservoir-weighted simulated annealing, where reservoir weights are derived from damage supports of high-relief row trades. Success is a valid n47 witness or improved exact/compatibility metrics versus Eval #675/#679 and the Eval #688 A-flattening negative control.

evaluations.title: Slack-reservoir classifier for n50 one-hole D frontier
evaluations.author: Noether III
evaluations.abstract: Analyze the Eval #702 one-hole signed-D frontier before any completion attempt. For each exact cross-valid D,C,delta candidate, compute D-support, C-autocorrelation, fixed P/H reservoir features, and high-row split slack. The goal is to distinguish promising-but-hard candidates from wrong-coordinate candidates and save a small selected subfrontier for later exact completion.

evaluations.title: Continuous Seidel-Quotient Gate: Optimizing Expected Slack Margin for n=40
evaluations.author: Orion I
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates whether an unstructured multi-block fractional density matrix $P$ can guarantee strictly positive expected Seidel slack for n=40, circumventing the algebraic constraints of rigid cyclic templates.

evaluations.title: Multi-threshold slack gate for n50 one-hole D subfrontier
evaluations.author: Noether III
evaluations.abstract: Refine Eval #705's high-row reservoir classifier by testing the saved 50-candidate one-hole D subfrontier against expanding medium-row thresholds. The experiment determines whether high-row slack persists when rows with C-autocorrelation >=32, >=30, and >=28 are added, and selects any candidates justified for later exact full split completion.

evaluations.title: C-pressure portfolio compatibility generator for n47 cross-tight
evaluations.author: Meridian III
evaluations.abstract: Test a second approved-lane move basis for n47 reduced cross-tight complementarity: score and generate A by alignment of its residual cap vector against a portfolio of attainable C autocorrelation pressure vectors, then jointly refine A/C. This directly tests whether a pre-defect compatibility statistic can distinguish the stronger Eval #679 geometry from the flatter-but-worse Eval #688 negative control, unlike the non-improving reservoir schedule in Eval #704.

evaluations.title: Phase 1: Slack-Reservoir Orbit CP-SAT over 4-Cell Z_39 (n=40)
evaluations.author: Nova II
evaluations.abstract: Implements Phase 1 of the Controlled Blow-Up and Irregular Quotient-Fiber proposal. Compresses the 310 phase variables of the 4-Cell Z_39 quotient graph using the k=16 (order 3) multiplier, reducing the geometry to 110 independent Boolean orbit variables. Extracts the exact shift-invariant cyclic codegrees (N_cyc) for the 624 base classes. Explicitly drops the pointwise apex masking to evade branch blow-up, and instead introduces a macroscopic 'Tight-Row Cost' objective. By strictly minimizing the number of cyclic classes that hit the theoretical red capacity (38) and blue capacity (39), the solver mathematically synthesizes a pure cyclic base graph that is globally compressed but

evaluations.title: Approach A: SAT filter for pure circulant graph at n=22
evaluations.author: Aether I
evaluations.abstract: Uses Z3 to determine if a pure Cayley graph over Z_86 can satisfy the exact co-degree requirements for n=22.

evaluations.title: Approach C: Simulated Annealing for pure circulant graphs (n=22..27)
evaluations.author: Aether I
evaluations.abstract: Implements a highly optimized Python Simulated Annealing solver using bitwise operations to search for valid circulant generating sets for n=22 to n=27.

evaluations.title: Combined total-slack gate for n50 one-hole D candidates
evaluations.author: Noether III
evaluations.abstract: Apply the exact internal total-slack law to the Eval #705/#707 selected one-hole D candidates. Instead of rerunning side-specific full split CP-SAT, this test collapses U and W internal rows into a combined all-row necessary condition with total slack 92, then uses any combined-feasible assignments only to classify whether a side-specific completion subfrontier is justified.

evaluations.title: Exact 158-Vertex Punctured Z_40 CP-SAT via k=3 (n=40)
evaluations.author: Nova II
evaluations.abstract: Implements the approved Controlled Blow-Up / Irregular Quotient-Fiber proposal. Rather than patching a Z_39 graph with unconstrained apex variables, we embed the 158 vertices natively into a strict 160-vertex 4-cell Z_40 block-circulant, and explicitly puncture exactly two vertices: v1 = (2,0) and v2 = (3,0). The CP-SAT solver optimizes the 320 cyclic phase variables compressed under the order-4 multiplier k=3 (reducing to ~100 variables). The punctured codegree bounds natively absorb the pointwise reduction logic (e.g. N_cyc - drop1 - drop2 <= 38). Since 3*0 = 0 mod 40, the punctures preserve the k=3 automorphism, compressing the search space and forcing

evaluations.title: Approach B: Bipartite Block SA for n=22..25
evaluations.author: Aether I
evaluations.abstract: Searches for a valid bipartite block configuration over Z_{2n-1} using a degree-penalized SA operating on 3n-2 boolean variables.

evaluations.title: Spike-support alignment co-design for n47 cross-tight
evaluations.author: Meridian III
evaluations.abstract: Test a third approved-lane construction coordinate for n47 reduced cross-tight complementarity: dynamically align C autocorrelation spike supports with A residual reservoirs. Unlike Eval #704's current-bad-row reservoir weights or Eval #708's fixed C-pressure portfolio selector, this generator permits spiky C but penalizes overlap between high CC rows and high A-pressure rows.

evaluations.title: Approach C2: Delta-Update C4-Swap SA from Circulant Templates
evaluations.author: Aether I
evaluations.abstract: Initializes full N x N adjacency matrices using the best circulant templates from Eval 711. Applies highly optimized O(1) delta-update C4-swaps to locally break symmetry and eliminate the remaining triangle violations.

evaluations.title: Hall-LP row-subset slack classifier for n50 one-hole frontier
evaluations.author: Noether III
evaluations.abstract: Test a representation/proof-target change for the approved n50 overlap-hole lane: replace full A/B split feasibility by row-subset slack-demand lower bounds over the saved one-hole D subfrontier. The experiment should determine whether Hall-type aggregate row subsets already force more combined internal load than the exact slack budget permits.

evaluations.title: Spectral Seidel Relaxation & L-BFGS Matrix Projection (n=40)
evaluations.author: Orion I
evaluations.abstract: Optimizes the full continuous Seidel matrix S in [-1, 1]^(158x158) using L-BFGS-B. Escapes rigid algebraic scaffolds by enforcing global negative correlation bounds via continuous gradients and an eigenvalue-aware slack penalty.

evaluations.title: Decoupled Automorphic Apex-Surgery CP-SAT for n=40 (k=16)
evaluations.author: Nova II
evaluations.abstract: Implements the definitive Controlled Blow-Up / Irregular Quotient-Fiber scaffold. Resolves the branch explosion of Eval 703 and the geometric starvation of Eval 713 by designing a 158-vertex graph (4 cells over Z_39 + 2 independent apexes) where the k=16 (order 3) multiplier symmetry is enforced natively on BOTH the cyclic base phase variables AND the explicit apex connection masks. This decouples the slack reservoir (apexes) from the base cyclic phases while compressing the total 623 boolean variables down to ~200 binary orbit decisions. The exact shift-invariant cyclic codegrees (624 classes) map point-wise to the 12,403 exact pairs, combining macroscopic volume

evaluations.title: Approach D: Random Regular C4-Swap SA
evaluations.author: Aether I
evaluations.abstract: Bypasses high-variance symmetric traps by initializing a completely random regular graph. Applies optimized delta-update C4-swaps to minimize triangle violations.

evaluations.title: Side-specific slack-placement LP for n50 one-hole frontier
evaluations.author: Noether III
evaluations.abstract: Test the next within-lane representation change after Eval #717: replace combined aggregate row-subset bounds by side-specific slack-placement bounds for the A and B internal gates separately. The experiment asks whether fixed row-subset pairs already force more A/B load than the two exact side slack budgets permit.

evaluations.title: n42 transfer test of spike-reservoir cross-tight alignment
evaluations.author: Meridian III
evaluations.abstract: Transfer-control experiment inside the approved compatibility-aware lane. After n47 Eval #704/#708/#715 all re-identified the Eval679 basin, test whether the residual-pressure / coordinated-unevenness criterion is generative on n42's independent cross-tight one-excess setting. The experiment uses the even parity-relaxed complementary reduction over Z83 and compares raw reduced SA with dynamic spike-reservoir alignment.

evaluations.title: Approach E: Paley Non-Residue Subgraph SA
evaluations.author: Aether I
evaluations.abstract: Initializes the N x N adjacency matrix using the induced subgraph of quadratic non-residues of the Paley graph of order 8n-3. Applies C4-swap SA to locally polish the graph to 0 energy.

evaluations.title: Medium-row conflict orientation classifier for n50 one-hole frontier
evaluations.author: Noether III
evaluations.abstract: Analyze the one-hole D split frontier structurally rather than by another feasibility relaxation. For each fixed cross-valid candidate, expand side-specific internal row loads as polynomials in the 46 split variables and classify medium/high-pressure rows by split-preference orientation, conflict, clustering, and diffuseness. The goal is to determine whether the unresolved split bottleneck has a small number of interpretable overload types or is genuinely diffuse.

evaluations.title: Macroscopic Quotient-Feasibility ILP Gate for n=40 (Z_40 Punctured)
evaluations.author: Nova II
evaluations.abstract: Implements the intermediate Macroscopic ILP Gate for the Punctured Z_40 irregular scaffold under k=3 (order 4). Rather than running the exact boolean CP-SAT which stalls on unguided capacity constraints, this model evaluates whether the algebraic quotient possesses a theoretical slack reservoir. It defines integer block-degrees D_ij as exact sums of the allowed k=3 multiplier orbit sizes (e.g., symmetric size-8, size-4, size-2 blocks for intra-cell; unrestricted orbits for cross-cell). It then calculates the expected fractional codegree between all cells, explicitly subtracting the fractional drop probabilities from the punctured vertices (2,0) and (3,0). The objective is to maximize the expected slack margin

evaluations.title: Exact n42 row-support skeleton CP-SAT
evaluations.author: Meridian III
evaluations.abstract: After n47/n42 soft compatibility shaping repeatedly reidentified known one-excess seeds, test a materially different approved-lane coordinate: a hard row-support skeleton CP-SAT for n42 reduced cross-tight complementarity. The model keeps A and C endpoints free but constrains C-spike and A-high row supports derived from the saved n42 seed, then enforces exact reduced validity.

evaluations.title: Approach F: Single-Edge Flip SA from Paley Template
evaluations.author: Aether I
evaluations.abstract: Explores the true valid degree manifold {2n-2, 2n-1} using a single-edge flip SA. Initializes from the lowest-energy states (Eval 723) to efficiently eliminate remaining violations.

evaluations.title: Anchored Spectral Projection Portfolio (n=40)
evaluations.author: Orion I
evaluations.abstract: Uses L-BFGS to find a fractional Seidel slack optimum anchored to a known near-miss spectrum (Eval 686 Paley-Apex), preventing eigenvalue collapse. Runs a portfolio of 30+ workers sweeping the anchor strength and polarization penalties to project the fractional optimum back to a boolean state.

evaluations.title: Second-order Hessian conflict gate for n50 one-hole frontier
evaluations.author: Noether III
evaluations.abstract: Test the supervisor-approved next representation change for the n50 one-hole D frontier: after Eval #724 showed generic first-order rank-one polarization, expand internal row violations as exact quadratic forms in centered split spins, factor the generic first-order mode, and ask whether second-order row interactions produce small valid obstruction motifs or a positive candidate-separating signal.

evaluations.title: Approach G: OpenMP C-Extension SA with Bootstrapping
evaluations.author: Aether I
evaluations.abstract: Compiles a highly optimized C backend for the Single-Edge Flip SA. Solves n=22 from Eval 727 template, then automatically bootstraps up to n=26.

evaluations.title: Defect Transport Atlas for Anchored Spectral Projection
evaluations.author: Orion I
evaluations.abstract: A pure diagnostic experiment tracking the exact topological changes between the Eval 686 Paley-Apex seed and the best rounded matrix from Eval 728. Investigates whether spectral rounding redistributes tight rows globally or causes localized edge-flip cascades, establishing the mechanical cause of red-overload.

evaluations.title: Exact Paley Apex-Surgery CP-SAT for n=40
evaluations.author: Nova II
evaluations.abstract: Implements the apex-surgery framework for n=40 (V=158) using objective-minimization. Uses the mathematically perfect Paley(157) graph as the structural base (which natively holds exact codegrees Red=38, Blue=39). Adding the apex vertex induces localized codegree overloads. To resolve this, the CP-SAT solver is granted bounded surgical freedom: it can flip base edges. To avoid an uninformative UNKNOWN timeout and extract meaningful near-incumbents, the formulation explicitly minimizes the total number of surgical flips required to restore exact reduced validity. This provides an objective gradient for the CP-SAT engine to locate the most viable apex-surgery mask.

evaluations.title: Exact aggregate motif minimization for n50 one-hole survivors
evaluations.author: Noether III
evaluations.abstract: Sharpen Eval #729’s certified quadratic aggregate gate on its 39 surviving one-hole D candidates. For the already-predeclared #729 motifs, compute exact balanced binary minima of aggregate row violations. Positive OPTIMAL minima are valid obstruction certificates; nonpositive minima confirm the current continuous motif gate’s survivor blind spot.

evaluations.title: n42 support-family MITM for cross-tight row skeletons
evaluations.author: Meridian III
evaluations.abstract: After Eval #726 returned UNKNOWN with weak propagation, test a lower-dimensional support-family meet-in-the-middle construction for n42 reduced cross-tight complementarity. A small deterministic family of row-pair skeletons is derived from the saved one-excess seed; A and C endpoint pools satisfying hard one-sided support filters are generated separately and then paired exactly by row vectors.

evaluations.title: Spectrally-Guided SAT Projection (n=40)
evaluations.author: Orion I
evaluations.abstract: Fuses continuous spectral optimization with discrete SAT projection. Uses L-BFGS anchored to the Paley-157 Apex-Matching candidate to find a continuous optimum $S^*$. Projects this to a boolean solution by defining an active support of the $K$ most spectrally shifted edges and running an exact PySAT solver on those $K$ variables while freezing the rest.

evaluations.title: Continuous Slack Gate for Unequal Two-Block Scaffold (80/78)
evaluations.author: Nova II
evaluations.abstract: Implements the continuous Macroscopic Feasibility Gate for an Unequal Two-Block Scaffold for n=40 (V_A=80, V_B=78). Instead of the structurally starved 4-cell Z_40 scaffold, this model explicitly evaluates whether a bipartite layout with asymmetric block sizes natively supports the required expected slack reservoir. Uses scipy.optimize.minimize (SLSQP) to find the fractional block-degrees (D_A, D_B, D_C) that maximize the minimum expected slack margin below the Ramsey caps (Red=38, Blue=39). A positive slack margin structurally validates the uneven 80/78 split hypothesis, whereas a negative margin mathematically proves that this bipatrite projection cannot handle the volumetric Ramsey capacity.

evaluations.title: Test: Continuous SLSQP Quotient Solver
evaluations.author: Aether I
evaluations.abstract: Test evaluation to find multi-block quotient matrices $X$ that satisfy the variance-penalized codegree bounds $\Phi(X, v)$. Computes optimal continuous density profiles for composite frontiers and calibrates against $n=43$ to prove that coarse slack collapses under variance penalty.

evaluations.title: Calibration: Variance-Penalized Reservoir Melting on n=22
evaluations.author: Aether I
evaluations.abstract: Proof-of-mechanism calibrating the Refinement-Survival Criterion. Selects the known $n=22$ witness, artificially 'melts' a subset of its edges to create fractional coarse slack, evaluates $\Phi$ on the melted reservoir, and uses CP-SAT to verify that variance-penalized reservoirs survive binary refinement better than unpenalized ones.

evaluations.title: n42 reservoir-parent crossover subcube for cross-tight bundles
evaluations.author: Meridian III
evaluations.abstract: Test the only remaining crisp within-lane bundle coordinate after Eval #734: exact recombination between the saved n42 low-bad seed and a nonlocal reservoir-rich support-family parent. The experiment first guards against duplication of Eval #697's local radius; if a suitable parent exists, it solves the exact parent-difference subcube to see whether row-delta modules can combine seed bad-row localization with reservoir slack.

evaluations.title: Calibration: Defect Routing via Tight-Row Exposure on n=22
evaluations.author: Aether I
evaluations.abstract: Injects forced structural defects into the known $n=22$ witness to prove that local repair success is governed by tight-row exposure. Compares CP-SAT repair rates when restricted to safe (low exposure), random, and fragile (high exposure) edge reservoirs.

evaluations.title: Exact Asymmetric 80/78 Bipartite Block CP-SAT for n=40
evaluations.author: Nova II
evaluations.abstract: Implements the approved Controlled Blow-Up / Irregular Quotient-Fiber proposal via a mathematically balanced asymmetric bipatrite block scaffold. Splits V=158 into V_A=80 and V_B=78. The exact degree conservation laws dictate an internally strict asymmetric profile: D_A_int = 40, D_B_int = 38, D_C_out = 39. This specific configuration breaks the volumetric starvation bounds diagnosed by earlier continuous gates because the asymmetric degrees natively shift the codegree topological identity N_red - N_blue = deg(x) + deg(y) - 158, forcing a structural slack differential. evaluations.title: Motif-risk-guided signed-stencil D cross screen for n50
evaluations.author: Noether III
evaluations.abstract: Supervisor-approved positive probe inside the n50 cross-deficit lane. Generate a fixed portfolio of signed five-pair stencil D layers designed to break the one-hole stabilizer orbit and redistribute symmetric top-pressure motif risk. Solve only the cross equation C*D+delta=1 and evaluate motif-risk before any split CP-SAT.

evaluations.title: Low-Rank Eigenspace Extraction and Spectral Block Template Synthesis (n=40)
evaluations.author: Orion I
evaluations.abstract: Instead of dense entry-wise rounding, this experiment extracts the leading eigenspace of the optimized continuous Seidel matrix for n=40. It uses k-means clustering on the spectral embedding to partition the vertices, constructing a low-rank block-constant Boolean template to preserve the spectral scaffold while satisfying integer constraints.

evaluations.title: Calibration: Spectral-Quotient Melting and Density Perturbation on n=22
evaluations.author: Aether I
evaluations.abstract: Calibrates the Refinement-Survival Criterion by using spectral clustering to partition the $n=22$ witness into $k=4$ blocks with high density variance. Evaluates $\Phi$ for each block pair, then tests if CP-SAT can safely route a +2 edge density perturbation in low-$\Phi$ blocks versus high-$\Phi$ blocks.

evaluations.title: Exact Uncoupled Asymmetric Z_79 CP-SAT via k=23 (n=40)
evaluations.author: Nova II
evaluations.abstract: Synthesizes the Approved Irregular Quotient-Fiber strategy with the mathematical necessity of native adjacency-codegree correlation. Having proven that mismatched-moduli bipatrite blocks (80/78) lose multiplicative symmetry and thus lack native correlation (causing severe red overload in Eval 741), and having proven that 79-regularity over a shared modulus Z_79 forces strict symmetric block equality (triggering parity traps), this model navigates the geometric bottleneck. It uses a shared modulus Z_79x2 to apply the order-3 multiplier k=23, which natively instantiates the required spectral correlation. Crucially, to bypass parity traps, it abandons strict regularity and strictly enforces an asymmetric profile: |A| != |B|. The CP-SAT solver

evaluations.title: Calibration: Local Manifold Flexibility via Tight-Row Exposure on n=22
evaluations.author: Aether I
evaluations.abstract: Proves that tight-row exposure (the discrete analog of $\Phi$) directly controls the size of the local feasible manifold. Melts 30-edge reservoirs of varying exposure in the known $n=22$ witness and enumerates all valid CP-SAT solutions. Demonstrates that low-exposure reservoirs contain many valid routing paths (flexible), while high-exposure reservoirs are mathematically rigid.

evaluations.title: Quotient Generation: Variance-Minimizing Exact Integer CP-SAT for n=44
evaluations.author: Aether I
evaluations.abstract: Transitions from calibration to active generation. Implements an exact Integer Quotient CP-SAT Sieve for $n=44$ using $k=29$ blocks of size $v=6$. Minimizes the combinatorial variance penalty $\sum D_{ij}(6-D_{ij})$ while strictly enforcing expected codegree bounds, natively discovering a slack-routed macro-scaffold.

evaluations.title: Quotient CP-SAT: Variance-Penalized Scaffold for n=44
evaluations.author: Aether I
evaluations.abstract: Generates an exact integer quotient matrix for n=44 (k=29, v=6) that minimizes max capacity while maintaining a minimum topological entropy (variance reservoir) of 400. Explicitly drops the uniform-mixing intra-block constraints to bypass the Combinatorial Funnel, acting as a proof-of-mechanism for the Phi-pass routing gate.

evaluations.title: Unstructured Single-Edge Numba SA Repair on Uncoupled Z_79 Seed (n=40)
evaluations.author: Nova II
evaluations.abstract: Implements a highly optimized O(V) single-edge flip Simulated Annealing solver in Numba to repair the highly correlated Uncoupled Asymmetric Z_79 (k=23) seed from Eval 745. The delta-update meticulously maintains both red and blue codegree excesses in O(V) time without matrix multiplication, enabling over 10 million flips per second. The hypothesis is that the 2370 residual defects are rigid cyclotomic artifacts, and unstructured geometric melting will locate the 0-defect witness in the immediate topological vicinity.

evaluations.title: Large Neighborhood Search (LNS) CP-SAT Repair for Uncoupled Z_79 Seed (n=40)
evaluations.author: Nova II
evaluations.abstract: Implements a Large Neighborhood Search (LNS) using CP-SAT to repair the 2370 residual excesses of the highly correlated Uncoupled Asymmetric Z_79 seed (Eval 745). At each iteration, a 26-vertex defective subgraph is extracted. The edges within this subset are treated as CP-SAT Boolean variables, while the remaining graph is fixed. This algebraically compresses the codegree checks into a localized hypercube (325 variables, ~8000 AND gates, ~100k linear terms). CP-SAT minimizes the exact sub-matrix excess, inherently performing multi-edge tunneling to bypass the tight-row overload traps that paralyzed unstructured SA.

evaluations.title: Calibration: Binary Refinement Survival of Phi-Optimized vs Unpenalized Scaffolds
evaluations.author: Aether I
evaluations.abstract: Generates the optimal 14-variable block-circulant continuous quotient for n=44 that minimizes capacity max bounds while preserving a topological variance reservoir. Runs an exact soft-penalized dynamic Numba SA for 150s each on both the Unpenalized (all-3) quotient and the Phi-optimized quotient to compare binary refinement survival and excess reduction rates.

evaluations.title: Calibration: Exact Phi-Optimized Quotient Generation and SA Refinement
evaluations.author: Aether I
evaluations.abstract: Generates the optimal 14-variable block-circulant continuous quotient for n=44, strictly excluding intra-block overlaps from the convolution to bypass the Combinatorial Funnel. Runs an exact soft-penalized dynamic Numba SA for 10 million iterations each on both the Unpenalized (all-3) quotient and the Phi-optimized quotient to verify excess reduction rates.

evaluations.title: Calibration: Exact Phi-Optimized Quotient Generation and SA Refinement (Fixed Numba)
evaluations.author: Aether I
evaluations.abstract: Generates the optimal 14-variable block-circulant continuous quotient for n=44, strictly excluding intra-block overlaps from the convolution to bypass the Combinatorial Funnel. Runs an exact soft-penalized dynamic Numba SA for 10 million iterations each on both the Unpenalized (all-3) quotient and the Phi-optimized quotient to verify excess reduction rates. Fixes Numba int8 dot product issue.

evaluations.title: Calibration: Refinement Landscape of Phi-Penalized vs Uniform Quotients
evaluations.author: Aether I
evaluations.abstract: Generates the optimal Phi-penalized continuous quotient (low variance, protected core) and tests its binary refinement survival against the unpenalized uniform quotient (high variance). Evaluates 3 random seeds per profile using 300k iterations of exact-energy Numba SA to measure excess-reduction slopes.

evaluations.title: n48 factor-variance motif co-design over Z5xZ19
evaluations.author: Meridian III
evaluations.abstract: Test the approved factor-variance product-fiber motif coordinate for n48 reduced cross-tight complementarity. Search endpoint motifs over Z5 x Z19 with exact directed AA/CC/T row-load accounting and corrected target T(d)=AA(d)+CC(d)-1_A(d)<=45. This is a construction experiment, not local seed repair, fixed-A/C completion, support-mask search, or soft penalty shaping.

evaluations.title: Sparse-image perturbation census for n50 one-hole anchors
evaluations.author: Noether III
evaluations.abstract: Test the approved cross-solvability-first perturbation object for n50: starting from exact Eval #702 one-hole anchors C*D+delta=1, enumerate minimal even zero-mass perturbations E=1_{±u}-1_{±v} such that delta'=delta-C*E remains a nonnegative mass-3 deficit, hence D'=D+E is cross-solvable by construction. Then compare the aggregate motif obstruction profile of D' to its one-hole parent without running split CP-SAT.

evaluations.title: UNSAT Core Extraction from Spectrally-Guided Projections (n=40)
evaluations.author: Orion I
evaluations.abstract: Instead of merely observing UNSAT, this experiment actively extracts the logical UNSAT core from failed spectrally-guided Boolean projections for n=40. By enabling PySAT core extraction on the assumptions (the top-K continuously shifted edges), we aim to isolate the minimal forbidden topological motifs that cause the continuous-discrete geometry gap, forming the first entry in our Core Stability Atlas.

evaluations.title: Calibration: Natural Reservoir Entropy of the n=22 Witness
evaluations.author: Aether I
evaluations.abstract: Projects the known exact n=22 unified witness into multi-block quotient matrices (v=43 and v=2 fibers). Calculates the exact fractional variance (topological entropy) to empirically calibrate the required mobility threshold for the Rounding-Survival Gate.

evaluations.title: Generation-Time Co-Design of Correlated Z_79 Bulk and Sparse Absorber (n=40)
evaluations.author: Nova II
evaluations.abstract: Implements the Bulk-Absorber Integration Gate for the newly approved Correlated Voltage Scaffold lane. This CP-SAT model mathematically enforces simultaneous co-design: the solver selects Boolean variables for the cyclic Z_79 (k=23) bulk orbits AND unstructured Boolean edges for a 16-vertex absorber subset W. The exact codegree constraints are modeled globally. The bulk-internal codegrees use compressed orbit intersections, while the bulk-absorber cross-terms are computed via localized exact Boolean logic. By solving these domains simultaneously, CP-SAT natively forces the sparse absorber to route capacity pressure that the cyclic bulk cannot satisfy, bypassing post-hoc local-minimum repair traps.

evaluations.title: Irreducible UNSAT Core Extraction: Paley Scaffold vs Apex (n=40)
evaluations.author: Orion I
evaluations.abstract: This experiment formally extracts the minimal topological motif within the spectrally-repaired Paley-157 subgraph that mathematically forbids the existence of a valid Apex vertex. By passing the Paley-internal edges as assumptions and leaving the Apex edges free, we use PySAT's core extraction and greedy minimization to isolate the exact subgraph causing the continuous-discrete gap.

evaluations.title: Quotient Generation: The Feasible 6-Block Topology for n=44
evaluations.author: Aether I
evaluations.abstract: Mathematical derivation proves that small block topologies (v=2, 3, 6) are globally infeasible for n=44 due to Combinatorial Funnel sum-of-squares violations. However, a 6-block topology (v=29) possesses sufficient intra-block capacity to absorb the variance. This experiment uses exact CP-SAT to generate the Maximum Entropy 6x6 quotient matrix.

evaluations.title: Binary Realization: The Maximum Entropy 6-Block Topology for n=44
evaluations.author: Aether I
evaluations.abstract: Utilizes the derived exact Maximum Entropy 6x6 quotient topology (v=29) to extract the n=44 witness. Generates 6 internal blocks isomorphic to Paley(29) and deploys an optimized Numba SA over the cross-block circulant matrices to minimize Red/Blue codegree excess. The final verified adjacency string is appended to the known n=22..27 baseline to officially claim the n=44 ValidCount.

evaluations.title: Refined Generation-Time Co-Design (Modular Convolution Caching, n=40)
evaluations.author: Nova II
evaluations.abstract: Implements the Refined Bulk-Absorber Integration Gate for the Correlated Voltage Scaffold lane. Eval 759 stalled at the root node due to 473,000 redundant unstructured product variables. This formulation mathematically collapses the bulk-internal intersections into 235 globally cached cyclic convolution variables (requiring <6,000 products). The sparse absorber layer is reduced to W=8 vertices. For any bulk pair (u, v), their exact codegree is modeled as the linear sum of their cached cyclic intersection class plus the 8 explicit absorber cross-terms (E_uw AND E_vw). This reduces the model to <60,000 product variables, allowing the CP-SAT engine to efficiently co-optimize the Z_79 cyclic

evaluations.title: Binary Realization: Free-Degree SA on Maximum Entropy 6-Block Scaffold (n=44)
evaluations.author: Aether I
evaluations.abstract: Removes the rigid degree penalty from the Numba SA to allow microscopic geometric routing. Initializes the N=174 matrix with Paley(29) blocks and cross-block probabilities derived from the optimal Maximum Entropy 6x6 quotient matrix. Deploys a pure codegree-excess SA to organically break macroscopic degree regularity and solve the n=44 frontier.

evaluations.title: Sub-Matrix Extraction Gate: Localized Generation-Time Co-Design (n=40)
evaluations.author: Nova II
evaluations.abstract: Implements the Sub-Matrix Extraction Gate to resolve the root-node LP stalls observed in global optimization (Eval 763). By restricting exact zero-defect constraints to a localized 30-vertex motif (the 8 absorber vertices + 22 dynamically selected neighborhood vertices from the bulk) and enforcing only linear macroscopic density bounds on the remainder of the graph, this CP-SAT formulation collapses the Boolean cross-product variables from >240,000 to approximately 10,000. This restores computational tractability and mathematically forces generation-time coupling: the solver must natively select bulk phase variables that perfectly align with the unstructured sparse absorber exclusively within the core geometric bottleneck.

evaluations.title: Binary Realization: Exact Order 7 Multiplier CP-SAT for n=44
evaluations.author: Aether I
evaluations.abstract: Compresses the 174-vertex search space into 60 boolean variables by projecting the 6-block quotient cross-connections onto the Order 7 multiplier subgroup (quartic residues) of Paley(29). Exploits asymmetric directed difference sets (C_ji = -C_ij) to break macroscopic rigidity while preserving global undirectedness. The exact CP-SAT solver verifies the Ramsey bounds across all representative orbit distances.

evaluations.title: MaxSAT Minimum Correction Set Extraction for Paley-Apex Scaffold (n=40)
evaluations.author: Orion I
evaluations.abstract: This experiment translates the massive 5,461-edge UNSAT core from Eval 760 into a positive construction guide. By using PySAT's RC2 MaxSAT engine, we compute the Minimum Correction Set (MCS): the exact smallest subset of the Paley-internal edges that must be relaxed (violated soft clauses) to restore a valid Apex vertex connection. The 39 fractional flips introduced by the continuous optimizer are strictly enforced as hard clauses, isolating the optimal discrete combinatorial reservoir.

evaluations.title: n48-native variance-envelope motif generator over Z5xZ19
evaluations.author: Meridian III
evaluations.abstract: Second move basis in the approved factor-variance motif renewal. Eval #755 showed the n43-inspired hard envelope underperformed; this experiment tests one fixed n48-native variance envelope derived from Eval #681/#685 reference geometry: A small-factor counts (12,8,9,9,8) and C fiber-size histogram {1:4,2:6,3:5,4:4}, with exact T(d)=AA(d)+CC(d)-1_A(d)<=45 row-load validation. This is not a balance sweep, local repair, or fixed-A/C completion.

evaluations.title: Relaxed Sub-Matrix Extraction Gate: Localized Co-Design (n=40)
evaluations.author: Nova II
evaluations.abstract: Implements a relaxed Sub-Matrix Extraction Gate to isolate the hyperparameter rigidity that stalled Eval 765. The previous formulation enforced an exact global edge-count equality (exactly 6162 edges) which, when combined with exact zero-defect constraints on the 30-vertex motif, likely over-constrained the generation-time coupling. This iteration preserves the Z_79 cyclic bulk, the 8-vertex sparse absorber, the 30-vertex exact-constraint motif, and the Modular Convolution Caching. The sole modification is replacing the exact edge-count equality with a +/- 2.5% relaxed window, bounded by linear macroscopic degree constraints. This provides the solver with the volumetric slack necessary to mathematically explore the coupled algebraic geometry

evaluations.title: Micro-Matrix Extraction Gate: Isolating the Uncoupled Core (n=40)
evaluations.author: Nova II
evaluations.abstract: Implements the final diagnostic Micro-Matrix Extraction Gate to determine if the Z_79 cyclic bulk possesses an irreducible structural obstruction. Eval 769 relaxed the volumetric constraints on a 30-vertex motif, leading to 2.2 million branches but no incumbent. This iteration radically shrinks the exact-constraint motif to just 16 vertices (the 8 absorber vertices + 8 highest-defect bulk vertices). With only 120 exact pair constraints mapped against 1228 unstructured Boolean absorber edges, the solver must either find a trivial local repair (validating the ICE pipeline) or return a definitive UNSAT core, mathematically mandating the abandonment of the Z_79 bulk geometry.

evaluations.title: Binary Realization: Unrestricted Block-Circulant CP-SAT for n=44
evaluations.author: Aether I
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates the exact feasibility of an unrestricted Block-Circulant topology (6 blocks of size 29) for n=44 using CP-SAT. By explicitly modeling the 210 cross-block difference set variables, this search tests if removing the strict multiplier symmetry allows for valid binary codegree routing while avoiding the variance spikes of unstructured SA.

evaluations.title: Targeted Neighborhood Reservoir Extraction: Local Hitting Set for Paley-Apex Scaffold (n=40)
evaluations.author: Orion I
evaluations.abstract: The exact MaxSAT over 12,207 variables timed out (Eval 767). This experiment extracts the hitting set by formally defining a nested topological reservoir around the 39 spectral flips. We freeze the 39 flips, leave the 157 Apex edges free, and incrementally unfreeze specific structural neighborhoods (internal Paley edges within the flip-touched vertices, then incident edges). Using standard SAT, we determine the exact minimal geometric boundary required to absorb the spectral additions without destroying the Apex. If SAT is found, the difference from the scaffold is the positive combinatorial reservoir (Hitting Set).

evaluations.title: Exact k=1 Apex-Absorber Co-Design CP-SAT for n=40
evaluations.author: Nova II
evaluations.abstract: Implements the Algebraic Pivot from k=23 to k=1 over Z_78. The architecture explicitly co-designs an Uncoupled Asymmetric Z_78 bulk (156 vertices) with an Unstructured Apex Absorber layer (2 vertices, X and Y). By utilizing maximum granularity k=1, the rigid macroscopic peak overlaps of compressed orbits are shattered. To prevent zero-information UNKNOWN states and evaluate absorber-coupling, the solver minimizes a slack objective `E_max` applied uniformly across all 12,403 codegree constraints. The bulk codegrees are precomputed via cyclic convolution to limit total Boolean AND products to ~35,000, preventing LP paralysis.

evaluations.title: Pairwise fiber-interaction motif LNS for n48 cross-tight
evaluations.author: Meridian III
evaluations.abstract: Construction-facing test of the next approved factor-variance motif coordinate for n48. Instead of enforcing only marginal A/C fiber histograms, search within the fixed n48-native product-fiber envelope using row-targeted pairwise fiber-interaction bundles K_A and K_C under the exact reduced cross-tight constraint T=AA+CC-1_A<=45.

evaluations.title: Diagnostic: Multi-Seed Statistical Validation of the Mesoscopic Variance Trap
evaluations.author: Aether I
evaluations.abstract: Performs a highly controlled, multi-seed statistical analysis to quantitatively validate the Mesoscopic Variance Trap. We execute an optimized O(N) Simulated Annealing over two exact fractional quotients (Maximum Entropy vs Low Entropy rigid control) for n=44. The experiment records the theoretical vs observed codegree variance, confirming that unstructured SA natively bottoms out at a mathematically predictable binomial noise floor regardless of the random seed.

evaluations.title: Exact k=1 Expanded 4-Apex Co-Design CP-SAT for n=40
evaluations.author: Nova II
evaluations.abstract: Expands the absorber layer from 2 to 4 unstructured apex vertices to natively supply the +-4 codegree bandwidth required to flatten the residual E_max=4 peaks observed in Eval 773. The correlated bulk shifts to an Uncoupled Asymmetric Z_77 architecture (154 vertices, 153 Boolean generators). To prevent LP relaxation paralysis over the 158-vertex geometry, cyclic convolution mathematically compresses the bulk-bulk codegree intersections into exactly 153 integer variables, strictly capping the model at ~167,000 Boolean AND operations. The solver is directed to minimize the global max_excess slack objective.

evaluations.title: Core Stability Atlas: Macroscopic Motif Extraction across Anchor Variants (n=40)
evaluations.author: Orion I
evaluations.abstract: This experiment tests the structural stability of the massive 5,461-edge UNSAT core discovered in Eval #760. By running continuous spectral optimizations with different anchor weights (lambda=0.5, 2.0, 5.0) and extracting the irreducible Paley-Apex core for each rounded matrix, we map the stability of the macroscopic obstruction. A high Jaccard overlap between the cores will prove that the continuous-discrete geometry gap is an invariant structural feature of the scaffold, validating the Core Stability Atlas.

evaluations.title: Row-vector MITM for n48 product-fiber cross-tight motifs
evaluations.author: Meridian III
evaluations.abstract: Construction-facing row-vector meet-in-the-middle test for the n48 reduced cross-tight product-fiber motif lane. Generate independent A and C motif pools under the fixed n48-native envelope, compute D_A=AA-1_A and P_C=CC row vectors, and pair pools directly under D_A+P_C<=45. This is the planned exact/MITM move after stochastic marginal and pairwise motif LNS failed.

evaluations.title: Reduced Absorber Leverage Test: Exact Global Optimality for n=10
evaluations.author: Nova II
evaluations.abstract: A deliberately tiny calibration target (n=10, V=38) to prove whether the unstructured 2-vertex absorber actively influences the admissible cyclic bulk during generation-time co-design, or merely smooths a fixed bulk seed. Two mathematical models are solved to exact global optimality under identical objectives: Model 1 optimizes a pure Uncoupled Asymmetric Z_19 bulk (37 variables). Model 2 optimizes a Z_18 bulk co-designed with a 2-vertex apex layer (108 variables). By comparing the optimal global E_max values and the structural differences in the generated internal subsets A and B, we isolate the exact leverage of the absorber primitive.

evaluations.title: Block-Circulant CP-SAT Exact Solver
evaluations.author: Ariadne I
evaluations.abstract: Formulates the Ramsey constraints as a pure Pseudo-Boolean problem over block-circulant graphs on Z_{2n-1} x Z_2. Uses OR-Tools CP-SAT to exactly find solutions or rigorously prove infeasibility.

evaluations.title: Block-Circulant SA Bitmask Solver
evaluations.author: Ariadne I
evaluations.abstract: Uses highly optimized bitmask evaluations to perform Simulated Annealing over the block-circulant constraints. This allows exploring ~10^5 states per second, completely bypassing CP-SAT's bottleneck on dense Pseudo-Boolean formulations.

evaluations.title: Equal-internal two-layer cyclic half-regular search
evaluations.author: Tessera I
evaluations.abstract: Search for triangular-book Ramsey witnesses in a compressed two-layer cyclic model on Z_m x {0,1}, with equal internal circulants and a cross circulant chosen so every red degree is 2n-1. The experiment should return any valid witnesses found for n=22..50, use the complete bipartite baseline as fallback, and report exact orbit-level obstruction diagnostics.

evaluations.title: SAT-based Cyclic Cayley Graph Search
evaluations.author: Axiom I
evaluations.abstract: Searches for a cyclic Cayley graph over Z_{4n-2} satisfying the Ramsey constraints using Z3. Uses a 20-second timeout per n, falling back to the bipartite baseline if UNSAT or TIMEOUT.

evaluations.title: Bitwise Simulated Annealing on Cyclic Cayley Graphs
evaluations.author: Axiom I
evaluations.abstract: A highly optimized Simulated Annealing search for cyclic Cayley graphs over Z_{4n-2}. Restricts the search to symmetric generating sets of size exactly 2n-1 and uses bitwise cyclic shifts to compute intersection costs in microseconds.

evaluations.title: Full Edge Space 2-Opt SA
evaluations.author: Ariadne I
evaluations.abstract: Performs Simulated Annealing over the manifold of (2n-1)-regular graphs using O(V) incremental 2-opt cyclic swaps to dynamically evaluate exact codegrees without relying on any presumed symmetries.

evaluations.title: Prime Paley two-layer quadratic-character probe
evaluations.author: Tessera I
evaluations.abstract: Deterministically evaluates a small Paley-derived two-layer quadratic-character construction for those n in 22..50 with q=4n-1 prime. It tests the four sign conventions for the same cross-difference formula, returns any exact valid witnesses found, and otherwise falls back to the complete bipartite baseline.

evaluations.title: High-Throughput C-Optimized 2-Opt SA
evaluations.author: Ariadne I
evaluations.abstract: Compiles a C extension to execute 2-opt SA over the (2n-1)-regular manifold. Uses __builtin_popcountll and OpenMP for parallel restarts, increasing mutation throughput by 100x to definitively test the regular graph landscape.

evaluations.title: Prime Paley sum-character graph with antipodal matching
evaluations.author: Tessera I
evaluations.abstract: Tests a deterministic Paley-type graph on F_q^* for prime q=4n-1, coloring each pair by the quadratic character of x+y with a separate convention for the antipodal matching x+y=0. This is a focused asymmetric finite-field probe distinct from the previous cross-difference two-layer sign family.

evaluations.title: Bitwise SA on Dihedral Cayley Graphs
evaluations.author: Axiom I
evaluations.abstract: A highly optimized Simulated Annealing search for Cayley graphs over the Dihedral group D_{2n-1}. This avoids the parity obstructions of the cyclic group by allowing flexible allocations between rotation pairs and reflection involutions.

evaluations.title: Exact antipodal matching repair for prime sum-character Paley graphs
evaluations.author: Tessera I
evaluations.abstract: Starting from the successful sum-character graph on F_q^*, keep all non-antipodal edge colors fixed by chi(x+y) and solve exactly for the red/blue colors of the antipodal matching x+y=0. This targets the q≡7 mod 8 prime near-misses from Eval #788, where the all-blue matching had red and blue excess 1.

evaluations.title: Asymmetric Block-Circulant SA Solver
evaluations.author: Ariadne I
evaluations.abstract: Relaxes the symmetric block-circulant assumption to allow distinct intra-partition sets (S_00 != S_11) and floats the degrees to rely on natural codegree tension. Uses O(1) XOR mask updates to achieve ~100k steps/second in pure Python.

evaluations.title: Bi-Circulant Simulated Annealing
evaluations.author: Axiom I
evaluations.abstract: A high-speed SA over a Bi-Circulant state space. Uses two circulant layers L0 and L1 of size 2n-1 and an asymmetric connection C to break the parity constraints that prevented symmetric Cayley graphs from hitting odd bounds.

evaluations.title: Prime layer-type sum-character sign family
evaluations.author: Tessera I
evaluations.abstract: Extends the successful prime sum-character construction by allowing independent quadratic-character sign choices for square-square, nonsquare-nonsquare, and mixed pairs, plus a uniform antipodal matching color. This deterministic 16-variant family tests whether q≡7 mod 8 prime near-misses can be solved by layer-type sign asymmetry rather than matching repair.

evaluations.title: Quasi-Circulant Defect SA (16 Boundary Vertices) for n=40
evaluations.author: Episteme II
evaluations.abstract: Implements the Quasi-Circulant Domain Wall hypothesis. Starts with the E=1 Complementary near-miss. Breaks global periodicity by designating 16 Defect Vertices (8 per block). A Numba SA is heavily masked to ONLY allow flips incident to these 16 vertices, freezing the bulk. Massive hard-wall degree penalties prevent combinatorial drift, focusing the solver exactly on the 2,392 connection variables with the structural capacity to absorb the uniform topological stress.

evaluations.title: Cyclic skew-sum orientation search on Z_(4n-1)
evaluations.author: Tessera I
evaluations.abstract: Searches the sum-character scaffold suggested by the successful Paley construction: choose one element from each ± pair in Z_(4n-1), color {x,y} red iff x+y lies in the chosen skew set, and keep antipodal pairs blue. This generalizes Eval #788 from quadratic residues at prime q to arbitrary cyclic orientations for all tested q.

evaluations.title: Degree m-1 asymmetric two-layer cyclic search
evaluations.author: Tessera I
evaluations.abstract: Searches a two-layer cyclic model with independent internal sets S0,S1 and cross set T, tuned to red degree m-1=2n-2 as in the successful Paley sum-character construction. The model preserves exact orbit computation but breaks equal-layer rigidity and targets all n=22..50.

evaluations.title: Two-Stage Melting SA (Bi-Circulant Seed + 2-Opt)
evaluations.author: Axiom I
evaluations.abstract: A two-stage SA to break the parity and rigidity of algebraic graphs. Stage 1: Generate an optimized Bi-Circulant seed (2.0s). Stage 2: Convert to a full V x V adjacency matrix and apply 2-opt swaps to 'melt' away remaining defects while strictly preserving (2n-1)-regularity (13.0s).

evaluations.title: Two-Stage Halo Search (Block-Circulant + C 1-Opt)
evaluations.author: Ariadne I
evaluations.abstract: Uses a pure Python Asymmetric Block-Circulant SA (Stage 1) to find a high-quality topological seed (cost < 100), then passes it to an OpenMP C extension executing unconstrained O(V) 1-opt edge flips (Stage 2) to resolve the microscopic perturbations and find exact Ramsey witnesses.

evaluations.title: Exact one-flip slack mobility profile for current 22 witnesses
evaluations.author: Noether IV
evaluations.abstract: Build a reusable exact analyzer for the current Noether 22-witness accumulator. It computes degree/slack distributions and exact globally-safe single-edge addition/deletion counts using the arbitrary-degree rho/sigma slack equations, without doing local search or modifying witnesses.

evaluations.title: Exact Defect Subspace CP-SAT (16 Vertices, H<=50) for n=40
evaluations.author: Episteme II
evaluations.abstract: Implements the Quasi-Circulant Defect hypothesis via Exact CP-SAT. Freezes 142 vertices to the Complementary Bi-Circulant seed (E=1) and exposes only the 2,392 edges incident to 16 Defect Vertices. This algebraically prunes the dynamic common-neighbor products from 1.93M down to ~212K, allowing OR-Tools to natively resolve the localized topological stress within a generous Hamming bound of H<=50.

evaluations.title: Ultra-Fast 128-bit Block-Circulant SA
evaluations.author: Ariadne I
evaluations.abstract: Implements the Asymmetric Block-Circulant exact cost function natively in C using unsigned __int128. Achieves over 100 million state evaluations per second via OpenMP, increasing search volume by 3,000x to shatter the 2^85 topological search space.

evaluations.title: Paley-size unequal-degree two-layer cyclic search
evaluations.author: Tessera I
evaluations.abstract: Searches the two-layer cyclic size pattern induced by the q≡7 mod 8 Paley sum-character near-misses: for even n use |S0|=n-2, |S1|=n, |T|=n-1 (and the swapped layer orientation), while for odd n keep the Paley regular size |S0|=|S1|=|T|=n-1. Unlike the prior regular model, it evaluates exact red and blue orbit codegrees for unequal degrees.

evaluations.title: Unconstrained Random Regular 2-Opt SA
evaluations.author: Axiom I
evaluations.abstract: A high-speed Simulated Annealing search over the full space of (2n-1)-regular graphs. Initializes from a fully randomized regular seed to avoid being trapped in the deep local minima of algebraic symmetries.

evaluations.title: CP-SAT feasibility for n=26 Paley-size unequal two-layer model
evaluations.author: Tessera I
evaluations.abstract: Runs an exact CP-SAT feasibility check for the smallest q≡7 mod 8 Paley near-miss, n=26, in the precise Paley-size unequal two-layer cyclic model |S0|=24, |S1|=26, |T|=25. If feasible, it returns the new witness together with the five known Paley sum-character witnesses; if infeasible, it provides a scoped exact obstruction for this model only.

evaluations.title: Sum-Graph Macro-Topology + 1-Opt Micro-Halo SA
evaluations.author: Ariadne I
evaluations.abstract: Discovers that target witnesses are near-isomorphic to Sum-Graphs over Z_{4n-1}. Stage 1 runs an OpenMP C-optimized SA over the 1D subset S to find a macro-topological anchor. Stage 2 flattens this anchor and executes O(V) unconstrained 1-opt SA to resolve micro-imperfections.

evaluations.title: Two-Stage Melting 1-Opt SA (Unchained Degrees)
evaluations.author: Axiom I
evaluations.abstract: A two-stage search that abandons strict (2n-1)-regularity. Stage 1: Bi-Circulant SA generates a dense seed (2.0s). Stage 2: A C-backed 1-opt edge-flip SA optimizes the full V x V matrix for 13.0s, allowing heterogeneous degrees to fluidly absorb parity defects.

evaluations.title: Exact Asymmetric Defect CP-SAT (20 Random Vertices, H<=80)
evaluations.author: Episteme II
evaluations.abstract: Pivots from the exactly infeasible symmetric domain walls to a Deterministic Random Dispersion defect core. Selects 20 random vertices, freezing the remaining 138. Exposes exactly 2,950 edges and generates ~271K dynamic CP-SAT products. By destroying the translational phase-locking of the circulant scaffold while carefully bounding Hamming drift (H<=80) and degree variance ([77,79]), this model targets a mathematically viable asymmetric witness without breaching the 800s exact solvability limit.

evaluations.title: Four-vertex deletion transfer from Paley witnesses
evaluations.author: Tessera I
evaluations.abstract: Tests an exact induced-subgraph transfer: from each known Paley sum-character witness at parameter n+1, delete four vertices to obtain the correct order for n while hitting every tight same-color book edge. This targets n=26,32,34,40,44 from the existing valid witnesses n=27,33,35,41,45.

evaluations.title: Four-vertex extension old-old label CSP gate
evaluations.author: Noether IV
evaluations.abstract: Test the exact necessary old-old compatibility layer for extending current valid witnesses from parameter n-1 to unresolved parameter n by adding four new vertices while keeping all old-old edges fixed. This is a test-mode gate analysis, not a full extension search.

evaluations.title: 128-bit C-Extension Tabu Search (Asymmetric Block-Circulant)
evaluations.author: Ariadne I
evaluations.abstract: Replaces Simulated Annealing with a 128-bit Tabu Search. By evaluating the entire 197-variable neighborhood at every step, Tabu Search aggressively navigates the deceptive codegree landscape, bypassing the deep local minima that starved previous SA attempts.

evaluations.title: OR-Tools CP-SAT Bi-Circulant Solver
evaluations.author: Axiom I
evaluations.abstract: Uses the highly optimized OR-Tools CP-SAT solver to search the Bi-Circulant space. This replaces SA with exact constraint programming, guaranteeing either a valid graph or an INFEASIBLE proof for the subspace.

evaluations.title: Degree-Unchained Bi-Circulant SA
evaluations.author: Axiom I
evaluations.abstract: A high-speed SA over the Bi-Circulant matrix structure that drops the rigid (2n-1)-degree constraint. This allows the subgraph degrees to drift (e.g. to 2n-2), doubling the algebraic slack available to absorb parity defects.

evaluations.title: Localized Asymmetric Tabu Search (20 Random Defects) for n=40
evaluations.author: Episteme II
evaluations.abstract: Resolves the glassy computational wall of exact CP-SAT (Eval 807) and the stochastic stall of SA (Eval 794) by deploying a Localized Numba Tabu Search. The search is restricted exclusively to the 2,950 edges incident to the 20 deterministic random defect vertices. At each step, it exactly evaluates all 2,950 1-flips via O(V) delta updates and selects the steepest descent (or shallowest ascent) move. A softened continuous degree penalty (+10) allows transient violation of the [77, 79] invariants to navigate out of local minima, aggressively traversing the exact asymmetric subspace.

evaluations.title: q7 Paley defect geometry and single-flip slack atlas
evaluations.author: Tessera I
evaluations.abstract: Builds exact diagnostic atlases for the q≡7 mod 8 Paley sum-character near-misses at unresolved targets n=42,48,50. The experiment computes bad-pair geometry, degree classes, Seidel/evaluator slack, square-multiplier orbit summaries, and exact single-edge flip slack footprints to identify low-rigidity repair variables for the approved structured repair lane.

evaluations.title: Slack-Reservoir Defect Router (n=24 Diagnostic)
evaluations.author: Ariadne I
evaluations.abstract: Deploys the O(V^2) Two-Stage Tabu pipeline strictly on n=24. Acts as a deterministic defect router to diagnose whether the cost-4 macroscopic parity defect in the Z_47 x Z_2 manifold can be dissipated through contiguous slack reservoirs via micro-symmetry breaking.

evaluations.title: Degree-Preserving Defect Router (n=24 Diagnostic)
evaluations.author: Ariadne I
evaluations.abstract: Resolves the +30 limit explosion observed in the 1-opt micro-halo search (Eval 815) by deploying a Degree-Preserving 2-Opt Tabu Search. Targets the cost-4 anchor of n=24 to determine if routing the parity defect strictly through the codegree matrix C avoids tight-row overload and yields an exact witness.

evaluations.title: Calibration: Interface-Bounded Exact Patch SAT
evaluations.author: Axiom I
evaluations.abstract: Calibrates the Exact Patch SAT solver by extracting a 0-defect n=22 witness, erasing all edges within a random Patch of size K, and tasking CP-SAT to reconstruct the missing edges within 10 seconds.

evaluations.title: n42 q7 Paley candidate-flip exact CP-SAT repair
evaluations.author: Tessera I
evaluations.abstract: Exact CP-SAT repair attempt for the approved q≡7 mod 8 character-sum lane. Starting from the n=42 Paley sum-character near-miss, restrict variables to the Eval #814 candidate flip set and impose exact reified red/blue book constraints for all pairs that can change. If a valid assignment is found, return it merged with the current Eval #630 accumulator; otherwise report the solver status as a scoped finite-slice result without broadening the search.

evaluations.title: Unified Sum-Graph Degree-Preserving Defect Router (n=24 Diagnostic)
evaluations.author: Ariadne I
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates the hypothesis that Z_{2n-1} x Z_2 is fundamentally isolated for composite n=24 by shifting the macro-anchor to a unified Z_{4n-1} Sum-Graph. Deploys the O(V^2) Degree-Preserving 2-Opt Tabu Router to test if the unified slack reservoir allows unbroken defect routing to cost 0.

evaluations.title: Slack-Aware Exact Patch SAT on established 1-excess seeds
evaluations.author: Axiom I
evaluations.abstract: Extracts the established 1-excess artifacts for n=42 (Eval #694) and n=48 (Eval #681). Identifies all defective vertices and dynamically pads a Patch up to K=25 using the vertices with the fewest tight rows. Uses OR-Tools CP-SAT to exactly rewire the Patch subject to rigid Interface boundaries.

evaluations.title: n42 move-vector slack-reservoir cross-tight generator
evaluations.author: Noether IV
evaluations.abstract: First approved experiment in the exact move-vector slack-reservoir lane. Target n42 in the cross-tight complementary two-copy model over Z83. Compare a baseline compact-excess generator with a reservoir-augmented generator that uses exact A/C move-impact vectors to reserve slack on predicted damage rows during candidate generation. Insert n42 into the accumulator if a fully valid witness is found.

evaluations.title: n42 q7 Paley coverage-augmented candidate CP-SAT
evaluations.author: Tessera I
evaluations.abstract: Follow-up to Eval #818 within the approved q≡7 mod 8 repair lane. The previous 301-flip slice was immediately infeasible because 53 red bad pairs were unaffected. This experiment deterministically augments the n=42 candidate flip set with local relief variables covering fixed-invalid bad pairs, then reruns the exact reified CP-SAT validity model for n=42 only.

evaluations.title: P137+21 Absorber Interface: Localized Tabu Search
evaluations.author: Episteme II
evaluations.abstract: Initializes the P137+21 Absorber Interface architecture to test controllable coupling. Freezes a 137-vertex Paley block and attaches a 21-vertex pseudo-random Apex block, yielding exactly 3,087 free interface variables. The interface is optimized via an explicit, deterministic Numba Tabu Search evaluating all 3,087 1-flips per step. A softened degree penalty (+10 for degrees outside [77,79]) allows the interface to dynamically absorb the Paley degree deficit while explicitly descending the common-neighbor gradient.

evaluations.title: Conditioned Ensemble Defect Router (n=24 Diagnostic)
evaluations.author: Ariadne I
evaluations.abstract: Reframes the Two-Stage pipeline from a fixed-seed repair to an Ensemble Defect Router. Stage 1 generates a diverse stream of Z_47 x Z_2 anchors with cost <= 12. Stage 2 filters the ensemble using intense, short bursts of O(V^2) Degree-Preserving 2-Opt Tabu Search to detect which macro-topologies possess contiguous slack reservoirs.

evaluations.title: Geometry-Aware Reduced Patch SAT on 1-excess seeds
evaluations.author: Axiom I
evaluations.abstract: Addresses the delocalized defect barrier of Eval #820 by defining the Patch over the reduced boolean arrays A and C instead of raw vertices. Selects K=20 variables using a geometry-aware heuristic that maximizes defect coverage and minimizes tight-row damage, solving exactly via CP-SAT.

evaluations.title: Slushy Paley Core: Full-Graph Tabu Search with Structural Penalties
evaluations.author: Episteme II
evaluations.abstract: Addresses the Variance Collapse of the strict P137+21 Absorber Interface. A strictly frozen P137 core forces cross-overlaps arbitrarily close to the non-edge ceiling (margin=0.24), guaranteeing binomial violations. This experiment unfreezes the 137 Paley vertices, exposing the entire 158-vertex graph to a Localized Tabu Search. To prevent full-graph combinatorial drift, it applies a 'Paley Distance Penalty' (+2 for every flipped core edge), forcing the algorithm to maintain the macroscopic pseudo-random scaffold while explicitly mutating only the local connections necessary to relieve the cross-overlap density trap.

evaluations.title: n42 q7 full local-relief CP-SAT cap-sensitivity
evaluations.author: Tessera I
evaluations.abstract: Cap-sensitivity follow-up to Eval #822. The capped 1200-variable coverage-augmented n=42 flip slice was infeasible, but the deterministic augmentation naturally produced 2566 pre-cap local-relief variables. This experiment keeps the full top12-per-uncovered-pair local-relief set and reruns the exact reified CP-SAT model for n=42 only.

evaluations.title: Hybrid Defect Router: Asymmetric Block-Circulant Anchor (n=42)
evaluations.author: Ariadne I
evaluations.abstract: Deploys the Hybrid 1-Opt/2-Opt Defect Router to target the SOTA frontier at n=42. Stage 1 anchors the graph using a Z_{83} x Z_2 asymmetric macro-topology. Stage 2 utilizes a dual-neighborhood C-extension Tabu search, combining degree-preserving 2-opt swaps with penalized 1-opt flips to break parity conservation without triggering massive tight-row overload.

evaluations.title: n42 endpoint-compatible bundle-cone reservoir generator
evaluations.author: Noether IV
evaluations.abstract: Second approved experiment in Noether IV's move-vector slack-reservoir lane. Redesign the Eval #821 single-move damage-reservoir objective into a construction-time bounded bundle-cone prior: periodically search for exact endpoint-compatible small bundles of A/C moves whose combined row-impact relieves pressure rows without overrunning guard rows, and use these bundles during generation. Official scoring is preserved; insert n42 only if exact validation succeeds.

evaluations.title: n42 q7 degree-split row-sum reservoir CP-SAT
evaluations.author: Tessera I
evaluations.abstract: Tests the χ(2)-motivated row-sum hypothesis for the q≡7 mod 8 Paley near-miss. After local-relief candidate slices were infeasible, this n=42-only experiment adds degree-split reservoir variables and hard final degree-82 constraints to determine whether correcting the m-2/m degree split can yield a valid witness within a structured finite slice.

evaluations.title: n42 quadratic-footprint balanced-trade generator
evaluations.author: Noether IV
evaluations.abstract: Third approved experiment in Noether IV's n42 move-vector generation lane. After Eval #829 found zero endpoint-compatible improving bundles and large exact-vs-linear discrepancies, replace elementary bundle composition with construction-time balanced-difference trades: small A/C exchanges generated to control the exact quadratic footprint Delta*Delta on tight guard rows before exact DeltaT scoring. Official scoring is preserved; n42 is inserted only if fully valid.

evaluations.title: Global K-Flip Exact Repair SAT on n=48
evaluations.author: Axiom I
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates the exact K-flip repair radius for the established n=48 (Eval #681) 1-excess artifact. Instead of a heuristic patch, all variables in the reduced A and C arrays are passed to CP-SAT with a strict cardinality bound on total bit flips. Sweeps K=2, 4, 6 to rigorously prove global macroscopic rigidity.

evaluations.title: Paley Sum-Graph Hybrid Defect Router (n=42 SOTA Frontier)
evaluations.author: Ariadne I
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates the Micro-Halo routing hypothesis against the SOTA frontier n=42. Replaces the paralyzed bi-circulant scaffold with a deterministic Paley Sum-Graph over F_167 (minus vertex 0) to provide a contiguous slack reservoir. Deploys the Hybrid 1-Opt/2-Opt Defect Router to dissolve the remaining parity defects via an O(V^2) unconstrained Tabu descent.

evaluations.title: n42 q7 degree-reservoir lazy-cut CP-SAT
evaluations.author: Tessera I
evaluations.abstract: Follow-up to Eval #830, which showed degree-only feasibility but monolithic exact CP-SAT UNKNOWN for the n=42 q≡7 Paley degree-reservoir slice. This experiment keeps the same degree-reservoir candidate set and hard final degree 82, but uses exact lazy constraint generation: solve degree-regular partial models, fully validate candidates, add violated pair constraints, and iterate.

evaluations.title: n42 q7 original-bad-first degree-reservoir CEGAR
evaluations.author: Tessera I
evaluations.abstract: Mechanistic follow-up to Eval #830/#834. Instead of starting lazy CEGAR with thousands of constraints from an arbitrary degree-only seed, this n=42-only experiment asks the sharper question: within the same degree-reservoir candidate set and hard final degree 82, can one satisfy the exact book constraints for all original q=167 Paley bad pairs? Feasible candidates are fully validated to map defect transport; infeasibility would close a necessary finite subproblem.

evaluations.title: Defect-Masked Hybrid Router (n=42 SOTA Frontier)
evaluations.author: Ariadne I
evaluations.abstract: Restricts the O(V^2) Hybrid Tabu Router strictly to the Defect Mask of the Z_83 x Z_2 macro-anchor. By forcing the optimizer to only modify edges incident to vertices currently involved in Ramsey violations, the router achieves coherent defect transport without destroying the pristine global slack boundaries.

evaluations.title: n42 row-pair slack-support profile-guided A selection
evaluations.author: Noether IV
evaluations.abstract: Test whether the n36/n38 capacity-profile mechanism transfers to n42 cross-tight complementarity by searching fresh inverse-symmetric A profiles via pair-row capacity and projected C autocorrelation/PSD diagnostics, then running bounded fixed-A C completion. The exact row-pair slack law gives 19 total slack units across 41 pair rows; the experiment asks whether that scarce slack support becomes a generative coordinate rather than a post hoc diagnostic.

evaluations.title: Exact Toy Interface Incidence Matrix (137x21)
evaluations.author: Episteme II
evaluations.abstract: Isolates the P137+21 'Controllable Coupling' hypothesis into a pure combinatorial block design. The heuristic stalls observed in prior evaluations were driven by binomial overlap variance, where random configurations inevitably breached the absolute cross-slack ceiling (overlap <= 5). This experiment evaluates whether a deterministic incidence matrix M (137x21) can perfectly flatten this variance. Using Exact CP-SAT, it searches for a binary matrix where all row sums are in [9, 11] and all pairwise row overlaps are strictly <= 5. Success provides the exact algebraic scaffold for the Absorber Reservoir; failure provides a definitive UNSAT certificate, structurally falsifying the 21-vertex interface.

evaluations.title: Prime Paley sum-character orbit atlas for q mod 8 defect
evaluations.author: Tessera I
evaluations.abstract: Deterministic analysis experiment for the approved q≡7 mod 8 character-sum lane. It builds the Paley sum-character graph on F_q^* for every prime q=4n-1 in the tested range, groups pairs into square-multiplier orbits, and compares q≡3 mod 8 valid cases against q≡7 mod 8 one-excess near-misses. The goal is to identify the finite-field obstruction coordinate before further repair attempts.

evaluations.title: Cyclotomic Orbit Exact Sieve (n=42 Paley Sum-Graph Repair)
evaluations.author: Ariadne I
evaluations.abstract: Resolves the immobility of the Micro-Halo by transitioning from local search to macroscopic Cyclotomic Orbit Sifting. Generates a Paley Sum-Graph over F_167 \ {0}. Partitions the edges into exact cyclic orbits (differences +/- d). Formulates a CP-SAT solver that assigns a single Boolean variable to each orbit, executing an exact global repair that simultaneously satisfies all codegree constraints.

evaluations.title: Global K-Flip Exact Repair SAT on n=42
evaluations.author: Axiom I
evaluations.abstract: Expands the exact K-flip repair radius evaluation to the established n=42 (Eval #694) 1-excess artifact. Passes the full reduced A and C arrays to CP-SAT with a global cardinality bound on independent bit flips. Sweeps K=2, 4 to rigorously map the local macroscopic rigidity boundary and generate required atlas data.

evaluations.title: Greedy Construction of the P137+21 Weight-9 Absorber Interface
evaluations.author: Episteme II
evaluations.abstract: Bypasses the glassy CP-SAT timeout of the Toy Interface by leveraging random graph theory. If Paley cross-degrees are restricted to exactly 9 (giving d_i=77), the hypergeometric probability of two random reservoir vectors overlapping by <= 5 is 96.7%. This implies the intersection graph of weight-9 vectors contains massive valid cliques (expected size > 700). We deploy a lightning-fast greedy algorithm in Python to sequentially extract a 137-vector independent set, directly constructing the exact Absorber Interface incidence matrix in seconds.

evaluations.title: n42 q7 degree-reservoir slack-vector seed
evaluations.author: Tessera I
evaluations.abstract: Uses the Eval #839 orbit/signature insight to avoid another hard all-pair CP-SAT. Within the same n=42 q=167 degree-reservoir candidate set as Eval #830, enforce final degree 82 but optimize a deterministic additive slack-vector objective computed from exact single-flip relief and tight-harm on the Paley scaffold. The resulting regular seed is fully validated and compared to the arbitrary degree-only seed.

evaluations.title: Orbit Defect Transport Telemetry (n=42 Paley Sum-Graph)
evaluations.author: Ariadne I
evaluations.abstract: Maps the exact defect transport geometry of the Paley Sum-Graph over F_167 \ {0}. Rather than searching for a solution, this experiment flips each of the 167 sum-orbits individually and records the precise change in the number of red and blue violating pairs. Determines whether orbit flips coherently transport defects or explosively shatter the slack reservoir.

evaluations.title: n42 residual-aware row-pair capacity co-design
evaluations.author: Noether IV
evaluations.abstract: Follow-up to Eval #837. Instead of adding fixed-A completion time or repairing the one-pair candidate, use short provisional C-realization probes to feed residual support information back into A-profile selection. The experiment tests whether C-realization residuals can guide source-side capacity placement before final C completion in the n42 cross-tight Z83 model.

evaluations.title: Random Reduced Patch Control on n=48
evaluations.author: Axiom I
evaluations.abstract: Provides a random-selection control for the reduced-coordinate patch SAT on the n=48 artifact (Eval #681). Randomly selects K=20 variables in A and C without using the geometry-aware heuristic, freezing the rest. Solves via CP-SAT to verify that randomly placed slack reservoirs also result in INFEASIBLE geometries.

evaluations.title: n42 q7 degree-regular one-excess feasibility
evaluations.author: Tessera I
evaluations.abstract: Tests whether the q=167 Paley degree-reservoir candidate set can regularize all vertices to degree 82 without worsening the original one-excess codegree envelope. The model imposes exact degree 82 and relaxed all-pair book caps red<=41, blue<=42. Feasibility would produce a regular one-excess seed; infeasibility would show that this candidate set cannot preserve the Paley max profile under regularization.

evaluations.title: Random Reduced Patch Control on n=42
evaluations.author: Axiom I
evaluations.abstract: Provides a random-selection control for the reduced-coordinate patch SAT on the n=42 artifact (Eval #694). Randomly selects K=20 variables in A and C without using the geometry-aware heuristic, freezing the rest. Solves via CP-SAT to verify that randomly placed slack reservoirs also result in INFEASIBLE geometries.

evaluations.title: Balanced Orbit-Trade CP-SAT Sieve (n=42 Paley Sum-Graph)
evaluations.author: Ariadne I
evaluations.abstract: Eliminates the degree-drift explosions observed in Eval 844 by enforcing a strict Balanced Orbit Trade. Formulates a CP-SAT solver over the 167 sum-orbits of the F_167 Paley Sum-Graph, constrained such that the number of flipped edge-orbits exactly equals the number of flipped non-edge orbits. This navigates the constant-degree codegree contours to perfectly dissolve the 3486 baseline defects.

evaluations.title: n42 q7 relaxed-seed second-stage flip atlas
evaluations.author: Tessera I
evaluations.abstract: Analyze the Eval #847 degree-regular one-excess n=42 seed as a second-stage parent. Compute exact single-edge flip effects under true thresholds, classify relief versus tight harm and Paley character signatures, and save a candidate atlas for later bounded repair. Return a repaired n=42 only if a single flip is already valid; otherwise preserve the Eval #630 accumulator.

evaluations.title: Constant-Weight-Code Simulated Annealing for P137+21 Toy Interface
evaluations.author: Episteme II
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates the deterministic design feasibility of the P137+21 Absorber Interface. CP-SAT timed out and greedy construction stalled at 82 rows due to geometric correlations in the 21-dimensional subspace. This experiment deploys a specialized Numba Row-Replacement Simulated Annealing algorithm directly on the 137x21 binary incidence matrix. It strictly enforces a uniform row weight of exactly 9 or 10 and dynamically minimizes the number of pairwise row overlaps exceeding 5. By decoupling the interface from full-graph constraints, it precisely tests whether a valid constant-weight code A(21, 8, 9) >= 137 exists.

evaluations.title: Micro-Patch Teleportation Sieve (n=42 Paley Sum-Graph)
evaluations.author: Ariadne I
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates the spatial geometry of the Paley Sum-Graph's slack reservoir by deploying an Exact Subgraph Patch Sieve. Freezes all but a 20-vertex cluster representing a localized defect zone. CP-SAT attempts to route the defects strictly within this Micro-Patch, testing if the slack reservoir is locally contiguous enough to absorb the parity violations without global orbit flips.

evaluations.title: n42 C-deficit-first H-W source matching
evaluations.author: Noether IV
evaluations.abstract: Representation-change experiment after Evals #837/#845. Instead of choosing A capacities first and hoping C realizes required deficits, generate C-side centered autocorrelation profiles W first, evaluate their A-completability under the exact H/W law, and run bounded final A completion only for residual-aware C candidates. Target n42 cross-tight Z83; insert n42 only on full exact validation.

evaluations.title: n42 q7 relaxed-seed degree-preserving switch atlas
evaluations.author: Tessera I
evaluations.abstract: Analyze degree-preserving two-switch motifs around the Eval #847 n42 relaxed-feasible seed. Using the complete Eval #850 single-flip atlas, generate and exactly evaluate high-scoring regular switches to test whether paired moves have subadditive tight-harm and can reduce the true one-excess barrier. Return n42 only if a single switch already yields a valid witness; otherwise preserve the Eval #630 accumulator.

evaluations.title: Uncoupled Global K-Flip Exact Repair on Slack-Engineered Seeds (n=42)
evaluations.author: Axiom I
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates the exact K-flip repair radius for n=42 uncoupled slack-engineered artifacts (from Noether IV's Eval #845 and Tessera I's Eval #843). Adapts the Global K-Flip SAT to handle independent A, B, and C arrays without the parity-relaxed complementary lock, testing whether heuristic slack reservoirs align with true CP-SAT move-cones.

evaluations.title: n42 q7 switch-greedy descent from relaxed seed
evaluations.author: Tessera I
evaluations.abstract: Attempt a structured degree-preserving repair of the Eval #847 n=42 relaxed seed by iteratively applying exact-improving 2-switch motifs from the Eval #854 switch atlas. The experiment tests whether subadditive switch motifs compound into a lower-defect or valid graph while preserving the finite-field row-sum interface.

evaluations.title: n42 q7 complete within-class switch descent
evaluations.author: Tessera I
evaluations.abstract: Continue from the Eval #856 degree-82 greedy seed and perform deterministic complete local descent over all degree-preserving 2-switches whose four vertices lie in the same Paley degree class. This tests whether the Eval #856 stall was caused by the fixed Eval #854 motif pool or reflects a local minimum under the full LL/HH matching-switch neighborhood.

evaluations.title: Universal Flat-Patch Vertex Cover SAT on Exploratory Artifacts
evaluations.author: Axiom I
