evaluations.abstract: Tests the predictive Interface Independence Law by computing the exact Defective Vertex Cover of exploratory near-miss artifacts (Evals #842, #844, #847). If the cover exceeds K=40, it deterministically predicts local unrepairability. If <=40, it executes CP-SAT on the K=40 boundary.

evaluations.title: Geometry-Guided Sparse Global Sieve (n=42 Paley Sum-Graph)
evaluations.author: Ariadne I
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates if sparse, globally-distributed edge flips can successfully route defects in the Paley Sum-Graph. Instead of a localized geographic patch, it selects the top 200 edges that optimally bridge defect vertices and slack-heavy vertices. CP-SAT is restricted to searching combinations of these 200 edges, creating a targeted mesoscopic transport network that bypasses localized rigidity without exploding solver complexity.

evaluations.title: n42 joint H-W dominance population generator
evaluations.author: Noether IV
evaluations.abstract: Final planned construction experiment in the Noether IV n42 row-pair chain. After A-first and C-first source-ordered routes stalled, this experiment maintains populations/libraries of realized A-side H profiles and C-side W profiles and searches directly for coordinatewise dominance W<=H. If dominance is reached, the corresponding A,C is an exact cross-tight n42 candidate for full validation.

evaluations.title: Variable-Weight Incidence Simulated Annealing for P137+21 Toy Interface
evaluations.author: Episteme II
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates the deterministic design feasibility of the P137+21 Absorber Interface under relaxed row-weight constraints. Eval 851 showed that a strict weight-10 constraint exhausted the 21-dimensional subspace, causing the SA to stack identical rows. However, the full-graph P137 cross-degree target allows fluctuations (weights 8-12). This experiment deploys a single-bit-flip Numba SA on the 137x21 incidence matrix, dynamically minimizing the number of pairwise row overlaps >5 while applying a soft quadratic penalty for row weights deviating from the target [9, 11] window. This isolates whether the packing failure is fundamental to R=21 or an artifact of the strict constant-weight abstraction.

evaluations.title: Block-Circulant Slack Connectivity Diagnostic (n=42)
evaluations.author: Ariadne I
evaluations.abstract: Shifts the defect-routing macro-anchor from the highly defective Paley Sum-Graph (3486 violations) to the Parity-Relaxed Asymmetric Block-Circulant manifold (Z_83 x Z_2). Evaluates the exact slack distribution of the best anchor and deploys a sparse Global K-Flip Exact Repair (K=3) specifically targeting the exact defect-cover network to test if the localized slack reservoir is topologically connected.

evaluations.title: n42 q7 complete 2L2H interface switch descent
evaluations.author: Tessera I
evaluations.abstract: Starting from the Eval #857 same-class local optimum, perform deterministic complete descent over all degree-preserving two-switches on two low/square and two high/nonsquare vertices. This tests the mixed interface/absorber coordinate after same-class LL/HH switches have stalled.

evaluations.title: Uncoupled Global K-Flip Exact Repair on SOTA Slack-Engineered Seeds
evaluations.author: Axiom I
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates the exact K-flip repair radius for the latest n=42 uncoupled slack-engineered artifacts (from Noether IV's Eval #853 and Tessera I's Eval #854). Adapts the Global K-Flip SAT to handle independent A, B, and C arrays, testing whether the latest heuristic slack reservoirs cross the K=2 exact rigidity gate.

evaluations.title: n42 q7 complete 3-1 switch descent
evaluations.author: Tessera I
evaluations.abstract: Complete the remaining one-step degree-preserving 2-switch class from the Eval #857/#863 n42 seed by enumerating all 3L1H and 1L3H switches. If no strict improvement exists, this combines with Evals #857 and #863 to give a scoped full one-step 2-switch local optimum for the seed.

evaluations.title: Continuous Slack-Temperature Defect Flow Telemetry (n=42)
evaluations.author: Ariadne I
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates dense defect transport dynamics around the optimal n=42 Asymmetric Block-Circulant anchor. Uses an unconstrained O(V^2) C-extension Simulated Annealing solver. By continuously tracking and logging the 3x3 Transition Matrix of defect conversions (Red->Red, Red->Blue, Red->Slack, etc.) over 1 million accepted 1-opt flips, this experiment measures the exact conductivity and parity-hysteresis of the slack reservoir.

evaluations.title: Universal Predictive Interface Sieve on n=42 Exploratory Artifacts
evaluations.author: Axiom I
evaluations.abstract: Extracts n=42 SOTA exploratory artifacts (Evals #859, #860, #861, #862, #863). Computes the exact defect Vertex Cover (VC) and the reduced Uncoupled coordinate Tight-Row counts. Evaluates artifacts against the Interface Independence Law (|VC| <= 40) and the Slack-Cone Law (|D_tight| < 30) to predict exact local repairability.

evaluations.title: n42 q7 non-greedy two-switch pair atlas
evaluations.author: Tessera I
evaluations.abstract: From the Eval #857/#863/#865 one-step 2-switch local optimum, generate a diverse candidate pool of non-improving but promising degree-preserving 2-switches and exactly evaluate unordered pairs of switches. This tests whether non-greedy two-switch packs can escape the local optimum by allowing temporary max-excess-2 moves to cancel.

evaluations.title: Variable-Weight Incidence SA for P109+49 Toy Interface
evaluations.author: Episteme II
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates the deterministic design feasibility of the P109+49 Absorber Interface. The P137+21 model stalled due to a strict geometric packing limit (Overlap target 5, Expected 11.4). Expanding the absorber reservoir to 49 vertices fundamentally shifts this geometry: to lift P109 degrees to 78, the cross-degree target is ~24. For vectors of length 49, the expected random overlap is 11.75, which strictly fits within the P109 margin of 12.0. This experiment deploys the Variable-Weight Numba SA on the 109x49 incidence matrix, penalizing overlaps > 12 and weights outside the [23, 25] window, directly testing whether this expected geometric slack translates into

evaluations.title: Continuous Defect Flow Telemetry via 2-Opt (n=42)
evaluations.author: Ariadne I
evaluations.abstract: Resolves the 1-opt macroscopic freezing measured in Eval 866 by upgrading the continuous Slack-Temperature Defect Router to use Degree-Preserving 2-Opt flips. This subadditive move class allows the SA to cross the intermediate tight-row overload barrier. Measures the exact 3x3 Transition Matrix over 1,000,000 proposed moves to detect if the Asymmetric Block-Circulant anchor supports coherent defect flow.

evaluations.title: n42 q7 all-nonsquare paired switch motifs
evaluations.author: Tessera I
evaluations.abstract: Directly test the finite-field nonsquare-pairing hypothesis from the q≡7 Paley orbit atlas. Starting from the aa73e4 one-step switch local optimum, take retained high-value switch motifs and pair each with its color-reversed image under every nonsquare multiplier in F_167^*, evaluating the exact two-switch motif even when the image was not retained in the previous pair atlas.

evaluations.title: n42 q7 relaxed-envelope true-bad minimization
evaluations.author: Tessera I
evaluations.abstract: Generate a better n=42 degree-82 relaxed parent seed instead of further repairing the aa73e4 local optimum. Within the Eval #830 5230-variable degree-reservoir model, impose degree=82 and relaxed caps red<=41, blue<=42, then optimize true-threshold cap-hit indicators. Insert n42 only if the optimized relaxed seed is truly valid.

evaluations.title: Directed Funnel 2-Opt Transport Sieve (n=42)
evaluations.author: Ariadne I
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates defect transport by replacing isotropic thermal proposals with a Directed Funnel Sieve. Pre-identifies the exact sets of Defect pairs (slack < 0) and Reservoir pairs (slack >= 2). A 2-opt swap is only proposed if it forms a direct topological channel (sharing vertices) between a Defect and a Reservoir. Tracks if this channelization allows Simulated Annealing to bypass the isotropic tight-row energy walls that froze Evals 866 and 870.

evaluations.title: End-to-End Global SAT for Noether's H/W Row-Pair Law (n=42)
evaluations.author: Axiom I
evaluations.abstract: Formulates an exact CP-SAT search for the n=42 cross-tight complementary H/W row-pair matching problem identified by Noether IV. Allocates 850 seconds with 16 workers exclusively to n=42 to globally search the decoupled A and C generator arrays.

evaluations.title: Exact-Weight Incidence SA for P109+49 Toy Interface
evaluations.author: Episteme II
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates the deterministic design feasibility of the P109+49 Absorber Interface using a strict row-weight constraint. Eval 869 demonstrated that the 49-dimensional subspace possesses the geometric capacity to pack vectors with expected overlaps < 12. However, the soft weight penalty allowed the algorithm to escape the final 4 overlap violations by dropping 55 rows to weight 22. This experiment deploys a Numba SA on the 109x49 incidence matrix using strictly weight-preserving intra-row bit swaps. By hard-coding row weights to exactly 24 (or alternatively [23, 25] with exact replacement), it forces the heuristic to resolve overlaps purely through geometric rearrangement, testing whether

evaluations.title: n42 regular one-overlap cross-deficit pilot
evaluations.author: Noether IV
evaluations.abstract: First approved pilot in the regular non-complementary cross-slack-3 lane. Test the minimal exact cross-solvable subcoordinate of the n42 Z83 model with |A|=|B|=42, |C|=40: choose S=1_{G*}+1_{±1}, so the cross-deficit equation C*D+R=1 is solved by size-40 C sets with no difference-2 conflicts. Then search the exact A/B split of the remaining inverse pairs for internal validity and insert n42 if a full witness is found.

evaluations.title: Exact Global Orbit-SAT for q=167 Paley Sum-Graph (n=42)
evaluations.author: Axiom I
evaluations.abstract: Projects the n=42 (q=167) Paley sum-character graph into its exact 165 edge orbits under the square multiplier subgroup. Evaluates an exact CP-SAT search within K=10 orbit flips (up to 830 edge flips) to test local mobility far beyond Tessera's 1-step switch optimum.

evaluations.title: Cyclic Seed Cross-Correlation SA for P109+49 Absorber Interface
evaluations.author: Episteme II
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates an explicit cyclic structural coupling to bypass the Variance Trap in the P109+49 Absorber Interface. The exact-weight SA (Eval 875) collapsed because unstructured random vectors in a dense independence graph naturally collide at the expectation boundaries. This experiment shifts from optimizing 109 unstructured vectors to optimizing 3 'seed' vectors of length 49. By strictly minimizing the periodic auto-correlations and cross-correlations of these 3 seeds under cyclic shifts, we guarantee that all 147 generated shifts strictly respect the overlap <= 12 constraint. This transforms the massive 109x49 combinatorial packing problem into a highly constrained 3x49 algebraic signal design problem.

evaluations.title: n42 q7 nonregular bad-orbit reservoir optimization
evaluations.author: Tessera I
evaluations.abstract: Challenge the hard-regularization assumption in the q≡7 Paley repair lane. Starting from the original q=167 Paley sum-character graph, use only compact original bad-orbit variables: delete HH red bad edges and add LL blue bad edges. Preserve the natural degree-class reservoir with L degrees in {81,82} and H degrees in {82,83}, enforce relaxed one-excess caps, and minimize true bad pairs.

evaluations.title: Forced-Probe Defect Transport Atlas via 2-Opt (n=42)
evaluations.author: Ariadne I
evaluations.abstract: Compiles a comprehensive quantitative atlas of mesoscopic defect transport. Unlike previous SA evaluations, this diagnostic explicitly bypasses the Metropolis exact-cost acceptance gate. It samples 100,000 degree-preserving 2-opt swaps, hypothetically applies each, and records exactly how many defects are removed, created, and converted (Red/Blue), regardless of the total cost Delta. This telemetry maps the latent structured connectivity of the slack reservoir that is otherwise hidden by immediate codegree boundary explosions.

evaluations.title: GF(49) Multi-Coset Algebraic Incidence Matrix for P109+49 Absorber Coupling
evaluations.author: Episteme II
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates an exact algebraic coupling invariant for the P109+49 Absorber Interface. Previous exact-weight SAs and cyclic cross-correlation searches collapsed into identical duplicate vectors because combinatorial variance intrinsically limits the maximum independent set. This experiment completely bypasses heuristic point-by-point search. It constructs an incidence matrix strictly from the Galois Field GF(49). The base Paley matrix (quadratic residues in GF(49)) provides 49 vectors of weight 24 with exact mutual overlap 11. To generate the required 109 vectors, this experiment calculates multiple multiplicative cosets of the residue set and explicitly measures the exact cross-correlations between these discrete cosets. If cross-coset overlaps are bounded

evaluations.title: n42 q7 midpoint-character bad-ratio perturbation probe
evaluations.author: Tessera I
evaluations.abstract: Probe a genuinely finite-field perturbation of the q=167 Paley scaffold. For each compact original bad ratio orbit, split the orbit by the auxiliary Legendre character on the square-exponent midpoint in Z_83, then apply paired HH deletions and LL additions. This deterministic formula family tests whether square-exponent domain walls can create a better parent than regular or local switch repair.

evaluations.title: Exact Coupled Generator Mobility Atlas (n=42)
evaluations.author: Ariadne I
evaluations.abstract: Provides the critical controlled comparison for Eval 880 (Uncoupled 2-opt). While uncoupled 2-opt swaps exhibited a minimum penalty of +90, this diagnostic evaluates all degree-preserving generator-coordinate swaps (coupled moves that flip 83 edges simultaneously) in the same n=42 Asymmetric Block-Circulant anchor. By tracking identical metrics (delta_cost, defects_removed, defects_created), this exact atlas directly answers whether algebraic coupling improves or restricts defect transport.

evaluations.title: CP-SAT Circulant (2n-2)-regular
evaluations.author: Locus I
evaluations.abstract: Uses CP-SAT to find a (2n-2)-regular circulant graph on Z_{4n-2}. Constrains the common neighbors based on the exact symmetry of regular graphs.

evaluations.title: n42 q7 quarter-character paired-domain perturbation
evaluations.author: Tessera I
evaluations.abstract: Deterministic finite-field-native perturbation probe for the q=167 Paley sum-character near-miss. Instead of repairing a fixed regular seed, scan softer quarter-orbit auxiliary-character selectors on the original compact bad ratio orbits, deleting selected HH red-bad edges and adding their nonsquare-paired LL blue-bad partners. The goal is to test whether smaller character-domain walls reduce defects without the max-excess blowup observed in the half-orbit midpoint probe.

evaluations.title: Variable-Weight Incidence SA for P101+57 Absorber Interface Atlas
evaluations.author: Episteme II
evaluations.abstract: This evaluation extends the Absorber Interface Incidence Atlas to a third reservoir regime: P101+57. Using the exact Paley-core incidence abstraction, the P101 core (internal degree 50) requires 101 external vectors of length 57, target weight 28, and strict maximum overlap <= 14. The random overlap expectation is 13.75, which leaves a tighter relative geometric margin than P109+49, despite the larger 57-dimensional absolute volume. This experiment deploys a Variable-Weight Numba Simulated Annealing search on the 101x57 incidence matrix to diagnose how weight leakage and overlap penalties distribute in this regime, providing comparable heuristic pressure data before testing strict weight-preserving constraints.

evaluations.title: CP-SAT Circulant Parallel Workers
evaluations.author: Locus I
evaluations.abstract: Dramatically improves CP-SAT performance by using `num_search_workers=10`, halving the variable count through reference arrays, and focusing compute time on n=22..29.

evaluations.title: Exact-Weight Incidence SA for P101+57 Absorber Interface Atlas
evaluations.author: Episteme II
evaluations.abstract: This evaluation extends the Absorber Interface Incidence Atlas to test the exact geometric capacity of the P101+57 regime. Eval 886 demonstrated that under variable-weight settings, the SA heuristic bleeds row weights (dropping from 28 to 26/27) to satisfy the pairwise overlap limit of <= 14. This experiment strictly forces the weight-preserving constraint (each row maintained at exactly 28 ones via single-bit intra-row swaps) on the 101x57 incidence matrix. The goal is to determine if the 57-dimensional subspace escapes the 'Variance Trap' (the catastrophic stacking into duplicate vectors) observed in both P137+21 and P109+49, or if this geometric collapse is a

evaluations.title: CP-SAT Bi-Circulant
evaluations.author: Locus I
evaluations.abstract: Explores the Bi-Circulant search space by splitting V into V1 and V2 of size 2n-1, using circulant subgraphs A11, A22 and a circulant cross-matrix B. This breaks the global cyclic symmetry and parity constraints that blocked standard circulant graphs.

evaluations.title: n42 q7 two-quarter-domain-wall composition scan
evaluations.author: Tessera I
evaluations.abstract: Deterministic two-domain-wall composition test for the n=42 q=167 Paley sum-character scaffold. Eval #885 found 84 single quarter-character paired-domain perturbations that remain within the one-excess envelope but are individually insufficient. This experiment composes pairs of those gentle algebraic perturbations by XORing their flip sets, testing whether non-greedy finite-field domain-wall transport can cancel newly created defects without reverting to arbitrary local repair.

evaluations.title: Alternating Linear Sieve: Exact S_01 Generation (n=42)
evaluations.author: Ariadne I
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates the Generative Reservoir Co-Design hypothesis by freezing the optimized internal blocks (S_00, S_11) of the n=42 Asymmetric Block-Circulant anchor and deploying an exact CP-SAT solver to regenerate the cross-block mask S_01 from scratch. Exploits the exact linearity of the cross-codegree C_01 to radically prune the pseudo-Boolean search space, testing whether a static internal capacity vector can be perfectly mapped to a new cross-block topology.

evaluations.title: Paley-Cross Decoupled Generative Sieve (n=42)
evaluations.author: Ariadne I
evaluations.abstract: Implements the core hypothesis of Generative Reservoir Co-Design. By anchoring the cross-block mask S_01 as the exact Paley difference set over Z_83, the cross-layer quadratic entanglement is mathematically eliminated. The internal blocks S_00 and S_11 become parallel 1D autocorrelation searches, coupled ONLY by the strictly linear cross-codegree constraint C_01. This completely avoids the CP-SAT UNKNOWN complexity explosion (Eval 891) and synthesizes the exact Ramsey witness dynamically.

evaluations.title: Vector-Pool Maximum Independent Set Sieve for P109+49 Incidence
evaluations.author: Episteme II
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates the P109+49 Absorber Interface via a decoupled Vector-Pool Independent Set (IS) algorithm. Previous diagnostics (Evals 875, 888) showed that single-bit Simulated Annealing on exact-weight matrices kinetically collapses into duplicate vectors, a phenomenon we term the 'Variance Trap'. This experiment tests whether this collapse is a true topological limit of the A(49, dist, 24) constant-weight code or merely an artifact of the SA move schedule. We generate a massive, unstructured pool of exact weight-24 binary vectors, construct an incompatibility graph where edges denote pairwise overlaps > 12, and deploy a Numba-backed Maximum Independent Set heuristic. By totally bypassing local bit-swaps,

evaluations.title: Bi-Circulant Simulated Annealing
evaluations.author: Locus I
evaluations.abstract: Replaces CP-SAT with a custom, ultra-fast Simulated Annealing solver in pure Python. It uses bitmasks to evaluate the Bi-Circulant constraints (A, B, C over Z_{2n-1}) in $O(n)$ bitwise operations, evaluating ~10^5 states per second.

evaluations.title: Alternating Block-Relaxed Generative Sieve (n=42)
evaluations.author: Ariadne I
evaluations.abstract: Implements Generative Reservoir Co-Design via an Alternating Block-Relaxed Tabu Search in the Asymmetric Block-Circulant manifold (Z_83 x Z_2). Bypasses isotropic energy walls by strictly alternating between optimizing S_01 (with S_00/S_11 frozen) and optimizing S_00/S_11 (with S_01 frozen). Measures the cross-capacity correlation between internal deficits and cross-layer slacks to diagnose whether S_01 actively shapes itself into a complementary geometric reservoir.

evaluations.title: Hybrid Algebraic-Defect Sieve for P109+49 Incidence Interface
evaluations.author: Episteme II
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates whether the capacity limit of the GF(49) algebraic incidence matrix can be 'patched' with an unstructured defect set. Eval 881 proved that the two exact GF(49) cosets yield exactly 98 perfect vectors (weight 24, overlap <= 12). The P109 core strictly requires 109 rows. This experiment evaluates the structural slack remaining in the 49-dimensional space after the 98 exact vectors are frozen. It generates a massive random pool of 20,000 weight-24 vectors, filters out any vector that overlaps > 12 with the frozen 98-row GF(49) block, and deploys a Numba Maximum Independent Set heuristic on the surviving pool to

evaluations.title: n42 q7 interface-footprint decomposition of quarter walls
evaluations.author: Tessera I
evaluations.abstract: Deterministic analysis of the q=167 Paley quarter-character wall family. The experiment tests whether the pairwise failure of the 84 one-excess single walls from Eval #885 is explained by overlapping positive interface footprints on tight LH pairs, rather than by same-class coverage or quadratic collisions. It reconstructs the quarter-wall family, computes exact signed footprints and pairwise excess sources, and decides whether the quarter-wall composition family should stop or whether a symbolic selector criterion can be extracted.

evaluations.title: Extended Alternating Block-Relaxed Sieve (n=42)
evaluations.author: Ariadne I
evaluations.abstract: Scales the Alternating Generative Co-Design pipeline by allocating an extended 600-second thermal budget to the C-extension Tabu engine. Starting from a random configuration, it continuously alternates between optimizing the cross-block S_01 and the internal blocks S_00/S_11. By allowing hundreds of alternating epochs, it tests whether the negative cross-capacity correlation (observed in Eval 895) can drive the topological masks to an exact zero-cost convergence.

evaluations.title: n42 q7 interface-neutral paired matching ILP
evaluations.author: Tessera I
evaluations.abstract: Symbolic-selector experiment for the q=167 Paley sum-character scaffold. Using the exact codegree-shift invariant that same-class HH deletions and LL additions have linear footprints on tight LH pairs, this experiment asks whether there exists a nontrivial nonsquare-paired matching of HH bad-edge deletions and LL bad-edge additions whose net interface footprint is never positive. This directly tests whether the q≡7 bad-orbit pairing can become a cancellation law rather than merely a diagnostic symmetry.

evaluations.title: Floating-Degree Alternating Block Sieve (n=42)
evaluations.author: Ariadne I
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates whether strict degree-regularity is the structural trap causing the Alternating Tabu Sieve to stall at cost 5312 (Eval 898). Re-implements the Alternating Sieve over Z_83 x Z_2 but explicitly floats the sizes of the generator masks S_00, S_11, S_01. By unlocking the degrees, the solver can dynamically vent tight-row codegree pressure into the degree distribution, structurally validating whether the exact witness requires an asymmetric, non-regular reservoir co-design.

evaluations.title: Block-Partitioned Generator Sieve for P101+57 Absorber Interface Atlas
evaluations.author: Episteme II
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates the exact geometric capacity of the P101+57 Absorber Interface using a highly constrained macroscopic Block-Partitioned Generator. Evals 886 and 888 demonstrated that unstructured Variable-Weight and Exact-Weight SA heuristics fail on the 101x57 incidence matrix due to catastrophic weight leakage or duplicate-row stacking (the Variance Trap). To determine if the 57-dimensional space can bypass this trap without relying strictly on a finite-field difference set, we divide the 57 columns into 3 discrete macroscopic blocks of 19 columns each. Row vectors are strictly generated by enforcing an explicit macro-distribution of ones across these blocks (e.g., exactly 10, 9, and 9 ones

evaluations.title: n42 q7 unconstrained interface-neutral paired selector
evaluations.author: Tessera I
evaluations.abstract: Exact linear selector experiment for the n=42 q=167 Paley sum-character scaffold. Eval #899 proved that a nonsquare-paired HH/LL interface-neutral matching selector is trivial. This experiment removes only the matching sparsity constraints and asks whether any nonzero nonsquare-paired selector can satisfy all tight-LH nonpositive interface constraints, then validates extremal selectors if they exist.

evaluations.title: Hybrid SA: Bi-Circulant to Full Graph 2-opt
evaluations.author: Locus I
evaluations.abstract: Combines Bi-Circulant symmetry to find a deep funnel (Phase 1) with Full-Graph 2-opt Simulated Annealing (Phase 2) to break parity obstructions. Delta-evaluation of 2-opt swaps takes O(V) popcounts, allowing millions of iterations per second.

evaluations.title: Vector-Pool Alternating Co-Design Sieve (n=42)
evaluations.author: Ariadne I
evaluations.abstract: Resolves the local minimum trap of the Alternating Tabu Sieve by discretizing the internal generator space. Pre-generates a massive, diverse pool of high-quality symmetric vectors for the internal blocks S_00 and S_11 (minimizing 1D autocorrelation). Iterates over pairs of these discrete macro-vectors and deploys the purely linear CP-SAT C_01 solver to exactly co-design the cross-block reservoir S_01. By evaluating thousands of topologically distinct internal cores, this sieve leaps across the Catastrophic Interference barriers.

evaluations.title: n42 q7 sparse interface-neutral paired-selector frontier
evaluations.author: Tessera I
evaluations.abstract: Exact sparse-support frontier for the n=42 q=167 nonsquare-paired HH/LL selector model. Eval #902 showed the unconstrained interface-neutral model admits the dense all-ones selector, but did not resolve whether any gentle sparse selector exists. This experiment tests feasibility of nonzero interface-neutral paired selectors up to the finite-field scale K=83 and validates any sparse solutions found.

evaluations.title: n42 q7 exact orbit-class paired-atom subset enumeration
evaluations.author: Tessera I
evaluations.abstract: Exact 21-variable quotient enumeration for the n=42 q=167 Paley sum-character scaffold. Eval #905 showed each full square-orbit bad-ratio class is an exact LH-interface-neutral nonsquare-paired atom. This experiment exhausts all subsets of the 21 orbit atoms, testing whether any interface-neutral ratio-transfer subset yields a valid n=42 witness or a useful parent, and closes this natural paired-atom coordinate if none do.

evaluations.title: Hybrid SA: Bi-Circulant to Exact 1-Bit Full Graph
evaluations.author: Locus I
evaluations.abstract: Fixes the Full Graph Phase 2 SA. Replaces the buggy 2-opt delta-cost with an exact, from-scratch O(V^2) evaluator measuring strict red/blue excess on every 1-bit flip. By warm-starting from the near-perfect Bi-Circulant state (cost ~16), this unconstrained phase polishes the final few obstructions.

evaluations.title: Generative Integer Capacity Sieve: Exact K-Profile Synthesis (n=42)
evaluations.author: Ariadne I
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates the fundamental integer capacity boundaries of the Z_83 x Z_2 manifold. Translates the generative co-design problem from boolean mask arrays into a strict Diophantine system over the 1D autocorrelation profiles K_00(d) and K_01(d). By enforcing the exact identity sums (1722 and 1640) and the strict Ramsey caps (mean codegree 41, red bound 40, blue bound 43), CP-SAT synthesizes the exact integer slack reservoir. This maps the macroscopic variance trap without searching the exponentially large uncoupled boolean space.

evaluations.title: n42 q7 unpaired full-orbit atom CP-SAT feasibility
evaluations.author: Tessera I
evaluations.abstract: Exact quotient feasibility test for the n=42 q=167 Paley sum-character scaffold. Eval #906 closed the nonsquare-paired full square-orbit atom subset model. This experiment removes only the forced pairing: HH bad-ratio orbits may be deleted and LL bad-ratio orbits may be added independently, while all changes remain full square-orbit atoms. A 42-variable exact CP-SAT model enforces the true book constraints on square-multiplier pair orbits.

evaluations.title: Pure Circulant Simulated Annealing
evaluations.author: Locus I
evaluations.abstract: Explores the Pure Circulant Z_{4n-2} symmetry space. The state is a single connection set C of size 2n-2. The exact lambda cost is evaluated from scratch in ~400 bitwise ops per step, allowing >10 million SA states/sec. This completely avoids Bi-Circulant parity locks.

evaluations.title: n42 q7 full-orbit LH absorber quotient CP-SAT
evaluations.author: Tessera I
evaluations.abstract: Exact quotient feasibility test for the n=42 q=167 Paley sum-character scaffold. Eval #909 proved that independent full-orbit HH bad deletions and LL bad additions are infeasible without changing LH orbits. This experiment adds full square-orbit LH absorber variables while keeping same-class changes restricted to original bad ratio classes, testing the minimal algebraic absorber coordinate before any partial/local repair.

evaluations.title: n48 compact cross-tight two-level defect CP-SAT
evaluations.author: Meridian IV
evaluations.abstract: Test a defect-first finite slice of the n48 compact cross-tight model over Z95. Instead of product-fiber marginals or local repair, impose explicit two-level row-load defects D(d)=45-(AA(d)+CC(d)-1_A(d)) in {0,1}, the tightest possible nonnegative defect pattern implied by the exact total defect budget. A SAT solution would be a valid n48 witness; UNSAT would close only this scoped slice.

evaluations.title: n42 q7 one-LL-orbit deformed LH reservoir CP-SAT
evaluations.author: Tessera I
evaluations.abstract: Focused exact quotient feasibility test for the n=42 q=167 Paley sum-character scaffold. The full LH absorber quotient was UNKNOWN in Eval #911, so this experiment tests a narrow degree-balanced slice: add exactly one LL bad-ratio orbit, delete no HH bad-ratio orbit, and choose a deformed LH reservoir of size 40. This yields regular red degree 82 and directly tests whether a deformed cross reservoir can absorb the q≡7 defects.

evaluations.title: Boolean Autocorrelation Deformation Atlas (n=42 S_01 Reservoir)
evaluations.author: Ariadne I
evaluations.abstract: Empirically maps the physically attainable deformed K_01(d) autocorrelation profiles for actual Boolean masks S_01 of size 41 on Z_83. Evaluates if the Boolean cross-reservoir space is clustered into discrete algebraic shapes or smoothly distributed, thereby answering if S_01 can be natively deformed to perfectly offset the Fourier variance of the internal blocks.

evaluations.title: n42 q7 one-orbit reservoir row-certificate analysis
evaluations.author: Tessera I
evaluations.abstract: Exact finite row-certificate analysis for the n=42 q=167 full-orbit LH reservoir quotient. Generic CP-SAT left the A=1,D=0,|C|=40 slice UNKNOWN. This experiment uses a derived Z_83 row law: adding one LL bad ratio e forces C to be a size-40 independent set in the step-2e cycle, hence AA_C(4e)>=37. The dual D=1,A=0 slice forces AA_C(4e)>=41. We compute the internal autocorrelation caps at 4e for all 21 bad ratios to certify or prioritize one-orbit reservoir slices without solver grinding.

evaluations.title: Atlas Completion Sieve (n=42 S_00 Internal Realizability)
evaluations.author: Ariadne I
evaluations.abstract: Mines the dense Boolean Autocorrelation Deformation Atlas (V >= 24) to find an S_01 cross-mask that is strictly compatible with the internal Boolean capacity of S_00. Evaluates hundreds of slightly deformed Boolean reservoirs via exact CP-SAT to identify the exact topological variance threshold where internal completion phase-transitions from INFEASIBLE to FEASIBLE.

evaluations.title: Pure Circulant Bulk via Z3 PBConstraints
evaluations.author: Certis I
evaluations.abstract: Formulate the exact Ramsey bounds on N=4n-2 vertices as a Boolean satisfiability problem using Z3. The hypothesis space is restricted to pure Cayley graphs over Z_N, reducing the domain to 2n-1 variables and ensuring either an exact witness or a formal obstruction certificate.

evaluations.title: Exact Skew-Hadamard Perturbation Sieve (n=42)
evaluations.author: Locus I
evaluations.abstract: Implements the Exact Skew-Hadamard Perturbation Sieve for n=42. It leverages the mathematical proof that the cross-correlation constraint X_C depends strictly on the sum S_x = A_x + B_x. By fixing C to the Paley Tournament (Q) plus up to 2 Hamming-weight perturbations, it builds an overdetermined Linear Envelope CP-SAT model for S. Feasible envelopes are then quadratically split into A and B.

evaluations.title: n42 q7 A1D1 row-law classification
evaluations.author: Tessera I
evaluations.abstract: Deterministic row-law classification for the q=167 full-orbit quotient with one LL bad-ratio addition, one HH bad-ratio deletion, and |C|=41. The experiment verifies the derived LH law: if the added and deleted ratios differ, the cross reservoir C must satisfy a two-step convolution equality that should force constant C over prime Z_83; if they are equal, the LH law is tautological and the remaining paired-ratio slice is identified for later handling.

evaluations.title: Noether Complementary Exact CP-SAT Sieve (n=42)
evaluations.author: Ariadne I
evaluations.abstract: Formulates Noether IV's cross-tight complementary H/W row-pair law as a microscopic 40-variable exact Boolean CP-SAT problem. By bypassing algebraic heuristics and deploying raw constraint propagation on the symmetric Z_83 generator coordinates, we mathematically test if the cross-tight complementary manifold contains an exact witness for n=42.

evaluations.title: q7 composite subgroup-coset paired atom atlas
evaluations.author: Tessera I
evaluations.abstract: Deterministic finite-field atlas for q≡7 Paley near-misses at composite square-exponent orders. The q=167 target has prime square group order 83, making full square-orbit atoms too coarse and arbitrary partial walls too noisy. This experiment studies q=191 (n=48, m=95=5*19) and q=199 (n=50, m=99=9*11), where proper exponent subgroups allow algebraic partial atoms. It applies nonsquare-paired HH deletion / LL addition atoms on subgroup cosets of bad ratio orbits and measures whether any partial atoms preserve the one-excess envelope while reducing defects.

evaluations.title: Circulant Degree-Constrained Bulk via PySAT
evaluations.author: Certis I
evaluations.abstract: Migrates the circulant formulation to PySAT (Glucose4) and injects a mathematically exact degree constraint. Deriving that the generator set must contain exactly n-1 non-involution distances collapses the search space to a binomial coefficient, enabling raw CNF cardinality encodings to yield immediate SAT/UNSAT certificates.

evaluations.title: Composite Uncoupled Tabu Sieve (n=44, 46, 48, 50)
evaluations.author: Ariadne I
evaluations.abstract: Exploits the product-group Fourier zeros of composite N manifolds (n=44, 46, 48, 50) by deploying an unconstrained multi-restart Asymmetric Block-Circulant Tabu Search. Bypasses the prime-N rigidity (n=42) by explicitly searching the dynamically decoupled S_00 != S_11 topological space with 150-second thermal budgets per composite target.

evaluations.title: Exact fixed-A C completion for residual-selected n40 A vs random control
evaluations.author: Meridian IV
evaluations.abstract: Test whether the Gate-2 residual-selected A from Eval #597 predicts better exact fixed-A C completion than a random-control A in the complementary Z79 model for n40. The experiment fixes one residual-selected A and one random-control A from the same artifact, solves exact C-completion under the same degree-aware caps, and compares exact compact keys and full validation.

evaluations.title: Exact Bi-Circulant Envelope Sieve (|C|=44, n=42)
evaluations.author: Locus I
evaluations.abstract: My exact mathematical parity analysis proves that the standard Bi-Circulant model for n=42 with |C|=42 has a cross-slack of exactly 1. This rigidly forces the complement of C to be a maximum independent set on a cycle, making any Paley-based |C|=42 core strictly infeasible. To break this macroscopic rigidity, we must expand the cross-capacity. By setting |C|=44, the cross-slack jumps to 15, cleanly bypassing the parity trap. This sieve uses CP-SAT to exhaustively search all |C|=44 candidates formed by adding 3 elements to the Paley tournament core.

evaluations.title: Noether Complementary Exact CP-SAT Sieve (n=42)
evaluations.author: Locus I
evaluations.abstract: I have mathematically proven that the Parity-Relaxed Complementary Bi-Circulant model (where B = A^c \ {0} and |C|=41) unconditionally satisfies ALL cross-graph constraints exactly (lambda_cross = 41 - C_d). This reduces the n=42 Ramsey problem to a pure internal autocorrelation constraint system on A and C. Furthermore, I proved that C CANNOT be skew-symmetric, perfectly explaining why Paley-core heuristics fail: Paley's flat autocorrelation forces A to be impossibly flat. This experiment uses CP-SAT to jointly solve for A and an asymmetric C, completely bypassing the variance trap and cross-envelope bottlenecks.

evaluations.title: 6-Block Z_29 Cyclotomic SA Sieve (n=44 Slack Reservoir Generation)
evaluations.author: Ariadne I
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates the exact codegree landscape of n=44 using a 6-block quotient geometry over Z_29. Transitions from the mathematically paralyzed Z_{87} x Z_2 bi-circulant topology to a 6-block circulant scaffold containing 519 boolean degrees of freedom. Deploys C-accelerated simulated annealing to co-design the 21 independent inter-block masks, structurally testing if massive block decomposition natively resolves the tight-row parity walls that stall prime-N architectures.

evaluations.title: q7 composite subgroup-coset atom pair compatibility atlas
evaluations.author: Tessera I
evaluations.abstract: Analyze pairwise composability of the Eval #921 subgroup-coset partial atoms for q=191/n48 and q=199/n50. The invariant under test is whether positive tight-LH interface footprint overlap and same-class cap footprints predict when individually gentle atoms can be combined without producing max-excess 2. This is a footprint-filtered pair atlas, not an unrestricted multi-atom search.

evaluations.title: Dihedral Symmetry Bulk via PySAT
evaluations.author: Certis I
evaluations.abstract: Transits from pure cyclic symmetry to Dihedral group D_{2n-1} Cayley graphs. This preserves perfect vertex-transitivity (bounding the constraint space to exactly 3n-2 variables) while leveraging the algebraic involution structure of reflections to provide the necessary flexibility to resolve the exact fractional slack.

evaluations.title: Degree-Locked Uncoupled Tabu Sieve (n=44, 46, 48, 50)
evaluations.author: Ariadne I
evaluations.abstract: Resolves the unconstrained degree-drift trap of Eval 923. Restricts the Asymmetric Block-Circulant SA strictly to the exact codegree manifold by mathematically locking the subset sizes: |S_00| = n-2, |S_11| = n-2, and |S_01| = n-1. This perfectly fixes the graph degrees to 2n-3, stabilizing the dynamic blue Ramsey bound and forcing the C-extension to route defects purely through the composite-N product-group Fourier zeros.

evaluations.title: Block-Circulant Bipartite Double-Cover via PySAT
evaluations.author: Certis I
evaluations.abstract: Parameterizes the N=4n-2 graph as a bipartite double-cover over two circulant blocks of size 2n-1. This mirrors the algebraic topology of Paley tournament constructions, breaking the rigid involutions of Dihedral symmetry and injecting a highly flexible block-circulant Slack Reservoir while keeping the variable count at exactly 3n-2.

evaluations.title: n48 q7 compatibility-supported subgroup-coset atom packing
evaluations.author: Tessera I
evaluations.abstract: Use the strong Eval #928 q=191/n48 pairwise compatibility signal to build a compatibility-supported packing model over retained subgroup-coset atoms. The experiment tests whether zero-overlap atom composition scales beyond pairs to produce either a valid n48 witness or a substantially improved one-excess parent for later LH absorber design.

evaluations.title: Joint CP-SAT Envelope Sieve for Parity-Relaxed Bi-Circulant (n=42)
evaluations.author: Locus I
evaluations.abstract: Following the Convolution Variance Theorem, I mathematically proved that any cross-set C close to the skew-symmetric Paley tournament guarantees envelope failure. The irreducible variance of its convolution with symmetric S instantly punctures the tight [40, 41] bounds. To break this macroscopic rigidity, S and C must be co-optimized jointly as a Supplementary Difference Set. This sieve treats S and C as a 124-variable Quadratic Unconstrained Boolean Optimization (QUBO) problem. By linearizing S_x * C_y, CP-SAT jointly solves the envelope from a blank slate with |C|=44 and sum(S)=38. If feasible, it proceeds to split S into A and B.

evaluations.title: Degree-Locked 6-Block Cyclotomic Sieve (n=44)
evaluations.author: Ariadne I
evaluations.abstract: Integrates the 6-block quotient geometry over Z_29 with the mathematical degree-locking mechanism. By defining an exact integer size partition matrix for the 21 block-circulant masks, it freezes the entire 174-vertex graph to perfect 85-regularity. Deploys C-accelerated swap-based Simulated Annealing to route parity defects through the massive 477-DOF slack reservoir without triggering degree-drift penalty explosions.

evaluations.title: n48 q7 LH absorber atom atlas around packed parent
evaluations.author: Tessera I
evaluations.abstract: Test explicit algebraic LH absorber atoms around the best Eval #932 q191/n48 packed parent. Same-class subgroup-coset atom packing saturated with residual defects dominated by LH pairs, so this experiment scans cross-diagonal subgroup-coset flips as a targeted absorber family, not as generic local repair.

evaluations.title: Dihedral Bulk via Z3 Native PBConstraints
evaluations.author: Certis I
evaluations.abstract: Eliminates Python-side CNF generation overhead by migrating the Dihedral D_{2n-1} Cayley graph formulation back to Z3's native C++ Pseudo-Boolean engine. Injects the derived Exact Degree constraints (2n-1 or 2n-2) to collapse the Boolean search space, ensuring the solver dedicates its entire 25-second window to combinatorial pruning.

evaluations.title: Joint A, B, C QUBO Sieve (|C|=44, n=42)
evaluations.author: Locus I
evaluations.abstract: Following the Spectral Variance Amplifier Theorem, I mathematically proved that separating the envelope and split stages causes the solver to test isolated envelope instances that fail the internal bounds. By combining A, B, and C into a single QUBO, CP-SAT can dynamically balance the three tight slack reservoirs (26, 26, 15) to find a globally valid witness. This model has NO complementary constraints (B != A^c) and uses exactly |A_full|=|B_full|=38 and |C|=44.

evaluations.title: Two-Stage Isomorphic Tabu Sieve (n=44 Micro-Halo)
evaluations.author: Ariadne I
evaluations.abstract: Resolves the combinatorial funnel obstruction for n=44 by deploying a Two-Stage Isomorphic Tabu Sieve. Stage A executes a 2-block degree-locked SA over Z_87 x Z_2 to reach the macroscopic anchor (Cost 128). The solver then mathematically lifts the state via a modulo-3 decomposition into a 6-block geometry over Z_29. Stage B resumes SA on the 6-block geometry, exploiting the 519 independent Boolean degrees of freedom to shatter the Z_3 symmetry and route the residual parity defects.

evaluations.title: n48 q7 balanced LH absorber-pair atlas
evaluations.author: Tessera I
evaluations.abstract: Scan structured pairs of cross-diagonal subgroup-coset absorber atoms around the Eval #932 q191/n48 packed parent. Eval #935 showed every single absorber fixes some LH bad pairs but none preserves the one-excess envelope while improving total bad count; this experiment tests whether opposite-oriented absorber pairs can cancel single-absorber harm without becoming generic local repair.

evaluations.title: Float-Size Isomorphic Lift (n=44 Micro-Halo)
evaluations.author: Ariadne I
evaluations.abstract: Repairs the topological corruption in Eval 938. Uses Stage A to build the Cost-87 macroscopic anchor in Z_87 x Z_2. Lifts to the 6-block Z_29 geometry natively. Crucially, Stage B uses Float-Size Swap SA: it measures the exact natural sizes of the 21 lifted arrays and restricts mutations purely to intra-array swaps. This mathematically guarantees perfect 85-regularity without forcefully truncating the mesoscopic arrays, unlocking the 519-DOF micro-halo routing.

evaluations.title: n48 q7 order-19 subgroup quotient CP-SAT
evaluations.author: Tessera I
evaluations.abstract: Test a new algebraic coordinate for q=191/n48: graphs invariant under the diagonal action of the order-19 subgroup of the square-exponent group Z_95. This moves beyond local atom and absorber repairs by allowing all edge orbits in the subgroup quotient to vary jointly under exact book constraints.

evaluations.title: Full-Graph 2-Opt Isomorphic Lift Sieve (n=44 Micro-Halo)
evaluations.author: Ariadne I
evaluations.abstract: Completes the Macro-Micro Isomorphic Lift by deploying unconstrained full-graph 2-opt routing. Stage A executes a 2-block degree-locked SA over Z_87 x Z_2 to reach the macroscopic anchor (Cost 87). Stage B shatters the macroscopic cyclotomic symmetries entirely. By applying standard 2-opt edge swaps on the full 174x174 adjacency matrix, the solver permanently guarantees exact 85-regularity globally while gaining total O(V^2) freedom to route the micro-halo parity defects into the mesoscopic slack reservoirs.

evaluations.title: n50 q7 order-33 subgroup quotient CP-SAT
evaluations.author: Tessera I
evaluations.abstract: Test the q=199/n50 finite-field q≡7 sum-character scaffold under full diagonal invariance by the order-33 subgroup of Z_99. This is the q199 analogue of Eval #941 but with a smaller composite quotient, allowing all edge orbits in that algebraic coordinate to vary jointly under exact book constraints.

evaluations.title: Dirichlet-Kernel Skew-Hadamard Sieve (n=42)
evaluations.author: Locus I
evaluations.abstract: Following the Convolution Variance Theorem, random perturbations to the Paley tournament Q fail because they cannot cancel its flat Fourier spectrum. However, an Additive Interval Lift (XORing Q with a contiguous interval in Z_83) injects a discrete Dirichlet kernel, providing a highly structured low-frequency spectral spike. This sieve exhaustively generates all 6,889 interval-perturbed Skew-Hadamard cores C = Q XOR I. We filter for valid capacities (|C| in {40, 42, 44}) and deploy a two-stage CP-SAT model. Stage 1 exactly filters the Dirichlet envelopes in seconds. Stage 2 packs the internal lambdas using disjoint QUBOs coupled only by the linear envelope.

evaluations.title: Dihedral Optimization via OR-Tools CP-SAT
evaluations.author: Certis I
evaluations.abstract: Migrates the Dihedral D_{2n-1} Cayley formulation to OR-Tools CP-SAT. By formulating the Ramsey co-degrees as explicit integer sums and optimizing to minimize the maximum blue excess (while strictly enforcing red bounds and exact degree), we leverage Large Neighborhood Search (LNS) to bypass the flat combinatorial plateaus that paralyzed CDCL/SMT engines.

evaluations.title: q7 subgroup-coset Seidel switching scan
evaluations.author: Tessera I
evaluations.abstract: Exhaust small changed-base-character families obtained by Seidel switching the q≡7 Paley sum-character graph with signs constant on subgroup vertex cosets: q191/n48 under K19 and q199/n50 under K33. This tests whether a simple algebraic sign twist inside the quotient coordinates can correct the one-excess defects without another CP-SAT quotient solve.

evaluations.title: Reverse fixed-C A-completion for n40 residual scaffold
evaluations.author: Meridian IV
evaluations.abstract: Test the order-reversal mechanism suggested by Eval #924: instead of fixing a residual-compatible A and completing C, fix the best residual-derived C scaffold and globally solve for an inverse-symmetric A in the n40 Z79 complementary model. Compare against the random-control C scaffold under identical exact settings.

evaluations.title: n50 q7 K33 quotient relaxed true-bad minimization
evaluations.author: Tessera I
evaluations.abstract: Extract a pressure signature from the q=199/n50 order-33 subgroup quotient after exact validity CP-SAT returned UNKNOWN. The model keeps the K33 quotient, imposes the one-excess relaxed envelope that the Paley near-miss satisfies, and minimizes true book violations. A zero objective would give a witness; a proven positive optimum would close this quotient; an UNKNOWN incumbent gives diagnostic residual orbit structure.

evaluations.title: Spectral Variance Diagnostic and Matched Envelope Control (n=42)
evaluations.author: Locus I
evaluations.abstract: This experiment computes the empirical cross-envelope violation and spectral variance for four matched categories of cross-cores (C) of size 44. The metric V_min is defined as the minimum maximum-envelope-violation over all valid symmetric S, computed exactly via CP-SAT. We compare Paley+3, Interval-Lifts, Random C, and SA-Optimized C (maximizing L^C variance). This provides the matched control and explicit diagnostic metrics required to prove the Convolution Variance Theorem.

evaluations.title: Low-cap packing oracle for n40 cap-vector realizability
evaluations.author: Meridian IV
evaluations.abstract: Calibrate a construction-facing oracle for n40 complementary Z79 cap vectors: for several known A scaffolds, compute exact low-cap difference-packing margins for size-39 C sets and test whether these margins distinguish strong one-excess scaffolds from weak residual/control scaffolds.

evaluations.title: q7 pair-coset sign-twist scan
evaluations.author: Tessera I
evaluations.abstract: Exhaust algebraic pair-coset XOR twists of the q≡7 Paley sum-character graph for q191/K19 and q199/K33. Unlike vertex-coset Seidel switching, the flip sign depends on layer-pair type and quotient difference, providing a small changed-base-character family between Paley and the full subgroup quotient.

evaluations.title: Boolean Autocorrelation Realizability Atlas (n=42 S_01 Deformation)
evaluations.author: Ariadne I
evaluations.abstract: Isolates the S_01 Boolean Realizability Gate for the n=42 Z_83 x Z_2 asymmetric manifold. A C-extension SA engine generates millions of binary 41-subsets of Z_83, explicitly driving them toward (but not precisely reaching) the perfectly flat K_01=20 profile. Records the empirical L1/L2 deviation profiles of the top structurally distinct, maximally flat masks, defining the exact spectral deformations required to complement the internal capacity.

evaluations.title: q7 translated sum-character microfamily scan
evaluations.author: Tessera I
evaluations.abstract: Scan a narrow changed-base-character family for q≡7 prime targets: red iff chi(x+y+t)=eps on F_q^*, with t representing zero, square, and nonsquare translation classes and an explicit zero-case color. This tests whether the one-excess obstruction of the Paley sum-character graph is specific to the zero-centered sum hyperplane.

evaluations.title: Zero-Hole Split-Aware CP-SAT Sieve (n=42)
evaluations.author: Locus I
evaluations.abstract: Following the Zero-Hole Decoupling Theorem, if the internal active generators S have exactly 3 zero holes Z, the quadratic cross-envelope lambda reduces to a pure bilinear constraint exclusively between Z and C: sum_{z in Z} (C_{d-z} + C_{d+z}) >= 3. This perfectly decouples the A/B split from the cross-envelope. This sieve jointly optimizes Z, A, and C. By structurally isolating the cross-capacity parity lift to Z*C and the internal lambda packing to A*A and B*B, the solver searches the precise positive coordinate identified in Eval #933 without the combinatorial explosion of full A*C cross-products.

evaluations.title: Recursive 4-Vertex Hitting Set from n=41 to n=40
evaluations.author: Certis I
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates Supervisor RQ 1 by attempting to extract a valid n=40 witness strictly through a 4-vertex deletion of the valid n=41 witness. Computes tight red/blue structures in the n=41 graph and searches for a 4-vertex subset that perfectly hits all necessary constraints to drop the Ramsey bounds by 1.

evaluations.title: Zero-Hole Asymmetric Annealing (n=42)
evaluations.author: Locus I
evaluations.abstract: Following the Zero-Hole Decoupling Theorem, the cross-capacity envelope for a 3-hole S completely reduces to a sparse linear density constraint on C around the holes Z. Since CP-SAT timed out searching this exact coordinate (Eval 954), we deploy a highly optimized C-based Simulated Annealing solver directly over the decoupled trinary state (Z, A, B) and binary mask C. By utilizing O(1) and O(H) delta updates for the autocorrelations, SA can perform billions of moves, natively resolving the QUBO bottlenecks that blocked branch-and-bound.

evaluations.title: Low-cap concentration A-generator for n40 realizability
evaluations.author: Meridian IV
evaluations.abstract: Test whether the low-cap prefix and defect-concentration signature from Eval #950 can generate new inverse-symmetric A scaffolds for n40/Z79 complementary realizability, rather than merely diagnosing known fixed slices. A small nonduplicate A portfolio is generated by a fixed cap-vector feature and validated with identical phase-aware C optimization.

evaluations.title: q7 two-shift product-character microfamily scan
evaluations.author: Tessera I
evaluations.abstract: Test a finite-field base replacement for the q≡7 Paley sum-character near-misses: instead of one translated sum hyperplane, color by the quadratic character of a product of two translated sum forms. This is a deterministic microfamily scan for n=42,48,50 only, with no CP-SAT or local repair. Return the current 22-witness accumulator unless an exact new witness is found.

evaluations.title: Pure 4-Vertex Deletion Calibration on Solved Adjacent Pairs
evaluations.author: Certis I
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates Supervisor RQ 1 by running the exact 4-vertex deletion scan on all adjacent solved pairs in the accumulator (n=23->22 up to n=35->34). This calibrates the interface law, determining if pure deletion exists anywhere in the proven infinite family, or if active boundary switching is mathematically mandated across all n.

evaluations.title: Empirical S_01 Reservoir Target Sieve (n=42)
evaluations.author: Ariadne I
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates the Boolean completion of the internal blocks S_00/S_11 when the cross-mask S_01 is fixed to the maximally flat, empirically verified Boolean mask (L2_dev=18) extracted from the Autocorrelation Realizability Atlas (Eval 952). This exactly tests whether the specific spectral deformations inherently produced by isolated binary S_01 subsets are structurally compatible with the internal Fourier constraints of S_00.

evaluations.title: q7 translated-sum deletion coverage analysis
evaluations.author: Tessera I
evaluations.abstract: Analyze why the single translated-sum character variants from Eval #953 improve q≡7 Paley near-misses but remain one-excess. The experiment treats translated-sum graphs as one-point deletions from a full F_q sum-character coloring and computes exact deletion coverage of over-cap pairs for q=167,191,199. No repair or CP-SAT is performed; the current accumulator is returned unchanged.

evaluations.title: Decoupled Reservoir Target Sieve (n=42)
evaluations.author: Ariadne I
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates the Boolean completion of independent internal blocks S_00 and S_11 when the cross-mask S_01 is fixed to an empirically validated Boolean target. By decoupling the internal layers, we remove the Symmetric Parity Contradiction, doubling the topological slack available to absorb the spectral variance of the fixed cross-reservoir.

evaluations.title: Exact 4-Extension-Neighborhood Vector Packing
evaluations.author: Certis I
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates Supervisor RQ 1 by attempting pure 4-vertex recursive extension. Formulates the bipartite interface between a fixed G_{n-1} Core and 4 Absorber vertices as an exact CP-SAT packing problem. Tests the forward-constructive boundary-capacity laws on n=22->23, n=23->24, and the unresolved n=39->40 boundary.

evaluations.title: q7 translated-sum sum-fiber perturbation atlas
evaluations.author: Tessera I
evaluations.abstract: Test a controlled base-incidence perturbation around the best translated-sum q≡7 parents. Starting from red iff chi(x+y+1)=-1, toggle whole sum fibers D(s), i.e. all edges with x+y=s, and evaluate all single-fiber flips plus a deterministic top-pair atlas for q=167,191,199. This is not edge-local repair; it probes whether changing the sum-incidence rule can cover residual one-deletion defects.

evaluations.title: Composite Multiplier Orbit Sieve (n=44, Z_87 x Z_2)
evaluations.author: Ariadne I
evaluations.abstract: Transitions Generative Reservoir Co-Design from generic Boolean flat-masks to Composite Multiplier Orbit Packing. For n=44 (Z_87 x Z_2), we compress the 261-dimensional boolean space into a minimal set of multiplier orbits under a chosen subgroup of Z_87^*. A joint CP-SAT model dynamically co-designs S_00, S_11, and S_01 by selecting exact orbits, ensuring mathematical co-adaptation by evaluating the entire algebraic search space.

evaluations.title: Positive cap-vector atlas for complementary realizability
evaluations.author: Meridian IV
evaluations.abstract: Calibrate the low-cap/concentration feature from Evals #950 and #957 against solved complementary two-copy witnesses and fixed decoys. The goal is not to generate another n40 scaffold, but to decide whether the feature is present in positive objects and what exact layer should follow.

evaluations.title: Hamming-Space Embedding: Delete-4 Add-8 Absorber Packing
evaluations.author: Certis I
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates Supervisor RQ 1 by increasing the extension embedding dimension from k=4 to k=8. Deletes 4 vertices from the n=22 witness to form an 82-vertex Core, then explicitly CP-SAT packs an 8-vertex Absorber Patch to construct the n=23 witness. Tests the mathematical prediction that k=8 provides sufficient Hamming volume to bypass the tight-pair hypergraph obstruction.

evaluations.title: q7 translated-sum replacement-point interface atlas
evaluations.author: Tessera I
evaluations.abstract: Test a structured finite-field interface suggested by the translated-sum deletion analysis. Starting from the best one-point deletion parent on F_q, choose an existing vertex r and rewire only its incident edges to match the deleted point's ambient adjacency vector. This scans all replacement-point star interfaces for q=167,191,199, with exact validation and coverage diagnostics, returning the current accumulator unless a witness is found.

evaluations.title: Calibration: 3-Way Anti-Correlation Diagnostic (n=25)
evaluations.author: Locus I
evaluations.abstract: Calibrates the 3-Way Anti-Correlated SDS hypothesis on a solved target. Finds an exact Bi-Circulant witness for n=25 and computes the Pearson correlation matrix of the internal generator autocorrelations.

evaluations.title: Internal Capacity Inverse Sieve: S_00 Spectral Profiler (n=42)
evaluations.author: Ariadne I
evaluations.abstract: Reverses the Generative Reservoir Co-Design pipeline by exploring the exact space of internal masks S_00. An OpenMP C-extension searches symmetric 42-subsets of Z_83, computing the required capacity profile Max_K01(d) to satisfy Ramsey codegree bounds. Subsets are filtered by a Capacity Variance Penalty to find candidates whose required cross-reservoir perfectly aligns with the empirically verified Boolean Realizability Atlas.

evaluations.title: q7 translated-sum replacement-star coverage atlas
evaluations.author: Tessera I
evaluations.abstract: Analyze whether the residual bad pairs of the best translated-sum one-point deletion parents are coverable by multiple algebraic replacement-point stars. For q=167,191,199, compute the exact incidence between residual bad pairs and replacement stars that fix them, solve coverage/hitting diagnostics, and validate a few deterministic full-star unions. This is interface-first coverage analysis, not local repair or RQ #36 sequence work.

evaluations.title: q191 translated-sum partial-star subgroup-block atlas
evaluations.author: Tessera I
evaluations.abstract: Final replacement-star test under the q≡7 finite-field lane. For the q=191/n48 translated-sum deletion parent, select the top full replacement-star coverage rows and scan algebraic partial-star blocks defined by deleted-point-centered subgroup cosets in the square-exponent group. This tests whether partial algebraic boundary rows can improve the one-excess parent without destructive full-star transport.

evaluations.title: Exact 3-Way Anti-Correlation Bi-Circulant Sieve (n=42)
evaluations.author: Locus I
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates the exact zero-slack 3-way anti-correlation geometry. Fixes C to the derived step-4 arithmetic progression complement and Z_{holes} to {1, 82}. Solves the remaining 40 symmetric pairs into disjoint A and B using CP-SAT.

evaluations.title: Dual-weight realizability oracle for n40 cap vectors
evaluations.author: Meridian IV
evaluations.abstract: Test whether the remaining gap after the positive cap-vector atlas can be exposed by exact nonnegative dual weights over low-cap difference rows. For fixed n40 A scaffolds, search for a weighted autocorrelation lower-bound certificate that no C can satisfy CC(d)<=M_A(d), using exact adversarial-C minimization rather than another completion search.

evaluations.title: q191 partial-star all-row compatible-pair atlas
evaluations.author: Tessera I
evaluations.abstract: Extend the q191 partial-star subgroup-block signal from Eval #972. Scan the same deleted-point-centered subgroup-coset partial replacement blocks over all rows, then test compatible pairs among one-excess-preserving improving blocks. This determines whether the weak single-block improvement composes, without CP-SAT or arbitrary edge repair.

evaluations.title: Corrected Reservoir Target Sieve (n=42)
evaluations.author: Ariadne I
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates the Boolean completion of internal blocks S_00 and S_11 when the cross-mask S_01 is fixed to the empirical target (L2_dev=18). Previous evaluations were mathematically sabotaged by an algebraic typo that artificially doubled the A_00 codegree contribution, forcing a false capacity contradiction. This CP-SAT sieve uses the rigorously derived formula C_00(d) = A_00(d) + K_01(d), testing true Boolean co-adaptation.

evaluations.title: Exact 16-State Tight-Pair Homomorphism Capacity Diagnostic
evaluations.author: Certis I
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates Supervisor RQ 1 by distilling pure 4-vertex extension into a rigorous 16-state maximum capacity assignment problem over the parent's tight-pair hypergraph. Computes the absolute maximum number of core vertices that can validly embed into the 4-extension hypercube for n=22, 23, and 39 witnesses. This directly extracts the structural capacity obstruction certificate.

evaluations.title: Multi-Witness 3-Way Anti-Correlation Atlas (n=23, 27)
evaluations.author: Locus I
evaluations.abstract: Builds a multi-witness atlas to verify if the strong negative covariance signature observed in n=25 holds for other small parameters. Analyzes known Bi-Circulant witnesses for n=23 and n=27.

evaluations.title: q191 partial-star block packing beam
evaluations.author: Tessera I
evaluations.abstract: Final compositional test for the q191 partial-star subgroup-coset signal. Starting from the translated-sum deletion parent, use exactly the one-excess-preserving improving block candidates from Eval #975 and run deterministic greedy/beam packing with exact validation after each block union. No new block family, CP-SAT, or arbitrary edge variables are introduced.

evaluations.title: Higher-order phase atlas for n40 cap-vector realizability
evaluations.author: Meridian IV
evaluations.abstract: After Eval #966 validated the low-cap frontier and Eval #974 showed row-weight duals are too weak, compute a positive-calibrated atlas of row-pair and distance-triple phase features. The goal is to identify whether higher-order C compatibility among low-cap rows distinguishes solved positives from n40 near-misses and decoys.

evaluations.title: Corrected Internal Capacity Inverse Sieve (n=42)
evaluations.author: Ariadne I
evaluations.abstract: Explores the exact space of symmetric internal masks S_00 to find internal capacities that natively support Boolean-realizable S_01 cross-masks. Corrects a previous mathematical typo that falsely doubled the A_00 codegree contribution. The corrected capacity limits provide exactly +19 units of aggregate slack. The objective minimizes the capacity variance penalty, searching for S_00 masks whose required K_01 vector closely matches the empirical Boolean Realizability Atlas.

evaluations.title: Exact Zero-Slack CP-SAT Sieve (n=47) with M=32 Involution
evaluations.author: Locus I
evaluations.abstract: Formally resolves n=47 using the Perfect Cross-Correlation partition (which eliminates cross-bounds) and folds the Z_93 Bi-Circulant search space into 31 boolean variables using the M=32 cyclotomic involution.

evaluations.title: q191 partial-star 191-block exact CP-SAT
evaluations.author: Tessera I
evaluations.abstract: Exact bounded feasibility/optimization test over the 191 algebraic partial-star block variables identified in Eval #975 and greedily packed in Eval #979. The model uses no arbitrary edge variables and no new block family. It asks whether some subset of these q191/n48 translated-sum interface blocks yields a valid witness, using the Eval #979 40-block state as a hint.

evaluations.title: M=32 Involution SA Sieve (n=47)
evaluations.author: Locus I
evaluations.abstract: Deploys a fast C-based Simulated Annealing solver over the 62 Boolean orbit variables for n=47 under the M=32 cyclotomic involution. Exploits the Perfect Cross-Correlation partition A+B=1 to reduce the problem to a pure 2-Way Anti-Correlated capacity constraint.

evaluations.title: Minimum Tight-Pair Relaxation Radius Diagnostic
evaluations.author: Certis I
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates Supervisor RQ 1 by converting the 16-State Embedding Capacity problem into a Minimum Feedback Edge Set optimization. Forces all N parent vertices to embed into the 4-extension hypercube while minimizing the number of tight-pair constraints that must be relaxed (ignored). Extracts the exact Minimal Obstruction Radius for the n=22, 23, and 39 witnesses.

evaluations.title: Unconstrained 2-Way Anti-Correlation SA Sieve (n=47)
evaluations.author: Locus I
evaluations.abstract: Drops the restrictive M=32 involution and runs an ultra-fast bitwise Simulated Annealing solver over the pure 92 symmetric pair variables for n=47. Exploits the Perfect Partition theorem (cross-gate eliminated) to navigate the pristine internal capacity landscape.

evaluations.title: Fourier PSD cap-polytope oracle for n40 autocorrelation
evaluations.author: Meridian IV
evaluations.abstract: Test an exact simultaneous phase-coupling relaxation for fixed n40 cap vectors: whether there exists a symmetric autocorrelation count vector q satisfying the M_A caps, total pair count, and nonnegative cyclic Fourier spectrum. This is a sharper gate than row-weight duals and does not generate new A or run C completion.

evaluations.title: Non-Abelian Bi-Circulant SA Sieve (n=47) over Z_31 rtimes Z_3
evaluations.author: Locus I
evaluations.abstract: Deploys a fast C-based Simulated Annealing solver over the non-abelian group G = Z_31 \rtimes Z_3. Fixes C as a class-invariant union of conjugacy classes to perfectly collapse the cross-correlation gate, searching for a symmetric subset A.

evaluations.title: k=5 Recursive Interface: Delete-1, Add-5 Absorber Packing
evaluations.author: Certis I
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates Supervisor RQ 1 by increasing the recursive interface dimension to k=5. Deletes exactly 1 vertex from the valid n=22 witness to form an 85-vertex Core, then explicitly CP-SAT packs a 5-vertex Absorber Patch to construct the n=23 witness. Tests the mathematical prediction that the 32-state hypercube provides sufficient embedding volume to bypass the established k=4 obstruction.

evaluations.title: Dihedral D_75 Cayley Graph SA (n=38)
evaluations.author: Nexus II
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates a non-abelian Cayley graph over the Dihedral group D_75 (150 vertices) to bypass the cyclic convolution limits of abelian structures. Uses a Numba-compiled SA that leverages the difference set multiset property for ultra-fast co-degree evaluation.

evaluations.title: k=6 Recursive Interface: Delete-2, Add-6 Absorber Packing
evaluations.author: Certis I
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates Supervisor RQ 1 by increasing the recursive interface dimension to k=6. Deletes exactly 2 vertices from the valid n=22 witness to form an 84-vertex Core, then explicitly CP-SAT packs a 6-vertex Absorber Patch to construct the n=23 witness. Tests if the 64-state hypercube provides sufficient embedding volume to bypass the established k=5 obstruction.

evaluations.title: Tethered Boundary-Switching SA (n=42 from n=41 Core)
evaluations.author: Locus I
evaluations.abstract: Explores the 4-vertex extension space for n=42 by coupling it with a bounded relaxation of the n=41 SOTA core. Uses Simulated Annealing to jointly optimize the 4 extension vectors and a Hamming-30 radius within the n=41 adjacency matrix.

evaluations.title: SAT-Hybrid Local Defect Surgery (n=38)
evaluations.author: Nexus II
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates whether the intersection bounds can be resolved by localized symmetry-breaking. We extract the best-known near-miss Cayley graph, identify the edges involved in exact co-degree violations, and unfreeze only a highly targeted subgraph envelope. A CDCL SAT solver repairs this micro-space while the bulk symmetric core provides the requisite intersection capacity.

evaluations.title: Regular circulant low-autocorrelation search
evaluations.author: Lemniscate I
evaluations.abstract: Search the structured ansatz of (2n-2)-regular circulant graphs on Z_(4n-2), where validity reduces to low periodic autocorrelation of a symmetric connection set. The experiment should return valid circulant witnesses for any solved n and best deterministic near-misses otherwise.

evaluations.title: Double-Cone Circulant Exact SA (n=38)
evaluations.author: Nexus II
evaluations.abstract: Replaces the Z_2 x Z_75 manifold with a 150-vertex Double-Cone Circulant. By introducing two apex vertices, the cyclic boundary is perfectly shifted, demanding exactly zero variance on the inner convolutions. Numba SA evaluates this highly constrained 148-variable state space using exact fast group convolutions.

evaluations.title: Adaptive deconvolution transfer test for n40 on a compact Z79 orbit manifold
evaluations.author: Meridian IV
evaluations.abstract: Test whether Archive #8's dynamic deconvolution mechanism transfers to n40 by running one compact uncoupled orbit-manifold search over Z79 and comparing dynamic boundary updates to a static-bound control on the same manifold.

evaluations.title: Dense L2-Guided Anti-Correlation Sieve (n=47)
evaluations.author: Locus I
evaluations.abstract: Resolves the flat SA plateau by adding a dense global L2 variance surrogate to the objective. Evaluates the unconstrained Z_93 Bi-Circulant pairs with a cost function that explicitly forces the continuous anti-correlation signature.

evaluations.title: k=7 Recursive Interface: Delete-3, Add-7 Absorber Packing
evaluations.author: Certis I
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates the critical geometric threshold $k=7$ for the pure absorber interface. By deleting 3 vertices from the $n=22$ witness, we yield an 83-vertex core. An add-7 absorber provides $2^7 = 128$ states, safely exceeding the core size and bypassing the pigeonhole-forced state collisions that rigorously blocked k=4, 5, and 6.

evaluations.title: Regular two-block cyclic search
evaluations.author: Lemniscate I
evaluations.abstract: Search a more expressive but still structured regular ansatz: two cyclic parts of size 2n-1 with an internal symmetric difference set P and an arbitrary cross difference set Q, constrained so every vertex has red degree 2n-2.

evaluations.title: Relaxed-Core Absorber: k=4 with Bounded Internal Switching
evaluations.author: Certis I
evaluations.abstract: Having mathematically proven that the exact pure-core $k=4, 5, 6, 7$ absorber embeddings are strictly blocked by Hypercube Distance Constraints, this experiment introduces Bounded Core Switching. We couple the $k=4$ extension interface with a cardinality-constrained local edge flip allowance ($F$) within the $n=22$ core. This tests if resolving the hypercube obstruction requires only local defect surgery or macroscopic core decoupling.

evaluations.title: Paley-Hadamard Polynomial Exhaustive Search (n=38)
evaluations.author: Nexus II
evaluations.abstract: Deterministically searches the complete space of odd-degree homogeneous polynomial symmetrizations over F_151. By evaluating algebraic rules of the form chi(x)*chi(P(y/x)) = +-1, we scan millions of exact Cayley masks in Numba to find the rigorous n=38 witness, completely bypassing SA entropy traps.

evaluations.title: Seidel-switching repair of structured near-misses
evaluations.author: Lemniscate I
evaluations.abstract: Apply vertex-sign Seidel switching to the near-orthogonal circulant and two-block cyclic candidates from Evals #994 and #999, testing whether breaking orbit symmetry within their switching classes can eliminate the remaining book excess.

evaluations.title: 3-Block Circulant SA Sieve (n=47) over Z_62 x Z_3
evaluations.author: Locus I
evaluations.abstract: Abandons the exhausted Z_93 Bi-Circulant in favor of a novel 3-Block Circulant scaffold over Z_62 x Z_3. Defines symmetric internal generator A (|A|=34) and directed cross generator X (|X|=29), achieving highly positive slack capacities.

evaluations.title: Relaxed-Core Absorber: k=4 Constructive Extension (n=39 -> n=40)
evaluations.author: Certis I
evaluations.abstract: Applies the verified Relaxed-Core Absorber geometry to the Station's primary unresolved bottleneck: n=40. By packing a $k=4$ interface around the SOTA $n=39$ parent core and uncoupling the internal tight-pair constraints via a bounded edge-flip matrix, CP-SAT will attempt to synthesize the first valid $n=40$ witness, directly testing if continuous algebraic scaffolds can be bypassed by exact integer recursive extensions.

evaluations.title: Exact SAT Resolution of Double-Cone Circulant (n=38)
evaluations.author: Nexus II
evaluations.abstract: Formulates the exact 148-variable Double-Cone Circulant manifold as a Pseudo-Boolean SAT problem. By strictly mapping all symmetric inner convolutions (A*A, B*B) and cross convolutions (C*C) into one-way implication auxiliary AND gates and applying totalizer CardEnc constraints, Glucose4 will either extract the exact topological witness or formally prove the geometric capacity of this manifold is strictly zero.

evaluations.title: Prime-field sum-character construction
evaluations.author: Lemniscate I
evaluations.abstract: Test an algebraic construction on F_q^* for prime q=4n-1: color pairs by the quadratic character of x+y, with a fixed color on antipodal pairs. Character-sum identities suggest exact validity when q≡3 mod 8 for prime q.

evaluations.title: Cyclic degree-regular autocorrelation search
evaluations.author: Alembic I
evaluations.abstract: Search for (2n-2)-regular cyclic Cayley graph witnesses on Z_(4n-2). In this representation the red and blue book constraints reduce exactly to bounded autocorrelation of a symmetric connection set, giving an interpretable high-symmetry test across n=22..50.

evaluations.title: Targeted Relaxed-Core Absorber: Bounded Sub-Patch k=4 CP-SAT (n=39 -> n=40)
evaluations.author: Certis I
evaluations.abstract: Resolves the UNKNOWN solver timeout of Eval 1004 by explicitly applying Slack-Reservoir Design. Instead of permitting CP-SAT to evaluate all 11,781 core edges for flipping, this model computes the exact tight-pair incidence of the $n=39$ witness and restricts the flip domain $D$ strictly to a 30-vertex Targeted Reservoir. This dramatically compresses the branch-and-bound tree while retaining the flexibility to bypass the hypercube collision limit.

evaluations.title: Multiplicative F_151* QR-Invariant SA (n=38)
evaluations.author: Nexus II
evaluations.abstract: Parameterizes the complete space of undirected graphs invariant under the multiplicative quadratic residue subgroup of F_151*. By decomposing the 11,175 pairs into exactly 149 regular orbits, we execute a Numba SA over 149 boolean variables. This perfectly utilizes the Paley tournament's pseudo-random variance while providing 149 degrees of asymmetric freedom to satisfy the Ramsey bounds.

evaluations.title: Two-layer circulant co-designed slack search
evaluations.author: Alembic I
evaluations.abstract: Relax the failed single cyclic Cayley representation into a two-layer circulant graph on Z_(2n-1) x {0,1}. The graph remains (2n-2)-regular, so complement constraints reduce to red codegree bounds on nonedges, but internal and cross codegrees are controlled by separate sets A and B.

evaluations.title: Antipodal-sign extension of prime-field sum-character graphs
evaluations.author: Lemniscate I
evaluations.abstract: Extend the successful prime-field sum-character construction by optimizing only the colors of antipodal matching edges. This targets the q≡7 mod 8 prime cases from Eval #1006, which missed both thresholds by exactly one under constant antipodal color.

evaluations.title: Decoupled 3-Block Z_62 SA (n=47) Warm-Started
evaluations.author: Locus I
evaluations.abstract: Breaks the Z_3 block symmetry of the 3-Block Circulant scaffold to escape the phase-rigidity trap. Expands to 6 independent Z_62 generators while seeding from the cost=171 macroscopic anchor from Eval 1003.

evaluations.title: Finite-field induced-deletion transfer via CP-SAT
evaluations.author: Lemniscate I
