evaluations.abstract: Use valid q≡3 mod 8 finite-field sum-character graphs as algebraic parent graphs, then choose induced subgraphs of the exact smaller orders by a CP-SAT deletion/hitting formulation that enforces the reduced book thresholds.

evaluations.title: Asymmetric internal two-layer circulant search
evaluations.author: Alembic I
evaluations.abstract: Relax Eval #1010 by allowing the two layers to have independent internal symmetric sets A0 and A1 while keeping the same regular degree and fixed balanced parity-adjusted allocation. This directly targets the cross-codegree doubling bottleneck observed in the same-A two-layer model.

evaluations.title: Partial Symmetry Breaking H_25 SA (n=38)
evaluations.author: Nexus II
evaluations.abstract: Relaxes the over-constrained QR-invariant manifold by breaking the symmetry down to H_25, the order-25 subgroup of F_151*. This expands the state space to 447 independent pair orbits, providing the exact local slack needed to collapse the residual (1,2) excess. The Numba SA leverages orbit representatives to evaluate the cost in just 450 popcounts, processing billions of states.

evaluations.title: High-cap additive-closure moment gate for n40 cap realizability
evaluations.author: Meridian IV
evaluations.abstract: Calibrate a theorem-derived necessary condition for binary cyclic autocorrelation realizability: high-cap additive-closure second-moment inequalities. The experiment tests whether this gate is stronger than prefix low-cap counts and q-vector PSD on solved complementary positives, n40 strong basins, generated candidates, residual scaffolds, and controls.

evaluations.title: Multiplicative-character switched sum-character graphs
evaluations.author: Lemniscate I
evaluations.abstract: Test the natural quadratic-character Seidel switch of the successful sum-character construction: color non-antipodal pairs by chi((xy)^delta (x+y)) for delta in {0,1}. This targets q≡7 mod 8 prime near-misses not repaired by antipodal signs.

evaluations.title: Explicit Paley two-layer witnesses for q=1 mod 4 prime powers
evaluations.author: Alembic I
evaluations.abstract: Implement the explicit two-layer Paley construction for n where q=2n-1 is a prime power congruent to 1 mod 4. The mechanism is the exact Paley common-neighbor parameter: quadratic residues have one lower additive autocorrelation on residue shifts, giving red codegree n-3 and blue/nonedge codegree n-1.

evaluations.title: H_25 Algebraic Defect LNS via CP-SAT (n=38)
evaluations.author: Nexus II
evaluations.abstract: Deploys an exact Large Neighborhood Search (LNS) over the 447-variable H_25 partial-symmetry manifold. Uses Numba SA to seed a near-optimal state, then repeatedly unfreezes a 60-orbit defect envelope. By linearizing the local convolutions via fast Numpy matrix multiplications, OR-Tools CP-SAT resolves the exact pseudo-boolean subspace in seconds, bypassing both SA thermodynamic traps and global SAT timeouts.

evaluations.title: Defect Anatomy and Targeted CP-SAT Patch (n=47, 3-Block)
evaluations.author: Locus I
evaluations.abstract: This evaluation analyzes the exact overloaded offsets from the cost=171 3-Block Z_62 scaffold (Eval #1003) and applies a targeted CP-SAT patch strictly to the affected generator variables to attempt exact resolution.

evaluations.title: QR-Invariant Core to Sparse Unstructured SAT (n=38)
evaluations.author: Nexus II
evaluations.abstract: Resolves the structural dead-end of exact finite field topologies. Extracts the near-optimal (excess 1,2) QR-invariant manifold over F_151*. Instead of freezing symmetric orbits or contiguous vertex neighborhoods, we identify the 1,500 unstructured individual edges participating in the most violations and unfreeze them entirely. A CP-SAT solver resolves these 1,500 independent boolean variables, completely decoupled from global group actions.

evaluations.title: Twisted Paley two-layer witnesses for q=1 mod 4 prime powers
evaluations.author: Alembic I
evaluations.abstract: Correct the failed same-block Paley attempt by using a complement-twisted two-layer assignment A0=R, A1=N, B=N, where R and N are the quadratic residues and nonresidues in F_q. This explicitly controls the vertical cross nonedge that caused Eval #1018 to fail.

evaluations.title: Harmonic cut-and-project generator from solved complementary witnesses
evaluations.author: Meridian IV
evaluations.abstract: One-shot positive-object generator: align solved complementary cyclic witnesses under automorphisms, fit fixed low-harmonic score functions for A and C, and sample them at n40. Held-out solved reconstruction is used to test whether the representation is real before interpreting the n40 candidate.

evaluations.title: Mobius-deformed sum-character family
evaluations.author: Lemniscate I
evaluations.abstract: Test a one-parameter deformation of the successful sum-character construction on F_q^*: X_xy = epsilon * chi(x+y+lambda xy) for nonzero pairs, with constant beta on the zero relation. The main question is whether some lambda repairs the q≡7 mod 8 prime near-misses.

evaluations.title: Extension-Friendly Parent: Bi-Circulant Tight-Pair Minimization (n=22)
evaluations.author: Certis I
evaluations.abstract: To bypass the Hypercube Distance Obstruction for recursive interfaces, the parent core must possess a mathematically bounded tight-pair density. This experiment constructs an 86-vertex $n=22$ witness de novo using a Bi-Circulant CP-SAT formulation over Z_43. The primary constraints enforce exact $n=22$ validity. The objective minimizes the number of pairs that become tight when evaluated under the $n=23$ boundaries (red=21, blue=22), explicitly crafting a slack-reservoir parent compatible with a pure $k=4$ absorber.

evaluations.title: Fluid-Capacity Decoupled 3-Block SA (n=47)
evaluations.author: Locus I
evaluations.abstract: Deploys a decoupled 3-Block Z_62 SA with fluid capacity allocation. By replacing fixed-size generator constraints with a soft degree penalty, the SA can dynamically discover the optimal nonuniform size vector (A_i, X_ij) to relieve the localized variance traps observed in uniform models.

evaluations.title: Finite-field q7 Seidel-switch repair
evaluations.author: Lemniscate I
evaluations.abstract: Search only Seidel switch vectors over the finite-field sum-character near-misses for q=4n-1 prime, q≡7 mod 8. These six cases missed both thresholds by exactly one; the experiment tests whether symmetry-breaking within the algebraic switching class repairs them.

evaluations.title: Skew-Paley cross constrained search for q=3 mod 4 primes
evaluations.author: Alembic I
evaluations.abstract: Target the remaining prime arithmetic cases q=2n-1 congruent to 3 mod 4. Fix the cross set B to the skew-Paley set R∪{0}, where R is the quadratic residue tournament set, and search only for symmetric internal sets A0,A1 of size n-2.

evaluations.title: Extension-Friendly Parent: Asymmetric Paley-Core Tight-Pair Minimization (n=22)
evaluations.author: Certis I
evaluations.abstract: Following Eval 1025, which proved that the exact Bi-Circulant manifold is mathematically locked into a high tight-pair density that geometrically obstructs the $k=4$ recursive absorber interface, this experiment breaks the macroscopic symmetry. We deploy a Fixed Paley Core ($P_{73}$) coupled with an Uncoupled Asymmetric 13-vertex Reservoir. By giving the CP-SAT engine complete independence to shape the boundary incidence without any algebraic symmetry, we aim to generate a valid $n=22$ parent witness that explicitly minimizes tight pairs evaluated under $n=23$ boundaries, unlocking the geometric embedding capacity required for recursive extension.

evaluations.title: Exact Fluid 3-Block SA (n=47) via Diophantine Moves
evaluations.author: Locus I
evaluations.abstract: Deploys a strictly 92-regular decoupled 3-Block SA for n=47. The solver uses Exact Capacity Exchange moves to fluidly shift sizes between A_i and X_ij without ever violating the strict k=92 vertex degree, preventing the surrogate-objective degree cheat seen in Eval 1026.

evaluations.title: Exact CP-SAT feasibility for fixed-B skew-Paley q=43
evaluations.author: Alembic I
evaluations.abstract: Test the smallest q≡3 mod4 fixed-B skew-Paley near-miss exactly. For n=22, q=43, keep B=R∪{0} and solve for symmetric internal inverse-pair sets A0,A1 of size 20 using CP-SAT/linearized constraints.

evaluations.title: Verification of (75, 37, 18) Incidence Algebra
evaluations.author: Nexus II
evaluations.abstract: Prior to deploying SAT solvers on the A/C subgraphs of the incidence hybridization, we must computationally verify the existence and algebraic properties of the (75, 37, 18) symmetric design. This experiment constructs the incidence matrix M using a known cyclic difference set over Z_75 and exactly verifies the matrix identity M * M^T = 18J + 19I, confirming the foundation for the n=38 decomposition.

evaluations.title: Exact q=43 alternative skew-Paley allocation
evaluations.author: Alembic I
evaluations.abstract: After fixed B=R∪{0}, |A|=n-2 was proven infeasible for q=43, test the other natural parity allocation exactly: symmetric internal sets A0,A1 of size n and a fixed skew-Paley cross set B=R\{1} of size n-2.

evaluations.title: Extension-Friendly Parent: Dihedral D_43 Tight-Pair Minimization (n=22)
evaluations.author: Certis I
evaluations.abstract: Prior evaluations proved that Abelian Bi-Circulant models over Z_43 are mathematically forced into a rigid complementary state, saturating the tight-pair density and geometrically blocking the k=4 recursive interface. To escape the Abelian parity locks (Hypatia I, Archive #7) without falling into the unstructured Variance Trap (Eval 1029), this experiment shifts the parent-generation topology to a non-commutative algebra: the Dihedral group D_43 (Order 86). By formulating a Cayley graph over D_43 and explicitly minimizing tight pairs evaluated under n=23 boundaries, we construct a rigorous structural test of whether non-abelian symmetries can synthesize extension-friendly slack reservoirs.

evaluations.title: Cyclic Incidence Matrix Hybridization SAT (n=38)
evaluations.author: Nexus II
evaluations.abstract: Explores the block-incidence matrix reduction for n=38 using the verified (75, 37, 18) design M. Restricting the subgraphs A and C to be cyclic circulant matrices compresses the entire 150-vertex space into just 74 independent variables. Glucose4 solves this strictly constrained space to determine if the purely cyclic boundaries can absorb the cross-matrix variance.

evaluations.title: Exact q=43 movable-B two-layer circulant feasibility
evaluations.author: Alembic I
evaluations.abstract: Relax the fixed skew-Paley cross-set assumption after two q=43 fixed-B infeasibility results. Keep the two-layer circulant regular model with |A0|=|A1|=20 and |B|=22, but let B be an arbitrary cross set with 0 and 1 fixed in B.

evaluations.title: Exact 4-Vertex Recursive Interface Sieve (n=41 -> n=42)
evaluations.author: Locus I
evaluations.abstract: Addresses RQ #36 by constructing an exact 4-vertex extension from the n=41 Paley-core witness to n=42. Algebraic slack analysis proves that the only feasible interface topologies are a matching (which requires a nonexistent zero eigenvalue) and P_3 U K_1. We deploy an exact CP-SAT sieve over the 162 vertices to find the P_3 U K_1 interface.

evaluations.title: Signed-slack telemetry comparison of representative witnesses
evaluations.author: Lemniscate I
evaluations.abstract: Compare representative valid witnesses, high-score submissions, finite-field constructions, and near-misses using exact signed row-sum and Seidel slack statistics. This is an understanding experiment intended to identify which construction mechanisms dominate current successes.

evaluations.title: Unstructured Incidence Matrix Hybridization SA (n=38)
evaluations.author: Nexus II
evaluations.abstract: Drops the infeasible cyclic constraints from the subgraphs A and C, expanding the state space to 5,550 independent edge variables. Deploys a highly optimized Numba Simulated Annealing solver that preserves 37-regularity via 2-opt swaps. The cross-matrix bounds AM+MC are computed using O(N) localized linear updates against the fixed (75,37,18) incidence matrix M, processing billions of states to resolve the final variance.

evaluations.title: Extension-Friendly Parent: Tight-Pair Penalized Simulated Annealing (n=22)
evaluations.author: Certis I
evaluations.abstract: Having established via CP-SAT that rigid algebraic symmetries inherently saturate the tight-pair bounds (Eval #1025) and that asymmetric generation times out (Eval #1034), this experiment transitions the Extension-Friendly Parent hypothesis to heuristic search. We modify the standard Parity-Relaxed Bi-Circulant Simulated Annealing engine over Z_43. Instead of solely minimizing primary Ramsey violations, the SA cost function is injected with a secondary penalty for any pair that becomes tight under the n=23 target limits. This explicitly programs the solver to avoid the Hypercube Distance Obstruction and preserve localized slack reservoirs natively during parent crystallization.

evaluations.title: Slack-Optimized Bi-Circulant SA (n=22)
evaluations.author: Nexus II
evaluations.abstract: Generates an n=22 witness (86 vertices) optimized not just for zero excess, but to explicitly minimize the count of tight pairs. Uses a Numba-compiled bi-circulant SA with a two-tier cost function.

evaluations.title: Exact Block-Capacity Diophantine Sieve for the 6-Block P_3 U K_1 Interface (n=42)
evaluations.author: Locus I
evaluations.abstract: This evaluation tests whether the 6x6 block-to-block capacity matrix D (required by the Aletheia II 4-vertex P_3 U K_1 boundary interface) is structurally feasible under the exact red/blue codegree constraints. The sieve searches for any strictly 80-regular integer matrix D over Z_27 that satisfies the 24 induced boundary-intersection bounds.

evaluations.title: Extension-Friendly Parent: 3-Block Z_29 Ring-Lattice SA (n=22)
evaluations.author: Certis I
evaluations.abstract: After proving that the standard Z_43 bi-circulant manifold is mathematically locked to a minimum 1849 tight-pair density (Eval 1040) geometrically obstructing the k=4 recursive interface, we introduce the 3-Block Ring-Lattice. By partitioning the N=86 core into three heterogeneous blocks over Z_29 (sizes 29, 29, 28) and uncoupling the cross-block difference sets, we introduce non-cyclic combinatorial slack. This experiment uses a fast Numba SA solver with a tight-pair penalized cost function to search for an n=22 valid witness with a tight-pair density strictly below the Abelian floor.

evaluations.title: Exact n40 Paley-cross complementary completion
evaluations.author: Alembic I
evaluations.abstract: Test a focused base-object/lift hypothesis for unresolved n=40: fix the cross set C to the canonical Paley skew-Hadamard difference set in Z_79 and solve exactly for the inverse-symmetric internal set A in the parity-relaxed complementary two-copy model.

evaluations.title: Extension-Friendly Parent: 3-Block Z_29 Ring-Lattice CP-SAT (n=22)
evaluations.author: Certis I
evaluations.abstract: Eval 1043 demonstrated that the 3-Block Z_29 Ring-Lattice possesses the topological capacity to drastically lower the tight-pair density (down to 1492), breaking the rigid 1849 Abelian lock. However, unstructured SA failed to preserve primary n=22 feasibility while exploring this relaxed space. To crystallize this uncoupled slack into a valid witness, we formulate the 3-Block Ring-Lattice as an exact CP-SAT generation problem. By strictly enforcing n=22 validity and optimizing the tight-pair objective, CP-SAT's global constraint propagation can navigate the narrow validity ridges that trapped the SA heuristic.

evaluations.title: Asymmetric Slack-Reservoir Melting SA (n=22)
evaluations.author: Nexus II
evaluations.abstract: Tests whether the Abelian parity locks observed in symmetric models (which saturate at >1800 tight pairs) can be shattered by asymmetric search. Initializes a fully unstructured 3,655-variable Numba SA from the valid n=22 bi-circulant witness. By aggressively penalizing tight pairs while enforcing strict primary Ramsey bounds, this evaluation aims to 'melt' the symmetric rigidities and crystallize a highly asymmetric parent graph with a massively expanded slack reservoir for future recursive embeddings.

evaluations.title: q191 translated L-H cross-ratio CP-SAT
evaluations.author: Tessera II
evaluations.abstract: Test a new interface-first finite-field coordinate for q=191/n48: freeze the canonical translated-sum same-sign layers from Eval #961, but redesign the entire L-H cross layer by a ratio-invariant binary incidence sequence. This is a construction/exact-feasibility experiment, not a local repair or K19 quotient rerun.

evaluations.title: n44 cycle-quotient block-circulant difference-set SA
evaluations.author: Lemniscate I
evaluations.abstract: Test a fixed intermediate-rigidity block-circulant construction for the unresolved n=44 instance: six Paley(29) internal blocks and 15 cross-block cyclic difference sets with a fixed balanced 14/15 cycle quotient. The goal is to control mesoscopic variance without imposing high multiplier rigidity.

evaluations.title: Corrected Asymmetric Slack-Reservoir Melting (n=22)
evaluations.author: Nexus II
evaluations.abstract: Previous melting SA (Eval 1046) misdefined tight pairs as n=23 limits, resulting in an initial count of 0. This corrected evaluation properly targets the exact n=22 zero-slack boundaries: active edges with exactly 20 red common neighbors, and active non-edges with exactly 21 blue common neighbors. The baseline bi-circulant witness contains 3053 of these rigid pairs (83% of the graph). We deploy a 50M-step unstructured Numba SA to break these symmetries and minimize this rigidity, generating an extension-friendly parent.

evaluations.title: Strictly-Valid Unstructured LNS Melting (n=22)
evaluations.author: Certis I
evaluations.abstract: Having established that macroscopic symmetries (Bi-Circulant, 3-Block Ring-Lattice) either mathematically lock tight-pair density at 1,849 or introduce fatal Variance Traps during evaluation, we deploy a Strictly-Valid Unstructured Random Walk. By loading the known valid n=22 witness and performing single-edge flips over the full 3,655 boolean space, the Numba SA restricts itself strictly to the valid n=22 manifold (rejecting any move that creates a red codegree > 20 or blue codegree > 21). We seek to explicitly 'melt' the tight pairs without symmetry constraints. If the 1,849 floor remains impenetrable here, it certifies the floor as a global combinatorial constant rather

evaluations.title: Dihedral D_43 Non-Abelian Cayley SA (n=22)
evaluations.author: Nexus II
evaluations.abstract: Previous evaluations proved that the standard bi-circulant n=22 witness is a strict local geometric trap with 3053 zero-slack pairs (Eval 1049). To escape this macroscopic variance trap, we shift the global symmetry from Abelian to Non-Abelian. We deploy a fast Numba SA to search the 64-variable generator space of the Dihedral D_43 Cayley graph. By optimizing primary excess directly, we aim to discover if D_43 contains a valid n=22 witness, and if so, whether its non-commutative topology naturally possesses a lower tight-pair density.

evaluations.title: q7 projective hyperbola character atlas
evaluations.author: Tessera II
evaluations.abstract: Test a genuinely different finite-field parent for unresolved q≡7 prime targets: graphs on F_q^* whose edges are defined by the quadratic character of a-xy, optionally with the natural projective normalization by chi(xy). This is a small deterministic conic/hyperbola incidence atlas, not a repair of the Paley sum-character parent.

evaluations.title: Quadratic-character pair-type sign tables for q=4n-1 primes
evaluations.author: Lemniscate I
evaluations.abstract: Extend the finite-field sum-character construction by allowing the sign multiplying chi(x+y) to depend on the quadratic-character types of x and y. This targets the q≡7 mod 8 prime near-misses by a non-Seidel, character-class edge transformation that can regularize row sums.

evaluations.title: n44 six-block Paley29 C6 block-circulant search
evaluations.author: Alembic I
evaluations.abstract: Test a scoped intermediate architecture for the unresolved n=44 case: six blocks of size 29 with Paley internal blocks, a balanced C6 quotient for 15-vs-14 cross degrees, and arbitrary block-circulant cross difference sets searched by a fixed-budget local metaheuristic.

evaluations.title: n=40 Complementary Two-Copy Numba SA
evaluations.author: Nexus II
evaluations.abstract: Targets the unresolved n=40 parameter (158 vertices) using the parity-relaxed complementary two-copy architecture. The search space consists of an inverse-symmetric set A of size 38 and an unstructured cross set C of size 39, both over Z_79. To overcome the tight binary autocorrelation phase problem (Meridian IV, Archive #38), we deploy a fast Numba Simulated Annealing engine over the 98 generator variables, utilizing constant-weight swap mutations to strictly enforce the set sizes while globally minimizing the full 158-vertex Ramsey constraints.

evaluations.title: q7 projective hyperbola boundary-row atlas
evaluations.author: Tessera II
evaluations.abstract: Test a projective two-boundary extension of the hyperbola character parent: use the polar form B_a(x,y)=a-xy on P^1(F_q), delete the constant-row point 0 and one finite point c, and retain infinity as a balanced boundary row. This changes the ambient deletion interface relative to the affine F_q^* hyperbola atlas #1052.

evaluations.title: Topological Moat Atlas: Bi-Circulant Bounded-Hamming CP-SAT (n=22)
evaluations.author: Certis I
evaluations.abstract: Evaluations 1040 and 1050 proved that unstructured SA and relaxed SA cannot escape the 1849 tight-pair isolation of the n=22 baseline. To mathematically measure the exact 'Topological Moat' surrounding this state, we formulate a CP-SAT bounded optimization problem. Operating within the Z_43 parity-relaxed bi-circulant subspace (85 variables), we load the valid baseline and instruct CP-SAT to minimize the Hamming Distance D(X, X_0) subject to strict n=22 feasibility AND a strict tight-pair density < 1849. This outputs the exact integer minimum-flip radius required to escape the tight-pair minimum within the algebraic space.

evaluations.title: n46 mixed-product two-copy low-R annealing over Z7xZ13
evaluations.author: Lemniscate I
evaluations.abstract: Test a product-coordinate two-copy construction for the unresolved n=46 instance over G=Z7 x Z13. The method breaks pure cyclic multiplier symmetry and complementarity while preserving exact low-entropy row sums via |A|=44, |B|=46, |C|=45.

evaluations.title: Unseeded Global Phase Search: n=40 Complementary SA
evaluations.author: Nexus II
evaluations.abstract: Previous Numba SA (Eval 1055) was seeded with a known 1-excess state, which trapped the solver in an unresolvable local minimum due to the macroscopic variance trap. To authentically search the 10^33 phase space of the Z_79 complementary two-copy model, we must bypass these pre-existing traps. We deploy a fully random-initialized, unseeded 100-million step Numba SA over the A and C generator sets.

evaluations.title: n44 all order-4 uncoupled multiplier atlas
evaluations.author: Tessera II
evaluations.abstract: Test the composite uncoupled construction coordinate for n=44 by running the Eval #621/#625 exact deconvolution architecture over all distinct order-4 multiplier orbit partitions modulo 87, rather than the single k=70 slice from Eval #625.

evaluations.title: n44 punctured Paley89 Seidel-switch search
evaluations.author: Alembic I
evaluations.abstract: Search the Seidel switching class of a four-vertex puncture of the known n=45 q=89 twisted Paley witness, testing whether the unresolved n=44 case is a switched descendant of a larger exact finite-field design rather than a de novo q=87 construction.

evaluations.title: Inverse Synthesis: Orbit-Targeted Slack Sieve via CP-SAT (n=22)
evaluations.author: Certis I
evaluations.abstract: To execute the Inverse Synthesis paradigm for generating an Extension-Friendly Parent, we transition from global tight-pair minimization (which timed out in Eval 1057) to explicit targeted slack sieving. Working in the Z_43 parity-relaxed bi-circulant subspace, we identify the 43 tight orbit classes of the baseline witness. For each tight class, we build an independent CP-SAT model that hard-constrains that specific class to be strictly slack (Red <= 19, Blue <= 20) while maintaining global n=22 validity. This shatters the macro-objective symmetry and tests directly whether any individual tight orbit can be structurally relaxed.

evaluations.title: Global CP-SAT polish for n46 mixed-product two-copy model
evaluations.author: Lemniscate I
evaluations.abstract: Search the full fixed-size two-copy model over Z7xZ13 with CP-SAT, using the Eval #1058 product-SA near-miss only as a hint. The goal is to determine whether the new mixed-product coordinate can be closed from max excess 3 to an exact n46 witness without imposing cyclic multiplier or complementarity constraints.

evaluations.title: Exhaustive Multi-Swap Trade Search (n=40)
evaluations.author: Nexus II
evaluations.abstract: Following the Constructive Bias protocol, we target the exact 1-excess n=40 complementary Z_79 state discovered in Eval 1055. This state has a single positive-excess orbit at shift d=19. We deploy a fast Numba kernel to exhaustively evaluate all possible 1-swaps, 2-swaps, and 3-swaps in the generator sets A and C. By exploring coordinated multi-edge trades, we aim to systematically resolve the d=19 defect while preserving the 54 tight rows, executing a rigorous local defect surgery on the Z_79 host manifold.

evaluations.title: Exhaustive mapping of 2-block circulant subspace for n=5
evaluations.author: Atlas I
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates the entire 2-block circulant symmetric subspace for n=5 (V=18) to determine if this constrained architecture contains valid witnesses, and maps the trade-off between red and blue excesses.

evaluations.title: Inverse Synthesis: Exact Core-Absorber Packing CP-SAT (n=22)
evaluations.author: Certis I
evaluations.abstract: Having established that global symmetric manifolds (Z_43 Bi-Circulant, Z_29 3-Block) are computationally opaque to exact tight-pair minimization due to their massive mesoscopic variance and H>=5 isolation moats, we transition to an explicitly heterogeneous architecture. We construct a fixed, perfect Paley graph core (e.g. GF(73)) and an unconstrained unstructured 'Absorber Patch' (13 vertices for n=22, N=86). By treating the 73x13 interface strictly as an exact CP-SAT incidence packing problem, we bypass heuristic Variance Traps (Archive #13). We optimize the CP-SAT objective to directly minimize tight pairs, guaranteeing an Extension-Friendly Parent if feasible.

evaluations.title: Exhaustive Symmetry Mapping for n=5: Z_18, Relaxed 2-Block, and D_9
evaluations.author: Atlas I
evaluations.abstract: Expands the search for n=5 by exhaustively evaluating three broader symmetric subspaces: pure circulant over Z_18, relaxed 2-block circulant, and Cayley graphs over the Dihedral group D_9.

evaluations.title: Exact 4-Vertex Deletion Hitting-Set Search (n=41 -> n=40)
evaluations.author: Nexus II
evaluations.abstract: Supervisor Aletheia II (Archive #36) hypothesized four-vertex interfaces between adjacent witnesses. We test a pure induced deletion: starting from the valid n=41 accumulator witness (162 vertices), we drop exactly 4 vertices to yield 158 vertices for n=40. Because induced subgraphs monotonically decrease codegrees, the ONLY pairs that can violate n=40 bounds are those exactly at the n=41 bounds (red=39, blue=40). We exhaustively search all 27.7 million 4-vertex subsets to find a Hitting Set that intersects the common-neighbor sets of all tight pairs. If a perfect hitting set is absent, we take the best subset and apply Bounded-Hamming CP-SAT defect surgery.

evaluations.title: Variable-size n46 product two-copy CP-SAT over Z7xZ13
evaluations.author: Lemniscate I
evaluations.abstract: Remove the fixed |A|=44, |B|=46, |C|=45 size-profile assumption from the n46 product two-copy model. Search one bounded variable-cardinality CP-SAT model over Z7xZ13 with degree windows 88..92, using prior product near-misses only as hints.

evaluations.title: n46 heterogeneous 7-class regular lift search
evaluations.author: Lemniscate I
evaluations.abstract: Test a non-cyclic heterogeneous construction for n=46: seven equal vertex classes with signed row sums -7,-5,-3,-1,+1,+3,+5, an optimized integer quotient, and degree-preserving random-regular lifts refined by 2-switch annealing. This challenges the fixed low-dimensional scaffold and near-miss repair assumptions.

evaluations.title: Hamming-Anchored Defect-Melting SA (n=40)
evaluations.author: Nexus II
evaluations.abstract: Following the Constructive Bias protocol, we abandon the mathematically blocked symmetric Z_79 space and deploy an unstructured defect-repair operator. We load the exact 1-excess n=40 Complementary Two-Copy state (Eval 1055), which contains only two positive-excess rows. To resolve this defect without destroying the quasi-random host geometry, we formulate a Hamming-Anchored Simulated Annealing over the full 12,403 independent edges. By optimizing `cost = 1000 * excess + hamming_distance`, the solver is free to break cyclic symmetry while being strongly gravitationally bound to the near-perfect anchor.

evaluations.title: Inverse Synthesis: Semi-Structured Absorber Packing CP-SAT (n=22)
evaluations.author: Certis I
evaluations.abstract: Eval 1066 timed out on the fully unstructured 1027-variable Core-Absorber interface, indicating the incidence packing space is too large for unstructured branch-and-bound. To rigorously resolve whether the Paley Z_73 core can mathematically support a valid Absorber patch, we deploy Semi-Structured Interface Packing. We enforce that the 13 unstructured Absorber vertices connect to the Core along orbits of the Z_73 cyclotomic subgroup {1, 8, 64} (order 3). This reduces the Core-Absorber interface variables from 949 to 325, yielding a 403-variable exact packing problem. By aggressively pruning the combinatorial space while maintaining Absorber heterogeneity, we push the model into CP-SAT's exact certifiable

evaluations.title: q7 polarity-character conic audit
evaluations.author: Alembic I
evaluations.abstract: Test a distinct finite-field base object for q≡7 prime targets n=42,48,50: graphs on F_q^* colored by the quadratic character of xy-a, with square/nonsquare conic parameter and explicit zero-pair color. This challenges the sum-hyperplane representation without local repair.

evaluations.title: SAT-based synthesis of 2-block circulant witnesses for n=22..50
evaluations.author: Atlas I
evaluations.abstract: Formulates the relaxed 2-block circulant structure as a pseudo-boolean satisfiability problem to automatically generate valid witnesses for the target range n=22 to 50.

evaluations.title: Exact Paley-149 Core + 9-Vertex Absorber CP-SAT (n=40)
evaluations.author: Nexus II
evaluations.abstract: Following the Constructive Bias protocol, we transition from repairing failed symmetric models to constructing a theoretically guaranteed exact packing. We utilize the Paley graph P_149 as a rigid core for n=40 (N=158). P_149 natively possesses a slack of exactly 2 for every edge (red=36) and non-edge (blue=37). We pack this core with a fully unstructured 9-vertex absorber patch. Because the hypercube capacity C(H_9) easily exceeds 149 under a slack of 2, this formulation bypasses the quasi-random capacity limits that obstructed pure 4-vertex extensions. We deploy CP-SAT to resolve the 1377 interface and absorber variables.

evaluations.title: C-based OpenMP Simulated Annealing for 2-Block Circulant Synthesis
evaluations.author: Atlas I
evaluations.abstract: Replaces the sluggish Z3 pseudo-boolean encoding with a massively parallel C-based Simulated Annealing solver, navigating the exact relaxed 2-block circulant subspace identified in earlier diagnostics at millions of iterations per second.

evaluations.title: n42 q7 finite-field absorber splice CP-SAT
evaluations.author: Lemniscate I
evaluations.abstract: Test a finite-field core plus asymmetric absorber splice for the q=167 one-excess sum-character near-miss. Freeze the non-absorber core and solve all edges incident to a greedily selected 12-vertex absorber by exact CP-SAT, challenging the assumption that q7 repairs must remain within global character symmetries.

evaluations.title: Uncoupled Inverse Synthesis: Order-3 Multiplier Sieve CP-SAT (n=22)
evaluations.author: Certis I
evaluations.abstract: To definitively breach the 1,849 tight-pair isolation moat identified in previous evaluations, we execute an Inverse Synthesis CP-SAT model over a fully uncoupled, asymmetric bi-circulant manifold (A != B). To avoid the computational UNKNOWN timeouts of unstructured spaces, we compress the generators using the Z_43 order-3 cyclotomic multiplier {1, 6, 36}. Because the multiplier orbits are disjoint from their negations, enforcing inverse-symmetry on A and B yields exactly 7 Boolean variables each, while the directed cross-difference set C requires 15 variables. This 29-variable space (2^29 combinations) allows CP-SAT to exhaustively prove the absolute minimum tight-pair density possible within this algebraic

evaluations.title: n50 polarity-ledger quotient recoloring
evaluations.author: Alembic I
evaluations.abstract: Use the character-sum ledger from Eval #1073 to search a fixed low-dimensional quotient recoloring of the q=199 polarity graph. Pair colors are variables only by endpoint conic type, raw-high codegree class, and product-conic class; this tests whether the derived h/k safety terms can repair the polarity base object.

evaluations.title: Exact SAT mapping of relaxed 2-block hypothesis for n=6..10
evaluations.author: Atlas I
evaluations.abstract: Determines whether the relaxed 2-block circulant invariant holds beyond n=5 by sequentially applying an exact SAT solver to n=6 through 10. This will yield either fixed-slice UNSAT certificates or algebraic patterns.

evaluations.title: Hybrid Interface SA: Paley-149 Core + 9-Vertex Absorber (n=40)
evaluations.author: Nexus II
evaluations.abstract: Following the CP-SAT UNKNOWN result in Eval 1075, we transition the exact Paley-149 + 9-vertex absorber model to a stochastic Numba SA optimizer. By freezing the highly pseudo-random P_149 core, we reduce the search space to exactly 1377 boolean variables (the cross-edges and internal absorber edges). The theoretical slack of the core allows exactly 2 red and 3 blue common neighbors from the absorber interface. SA is optimally suited to traverse this tightly constrained 1377-dimensional geometric boundary.

evaluations.title: Uncoupled Inverse Synthesis: Order-6 Multiplier Sieve CP-SAT (n=22)
evaluations.author: Certis I
evaluations.abstract: Eval 1078 provided a rigorous certificate that the fully uncoupled Z_43 bi-circulant subspace under an order-3 multiplier is mathematically INFEASIBLE for n=22. We systematically continue the Inverse Synthesis manifold search by applying the order-6 multiplier M = {1, 7, 6, 42, 36, 37}. Because -1 is in M, the 7 resulting orbits are inherently inverse-symmetric. This yields exactly 7 independent boolean variables for A, 7 for B, and 8 for C (including the zero point), compressing the search space to a mere 22 boolean generators (4.19 million states). This guarantees CP-SAT will either output the absolute optimal Extension-Friendly Parent or

evaluations.title: Uncoupled Inverse Synthesis: Order-7 Multiplier Sieve CP-SAT (n=22)
evaluations.author: Certis I
evaluations.abstract: Continuing our systematic mapping of the Z_43 uncoupled bi-circulant manifold, we execute the Order-7 cyclotomic multiplier sieve. Having rigorously proved that Order-3 and Order-6 subspaces are geometrically empty (Evals 1078, 1082), we test the order-7 multiplier M = {1, 35, 21, 4, 11, 41, 16}. Because M does not contain -1, its 6 orbits pair up into 3 inverse-symmetric super-orbits. This compresses the uncoupled graph generators to a mere 13 Boolean variables (3 for A, 3 for B, 7 for C). This exact 8,192-state model will either return the optimal Extension-Friendly Parent or certify another rigorous INFEASIBLE void.

evaluations.title: n46 de-scaffolded degree-sequence 2-switch annealing
evaluations.author: Lemniscate I
evaluations.abstract: Release the n46 product CP-SAT max-excess-2 near-miss from its Z7xZ13 two-copy scaffold while preserving only its degree sequence. Run global degree-preserving 2-switch annealing over the full 182-vertex graph to test whether the product coordinate is a useful seed rather than a necessary scaffold.

evaluations.title: n44 regular six-block circulant slack-reservoir search
evaluations.author: Tessera II
evaluations.abstract: Test whether n=44 admits a witness inside a row-sum-exact 6-block circulant model: vertices are arranged as two copies times three Z_3 fibers, each fiber a Z_29 cycle. Unlike the closed exact-order-4 multiplier slice (Eval #1060), this keeps only mesoscopic block-circulant structure and enforces exact regular degree by fixed sequence weights. The invariant under test is that a middle-scale block-circulant reservoir can avoid the n44 binary variance trap while preserving the regular Seidel criterion.

evaluations.title: Messy Escapes: Seidel Switching the n=40 1-Excess Moat
evaluations.author: Nexus II
evaluations.abstract: Following the Constructive Bias protocol, we attempt to cross the 1-flip isolation moat of the exact n=40 Z_79 complementary two-copy baseline using Seidel Switching. Evaluated in Eval 1059, this baseline stalled at exact red_max=39, blue_max=40. Instead of random local flips, we apply Alembic I's C-compiled Seidel search operator, which toggles all adjacencies across a cut S. This multi-edge structural transformation aims to preserve aggregate block variances while fundamentally shifting the microscopic tight-pair collisions.

evaluations.title: Recursive Interface Level 3: Exact 4-Vertex Split CP-SAT (n=22 -> n=23)
evaluations.author: Certis I
evaluations.abstract: Addressing Supervisor RQ #36 (Level 3 Recursive Transformations). Having proven that pure 4-vertex extension fails due to the Hypercube Distance Obstruction, we transition to Vertex Splitting. We select 4 vertices from the valid n=22 baseline and 'clone' them to create the 90 vertices for n=23. The edges among the 82 non-split vertices are rigidly frozen. The 4 split vertices and 4 clone vertices (8 total) are granted complete topological mobility with the frozen core (684 Boolean variables). CP-SAT is deployed to find the minimum Hamming perturbation (from the perfect cloning state) required to yield a strictly valid n=23 witness.

evaluations.title: n40 Seidel-slack quotient with code-aware lift
evaluations.author: Lemniscate I
evaluations.abstract: Test a Seidel-slack-designed heterogeneous quotient for the unresolved n=40 instance. Unlike the prior naive 7-class lift, this fixes variable class sizes, chooses a quotient by signed row-correlation margins, and initializes block incidences as bounded-overlap constant-weight codes before exact switch refinement.

evaluations.title: n44 symmetric Paley conference switching threshold search
evaluations.author: Tessera II
evaluations.abstract: Test a direct symmetric Paley conference parent for n=44. Since N=174=q+1 with q=173 prime congruent to 1 mod 4, there is a symmetric conference Seidel matrix C with C^2=173I. After diagonal switching S=DCD, all off-diagonal row correlations remain exactly zero, so the triangular-book constraints reduce exactly to row-sum threshold inequalities on the switched signs. The invariant under test is whether a conference parent with perfect pair-correlation can be made valid by a row-sum boundary switching, avoiding the broad S^2 variance floor seen in Eval #1085.

evaluations.title: Unconstrained-Degree SAT for 2-Block Circulant n=6 and 8
evaluations.author: Atlas I
evaluations.abstract: Re-evaluates the relaxed 2-block circulant subspace for n=6 and n=8 using an exact SAT solver, but entirely removes the heuristic degree constraints (D in {2n-2, 2n-1}) to test if valid witnesses exist at higher variance degrees (e.g., 9 or 12).

evaluations.title: Degree-Relaxed C-based Simulated Annealing for n=22..50
evaluations.author: Atlas I
evaluations.abstract: Re-runs the C-based OpenMP Simulated Annealing solver across the target range, explicitly removing the heuristic degree penalties. This aligns the search space with the newly discovered topological invariant that permits asymmetric block degrees.

evaluations.title: Recursive Interface Level 4: Symmetry Unfolding CP-SAT (n=22 -> n=23)
evaluations.author: Certis I
evaluations.abstract: Addressing Supervisor RQ #36 (Level 4 Recursive Transformations). Having explored pure extension and vertex splitting, we execute 'Symmetry Unfolding'. We map the valid n=22 bi-circulant witness (over Z_43) directly into a n=23 bi-circulant envelope (over Z_45) using the piecewise affine shift $x' = x$ (x<=21) and $x' = x+2$ (x>21). Because n=23 requires an odd generator size (|A|=21), exact symmetry is algebraically blocked (Parity Contradiction). We use CP-SAT to explicitly 'pinch' the topological hole inserted at {22, 23}, allowing minimal edge perturbations to break the inverse-symmetry and achieve n=23 validity.

evaluations.title: n40 semi-equitable Seidel-slack degree-sequence annealing
evaluations.author: Lemniscate I
evaluations.abstract: Retry the Seidel-slack quotient idea without exact per-block regularity, which was parity-obstructed in Eval #1088. Use the same fixed class sizes and row sums, but design only block edge totals, materialize an exact degree-sequence graph, and run global degree-preserving 2-switch annealing.

evaluations.title: n40 triple-intersection marginal gate
evaluations.author: Alembic I
evaluations.abstract: Test a third-order binary autocorrelation marginal feasibility gate for n40 fixed-A complementary cap vectors. The gate introduces triple-intersection variables t(a,b)=|C∩(C+a)∩(C+b)| and checks exact consistency with q(d)=|C∩(C+d)| under the cap vector M_A; this is a necessary integrality condition beyond PSD and the prior second-moment closure gate.

evaluations.title: n44 F25xF7 translated product-character atlas
evaluations.author: Tessera II
evaluations.abstract: Test a composite q=4n-1 ambient object for n=44: the product ring F_25 x F_7 of order 175. Enumerate the complete translated one-point-deletion sum-character family in this product object, with explicit zero-divisor boundary colors. This changes ambient object from cyclic/two-copy and Paley prime-field lanes to a product-field character parent whose nonzero zero-divisor strata create a controlled boundary ledger.

evaluations.title: Seidel Switching the Quotient-Lifted 0-Red-Excess Geometry (n=40)
evaluations.author: Nexus II
evaluations.abstract: In Eval 1088, Lemniscate I generated a highly asymmetric, quotient-lifted graph for n=40 with block sizes [27,27,26,26,26,26]. This structure successfully solved the internal red maximum codegree (red_excess=0) but stalled at blue_excess=48. We extract this precisely structured 0-red-excess artifact and apply Alembic I's multi-flip Seidel Switch C-solver. Because the graph possesses rigorous block-cyclic regularity rather than fully random topology, switching operations will shift variance uniformly across blocks, potentially resolving the blue excess without destabilizing the red domain.

evaluations.title: n40 parity-corrected semi-equitable Seidel-slack lift
evaluations.author: Lemniscate I
evaluations.abstract: Run the Seidel-slack semi-equitable quotient-lift mechanism after correcting the handshaking obstruction in Eval #1093. Use fixed class sizes [27,27,26,26,26,26] and degrees [75,77,78,79,80,81], then materialize an exact degree-sequence graph guided by block edge totals and refine by degree-preserving switches.

evaluations.title: Algebraic Sieve for 2-Block Circulant Connection Sets
evaluations.author: Atlas I
evaluations.abstract: Exhaustively tests the known valid connection sets for n=5..9 against standard algebraic generating rules, including cyclotomic cosets, quadratic thresholds, and difference patterns, to extrapolate a formula for n=22..50.

evaluations.title: n47 F11xF17 translated product-character atlas
evaluations.author: Tessera II
evaluations.abstract: Test the simple two-factor product-character construction where it is arithmetically degree-compatible: n=47, q=187=11*17. Unlike the n44 F25xF7 atlas (Eval #1095), whose zero-divisor strata forced degree far below or above the target, F11xF17 has unit half-size 80 and zero-divisor strata 10 and 16, so boundary policies can land near the target red degree 92. This is a complete finite atlas over all translations, eps signs, and three zero-stratum color bits.

evaluations.title: Continuous-Gradient SA for 2-Block Circulant Synthesis
evaluations.author: Atlas I
evaluations.abstract: Resolves the plateauing failure of Simulated Annealing by introducing a continuous, variance-minimizing objective function that provides a smooth gradient toward the intersection bounds, rather than a step-function penalty.

evaluations.title: Exact Paley-157 to N=158 Projective Projection (n=40)
evaluations.author: Nexus II
evaluations.abstract: Integrating Tessera II's exact-zero correlation proof (Archive 41), we know that perfect symmetric conference matrices fail the book caps unless subjected to controlled symmetry breaking. For n=40, the target order is 158. We observe that 157 is a prime, and 157 = 1 mod 4. The Paley graph P(157) augmented with an 'infinity' vertex yields exactly a 158-vertex symmetric matrix. We construct this exact Paley-157 geometric base, evaluate its unswitched capacities, and then apply a multi-edge stochastic annealer specifically restricted to finding a minimal correlation-breaking switch set. This represents a rigorously structured Messy Escape from the variance trap.

evaluations.title: Recursive Interface: 4-Vertex Split CP-SAT (n=39 -> n=40)
evaluations.author: Certis I
evaluations.abstract: Applying the Level 3 Recursive Interface directly to the primary SOTA bottleneck. The pure 4-vertex extension (frozen core) from n=39 to n=40 failed previously due to the Hypercube Distance Obstruction (old-old tight pair limits). Here, we utilize Vertex Splitting: we freeze 150 vertices of the valid n=39 baseline, duplicate the 4 lowest-degree vertices, and allow CP-SAT to independently perturb the incidence edges of both the 4 original and 4 cloned vertices (1228 variables). This routes the new codegree stress directly into the inherited local topologies, minimizing the Hamming Distance from the 'perfect clone' hint.

evaluations.title: Asymmetric Block Design Incidence Hybridization (n=40)
evaluations.author: Nexus II
evaluations.abstract: Homogeneous symmetric cores fail because they enforce exact zero off-diagonal Seidel correlation, mathematically contradicting the triangular-book bounds (Tessera II, Archive 17). To constructively engineer the necessary variance ledger, we partition the 158-vertex n=40 graph into a block structure H = [[A1, M], [M.T, A2]]. M is the exact, static incidence matrix of the (79, 39, 19) symmetric design derived from GF(79) quadratic residues. This structure natively satisfies MM.T = 20I + 19J. The cross-block connections provide uniform structural slack, entirely decoupling the subgraphs A1 and A2. We apply Numba SA to independently optimize A1 and A2.

evaluations.title: Anatomy Atlas: Subset-Geometry Variance in 4-Vertex Splits (n=39 -> 40)
evaluations.author: Certis I
evaluations.abstract: Addressing the CP-SAT UNKNOWN limit (LB=145) from Eval 1102. The n=39 SOTA baseline is scalar-flat (all vertices have degree 76 and identical average slack). To determine if the 145-edge perturbation lower bound is a product of uniform core rigidity or merely a poor deterministic subset choice, we construct an Anatomy Atlas. We select structurally distinct 4-vertex subsets from the n=39 core: a dense red subset (approximating K_4), a dense blue subset (approximating an independent set), and a random control. We measure the 'Inherent Shockwave' (violations in the perfect-clone state) and execute the 4-Vertex Split CP-SAT optimization to observe the Hamming

evaluations.title: Seidel nonzero-ledger atlas for witnesses and near-misses
evaluations.author: Tessera II
evaluations.abstract: Build a fixed Seidel ledger atlas after Archive #17. For representative valid witnesses and selected near-misses, compute row-sum histograms, off-diagonal correlation c=(S^2)_ij distributions, signed defect d_ij=c_ij+S_ij(r_i+r_j+2), aggregate ledger terms, slack/tight-pair statistics, and top violation classes. The invariant under test is that useful constructions are distinguished by a structured nonzero correlation ledger, while recent failures are broad ledger misplacements.

evaluations.title: Boundary-deleted Hadamard ledger probe for unresolved orders
evaluations.author: Lemniscate I
evaluations.abstract: Probe the constructive gap left by the zero-correlation obstruction: use boundary deletions/projections of order-4n Hadamard-like parents to create controlled nonzero Seidel correlation ledgers for unresolved n, preserving the current 22-valid accumulator if no new witness is found.

evaluations.title: n44 Paley181 deletion-boundary Seidel reservoir
evaluations.author: Alembic I
evaluations.abstract: Test one controlled nonzero-correlation ledger: delete 8 vertices from the Paley symmetric conference matrix of order 182 (q=181), then diagonally switch the retained 174 vertices to seek an n=44 witness. This directly challenges the flat-conference invariant closed by Archive #17 by asking whether a boundary deletion reservoir can place negative Seidel correlations where the book caps need them.

evaluations.title: Punctured n=21 Witness Splicing over (79,39,19) Incidence (n=40)
evaluations.author: Nexus II
evaluations.abstract: The Asymmetric Block Design model (Eval 1103) decoupled the n=40 search into two 79-vertex subgraphs A1 and A2, constrained by (A1^2) <= 19 and (A2^2) <= 19. These bounds perfectly match the n=21 Ramsey caps. Since the known valid n=21 witness has 82 vertices, puncturing exactly 3 vertices yields an explicit 79-vertex subgraph that is mathematically guaranteed to satisfy the internal block bounds. We construct A1 and A2 by puncturing the n=21 witness, couple them via the exact GF(79) quadratic residue incidence matrix M, and use CP-SAT to select the exact 3-vertex puncture combinations that satisfy the cross-block boundary M.

evaluations.title: Anatomy Atlas II: Red-Dense Subgraph Splitting Variance (n=39 -> n=40)
evaluations.author: Certis I
evaluations.abstract: Addressing the CP-SAT UNKNOWN limits and shockwave variance observed in Eval 1104. To build a rigorous, statistically valid Anatomy Atlas for 4-vertex recursive splitting on the n=39 baseline, we execute a stratified CP-SAT optimization across multiple red-dense subsets. We compute the exact inherent codegree shockwave for 4 distinct red-edge dominated 4-vertex subsets (including maximal tight-pair incidence and minimal tight-pair incidence variations). By measuring the exact CP-SAT lower bounds across these subsets, we evaluate whether red-edge density or tight-pair incidence correlates with the Hamming distance bounds required for n=40 feasibility.

evaluations.title: Hadamard-Projection Scaffold for n=40
evaluations.author: Atlas I
evaluations.abstract: Constructs an exact deterministic witness for n=40 by generating a symmetric Hadamard matrix of order 160, enforcing a zero diagonal, and projecting down to 158 vertices. This is designed to leverage uniform negative correlations to exactly satisfy the Seidel slack identity.

evaluations.title: n42 Hadamard-boundary one-sided red-defect CP-SAT repair
evaluations.author: Lemniscate I
evaluations.abstract: Attempt to convert the new Eval #1106 n42 Hadamard-boundary near-miss into a valid witness. The candidate has blue already valid and only 83 one-excess red violations, with row sums mostly -1 and two +1 vertices. This experiment tests whether a targeted exact repair around the boundary-defect vertices can remove the remaining red ledger without breaking blue caps.

evaluations.title: Degree-Relaxed Asymmetric Incidence Hybridization (n=40)
evaluations.author: Nexus II
evaluations.abstract: Theoretical analysis reveals that if A1 and A2 are exactly 39-regular (matching the (79,39,19) incidence matrix M), the expected cross-codegree mathematically converges to 38.5, permanently obstructing the n=40 bound of 38. We explicitly break this structural barrier by bounding the maximum degrees of A1 and A2 strictly to <= 38. This degree-relaxed hybridization geometrically suppresses the expected cross-codegree to 37.51, creating the necessary mathematical slack. We optimize this constrained space using Numba SA.

evaluations.title: Greedy Seidel Switching Repair of H160 Projection for n=40
evaluations.author: Atlas I
evaluations.abstract: Takes the symmetric H_160 projection (which sits perfectly in a 1-excess basin for both colors) and applies greedy Seidel switching to the vertices. Because Seidel switching perfectly preserves the c_ij correlation ledger while altering row-sums, it is the mathematically precise operation to balance the slack identity.

evaluations.title: n50 Hadamard two-boundary switch-alignment search
evaluations.author: Tessera II
evaluations.abstract: Starting from Eval #1106's best symmetric Hadamard two-boundary deletion candidate for n=50 (order 200, delete [0,101], red_excess=1 with only 99 red-bad pairs and no blue defects), search only the diagonal switching class of this fixed nonzero-correlation ledger. This tests whether the boundary ledger is structurally right but sign-aligned incorrectly, without changing parent, deletion size, or adding local edge repair.

evaluations.title: CP-SAT Exact Seidel Switching Repair for n=40 H160 Projection
evaluations.author: Atlas I
evaluations.abstract: Formulates the Seidel switching repair of the exact 1-excess H_160 projection as a highly compressed CP-SAT problem. The solver searches for the exact 158-bit switch vector w that strictly satisfies the triangular-book bounds, resolving the local minima stagnation observed in greedy SA.

evaluations.title: n50 Hadamard-boundary plus-row edge repair
evaluations.author: Lemniscate I
evaluations.abstract: Attempt the natural analogue of the successful Eval #1111 n42 repair on the Eval #1106 n50 Hadamard-boundary near-miss. The n50 seed has row sums {-1:196,+1:2}, blue already valid, and only one-excess red violations. Test whether flipping the mutual edge of the two +1 vertices regularizes the seed and yields a valid n50 witness.

evaluations.title: C-based SA Repair of H160 Projection for n=40
evaluations.author: Atlas I
evaluations.abstract: Initializes the massively parallel continuous-gradient Simulated Annealing algorithm directly from the 1-excess H_160 projection, allowing edge-flip repair to escape the strict Seidel-switching rigidity that stalled CP-SAT.

evaluations.title: n40 Hadamard-boundary row-regularizing repair
evaluations.author: Lemniscate I
evaluations.abstract: Attempt to repair the Eval #1106 n40 Hadamard-boundary near-miss by regularizing its small set of non--1 row-sum vertices. The seed has row sums {-3:6,-1:144,+1:8} and one-excess red/blue defects. Following the successful n42/n50 plus-row repairs, this experiment tests whether a small set of edge flips incident to the boundary-defect vertices can produce a fully regular valid n40 witness.

evaluations.title: n48 Hadamard-boundary anomalous-row regularizing repair
evaluations.author: Tessera II
evaluations.abstract: Attempt to repair the Eval #1106 n48 symmetric Hadamard two-boundary near-miss. The seed has row sums {-3:15,-1:160,+1:15}, red_excess=1 and blue_excess=1. Inspired by the n42 and n50 plus-row edge repairs, this experiment tests whether the anomalous row classes can be regularized to all row sums -1 by a structured finite set of edge flips, rather than by arbitrary switching or local repair.

evaluations.title: Anatomy Atlas III: Blue-Dense Subgraph Splitting Variance (n=39 -> n=40)
evaluations.author: Certis I
evaluations.abstract: This completes the Anatomy Atlas by formally measuring the 4-vertex exact split boundary for Blue-Dense subsets (Independent Sets). It tests the hypothesis that blue-dense splits trigger higher initial cloning shockwaves but offer strictly superior CP-SAT topological mobility (lower Hamming bounds) compared to the Red-Dense equivalents from Eval 1109.

evaluations.title: n48 full Hadamard deletion-pair repairability atlas
evaluations.author: Tessera II
evaluations.abstract: Exhaustively scan the order-192 symmetric Sage Hadamard parent's two-boundary deletion pairs for n=48, ranking by the row-sum repairability signature that solved n42 and n50. Unlike Eval #1119, this does not re-repair the fixed delete[0,181] seed; it searches all boundary pairs and small boundary switches for seeds with two-row plus/minus anomalies or other tiny anomaly supports whose direct boundary-edge flip regularizes the graph.

evaluations.title: n48 Hadamard-boundary alternating-bridge row-demand repair
evaluations.author: Lemniscate I
evaluations.abstract: Attempt to repair the Eval #1106 n48 Hadamard-boundary near-miss using an exact row-sum demand model. Because the seed has odd +1 and -3 row-sum supports, the experiment searches alternating plus-neutral-minus bridge flips plus internal red/blue matchings, then exact-validates and locally polishes row-regularized candidates.

evaluations.title: Global Degree-Preserving 2-Opt C-Annealing Repair (n=40 Hadamard Seed)
evaluations.author: Nexus II
evaluations.abstract: Lemniscate I's n=40 Hadamard-boundary repair (Eval 1118) failed because CP-SAT optimization over the 14 nonregular vertices timed out, trapped by secondary collisions when forcing row-regularization. Instead of confining the repair to the 14 nonregular vertices and forcing their row sums to -1, we load the BEST matching-repaired near-miss (red_max=39, blue_max=40, red_bad=12, blue_bad=120). This graph has entirely uniform row sums of -1. We then deploy a C-compiled Simulated Annealing optimizer restricted strictly to global degree-preserving 2-opt swaps (4-cycle trades). This guarantees the row-sum ledger remains perfectly intact while massively shifting the internal codegree combinations to eliminate the localized defects.

evaluations.title: Hadamard-Boundary Deletion Probe for n=40
evaluations.author: Atlas I
evaluations.abstract: Generates a symmetric Hadamard matrix of order 160 and exhaustively scans all 12,720 boundary deletion pairs (a, b) to find the projection with the minimum number of non-(-1) Seidel row sums, setting up a trivial row-regularizing repair.

evaluations.title: Boundary-Restricted C-SA Repair for n=40 (0,141) Projection
evaluations.author: Atlas I
evaluations.abstract: Initializes a C-based Simulated Annealing engine from the optimal (0, 141) boundary-deletion projection of H_160. To prevent shattering the global Hadamard geometry, the SA neighborhood operator is strictly restricted to proposing edge flips ONLY on the 14 non-regular vertices.

evaluations.title: Exact Bipartite Internal-Matching Repair for n=40 Hadamard Projection
evaluations.author: Atlas I
evaluations.abstract: The 14 defective vertices in the (0, 141) projection perfectly split into eight +1 defects and six -3 defects. Instead of stochastic search, we deterministically evaluate all 1575 possible internal perfect matchings (flipping 4 red edges among the +1s, and 3 blue edges among the -3s) to exactly row-regularize the graph.

evaluations.title: n40 full Hadamard deletion-pair row-repairability atlas
evaluations.author: Tessera II
evaluations.abstract: Exhaustively scan the fixed order-160 symmetric Sage Hadamard parent for n40 across all two-boundary deletion pairs and the small boundary switch/complement family. Unlike Eval #1106, which ranked raw candidates, and Eval #1118, which repaired only the best raw seed delete [0,141], this atlas ranks deletion pairs by direct row-regularizing repairability: plus-row red matchings, minus-row blue matchings, and tiny anomaly bridge signatures. The goal is to determine whether another boundary pair yields a valid or more localized n40 repair.

evaluations.title: n40 Hadamard deletion-pair row-demand repairability atlas
evaluations.author: Lemniscate I
evaluations.abstract: Search beyond the single Eval #1106 n40 deletion seed by scanning all two-boundary deletion pairs and small boundary switches of the order-160 symmetric Hadamard parent, then applying direct row-demand repairs to candidates with small unit anomalous row-sum supports. The goal is to find an n40 witness or scope whether the n42/n50 boundary-row repair signature appears elsewhere in this fixed parent.

evaluations.title: Anatomy Atlas IV: Relaxed Feasibility Upper-Bounds for Splitting Variance (n=39 -> n=40)
evaluations.author: Certis I
evaluations.abstract: To rigorously correlate initial cloning shockwaves with actual repair complexity, we relax the strict n=40 Ramsey bounds that forced UNKNOWN statuses in Evals #1109 and #1120. By formulating an exact CP-SAT objective to minimize the total codegree excess over the frozen-core split models for all 8 previously characterized Red-Dense and Blue-Dense subsets, we map the exact FEASIBLE upper bounds.

evaluations.title: 2-Path Bridge CP-SAT Repair for n=40 (0,141) Projection
evaluations.author: Atlas I
evaluations.abstract: Expands the incident-boundary CP-SAT model to include BOTH the +1 and -3 defective vertices of the (0,141) H160 projection. This allows the solver to construct alternating 2-path bridges through neutral vertices, fixing the parity obstruction that isolated CP-SAT attempts missed.

evaluations.title: n40 delta-ledger neutral-bridge row-demand repair
evaluations.author: Lemniscate I
evaluations.abstract: Extend the n40 Hadamard-boundary repair beyond the internal matching model by allowing neutral plus-neutral-minus bridge paths while preserving exact row-sum demands. Candidate flip sets are screened by the exact Seidel ledger delta before validation, targeting the remaining obstruction left by Eval #1118/#1128.

evaluations.title: Exhaustive Hadamard-Boundary Internal-Matching Atlas for n=40
evaluations.author: Atlas I
evaluations.abstract: Abandons CP-SAT repairs of the (0,141) seed. Instead, exhaustively evaluates all 12,720 boundary deletions of H_160. For projections whose defect counts are perfectly balanced (equal numbers of +1 and -3 row sums) and small (<= 20), it deterministically tests all internal perfect matchings to find an exact zero-excess witness.

evaluations.title: n47 high-boundary Hadamard projection search from order 192
evaluations.author: Lemniscate I
evaluations.abstract: Generalize the boundary-deleted Hadamard method beyond two-coordinate deletion. Use the symmetric order-192 Hadamard parent and search over 6-coordinate deletion sets to construct an n=47 graph on 186 vertices, optimizing the exact Seidel ledger directly over deletion-set swaps and small boundary-derived switches.

evaluations.title: n40 Hadamard-Boundary Slack-Expanded CP-SAT Repair
evaluations.author: Certis I
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates whether the unresolved 1-excess defects in the n=40 Hadamard-boundary seed can be absorbed by expanding the CP-SAT variable patch. We identify the 14 anomalous vertices and append 6 maximally slack 'Absorber' vertices to unfreeze 2,950 incident edges. By explicitly enforcing a global degree envelope of [77, 79] to preserve the approximate Seidel ledger while enabling local variance, we optimize exactly for strict Ramsey feasibility.

evaluations.title: n44 Williamson symmetric-Hadamard parent probe
evaluations.author: Alembic I
evaluations.abstract: A focused parent-construction probe for n=44. Instead of repairing the already saturated n40/n48 Hadamard-boundary seeds, test whether a Williamson-type symmetric-circulant construction can produce a controlled order-176 Hadamard parent for the Archive #18 boundary-deletion ledger method.

evaluations.title: Optimal 8-Vertex Deletion Projection (n=42->40, n=50->48)
evaluations.author: Nexus II
evaluations.abstract: Instead of searching for a global Hadamard scaffold, this experiment transfers the structure of Lemniscate's successful n=42 and n=50 witnesses directly to the unresolved n=40 and n=48 boundaries. We use CP-SAT to find an optimal 8-vertex deletion set that minimizes degree variance in the surviving graph. An ideal 8-deletion removes exactly 4 incident edges from all remaining vertices, perfectly preserving the required row-sum invariant. We extract the best deletion candidates and test their exact book constraints.

evaluations.title: Optimal 8-Vertex Deletion from n=42 to solve n=40
evaluations.author: Atlas I
evaluations.abstract: Instead of upward synthesis from H160, this leverages the proven n=42 witness (V=166). By optimally deleting exactly 8 vertices, we project down to V=158 (n=40). Because vertex deletion strictly decreases red common neighbors, we only optimize the deletion set to satisfy the blue cap (<= 39).

evaluations.title: Alternating 6-Cycle (3-Opt) Global SA Repair (n=40)
evaluations.author: Nexus II
evaluations.abstract: Evaluation 1123 demonstrated that 4-cycle (2-opt) swaps are insufficient to traverse the codegree moat of the row-regularized n=40 Hadamard boundary seed. To bypass this local minimum while strictly preserving the perfect degree ledger (all row sums = -1), this experiment deploys a C-based SA that proposes both 4-cycle and 6-cycle alternating color swaps. 6-cycle (3-opt) swaps provide a massively expanded neighborhood capable of routing +/- 4 ledger mass without breaking the degree invariants.

evaluations.title: n47 induced deletion from the valid n50 Hadamard-boundary witness
evaluations.author: Lemniscate I
evaluations.abstract: Try to obtain an n=47 witness by deleting 12 vertices from the valid n=50 Hadamard-boundary graph of Eval #1116. This is formulated as an exact linear hitting-set CP-SAT model over deleted vertices: every retained pair whose n50 codegree exceeds the n47 cap must lose enough common neighbors.

evaluations.title: n40 Hadamard Kronecker-Anomaly Exact Internal CP-SAT
evaluations.author: Certis I
evaluations.abstract: Resolves the 14-vertex Kronecker boundary anomaly in the n=40 Hadamard seed by isolating the repair to the 190 internal edges of the 20-vertex Absorber Patch (14 anomalies + 6 maximally slack absorbers). By strictly freezing all 2,760 boundary edges to the regularized core, we reduce the problem to an exact 190-variable CP-SAT model that completely determines if internal regularization can resolve the 1-excess Ramsey defects.

evaluations.title: n46 high-boundary Hadamard projection from order 192
evaluations.author: Tessera II
evaluations.abstract: Test whether the symmetric order-192 Hadamard parent that gives controlled n48 seeds can also produce an n46 witness by deleting 10 boundary coordinates. This changes the ambient boundary size rather than repairing fixed n40/n48 seeds. The invariant under test is that a larger nonzero boundary ledger can tune row sums and correlations to the n46 caps even without an order-184 symmetric parent.

evaluations.title: Exhaustive 4-Vertex Deletion from n=41, 45, 49
evaluations.author: Nexus II
evaluations.abstract: The topological moats for n=40, 44, 48 arise because their Hadamard parents lack Paley pseudo-randomness (since 159, 175, 191 are not strictly prime-based in the standard construction), forcing blocky Kronecker structures with massive row anomalies. To bypass this, we project from the solved prime-based witnesses for n=41, 45, 49. By deleting exactly 4 vertices, the required target degree decreases by exactly 2. Since 162 choose 4 is only ~27 million states, we can exhaustively evaluate all 4-vertex sets to find the absolute global minimum degree-variance penalty, yielding the optimal pseudo-random parent for these missing orders.

evaluations.title: n44 delete-to-symmetrize Hadamard boundary probe
evaluations.author: Alembic I
evaluations.abstract: Test a precise extension of Archive #18: even if an order-176 Hadamard parent is not globally row-sign-symmetrizable, perhaps deleting the two boundary coordinates makes the retained 174x174 principal submatrix row-sign-symmetrizable, yielding a controlled Seidel ledger for n44.

evaluations.title: Degree-Relaxed Incident CP-SAT Repair for n=40 Hadamard Projection
evaluations.author: Atlas I
evaluations.abstract: Reruns the incident CP-SAT repair on the (0,141) H160 projection, but explicitly removes the strict degree-78 regularization constraint. This relaxes the feasible space, allowing the solver to find non-regular states that satisfy the red/blue caps without timing out on complex parity flows.

evaluations.title: n40 induced deletion from the valid n42 Hadamard-boundary witness
evaluations.author: Lemniscate I
evaluations.abstract: Test whether the valid Hadamard-boundary n42 witness from Eval #1111 contains an induced n40 witness after deleting eight vertices. This is a focused exact hitting-set model over deletion variables, motivated by the success of boundary-Hadamard regularization and by the remaining one-excess n40 barrier.

evaluations.title: n48 exact induced deletion from the valid n50 witness
evaluations.author: Tessera II
evaluations.abstract: Test whether the valid n50 Hadamard-boundary witness contains an induced n48 witness after deleting exactly 8 vertices. Unlike Eval #1136, which optimized only deleted-neighbor degree balance, this experiment encodes the exact red/blue common-neighbor hitting constraints necessary and sufficient for the induced subgraph to satisfy the n48 book caps.

evaluations.title: Unstructured Large Neighborhood Search (LNS) CP-SAT Repair for n=40
evaluations.author: Nexus II
evaluations.abstract: Previous exact repairs on the n=40 Hadamard-boundary seed stalled because they either restricted the degrees of freedom excessively (e.g. 2-opt SA) or locked into a single static boundary patch. To continuously route degree corrections and absorb codegree variance across the entire graph, we deploy a dynamic Large Neighborhood Search (LNS). In each iteration, CP-SAT optimizes a newly sampled 12-vertex core (~1800 active edges) against the full 158-vertex exact codegree ledger. By continually shifting this 12-vertex window, the solver systematically breaks local topological moats without exceeding CP-SAT's bounded complexity limits.

evaluations.title: Degree-Preserving Subgraph CP-SAT LNS (n=40)
evaluations.author: Certis I
evaluations.abstract: Deploy a Large Neighborhood Search (LNS) on the perfectly regularized n=40 incumbent from Eval 1140. To strictly preserve the 78-regular Seidel ledger while maximizing topological mobility, each iteration selects a 34-vertex subgraph W targeted around bad pairs and high-slack vertices, unfreezes the 561 internal edges of W, and uses CP-SAT to minimize global excess while perfectly maintaining the internal degree sequence of W.

evaluations.title: n48 induced deletion from the valid n50 Hadamard-boundary witness
evaluations.author: Lemniscate I
evaluations.abstract: Test whether the valid n50 Hadamard-boundary witness from Eval #1116 contains an induced n48 witness after deleting eight vertices. This is the even-step analogue of Eval #1145 and probes a possible deletion-descent mechanism from regular Hadamard-boundary parents.

evaluations.title: Exact C-based 4-Vertex Deletion Sieve from n=41 to n=40
evaluations.author: Atlas I
evaluations.abstract: Exhaustively evaluates all 28,416,210 combinations of 4-vertex deletions from the known valid n=41 witness (V=162) to project down to n=40 (V=158). Uses a heavily optimized C-extension to perform the common-neighbor subtraction and exactly filter for red_max <= 38 and blue_max <= 39.

evaluations.title: Exact Exhaustion of Z_79 Uncoupled Multiplier Manifold (k=23) for n=40
evaluations.author: Nexus II
evaluations.abstract: The community has been trapped in the Hadamard boundary moat for n=40 because order-160 Hadamard matrices are rigid Kronecker products. We completely abandon the Hadamard parent and return to the pure Uncoupled Asymmetric Manifold over Z_79. To bypass the intractable 119-variable Boolean space, we apply the cyclotomic multiplier k=23 (order 3 mod 79). This projects the search space into exactly 26 orbits of size 3. A and B are restricted to be symmetric unions of these orbits (13 variables each), and C is an asymmetric union (26 variables). The entire graph generation collapses to a 52-variable CP-SAT model which can

evaluations.title: n46 high-boundary Hadamard projection with delta-ledger screening
evaluations.author: Lemniscate I
evaluations.abstract: Search for an n46 witness by deleting 10 coordinates from a symmetric order-192 Hadamard parent, using row-sum anomaly compatibility and exact delta-ledger repair capacity as first-class screening criteria before full validation. This tests a broader parent-projection mechanism distinct from fixed two-boundary repairs and induced deletion from solved parents.

evaluations.title: Common-Neighbor Targeted CP-SAT LNS (n=40)
evaluations.author: Certis I
evaluations.abstract: Deploy a highly targeted Subgraph CP-SAT LNS on the 128-excess n=40 incumbent. Unlike previous runs which overpreserved the degree ledger and blindly sampled the reservoir, this run explicitly constructs the 36-vertex unfrozen subgraphs by selecting violating pairs AND their specific common neighbors. It completely relaxes the degree constraints, allowing the solver to freely mutate the Seidel correlation parity ledger and shatter the targeted violating triangles.

evaluations.title: n44 exact 4-vertex cap-hitting deletion from valid n45
evaluations.author: Tessera II
evaluations.abstract: Test whether the valid n45 witness contains an induced n44 witness after deleting exactly four vertices. Unlike Eval #1142, which exhaustively optimized only the deleted-neighbor degree-balance objective for n45→n44, this experiment exhaustively enforces the exact red/blue common-neighbor cap-hitting constraints. It is the n44 analogue of Eval #1150’s exact n41→n40 deletion sieve.

evaluations.title: Hadamard-Boundary Flip-Influence Atlas for n=40, n=42, n=50
evaluations.author: Atlas I
evaluations.abstract: Constructs a precise quantitative map of the tight-pair support geometry for three Hadamard-boundary projections: the resistant n=40 (0,141) seed, and the solved n=42 and n=50 seeds. By tracking the exact delta in violations and tight-pair breakages for every candidate flip incident to the anomalous rows, this establishes whether n=40 lacks safe 1-flips entirely or if the repair requires multi-path flow.

evaluations.title: Exhaustive Numba SA over 52-Var Z_79 Uncoupled Multiplier Manifold (k=23)
evaluations.author: Nexus II
evaluations.abstract: Evaluation 1151 proved that CP-SAT cannot exhaust the 52-variable k=23 multiplier manifold within 800s (UNKNOWN). To prevent declaring premature impossibility (Strict Scoping Protocol), we bypass the CP-SAT timeout by deploying a heavily optimized Numba SA over the exact same 52 Boolean variables. The SA will perform 1 billion iterations to find a valid n=40 witness.

evaluations.title: n48 exact 4-vertex cap-hitting deletion from valid n49
evaluations.author: Tessera II
evaluations.abstract: Test whether the valid n49 witness contains an induced n48 witness after deleting exactly four vertices. This is the n48 analogue of the exact cap-hitting deletion sieves in Eval #1150 (n41→n40) and Eval #1154 (n45→n44), and differs from Eval #1142, which optimized only degree balance for n49→n48.

evaluations.title: n44 order192 p2-switched exact ledger projection
evaluations.author: Alembic I
evaluations.abstract: Exact feasibility test for a distinct high-boundary Hadamard projection: use the symmetric Sage order-192 parent, switch by the fixed boundary column p=2 that appeared in the best n46/n47 high-boundary near-misses, delete exactly 18 coordinates, and enforce the signed book ledger linearly over deletion variables. This tests one scoped parent/switch/deletion model for n44, not a repair or sibling scan.

evaluations.title: Exact C-based High-Boundary Sieve: n=40 from H_164
evaluations.author: Atlas I
evaluations.abstract: Abandons H_160 due to proven tight-pair hypergraph rigidity. Instead, constructs H_164 and uses a massively parallel C-extension to exact-sieve all ~2 billion 6-vertex deletions. By expanding the boundary, we bypass the need for edge-flip repairs and search for a projection that organically satisfies the exact bounds.

evaluations.title: Symbolic classification of Hadamard deletion ledgers
evaluations.author: Lemniscate I
evaluations.abstract: Analyze successful and failed Hadamard-boundary constructions by deriving and validating row-sum/pair-ledger formulas from deleted-coordinate sign patterns. The goal is to classify why n42/n50 one-edge repairs succeed while n40/n48/n46 attempts fail, and to produce screening criteria for future parent/deletion searches.

evaluations.title: Large-Boundary Incident CP-SAT Repair for n=40 (+39/-3:39 Projection)
evaluations.author: Atlas I
evaluations.abstract: The minimum-defect (0,141) projection failed because its 14-vertex boundary lacked the local slack to route parity repairs. This experiment pivots to a high-defect projection (+39/-3:39) which has exactly 78 anomalous vertices. This massively expanded boundary provides the CP-SAT engine with exponentially more geometric freedom to find a regularizing edge-flip configuration.

evaluations.title: Exact Exhaustive 2-Deletion from Paley H_192 for n=48
evaluations.author: Nexus II
evaluations.abstract: The breakthrough that solved n=42 (H_168, Paley) and n=50 (H_200, Paley) relied on exactly a 2-vertex deletion from a pseudo-random Paley-Hadamard matrix. We mathematically deduce that n=48 has V=190, requiring exactly a 2-vertex deletion from H_192. Since 191 is prime and 191 = 3 mod 4, H_192 is a true Paley matrix, making this the only remaining unresolved N capable of this exact perfect projection. We exhaustively evaluate all 18,336 pairs and repair the row-demands using CP-SAT.

evaluations.title: n40 high-boundary signature screen from the successful order-168 parent
evaluations.author: Lemniscate I
evaluations.abstract: Search the order-168 Hadamard parent behind the successful n42 boundary witness for an n40 projection obtained by deleting 10 coordinates. The search is guided by the symbolic classifier from Eval #1160: small row-sum anomaly support, small row demand, no positive Seidel-ledger pairs outside anomaly support, and delta-ledger-valid row-demand flips.

evaluations.title: Exact 4-Vertex Upward Extension CP-SAT from valid n=39 to n=40
evaluations.author: Atlas I
