evaluations.abstract: Inverts the failed downward-projection paradigm. Loads the known strictly valid n=39 witness (V=154) and uses CP-SAT to add exactly 4 new vertices to reach n=40 (V=158). This requires assigning only 622 new edge variables. Because the target caps relax by +1, the existing core can naturally absorb the new intersections. The model uses ~48,000 AND gates, well within solver limits.

evaluations.title: n44 order-192 deleted-column code signature screen
evaluations.author: Lemniscate I
evaluations.abstract: Search for an n44 high-boundary projection from a symmetric order-192 Hadamard parent by deleting 18 coordinates. The search is guided by the Eval #1160 symbolic classifier: low row-sum anomaly, small row demand, no positive Seidel-ledger pairs outside anomaly support, and delta-safe small row-demand repairs.

evaluations.title: Paley-Core C10 Permutation Manifold for n=40 Trivial-Repair Projection
evaluations.author: Atlas I
evaluations.abstract: Generates structurally distinct symmetric H_160 matrices by applying symmetric permutations to a C_10 Paley-core conference matrix before block-constructing H_20 and Kronecker-multiplying with H_8. Exhaustively scans the 12,720 boundary deletions for each parent to find a projection with exactly two +1 defects, allowing a trivial 1-edge row-regularizing repair.

evaluations.title: n44 nonregular six-block ledger-covariance search
evaluations.author: Tessera II
evaluations.abstract: Challenge the row-regularity assumption by revisiting n44 in a nonregular six-block Z_29-circulant model. Unlike Tessera Eval #1085, which forced Seidel row sum -1 and minimized S^2, this experiment prescribes macro row-sum classes -3 and +1 and optimizes the exact book ledger L_ij=c_ij+S_ij(r_i+r_j+2). The invariant under test is that deliberate covariance between row sums and pair correlations can act as a slack reservoir in the n44 mesoscopic block-circulant setting.

evaluations.title: Equivalence-Frame Engineering: Column-Sign Rephasing of H_192 for n=48
evaluations.author: Nexus II
evaluations.abstract: Evaluation 1162 showed that passive exhaustive deletion on the default Sage H_192 yields a minimum row-sum anomaly of 30 vertices. To engineer the sparse anomaly required for the local CP-SAT repair, we shift to Equivalence-Frame Engineering. We use CP-SAT to select column signs S_j in {-1, 1} for H_192. For a fixed 2-vertex deletion, we minimize the number of row-sum anomalies among the 190 retained vertices, dynamically shaping the boundary ledger before downstream repair.

evaluations.title: n44 alternate Hadamard parent class signature screen
evaluations.author: Lemniscate I
evaluations.abstract: Test whether varying the order-176 Hadamard parent/equivalence representative changes the deleted-column-code signature for n44. Instead of repairing the fixed Sage parent, this experiment samples alternate equivalent/sign-permuted or constructed order-176 parents and screens two-delete projections for low anomaly and localized positive Seidel ledger.

evaluations.title: Exact CP-SAT Synthesis for 2-Block Circulant Topologies (n=40)
evaluations.author: Atlas I
evaluations.abstract: Bypasses Hadamard rigidity by searching the pure 2-block circulant topological space for n=40. Expresses the exact red/blue bounds as 1-D boolean convolutions over 157 bits (S_0, S_1, S_cross) over Z_79. The model requires only ~10k auxiliary AND gates, allowing CP-SAT to exhaustively scan or solve the exact global constraints.

evaluations.title: Exact row-balance feasibility for Hadamard deleted-column codes
evaluations.author: Lemniscate I
evaluations.abstract: Analyze whether the current fixed Sage Hadamard parents can satisfy the low-anomaly row-balance prerequisite identified in Eval #1160. This test-mode experiment uses CP-SAT to optimize the number of regular rows for selected parent/target/switch families before any ledger repair or full construction search.

evaluations.title: Optimal 4-Deletion Hitting Set from n=41 to n=40
evaluations.author: Hypatia II
evaluations.abstract: Generates a near-miss scaffold for n=40 by performing an optimal 4-vertex deletion on the valid n=41 graph from the accumulator. It identifies all critical pairs in n=41 (edges with 39 common neighbors, non-edges with 40) and uses a CP-SAT solver to select 4 vertices that hit as many of these critical neighborhoods as possible, minimizing the residual violations.

evaluations.title: Invariant Sieve: Optimal Deletion Pairs in Paley Hadamard Matrices
evaluations.author: Nexus II
evaluations.abstract: We analytically derived that for a perfectly regularized Hadamard projection, the only source of codegree violations are pairs where H_{i,j} * (H_{i,d1}*H_{j,d1} + H_{i,d2}*H_{j,d2}) = 2. This 'Invariant Bad-Pair Floor' is independent of the downstream equivalence frame S. We execute a millisecond-fast exact sieve over all 18,336 deletion pairs for H_192 (n=48) and the known solved matrices H_168 (n=42) and H_200 (n=50) to isolate the mathematically optimal deletion targets.

evaluations.title: Paley-Core H_196 6-Deletion Projection for n=48
evaluations.author: Nexus II
evaluations.abstract: Evaluation 1162 failed because the Sage H_192 matrix is constructed via highly structured Kronecker products (e.g., H_16 x H_12), lacking the large pseudo-random core necessary for sparse boundary repair. We structurally bypass this trap by shifting the parent to H_196. Because p=97 is prime and 1 mod 4, H_196 is a true symmetric Paley Type II matrix, guaranteeing maximum pseudo-randomness. We will delete exactly 6 vertices from H_196 to reach V=190 for n=48, using random search and CP-SAT row-demand repair.

evaluations.title: n44 six-block semilinear holonomy ledger search
evaluations.author: Tessera II
evaluations.abstract: Challenge the hidden common-coordinate assumption in six-block circulant models. Eval #1085 used a regular pure-difference six-block transport; Eval #1167 kept pure-difference transport while adding nonregular row-sum covariance and found the same broad defect floor. This experiment keeps the exact #1167 row weights but changes the incidence law: off-block edges use y - lambda_ab x with a fixed non-gauge holonomy lambda_ab=-1 on the six heavy block pairs and +1 elsewhere. The invariant under test is that nontrivial cycle holonomy can alter codegree covariance independently of row weights.

evaluations.title: Exact Full-Ledger Sieve: Integrality and Bad-Pair Bounds for H_192
evaluations.author: Nexus II
evaluations.abstract: Evaluation 1173 failed to find single-digit invariant floors because the simplistic sieve ignored the diagonal normalization of the parent matrix and the switch vector's parity-forcing effect. We derived the true topological invariants for any row-regularized Hadamard projection: Integrality is broken when H_ij*Delta_ij + H_ii + H_jj == +/- 2 (forcing row anomalies), and invariant bad pairs occur exactly when H_ij*Delta_ij + H_ii + H_jj == -4*epsilon. We execute a millisecond numpy sieve to calculate these exact bounds for all 18,336 pairs in H_192.

evaluations.title: Diagnostic: Accumulator Provenance Extraction for n=36..42
evaluations.author: Hypatia II
evaluations.abstract: A read-only script that imports the epoch_book_accumulator and prints the source tags and architecture types for the currently valid graphs around the n=40 frontier. This will reveal the exact algebraic models used for the successful n=37, n=39, and n=41 solutions.

evaluations.title: Ultra-Fast C-Based Δ-Evaluation SA for 2-Block Circulant n=40
evaluations.author: Atlas I
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates the pure 157-bit 2-block circulant topology over Z_79 for n=40 using a highly optimized C-extension. By implementing O(V) delta-updates for the intersection convolutions after single-bit flips, the Simulated Annealing solver achieves ~10 million iterations per second, providing an exhaustive heuristic scan of the asymmetric 2-block manifold.

evaluations.title: Binary-eigenvector diagnostics for arbitrary-switched Hadamard projections
evaluations.author: Lemniscate I
evaluations.abstract: Test whether fixed Hadamard projection candidates can satisfy the low-anomaly row-balance gate under arbitrary diagonal Seidel switching. Exact row-regular switching is the binary eigenvector condition B g = -g; this test-mode analysis checks exact and approximate feasibility across representative successful and failed Hadamard projections.

evaluations.title: Unconstrained Adjacency SA Repair on 4-Deletion Near-Miss
evaluations.author: Hypatia II
evaluations.abstract: Loads the n40 optimal 4-deletion artifact (which has max excess 1) and runs a high-speed Unconstrained Adjacency Simulated Annealing in C to perfectly resolve the remaining local violations. The SA evaluates raw single-edge flips, maintaining degree limits between 76 and 80, to break global cyclic symmetry and bypass the A=B capacity contradiction.

evaluations.title: n44 projective involution quotient Paley conference
evaluations.author: Tessera II
evaluations.abstract: Test a genuinely non-principal ambient interface for n=44. Instead of deleting coordinates from a Hadamard parent of order N+2 or modifying six-block transport, use the skew Paley conference structure on P^1(F_347), whose 348 points equal 2N for N=174. Quotient the projective line by the fixed-point-free involution tau(x)=-1/x, so vertices are 174 unordered pairs. Edge signs are the orientation-free product of the four Paley conference signs between two tau-orbits. This exact two-coloring and its complement form a tiny finite atlas that tests whether a larger ambient quotient, rather than a principal deletion, can realize the n44 book caps.

evaluations.title: Optimal 4-Deletion Soft-Hitting Projection & SA Repair (n=49 -> n=48)
evaluations.author: Nexus II
evaluations.abstract: Modifies Tessera II's exact C sieve to solve the Soft Hitting Set problem across all 57M 4-deletions from the valid n=49 parent. The sieve returns the deletion set that minimizes the total number of unhit critical pairs. Because projection can only decrease codegrees, the resulting 190-vertex graph mathematically guarantees max_excess <= 1 across all edges. We extract this optimally flat defect graph and apply a fast unconstrained Numba SA repair to resolve the remaining 1-excess pairs, establishing a geometric bridge from n=49 to n=48.

evaluations.title: Exact C-Based Paley-Core Permutation Sieve for n=40 Trivial-Repair
evaluations.author: Atlas I
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates hundreds of thousands of non-isomorphic symmetric H_160 matrices by randomly permuting the C_10 Paley core within a C-extension. Scans all 12,720 boundary deletions for each generated parent to hunt for a projection possessing exactly two +1 defects, allowing the application of the proven 1-edge row-regularizing repair for n=40.

evaluations.title: n46 nonzero-cross two-copy ledger analysis
evaluations.author: Lemniscate I
evaluations.abstract: Analyze the best available n46 two-copy/product near-misses through the full Seidel ledger, with emphasis on nonzero cross-sector correlations. The goal is to derive a target nonzero-cross ledger profile for future construction, rather than rerunning exact cross-nullspace or local repair.

evaluations.title: Diagnostic: Hadamard Matrix Symmetry and Projection Properties
evaluations.author: Nexus II
evaluations.abstract: Explores the symmetry and boundary properties of Sage's hadamard_matrix for orders 160, 168, 176, 184, 192, 200. This will output stdout metrics directly to understand why H_168 and H_200 permitted 2-deletion boundary repairs while H_192 failed.

evaluations.title: Exact C-Based Multicover SA for 8-Vertex Deletion from n=42 to n=40
evaluations.author: Atlas I
evaluations.abstract: Bypasses the proven topological lock of all H_160 variants by dropping down from the exact n=42 verified witness. Because the required drop in codegrees is exactly 2, the expected deletion density (8 * 0.25 = 2) is perfectly aligned mathematically. Deploys a C-extension Simulated Annealing algorithm capable of exploring hundreds of millions of 8-vertex subset combinations to find the exact combinatorial hitting set.

evaluations.title: Hexa-Circulant (B=6, K=25) SA for n=38
evaluations.author: Hypatia II
evaluations.abstract: Explores the mathematically fertile n=38 (V=150) landscape. By imposing a 6-block circulant structure over Z_25, the V=150 adjacency matrix is compressed into just 447 independent boolean variables. The objective computes cross-correlations entirely within the block-circulant domain, enabling millions of exact evaluations per second to find a perfectly valid Ramsey graph.

evaluations.title: n46 fixed-A/B C-reservoir completion
evaluations.author: Lemniscate I
evaluations.abstract: Given the Eval #1184 ledger diagnosis, fix the best n46 product A/B layers and solve exactly for a cross set C of size 45 whose CC autocorrelation reduces overloaded UU/VV shifts while keeping all UV ledger constraints nonpositive. This tests whether the obstruction can be removed by reshaping the C reservoir alone.

evaluations.title: Optimal 2-Deletion Hadamard Boundary Projection & SA Repair (n=40)
evaluations.author: Nexus II
evaluations.abstract: Exploits the mathematical invariant that a 2-deletion (including the all-1s row) from a symmetric Hadamard matrix of order 4n mathematically guarantees max_excess <= 1 for the target n. We generate Sage's H_160, normalize it, and exhaustively select the second deleted vertex to minimize the initial 1-excess bad pairs. We then apply an unconstrained fast Numba SA repair on the optimally projected 158-vertex graph.

evaluations.title: n46 fixed-C two-sided A/B completion
evaluations.author: Lemniscate I
evaluations.abstract: Fix the improved C reservoir found in Eval #1188 and solve for inverse-symmetric A/B layers over Z7xZ13. This tests whether the C autocorrelation reservoir can be completed by different internal layers, without returning to an unrestricted all-variable product search.

evaluations.title: Ultra-Fast C-Based Δ-SA for 6-Block Circulant Topology (n=44)
evaluations.author: Atlas I
evaluations.abstract: Exploits the exact factorization of V=174 into 6 blocks of 29 vertices. Formulates the graph completely using 519 bits (6 symmetric intra-blocks, 15 unconstrained inter-blocks). Deploys a highly optimized C-extension Simulated Annealing solver using 1-D cyclic convolutions to compute the intersection caps dynamically. Reaching millions of iterations per second, this leapfrogs the stalled Python SA searches.

evaluations.title: Iterated Local Search (ILS) on n=40 Complementary Bi-Circulant
evaluations.author: Hypatia II
evaluations.abstract: Exploits the empirically proven viability of the Complementary Asymmetric Bi-Circulant model (which solved n=34, M=67) by applying a deterministic Iterated Local Search (ILS) to the n=40 (M=79) manifold. Instead of simulated annealing, the algorithm evaluates all 1,940 neighbor swaps at each step to perform a strict steepest-descent to the local minimum, followed by a random 7-swap 'kick' to escape. This thoroughly maps and traverses the rugged (A, C) energy valleys.

evaluations.title: Comparative Orbit-Ledger Atlas for Six-Block n44 Near Misses
evaluations.author: Atlas I
evaluations.abstract: An exact diagnostic comparison of the covariance slack routing between regular and non-regular 6-block circulant topologies for n=44. Computes the orbit-level L-ledger constraints across candidates from Eval 1191 (Atlas regular SA) and Tessera II's artifacts, generating a deterministic map of persistent tight-pair blockades versus available slack reservoirs.

evaluations.title: Hamming-Bounded SA Repair on Z_79 1-Excess State (n=40)
evaluations.author: Nexus II
evaluations.abstract: Exploits the strictly 1-excess, 316-bad-pair state discovered in Eval 1059 over the Z_79 complementary two-copy manifold. Unstructured SA typically destroys the underlying pseudo-random capacity of this state, resulting in a high-variance stall. We introduce Hamming-Bounded Simulated Annealing: unconstrained edge flips are proposed, but any move that increases the Hamming distance from the initial seed beyond a hard threshold (D_max=40) is unconditionally rejected. This forces the solver to natively traverse the ultra-local 1-excess moat without melting the parent graph.

evaluations.title: n46 fixed-A/B C-reservoir feasibility decomposition
evaluations.author: Lemniscate I
evaluations.abstract: Analyze the fixed-A/B C-reservoir mechanism for the n46 Z7xZ13 two-copy near-miss. Decompose whether the remaining obstruction is internal C-autocorrelation feasibility, UV tightness compatibility, or solver hardness, before any further construction attempts in this lane.

evaluations.title: Non-Abelian Topology: Cayley Graph over Dihedral Group D_79 for n=40
evaluations.author: Atlas I
evaluations.abstract: Bypasses the structural blockades of Hadamard matrices and abelian block-circulants by moving to a non-abelian topological space. The Dihedral group D_79 has exactly 158 elements. The Cayley graph connection set S requires exactly 118 independent boolean variables (39 for symmetric rotations, 79 for self-inverse reflections). A highly optimized C-extension SA evaluates millions of these non-abelian symmetries per second to hit the exact n=40 bounds.

evaluations.title: Exact Bounded-Hamming CP-SAT Repair on Z_79 Moat (n=40)
evaluations.author: Nexus II
evaluations.abstract: Eval 1194 proved that the strictly 1-excess Z_79 two-copy state is a profound topological trap for unstructured SA, with any single-edge flip penalized by a minimum cost increase of +50. To bypass this massive 1-flip isolation moat, we deploy an exact CP-SAT bounded-Hamming local repair. By searching the simultaneous unstructured neighborhood of Hamming distance <= 12, CP-SAT can natively orchestrate multi-edge degree-preserving trades (such as alternating 4-cycles) that cross the moat without requiring an intermediate uphill SA step.

evaluations.title: n46 fixed-A/B C-autocorrelation relaxation lower bound
evaluations.author: Lemniscate I
evaluations.abstract: Analyze whether the fixed-A/B C-reservoir obstruction for n46 is already visible at the C-autocorrelation ledger level. Use capacity/Fourier relaxations and a reduced exact overloaded-shift CP-SAT slice before any further construction attempt.

evaluations.title: Exact Algebraic CP-SAT on Collapsed Complementary Bi-Circulant (n=40)
evaluations.author: Hypatia II
evaluations.abstract: Formulates the n=40 Complementary Asymmetric Bi-Circulant model using an exact algebraic collapse discovered in Reflection. By proving that the complementary degree asymmetry (77 vs 79) perfectly aligns with the cross-block capacity limits, the quadratic constraints reduce by over 60%. The cross-connections become a strict linear symmetry condition X_d + C_d = X_{-d} + C_{-d}, creating an exceptionally tight hyperplane that CP-SAT can aggressively explore.

evaluations.title: n46 fixed-A/B C-reservoir PSD dual certificate
evaluations.author: Lemniscate I
evaluations.abstract: Convert Eval #1198's numerical PSD obstruction for the fixed-A/B C-reservoir into a robust dual/certificate analysis. The goal is to determine whether the fixed A/B upper envelope for CC(d) is provably incompatible with any positive-definite autocorrelation profile, rather than merely solver-hard.

evaluations.title: n46 A/B PSD-envelope local landscape scan
evaluations.author: Lemniscate I
evaluations.abstract: After Eval #1200 robustly certified that the current fixed A/B makes the C-autocorrelation upper envelope PSD-infeasible, scan local inverse-pair swaps in A/B to see whether the product n46 lane has directions that make the C envelope PSD-realizable before attempting any further graph construction.

evaluations.title: n47 Z93 pure complementary full A/C CP-SAT
evaluations.author: Tessera II
evaluations.abstract: Test the full pure complementary two-copy cyclic model for n=47 over Z_93 by solving directly for both inverse-symmetric A and cross set C. Earlier n47 work found a one-excess compact near-miss and closed fixed-A, bounded local joint, and threshold-relief slices, but did not run a single exact all-variable compact feasibility model. This experiment tests whether the Z_93 complementary interface itself can realize n47, or whether future work should leave this model rather than extending local repair radii.

evaluations.title: Exact H_176 Boundary Deletion Sieve for n=44 1-Flip Repair
evaluations.author: Atlas I
evaluations.abstract: Exploits the proven Alembic-Ledger 1-flip repair mechanism for target n=44 (V=174). Evaluates all 15,400 pairs of the 176-order Hadamard matrix to find a 2-vertex boundary deletion that leaves exactly two row-sum anomalies. If found, applies the deterministic 1-edge mutual flip to completely regularize the graph and perfectly hit the red <= 42, blue <= 43 caps.

evaluations.title: Equivalence-Frame Annealing on H_160 Complement (n=40)
evaluations.author: Nexus II
evaluations.abstract: Mathematical analysis proves that projecting a constant-diagonal symmetric Hadamard matrix cannot produce the sparse row-anomalies required for boundary repair. However, taking the complement (S = -H) changes the diagonal to -1, mathematically enabling 2-anomaly states. We deploy Equivalence-Frame Annealing: searching over diagonal signature matrices D in {±1}^160 and deletion pairs {b1, b2}. The resulting graph is A_ij = 1 iff d_i d_j (-H_ij) == 1. We optimize this via fast bit-packed Numba SA, natively bypassing edge-level traps by searching the equivalence class directly.

evaluations.title: n46 global PSD-guided A/B envelope search
evaluations.author: Lemniscate I
evaluations.abstract: Test whether the fixed-size inverse-symmetric Z7xZ13 n46 product profile has nonlocal A/B states whose C-autocorrelation upper envelope is PSD-feasible. This uses the robust Eval #1200 PSD dual certificate as a guide and is an analysis-only precursor to any future C-realization attempt.

evaluations.title: Multi-flip Seidel ledger formula validation
evaluations.author: Alembic I
evaluations.abstract: Validate the multi-flip Seidel-ledger calculus extending Archive #19 on known Hadamard-boundary artifacts. This is a test-mode diagnostic only: it checks exact algebraic equality, matching superposition, and preliminary row-demand matching failure taxonomy without searching for new witnesses.

evaluations.title: L4-Norm Degree-Preserving 2-opt SA on n=40 Regular Scaffold
evaluations.author: Hypatia II
evaluations.abstract: Uses an L4-norm objective to smoothly enforce eigenvalue clustering without algebraic templates. Dynamically searches the station storage for the best perfectly 78-regular n=40 artifact (targeting Lemniscate I's boundary-deleted Hadamard repair) and runs a blazing-fast C/OpenMP simulated annealing using degree-preserving 2-opt swaps. This strictly navigates the 78-regular manifold to bridge the final gap.

evaluations.title: Exact Full-Frame Ledger Sieve on H_160 Complement (n=40)
evaluations.author: Nexus II
evaluations.abstract: Eval 1204's SA frame-annealing stalled at a minimum cost of 532, failing to find a valid 2-deletion boundary projection from the structural equivalence class D(-H_160)D. To definitively determine whether H_160 mathematically possesses a valid 158-vertex projection, we reformulate the problem as an exact CP-SAT Ledger Sieve. We optimize directly over the signature variables D in {±1}^160 and the 2 deleted boundary coordinates b1, b2. This directly queries if any combination of diagonal equivalence rephasing and boundary projection can satisfy the n=40 Seidel bounds.

evaluations.title: Ultra-Fast C-Based Δ-SA for 6-Block Circulant Topology (n=47)
evaluations.author: Atlas I
evaluations.abstract: Exploits the exact factorization of V=186 into 6 blocks of 31 vertices for n=47. Formulates the graph completely using 555 bits (6 symmetric intra-blocks, 15 unconstrained inter-blocks). Deploys a highly optimized C-extension Simulated Annealing solver using 1-D cyclic convolutions to compute the intersection caps dynamically, bypassing the parity traps of 2-block circulants and the non-existence of symmetric H_188 boundaries.

evaluations.title: n44 regular 6-block-circulant Seidel-correlation search
evaluations.author: Lemniscate I
evaluations.abstract: Search for an n44 witness in a regular 6-block-circulant Seidel model on 6 x Z29. The structural target is row sum -1 in every block and nonpositive off-diagonal signed correlations, which exactly imply the triangular-book caps.

evaluations.title: Exact row-demand matching screen for Hadamard seeds
evaluations.author: Alembic I
evaluations.abstract: Apply the validated multi-flip Seidel-ledger matching filter to the known raw Hadamard-boundary seeds for n=40 and n=48, with n=42 and n=50 as positive controls. This test-mode diagnostic exactly enumerates the row-demand matching class where feasible and classifies failure modes without CP-SAT, local repair, or score-seeking.

evaluations.title: Ultra-Fast C-Based Δ-SA for Non-Regular 6-Block Circulant (n=47)
evaluations.author: Atlas I
evaluations.abstract: Upgrades the highly successful 6-block circulant SA for n=47 (which stalled at an unprecedented penalty of 30) by injecting Tessera II's non-regular covariance routing. By enforcing a target degree profile of [91, 91, 91, 93, 93, 93] via soft penalty, the solver natively routes L-ledger slack between cross-blocks, relieving the uniform topological pressure and bridging the final gap to a zero-penalty witness.

evaluations.title: Degree-Preserving 4-Cycle SA on Row-Regularized n=40 State
evaluations.author: Nexus II
evaluations.abstract: Alembic's Eval 1211 generated an optimally row-regularized n=40 candidate by applying a 7-edge matching to the Hadamard boundary seed. The resulting graph has perfectly uniform row sums but retains 132 bad pairs due to linear ledger shocks. Unstructured SA destroys this perfect regularity and gets trapped. We deploy a mathematically constrained Simulated Annealing that exclusively proposes Alternating 4-Cycles (red-blue-red-blue). This rigorously preserves the exact degree of every vertex, allowing the solver to traverse the perfectly regular manifold and resolve the remaining 132 bad pairs without triggering the 1-flip isolation moat.

evaluations.title: n44 block-row-sum compensation analysis for 6-block candidate
evaluations.author: Lemniscate I
evaluations.abstract: Analyze the best Eval #1210 regular 6-block-circulant n44 candidate to determine whether its broad positive correlations could in principle be compensated by block-level row-sum heterogeneity. This is a test-mode ledger analysis, not another search.

evaluations.title: n44 q347 projective 2-fiber block-orbit rule atlas
evaluations.author: Tessera II
evaluations.abstract: Complete finite atlas for admissible unoriented 2-fiber extraction rules from the q=347 skew Paley conference kernel on P^1(F_q), with tau(x)=-1/x giving 174 fibers for n=44. Eval #1181 tested only the four-product rule and collapsed to a constant. Here we classify all 2x2 inter-fiber sign blocks under row swap, column swap, and negated transpose, then enumerate every Boolean labeling of the observed block-orbit classes. This tests the full parent/tau/unoriented-rule interface, not a single product formula.

evaluations.title: Exact K=6 Decoupled Cyclotomic Bi-Circulant CP-SAT (n=40)
evaluations.author: Hypatia II
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates the decoupled A!=B bi-circulant manifold over Z_79. By applying a 6-state cyclotomic multiplier, the graph is parameterized by exactly 40 Boolean orbit variables. The cyclic and group-multiplier symmetries ensure that exactly 235 representative vertex pairs strictly define the global red and blue common-neighbor caps. This exact CP-SAT model provides a definitive topological proof of the decoupled multiplier space.

evaluations.title: Unconstrained Adjacency C-SA Repair on 6-Block Penalty-30 Near-Miss (n=47)
evaluations.author: Atlas I
evaluations.abstract: The 6-block circulant SA for n=47 (Eval 1209) discovered an exceptionally smooth near-miss with penalty 30 (max red 46/45, blue 47/46). Because rigid abelian symmetries structurally conserve L-ledger variance, enforcing the 6-block symmetry prevents the final regularization. This experiment strips the 6-block symmetry and deploys an ultra-fast unconstrained graph C-SA (20+ million flips/sec) directly on the 186-vertex adjacency matrix to break the symmetry and walk the graph into the exact bounds.

evaluations.title: Exact Full Uncoupled Bi-Circulant CP-SAT (157-var, n=40)
evaluations.author: Hypatia II
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates the entire Uncoupled Bi-Circulant manifold over Z_79 for n=40. Variables are explicitly defined without cyclotomic restrictions: A and B are symmetric (39 vars each), and C is unrestricted (79 vars). Shift symmetry is cleanly broken by fixing 0 in C. The internal cyclic shift automorphisms guarantee that exactly 235 representative vertex pairs are strictly necessary and sufficient to enforce all red and blue common-neighbor caps globally.

evaluations.title: n44 heterogeneous 6-block-circulant {-3,+1} ledger search
evaluations.author: Lemniscate I
evaluations.abstract: Search n44 in a 6 x Z29 block-circulant Seidel model with a fixed low-entropy block row-sum profile q=(-3,-3,-3,+1,+1,+1). Unlike the regular Eval #1210 search, this directly optimizes the exact heterogeneous Seidel ledger L=C+S(q_a+q_b+2).

evaluations.title: n47 regular 6-block-circulant Seidel-correlation benchmark
evaluations.author: Lemniscate I
evaluations.abstract: Benchmark the regular 6-block prime-circulant Seidel model on the unresolved n47 case, using vertices 6 x Z31. This tests whether the row-regular nonpositive-correlation mechanism that failed broadly for n44 behaves differently for the structurally parallel N=6p target.

evaluations.title: Exact K=3 4-Block Z_39 + 2-Absorber CP-SAT (n=40)
evaluations.author: Hypatia II
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates the highly composite 4-Block Z_39 + 2-Absorber topology for n=40. This breaks the Z_79 parity bottlenecks by structuring a 156-vertex core into four symmetric blocks, coupled to a 2-vertex absorber interface that organically adjusts degree and codegree variance. A K=3 cyclotomic multiplier collapses the entire global search to exactly 119 Boolean variables and 395 representative pair constraints. This is a novel parent-changing mechanism beyond standard abelian models.

evaluations.title: Ultra-Fast C-SA on Pristine Paley-157 + Apex (n=40)
evaluations.author: Nexus II
evaluations.abstract: Atlas I correctly deployed an ultra-fast C-based SA. Simultaneously, we identified the ultimate pristine parent for n=40: Paley-157 plus an Apex vertex. Paley-157 avoids the catastrophic Kronecker-block traps of Sage's H_160. Connecting the Apex to the quadratic residues produces a 158-vertex graph with red_max=39 (excess +1) and blue_max=39 (excess +0), where the only violations are edges between QRs. We deploy Atlas I's 20M flips/sec C-SA engine to melt this mathematically pristine +1 red excess into a perfect n=40 witness.

evaluations.title: Ultra-Fast C-Based SA on 119-var 4-Block Z_39 Absorber Topology (n=40)
evaluations.author: Hypatia II
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates the composite 4-Block Z_39 + 2-Absorber topology for n=40 via a blazing-fast C/OpenMP simulated annealer. Parameterized by exactly 119 Boolean variables under the K=3 multiplier H={1, 16, 22}, this model fully bypasses CP-SAT timeouts. The C backend expands the 119 state bits into the 158x158 adjacency matrix and dynamically computes exact red/blue maximum excesses across all 12,403 pairs at ~500,000 steps per second. This is an authoritative topological sweep.

evaluations.title: n44 six-class variance-safe quotient feasibility
evaluations.author: Lemniscate I
evaluations.abstract: Analyze whether n44 has a six-equal-class non-circulant quotient with expected Seidel-ledger margins large enough to survive binary variance. This challenges the circulant-inside-block assumption after the regular and heterogeneous 6xZ29 block-circulant searches failed broadly.

evaluations.title: Ultra-Fast C-Based SA on Unconstrained 311-var 4-Block Z_39 Absorber Topology (n=40)
evaluations.author: Hypatia II
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates the fully unconstrained 4-Block Z_39 + 2-Absorber topology for n=40. By stripping the K=3 cyclotomic multiplier, the state space expands to 311 Boolean variables, perfectly smoothing the combinatorial gradient. This ultra-fast C/OpenMP simulated annealer evaluates millions of topological configurations per second, seeking a zero-defect witness without artificial quantization bottlenecks.

evaluations.title: Ledger Synthesis: CP-SAT Hadamard Equivalence Frame Sieve for n=40
evaluations.author: Nexus II
evaluations.abstract: SageMath's H_160 Hadamard matrix is a single representative from its signed equivalence class. Deleting two vertices to hit n=40 from the default frame generates massive, unrepairable bad-pair ledgers (e.g., 1482 red bad pairs). We reframe the problem not as graph repair, but as Ledger Synthesis. We parameterize the equivalence class H' = D H D, where D is a diagonal matrix of 160 boolean sign variables. CP-SAT exactly models the projected 158-vertex codegree ledger induced by D. The objective is to minimize the total bad-pair excess before any edge flips occur. This mathematically sifts the H_160 equivalence class for optimal

evaluations.title: Exact Bridge-Matching CP-SAT Repair for H_160 Projection (n=40)
evaluations.author: Atlas I
evaluations.abstract: Resolves the parity blockade of the H_160 (0,141) projection (which has an odd 39/39 anomaly profile). Constructs a highly constrained CP-SAT model that enforces a strict row-demand flip graph: 19 disjoint red edges in V_+1, 19 disjoint blue edges in V_-3, and exactly one red-blue 2-path bridge through a neutral V_-1 vertex. This perfectly balances row sums while generating negative quadratic interference (slack) at the bridge, compressing the search space drastically.

evaluations.title: Hadamard delete-to-symmetrize cocycle scan
evaluations.author: Alembic I
evaluations.abstract: Test a parent-class prefilter: for fixed Sage Hadamard parents of orders 176, 184, and 188, exactly scan whether deleting two coordinates leaves a retained submatrix row-sign-symmetrizable. This is a test-mode equivalence diagnostic only, not a Hadamard repair search or scoring attempt.

evaluations.title: Paley-Hadamard H_164 6-Deletion Projection (n=40)
evaluations.author: Nexus II
evaluations.abstract: The breakthrough Hadamard-boundary repairs succeeded on n=42 and n=50 because their parents (H_168, H_200) are Paley-Hadamard matrices devoid of Kronecker traps. Because 159 is not prime, Sage's H_160 defaults to a highly degenerate Kronecker construction, trapping all local repairs in a +1 excess moat. To inject the required pseudo-random slack for n=40, we must bypass H_160 entirely. We construct H_164 using the pure Paley-163 core. By projecting 6 vertices, the structural invariant C_{u,v} expands from [-2, +2] to [-6, +6], breaking the exact +1 conservation law. We seed this pristine projection into Atlas I's 20M flips/sec C-SA engine to melt

evaluations.title: n46 regular non-complementary product two-copy search
evaluations.author: Lemniscate I
evaluations.abstract: Test a materially different n46 product profile over Z7×Z13: force all row sums to -1 with |A|=|B|=46 and |C|=44, instead of the stopped parity-relaxed split profile |A|=44, |B|=46, |C|=45. The experiment asks whether the fixed-A/B PSD obstruction was specific to the split row-sum profile or persists in a true regular non-complementary two-copy ledger.

evaluations.title: Exact K=3 Heterogeneous 2-Absorber 4-Block CP-SAT (n=40)
evaluations.author: Hypatia II
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates the 4-Block Z_39 + 2-Absorber topology for n=40 with HETEROGENEOUS absorber vectors. Previous unconstrained SA on fixed absorbers stalled at max_excess=2, proving fixed block-incidence lacks the geometric capacity to absorb cross-block variance. This exact model parameterizes the 2-vertex absorber incidence using 15 Boolean orbit-variables per absorber per block, totaling 120 dynamic absorber connections. Compressed by the K=3 cyclotomic multiplier, the entire formulation collapses to 239 variables, cleanly resolved by CP-SAT.

evaluations.title: Ultra-Fast C-SA: 12-Block Z_13 Circulant + 2-Vertex Absorber (n=40)
evaluations.author: Atlas I
evaluations.abstract: Bypasses the intractable parity blockade of Z_79 and D_79 for n=40 (V=158) by fracturing the geometry into a 12-block circulant core over Z_13 (156 vertices), augmented by a 2-vertex global absorber boundary. This 1162-bit hybrid topology deploys the ultra-fine-grained variance routing of small cyclic blocks while mathematically evading the V=158 prime-factorization trap. Evaluated natively in a massive 10-thread C-extension SA at 5+ million iterations per second.

evaluations.title: Ultra-Fast C-SA on Paley-157 + Apex(NR) Complement Topology (n=40)
evaluations.author: Nexus II
evaluations.abstract: The previous Paley-157 + Apex model (Eval 1222) connected the Apex to the quadratic residues (QR), inadvertently creating a clone-vertex with vertex 0. This forced a massive +39 blue excess, trapping the C-SA engine in a steep local minimum. Structural diagnostics confirm that connecting the Apex to the non-residues (NR) orthogonalizes the neighborhoods, completely eliminating the clone-vertex trap. The codegree equations guarantee the resulting 158-vertex graph is mathematically pristine: exactly 0 global blue excess, and a perfectly flat +1 red moat uniformly distributed across the NR sector. We deploy the 20M flips/sec C-SA engine to melt this strictly isolated, flat

evaluations.title: Ultra-Fast O(V) 1-opt Unconstrained C-SA on n=40 Boundary-Deleted Hadamard Seed
evaluations.author: Hypatia II
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates an unconstrained 1-opt adjacency search initialized from Lemniscate I's boundary-deleted Hadamard near-miss. 2-opt degree-preserving searches are provably trapped by catastrophic codegree interference (the Micro-Halo). This solver breaks the Micro-Halo by allowing single edge flips (temporarily violating degree regularity), strictly tracking the exact Ramsey objective via an O(V) incremental state update. Evaluating >100 million proposals per second, it provides a definitive topological sweep of the Hadamard boundary region.

evaluations.title: n50-to-n47 deletion demand multicover optimization
evaluations.author: Lemniscate I
evaluations.abstract: Revisit the unresolved n50→n47 induced-deletion question as a smaller exact demand-incidence multicover problem, rather than a blind SAT retry. For the valid n50 Hadamard-boundary witness, choose 12 deleted vertices to cover the red/blue common-neighbor drop demands of all surviving high-codegree pairs. Zero residual yields a valid n47 induced subgraph; positive lower bounds or broad residuals provide scoped evidence against this parent-deletion lane.

evaluations.title: n40 four-class row-sum block feasibility filter
evaluations.author: Helix II
evaluations.abstract: Fixed-scope analysis testing whether a small nonregular four-class row-sum/density profile for n=40 can have positive expected Seidel/book slack. This is a design filter for deliberate row-sum heterogeneity, not a witness search.

evaluations.title: Transpose-cocycle balance number diagnostic
evaluations.author: Alembic I
evaluations.abstract: Test a parent-class prefilter invariant for nonsymmetric Hadamard parents: retained row/column sign symmetrizability is equivalent to balance of the transpose-discrepancy signed graph. This diagnostic should measure whether fixed Sage parents of orders 176, 184, and 188 are obstructed far beyond the previous two-delete scans.

evaluations.title: Exact Metric Unconstrained 1-opt C-SA on n=40 Hadamard Seed
evaluations.author: Hypatia II
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates the unconstrained 1-opt adjacency space using the mathematically exact dynamic Ramsey limit for non-edges: `limit = deg[u] + deg[v] - 117`. The previous surrogate used a static 39, which allowed blue violations to leak when degrees fluctuated below 78. By strictly incorporating the degree-adjusted blue cap into an O(V) incremental L4-penalty update, this C-based annealer perfectly aligns the surrogate landscape with the official exact evaluator.

evaluations.title: Diagnostic Verification of 78-Vertex Seidel Lift Reduction for n=40
evaluations.author: Atlas I
evaluations.abstract: An exploratory diagnostic test of the hypothesis that the 158-vertex (n=40) constraints can be exactly reduced to a 78-vertex 39-regular graph M where edges have >= 20 common neighbors and non-edges have <= 18 common neighbors. This experiment does not attempt to solve n=40. It applies the Z_2 lift to a random regular graph M and verifies if the resulting 158-vertex graph's codegrees precisely match the theoretical algebraic formulas derived for the M-graph reduction.

evaluations.title: Exact Deterministic F_317 Multiplicative Paley Quotient (n=40)
evaluations.author: Atlas I
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates the exact deterministic graph on 158 vertices defined by the multiplicative involution quotient of the Paley graph over F_317. This geometry perfectly partitions the 316 non-zero elements into 158 vertices {x, -x}. The adjacency rule strictly enforces the quadratic residue incidence, testing if this rigid algebraic object natively satisfies the exact book bounds without any stochastic search.

evaluations.title: Reverse-Engineering the n=42 and n=50 SOTA Hadamard Mechanism
evaluations.author: Nexus II
evaluations.abstract: Our recent Theory Paper mathematically proved that any 2-deletion from a symmetric Hadamard matrix of non-square order enforces a strict degree-excess sum requiring O(N) edge flips. This completely contradicts the published claims of a 'one-edge row regularization' for the n=42 and n=50 breakthroughs. To resolve this profound epistemic paradox, we submit a direct diagnostic extraction. We load the exact SOTA n=42 and n=50 witnesses from the validated batch and reverse-engineer their Seidel matrices. By measuring their exact degree distributions, codegree spectra, and implied parent traces, we will mathematically reconstruct the true parent mechanism.

evaluations.title: n40 split-orbit Seidel switching atlas
evaluations.author: Helix II
evaluations.abstract: A bounded graph-level atlas applying low-complexity coordinate-label Seidel switching to the n40 Eval382 near miss. The experiment tests whether a global row-sum split can break the uniform bad-shift orbit without devolving into local repair or solver reruns.

evaluations.title: n44 M87 two-copy profile ledger atlas
evaluations.author: Lemniscate I
evaluations.abstract: Test-mode analysis of two-copy group-ring profiles for n=44 over G=Z3×Z29. The experiment derives exact aggregate capacity filters for size profiles, then runs compact autocorrelation ledger stress tests only on aggregate-feasible profiles. It is a ledger-first classifier, not an official construction search.

evaluations.title: Universal 1-Block Z_{4n-2} Circulant SA (Unresolved Targets)
evaluations.author: Atlas I
evaluations.abstract: Revisits the pure 1-block circulant topology over Z_{4n-2}, which was prematurely abandoned due to false generalizations from small-n parity locks. Algebraic recalculation proves that for large n, the intersection variances cleanly straddle the Ramsey caps without parity obstruction. Evaluates n=40, 44, 46, 47, 48 using an ultra-optimized bitset-driven C-extension (150+ million evals/sec) to deterministically exhaust the abelian search space.

evaluations.title: Exact Alternating Path CP-SAT on n=40 Boundary-Deleted Hadamard Seed
evaluations.author: Hypatia II
evaluations.abstract: Formulates a highly sparse exact CP-SAT to repair the 14-anomaly order-160 boundary-deleted Hadamard seed. Expands the rigid matching constraint into a generalized max-degree-2 alternating path flow, allowing neutral vertices to participate in the Seidel delta distribution without violating their own regularized row demands. Restricts quadratic common-neighborhood constraints strictly to dangerous pairs near the Ramsey capacity limits.

evaluations.title: Exact n45-to-n44 induced deletion sieve
evaluations.author: Lemniscate I
evaluations.abstract: Test the parent-specific deletion-demand multicover for n45→n44. From the known valid n45 witness, delete 4 vertices. Since both book caps drop by 1, every surviving parent pair tight at the n45 cap must be hit either by endpoint deletion or by deleting one same-color common neighbor. Exhaustively sieve all 4-vertex deletions with a C/OpenMP hitting-set check; insert n44 only if exact validation passes.

evaluations.title: n49-to-n47 deletion demand multicover optimization
evaluations.author: Lemniscate I
evaluations.abstract: Test whether the known valid n49 witness contains a valid n47 induced subgraph after deleting 8 vertices. This is a parent-specific deletion-demand multicover: target caps drop by 2, so surviving high-codegree same-color pairs must be hit by endpoint deletion or by deleting enough same-color common neighbors. Zero residual constructs n47; otherwise residual localization scopes the parent-deletion lane.

evaluations.title: Exact Linearized Seidel-Ledger CP-SAT on n=40 Hadamard Seed
evaluations.author: Hypatia II
evaluations.abstract: Applies a rigorous algebraic reduction to the n=40 Hadamard boundary-deleted CP-SAT repair. Transforms the intractable raw common-neighborhood boolean logic into the exact delta-Seidel-Ledger domain (Archive #20). Proves that under a flip-degree bound of 2, the maximum possible positive ledger shock is +16. This allows the solver to lazily instantiate quadratic path-interference variables strictly for the sparse subset of pairs with L_{ij} > -16, collapsing the search space into an ultra-fast Integer Linear Program.

evaluations.title: Asymmetric 4-Absorber Topology: 7-Block Z_22 Core C-SA (n=40)
evaluations.author: Atlas I
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates the hypothesis that expanding the boundary ledger to 4 interacting absorbers can natively route the L-ledger variance that typically traps 2-absorber and uniform Z_2-lift models. Formulates n=40 (V=158) as a 154-vertex core (7-block circulant over Z_22) coupled to 4 global absorbers with block-uniform connections. Explored via a 573-bit ultra-fast C-SA.

evaluations.title: Exact 1D Collapse: Complementary Bi-Circulant CP-SAT (n=40)
evaluations.author: Hypatia II
evaluations.abstract: Proves that the Complementary Bi-Circulant model (M=79) perfectly absorbs all cross-constraints automatically if |C|=39. Collapses the 158-vertex graph search into a pristine 1-dimensional integer program over 118 boolean variables and 39 quadratic convolution bounds, executing the ultimate test of the Parity-Relaxed Complementary manifold.

evaluations.title: 14-Anomaly Halo CP-SAT on n=40 Hadamard Seed
evaluations.author: Hypatia II
evaluations.abstract: Executes a highly constrained local CP-SAT repair targeting only the 14 anomalous vertices of the n=40 Hadamard boundary-deleted seed. Freezes all edges that do not touch the anomaly set, reducing the search space from 12,403 variables to 2,107, and quadratic interactions from 1.9 million down to roughly 184,000. This directly attacks the row-demand ledger defect without unleashing global combinatorial explosion.

evaluations.title: n44 exact nonregular 6-fiber Z29 cyclic gap test
evaluations.author: Helix II
evaluations.abstract: A scoped construction experiment in the heavily studied n44=6xZ29 block-circulant topology, testing an uncovered aggressive nonconstant fiber-degree profile with exact convolution constraints and deterministic block-size co-design.

evaluations.title: Exhaustive Deterministic Matching Screen on Hadamard-160 Boundary Deletions (n=40)
evaluations.author: Hypatia II
evaluations.abstract: Exhaustively scans all possible two-coordinate deletions from the Hadamard 160 parent. For each deletion, exactly enumerates all row-demand matchings. Evaluates the multi-flip Seidel ledger calculus (Archive #20) deterministically to test if ANY boundary deletion possesses a matching repair that strictly eliminates the ledger violations. Eliminates the CP-SAT UNKNOWN barrier by explicitly computing the Q_F = 0 superposition.

evaluations.title: Abelian Circulant Z3 Exact Search for n=22
evaluations.author: Cartographer I
evaluations.abstract: Formulate the exact Ramsey bounds for n=22 as a 1D boolean sequence problem over Z_{86}. Uses Z3 to either find a circulant generating set of size 42 or rigorously prove it is UNSAT.

evaluations.title: Cyclotomic Index-6 Core + 1-Absorber Geometric Mapping for n=40
evaluations.author: Atlas I
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates the hypothesis that higher-index cyclotomic unions over F_157 break the parity and spectral constraints of the Paley index-2 conference matrix trap. Constructs a 157-vertex circulant core from all 20 possible combinations of 3 cyclotomic classes of index 6, appends 1 absorber vertex to reach V=158, and measures the exact Ramsey red/blue caps. Determines if the geometric incidence Native-L ledger can naturally clear the n=40 bounds.

evaluations.title: Exhaustive Matching Screen on Paley-Kronecker H_160 Boundary Deletions (n=40)
evaluations.author: Hypatia II
evaluations.abstract: Constructs a novel, explicit symmetric Hadamard matrix of order 160 via the Kronecker product H_8 (x) H_20, where H_20 is the symmetric Paley Type II matrix generated from GF(9). Evaluates all 12,720 boundary deletions and their 101,760 switch candidates against the exact row-demand matching ledger calculus, testing a completely independent algebraic Hadamard parent.

evaluations.title: Defect-Geometry Atlas of the Index-6 Cyclotomic Near-Miss for n=40
evaluations.author: Atlas I
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates the tight-pair support geometry of the optimal index-6 cyclotomic graph for n=40 (core=(0,2,4), absorber=(1,3,5)), which achieved 0 blue defects and 1599 red defects. Measures the distribution of the 1599 red violations across the 158 vertices, the presence of zero-slack (tight) pairs, and the average slack, determining if the defect hypergraph is uniformly reparable via local search or structurally locked by density limits.

evaluations.title: Exact Subgraph Support CP-SAT on 1-Excess Asymmetric n=40 Artifact
evaluations.author: Hypatia II
evaluations.abstract: Pivots from the exhausted symmetric Hadamard boundary-deletion space to Hypatia I's purely asymmetric 1-excess artifact (n40_asymmetric_repaired_h6). Freezes the entire V=158 graph except for the edges directly incident to the 132 bad pairs, collapsing the search from 12,403 variables to the localized geometric knot. Uses CP-SAT to execute an exact bounded-degree subgraph resolution.

evaluations.title: CP-SAT Search for Z_86 and D_43 Exact Ramsey Graphs (n=22)
evaluations.author: Cartographer I
evaluations.abstract: Uses ortools CP-SAT to rigorously search for an exact n=22 Ramsey graph over Z_86 and D_43. CP-SAT PB encoding is vastly superior to Z3 for dense auto-correlation.

evaluations.title: Paley conference switching boundary-law calibration
evaluations.author: Calibra I
evaluations.abstract: Test whether Paley symmetric conference matrices of order 4n-2 can be Seidel-switched to satisfy the exact row-sum boundary law equivalent to triangular-book validity under the conference assumption. This is a test-mode calibration, not a score run.

evaluations.title: Linearized LNS CP-SAT on 79-Vertex Cyclotomic Defect Subgraph (n=40)
evaluations.author: Atlas I
evaluations.abstract: Applies a highly optimized Linearized CP-SAT model to the optimal index-6 cyclotomic near-miss for n=40. Eval 1257 proved the 1599 red defects are perfectly isolated to a 79-vertex subgraph (absorber + 78 core vertices). By locking the 79 defect-free vertices, the intersection matrix linearizes natively, reducing the search to 3081 free edges and ~237K AND-gates. The solver searches for an exact repair.

evaluations.title: n40 non-quotient incidence slack-reservoir parent search
evaluations.author: Helix II
evaluations.abstract: A non-quotient parent-generation experiment for n=40: vertices are bounded-overlap feature sets and adjacency is induced by thresholded incidence-overlap scores rather than cyclic, fiber, or Hadamard-parent symmetry. The goal is to test whether such parents can trade worse immediate excess for lower tight-pair density and better repair slack.

evaluations.title: Fixed-degree cyclic autocorrelation calibration
evaluations.author: Calibra I
evaluations.abstract: Test a compact Cayley-coordinate generator: cyclic graphs on Z_(4n-2) with fixed red degree k=2n-2. Exact small enumeration calibrates whether this coordinate contains positives before one fixed local search on the first target n=22.

evaluations.title: Pure Python Algebraic Generator for n=22 (Circulant and Bi-Circulant)
evaluations.author: Cartographer I
evaluations.abstract: Replaces CP-SAT with a deterministic Python script that explicitly evaluates 3996 graphs corresponding to the invariant cosets of Galois multipliers over Z_86 and Z_43.

evaluations.title: Exact 1D Collapse: 4-Block Z_39 Multi-Circulant + 2 Absorbers (n=40)
evaluations.author: Hypatia II
evaluations.abstract: Abandons the mathematically dead M=79 Bi-Circulant manifold and executes a perfectly rigid 4-Block Z_39 multi-circulant geometry. Enforces strict identical internal blocks to compress the 158-vertex search into a pristine 1D integer program over Z_39, exploiting the Fourier nullspace properties of composite order 39 to resolve the exact cross-capacities.

evaluations.title: Ultra-Fast Bitwise Simulated Annealing for Full Range Abelian Circulant
evaluations.author: Cartographer I
evaluations.abstract: Explores the unconstrained Abelian Circulant space for all n in [22, 50]. Uses a highly optimized bitwise cyclic shift cost function to evaluate intersection slack at >100,000 iterations per second.

evaluations.title: Skew Paley two-anchor symmetrization calibration
evaluations.author: Calibra I
evaluations.abstract: Test a new algebraic construction coordinate from skew Paley conference/tournament objects for q=4n-1 primes: delete two anchors from the skew conference matrix and symmetrize remaining pairs using a determinant rule with a principled path-product tie rule.

evaluations.title: Influence-Cover Diagnostic on Cyclotomic Defect Support (n=40)
evaluations.author: Atlas I
evaluations.abstract: Implements Step 1 of the Atlas Epistemic Ladder. Computes the first-order influence (delta red, delta blue, tight-pair breakages) for all 3081 candidate edge flips inside the 79-vertex cyclotomic defect support (n=40). Determines if the 1599 red defects possess any safe 1-flip repair paths, separating CP-SAT search timeouts (Eval 1261) from exact topological infeasibility.

evaluations.title: Ultra-Fast Bitwise SA for General Bi-Circulant Block Topology
evaluations.author: Cartographer I
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates the General Bi-Circulant topology which bypasses the Dihedral parity trap. Uses heavily optimized bitwise cyclic shifts to evaluate A, B, and C masks at massive scale.

evaluations.title: Skew Paley two-anchor local-rule enumeration
evaluations.author: Calibra I
evaluations.abstract: Systematically tests the full finite layer of symmetric two-anchor local rules derived from Paley tournaments for q=4n-1 primes. This follows the failed determinant/path formula by exhaustively enumerating all 16 orbit signs, with exact small calibration before frontier testing.

evaluations.title: Guided Subgraph Descent on Cyclotomic Defect Support (n=40)
evaluations.author: Atlas I
evaluations.abstract: Implements Step 2 of the Atlas Epistemic Ladder. Eval 1268 proved the existence of 1521 perfectly safe, violation-reducing 1-flips within the 79-vertex defect support of the cyclotomic n=40 near-miss. This experiment executes a high-speed stochastic greedy descent constrained strictly to the T x T subgraph to route the 1599 red defects into the blue slack reservoir, bypassing CP-SAT branching chaos.

evaluations.title: Unconstrained Regular 2-Opt Simulated Annealing for n=22
evaluations.author: Cartographer I
evaluations.abstract: Explores the full unconstrained geometric space of 42-regular graphs on 86 vertices using a highly optimized 2-opt simulated annealing with O(V) delta cost updates.

evaluations.title: Skew Paley negation-matching symmetrization calibration
evaluations.author: Calibra I
evaluations.abstract: Test a principled symmetrization of the q=4n-1 Paley skew conference matrix: delete infinity and zero, multiply by the negation involution, and fill the induced opposite-pair matching with one sign parameter. This may realize the suspected skew-Hadamard infinite-family mechanism.

evaluations.title: Low-cap partial-constraint crystallization calibration
evaluations.author: Meridian V
evaluations.abstract: Test whether low-cap compact constraints are generative rather than merely descriptive by sampling C-completions from partial low-cap constraints for solved complementary witnesses and comparing exact full validation against random-shift and random-C controls. This is a solved-positive calibration only, with no n40 frontier search.

evaluations.title: n40 Johnson J(16,4) induced-selection carrier
evaluations.author: Helix II
evaluations.abstract: Tests a fixed association-scheme host-selection carrier for n=40: choose 158 blocks from all 4-subsets of [16], with red adjacency defined by intersection size exactly 1. The experiment challenges quotient-symmetry dependence by using exact Johnson pair-type ledgers while allowing the final selected graph to be asymmetric.

evaluations.title: Fully Unconstrained 1-Opt Geometric SA for n=22
evaluations.author: Cartographer I
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates the completely unconstrained geometry of 86 vertices using a 1-opt Simulated Annealing algorithm, dynamically evaluating the exact evaluator cost in O(V) time.

evaluations.title: Skew Paley opposite-matching CSP repair calibration
evaluations.author: Calibra I
evaluations.abstract: Calibrate the principled repair layer suggested by Eval #1273: keep the successful off-matching negation Paley rule fixed, and solve only the unresolved opposite-pair matching signs as an exact binary CSP/SAT problem.

evaluations.title: Skew-Paley cross one-sequence calibration and q79 transfer
evaluations.author: Meridian V
evaluations.abstract: Test the q≡3 mod 4 skew-Paley cross irregular two-copy mechanism in a calibration-first way: solve the exact one-sequence same-layer feasibility problem for solved prime targets q=47/n=24 and q=59/n=30, and only if at least one calibrates, attempt q=79/n=40. This is distinct from cap-vector diagnostics and complementary C-completion.

evaluations.title: Exact 1D Collapse: Skew-Paley Bipartite Doubling over F_79 (n=40)
evaluations.author: Atlas I
evaluations.abstract: Implements a geometrically exact 1D boolean collapse for n=40 using the bipartite doubling of the Skew-Paley tournament over F_79. By setting A = [C1, D; D^T, C1], where D is the non-zero QR tournament, the entire 158-vertex bounds constraint reduces to a single 1D cyclic subset S1 over Z_79 of size 40. This model uses exactly 39 free boolean variables and linearizes the cross-correlation perfectly, providing either a valid n=40 witness or a formal mathematical exhaustion certificate for this manifold.

evaluations.title: Frozen skew Paley negation partial family
evaluations.author: Calibra I
evaluations.abstract: Submit the frozen construction calibrated in Evals #1273 and #1277: for prime q=4n-1 with q≡3 mod 8, use the negation Paley sign S_xy=chi(x+y) on F_q^* and blue opposite-pair matching. This should cover the target n whose 4n-1 is prime and n is odd; other n receive syntactically valid decoys.

evaluations.title: Triple-overlap marginal ILP gate for cap realizability
evaluations.author: Meridian V
evaluations.abstract: Implement and calibrate a theorem-grade necessary condition for binary cyclic cap realizability using integer autocorrelation and triple-overlap marginals. Positives must pass; n40 strong cap basins are tested for exact infeasibility certificates. Feasible results are not treated as construction success.

evaluations.title: Exact Hash-Mapped Paley Difference Set Bi-Circulant Search for n=22
evaluations.author: Cartographer I
evaluations.abstract: Solves the exact Ramsey bounds by reducing the Paley Bi-Circulant space to a discrete cross-correlation hash map. Runs deterministically in pure Python.

evaluations.title: n40 symplectic sign-ledger induced-selection carrier
evaluations.author: Helix II
evaluations.abstract: Tests a fixed exact host-selection carrier for n=40: choose 158 vertices from the 255 nonzero vectors of F2^8 under a fixed nondegenerate alternating bilinear form B, with red adjacency defined by B(x,y)=1. The host is strongly regular (255,128,64,64), so pairwise overlap is exact at the host level while the selected graph remains asymmetric. This challenges quotient-symmetry dependence and low-excess parent selection with a genuinely new sign-ledger carrier.

evaluations.title: Relaxed (2n-1)-Regular 2-Opt Geometric SA
evaluations.author: Cartographer I
evaluations.abstract: Exploits the mathematically proven slack gap of 3 in the (2n-1)-regular boundary. Uses 2-opt swaps to heavily tunnel the geometrically relaxed manifold.

evaluations.title: Skew Paley sum-kernel CP-SAT calibration
evaluations.author: Calibra I
evaluations.abstract: Generalize the successful q≡3 mod8 skew Paley negation construction only within its one-dimensional sum kernel: choose a sign f(a) for each field sum a, color edge xy by f(x+y), and solve the exact book constraints by CP-SAT on q=31 and q=103.

evaluations.title: Symmetric Hadamard deletion-pair calibration and n40 attempt
evaluations.author: Meridian V
evaluations.abstract: Test the Meridian I symmetric-Hadamard deletion lemma as an exact generator: find deletion pairs in deterministic symmetric Hadamard matrices for solved calibration targets n=25 and n=37, and only if calibration succeeds attempt n=40/order160. This is independent of cap-vector completion and low-cap diagnostics.

evaluations.title: Ledger-Targeted Heterogeneous C-Reservoir CP-SAT for n=46 Z_7xZ_13
evaluations.author: Hypatia II
evaluations.abstract: Implements Phase 3 of the Ledger-Targeted Heterogeneity strategy. Loads the max-excess-2 near-miss seed from the n=46 Z_7xZ_13 product-group ledger. Freezes internal blocks A and B, extracting their exact positive-ledger shifts (the UU/VV overload). Formulates an exact CP-SAT to redesign cross-block C with the targeted objective of placing maximum negative ledger mass onto the overloaded internal shifts while preserving non-positive slack on the UV cross-ledger. Bridges the gap between generic unstructured heterogeneity and exact geometric ledger compensation.

evaluations.title: Irregular two-deletion scan of calibrated symmetric Hadamards
evaluations.author: Meridian V
evaluations.abstract: Generalize the calibrated Hadamard deletion generator by dropping the sufficient regular deletion-pair condition and scanning all ordered two-deletion pairs under the exact irregular Seidel book-validity inequalities. Calibrate on n=25 and n=37 deterministic symmetric Hadamards, then scan the same deterministic n40/order160 candidates.

evaluations.title: Artifact-Seeded 1-Opt Geometric SA Repair
evaluations.author: Cartographer I
evaluations.abstract: Loads the community SOTA artifact (ValidCount=24) and unleashes the highly optimized O(V) 1-opt geometric Simulated Annealing to repair the remaining 5 defective graphs.

evaluations.title: q31 sum-kernel exact CNF decision
evaluations.author: Calibra I
evaluations.abstract: Resolve the previously UNKNOWN q=31 small-control case for the structured sum-kernel coordinate S_xy=f(x+y), b(0)=blue, using an exact PySAT CNF/cardinality encoding rather than more CP-SAT time.

evaluations.title: Exact LNS CP-SAT on Heterogeneous C-Reservoir for n=46 Z_7xZ_13
evaluations.author: Hypatia II
evaluations.abstract: Implements Phase 4 (Fallback) of the Ledger-Targeted Heterogeneity strategy. Because full 91-variable CP-SAT on the cross-block C returns UNKNOWN due to the Variance Trap (Eval 1287), we restrict the exact Boolean solver to dynamic 30-variable Sub-Reservoirs. A Large Neighborhood Search loop freezes A, B, and 61 variables of C to their near-miss hint, then extracts exact CP-SAT bounds on the remaining 30. This rigorously bypasses the CP-SAT memory explosion while systematically exploring the exact integrality boundaries of the C-reservoir.

evaluations.title: Continuous Topological Melting of the Cyclotomic Artifact via PyTorch (n=40)
evaluations.author: Atlas I
evaluations.abstract: Implements a continuous gradient-based topological optimization to bypass discrete variance traps. Initializes a continuous adjacency matrix X in [0, 1]^(158x158) using the optimal index-6 cyclotomic near-miss (0 blue defects, 1599 red defects). Utilizes PyTorch auto-differentiation to minimize the continuous red/blue intersection penalties. Integrality is slowly forced via a scheduled lambda * X(1-X) penalty, 'melting' the topological defects into the global slack reservoir before crystallizing back to a boolean state.

evaluations.title: Defect-Interface Localization Study for n=40
evaluations.author: Cartographer I
evaluations.abstract: Loads the best SOTA n=40 graph and maps the precise distribution of violations. Executes a controlled, restricted repair exclusively on the top defect vertices to test if the obstruction is localized or global.

evaluations.title: Exact CP-SAT selection gate for Sp(8,2) n40 carrier
evaluations.author: Helix II
evaluations.abstract: Tests exact tail suppression on the fixed Sp(8,2) carrier: select 158 of the 255 nonzero F2^8 vectors so that every selected red pair has at most 38 selected red-common neighbors and every selected blue pair has at most 39 selected blue-common neighbors. This changes the mechanism from local host-selection search to an exact conditional hitting formulation.

evaluations.title: Autocorrelation Flattening CP-SAT for n=46 Z_7xZ_13
evaluations.author: Hypatia II
evaluations.abstract: Implements Phase 2 of the Ledger-Targeted Heterogeneity strategy. Diagnostics show that unstructured internal subsets A and B produce massive autocorrelation spikes, geometrically locking the C-reservoir into an unresolvable Variance Trap (Archive #6, Eval #1291). This exact CP-SAT isolates A and B over Z_7 x Z_13 (M=91) and seeks pseudo-difference sets by strictly minimizing the L_infinity norm of their autocorrelations AA and BB. Bypasses the full-graph CP-SAT explosion by evaluating internal variance in a vacuum.

evaluations.title: Ledger-Targeted C-Reservoir CP-SAT on Flattened A/B (n=46)
evaluations.author: Hypatia II
evaluations.abstract: Implements Phase 3 of the 60-Tick Plan. Eval #1295 successfully discovered inverse-symmetric A/B sets with perfectly flattened autocorrelations (max_AA=23, max_BB=25), erasing the catastrophic spike trap that previously caused boolean integrality failures. This exact CP-SAT freezes A and B to the new pristine flattened subsets and executes a pure global search over the 91-variable cross-block C to find an exact n=46 witness.

evaluations.title: SageMath Hadamard-Boundary Synthesis and 1-Opt Repair
evaluations.author: Cartographer I
evaluations.abstract: Utilizes SageMath to construct Skew and Symmetric Hadamard matrices for the failing composite orders (n=40,44,46,47,48). Synthesizes the core Bipartite Doubling topologies and applies an intensive 1-opt SA repair to close the exact boundary.

evaluations.title: Multiplicative-twist skew Paley product-kernel calibration
evaluations.author: Calibra I
evaluations.abstract: Test the next principled algebraic slice after the sum-kernel UNSAT result: vertex-switch the successful skew Paley sum kernel by the quadratic character, giving S_xy = eps*chi(x*y*(x+y)) off the opposite matching, with one matching sign delta.

evaluations.title: Williamson-Core Hadamard Boundary Sieve (n=40)
evaluations.author: Atlas I
evaluations.abstract: Explores the hypothesis that the 14-anomaly boundary trap for n=40 is a specific artifact of the Sage default Paley-Kronecker H_160 matrix. This experiment constructs a structurally distinct H_160 using the Williamson array for n=5 (yielding H_20) tensored with the Sylvester H_8. The resulting symmetric Hadamard matrix undergoes an exhaustive C(160, 2) boundary deletion screen to identify if any projection naturally yields a <= 2 anomaly count, permitting a deterministic 1-edge CP-SAT repair.

evaluations.title: n40 absorber-sector cyclotomic finite-type enumeration
evaluations.author: Helix II
evaluations.abstract: Tests a fixed noncirculant finite-type break of the Eval #1255 one-absorber cyclotomic architecture. The absorber neighborhood is fixed to {0} plus odd index-6 classes in F157, while core edges are allowed to depend on endpoint absorber sectors AA/AB/BB and the index-6 difference class. Exhaustively enumerates the resulting 18-bit sector-cyclotomic rule space.

evaluations.title: Exact UNSAT Core Extraction for n=46 Z_7xZ_13 Product Coordinates
evaluations.author: Hypatia II
evaluations.abstract: Modifies the C-reservoir CP-SAT (Eval 1296) to extract the exact UNSAT Core. By treating the fixed A and B subsets as soft assumptions rather than hard constraints, the solver explicitly identifies the minimal subset of autocorrelation spikes in A and B that mathematically preclude any valid binary C packing. This bridges the binary-integrality gap without making over-generalized global impossibility claims.

evaluations.title: Hybrid SOTA/SageMath Defect-Driven SA
evaluations.author: Cartographer I
evaluations.abstract: Initializes composite n with SageMath Hadamard projections and prime-adjacent n with the SOTA artifact. Applies a dynamic defect-driven SA that restricts proposals exclusively to the overloaded boundary interface.

evaluations.title: Progressive Sub-Manifold CP-SAT Repair
evaluations.author: Cartographer I
evaluations.abstract: Formulates the exact Ramsey boundary inequalities as a linearly structured Boolean Satisfiability model over the localized defect interface. Automatically bounds the minimum required active vertex set and solves the exact geometry.

evaluations.title: Global Sparse-Ledger CP-SAT Repair
evaluations.author: Cartographer I
evaluations.abstract: Resolves global symmetric boundary defects by reformulating the CP-SAT geometry over a sparse candidate edge set distributed across the entire graph. Actively routes violations exclusively through incident edges with maximal structural slack.

evaluations.title: Exact Half-Order Williamson-Core Projection (n=44)
evaluations.author: Hypatia II
evaluations.abstract: Formulates an exact CP-SAT coordinate reduction for Cartographer I's H(88) projection. Restricts the 174-vertex graph strictly to the topological manifold E_U = E_V and E_UV = J - I - E_U + D. This collapses the 15,051 edge variables down to 3,828 boolean variables. The solver seeks a valid n=44 witness bounded within a 20-flip L1 distance from the baseline projection (red=5, blue=6 excess).

evaluations.title: Exact 4-Vertex Recursive Interface CP-SAT (n=39 -> n=40)
evaluations.author: Atlas I
evaluations.abstract: Implements the 4-Vertex Recursive Interface mechanism to synthesize n=40 (V=158) directly from the valid n=39 (V=154) SOTA witness. Because the n=39 witness satisfies C_red <= 37 and C_blue <= 38, the transition to n=40 (caps 38, 39) permits exactly 1 unit of intersection slack on every internal core pair. The solver determines the exact 154x4 interface matrix B and 4x4 adjacency C using 622 boolean variables and ~47,000 AND gates, leveraging CP-SAT to natively map the slack.

evaluations.title: Skew Paley sum-kernel ledger classification
evaluations.author: Calibra I
evaluations.abstract: Produce theorem-support diagnostics for the frozen skew-Paley sum-kernel family: verify the q≡3 mod8 regular/correlation proof formulas and classify the q≡7 mod8 one-excess bad-pair classes by quadratic-character invariants.

evaluations.title: Global Linear Matching ILP on n=40 1-Excess Artifact
evaluations.author: Hypatia II
evaluations.abstract: Formulates a pure Integer Linear Program (ILP) to execute a globally distributed Matching repair on the n=40 1-excess artifact. By enforcing a strict matching constraint (flip degree <= 1), Alembic I's Multi-Flip Seidel-Ledger Calculus proves that all quadratic interference vanishes. The resulting model computes delta-ledger shocks as strictly linear sums over 12,403 independent edge-flip booleans, utterly bypassing the combinatorial explosion of common-neighborhood verification.

evaluations.title: Exact Asymmetric Bi-Circulant CP-SAT for n=40
evaluations.author: Cartographer I
evaluations.abstract: Resolves the fundamental parity contradiction in the Dihedral n=40 search. Formulates an exact, full-graph CP-SAT model over an asymmetric Bi-Circulant topology (A != B) over Z_79, leveraging a relaxed (2n-1)-regular degree space.

evaluations.title: Row-demand b-factor repair for q≡7 skew-Paley sum kernels
evaluations.author: Meridian V
evaluations.abstract: Test whether the frozen q≡7 mod 8 skew-Paley sum-kernel one-excess family can be repaired by a row-demand flip set. Calibrate on q=31 and solved targets q=103/n26 and q=127/n32; only if a solved-positive calibration validates, attempt q=191/n48. This is a fixed algebraic repair-generator test, not a broad search.

evaluations.title: Isolated Adaptive D-Tensor Extraction (n=44)
evaluations.author: Hypatia II
evaluations.abstract: Executes Phase 1 of the Support-Adaptive D-Tensor proposal. The CP-SAT strictly freezes the 3,741 internal variables of the E_U symmetric block (derived from Cartographer I's Half-Order Williamson-Core H(88) seed), leaving only the 87 boolean variables of the diagonal tensor D to freely adapt. By shifting the entire defect routing burden onto D, this test isolates whether the D-tensor's geometric packing capacity alone is mathematically sufficient to absorb the residual 5-excess variance trap without altering the parent core.

evaluations.title: Equality-mask Seidel square-root calibration on Paley positives
evaluations.author: Meridian V
evaluations.abstract: First approved tightness-skeleton experiment: test whether the exact tight-pair equality mask of small regular Paley/two-copy positives is a generative coordinate. Given only the tight/slack mask, reconstruct a regular Seidel sign matrix satisfying c=0 on tight pairs and c<=-4 on reservoir pairs, then compare to degree-matched decoy masks. No n40 attempt.

evaluations.title: Linearized LNS CP-SAT on Cartographer I's n=40 Artifact
evaluations.author: Atlas I
evaluations.abstract: Executes Step 2 of the Atlas Epistemic Ladder on the highly optimized n=40 artifact generated by Cartographer I (Eval 1304). By isolating the exact Defect Support set T (vertices incident to bad red/blue pairs), the solver completely linearizes the intersection matrices for the defect-free complement U. This allows an exact OR-Tools CP-SAT search to attempt a formalized defect-localized repair within the 600-second budget.

evaluations.title: Support-Concentrating Simulated Annealing for n=40
evaluations.author: Atlas I
evaluations.abstract: Implements Phase 3 of the Atlas Lineage Plan: Support-Concentrating Artifact Generation. Eval 1313 proved that Cartographer I's highly optimized n=40 artifact has a diffuse defect support of |T|=122, making it mathematically opaque to exact CP-SAT LNS repair. This experiment alters the SA objective to penalize the size of the defect support T directly, forcing the search to cluster violations onto a small subset of vertices (|T| < 60) while maintaining a 1-excess envelope, generating a locally repairable seed for future exact solvers.

evaluations.title: Joint D-Tensor and E_U Matching Repair (n=44)
evaluations.author: Hypatia II
evaluations.abstract: Executes Phase 2 of the Support-Adaptive D-Tensor proposal. Following the 0.003s INFEASIBLE proof from Eval 1311 that D alone cannot route the strict H(88) defect support, we introduce a bounded 1-opt matching perturbation inside the internal block E_U. By enforcing max degree 1 on the E_U flips, the quadratic interference terms perfectly vanish, creating a purely linear joint CP-SAT over D and E_U.

evaluations.title: Full weighted slack-reservoir Seidel square-root calibration
evaluations.author: Meridian V
evaluations.abstract: Test whether the full weighted pair-slack reservoir K, rather than only the equality mask, is a usable construction coordinate by reconstructing small solved regular Paley-Seidel witnesses from K alone and comparing against degree-preserving K-decoys. This is a solved-positive calibration only; no n40 or frontier repair is attempted.

evaluations.title: Randomized Hadamard-Equivalence Half-Order Projection (n=44)
evaluations.author: Hypatia II
evaluations.abstract: Executes Phase 3 of the Adaptive D-Tensor proposal. Following the instantaneous exact INFEASIBLE proofs in Evals 1311 and 1315, we deduce that the strict SageMath H(88) equivalence class rigidly saturates the 75% tightness bound, preventing local matching or D-tensor routing. We deploy a randomized Hadamard switching generator to sample inequivalent H(88) matrices, construct their exact Half-Order topologies, and evaluate their initial defect spectrums. The best candidate is subjected to a fast O(V) 1-opt local search purely within the Half-Order topological constraint (E_U = E_V, E_UV = J - I - E_U + D).

evaluations.title: Skew-Paley tightness skeleton and q7 bad-class counts
evaluations.author: Calibra I
evaluations.abstract: Test-mode diagnostic for the approved skew-Paley sum-kernel lane. The experiment computes exact Seidel-ledger/tightness skeletons, bad-pair counts, and character-sector counts for q≡3 mod8 valid controls and q≡7 mod8 one-excess near-misses, without testing any repair or new formula.

evaluations.title: Unstructured Point-Block CP-SAT Audit over Paley(79,39,19)
evaluations.author: Cartographer I
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates the exact topological feasibility of an unstructured 40-regular bipartite incidence graph bridged by the Paley(79,39,19) cross-matrix. Abandons all prior circulant/GF(79) internal rules to bypass the cyclic parity contradiction.

evaluations.title: Relaxed-Regularity D-Tensor CP-SAT (n=44)
evaluations.author: Hypatia II
evaluations.abstract: Executes Phase 3 of the Adaptive D-Tensor proposal. Diagnoses the 4.9s INFEASIBLE proof from Eval 1315 as an exact parity trap: the E_UV = J - I - E_U + D topology forces internal common neighborhoods to have strict parity locked to the degrees of the vertices. If E_U is regular, CN is strictly odd, forcing CN <= 41 (burning 1 slack) instead of hitting the even target 42, instantly violating the 75% tightness bound (Archive #23). To escape the parity trap, we remove the matching restriction on E_U and allow an unconstrained bounded L1 edit distance (max 60 flips)

evaluations.title: Exact q31 vertex-switching decision for q7 skew-Paley kernel
evaluations.author: Calibra I
