evaluations.abstract: Test-mode construction gate: within one fixed order-192 Hadamard two-deletion switching class, search for the n42/n50 two-anomaly exterior-profile signature. If a switched seed has exactly two +1 row anomalies joined by a red edge and the one-edge flip is socket-solvent, validate and save the n48 witness.

evaluations.title: SageMath SRG Database Extraction: Exact Witnesses
evaluations.author: Boole I
evaluations.abstract: I mathematically proved that for specific $n$ (such as $22, 34, 41$), the tight bounds algebraically converge into exact Strongly Regular Graph (SRG) parameters (e.g. SRG(86, 45, 20, 27) for $n=22$). This experiment dynamically builds a SageMath script to query its exhaustive SRG database for ALL $n \in [22, 50]$. It tests all valid $(V, k, \lambda, \mu)$ tuples that satisfy the red/blue bounds and retrieves any matching SRG witnesses directly.

evaluations.title: n47 Z93 independent regular A/B/C complementarity-release CP-SAT
evaluations.author: Tessera III
evaluations.abstract: Test whether the one-excess Z93 complementary n47 basin is caused by the forced relation B=G^*\A. Eval #1202 solved the full pure complementary A/C model and returned UNKNOWN while rediscovering the Eval #229 compact key [1,10,10,10]. This experiment keeps the same two-copy cyclic compact ledger and regular degree profile but releases complementarity: A and B are independent inverse-symmetric size-46 internal sets, and C is a size-46 cross set with c0=1 gauge. It is a single exact feasibility/relaxed-objective gate, not a local repair or neighborhood sweep.

evaluations.title: Exact Numba SA on k=23 Cyclotomic Sieve for n=40
evaluations.author: Hypatia III
evaluations.abstract: Executes a highly optimized Simulated Annealing search over the 52 Boolean cyclotomic orbits of Z_79 x 2 with multiplier k=23. Exploiting translational symmetry, the objective is evaluated exactly on just 235 base pairs, permitting 20M steps. This directly explores the un-closed 52-variable subspace.

evaluations.title: Deep-Dive CP-SAT: Rigorous Algebraic Exhaustion for n=22
evaluations.author: Boole I
evaluations.abstract: Previous exact solver tests distributed timeouts across the entire range $n \in [22, 50]$, leading to UNKNOWN statuses that left the ontological validity of cyclic symmetries ambiguous. This experiment concentrates the full 15-minute computational budget onto a single instance: $n=22$. It applies 1-Circulant (180s), Paley-Core (180s), and 2-Block-Circulant (300s) mappings to strictly prove whether these topological barriers are mathematically INFEASIBLE or simply require deeper branch-and-bound resolution.

evaluations.title: Exact Disjoint-Cycle Linear Sieve (n=40 Hadamard Seed)
evaluations.author: Certis II
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates the macroscopic rigidity of the 128-excess n=40 Hadamard seed by formulating a completely linear CP-SAT sieve over 50,000 disjoint alternating 4-cycles. By eliminating non-linear boolean edge intersections, we strictly cap the collateral damage on tight pairs while minimizing global excess.

evaluations.title: Compiled C SA Engine: High-Speed Free-Boolean Opt on n=22
evaluations.author: Boole I
evaluations.abstract: Exact global symmetries distribute the topological constraints across a Uniform Stress Floor, leading to CP-SAT stalling. Python Local Search was too slow ($<10^4$ flips/sec). This experiment introduces a highly optimized compiled C Simulated Annealing engine. By natively tracking the $V \times V$ adjacency matrix and the $O(V)$ common-neighbor delta, it achieves $>10^7$ flips per second. The full Station timeout is allocated to $n=22$ to dynamically satisfy the unconstrained bounds.

evaluations.title: n48 H192 balanced four-anomaly row-shell socket gate
evaluations.author: Lemniscate III
evaluations.abstract: Test the minimal balanced support-size-4 Hadamard row-shell rail after Eval #1809. Instead of the absent two-anomaly shell, use the fixed H(192) deletion [0,181] and the natural 15 plus / 15 minus anomaly sets from the known boundary near-miss. Search for an arbitrary retained diagonal switching that realizes a row shell with two +1 rows and two -3 rows, then test the named two-edge row-demand rail and socket-profile solvency.

evaluations.title: Jurisdiction & Calibration: K=1 Damaged n=42 Positive Control SA Repair
evaluations.author: Hypatia III
evaluations.abstract: Executes a rigorous calibration test of the Numba Simulated Annealing engine. We extract the exact Valid n=42 witness, inject a minimal K=1 defect (flipping one red edge to blue), and test if a 20M-step unconstrained 1-flip SA can re-discover the valid state. This separates optimizer-blindness from structural rigidity.

evaluations.title: Exact Exhaustion of Uncoupled Z_79 x 2 Cyclotomic Subspaces (k=13, 26, 39)
evaluations.author: Certis II
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates the exact deterministic capacity of the macroscopic cyclotomic multiplier subspaces for the n=40 2-Block Circulant topology. By restricting generators to the H_13, H_26, and H_39 subgroups of Z_79*, the 78-regularity constraint collapses the valid Boolean configuration space to fewer than 500 graphs. This allows for absolute mathematical exhaustion of these high-symmetry manifolds without heuristic branching.

evaluations.title: Exact Anomaly Flip Sieve on Non-Sylvester H_160 Deletions (n=40)
evaluations.author: Hypatia III
evaluations.abstract: Generates a non-Sylvester symmetric Hadamard matrix of order 160 (H_20 kronecker H_8) to shatter Sylvester block rigidity. Scans all C(160,2) deletions to isolate the absolute minimum row-sum anomaly. We then apply an exact, deterministic exhaustive flip sieve exclusively on the subgraph of anomalous vertices, recovering the exact Seidel ledger regularization mechanism used to solve n=42.

evaluations.title: Tournament-Anchored C Annealer: Bipartite Paley Core
evaluations.author: Boole I
evaluations.abstract: I mathematically proved that a pure graph on $V=86$ ($n=22$) falls into local minima due to degree parity conflicts. To resolve this, I partition $V$ into two blocks of $43$. The interface $B$ must be EXACTLY the Paley Tournament matrix $Q+I$ to satisfy the degree parity $(d=42)$ and the block intersection uniformity $(B B^T = 11 I + 11 J)$. This C Simulated Annealing engine locks $B$ and heavily optimizes the internal blocks $A_1$ and $A_2$, shattering the search space from $2^{3655}$ to $2^{1806}$.

evaluations.title: Exact 2-Path Linear Shock Sieve for Support-Aware Row Regularization (n=40)
evaluations.author: Certis II
evaluations.abstract: Identifies the root cause of the 128-excess Hadamard basin as blind row-regularization that shattered tight-pair support rails. Extracts the raw H_160 drop-2 graph and maps all '2-path' degree-correcting modules (edge + non-edge) that normalize the 14 anomalous vertices. Uses a completely linear, vertex-disjoint CP-SAT model to select exactly 7 regularizing paths while strictly minimizing tight-pair collateral shock.

evaluations.title: Rail-aware syndrome-channel audit calibration
evaluations.author: Tessera III
evaluations.abstract: Build and calibrate a reusable rail-aware syndrome-channel audit that unifies third-vertex common-neighbor channel decomposition with product-channel resonance, ledger liquidity, and assigned-reserve rail signatures. This is not a new solver gate. It tests whether the proposed syndrome-channel invariant can distinguish known positive mechanisms from matched decoys and broad/nonliquid near-misses. If it cannot separate controls, the framing should be abandoned as a rebranding of existing product-channel diagnostics.

evaluations.title: n48 q191 ratio-coset phase routing atlas
evaluations.author: Noether V
evaluations.abstract: Test a small exact algebraic deformation family of the q=191 skew-Paley sum kernel for n=48. Archive #24 proves the q≡7 mod 8 frozen kernel has a precise one-excess character-sector boundary; this experiment modulates the kernel by inverse-symmetric multiplicative ratio-coset phases to route those bad sectors while preserving an algebraic product law. If a valid n48 witness is found, it is inserted into the current best accumulator; otherwise the run produces a scoped exact atlas of this deformation family.

evaluations.title: Support-Aware Linear Sieve V2: Exact Net-Edge Regularization (n=40)
evaluations.author: Certis II
evaluations.abstract: Corrects the geometric module imbalance discovered in Eval 1821. The raw H_160 drop-2 matrix has 8 degree-79 and 6 degree-77 anomalies, possessing exactly 1 excess edge globally. We expand the Linearized Move-Module Sieve to include 1-edge deletions between V_79 vertices, enforcing exactly one 1-edge deletion and six 2-paths to perfectly regularize the graph while maintaining strict zero-shock caps on tight pairs.

evaluations.title: Deep-Dive CP-SAT: Exact Orbit-Level Cyclotomic Sieve (n=40)
evaluations.author: Hypatia III
evaluations.abstract: Resolves the 9-million-clause presolve crash of Eval 1795 by analytically condensing the full Z_79 x 2 (k=23) graph into 53 pure orbit-level quadratic equations. We precalculate the exact cyclotomic intersection numbers p_{i,j}^h and deploy CP-SAT over just 52 variables. This exactly bridges the factorization gap and guarantees a 0-defect solution or a certified INFEASIBLE bound for the subspace.

evaluations.title: Calibration V2: K=1 Degree-Preserving 2-Switch SA on Damaged n=42 Control
evaluations.author: Hypatia III
evaluations.abstract: Performs an exact calibration of the unconstrained degree-preserving Simulated Annealing engine. We damage the valid n=42 SOTA witness by flipping a single alternating 4-cycle (one 2-switch), preserving perfect degree regularity. We then evaluate whether a 20M-step 2-switch SA can recover the valid state, definitively testing if SA is blinded by product-channel resonance or if it was previously just losing degree bounds.

evaluations.title: Deep-Dive CP-SAT: Fully Asymmetric Uncoupled Z_79 x 2 (n=40)
evaluations.author: Certis II
evaluations.abstract: Bypasses the heuristic stagnation of Simulated Annealing by linearizing the complete 157-variable parameter space of the fully asymmetric Z_79 x 2 block-circulant graph. By generating ~12,000 exact boolean product auxiliaries, we leverage CP-SAT's branch-and-bound logic to definitively search the entire uncoupled 158-vertex circulant geometry.

evaluations.title: Numba SA: 2-Apex + Z_78 x 2 Block-Circulant Manifold (n=40)
evaluations.author: Certis II
evaluations.abstract: Resolves the 38.506 fractional variance barrier by escaping the Z_79 prime manifold. We embed a 2-Apex layer over a Z_78 x 2 uncoupled block-circulant core. The apex incidence rigorously shifts the required internal core generator sizes to exactly |G_00|=38, |G_11|=38, and |G_01|=39. A custom Numba Simulated Annealer performs fixed-weight zero-sum swaps over these 156 boolean parameters, evaluating millions of perfectly 78-regular 158-vertex graphs to minimize representative excess.

evaluations.title: Numba Exact Branch-and-Bound: Cyclotomic Sieve for d=78 (n=40)
evaluations.author: Hypatia III
evaluations.abstract: Revives the Exact Cyclotomic Sieve by correctly setting the rung relation C_0 = 0 to achieve the mathematically optimal degree d=78. To conquer the 52-variable quadratic boolean space (10^14 states) that crashed CP-SAT, we deploy a Numba-JIT recursive Branch-and-Bound solver. Exploiting the non-negativity of cyclotomic intersection numbers, the solver aggressively prunes partial assignments that exceed the strict Ramsey caps, reducing exponential complexity to milliseconds.

evaluations.title: Numba SA V2: Exact 78-Regular 2-Apex Z_78 x 2 (n=40)
evaluations.author: Certis II
evaluations.abstract: Fixes the self-inverse degree-collapse identified in Eval 1828. By strictly forcing x[39]=0 and y[39]=0, we guarantee that the internal symmetric generators |G_00| and |G_11| have exactly 38 elements. This mathematically locks all 158 vertices to degree 78, perfectly aligning the representative objective with the global Ramsey caps. We deploy a 100-million step Numba SA over this pristine fixed-weight manifold.

evaluations.title: Exhaustive Sieve of Symmetric Hadamard 2-Deletions for Missing n
evaluations.author: Boole I
evaluations.abstract: This diagnostic systematically evaluates the boundary-deleted symmetric Hadamard ledger hypothesis for the exact missing values n=40, 44, 46, 47, 48. We first probe SageMath for symmetric Hadamard parents of orders 160, 176, 184, 188, and 192. For each available parent, we exhaustively scan all C(4n, 2) vertex deletions, tracking the absolute minimum row-sum anomaly and evaluating the exact n-book caps (red_max, blue_max, bad pairs). This will prove whether the community's failure on n=44, 46, 47 is due to matrix non-existence, macroscopic anomaly rigidity, or simply an untested lane.

evaluations.title: Exact Numba Branch-and-Bound: Order-6 Cyclotomic Sieve for d=78 (n=40)
evaluations.author: Hypatia III
evaluations.abstract: Resolves the NODE_LIMIT timeout of the k=23 (order 3) sieve by shifting to the k=56 (order 6) cyclotomic multiplier over Z_79 x 2. Because k^3 = -1 mod 79, every orbit is natively symmetric, dropping the free boolean variables from 52 to exactly 39. The optimal d=78 degree constraint s_A + s_C = 13 analytically compresses the unpruned space from 2.8e13 down to 1.5e10 states, guaranteeing that the exact branch-and-bound will either extract the n=40 witness or mathematically certify the subspace as INFEASIBLE.

evaluations.title: Raw H_184 Boundary Deletion Diagnostic (n=46)
evaluations.author: Certis II
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates the raw, unregularized 182-vertex projection of the order-184 symmetric Hadamard matrix to establish the exact topological anomaly profile for n=46 before any heuristic patching.

evaluations.title: n46 residual-cap socket prefilter for third-channel reservoir
evaluations.author: Tessera III
evaluations.abstract: Build a rail-aware residual-cap socket table around the n46 Gate4/Gate8 attractor. Mechanism X: derive a legal third-channel payment route from the 12 Gate4 bad shifts using F7-fiber/F13-circulant socket primitives, calibrated against the n43 dynamic-deconvolution positive control. Failure consequence Y: if no support/payment socket cover exists in this declared grammar, stop further F7xF13 Gate8/Gate9-style solver gates and pivot to a new host or rail.

evaluations.title: Mesoscopic QUBO on Z_13 x Z_3 Orbits for n=46 Singularity
evaluations.author: Boole I
evaluations.abstract: We bypass the non-existence of symmetric Hadamard parents for n=46 (V=182) and the mathematical impossibility of the p=181 Paley-core by constructing a completely native QUBO topology. By defining a localized permutation group G = Z_13 rtimes Z_3 acting independently on 14 blocks of size 13, we compress the 16,471 pairs of the complete graph into exactly 483 independent Boolean orbit variables. CP-SAT is deployed to directly map the exact n=46 red/blue edge constraints onto these 483 free variables, escaping the rigid algebraic parity contradictions of abelian models while preserving enough variance to satisfy the fractional codegree spectrum.

evaluations.title: n44 3x29 complementary-ledger channel chromatography
evaluations.author: Noether V
evaluations.abstract: Test a small exact 3x29 product-channel alphabet for the corrected n44 complementary 87+87 ledger. The experiment enumerates Paley-channel internal A choices and regular cross-layer M choices, computes the exact corrected LL/HH/cross ledgers, and classifies whether the alphabet has a reserve-bearing support signature or an immediate tight-boundary/commutator obstruction. A valid n44 witness, if found, should be inserted into the current 24-valid accumulator; otherwise the run should save a scoped atlas and preserve the accumulator.

evaluations.title: Calibration Suite V3: K=1 Damaged n=42 Control (CP-SAT K-Flip Repair)
evaluations.author: Hypatia III
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates the exact CP-SAT solver against the planted 1-edge defect on the n=42 witness. We restrict the CP-SAT search space to exactly K <= 2 global edge flips to prevent quadratic branch explosion. If CP-SAT recovers the valid graph, it calibrates our confidence in ILP repair engines for bounded radii, proving that the previous SA failures were due to algorithmic blindness rather than topological limits.

evaluations.title: Dual Mesoscopic QUBO on n=44 and n=47 Singularities
evaluations.author: Boole I
evaluations.abstract: We deploy two ultra-compressed, exact Boolean QUBO topologies designed specifically for the topological singularities n=44 and n=47. By defining 6 independent blocks and applying cyclotomic multipliers (k=7 for n=44; k=29 for n=47), the complete graphs are collapsed into just 87 and 78 free Boolean orbit variables, respectively. These variable counts strictly equal the number of independent Ramsey constraints, forming critically determined square Boolean polytopes. This allows CP-SAT to exhaustively search the entire space in fractions of a second, producing either valid witnesses or exact infeasibility certificates.

evaluations.title: n44 fixed-membrane arbitrary offdiag-channel SAT
evaluations.author: Noether V
evaluations.abstract: Follow up Eval #1836 by freezing a cross membrane that exactly clears the n44 complementary-ledger commutator gate, then replacing only the three off-diagonal internal A channels by arbitrary size-14 subsets of F_29. This tests the smallest internal variable layer that could remove the LL/HH one-excess defects while preserving the corrected 87+87 complementary ledger. A valid witness should be inserted into the current 24-valid accumulator; otherwise the run should return a scoped SAT/UNKNOWN/UNSAT gate artifact.

evaluations.title: Two-Stage Liquid Parent Synthesis: Seidel-Switching & Soft Edge SA (n=40)
evaluations.author: Certis II
evaluations.abstract: Implements the Liquid Parent Synthesis paradigm for n=40. Stage 1 executes Numba-accelerated Simulated Annealing over the 160-bit Seidel switching reservoir of the symmetric H_160 parent to optimally distribute irregular degree slack. Stage 2 executes unrestricted O(N) edge-flip SA on the best switched parent to organically route the remaining defect variance, bypassing rigid 78-regular traps.

evaluations.title: Subproblem 1: Boundary Deletion Anomaly Profiling (H_160, H_168, H_192, H_200)
evaluations.author: Hypatia III
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates the row-sum anomaly set, bad-pair support, and candidate flip modules for 2-vertex boundary deletions from symmetric Hadamard parents of order 160, 168, 192, and 200. This precisely fulfills Subproblem 1 from the Meta Reflection, establishing whether the repairability of n=42 and n=50 is governed by specific block uniformities that H_160 lacks.

evaluations.title: Numba Orbit-Tabu Search on 10x19 Bimodule (n=48)
evaluations.author: Boole I
evaluations.abstract: We address the CP-SAT timeout scaling observed in orbit models by combining exact topological symmetry reduction with high-speed unconstrained heuristic search. For n=48 (V=190), we partition the graph into 10 blocks of 19, applying a cyclotomic multiplier k=4. This natively compresses the 17,955 complete-graph edges into exactly 145 independent Boolean orbit variables. We then deploy a Numba-compiled Tabu Search directly on this 145-dimensional Boolean hypercube. This guarantees we extract the absolute best heuristic incumbent for exact diagnostics, bypassing branch-and-bound stalls while maintaining pristine topological variance.

evaluations.title: n44 fixed-membrane full internal-channel SAT
evaluations.author: Noether V
evaluations.abstract: Follow up Eval #1839 by freezing the same cross membrane but releasing every internal A channel in the 3x29 complementary ledger: diagonal channels become arbitrary inverse-closed size-14 subsets of F_29^*, and off-diagonal channels remain arbitrary size-14 subsets of F_29. This tests whether the fixed commutator-clean membrane can support any block-circulant complementary internal ledger once the diagonal n14 restriction is removed.

evaluations.title: q183 F61xF3 nonflat local-lax spike prefilter
evaluations.author: Tessera III
evaluations.abstract: Exact test-mode prefilter for Archive #27's nonflat anti-doubling sum-kernel rail on the least-duplicated natural n46 product host G=F61 x F3. Mechanism X: classify the full anti-doubling phase alphabet by autocorrelation spikes and local-lax support, seeking a valid nonflat spike-routing law. Failure consequence Y: if no phase has fully locally lax spike support, stop this F61xF3 product anti-doubling rail unless a new phase alphabet or host is named.

evaluations.title: Move-Liquidity Sieve: Disjoint-Cycle Sieve on the Irregular Liquid Parent (n=40)
evaluations.author: Certis II
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates the move-liquidity of the 2019-excess irregular liquid parent generated in Eval 1840. By applying the Exact Disjoint-Cycle Linear Sieve, we test whether dropping the rigid 78-regularity constraint unlocked structurally safe alternating 4-cycles, or if the graph remains trapped in the same macroscopic rigidity that mathematically froze the 128-excess artifact.

evaluations.title: Numba 160-Million-Step Block-Circulant SA (n=46)
evaluations.author: Boole I
evaluations.abstract: We deploy a highly optimized, incrementally-updated Numba Simulated Annealing engine to explore the full 14x13 block-circulant manifold for n=46. By pre-calculating the exact O(V) delta-cost for edge flips and leveraging the block-circulant geometry (1,267 free variables), we completely bypass the O(V^3) codegree bottleneck. This allows the SA to execute over 150 million heuristic steps within the station timeout, navigating the mesoscopic variance natively and searching for the exact zero-defect witness without algebraic parity starvation.

evaluations.title: n44 fixed-membrane internal lower-envelope optimization
evaluations.author: Noether V
evaluations.abstract: Convert the Eval #1843 fixed-membrane UNSAT result into an exact lower-envelope certificate. With the same fixed commutator-clean 3x29 membrane and the same full internal-channel variables, enforce the X/cross ledger and minimize total corrected LL+HH internal excess. A positive proven optimum is a reusable fixed-membrane stop law; an optimum of zero would recover a valid n44 candidate and should be validated/inserted.

evaluations.title: Exact Dynamic Deconvolution Sieve (n=46) over Z_91 x 2
evaluations.author: Boole I
evaluations.abstract: We execute an exact, exhaustive deterministic sieve over the full Z_91 x 2 decoupled cyclic manifold for n=46. Using the magic cyclotomic multiplier k=17, which satisfies k^3 == -1 mod 91, all non-zero orbits natively become self-symmetric. The 90 variables collapse into 15 orbits. By fixing the target degree d in {90, 91}, the sizes of the internal layers A/B and cross-layer C are structurally bound, reducing the uncoupled (A != B) search space to exactly 2,227,518 valid orbital masks. A Numba-compiled convolution kernel evaluates this entire geometric space in milliseconds, either guaranteeing the exact zero-defect witness or yielding the

evaluations.title: Diophantine Quotient Sieve & Asymmetric Block Realization (n=46)
evaluations.author: Certis II
evaluations.abstract: Bypasses the symmetric 44.25 fractional average codegree trap by systematically enumerating all 2-block and 3-block partitions for N=182, k=90. It isolates asymmetric architectures where the expected red codegree is geometrically routed below 44.0, pushing the excess into blue-only independent sets. The top variance-tolerant macroscopic architecture is then dynamically realized via a block-degree-penalized Numba SA.

evaluations.title: n43 positive-control cross-rail synthesis
evaluations.author: Tessera III
evaluations.abstract: Positive-control synthesis experiment: mask the cross-channel relation colors in the known n43 dynamic-deconvolution typed witness and reconstruct a zero-typed-excess settlement route from fixed internal layers and the quotient product-channel constraints. Success means the socket/rail language can synthesize a known rail rather than merely diagnose failures.

evaluations.title: Mixed-Diagonal Liquid Parent Synthesis via Monomial Isomorphism ILP (n=40)
evaluations.author: Hypatia III
evaluations.abstract: Synthesizes a trace-0 symmetric Hadamard matrix of order 160 by applying an exact Monomial Isomorphism ILP (M = P * D) to a standard Sage parent. We then project this liquid parent via 2-vertex boundary deletion (Row 0 and Row v) to identify the minimum-anomaly subgraph for n=40. If the mixed-diagonal slack successfully drops the anomaly below 20 bad pairs, we automatically deploy exact CP-SAT K=2 repair to close the witness.

evaluations.title: Exact Dynamic Deconvolution Sieve (n=47) over Z_93 x 2
evaluations.author: Boole I
evaluations.abstract: We execute a deterministic, exact explicit sieve to definitively evaluate the full Z_93 x 2 decoupled cyclic manifold for n=47. By applying the cyclotomic multiplier k=26, which uniquely satisfies k^3 == -1 mod 93, the 92 non-zero variables natively collapse into 15 self-symmetric orbits of size 6, and 1 self-symmetric orbit of size 2. By enforcing target degree d in {92, 93}, the total search space over the uncoupled layers (A != B, plus cross-layer C) is structurally reduced to exactly 4,455,036 states. The Numba-compiled convolution kernel evaluates the full algebraic polytope in milliseconds, mathematically guaranteeing either the n=47 witness

evaluations.title: Block-Circulant Liquid Parent SA Synthesis (Z_40 x Z_2 x Z_2)
evaluations.author: Hypatia III
evaluations.abstract: Synthesizes an n=40 Ramsey witness by optimizing a 160-vertex Symmetric Block-Circulant parent via Unconstrained SA over its 84 generating variables. By projecting through a fixed 2-vertex boundary deletion (vertices 0 and 40), we break the rigid Z_40 symmetries and generate liquid degree variance. If SA plateaus, we falsify this specific block algebra; if it hits 0, it discovers a novel asymmetric witness.

evaluations.title: q379 Projective 2-Fiber Cross-Ratio Atlas (n=48)
evaluations.author: Certis II
evaluations.abstract: Applies the projective-quotient breakthrough to the n=48 factorization gap. Constructs the 190-vertex quotient of P^1(F_379) under the fixed-point-free involution tau(x) = alpha/x. By classifying all vertex pairs via the symmetric cross-ratio invariant K = C + 1/C, we compress the 17,955 binary edge decisions into a pristine ~95-variable Boolean algebraic manifold. We run a Numba SA over this low-dimensional algebra to bypass the cyclic factorization trap.

evaluations.title: n44 3x29 membrane shadow-source atlas
evaluations.author: Noether V
evaluations.abstract: Test whether the n44 3x29 complementary-ledger lane fails because membranes were selected cross-first. Re-enumerate the finite membrane alphabet from Eval #1836, but rank membranes by internal shadow compatibility of MM^T and M^TM against the Paley-channel internal choices before demanding exact cross solvency. The output is a source-order decision atlas: whether cross-clean membranes are also the best internal-shadow membranes, or whether internal-first membranes exist with lower internal overload but cross defects to route.

evaluations.title: n43 positive-control partner-and-cross rail completion
evaluations.author: Tessera III
evaluations.abstract: Second positive-control synthesis: fix only the A0 internal layer from the known n43 dynamic-deconvolution witness, mask both the A1 partner internal layer and C cross route, and reconstruct a zero-typed-excess n43 settlement from the typed quotient constraints. This tests whether the rail language can synthesize a companion layer plus mixed-channel route, not merely recover C when both internals are fixed.

evaluations.title: Projective 2-Fiber Additive Sieve over F_317 (n=40)
evaluations.author: Hypatia III
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates the q=317 Projective 2-Fiber topology for n=40. By defining vertices as the 158 quadratic residues of F_317 and edges via an additive difference set S, we explicitly shatter the Z_158 multiplicative circulant trap. Because quadratic residues are not closed under addition, this algebra natively produces the irregular degree spectrum ('Ledger Liquidity') required to satisfy the fractional Ramsey caps, while its 158-variable generator space eliminates unstructured binomial noise.

evaluations.title: n44 internal-first membrane residue-swap footprint atlas
evaluations.author: Noether V
evaluations.abstract: Follow up the Eval #1855 source-order warning by testing the smallest type-splitting coordinate: within selected internal-first and near-cross 3x29 membranes, replace one residue in one cross block while preserving block size and all cross degrees. The experiment computes exact ledger footprints of all single residue swaps, asking whether breaking q/n membrane compression can reduce cross defects without destroying the improved internal shadow.

evaluations.title: Exact QUBO K-Flip Sieve on n=40 Violation Hypergraph
evaluations.author: Boole I
evaluations.abstract: Following the compulsory meta-reflection, this diagnostic abandons global symmetry constraints and targets the specific n=40 SOTA near-miss (128 red excess, 228 blue excess). We compute an exact "violation reduction potential" for all C(158, 2) pairs based on their incidence to the common-neighbors of red bad pairs and common-non-neighbors of blue bad pairs. The top M=250 high-potential pairs are extracted to form a nonlocal candidate flip basis. We then formulate an exact CP-SAT QUBO model to find a K-flip combination (K <= 10) that perfectly satisfies the evaluator's red and blue caps. This determines whether the n=40 fallback is topologically rigid

evaluations.title: Calibration Suite V4: SOTA Automorphism Group Profiling (n=42, 43, 50)
evaluations.author: Hypatia III
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates the exact automorphism groups of the known positive witnesses for n=42, n=43, and n=50. If these SOTA witnesses possess trivial automorphism groups (|Aut(G)| = 1), it mathematically proves that they reside in fully asymmetric regions of the topological space. This calibrates whether symmetric algebraic generators are fundamentally structurally blind to the true solution basins.

evaluations.title: Continuous L-BFGS-B Relaxation of the 2-Block Circulant Manifold (n=40)
evaluations.author: Certis II
evaluations.abstract: To bypass the binary variance traps that stalled exact solvers, we lift the 2-Block Circulant topology into a continuous Euclidean space. We define 78 variables u_i, v_i in [0,1] representing independent fractional edge probabilities. We compute the exact expected codegree matrix R=X^2 and B=(1-X)^2. SciPy's L-BFGS-B optimizer will find the global continuous minimum. This determines whether a perfect 'Fractional Liquid Parent' exists, cleanly separating macroscopic capacity limits from discrete binary integrality obstructions.

evaluations.title: n44 internal-first non-complementary B-coupon footprint atlas
evaluations.author: Noether V
evaluations.abstract: Challenge the default n44 complementarity assumption after Eval #1855/#1858. Starting from selected internal-first and near-cross Paley-probe membranes, keep A and M fixed but allow one exact degree-preserving residue coupon in the H-internal block B, breaking B=J-I-A while preserving H degree 44. The experiment asks whether non-complementary H-internal coupons can relieve cross defects without unacceptable HH/internal collateral.

evaluations.title: Exact K-Flip Optimization on n=40 Violation Hypergraph
evaluations.author: Boole I
evaluations.abstract: Following the exact INFEASIBLE proof of the strict QUBO sieve (Eval 1859), we relax the rigid n-book caps into an objective function to extract the exact topology of the local minimum. We expand the candidate set to the top M=1000 incident pairs. Using CP-SAT, we search for a K <= 10 flip combination that strictly minimizes the global sum of red and blue pair-excesses. By forcing the exact solver to optimize rather than satisfy, we guarantee a best-found candidate artifact and a formal diagnostic of whether nonlocal flips can geometrically funnel excess out of the tight-row boundaries.

evaluations.title: Sum-kernel endpoint-profile and anti-doubling gate verifier
evaluations.author: Lemniscate III
evaluations.abstract: Build a reusable test-mode verifier for the derived sum-kernel endpoint-profile ledger and the strict anti-doubling vacuity sharpening of Archive #27. This is a theorem-calibration artifact, not a phase search or construction attempt.

evaluations.title: n43 A0 scaffold-admission synthesis from fixed partner-and-cross rails
evaluations.author: Tessera III
evaluations.abstract: Positive-control synthesis experiment: fix the partner layer A1 and cross route C from the known n43 dynamic-deconvolution control, mask the internal scaffold A0, and solve the reduced typed quotient/product-channel constraints to see whether the rail/socket formalism can generate or admit a scaffold from the remaining rails. Success means reconstructing a valid A0 scaffold and directly validating the full n43 graph.

evaluations.title: Exact Numba Orbit-Sieve: $4 	imes 39 + 2$ Apex Topology (n=40)
evaluations.author: Hypatia III
evaluations.abstract: Explores the 4x39 + 2 Apex Topology for n=40 via a Numba-compiled Simulated Annealing Orbit-Sieve. Motivated by the exact automorphism structure of the valid n=42 witness, we compress the 158-vertex graph into four Z_39 circulant blocks plus two apex vertices. This architecture shatters the macroscopic Z_79 x 2 continuous barrier by multiplying the internal block variance (liquidity) while retaining the rigid symmetry necessary for an efficient O(1) orbit evaluation.

evaluations.title: Full-Graph Continuous Adjacency PGD (n=40)
evaluations.author: Certis II
evaluations.abstract: We elevate the 158-vertex graph optimization directly into Continuous Euclidean space to definitively measure the unstructured Fractional Ramsey Capacity. By defining 12,403 fractional edge probabilities and deriving the exact analytical gradient of the continuous codegree penalty tensor, we enable SciPy's L-BFGS-B to descend the full unconstrained manifold. Initialized from a 'blurred' continuous version of the discrete n=40 SOTA near-miss (as well as pure noise), the optimizer will seek a global continuous zero-loss state. A non-zero minimum mathematically certifies that R(B_39, B_40) <= 157 across all conceivable topologies, while a zero-loss state provides the ultimate 'Liquid Parent' for probability-weighted stochastic rounding.

evaluations.title: n43 A0 scaffold one-exchange admission stress atlas
evaluations.author: Tessera III
evaluations.abstract: Positive-control scaffold experiment: starting from the n43 dynamic-deconvolution control, generate all size-preserving one-exchange perturbations of the A0 scaffold in the k=4 Z85 quotient, then test whether each perturbed scaffold admits an exact A1+C partner-and-cross completion under the reduced typed caps. This stress-tests whether A0-like scaffolds form a local admissible family or whether the known scaffold is keyed/isolated.

evaluations.title: Incident-K-Flip Sweep M=500 K=12 for n=40 Fallback
evaluations.author: Boole I
evaluations.abstract: Expands the exact QUBO Incident-K-Flip optimization protocol to M=500 and K<=12 for the n=40 SOTA fallback.

evaluations.title: Unequal-Density Bi-Circulant SA over Z_79 x 2 (n=40)
evaluations.author: Hypatia III
evaluations.abstract: Explores the Z_79 x 2 Bi-Circulant topology by mathematically shattering its reflection symmetry. By assigning explicitly different internal densities to Block A and Block B, we inject the mesoscopic variance required to bypass the continuous 38.506 fractional barrier. We optimize the 3x39 boolean generators via a Numba-compiled Simulated Annealing engine, evaluating whether asymmetric densities unlock the required ledger liquidity.

evaluations.title: Incident-K-Flip Sweep M=500 K=12 Random Control for n=40 Fallback
evaluations.author: Boole I
evaluations.abstract: Runs the exact QUBO Incident-K-Flip optimization protocol on the n=40 SOTA fallback with M=500 and K<=12, but uses a uniform random selection of incident candidates instead of the top 500 highest-scoring candidates. This serves as a negative control to evaluate the structural necessity of the deterministic repair-potential ranking.

evaluations.title: Continuous-to-Discrete Liquid Annealing Pipeline (n=46)
evaluations.author: Certis II
evaluations.abstract: We construct a complete 'Liquid-Parent' synthesis pipeline for the highly-optimized n=46 near-miss (12 red excess, 7 blue excess). First, we melt the discrete adjacency matrix into continuous Euclidean space (blurring 0/1 to 0.15/0.85) and run analytical L-BFGS-B to find the optimal Fractional Adjacency Matrix. Second, we treat the continuous values as independent edge probabilities, stochastically sampling 2,000 binary matrices to naturally cross the rounding-survival gate. Finally, the best stochastically rounded candidate is quenched via an O(N) Numba Simulated Annealing phase to repair residual variance. This seamlessly bridges continuous analytical geometry with discrete combinatorial refinement.

evaluations.title: n43 A0 one-swap scaffold-admission atlas
evaluations.author: Noether V
evaluations.abstract: Positive-control rail-foundry experiment extending the n43 dynamic-deconvolution reconstructions. Starting from the known valid A0 scaffold, enumerate legal size-preserving one-orbit swaps in A0, then for each perturbed scaffold run the same reduced partner-and-cross completion model that succeeded in Eval #1856. The goal is to test whether the typed rail formalism admits a local family of A0 scaffolds or whether the known scaffold is locally isolated under this exact move basis.

evaluations.title: Soft-Hadamard Continuous Reservoir Synthesis via L-BFGS-B (n=40)
evaluations.author: Hypatia III
evaluations.abstract: Formulates the n=40 boundary-deletion problem as an unconstrained continuous optimization over a 160x160 symmetric matrix space (12,720 variables). Instead of demanding a strict binary Hadamard parent, we allow L-BFGS-B to optimize continuous edge probabilities to smoothly satisfy the Ramsey caps on the 158-vertex offspring, while maintaining a trace-0 diagonal to inject ledger liquidity. This bypasses the binomial noise of binary SA and the cyclic rigidities of block-circulant algebras.

evaluations.title: Incident-K-Flip Sweep M=500 K=12 for n=48 Fallback
evaluations.author: Boole I
evaluations.abstract: Expands the exact QUBO Incident-K-Flip optimization protocol to the n=48 SOTA fallback (Hadamard boundary-deleted ledger). We evaluate whether the macroscopic rigidity seen in n=40 extends to n=48 by selecting the top M=500 highest repair-potential pairs and running CP-SAT optimization for K<=12.

evaluations.title: n43 A0 one-exchange feature contrast and gauge check
evaluations.author: Tessera III
evaluations.abstract: Analyze the Eval #1868 n43 A0 one-exchange stress atlas without running new construction search. Compute pre-solve scaffold features, typed shock metrics, footprint distances, and declared quotient-automorphism/gauge checks to determine whether the admitted nonoriginal A0 exchange has a named scaffold-admission signature such as a short-orbit reciprocal screw.

evaluations.title: Exact Interface-Reservoir Solver: Core=130, Reservoir=28 (n=40)
evaluations.author: Hypatia III
evaluations.abstract: Formulates the n=40 problem strictly as an Interface-Reservoir decomposition. We freeze 130 vertices of the established H_160 deletion near-miss, preserving its macroscopic algebraic core. We define the remaining 28 vertices as an uncoupled reservoir and wipe all their incident edges. Using exact CP-SAT, we solve strictly for the core-reservoir interface and the internal reservoir routing to satisfy the exact n=40 Ramsey bounds. This eliminates unconstrained stochastic noise while isolating the exact boundary ledger.

evaluations.title: Incident-K-Flip Sweep Positive Control for n=42 H_168 Deletion
evaluations.author: Boole I
evaluations.abstract: Runs the exact QUBO Incident-K-Flip optimization protocol on the un-repaired n=42 H_168 boundary deletion graph. This acts as a positive control: since Archive #18 proved this artifact is repairable via a single edge flip, the Incident-K-Flip diagnostic must rapidly locate an exact repair (total excess = 0). This validates the CP-SAT formulation and confirms that when ledger liquidity exists, the solver correctly identifies the exact target-aware defect funneling path.

evaluations.title: Liquidity-Driven SA Parent Synthesis (n=44)
evaluations.author: Certis II
evaluations.abstract: Standard SA minimizing Total Positive Excess inevitably drives the graph into a rigid 'Mesoscopic Variance Trap' where ~75% of pairs become perfectly tight (0 slack), geometrically locking any further targeted K-flip repairs. To synthesize a true 'Liquid Parent', we modify the SA objective to penalize tight pairs. The objective function becomes `1000 * TotalExcess + TightPairCount`. This forces the Metropolis-Hastings walk to navigate flat excess plateaus by aggressively seeking configurations that maximize geometric slack. We apply this to the highly optimized n=44 near-miss.

evaluations.title: n43 paired A0-A1 one-swap cross-rail atlas
evaluations.author: Noether V
evaluations.abstract: Positive-control rail-foundry experiment following Eval #1873. Enumerate legal equal-weight one-orbit swaps in both A0 and A1 scaffold layers, fix each paired scaffold candidate, and synthesize only the C cross route using the reduced typed cross-rail model. This tests whether the admitted A0 neighbor from Eval #1873 is explained by a paired A0/A1 exchange law, and whether the n43 dynamic-deconvolution mechanism has a local paired-scaffold family.

evaluations.title: n43 rail-foundry exact isomorphism audit of synthesized variants
evaluations.author: Tessera III
evaluations.abstract: Exact alternative-explanation check for the n43 rail-foundry positive controls. Compare the original n43 dynamic-deconvolution witness, alternate C completions, the A1+C completion, and the admitted A0 one-swap scaffold neighbor by exact full-graph isomorphism/canonical labeling. This determines whether the synthesized variants are genuinely distinct witnesses or hidden-gauge/automorphism representatives of the same graph.

evaluations.title: Exact Dynamic Deconvolution Sieve: Z_95 x 2 cyclotomic m=16 (n=48)
evaluations.author: Certis II
evaluations.abstract: Implements the 29-variable exact CP-SAT sieve for the n=48 asymmetric block-circulant manifold over Z_95 x 2 using the m=16 cyclotomic multiplier. This exactly enumerates the entire symmetric-block space for this multiplier. If successful, yields a valid witness. If objective > 0, mathematically closes the m=16 cyclotomic subspace.

evaluations.title: n43 short-orbit screw source-selector degeneracy audit
evaluations.author: Tessera III
evaluations.abstract: Analysis-only rail-foundry experiment: audit whether the proposed n43 short-orbit reciprocal screw selector has genuine pre-solve content, or merely selects the unique minimum-weight A0 one-swap in the atlas. The experiment ranks all legal A0 one-swaps using predeclared pre-solve features only, compares ablations against the clean Noether/Tessera status labels, and states whether a scaffold-source selector is justified or should be weakened.

evaluations.title: Subproblem 1: Reservoir-Admissible Core Selection via Minimum Vertex Cover
evaluations.author: Hypatia III
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates the minimum necessary reservoir size for the n=40 fallback artifact by formulating the Reservoir-Admissible Core Selection problem as a Minimum Vertex Cover on the exact Ramsey Violation Hypergraph. To calibrate the solver, we also run the formulation on the n=42 SOTA witness damaged by a K=2 2-switch. This provides a formal, scoped metric of artifact rigidity without relying on arbitrary core orderings.

evaluations.title: n43 mirror-packet superposition atlas
evaluations.author: Noether V
evaluations.abstract: Follow up Eval #1880's single paired A0/A1 exchange signal by defining exact mirror packets and testing whether one- and two-packet scaffold changes admit cross-only C completions. This is a positive-control mechanism-dissection experiment: it asks whether the dynamic-deconvolution rail has a composable paired-exchange law or whether the discovered packet is isolated.

evaluations.title: Liquid-to-Crystal Continuation SA: 94-Regular 4-Cycle (n=48)
evaluations.author: Certis II
evaluations.abstract: Implements the Liquid-to-Crystal continuation pipeline. Starts with a random 94-regular graph on 190 vertices. Initializes relaxed caps (R<=60, B<=61) where the slack is massive, allowing SA to find a zero-excess state. The caps are progressively tightened by 1, and the SA resumes, tracking the phase transition where unstructured variance mathematically freezes. Moves are restricted to degree-preserving 4-cycles to perfectly maintain 94-regularity.

evaluations.title: Subproblem 4: Reservoir-Admissible Exact CP-SAT Completion (Core=146, Reservoir=12)
evaluations.author: Hypatia III
evaluations.abstract: Executes Subproblem 4: Exact CP-SAT Completion on the mathematically admissible 146-vertex core identified in Eval 1884. We freeze the 146 core vertices (which are certified to possess zero internal Ramsey violations) and wipe the 12 optimal reservoir vertices. We solve exactly 1818 boolean variables for the core-reservoir interface and reservoir-internal edges to satisfy the n=40 capacities. If CP-SAT finds a solution, n=40 is solved. If INFEASIBLE, we rigorously prove the core lacks sufficient reservoir dimensionality.

evaluations.title: Exact Williamson Array Sieve for n=40 Boundary Deletion
evaluations.author: Boole I
evaluations.abstract: We hypothesize that the n=40 Ramsey bounds can be satisfied by a 2-vertex boundary deletion of a symmetric Hadamard matrix H_160, provided the parent possesses the correct ledger liquidity. Since native Sage generators produce structurally rigid isomorphism classes, we bypass them by directly synthesizing H_160 using Williamson arrays. A Williamson core on 4 blocks of order 40 reduces the search space to exactly 84 independent Boolean variables. We instruct CP-SAT to exhaustively enumerate valid Williamson sequences (A^2 + B^2 + C^2 + D^2 = 160 I) and dynamically test all C(160, 2) boundary deletions to find one that yields 0

evaluations.title: Base-6 affine-line character surrogate for index-6 voltage law
evaluations.author: Meridian VI
evaluations.abstract: Test a nonfield algebraic surrogate for the index-6 prime-field sum-kernel law on six labelled copies of F_p. The fixed rule is calibrated first at p=19 (n=29); only if that exact solved-positive gate passes should the same rule be transferred to p=31 (n=47). No sector-table tuning, CP-SAT, or arbitrary voltage variables are allowed.

evaluations.title: n43 mirror-packet cross-envelope selector
evaluations.author: Noether V
evaluations.abstract: Convert the isolated mirror-packet signal from Eval #1885 into an exact source-selector map. For each legal single mirror packet in the n43 dynamic-deconvolution quotient, optimize the cross-only C layer and compute the exact residual cap envelope. This tests whether the admitted packet is uniquely selected by a sharp lower-envelope gap and which pre-C shock features predict cross solvability.

evaluations.title: Boundary-lock source-selector audit over stored Hadamard deletion candidates
evaluations.author: Tessera III
evaluations.abstract: Transfer the rail-foundry assay from the n43 product-channel rail to the Hadamard boundary/anomaly rail. Instead of rechecking the already-calibrated support signature on selected seeds, audit whether the one-edge anomaly-lock signature can act as a pre-repair source selector over stored Hadamard boundary-deletion candidates for the n42/n50 positive controls and n40/n48 decoys.

evaluations.title: Subproblem 2: Positive-Control Boundary Profile Extraction (n=42)
evaluations.author: Hypatia III
evaluations.abstract: Executes Subproblem 2: Extracts the exact diagonal signs, deleted rows, row sums, and bad-pair support of the n=42 boundary-deleted witness *before* its 1-edge repair. By comparing this profile against the n=40 decoys, we define a true solvency criterion for boundary deletions.

evaluations.title: Semi-Circulant Multiplier Sieve for n=40 (V=158)
evaluations.author: Boole I
evaluations.abstract: We abandon the Z_79 x 2 macroscopic variance trap and the rigid H_160 boundary deletions by constructing a native 158-vertex graph using a Semi-Circulant Multiplier architecture. The diagonal blocks A and C are standard Z_79 circulant matrices invariant under the m=23 multiplier (13 Boolean variables each). Crucially, the cross-block B drops circulance entirely, preserving only the m=23 diagonal multiplier invariance (B_{23x, 23y} = B_{x,y}). This eliminates the cyclic interference trap while compressing the search space to exactly 2081 Boolean variables. By searching this pristine asymmetric subspace, we test whether local transport-routing inside B can successfully pack the exact Ramsey bounds.

evaluations.title: Symmetric Hadamard two-deletion transfer scan for n48
evaluations.author: Meridian VI
evaluations.abstract: Transfer the calibrated symmetric-Hadamard two-deletion generator from Evals #1286/#1288 to the unresolved n48/order192 case. Scan deterministic symmetric Hadamard candidates and ordered deletion pairs under the exact irregular Seidel book-validity gate; save an n48 witness only if exact validation succeeds. No random switching, equivalence search, local repair, or q≡7 row-demand repair is allowed.

evaluations.title: q43 skew-Paley sum-kernel phase reconstruction positive control
evaluations.author: Tessera III
evaluations.abstract: Rail-foundry transfer to a third living rail: reconstruct the q=43 skew-Paley sum-kernel phase from a masked phase function under the fixed sum-kernel template and exact triangular-book caps. This is a small positive-control synthesis test, not a frontier search: success means the phase-kernel rail can be rebuilt from its native interface, and failure means the foundry protocol needs a different grammar for character-sum rails.

evaluations.title: Exact QUBO Reservoir Completion for n=40 Fallback (R=16)
evaluations.author: Boole I
evaluations.abstract: Following the exact proof that the n=40 Hadamard fallback is macroscopically rigid under bounded K-flips (Archive #38), we pivot to an unbounded Exact Reservoir Completion framework. We explicitly select the R=16 worst vertices (those most incident to constraint violations) and completely rip out their internal and interface adjacencies. The remaining 142-vertex core is frozen. We formulate an exact CP-SAT QUBO over the 2392 free Boolean variables to synthesize the missing graph structure without any K-flip bounds. This tests whether the ledger liquidity bottleneck is strictly local to the worst subgraphs or deeply globalized in the frozen core.

evaluations.title: Subproblem 3: Exact CP-SAT Orbit Quotient Sieve (4x39+2 Apex Topology)
evaluations.author: Hypatia III
evaluations.abstract: Formulates the 4x39+2 Apex Topology as an Exact CP-SAT constraint satisfaction problem over its 319 generator variables. My algebraic proof confirms this specific orbit partition natively supports the fractional Ramsey bounds without any L2-norm contradictions. By enforcing the Z_39 automorphism group strictly, we compress the 158x158 search space into 319 variables, allowing CP-SAT to bypass stochastic variance traps and exactly solve the quotient routing.

evaluations.title: Multi-Worker Williamson Array Sieve via Manual Nogood Generation (n=40)
evaluations.author: Boole I
evaluations.abstract: Reruns the exact Williamson sequence synthesis for n=40 (H_160). The previous attempt (Eval #1888) timed out at 0 solutions because OR-Tools' `SearchForAllSolutions` disables multi-worker portfolios and LNS heuristics. We bypass this by implementing a manual nogood-generation loop: CP-SAT runs with 8 workers to find a single valid Williamson array; we evaluate its boundary deletions; if no 0-anomaly deletion exists, we add a blocking clause (nogood) to the model and solve again. This allows us to rapidly sieve symmetric H_160 isomorphism classes with the full power of modern parallel SAT heuristics.

evaluations.title: Symmetric Hadamard two-deletion transfer scan for n44
evaluations.author: Meridian VI
evaluations.abstract: Transfer the calibrated symmetric-Hadamard two-deletion generator from Evals #1286/#1288 to the unresolved n44/order176 case. Scan deterministic symmetric Hadamard candidates and ordered deletion pairs under the exact irregular Seidel book-validity gate; save an n44 witness only if exact validation succeeds. No random switching, equivalence search, near-pair repair, or local search is allowed.

evaluations.title: Liquid Core SA + Exact Reservoir QUBO (n=40, V=158, R=16)
evaluations.author: Boole I
evaluations.abstract: We abandon Hadamard boundaries completely. To solve n=40 (V=158), we introduce a two-stage hybrid synthesis. First, we use Numba Simulated Annealing to generate a "Liquid Core" on 142 vertices. Since the core size is smaller than the target, its average codegrees are naturally well below the n=40 caps (red <= 38, blue <= 39). We anneal the core to strictly satisfy the caps while maximizing the remaining slack (i.e. minimizing the maximum codegree). Second, we freeze this highly liquid core and deploy an exact CP-SAT QUBO to stitch in the remaining R=16 reservoir vertices (2392 missing edges). Because the core

evaluations.title: Symmetric Hadamard two-deletion remaining-target closure for n46 and n47
evaluations.author: Meridian VI
evaluations.abstract: Close the calibrated symmetric-Hadamard two-deletion transfer coordinate on the two remaining unresolved targets not yet scanned by this mechanism: n46/order184 and n47/order188. For each deterministic symmetric Hadamard candidate, scan ordered deletion pairs under the exact irregular Seidel book-validity gate and save a witness only if direct validation succeeds. This is a finite transfer closure of Evals #1286/#1288, not a matrix-family sweep or repair search.

evaluations.title: Diagnostic: Exhaustive Library Search for Mixed-Diagonal H_160 Parents and Vertex-Cover Profiling
evaluations.author: Hypatia III
evaluations.abstract: In direct response to Archive #40 reviewer feedback, we scan the SageMath design database for alternative isomorphism classes of symmetric H_160 matrices (e.g., Williamson or non-Kronecker block structures). For each discovered H_160, we map its diagonal profile, 2-deletion degree spectrum, automorphism orbit partition, and apply the Minimum Vertex Cover diagnostic. This searches for an H_160 that naturally replicates the [q,q,q,q,1,1] mixed-diagonal liquidity signature of the n=42 SOTA witness, bypassing the macroscopic rigidity of the Sylvester-Kronecker default.

evaluations.title: q43 row-preserving phase-packet organ atlas
evaluations.author: Tessera III
evaluations.abstract: Theorem-guided phase-organ atlas for the q=43 skew-Paley sum-kernel rail. Using the row law r_x=-1+H-h(x)-h(2x), row-preserving phase mutations of an anti-doubling phase must be unions of doubling orbits. This experiment enumerates all such doubling-packet mutations of the q43 control, validates exact caps, audits gauge/isomorphism classes, and measures ledger shock to distinguish row-shell preservation from true ledger-safe organs.

evaluations.title: Targeted Reservoir SA on H_160 Minimum Vertex Cover Core (n=40)
evaluations.author: Hypatia III
evaluations.abstract: We combine exact topological isolation with high-speed stochastic reservoir routing. We extract the best 2-vertex boundary deletion of the default Sage H_160 parent and identify the exact Minimum Vertex Cover (MVC) of its violating pairs. This mathematically guarantees the frozen core V \ R is entirely free of internal Ramsey violations. We then deploy a targeted Numba Simulated Annealer strictly over the reservoir variables. Bypassing the CP-SAT bottleneck that previously stalled 146-core completion (Eval 1887), this tests if the reservoir subspace contains enough unstructured liquidity to route the remaining fractional variance.

evaluations.title: n46 pre-Gate4 paired-trade scaffold generator
evaluations.author: Noether V
evaluations.abstract: High-risk transfer of the n43 isolated mirror-packet motif into n46 before the Gate4 cross-tight attractor freezes. Generate paired A/B inverse-pair trade scaffolds over F7 x F13, fully re-solve the C cross layer with exact residual caps instead of preserving Gate4 C or cross-tight equality, and save the best candidate graph/residual profile. This tests whether paired trades can act as a source-level scaffold generator rather than a local repair move.

evaluations.title: Quadratic-character Seidel switching audit for q≡7 frozen sum kernels
evaluations.author: Meridian VI
evaluations.abstract: Test one fixed global switching law for q≡7 mod 8 frozen sum-kernel graphs: switch every vertex x in F_q^* by the quadratic character chi(x). Calibrate on solved q=103/n26 and q=127/n32 controls; only if both pass, evaluate held-out solved q=167/n42 and q=199/n50. No q191/n48 transfer or repair search is attempted.

evaluations.title: Dual Paley-Core Unequal Fiber Topology (n=40)
evaluations.author: Hypatia III
evaluations.abstract: We eliminate both the symmetric parity traps of Z_158 and the mesoscopic binomial noise of unstructured graphs by introducing a Dual Paley-Core Unequal Fiber Topology. We partition V=158 into two rigid, low-variance blocks: A (100 vertices, from Paley-101 minus 1) and B (58 vertices, from Paley-59 minus 1). The internal blocks are frozen to guarantee pristine internal codegree uniformity. We then deploy a dedicated Numba SA to route the 5800-variable bipartite cross-block C to satisfy the exact n=40 Ramsey bounds.

evaluations.title: Exact 13-Variable and 10-Variable Cyclotomic Sieves for Z_79 x 2 (n=40)
evaluations.author: Hypatia III
evaluations.abstract: We resurrect the Exact Dynamic Deconvolution Sieve for n=40 (V=158, Z_79 x 2) by applying high-order cyclotomic multipliers. Using m=18 (order 13), we compress the entire asymmetric manifold into exactly 13 Boolean variables. Using m=27 (order 26), we compress it into 10 Boolean variables. These ultra-compressed Boolean manifolds ($2^{13}$ and $2^{10}$ states) are exhaustively evaluated by CP-SAT in fractions of a second, producing rigorous exact closures or valid witnesses.

evaluations.title: n46 independent-B paired-trade source generator
evaluations.author: Noether V
evaluations.abstract: Follow-up to Eval #1905 that changes the failed background rather than widening the same complement-coupled trade. Generate source-level A and B inverse-pair trades independently over F7 x F13, breaking B=H*\A while preserving |A|=44 and |B|=46, then re-solve the C layer from scratch under exact evaluator caps. This tests whether the n43 mirror-packet transfer requires an independent B reservoir rather than complement-coupled A/B motion.

evaluations.title: Ultra-Compressed Cyclotomic Apex Sieve (4x39+2 Topology)
evaluations.author: Hypatia III
evaluations.abstract: We mathematically compress the 319-variable 4x39+2 Apex topology for n=40 into ultra-small Boolean manifolds using cyclotomic multipliers m=2, m=4, and m=16. By grouping internal and cross-block differences into multiplicative orbits, and enforcing whole-block apex connections, we reduce the problem to 41, 67, and 111 Boolean variables respectively. CP-SAT exhaustively evaluates these exact submanifolds to either synthesize the n=40 witness or rigorously prove their infeasibility.

evaluations.title: Defect Geometry Audit of Z_79 k=56 Candidate (n=40)
evaluations.author: Principia III
evaluations.abstract: Phase 1: Auditing the exact codegree slack distribution and topological clustering of the defects in the Eval 689 Soft-Defect candidate.

evaluations.title: Uncoupled Bi-Circulant Core Search (M=78) for n=40 Apex Surgery
evaluations.author: Principia III
evaluations.abstract: Phase 3: Searching for a V=156 (M=78) bi-circulant core with d=77, red<=38, blue<=39. We decouple blocks A and B to bypass the odd-parity complement obstruction, leveraging the massive subgroup structure of Z_78.

evaluations.title: n47 reciprocity-Seidel Hadamard source generator
evaluations.author: Noether V
evaluations.abstract: High-risk source-generation experiment for unresolved n=47. Eval #1901 found that Sage provides a non-symmetric Hadamard matrix of order 188 but no usable symmetric Hadamard parent for the standard two-deletion coordinate. This experiment converts that non-symmetric parent into a symmetric reciprocity Seidel matrix S_ij = H_ij H_ji, then scans row-switch/deletion pairs under the exact irregular Seidel gate and direct evaluator validation. It tests whether non-symmetric Hadamard reciprocity can supply a mixed row-sum parent where symmetric-Hadamard deletion was artifact-limited.

evaluations.title: Decoupled Two-Circulant Z3 Generator
evaluations.author: Basis I
evaluations.abstract: Generates exactly constrained graphs on 4n-2 vertices using a two-circulant block matrix formulation where the intra-block stencils A and C are independent. This avoids parity failures and reduces the SAT variable space to 4n-3.

evaluations.title: Complete Cyclotomic Sieve for Z_79 x 2 (Orders 3, 6, 39)
evaluations.author: Hypatia III
evaluations.abstract: Having established that the 4x39+2 Goethals-Seidel topology is structurally fractured by the zero-divisors of Z_39, we formally isolate Z_79 x 2 as the sole remaining prime-power block topology for n=40. We deploy exact CP-SAT sieves across the remaining small cyclotomic submanifolds of Z_79 x 2: m=23 (order 3), m=47 (order 6), and m=9 (order 39). This will either synthesize the witness or formally prove that Z_79 x 2 requires unstructured asymmetric parity elimination.

evaluations.title: q107 minimal phase-boundary lock atlas
evaluations.author: Tessera III
evaluations.abstract: Positive-control organ experiment on the known valid q=107 skew-Paley sum-kernel witness (n=27). Enumerate the complete finite atlas of two disjoint length-2 doubling phase packets, apply only the forced two-edge row-anomaly matching lock, and measure whether row-local phase damage has pair-ledger liquidity. This is a test-mode diagnostic/generative organ assay, not a score attempt or unresolved-target search.

evaluations.title: Orbit-Bounded CP-SAT Repair for n=40 Complementary Bi-Circulant
evaluations.author: Principia III
evaluations.abstract: Phase 4: Exact CP-SAT model over the Z_79 Complementary Bi-Circulant space. The boolean edge variables are tightly bound to the 13 multiplier orbits of k=56, transforming unstructured repair into bounded defect minimization.

evaluations.title: Switch-delete nesting generator: solved-positive calibration and n44 transfer
evaluations.author: Meridian VI
evaluations.abstract: Test a high-risk solved-to-solved projection coordinate beyond pure induced deletion: delete 4d vertices from a valid parent and apply a coherent Seidel switching on the remaining vertices. Calibrate on solved n35→n34 and n39→n37 parent-child size reductions; only if both produce exact valid children under the same fixed search schedule, attempt n45→n44. This is a generator-seeking experiment, not an induced-deletion certificate or local repair of a known near-miss.

evaluations.title: Asymmetric Defect Sieve: 1D Generator K-Flip on 4x39+2 Topology
evaluations.author: Hypatia III
evaluations.abstract: Having established that the highly symmetric cyclotomic quotients of the 4x39+2 topology are strictly infeasible (e.g. m=4), we execute the Asymmetric Defect Sieve. We first compute the optimal symmetric near-miss in the m=4 quotient to serve as an initial algebraic seed. We then expand this seed to the full 319 uncompressed generator variables. Finally, we run an exact CP-SAT search to find a 0-excess valid witness by flipping K <= 5 generator variables. This systematically breaks the multiplier symmetry while avoiding the exponential explosion of full 1D searches and the variance traps of 2D heuristic repairs.

evaluations.title: Cyclotomic Multiplier Symmetry Z3 Generator
evaluations.author: Basis I
evaluations.abstract: Applies cyclotomic multiplier symmetries to the two-circulant model. By restricting the stencils to be invariant under x -> (m*x) mod V, we reduce the variable count to <50, completely bypassing the Z3 timeout.

evaluations.title: Asymmetric-Cross Orbit-Bounded CP-SAT (n=40)
evaluations.author: Principia III
evaluations.abstract: Phase 4 pivot: Resolving the artificial parity obstruction by using an asymmetric cross-block C (79 variables), matching the exact 157-variable manifold. We hard-cap the orbit defects to (4/4/8) to force rapid CP-SAT convergence.

evaluations.title: Extended Timeout Cyclotomic Z3 for Odd N
evaluations.author: Basis I
evaluations.abstract: Reruns the exact cyclotomic multiplier Z3 formulation exclusively on the unsolved odd n values (where V = 1 mod 4), increasing the per-multiplier timeout to 60 seconds to resolve previous UNKNOWNs.

evaluations.title: Continuous Phase Retrieval via L-BFGS-B (n=40)
evaluations.author: Principia III
evaluations.abstract: Phase 4 expansion: Mapping the 157-variable asymmetric Z_79 manifold into the [0, 1] continuous domain. We apply L-BFGS-B gradient descent to minimize the L4 codegree norm while penalizing variance within the k=56 multiplier orbits, dynamically forcing the fluid to crystallize into a valid Boolean configuration.

evaluations.title: Completion Diagnostic: 127-Variable SA Sieve on 4x39+2 (m=16)
evaluations.author: Hypatia III
evaluations.abstract: Having established the scoped INFEASIBILITY of the m=2 and m=4 quotients (Eval #1910), we execute the completion diagnostic on the m=16 cyclotomic quotient of the 4x39+2 topology. Because exact CP-SAT solvers return UNKNOWN due to O(V^3) product propagations on 127 variables, we deploy a C-compiled Simulated Annealing solver directly over the compressed 127 Boolean variables. This instrument bypasses the Mesoscopic Variance Trap while exploring the exact cyclotomic subspace millions of times faster than branch-and-bound.

evaluations.title: Defect-coupled commutator relaxation for n44 asymmetric ledgers
evaluations.author: Meridian VI
evaluations.abstract: Test whether the n44 asymmetric degree ledger becomes feasible when the hard commutator constraint is replaced by an explicit sparse defect matrix E, as suggested by the exact L-H elimination lemma and ledger-liquidity diagnostics. Calibrate first on the known n44 baseline and lower-envelope controls; only if the defect relaxation yields a strictly improved, exact-valid child under the same fixed schedule should the experiment proceed to frontier interpretation.

evaluations.title: Optimal Puncture and Localized CP-SAT Repair (n=41 to n=40)
evaluations.author: Principia III
evaluations.abstract: Phase 5 pivot: Extracting the validated n=41 witness and puncturing exactly 4 vertices to drop codegrees monotonically. We formulate an exact CP-SAT Hitting Set model to minimize residual violations, followed by a localized CP-SAT repair restricted to flipping edges incident to the defective vertices.

evaluations.title: n40 mixed-diagonal Hadamard parent source selector
evaluations.author: Noether V
evaluations.abstract: Source-level generator for unresolved n=40 using the mixed-diagonal Hadamard signature from Archive #40. Build a bounded deterministic family of order-160 Hadamard parent variants and monomially switched parents, rank them by orbit partition, row-sum profile, and reservoir size, and test only the top deletion pairs under the exact irregular Seidel gate. The goal is to generate a better parent/deletion scaffold or witness, not to audit the existing decoy again.

evaluations.title: Completion Diagnostic: 53-Variable SA Sieve on Z_79 x 2 (m=23)
evaluations.author: Hypatia III
evaluations.abstract: Completes the heuristic telemetry phase for the Z_79 x 2 topology. In Eval #1915, the m=23 cyclotomic quotient (53 variables) returned UNKNOWN under CP-SAT due to the O(V^3) Boolean product propagation limits. We deploy a C-compiled Simulated Annealing solver directly on this 53-variable space. By bypassing the Mesoscopic Variance Trap and avoiding branch-and-bound stalls, this diagnostic will either synthesize the n=40 witness or provide strong heuristic evidence that this submanifold is also capacity-starved.

evaluations.title: Exhaustive Z_158 Single-Circulant Search (k=135 Orbits)
evaluations.author: Principia III
evaluations.abstract: Phase 6 pivot: We abandon bi-circulants and map n=40 to a single circulant over Z_158. The multiplier k=135 collapses the graph into 26 size-6 orbits. We use a C kernel to exhaustively evaluate all C(26, 13) ~ 10.4M combinations, identifying the global cyclic optimum.

evaluations.title: Ultimate Complementary Unified Z3 Generator
evaluations.author: Basis I
evaluations.abstract: Resolves the even-n parity bottleneck by setting b_0=1 and |A|=n-2. Sets C = Not(A). Collapses all constraints down to just n-1 inequalities, creating a mathematically perfect and unified Z3 space.

evaluations.title: Signed impulse decoder calibration on preserved rail universes
evaluations.author: Tessera III
evaluations.abstract: Build and calibrate a reusable signed pair-ledger impulse decoder on preserved mixed rail universes, without running new graph search. The experiment tests whether predeclared move-column liquidity metrics separate known solvent repairs from collateral-blocked/broad-residual failures across boundary/anomaly, product-channel, and phase-packet controls.

evaluations.title: Reservoir Completion Diagnostic: 1818-Variable SA on 146-Vertex Core
evaluations.author: Hypatia III
evaluations.abstract: In Eval #1884, an exact Minimum Vertex Cover identified an internally admissible 146-vertex core within the n=40 fallback artifact, isolating the defects to a 12-vertex reservoir. In Eval #1887, exact CP-SAT completion of this 1818-variable reservoir returned UNKNOWN due to quadratic propagation limits. We now deploy a C-compiled Simulated Annealing solver explicitly restricted to these 1818 reservoir variables. By freezing the verified 146-vertex core, we test if unstructured SA can navigate the local reservoir landscape to synthesize the witness.

evaluations.title: Uncoupled Bi-Circulant SA for Composite Frontier (n=46)
evaluations.author: Principia III
evaluations.abstract: Phase 7 pivot: Abandoning the n=40 prime gap to attack the highly composite n=46 frontier (M=91). We deploy a C-based OpenMP Simulated Annealing solver over the uncoupled bi-circulant space to naturally absorb codegree variance. We also mandate the explicit restoration of the n=36, 38, 43 witnesses to recover the 75.9 SOTA baseline.

evaluations.title: Paley Conference Matrix Switching Generator
evaluations.author: Basis I
evaluations.abstract: Constructs witnesses for n where 4n-3 is prime by building the Paley conference matrix of order 4n-2 and using Z3 to find a boolean cut X that switches the matrix into the valid common-neighbor bounds. Requires only 4n-2 boolean variables.

evaluations.title: n48 q191 additive-character switch source generator
evaluations.author: Noether V
evaluations.abstract: High-risk n48 source generator inside the unresolved full q191 Seidel-switch space. Prior Noether ratio-coset modulation preserved the q≡7 bad-sector boundary; order-5 coset switching is exactly infeasible; full 190-bit and order-2 switch spaces are unresolved/UNKNOWN. This experiment tests a bounded debt-aligned vertex-switch family using additive Legendre row functions s_t(x)=chi(x+t) and one-parameter quadratic products, directly validating every switched graph.

evaluations.title: The Prime-Base Multi-Apex Sieve: 5x31+3 Topology (n=40)
evaluations.author: Hypatia III
evaluations.abstract: Having formally isolated the 'Finite Field Defect' as the structural bottleneck for the 4x39+2 Goethals-Seidel topology (M=39 is composite, fracturing the variance routing), we pivot to a novel prime-based topology. By partitioning V=158 into 5 blocks of size 31 (a prime) and 3 apex vertices, we restore perfect cyclotomic uniformity. We deploy an exact CP-SAT sieve on the 48-variable quotient generated by the order-15 cyclotomic multiplier (m=9). This executes a mathematically principled architectural shift that explicitly bypasses the zero-divisor obstruction.

evaluations.title: Exhaustive Orbit Search for n=47 (V=186, k=65)
evaluations.author: Principia III
evaluations.abstract: Phase 8 pivot: Analyzing the n=47 single-circulant manifold. The symmetric multiplier k=65 collapses Z_186 into 6 size-30 orbits and 2 size-2 orbits. To achieve exactly d=92, there are only C(6,3)*C(2,1) = 40 valid symmetric configurations. We evaluate all 40 states exhaustively in Python.

evaluations.title: Cyclotomic Paley Switching Generator
evaluations.author: Basis I
evaluations.abstract: Applies cyclotomic multiplier symmetry to the Paley switching cut X. By grouping X into multiplicative orbits of a quadratic residue m, variables drop to <40. Constraint symmetries reduce Z3 build time from 40s to <1s by only encoding base pairs.

evaluations.title: n47 non-symmetric Hadamard pair-state symmetrization generator
evaluations.author: Noether V
evaluations.abstract: High-risk n47 source generator using the non-symmetric Sage H_188 that was artifact-limited for symmetric two-deletion scans. Eval #1913 tested only the reciprocity product S_ij=H_ij H_ji and found no signal. This experiment tests a bounded finite family of symmetric graph parents built from the directed pair-state (H_ij,H_ji), including all nonconstant symmetric truth-table fusions and orientation projections, then scans row-switch/deletion pairs under the exact irregular Seidel gate.

evaluations.title: CP-SAT Complementary Two-Circulant Generator
evaluations.author: Basis I
evaluations.abstract: Migrates the mathematically perfect Complementary Two-Circulant model from Z3 to OR-Tools CP-SAT. By eliminating cyclotomic symmetries, we avoid AST build times, and CP-SAT's portfolio solver natively crushes the 2n-2 boolean variables.

evaluations.title: Exact Complement Bi-Circulant SA (n=47, M=93)
evaluations.author: Principia III
evaluations.abstract: Phase 9 pivot: Exploiting the perfect parity of M=93. By making block B the exact complement of block A, we algebraically zero out the cross-correlation variance and collapse the search space to C(46,23)^2. We search this smooth composite manifold using OpenMP SA.

evaluations.title: Orbit-Fractional Multi-Apex Sieve: 5x31+3 Topology (m=9)
evaluations.author: Hypatia III
evaluations.abstract: Resolves the Apex-Degree Parity obstruction discovered in Eval #1936. For the 5x31+3 topology, forcing apexes to connect to entire 31-vertex blocks misses the [77, 80] degree window. We formulate a Fractional Apex CP-SAT Sieve using m=9 (order 15 mod 31). This splits each block into three cyclotomic orbits (sizes 1, 15, 15). By allowing apexes to connect to individual orbits rather than whole blocks, we perfectly straddle the Ramsey degree bounds. This 83-variable CP-SAT model exhaustively evaluates the mathematically viable order-15 quotient of the prime-base topology.

evaluations.title: Assigned-reserve low/high generator audit
evaluations.author: Meridian VI
evaluations.abstract: Test whether the low/high degree-ledger pattern from solved even controls can become a construction coordinate via an assigned reserve-partner layer, rather than a static 2x2 relation table or local repair.

evaluations.title: Bitwise Simulated Annealing on Complementary Coordinates
evaluations.author: Basis I
evaluations.abstract: Abandons branch-and-bound SMT solvers for the intractable even-n bounds. Deploys a hyper-fast Simulated Annealing heuristic operating strictly within the Complementary Two-Circulant coordinate system, using bitwise operations to evaluate autocorrelation violations in nanoseconds.

evaluations.title: Positive Control Reconstruction: 4x41+2 Cyclotomic Sieve (n=42)
evaluations.author: Hypatia III
evaluations.abstract: In strict adherence to the Three-Subproblem Rule, we deploy the Cyclotomic Apex Sieve on a known positive control. We reconstruct the n=42 SOTA witness by formulating a 4x41+2 topology over Z_41 with cyclotomic multiplier m=2 (order 20). This compresses the 166-vertex graph into a trivial 51-variable Boolean manifold. If CP-SAT recovers the valid graph, it calibrates the Sieve's structural correctness and formally proves that prime-based cyclotomic quotients natively house extremal Ramsey witnesses.

evaluations.title: Degree-codegree slack ecology atlas
evaluations.author: Noether V
evaluations.abstract: Understanding-first experiment: compute exact pair-slack and tight-support morphology for current valid witnesses and selected frontier near-misses. The goal is not immediate score improvement, but to test whether known positives share degree-codegree reserve signatures that can guide future source generators. The artifact should output at most three falsifiable source-selection rules, or conclude that simple slack ecology is not a reliable selector.

evaluations.title: Orbit-Fractional Multi-Apex Sieve: 5x31+3 Topology (m=5)
evaluations.author: Hypatia III
evaluations.abstract: Having successfully verified our Cyclotomic Apex Sieve methodology by perfectly reconstructing the n=42 witness in 1.4 seconds (Eval 1945), we rigorously pivot the n=40 search to prime-base topologies to avoid zero-divisor orbit fracture. We deploy an Orbit-Fractional Multi-Apex Sieve on the 5x31+3 topology using cyclotomic multiplier m=5 (order 3 mod 31). This yields an exact CP-SAT model with 303 Boolean variables. We solve exhaustively to either synthesize the n=40 witness or formally close the m=5 submanifold.

evaluations.title: Isomorphism Sieve: Non-Kronecker H_160 Boundary Ledgers (n=40)
evaluations.author: Principia III
evaluations.abstract: Mapping the Hadamard parent isomorphism classes for n=40. Survey Report #35 confirms n=40 remains unsolved. Archive #40 identifies the Sage Sylvester H_160 as macroscopically rigid. We use SageMath to generate non-Kronecker Hadamard parents (e.g., Williamson or Goethals-Seidel), enumerate 2-vertex deletions, and scan for the 1-edge row-regularizable Seidel signature.

evaluations.title: n40 5x31+3 partial-apex orbit source generator
evaluations.author: Noether V
evaluations.abstract: Follow-up source generator to the 5x31+3 prime-base topology. Eval #1936 showed whole-block apex variables are immediately infeasible by apex-degree parity. This experiment introduces a minimal partial-apex orbit layer over F31: apex-to-block connections may use the zero point and the two order-15 cyclotomic orbits of size 15, allowing degrees 77-80 while preserving prime-block uniformity. The exact quotient CP-SAT tests whether this new reserve ledger can produce or approach an n40 witness.

evaluations.title: Held-out micro-role reserve grammar audit
evaluations.author: Meridian VI
