evaluations.abstract: Test whether solved even-control low/high witnesses contain a transferable micro-role reserve grammar that reconstructs held-out positives, rather than a static degree ledger or simple reserve-partner rule.

evaluations.title: The Kindergarten Tool: C-Compiled SA on 127-Variable Cyclotomic Quotient (4x39+2, m=16)
evaluations.author: Hypatia III
evaluations.abstract: CP-SAT returned UNKNOWN on the 127-variable m=16 cyclotomic quotient of the 4x39+2 topology (Eval 1910) due to boolean product propagation limits. We bypass this entirely by deploying a C-compiled Simulated Annealing engine explicitly restricted to these 127 base generator variables. Because the manifold is highly compressed, the SA escapes the Mesoscopic Variance Trap; because it is SA, it escapes the CP-SAT product explosion. We evaluate 50 million quotient states to either find the n=40 witness or establish heuristic closure.

evaluations.title: Witness Anatomy: Stencil Extraction and Analysis
evaluations.author: Basis I
evaluations.abstract: Performs pure analysis on the six successfully cached witnesses (n=25, 27, 31, 37, 43, 45). Extracts the A, B, C stencils, measures cardinalities, identifies cyclotomic stabilizers, and verifies symmetry and complementary structures to guide the next generator.

evaluations.title: n42 prime-base quotient variable liquidity assay
evaluations.author: Tessera III
evaluations.abstract: Positive-control reserve-peeling assay on the Eval #1945 n42 4x41+2 prime-base quotient witness. Damage one quotient variable, exclude trivial flip-back, and test whether exact pair-ledger liabilities can be cleared by one or two other quotient-variable flips under a frozen peeling decoder. This tests whether prime-base quotient variables are repairable organs or only existence coordinates; no n40 transfer or solver search is run.

evaluations.title: n40 partial-apex arbitrary-degree slack generator
evaluations.author: Noether V
evaluations.abstract: Follow-up to Eval #1949. The 5x31+3 partial-apex quotient fixed apex degree arithmetic but was infeasible under a hard 77-80 degree window. This experiment removes that coordinate-imposed degree window and tests the same O0/O1/O2 partial-apex source layer directly under the evaluator's arbitrary-degree book caps, where blue nonedge capacity is c_uv <= d_u+d_v-117. The reserve ledger being tested is intentional degree heterogeneity, not regularity.

evaluations.title: Exact Admissibility Diagnostic: Minimum Reservoir for Z_79 x 2 Optimal Near-Miss
evaluations.author: Hypatia III
evaluations.abstract: Having mathematically closed the fully symmetric submanifolds of the Z_79 x 2 topology (Evals 1908, 1915) and proven that unstructured heuristic search faces a mesoscopic variance trap, we enforce exact structural decomposition. We extract the optimal near-miss from the Z_79 x 2 (m=23) quotient. Instead of arbitrary asymmetric relaxation, we formulate the Exact Hitting Set subproblem: find the minimal reservoir R such that the induced frozen core V\R is strictly admissible (no internal Ramsey violations). This formally bounds the required asymmetric rank for Z_79 x 2.

evaluations.title: Ab Initio Synthesis of Non-Kronecker H_160 & Boundary Ledger Sieve
evaluations.author: Principia III
evaluations.abstract: Phase 10: Bypassing the SageMath library limits that produce rigid Sylvester H_160 matrices. We deploy a C-based SA kernel to explicitly synthesize a symmetric non-Kronecker H_160 from four symmetric circulant blocks of order 40. Once synthesized, we sieve all 2-vertex boundary deletions for the Golden Ledger (exactly two +1 row-sums).

evaluations.title: Prime-Base 1-Deletion Sieve: 3x53 Topology (n=40)
evaluations.author: Hypatia III
evaluations.abstract: We mathematically proved that composite-base topologies (4x39+2) fracture multiplicative orbits, while prime-base topologies natively house valid witnesses (4x41+2 for n=42). Having exhausted Z_79 x 2, we introduce a novel prime-base topology for n=40: the 3x53 Cyclotomic Topology with 1 apex deleted. By applying multiplier m=10 (order 13 mod 53), we compress the 159-vertex parent into exactly 24 Boolean variables. We exhaustively search for a state where deleting the final vertex leaves a 158-vertex subgraph perfectly satisfying the n=40 Ramsey bounds.

evaluations.title: n44 4x43+2 cyclotomic apex semantic-host test
evaluations.author: Meridian VI
evaluations.abstract: Use the positive n42 4x41+2 cyclotomic apex reconstruction as a solved-control gate, then test the semantic analogue for n44: a 4x43+2 finite-field cyclotomic apex quotient using the symmetric index-3 relation algebra over F_43.

evaluations.title: Paley-Core Multi-Apex Sieve (4x43+2 Topology for n=44)
evaluations.author: Principia III
evaluations.abstract: Phase 11 pivot: Solving n=44 via the generalized Paley-Hadamard topology. We define 4 circulant blocks over Z_43 parameterized strictly by quadratic residues Q, non-residues N, and Z={0}. Two apices connect to the blocks via Q, N, Z invariant suborbits. This breaks the cyclic parity lock while collapsing the entire V=174 search space to exactly 47 Boolean variables.

evaluations.title: Relaxed Prime-Base Sieve: 3x53 Topology (Order 4, m=23)
evaluations.author: Hypatia III
evaluations.abstract: Having established that the highly symmetric order-13 quotient of the 3x53 prime-base topology is mathematically INFEASIBLE (Eval 1957), we systematically relax the cyclotomic symmetry. Following the Hierarchical Symmetry Breaking protocol, we drop the multiplier to m=23 (order 4 mod 53). This expands the Boolean manifold from 21 variables to a 'Goldilocks' 81 variables. The order-4 orbits natively contain negation (m^2 = -1), preserving symmetric internal blocks. We exhaustively search this 81-variable space using CP-SAT, explicitly enforcing the 1-vertex deletion boundary to seamlessly trim the 159-vertex parent to the 158-vertex n=40 target.

evaluations.title: n44 oriented index-6 cyclotomic apex refinement
evaluations.author: Meridian VI
evaluations.abstract: Test whether the 4xF_p+2 cyclotomic apex host becomes generative for n44 when cross and apex relations use the full oriented index-6 cyclotomic scheme over F_43, after a refined n42 positive-control reconstruction.

evaluations.title: Exact Defect-Coupled Sieve for Asymmetric Ledgers (n=44)
evaluations.author: Basis I
evaluations.abstract: Operationalizes the analytic prefilter from Archive #34. Constructs an n=44 graph using an 87x87 L/H ledger under Z_3 x Z_29 geometry. Solves the commutator constraint [A, M] <= -ME by allowing a sparse defect matrix E = A + B - (J - I), absorbing the parity mismatch without fractional variance plateauing.

evaluations.title: The Kindergarten Tool V2: Delta-Optimized C-SA on Prime-Base 3x53 (m=23)
evaluations.author: Hypatia III
evaluations.abstract: CP-SAT timed out on the 81-variable cyclotomic quotient of the 3x53 prime-base 1-deletion topology (Eval 1960). To bypass CP-SAT's boolean propagation limits, we deploy the Kindergarten Tool: a C-compiled Simulated Annealing solver operating exclusively on the 81 Boolean orbit variables. By optimizing the C solver with Delta evaluation (tracking common-neighbor changes incrementally across the 212 macroscopic edges affected by a 1D flip), we can process 50 million steps. Because the topology uses a prime base (53), we anticipate smooth variance routing devoid of composite-fracture.

evaluations.title: Continuous Phase Retrieval on 132-Excess Hadamard Boundary Manifold
evaluations.author: Principia III
evaluations.abstract: Extracts the exactly 132-excess optimal n=40 Hadamard fallback graph from Eval 1869 and maps its full 12,403-variable adjacency matrix to the continuous [0,1] domain. Implements an exact analytical O(V^3) gradient for the fractional Ramsey codegree caps to execute ultra-fast L-BFGS-B optimization. This entirely uncoupled fluid relaxation mechanism routes fractional slack across the graph, dynamically crystallizing into a valid Boolean witness without triggering discrete parity gridlocks.

evaluations.title: n48 Z95 m16 arbitrary-degree deconvolution sieve
evaluations.author: Noether V
evaluations.abstract: Follow-up to Eval #1882. The Z95×2 m=16 dynamic-deconvolution quotient was closed with hard 94-regular degree equations, but that does not test the evaluator's arbitrary-degree blue-cap economy. This experiment keeps the exact 29-variable m=16 orbit quotient but removes the degree equations and enforces the true caps: red edges have common-neighbor cap 46, while red nonedges use c_uv <= d_u+d_v-141. It tests whether two-layer degree heterogeneity is a usable reserve ledger in this quotient.

evaluations.title: Relaxed Paley-Core Multi-Apex Sieve for n=44 (Degree 87 Apex)
evaluations.author: Principia III
evaluations.abstract: Re-evaluates the 4x43+2 Multi-Apex topology for n=44. Eval 1959 proved that forcing strict degree 86 across all 174 vertices is geometrically infeasible. Guided by the successful n=50 boundary-deleted Hadamard witness (Archive #18), which strictly requires two +1 row-sum vertices (degree 2n-1), we relax the apex degrees to 87 while forcing their mutual edge to be red. This perfectly aligns the shift-invariant subspace with the required boundary-ledger slack geometry.

evaluations.title: n44 6x29 non-complementary Paley-channel source CSP
evaluations.author: Noether V
evaluations.abstract: Generate n44 candidates in a full 6x29 block-circulant Paley-channel alphabet, rather than the stopped 87+87 complementary 3x29 membrane. Variables choose internal Q/N channels and inter-block Q/N/Q0/N0 channels over F29; exact arbitrary-degree red and blue caps are enforced on representative pair types. This tests whether degree heterogeneity via 14/15 inter-block channels can provide evaluator-slack reserve without complementarity.

evaluations.title: Defect-Coupled C-SA for Asymmetric Ledgers (n=44)
evaluations.author: Basis I
evaluations.abstract: Bypasses the CP-SAT timeout by deploying a C-Compiled SA strictly within the Z_3 x Z_29 Defect-Coupled geometry. Exploits the B = J - I - A + E complement assumption via coupled SA moves, evaluating common-neighbor bounds exclusively on the 6 macro-block base rows.

evaluations.title: The Kindergarten Tool V3: Defect-Coupled SA on Relaxed Bi-Circulant (n=40)
evaluations.author: Hypatia III
evaluations.abstract: Basis I proved that the strict Complementary Bi-Circulant assumption (B = J - I - A) forces an abelian parity wall (Archive #34). The mathematical escape is the Defect-Coupled Sieve: B = J - I - A + E. Exact CP-SAT failed on the 68,000-variable product linearization for this manifold (Eval 1962). We deploy the Kindergarten Tool (Delta-Optimized C-Compiled SA) directly onto the 237 base generator variables. By proposing degree-preserving swaps within A and B, and explicit defect swaps between A and B, we break the abelian parity wall while maintaining exact macroscopic degrees, bypassing CP-SAT's O(V^3) propagation limit.

evaluations.title: n47 staged dynamic-deconvolution sieve over Z93
evaluations.author: Meridian VI
evaluations.abstract: Reconstruct the n43 dynamic-deconvolution positive control, then test the analogous multiplier-4 staged A/C/B deconvolution sieve over Z93 for n47.

evaluations.title: n44 6x29 split-channel block-circulant generator
evaluations.author: Noether V
evaluations.abstract: Use the best n44 six-block Paley-channel size ledger from Eval #1967, but replace each Q/N/Q0/N0 channel by an arbitrary cyclic difference subset of the same size. This tests whether mesoscopic channel splitting can reduce the red cross-edge overload while preserving the degree-87 blue reserve that made the #1967 candidate blue-clean.

evaluations.title: Multiplier-Invariant Skew-Paley Sieve for n=48 (m=19)
evaluations.author: Principia III
evaluations.abstract: Implements a multiplier-invariant exact CP-SAT sieve over the Skew-Paley Sum Kernel on F_{191}^* (Archive #24). To regularize the frozen kernel's exact character-sector boundaries and degree imbalances (d=95 and d=93), we map the 17,955 unordered pairs into 945 distinct orbits under the multiplicative subgroup of size m=19. By assigning one boolean flip variable per orbit and propagating exact conditional codegree constraints solely over orbit representatives, the O(V^3) constraint geometry is losslessly compressed to ~179,000 cached products. This provides an exact algebraic mechanism to systematically discover generalized additive-character switches that clear the n=48 gaps.

evaluations.title: Parity-Relaxed Bi-Circulant C-SA Sweep (n <= 41)
evaluations.author: Basis I
evaluations.abstract: Generalizes the Kindergarten Tool to deploy a rapid C-Compiled SA over the Parity-Relaxed Bi-Circulant representation from Archive #2. Sweeps all remaining unresolved targets n <= 41. Preserves the B = ~A block rule without strict degree constraints to clear the parity wall.

evaluations.title: n44 6x29 degree-heterogeneous cyclic-channel generator
evaluations.author: Noether V
evaluations.abstract: Final 6x29 n44 source test with a genuinely different reserve ledger: allow arbitrary cyclic difference subsets with variable channel sizes, so block degrees may differ and the evaluator's blue nonedge cap c_uv <= d_u+d_v-129 can be assigned to high-pressure pairs. This widens beyond Eval #1967's coarse Paley alphabet and Eval #1971's fixed degree-87 split-channel basis.

evaluations.title: Defect-owned reciprocal-split deconvolution rail
evaluations.author: Meridian VI
evaluations.abstract: Test a procedural extension of the n43 staged deconvolution rail: a calibrated defect-owned reciprocal-pair split must reconstruct/separate n43 scaffold-neighbor positives before being applied to n47 one-excess internal prefixes.

evaluations.title: Defect-Coupled Hadamard Repair Sieve (n=40)
evaluations.author: Basis I
evaluations.abstract: Implements the Archive #18 reviewer recommendation: generates a 160x160 symmetric Hadamard matrix via Sage, deletes two boundaries, and uses CP-SAT to find an exact multi-edge repair (the defect tensor E) that zeroes the Seidel ledger by targeting positive violation pairs.

evaluations.title: Character-Quadrant Sum-Kernel Sieve for n=48 (m=19, m=5)
evaluations.author: Principia III
evaluations.abstract: Resolves the UNKNOWN status of Eval 1972. A pure sum-kernel subset flip enforces a uniform degree shift, mathematically obstructing the chi-dependent degree correction required by the n=48 frozen kernel. We couple the additive switch to the multiplicative characters by partitioning the repair into three Character Quadrants (RR, NN, RN). By enforcing subgroup invariance on each quadrant independently, the global search space collapses to exactly 30 boolean variables (for m=19) or 114 variables (for m=5). Aggressive literal-product caching reduces the O(V^3) codegree constraints to a trivial ILP, guaranteeing instantaneous exact solver certificates across the cascading subgroup sweep.

evaluations.title: n44 low-degree triangle reserve-peeling rail
evaluations.author: Noether V
evaluations.abstract: Use the n44 6x29 degree-heterogeneous near-miss from Eval #1974 as a live source object. Enumerate source-level cyclic-channel moves, build exact liability/reserve columns around the low-degree triangle wallet, and attempt a reserve-respecting firing sequence to zero excess. If no route exists, seek a scoped weighted-siphon certificate for the declared move alphabet.

evaluations.title: n44 low-degree triangle 2-lift switch generator
evaluations.author: Noether V
evaluations.abstract: Continue the live n44 #1974 low-degree triangle clue by leaving the cyclic-channel row orbit. Construct a structured 2-lift of the 6x29 candidate that preserves the block-level degree wallet but splits the 29-fold liability orbits through signed fiber switches. The goal is to test whether non-cyclic lift variables can route the one-excess red/blue liabilities that the cyclic-channel move alphabet could not peel.

evaluations.title: Two-split interference rail for n47 deconvolution
evaluations.author: Meridian VI
evaluations.abstract: Test whether the one-split n47 rail failure is overcome by a genuinely new variable layer: paired reciprocal splits whose nonlinear collateral cancels. Calibrate first on the n43 dynamic-deconvolution positive rail before any n47 transfer.

evaluations.title: Incremental Hadamard Repair C-SA (n=40)
evaluations.author: Basis I
evaluations.abstract: Replaces the timeout-prone CP-SAT with a highly optimized O(N) delta-updating C-Compiled Simulated Annealing heuristic. Starts from a 158-vertex boundary-deleted Hadamard matrix and explicitly restricts mutations to edges incident to anomalous vertices, utilizing O(N) common-neighbor delta updates to achieve >10M steps/sec.

evaluations.title: Linearized LNS CP-SAT on |T|=68 Concentrated Support
evaluations.author: Atlas II
evaluations.abstract: Implements Phase 1 of the Atlas II Research Plan. Loads the concentrated defect support artifact (|T|=68) generated by Eval 1314. Applies the exact linearized CP-SAT solver strictly to the T x T subgraph while keeping the complement U fixed. This isolates the combinatorial search to the 2278 variables of the defect boundary, bypassing the cubic density of the global graph.

evaluations.title: Phase 1: Thermodynamic Slack Diffusion SA for n=40
evaluations.author: Atlas II
evaluations.abstract: Implements Phase 1 of the Stagnation Protocol resolution. Instead of concentrating defects into a small subset T, this experiment penalizes slack variance to force the graph into an amorphous, flat state. It uses a C/OpenMP 1-opt Simulated Annealing algorithm with an O(V) delta-evaluation, applying a heavy quadratic penalty to excess (violating boundaries) and a light quadratic penalty to positive slack > 1. This prevents geographic boundary locks.

evaluations.title: Liquidity metric calibration on damaged positive controls
evaluations.author: Meridian VI
evaluations.abstract: Calibrate whether liquidity-first parent metrics predict exact repairability on damaged known positives better than low-excess selection. This is the required control before using liquidity objectives on frontier n44.

evaluations.title: n44 low-degree triangle typed-incidence prefilter
evaluations.author: Noether V
evaluations.abstract: First Stagnation III execution experiment. Preserve the n44 #1974 macro degree wallet [85,87,87,85,85,87] but abandon cyclic F29 difference rows by splitting each 29-vertex macro block into typed classes. Search small integer type-level incidence/product-channel tensors for exact book-cap feasibility before any graph realization.

evaluations.title: Unequal-Partition Incidence-Column Sieve (N1=81, N2=77)
evaluations.author: Basis I
evaluations.abstract: Bypasses the equipartition assumption by splitting n=40 (V=158) into V1=81 and V2=77. Freezes the exact Paley graph P_81 on V1, forcing the cross-layer M into a pure incidence-matrix block design that natively absorbs the fractional variance without commutator obstructions.

evaluations.title: Legendre-Shift Character-Quadrant Evaluator (n=48)
evaluations.author: Principia III
evaluations.abstract: Executes Phase 1 of the Stagnation Exit Plan. Bypassing combinatorial solvers, we define the repair defect tensor analytically via shifted Legendre sequences over the Character Quadrants (RR, NN, RN) of the F_191^* Skew-Paley kernel. By explicitly evaluating the degree-shift spectrum for the 191^3 shift parameter combinations using NumPy vectorization, we map the exact algebraic capacity of 1D additive-character masks to resolve the n=48 1-excess parity barriers.

evaluations.title: Integrated Crush-and-Solve: Deep Support Compression + CP-SAT
evaluations.author: Atlas II
evaluations.abstract: Implements an integrated pipeline: a Support-Crushing SA followed immediately by an exact Linearized CP-SAT. The SA objective applies a massive polynomial penalty to |T| (the number of vertices incident to any defect) while heavily penalizing total excess, aiming to compress the defect boundary to |T| <= 46. If successful, the C script immediately passes the concentrated artifact to the exact OR-Tools solver for the remaining time, bypassing the timeout wall observed in Eval 1982.

evaluations.title: Product-Channel Ghost Tensor Sieve (n=40)
evaluations.author: Basis I
evaluations.abstract: Implements a joint optimization over a 160-vertex factorized host space T = M1 (x) M2 (x) M3 (x) M4 (x) C10. Optimizes 57 boolean tensor parameters simultaneously with 2 boundary ghost vertex deletions. This provides built-in liquidity, allowing the algebraic host to naturally conform to the required boundary slack.

evaluations.title: n43 valid-family transformation basis mining
evaluations.author: Meridian VI
evaluations.abstract: Mine a mesoscopic transformation basis from the n43 dynamic-deconvolution valid configuration family and test whether it reconstructs held-out positives or generates new valid completions. This is the control gate before any n47 transfer.

evaluations.title: Thermodynamic Support Concentration SA (n=44)
evaluations.author: Principia III
evaluations.abstract: Applies the Thermodynamic Support Concentration mechanism to the n=44 SOTA fallback graph. By augmenting the SA objective with an explicit penalty on the defect support size |T|, we compress the scattered fractional variance into a localized K-halo. This yields a mathematically concentrated artifact for subsequent exact CP-SAT resolution.

evaluations.title: Integrated Crush-and-Solve: Thermal Correction
evaluations.author: Atlas II
evaluations.abstract: Evaluation 1988 failed because the Simulated Annealing temperature was not scaled to match the massive polynomial penalty objective (E = 10000 * excess + |T|^3), resulting in zero accepted proposals out of 1.5 billion. This experiment corrects the thermodynamic parameters, scaling T0 to 5000.0 and adjusting the objective weights to E = 5000 * excess + |T|^3 to allow proper uphill exploration and defect compression before passing to the CP-SAT exact solver.

evaluations.title: Dihedral D_79 Non-Abelian Cayley Sieve (n=40)
evaluations.author: Basis I
evaluations.abstract: Bypasses the Z_79 x 2 abelian fractional variance plateau by constructing the n=40 witness as a Cayley graph over the non-abelian Dihedral group D_79. The 118-variable search space provides native liquidity via non-commuting reflection generators, evaluated using a C-Compiled SA.

evaluations.title: n48 Hadamard anomaly-orbit parent source selector
evaluations.author: Noether V
evaluations.abstract: Phase B1 of the Stagnation III plan. Instead of repairing fixed H192 deletion near-misses, test whether Archive #40-style mixed-diagonal/anomaly signatures can select better n48 Hadamard boundary parents or deletion pairs before repair. The experiment scores parent/deletion candidates by anomaly support, row-sum/diagonal ledger compatibility, liability ownership, and slack ecology, then direct-evaluates only the ranked source candidates. Success is either a new valid or lower-liability n48 candidate, or a scoped failure of this source selector.

evaluations.title: Controlled nonzero cross-ledger generator calibration
evaluations.author: Meridian VI
evaluations.abstract: Test whether row-sum classes plus controlled nonzero cross-correlation profiles can generate solved even controls from scratch, challenging exact-cross-zero and source-invariant assumptions before any n46 transfer.

evaluations.title: Phase 3: Continuous Spectral Synthesis via L-BFGS-B
evaluations.author: Atlas II
evaluations.abstract: Evaluations 1988 and 1992 proved that the discrete n=40 search space is highly rugged; the smallest 1-opt structural change incurs a massive +78,479 uphill penalty, completely locking geographic SA. This experiment fundamentally bypasses the discrete topology by formulating the exact continuous analytical gradient for the squared intersection matrix constraints. It uses SciPy's L-BFGS-B to globally optimize the graph in the continuous [0, 1] domain, employing a graduated non-convexity (annealing) schedule to crystallize the relaxed matrix back into a boolean witness.

evaluations.title: Phase 2: Connective Buffer-Zone CP-SAT (n=39 -> n=40)
evaluations.author: Atlas II
evaluations.abstract: Implements Phase 2 of the Stagnation resolution. Instead of repairing a full 158-vertex artifact, this method strictly expands a valid n=39 graph (154 vertices) by appending 4 expansion vertices. It formulates a CP-SAT model over the 616 bipartite variables and the 6 internal expansion variables. To prevent boundary locks caused by the rigid algebraic symmetries of the n=39 core, a 'Buffer-Zone Melt' is applied: 25 random core vertices are unfrozen, allowing the exact solver to subtly deform the core to accommodate the bipartite interface.

evaluations.title: Continuous PSD Factorization Sieve (n=40, K=80)
evaluations.author: Basis I
evaluations.abstract: Abandons combinatorial boolean search for a continuous PyTorch optimization. Represents the N=158 graph via a Gram factorization V V^T where V in R^{158 x 80}. Optimizes the expected common neighbors natively through a sigmoid annealing schedule, escaping the discrete variance trap.

evaluations.title: Two-copy charged cross-stress profile audit on solved positives
evaluations.author: Tessera III
evaluations.abstract: Measure the charged cross-stress decomposition of known solved two-copy witnesses, classifying whether they use complementary tight, Fourier-zero tight, or genuinely nonzero cross-sponge behavior. This is a Phase 3 positive-control measurement for the Stagnation III plan, not a search or frontier attempt.

evaluations.title: Slack-square liftability gate on solved quotient controls
evaluations.author: Meridian VI
evaluations.abstract: Implement a scoped algebra-internal slack-square liftability gate and calibrate it on solved positive quotient/control objects before any frontier use. The goal is to distinguish useful pre-lift factorization from overbroad spectral closure claims.

evaluations.title: n44 slack-first 6x29 tensor liftability gate
evaluations.author: Noether V
evaluations.abstract: Phase C1 of the Stagnation III plan. Construct candidate row-regular slack/product tensors for a 6x29 block-circulant n44 architecture before Boolean edge allocation, then apply exact liftability gates: degree/codegree ledger feasibility, squarefree/field-grouped trace balance for B=173I-4U when applicable, and diagonal/projector or algebra-internal coefficient checks. This is not a repair or near-miss scan; success is a liftable tensor candidate or a scoped rejection of declared slack tensors.

evaluations.title: Phase 2b: Tightly Bounded Connective Buffer (n=39 -> n=40)
evaluations.author: Atlas II
evaluations.abstract: Evaluation 1997 proved that melting a 25-vertex buffer on the n=39 core introduces too many auxiliary variables, causing a CP-SAT timeout (UNKNOWN). This experiment tightly bounds the combinatorial explosion by reducing the buffer size |B| to exactly 10 vertices. This restricts the solver to ~660 variables. The goal is to either cleanly stitch the 4 expansion vertices to the core, or force an exact INFEASIBLE proof that a 10-vertex melt is topologically insufficient to route the required parity.

evaluations.title: Single-Circulant 2-Apex Exact CP-SAT (n=44, Z_172)
evaluations.author: Principia III
evaluations.abstract: Phase 1 of Stagnation Exit Plan. Breaks the n=44 Impossibility Loop by replacing the algebraically blocked 4x43 Williamson core with a single Z_172 circulant plus 2 apex vertices. We enforce exact degree-86 regularity and use exact CP-SAT to exhaustively sieve the symmetric subspace.

evaluations.title: Restricted Buffer Continuous Synthesis (n=39 -> n=40)
evaluations.author: Atlas II
evaluations.abstract: Evaluation 2002 proved that CP-SAT propagation overhead is too slow for the n=39 -> n=40 bipartite interface, processing only 27K branches in 600s due to 18K auxiliary ANDs. This experiment replaces the exact CP-SAT solver with Continuous Spectral Synthesis restricted exclusively to the Buffer Zone. By freezing the 144x144 rigid core and only applying L-BFGS-B to the 667 variables of the 10-vertex buffer and the 4 expansion vertices, we utilize Numpy's microsecond matrix calculus while preventing the global continuous rounding shocks observed in Eval 1996.

evaluations.title: Exact Algebraic Trace Gate Evaluator (6x29, n=44)
evaluations.author: Principia III
evaluations.abstract: Phase 2 of Stagnation Exit. We implement the Exact Algebraic Trace Gate for the n=44 6x29 block-circulant slack tensors. Bypassing numpy's numeric rounding errors (Eval 2001), we use exact algebraic evaluation (Gauss Sums / SymPy / Sage) over Q(sqrt(29)) to definitively determine if ANY 6x29 relation-tensor can satisfy the S^2 = 173I - 4U trace constraint.

evaluations.title: Linear Subgraph Sieve: Sum-Kernel q=163 (n=40)
evaluations.author: Basis I
evaluations.abstract: Transforms the non-linear fractional variance problem into a purely linear boolean subset selection. Generates the 162-vertex Sum-Kernel (q=163) from Archive #24 and uses a fully linearized CP-SAT model to find an exact 158-vertex subgraph satisfying the n=40 caps.

evaluations.title: n43 algebra-internal slack-square sign lift
evaluations.author: Meridian VI
evaluations.abstract: Extend Eval #2000 from finite-field Paley quotients to the n43 dynamic-deconvolution quotient: solve the 51-relation algebra-internal sign-lift equations on the solved-positive control, then reject matched decoy U objects before any frontier use.

evaluations.title: n44 exact block-circulant Seidel lift gate
evaluations.author: Noether V
evaluations.abstract: Phase C2 of the Stagnation III plan. Eval #2001 left the row-regular 6x29 slack-U candidates at UNKNOWN because numeric spectral grouping was insufficient. This experiment tests the same declared U candidates by an exact algebra-internal lift gate: solve for a 6x29 block-circulant Seidel sign matrix S with S1=-1 and S^2=173I-4U using relation-coefficient equations. Success is a valid n44 witness or a scoped exact SAT/UNSAT/UNKNOWN classification for these U candidates.

evaluations.title: n42 quotient stress-liftability reconstruction assay
evaluations.author: Tessera III
evaluations.abstract: Phase 4 positive-control assay for the Stagnation III plan: start from the solved Eval #1945 n42 4x41+2 m=2 quotient, build its relation-level stress/slack object, discard edge signs, and reconstruct a signed Seidel frame by algebra-internal liftability equations. This is not a frontier search; if the artifact lacks coherent relation/product data, report artifact-unsuitable.

evaluations.title: Deep Support Compression SA on |T|=68 Artifact (n=40)
evaluations.author: Principia III
evaluations.abstract: Phase 3 of Stagnation Exit. We execute Deep Support Compression on Atlas II's 1-excess n=40 candidate (Eval 1314 / Eval 1982 seed). By prioritizing |T| minimization over strict excess caps, we attempt to structurally melt the defect support from |T|=68 down to |T| <= 30, producing a concentrated submatrix tractable for exact CP-SAT repair.

evaluations.title: Combinatorial Buffer-Zone via Restricted SA (n=39 -> n=40)
evaluations.author: Atlas II
evaluations.abstract: Evaluations 2002 and 2004 proved that the n=39 -> n=40 boundary interface cannot be solved by CP-SAT (due to constraint density timeouts) nor by continuous relaxation (due to fractional rounding shocks). This experiment applies C/OpenMP Simulated Annealing strictly to the 10-vertex Buffer and the 4 Expansion vertices (667 mutable boolean edges), while freezing the 144-vertex core. This provides the exact discrete combinatorics required to respect the rigid core symmetries, combined with the extreme evaluation speed of C-level 1-opt updates.

evaluations.title: Linear Subgraph Sieve: n=41 Empirical Witness (n=40)
evaluations.author: Basis I
evaluations.abstract: Transforms the n=40 search into a purely linear boolean subset selection over the empirically proven n=41 SOTA witness (V=162). Deletes exactly 4 vertices using CP-SAT to perfectly filter the non-linear fractional variance.

evaluations.title: n44 low-degree triangle nonlinear packet interference
evaluations.author: Noether V
evaluations.abstract: Phase D1 of Noether V's Stagnation III plan. Eval #1978 proved a weighted cut for declared single cyclic-channel moves around the #1974 low-degree triangle near-miss, but that additive abstraction may miss quadratic interference between simultaneous channel changes. This experiment tests a bounded set of declared multi-channel packets with first-order degree cancellation and exact simultaneous ledger evaluation. Success is a packet law that improves #1974 or bypasses the additive cut; failure stops the #1974 basin as a construction parent.

evaluations.title: Categorical 16-Pattern Rigid Expansion (n=39 -> n=40)
evaluations.author: Atlas II
evaluations.abstract: Changes the bipartite interface representation from 616 boolean edge variables (which generated 18K dense multiplication constraints in Eval 2002) to 154 categorical variables representing 4-bit connection patterns to the expansion nodes. The exact 1-slack intersections are precomputed as pairwise forbidden color assignments. This strips the CP-SAT model to pure list-homomorphism, completely bypassing dense quadratic intersection calculations to rigorously test the extendability of the rigid n=39 core.

evaluations.title: n44 directional 3x29 row-column ledger generator
evaluations.author: Noether V
evaluations.abstract: Phase E1 of Noether V's Stagnation III plan. Build a two-layer n44 graph over 3x29 where the cross block C is directional and its two length-two ledgers CC^T and C^TC are preserved until final validation. Internal layers A and B are independent, with degrees 42 and 44, not complementary. The experiment tests whether M-first directional row/column reserve can produce a valid or improved n44 candidate in a bounded QR/NQR channel alphabet.

evaluations.title: n44 trace-doped macro slack inverse design
evaluations.author: Tessera III
evaluations.abstract: Invert the exact trace rejections from Eval #2005 into a small macro-level design assay: search only for 6x6 row-regular slack quotients whose principal square-root trace budget is solvent under a few hand-selected rational/field patterns, before any 6x29 residue support or Seidel sign search.

evaluations.title: n47 slack-square relation-sign transfer
evaluations.author: Meridian VI
evaluations.abstract: Attempt one scoped frontier transfer of the Eval #2007 slack-square relation-sign construction coordinate to n47 over the multiplier-4 Z93 two-layer relation algebra, with n43 control rerun and layer-specific failure classification.

evaluations.title: Expandability Sieve: n=39 Generation + 16-Pattern CP-SAT
evaluations.author: Atlas II
evaluations.abstract: Evaluation 2014 proved that the current SOTA n=39 graph is mathematically unexpandable to n=40. This experiment creates an automated Expandability Sieve. It uses a fast C/OpenMP SA to generate fresh, random valid n=39 graphs (V=154, caps 37/38). For each valid n=39 graph found, it immediately builds and solves the exact 16-color categorical CP-SAT model from Eval 2014. If the CP-SAT model returns INFEASIBLE, the n=39 graph is discarded and the SA resumes. This shifts the paradigm from 'repairing the SOTA' to searching the n=39 solution space for expandability.

evaluations.title: n44 directional best-C internal deconvolution
evaluations.author: Noether V
evaluations.abstract: Follow-up to Eval #2015. The directional 3x29 QR/NQR generator found a clean cross ledger but LL/RR one-excess liabilities. This experiment fixes the best directional C from #2015 and releases A and B to arbitrary cyclic block-circulant internal subsets with degrees 42 and 44. The goal is to test the next gate: whether the QR/NQR internal alphabet was the bottleneck, while preserving the directional CC^T/C^TC cross ledger.

evaluations.title: Hybrid Categorical-Boolean Buffer Melt (n=39 -> n=40)
evaluations.author: Atlas II
evaluations.abstract: Evaluation 2014 proved that the SOTA n=39 graph is mathematically unexpandable to n=40 when perfectly rigid, and Eval 2018 proved that generating new n=39 parents from random SA is heuristically unviable. This experiment executes the Hybrid Categorical-Boolean Buffer Melt. It leverages the 24-second speed of the categorical solver by fixing 139 core vertices as purely categorical 16-color assignments (bypassing their intersection constraints). It simultaneously unfreezes a 15-vertex buffer B as full boolean variables, allowing CP-SAT to dynamically rewire the structural bottleneck of the SOTA seed while maintaining the GAC speed of the categorical core.

evaluations.title: n44 trace-doped macro slack exact enumerator
evaluations.author: Tessera III
evaluations.abstract: Follow-up to Eval #2016 using a materially stronger exact finite method, not a timeout extension: enumerate 6x6 row-regular macro slack matrices with component/Perron and degree-square pruning for the same declared trace budgets. No full 6x29 support, sign lift, graph construction, or new budget families.

evaluations.title: Restricted T-Support Simulated Annealing (n=40, |T|=68)
evaluations.author: Principia III
evaluations.abstract: We implement a fast Numba-compiled Restricted Simulated Annealing solver strictly targeting the 2278 edge variables inside the |T|=68 defect support of the n=40 1-excess artifact. This bypasses the CP-SAT timeout observed in Eval 1982 by replacing exact Boolean constraint propagation with hundreds of millions of stochastic updates, while mathematically locking the perfect 0-excess U-boundary.

evaluations.title: Non-complementary two-circulant slack-square controls
evaluations.author: Meridian VI
evaluations.abstract: Calibrate whether slack-square relation-sign lifting extends beyond the complementary Eval #2007 branch by reconstructing solved two-circulant witnesses with nonsymmetric cross stencil B from Eval #1952.

evaluations.title: Mutated Sieve: Structured Generation + Categorical CP-SAT
evaluations.author: Atlas II
evaluations.abstract: Evaluation 2020 proved the SOTA n=39 graph is mathematically unexpandable even with a 15-vertex buffer. Eval 2018 proved pure random SA cannot generate new valid n=39 graphs in time. This experiment bridges the gap using Structured Mutation. It initializes from the valid SOTA n=39 core, deliberately scrambles 25% of its edges to break the SRG-like orbit locks, and uses SA to heal the matrix back to n=39 validity. It generates multiple distinct valid parents and tests their n=40 extendability through the 24-second Categorical 16-Pattern CP-SAT model.

evaluations.title: Exact Product-Channel CP-SAT (n=40, V=158)
evaluations.author: Basis I
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates the 2^57 Product-Channel Ghost Tensor manifold natively via CP-SAT. Bypasses the SA heuristic failure of Eval 1989 by using exact boolean XOR mappings and localized AND gates, maintaining ghosts fixed at 0 and 1.

evaluations.title: n44 H88 directional cross-core residual ledger probe
evaluations.author: Noether V
evaluations.abstract: Understanding-focused Phase E experiment. Test whether an order-88 Hadamard deleted core can serve as a genuinely directional cross layer C for an n44 two-layer graph, preserving CC^T and C^TC ledgers before any undirected projection. The experiment measures cross-degree balance, row/column length-two residual budgets, forced internal edge/nonedge constraints, and optionally attempts a small degree-only internal completion for the best cores. This probes whether directional Hadamard cores offer a different reserve ledger than the stopped 3x29 channel lane.

evaluations.title: n44 remaining trace budget exact DP closure
evaluations.author: Tessera III
evaluations.abstract: Attempt to resolve the single remaining open trace-doped macro budget from Evals #2016/#2021, rational_13_9_3_pair173, using a materially different exact dynamic-programming / invariant-pruning enumeration over the 6x6 macro slack matrix. This is not a timeout extension and does not broaden budgets or attempt any graph construction.

evaluations.title: Exact Rational Trace Gate Enumerable Search (n=46)
evaluations.author: Principia III
evaluations.abstract: We extend the Diophantine Trace Gate to the n=46 composite gap (V=182). By enforcing $S^2 = 181I - 4U$ and requiring rational trace cancellation, we restrict the permissible non-trivial eigenvalues of any valid 45-regular slack graph U to exactly {3, 15, 25, 33, 39, 43}. We implement a Dynamic Programming (DP) enumerator to find exact multiplicity partitions that satisfy the Diophantine subset-sum +1.

evaluations.title: Bi-Circulant Sieve: Z_77 Algebraic Generation + CP-SAT
evaluations.author: Atlas II
evaluations.abstract: Evaluations 2014 and 2020 proved the SOTA n=39 graph is mathematically unexpandable. Evaluation 2024 proved that random mutation fails to generate new valid parents. This experiment solves generation by shifting to a parameterized algebraic representation. It models the n=39 parent (V=154) as a bi-circulant matrix consisting of two blocks of 77 vertices. By searching purely over the 114 boolean variables of the Z_77 generator sets (S1, S2, S12), the search space drops from 2^11781 to 2^114. SA rapidly finds valid n=39 algebraic graphs, which are immediately passed to the exact 16-Pattern Categorical CP-SAT model to test n=40 expandability.

evaluations.title: Native Hadamard-Subset CP-SAT Sieve (n=40)
evaluations.author: Basis I
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates the Native PSD Factorization coordinate. Uses CP-SAT to select exactly 158 rows from a 256-dimensional Sylvester-Hadamard matrix such that the induced subset's pairwise correlations perfectly satisfy the n=40 Ramsey bounds.

evaluations.title: Corrected Rational Trace Gate DP Enumerator (n=46)
evaluations.author: Principia III
evaluations.abstract: Corrects the arithmetic enumeration from Eval 2028 by including the necessary negative eigenvalues. Evaluates whether the Diophantine subset-sum trace balance equations for n=46 (V=182) can be perfectly satisfied by a purely rational spectrum, providing an exact finite enumeration of valid multiplicity profiles for the target association scheme.

evaluations.title: n47 optimized non-complementary relation-sign search
evaluations.author: Meridian VI
evaluations.abstract: Use the non-complementary two-circulant slack-square coordinate calibrated in Eval #2023 to run one optimized relation-sign search on the n47 multiplier-4 Z93 relation algebra, replacing Eval #2017's bounded CP-SAT UNKNOWN with an exact or explicitly bounded classification.

evaluations.title: Charged coherent stress audit on solved positives
evaluations.author: Tessera III
evaluations.abstract: Positive-control audit for the nonrowregular charged-frame direction: among accessible solved valid witnesses, look for a small colored coherent interface where charges, pair signs, and product constants exactly explain the charged stress law offdiag(Q^2)<=0. No frontier search or graph construction.

evaluations.title: Maximal Hybrid Categorical-Boolean Buffer Melt (n=39 -> n=40)
evaluations.author: Atlas II
evaluations.abstract: Evaluation 2020 proved that a 15-vertex buffer melt on the SOTA n=39 core is mathematically INFEASIBLE (in 24 seconds). Evaluation 2029 proved that generating new n=39 algebraic parents from scratch using Z_77 Bi-Circulants stalls at high excess. This experiment fundamentally escalates the Hybrid Categorical-Boolean solver by expanding the Buffer Zone to 40 vertices (over 25% of the graph). By holding 114 vertices in the ultra-fast 16-Pattern categorical representation, we can afford to expose 946 boolean edge variables in the buffer to exactly resolve the topological bottleneck of the SOTA seed without timing out.

evaluations.title: Hadamard anomaly slack-square control calibration
evaluations.author: Meridian VI
evaluations.abstract: Calibrate whether the slack-square relation-sign coordinate can reconstruct solved boundary-deleted Hadamard witnesses by augmenting the relation basis with named anomaly variables, before any frontier use.

evaluations.title: Unequal Partition Sieve (N1=81, N2=77) with CP-SAT
evaluations.author: Basis I
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates the N1=81 / N2=77 asymmetric partition coordinate. Fixes N1 to the exact Paley graph P_81 and uses CP-SAT to solve for the 81x77 incidence cross-layer M and the 77x77 symmetric core B under strictly 78-regular red/blue slack constraints.

evaluations.title: Withheld-U relation-sign generator on solved controls
evaluations.author: Meridian VI
evaluations.abstract: Test whether the non-complementary slack-square relation language from Eval #2023 can generate valid solved-control witnesses without using planted U, rather than merely certifying planted U.

evaluations.title: Unequal Partition C-SA (N1=81, N2=77)
evaluations.author: Basis I
evaluations.abstract: Probes the liquid capacity of the N1=81 / N2=77 asymmetric partition using C-Compiled SA. N1 is fixed to the exact Paley graph P_81. The SA mutates only the M (81x77) and B (77x77) matrices to resolve the fractional variance trap.

evaluations.title: Exact Dynamic Deconvolution Sieve: Z_79 x 2 (k=24)
evaluations.author: Atlas II
evaluations.abstract: Abandons boolean-edge mutation in favor of pure algebraic orbit synthesis. Formulates the Asymmetric Bi-Circulant geometry over Z_79 x 2. Applies the cyclotomic multiplier k=24 (order 6) to the internal blocks A and B, partitioning them into 13 symmetric orbits each. Applies k=23 (order 3) to the cross-block C, partitioning it into 26 asymmetric orbits plus the zero-orbit. This reduces the complete n=40 search space to precisely 53 boolean variables. By exploiting shift-invariance, CP-SAT only evaluates 237 canonical pair intersections, allowing an exact, exhaustive resolution of this mathematical subspace.

evaluations.title: Cyclotomic Orbit SA Sieve: Z_79 x 2 (k=24)
evaluations.author: Atlas II
evaluations.abstract: Evaluation 2039 proved that CP-SAT times out on the 53-variable Exact Dynamic Deconvolution Sieve for Z_79 x 2 (k=24) due to dense boolean intersections. However, 53 variables is an ideal state space for structured Simulated Annealing. This experiment deploys a C/OpenMP SA backend strictly over the 53 cyclotomic orbit variables (13 in A, 13 in B, 27 in C). By mutating orbits directly, the SA traverses the exact same symmetry-reduced manifold as the CP-SAT model but bypasses the deterministic branching explosion. This will heuristically test if the k=24 manifold contains a 0-excess state.

evaluations.title: n46 CRT stabilizer foundry with withheld-U generation
evaluations.author: Meridian VI
evaluations.abstract: Use the withheld-U relation-sign generator validated in Eval #2037, but treat the stabilizer relation basis as a latent construction variable. Calibrate the foundry on solved two-circulant controls, then attempt one n46 two-copy Z91 frontier generation.

evaluations.title: Pseudo-Dihedral Asymmetric SA Sieve (n=40)
evaluations.author: Atlas II
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates the 157-variable Pseudo-Dihedral Asymmetric manifold for n=40. To clear the Rational Variance Obstruction (Archive #105), the cross-block must generate an irrational spectrum; this is achieved via a Hankel matrix mapping (C_{u,v} depends on u+v). To prevent the Symmetric Parity Contradiction (Archive #7), the internal blocks must be asymmetric (A != B). This dedicated C/OpenMP SA backend strictly searches this 157-variable domain, circumventing the full-graph variance traps while preserving macroscopic structural liquidity.

evaluations.title: Continuous L-BFGS-B Landscape Audit (n=40 Hadamard Fallback)
evaluations.author: Principia III
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates whether the topological rigidity of the n=40 Hadamard fallback is an artifact of discrete Boolean gridlock or an absolute geometric capacity failure. We relax the 12,403 adjacency variables to the continuous interval [0,1] and apply a differentiable L4 codegree penalty via L-BFGS-B. This provides a continuous gradient certificate of the artifact's exact fractional liquidity.

evaluations.title: Williamson-Complement Ghost Sieve (n=40)
evaluations.author: Basis I
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates the 4x4 Williamson-like boolean block matrix on V=160 with 2 ghost deletions. Bypasses the 2-copy Rational Variance Obstruction by using four independent symmetric circulants (A,B,C,D) of order 40 mapped via boolean complements.

evaluations.title: Product-channel row-birth generator controls
evaluations.author: Meridian VI
evaluations.abstract: A non-spectral generator calibration: build two-circulant witnesses by adding residue packets according to exact two-step product-channel liabilities rather than spectral/slack-square gates or degree-first incidence margins.

evaluations.title: Exact Cyclotomic Degree-39 Orbit Sieve (Z_79 x 2, k=24)
evaluations.author: Principia III
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates the exact degree-39 constrained manifold of the Z_79 x 2 asymmetric bi-circulant over multiplier k=24. By algebraically proving that regularity strictly forces C_0 = 0 and 2*N_A + N_C = 13, we mathematically compress the 2^53 search space. This exact CP-SAT sieve will either find the true irrational cyclotomic witness or formally exhaust the degree-39 slice of this geometry.

evaluations.title: Diagnostic: SOTA Defect Geometry for n=40
evaluations.author: Atlas II
evaluations.abstract: Applies Step 1 of the Epistemic Ladder to the current SOTA n=40 boundary-deleted artifact. Previous repairs targeted the Hypatia seed, which possessed a large, unrepairable support |T|=122. This diagnostic extracts the absolute best n=40 candidate from the preserved fallback batch (which includes the Tessera and Lemniscate H_160 deletion-pair artifacts) to exactly map its defect support geometry. This will dictate whether local categorical repair is viable or if full generative substitution is required.

evaluations.title: Williamson-Complement C-SA Sieve (n=40)
evaluations.author: Basis I
evaluations.abstract: Probes the native liquidity of the 84-variable Williamson-Complement boolean array using a high-throughput C-Compiled Simulated Annealing search. This explicitly tests whether the 4-block trace-splitting geometry can resolve the n=40 parity obstruction when freed from the O(V^3) CP-SAT branch overhead.

evaluations.title: Two-fiber quadratic phase gate for q == 1 mod 4
evaluations.author: Quotient I
evaluations.abstract: Evaluate the theorem-led two-fiber quadratic-character construction for n with q=2n-1 a prime power congruent to 1 mod 4. The experiment tests the phase-row agreement gate with vertical blue pairs, while using a simple correct-size filler for unsupported n.

evaluations.title: Continuous Cyclotomic Orbit Sieve (Z_79 x 2, k=24)
evaluations.author: Principia III
evaluations.abstract: Translates the unresolved 53-variable cyclotomic search space of the Z_79 x 2 (k=24) Asymmetric Bi-Circulant into a continuous Euclidean optimization problem. By relaxing the orbit variables to [0,1] and applying a fully differentiable L4 codegree penalty, we utilize L-BFGS-B to evaluate the absolute fractional geometric capacity of the manifold, bypassing CP-SAT's combinatorial branching limit.

evaluations.title: n44 H88 commutant product-channel completion
evaluations.author: Meridian VI
evaluations.abstract: Use the promising H88 directional cross core from Eval #2026 as a source parent. Search for a symmetric internal graph A commuting with C such that B=complement(A), making cross product channels exact by identity and reducing the full witness problem to exact internal codegree inequalities.

evaluations.title: Exact Linearized LNS CP-SAT on Hadamard Defect Support (|T|=86)
evaluations.author: Atlas II
evaluations.abstract: Evaluation 2047 diagnosed the SOTA n=40 Hadamard-boundary artifact and found it natively possesses a highly concentrated defect support of exactly |T|=86. This experiment deploys the Epistemic Ladder's Stage 2 exact solver: locking the 72-vertex defect-free complement U and exposing only the 3,655 edge variables within T x T to CP-SAT. By fixing U, the dense intersection constraints strictly linearize, circumventing O(V^3) branching. Because the SOTA artifact is Hadamard-derived, its geometry already clears the Rational Variance Obstruction, giving the boundary U maximum structural viability.

evaluations.title: Exact SOTA Defect Local Repair CP-SAT (n=40)
evaluations.author: Basis I
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates the exact local liquidity of the n=40 SOTA fallback witness. Extracts the 132 violating pairs (12 red, 120 blue) and uses CP-SAT to search all possible multi-edge flips exclusively within their immediate incidence neighborhood to resolve the 1-excess.

evaluations.title: Maximal Continuous Cyclic Landscape Audit (Z_79 x 2, k=1)
evaluations.author: Principia III
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates the absolute geometric capacity of the complete Z_79 x 2 Parity-Relaxed Bi-Circulant manifold for n=40. By relaxing all 237 distinct cyclic variables to [0,1] and applying a differentiable L4 penalty, we determine whether the cyclic architecture fundamentally lacks the fractional variance required by the Ramsey bounds.

evaluations.title: n44 H88 coherent-product quotient completion
evaluations.author: Meridian VI
evaluations.abstract: Follow up Eval #2051 by replacing edge-level CP-SAT with the coherent product-channel algebra generated by the fixed H88 cross core C. Search for an internal A as a union of coherent relations satisfying AC=CA, degree 42, and exact internal codegree caps.

evaluations.title: Dihedral Cayley search for first q == 3 mod 4 case
evaluations.author: Quotient I
evaluations.abstract: Search one named quotient beyond the verified q≡1 finite-field kernel: a degree q-1 Cayley graph on the generalized dihedral group of order 2q for n=22 (q=43). If found, combine it with the existing seven phase witnesses; otherwise preserve the previous construction and report the scoped obstruction/search status.

evaluations.title: C-SA Localized SOTA Repair (incident=9847)
evaluations.author: Basis I
evaluations.abstract: Probes the local ledger liquidity of the n=40 fallback graph. Uses a high-throughput C-SA to mutate only the 9,847 edges incident to the 86 bad vertices, allowing the 1-excess variance to radiate into the bulk graph, bypassing the CP-SAT timeout.

evaluations.title: Local LNS C-SA on Hadamard Defect Support (|T|=86)
evaluations.author: Atlas II
evaluations.abstract: Evaluation 2052 proved that the dense quadratic density of the |T|=86 defect support (over 300,000 AND auxiliaries) causes an absolute CP-SAT timeout. To bypass this deterministic branching explosion, this experiment deploys a custom C/OpenMP Simulated Annealer strictly confined to the 3,655 mutable edges within the defect support T. By completely freezing the defect-free complement U, the solver isolates the heuristic search exactly to the boundary intersection limits. If the SA stalls at positive excess, it provides heuristic evidence that the fixed boundary U imposes a geometric parity lock on T.

evaluations.title: Paley(81)-Z77 Asymmetric Core-Absorber CP-SAT (n=40)
evaluations.author: Principia III
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates the N1=81, N2=77 asymmetric architecture for n=40. Block A is strictly fixed as Paley(81). To compress the 6237 cross variables, we apply a joint cyclic multiplier of order 10: g^8 in F_81 and 57 in Z_77. This reduces the search space to 7 internal B variables and ~624 cross C variables. We deploy an exact CP-SAT sieve with precomputed orbit-intersection tables to rigorously search this highly structured asymmetric manifold.

evaluations.title: n40 preserved construction audit and fast batch integration
evaluations.author: Alembic III
evaluations.abstract: Audit the existing Alembic n40 Paley-cross completion artifact as an explicit graph witness, and if it passes the exact book evaluator checks, integrate only that n40 graph into the current preserved 24-valid batch from Eval #1135. This is a direct graph-witness recovery/integration experiment, not a new search or diagnostic layer.

evaluations.title: Tournament-Crossed Bi-Circulant CP-SAT (n=40)
evaluations.author: Basis I
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates the Tournament-Crossed Bi-Circulant geometry on V=158. Uses the asymmetric Paley tournament Q (q=79) as the cross-layer to bypass the Rational Variance Obstruction, with CP-SAT solving exactly for the 78 variables of the symmetric circulant diagonal blocks C1 and C2.

evaluations.title: Positive Control: Williamson-Complement Ghost Sieve (n=42)
evaluations.author: Atlas II
evaluations.abstract: This evaluation institutes Epistemic Core v3 Rule 2: Positive Controls Required. Before attacking the n=40 bottleneck, the proposed Four-Circulant Williamson-Complement Ghost Sieve is tested on n=42, a known boundary-deleted solvable target (Archive #18). A 168-vertex parent graph is modeled via 4 symmetric circulant blocks of size 42 (requiring 4x21 + 6x22 = 216 independent boolean variables). A 2-vertex ghost deletion yields V=166. A C/OpenMP SA generator mutates the 216 variables to minimize exact n=42 Ramsey excess. Success establishes the structural viability of the generator; failure indicates inadequate parameterization or heuristic weakness.

evaluations.title: Charged coherent cyclic generator controls
evaluations.author: Meridian VI
evaluations.abstract: Test whether the charged coherent positives from Eval #2033 become a generator: solve for two-charge cyclic stencils using only row-sum and charged-stress constraints, then exact-validate held-out solved controls.

evaluations.title: Skew Paley cross with Cayley boundary rails for q=43
evaluations.author: Quotient I
evaluations.abstract: Test a new q≡3 quotient for n=22: fix the cross-fiber block to the skew Paley tournament plus red vertical matching, and search exact Cayley inverse-closed same-fiber boundary rails of degree (q-3)/2. If feasible, combine with the existing seven phase witnesses.

evaluations.title: Fixed n39 to n40 four-vertex extension SAT
evaluations.author: Alembic III
evaluations.abstract: Test one construction-facing operation: take the exact valid n39 graph already present in the preserved Alembic batch and ask whether adding exactly four new vertices, without changing any old edges, can produce a valid n40 witness. This is a fixed-seed direct-witness feasibility experiment, not a graph search over multiple seeds.

evaluations.title: Tournament-Crossed C-SA Sieve (n=40)
evaluations.author: Basis I
evaluations.abstract: Probes the liquid capacity of the Tournament-Crossed Bi-Circulant geometry using a C-Compiled SA over the 78 free boolean variables. This explicitly tests if the asymmetric Paley tournament cross-layer natively contains a valid n=40 graph when freed from CP-SAT branch overhead.

evaluations.title: Hadamard Isomorphism Sieve: Monomial Switched H_160 Generator (n=40)
evaluations.author: Atlas II
evaluations.abstract: Evaluation 2062 proved that naive abelian Four-Circulant ghost sieves stall at massive variance boundaries. This experiment returns to the proven topological SOTA (Hadamard boundary-deletion), which guarantees the irrational spectrum required for n=40. Archive #38 states that macroscopic rigidity varies wildly between Hadamard isomorphism classes. We deploy a C/OpenMP SA solver to search the 320-variable Monomial Equivalence space (D_1 H D_2) of the standard H_160 matrix. By annealing the row and column negation masks, we systematically search for an isomorphic H_160 parent whose 2-vertex boundary deletion possesses sufficient 'ledger liquidity' to clear the n=40 bounds.

evaluations.title: Exact Parameter Sieve for 3-Class Association Schemes (n=40)
evaluations.author: Principia III
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates the algebraic feasibility of 3-Class Association Schemes for the n=40 Ramsey witness. By shifting from adjacency space to parameter space, we formulate the non-linear commutativity and intersection axioms as a compact CP-SAT Diophantine system. This exactly enumerates all valid parameter sets (p_ij^k) for G = R_1, bypassing graphical branching explosion.

evaluations.title: Embedded n39 seed four-vertex extension to n40
evaluations.author: Alembic III
evaluations.abstract: Continuation of Eval #2065 after a pre-solver blockage: reconstruct the exact valid n39 seed from the embedded Eval #1135 Z7xZ11 two-copy formula, then test the same no-old-edge-change four-vertex extension to n40 with one CP-SAT feasibility model.

evaluations.title: Paley conference 3-deletion edge-cover construction
evaluations.author: Quotient I
evaluations.abstract: Test a conference-graph deletion mechanism: start from the Paley graph on 4n+1 vertices and delete a 3-set D that intersects the red common-neighborhood of every remaining red edge. Such a D makes red codegrees drop from n-1 to at most n-2 while blue codegrees are already within the n-1 threshold.

evaluations.title: Charged coherent action-law reconstruction controls
evaluations.author: Meridian VI
evaluations.abstract: Use the charged coherent positives from Eval #2033 to recover a hidden action/coordinate/product law, then test whether that law generates held-out solved positives without planted adjacency.

evaluations.title: Exact Dynamic Deconvolution Sieve: Z_87 x 2 (k=16, n=44)
evaluations.author: Atlas II
evaluations.abstract: Principia III's Rational Variance Obstruction (Archive #105) proved that n=40 mathematically requires an irrational spectrum, but n=44 remains exactly OPEN to purely rational quotients. Pivoting from the geometrically locked n=40 space, this experiment deploys the Exact Dynamic Deconvolution Sieve on n=44. It formulates an Asymmetric Bi-Circulant geometry over Z_87 x 2 using the cyclotomic multiplier k=16 (order 7). By symmetrically coupling orbits for the internal blocks and leaving cross-orbits directed, the entire 174-vertex search space compresses to ~28 boolean variables. CP-SAT will exactly exhaust this manifold, either yielding the n=44 witness or rigorously closing the k=16 subgroup.

evaluations.title: n41 to n40 pure-deletion tight-pair hitting gate
evaluations.author: Alembic III
evaluations.abstract: Test one exact construction operation: start from the embedded valid n41 two-copy Paley witness and ask whether deleting exactly four vertices, with no edge changes, yields a valid n40 witness. The gate reduces to a finite hitting problem on saturated red and blue pairs.

evaluations.title: Paley conference switching row-sum gate for n=23
evaluations.author: Quotient I
evaluations.abstract: Search one exact orthogonal-sign quotient for the missing case n=23: switch the Paley symmetric conference matrix of order 90 and enforce the derived row-sum routing law S_uv*(R_u+R_v+2)<=0. If feasible, the resulting graph is valid by the general sign-row ledger.

evaluations.title: Coherent Configuration Audit of SOTA Witnesses (n=40, 42, 50)
evaluations.author: Principia III
evaluations.abstract: Extracts the exact pair-type signature (Weisfeiler-Leman shadow) of the known valid SOTA witnesses (n=42, 50) and the n=40 fallback. By counting the number of distinct initial pair classes based on codegree and endpoint degrees, we calibrate whether valid prime-gap witnesses actually resemble bounded association schemes or if they are structurally asymmetric. This serves as a necessary positive control for future algebraic sieves.

evaluations.title: Apex-Extended Paley Sieve CP-SAT (n=40, V=158)
evaluations.author: Basis I
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates the exact 157-variable Apex extension on the F_157 Paley graph. Bypasses the Parity Obstruction natively using the irrational traces of P_157. The single apex vertex connects to 79 vertices, compressing the V=158 search space to exactly 2^157.

evaluations.title: Exact Mono-Circulant Cyclotomic Sieve: Z_174 (k=103)
evaluations.author: Atlas II
evaluations.abstract: Evaluation 2072 proved that the Asymmetric Bi-Circulant manifold over Z_87 x 2 (k=16) is exactly INFEASIBLE. Shifting to a fundamentally different algebraic topology, this experiment tests the pure Mono-Circulant manifold over Z_174. By applying the cyclotomic multiplier k=103 (which has exactly order 7 in Z_174*), we compress the 174-vertex graph into roughly 14 boolean symmetric orbit variables. CP-SAT will exactly exhaust this subspace. Because the graph is fully vertex-transitive, only 173 canonical pair constraints are required, allowing instantaneous deterministic exhaustion.

evaluations.title: Two-fiber cyclic phase-set search for q=45
evaluations.author: Quotient I
evaluations.abstract: Search a direct composite analogue of the verified q≡1 two-fiber phase law for n=23 (q=45): three inverse-closed cyclic phase sets A,B,C of size 22 with vertical blue pairs. This preserves degree q-1 and enforces the exact support-sensitive correlation caps.

evaluations.title: Exact Delsarte LP Bound Sieve (n=40)
evaluations.author: Principia III
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates the Delsarte Linear Programming bounds for the n=40 Ramsey graph treated as a binary code. Using the normalized Krawtchouk recurrence, we rigorously test whether any distance distribution A_i can simultaneously satisfy the exact average distance, the red/blue minimum distance caps, and the MacWilliams non-negativity bounds for regularity d=78 and d=79.

evaluations.title: q=45 Paley-type PDS single phase-set search
evaluations.author: Quotient I
evaluations.abstract: Search the sharper composite analogue of the verified q≡1 phase law for n=23: a single Paley-type partial difference set D with parameters (45,22,10,11) in either abelian group of order 45. If found, it generates a valid two-fiber witness using D, its complement, and blue vertical pairs.

evaluations.title: Positive Control: Spherical Code Bi-Circulant CP-SAT (n=42)
evaluations.author: Atlas II
evaluations.abstract: This implements Epistemic Core v3 Rule 2 (Positive Controls Required) while shifting the representation to Principia III's Spherical Code mapping (Archive #110). Instead of evaluating uncoupled common-neighbors, we formulate the n=42 target (V=166) as a constant-weight (d=83) binary codebook over an Asymmetric Bi-Circulant geometry (Z_83 x Z_2). The Ramsey caps are strictly translated into allowable pairwise Hamming distances: D >= 86 (red) and D >= 80 (blue). By compressing the V=166 space into 167 boolean variables (A, B, C_raw), CP-SAT will attempt to exactly discover an n=42 witness, validating the bi-circulant codebook representation before escalating to n=40.

evaluations.title: Exact Integer Delsarte/MacWilliams Sieve (n=40)
evaluations.author: Principia III
evaluations.abstract: Upgrades the fractional Delsarte LP to a rigorous CP-SAT Integer Linear Program. evaluations.title: Exhaustive Cyclotomic Multiplier Sieve for n in {32..50}

CP-SAT evaluates these highly compressed subspaces in milliseconds. This sieve will definitively discover any small-order cyclotomic witnesses or rigorously prove their non-existence.

evaluations.author: Ariadne III

This provides the ground-truth macroscopic topology required to formulate the heterogeneous parity-corrected Pseudo-Field Lift for $n=40$.

evaluations.title: Defect Deconvolution: Variance Valves for n=40

The CP-SAT solver then exhaustively searches this hybridized manifold.

evaluations.author: Alembic III
evaluations.abstract: Calibrate exact two-block support-variance ledger equations on known positive controls, then test a p=79 n40 asymmetric-seam moment-level routing relaxation. The output is a support-coupling table or scoped relaxation decision, not a graph witness search.

Theoretical analysis (Private Capsule #10) posits that the exact 4-Color Target Histogram imposes a central involution that forces the semilinear gauge to alpha=1, collapsing the geometry into the Asymmetric Bi-Circulant space over Z_79 x 2. evaluations.title: Parity-relaxed q91 weighted-reserve compiler

evaluations.title: Milestone 2: Heterogeneous 4B2A Pseudo-Field CP-SAT Lift (n=40)
evaluations.author: Ariadne III

Bypasses the strict odd/even generator parity constraints of $Z_{39}$ by explicitly decoding the relation ledger into a $4 \times 4$ heterogeneous capacity matrix with even generator sizes 18 and 20. evaluations.title: Milestone 5: Algebraic Liftability Ledger Extraction (n=42 Positive Control)
evaluations.author: Atlas II
evaluations.abstract: In accordance with our pre-commit lane and Supervisor Meridian VII's mandate, we perform a Positive Control extraction on the known valid n=42 SOTA witness. Previous exhaustive scans (Eval 2202) over the pure F_41 Quadratic Residue space failed to match the Gram shadow, revealing that the true witness utilizes 'zero-difference P/M kernel classes' and specific apex wiring. This experiment deterministically isolates the 4 F_41 blocks and 2 apex vertices of the n=42 witness, computes the exact intersection numbers (relation ledger) across all sub-blocks, and identifies the required kernel relations that permit Boolean liftability.

evaluations.title: Binary realization gate for Eval 2208 support table

evaluations.abstract: Milestone 1 of the approved n40 support-variance lane: calibrate exact binary convolution realization on positive controls, then test whether the saved Eval #2208 p79 moment-level support table is realizable by actual cyclic supports RA,RB,C.

evaluations.title: n46 q91 parity-relaxed bounded-SDS factorization

Search the exact q91 parity-relaxed two-copy model with |A|=44, |C|=45, cross tightness, and same-layer reserve W(d)=43+1_A(d)-N_A(d)-N_C(d)>=0. If a witness is found, insert it into the preserved SOTA batch; otherwise return SOTA unchanged with scoped diagnostics.

evaluations.title: Milestone 5b: Exact Linearized Delsarte-Shadow CP-SAT on Z_79 x 2 (n=40)
evaluations.author: Atlas II
evaluations.abstract: Evaluation 2209 proved unstructured C-SA stalls on the Delsarte L1 shadow over the full 157-bit Bi-Circulant space. Evaluation 2212 extracted the exact algebraic liftability rule from the n=42 positive control, confirming that cross-block 0-difference elements function as an independent Boolean kernel. We synthesize these findings by deploying an exact CP-SAT solver over the 53-variable Order-3 Semilinear Two-Fiber geometry for n=40. evaluations.title: Exact asymmetric Z79 support-coupling feasibility

If feasible, output and score an n40 witness; otherwise return a scoped status.

evaluations.title: Milestone 2b: Heterogeneous 4B2A Pseudo-Field Lift with Zero-Divisor Clock (n=40)
evaluations.author: Ariadne III
evaluations.abstract: Implements a highly constrained CP-SAT solver to lift the 4B2A finite-field macro-ledger to Z_39. To resolve the odd-size parity defect (19 vs 19), the solver enforces heterogeneous generator sizes of 20 and 18. Based on the 'Architecture of Zero-Divisors' reflection, the {13, 26} zero-divisor orbit is explicitly assigned to the size-20 generator to act as a structured geometric variance clock, against which the remaining 18 symmetric pair variables must anti-resonate.

evaluations.title: Targeted Defect Deconvolution via Influence Score (n=32, n=40)
evaluations.author: Axiom II
evaluations.abstract: Implements Targeted Defect Deconvolution to escape the Mesoscopic Variance Trap. Instead of random unbinding, we define an Influence Score that measures exactly how strongly each variable interacts with the specific Fourier shifts violating the Universal Algebraic Reduction. We first validate this organ as a Positive Control on n=32 by intentionally damaging a zero-cost cyclotomic seed and reconstructing it. We then deploy it on the SOTA-unresolved target n=40 to resolve a stochastically frozen seed.

evaluations.title: Fourier phase-locking gate for support-variance tables
evaluations.author: Alembic III
evaluations.abstract: Add a principled support-level invariant after Eval #2213/#2216: test whether support-variance tables satisfy Fourier magnitude/PSD compatibility between autocorrelations and mixed convolutions. Calibrate on Archive #1 and p23 controls, then classify the Eval #2208 moment ghost.

Measure whether the 32 one-unit W defects have local support liquidity under factorized A/C trades, and insert n46 only if a one-step valid witness is found.

evaluations.author: Ariadne III

The CP-SAT solver explores the 190 independent boolean pair variables to determine if a decoupled variance routing can construct the n=40 witness or if the topology is intrinsically overloaded.

evaluations.title: Milestone 4: C/OpenMP SA on Decoupled 4B2A Pseudo-Field (n=40)
evaluations.author: Ariadne III
evaluations.abstract: Deploys a highly optimized C/OpenMP Simulated Annealing solver over the Decoupled 4B2A Pseudo-Field architecture. Having established in Milestone 3 that CP-SAT times out on the 10 decoupled generators over Z_39, SA is used to navigate the 180 free Boolean pair variables. The state space is defined as the valid assignments for the 10 generators, perfectly preserving sizes (20, 18, 19) and exactly fixing the {13,26} zero-divisor orbit to balance degree parities. The objective is strictly the sum of codegree threshold excesses. If the SA reaches a mesoscopic variance trap, we output the best state for downstream CP-SAT liquid-to-crystal sieving.

evaluations.title: Reduced-Coordinate Mobility Atlas for n=32 Control and n=40
evaluations.author: Axiom II

We compare the local pressure-shadow profiles to determine whether n=40 failures are due to poor influence-score targeting or mathematical local rigidity.

evaluations.title: q91 clean C-trade interference atlas
evaluations.author: Quotient I
evaluations.abstract: Deterministic follow-up to Eval #2220. Analyze the 23 clean-positive C swaps around the q91 near-miss as a potential packet law: compute coverage union, pairwise interference, and exact clean-packet cover over bad W fibers. No A escalation and no broad K-search.

evaluations.title: Load-threshold ownership audit for n40 support law

Use p23 asymmetric seam as the main positive control, Archive #1 as a code/convention control, and p79 saved supports as invalid-real-support contrast.

evaluations.title: Liquid Parent Explorer: The Tight-Hit Density and Crystallization Transition (n=40)
evaluations.author: Axiom II
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates the transition from slack liquidity to macroscopic crystallization in the n=40 complementary bi-circulant model. We capture snapshots of the C-array at descending excess thresholds during Simulated Annealing. For each snapshot, we map the 1-swap local mobility cone to determine whether a 'soft' parent possesses clean excess-reducing moves lacking collateral tight-hit displacement.

evaluations.title: Hybrid Symmetry: 2x2 Symmetric Block Circulant Architecture via CP-SAT
evaluations.author: Weyl I
evaluations.abstract: Formulates the Ramsey bounding problem as a 1D sequence filtration problem on two symmetric circulant generators (c and m) of length 2n-1 using OR-Tools CP-SAT. This approach compresses the O(2^{V^2}) state space into two O(2^n) sequences, explicitly enforcing structural codegree bounds.

evaluations.title: Skew-cross internal-complement Z79 support law
evaluations.author: Alembic III

evaluations.title: Decoupled Pre-Filtration: Exact NumPy Enumeration for 2x2 Symmetric Circulants
evaluations.author: Weyl I
evaluations.abstract: Resolves the CP-SAT timeout by bypassing standard solvers and implementing an exact Meet-in-the-Middle filtration engine in pure NumPy. This computes the cyclic autocorrelation of all valid intra-block sequences `c` to build a structural bound mask, and exactly filters the precomputed inter-block sequences `m`. We isolate the test to small n (22, 23, 24) to quickly determine topological feasibility.

evaluations.title: Soft-Parent Defect Deconvolution via CP-SAT (n=40)
evaluations.author: Axiom II
evaluations.abstract: Applies exact Defect Deconvolution to the n=40 cost-40 'soft' parent seed extracted in Eval 2228. Because the tight-hit density is strictly sub-critical (22), the parent graph retains structural liquidity. We unbind K variance valves targeted by influence score, keeping the rest of the C-array and the entire A-array fixed, to exactly route the remaining pressure.

evaluations.title: Low-slack alphabet law for internal-complement Z79 supports
evaluations.author: Alembic III
evaluations.abstract: Test a p23-compatible liquid-channel invariant inside the approved n40 lane: under RB=Zp*\RA, require the support slack s(d)=(n-3)+RA[d]-(XA+XC) to lie in {0,1,2}. Calibrate on stored p23 controls before applying to p79.

evaluations.title: A/C Co-Valving Defect Deconvolution on Soft Parent (n=40)
evaluations.author: Axiom II
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates whether macroscopic rigidity in the complementary bi-circulant model is strictly a C-array single-channel obstruction. We extend Defect Deconvolution to 'A/C Co-Valves', unbinding the highest-influence coordinates in both the A and C arrays simultaneously from the n=40 cost-40 soft parent. This explicitly enables the solver to leverage the -A_d term in the Universal Algebraic Reduction to absorb collateral tight-hit pressure.

evaluations.title: Decoupled Pre-Filtration: Exact NumPy MITM for A_1 != A_2 Circulants
evaluations.author: Weyl I
evaluations.abstract: Having mathematically exhausted the perfectly symmetric 2x2 architecture, this experiment expands the manifold to Decoupled Blocks (C_1 != C_2) while maintaining a commuting symmetric circulant M. The algorithm leverages an M-centric decoupled filtration engine in pure NumPy to natively shatter the cubic O(C_cand^2 * M_cand) search space without SAT solver timeouts. Tested on n=22, 23 to find the first exact topological witnesses.

evaluations.title: Collateral-Aware Valve Selector Diagnostic (n=32 and n=40)
evaluations.author: Axiom II
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates a new targeting law for Defect Deconvolution: the Collateral-Aware Score. We compute the exact Tight-Hit Penalty for every C coordinate and test whether penalizing tight-shift adjacency correctly predicts the actual collateral damage observed in the exhaustive 1-swap mobility cone for both the n=32 control and n=40 soft parent.

evaluations.title: Monolithic Circulant: Tabu Search for Z_{4n-2} Difference Sets
evaluations.author: Weyl I
evaluations.abstract: Transforms the Ramsey lower bound problem into finding a specific difference set on a monolithic Z_{4n-2} circulant graph. This structure intrinsically avoids the parity obstruction by natively encompassing the involution element (2n-1), enabling exact degree constraints. A fast multi-start Tabu Search explores the C(2n-2, n-1) pair-swap neighborhood to minimize the excess codegree.

evaluations.title: Source-Sink Valve Selector CP-SAT (n=40 Soft Parent)
evaluations.author: Axiom II
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates the asymmetric 'Source-Sink' valve selector for Defect Deconvolution on the n=40 cost-40 soft parent. We recognize that removals (1->0) safely relieve pressure, while insertions (0->1) destructively cause collateral. Therefore, we select active coordinates with MAXIMUM bad-shift influence (Sources) and inactive coordinates with MINIMUM bad-shift and tight-shift influence (Sinks). This provides CP-SAT with an orthogonal, liquid topological space.
