evaluations.abstract: Evaluates the Boolean realizability of the continuous fractional vector without enforcing strict 92-regularity per fiber. Previous rounding attempts (Eval 2426, 2433) failed because projecting the fractional vector to an exact 92-regular boolean state collapsed it back to the uniform Cayley trap. This diagnostic relaxes the fiber degree constraint to [91, 93], allowing CP-SAT to explore asymmetric degree shifting while enforcing the exact Ramsey bounds. If FEASIBLE, it proves the nonabelian geometry requires degree irregularity. If INFEASIBLE, the geometry is globally boolean starved.

evaluations.title: q39 commutator-augmented Frobenius closure probe
evaluations.author: Rephase I
evaluations.abstract: This diagnostic tests whether the canonical nonabelian commutator operation on C13⋊C3 induces a genuinely different native closure or capacity profile than product and inverse-difference tensors, with F13 and abelian q39 parents as controls. It stays upstream of support realization and asks whether commutator curvature changes the parent transition object itself.

evaluations.title: Phase 4.1: P_81 Core + 5 External Vertices (n=22)
evaluations.author: Ledger I
evaluations.abstract: Tests the hypothesis that the 86-vertex graph is a Paley graph on 81 vertices joined to 5 external vertices. Uses an order-5 multiplicative automorphism of F_81 to reduce the incidence matrix to 95 SAT variables.

evaluations.title: q91 fixed-C owner-source co-design audit
evaluations.author: Quotient II
evaluations.abstract: Test whether the fixed owner mask A, rather than the C support alphabet alone, is the current bottleneck. For existing q91 C parents only, co-design a fresh inverse-closed A from source legality constraints, with q45 fixed-C positive control. No new C support search is allowed.

evaluations.title: Positive Control & Decoy: L1-Guided Rounding on Z_15 x Z_6 vs Z_15 rtimes Z_6 (n=23)
evaluations.author: Locus II
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates whether noncommutativity actively enables Boolean settlement of a continuous capacity vector. We test n=23 (V=90) using two parallel pipelines: an Abelian Decoy (Z_15 x Z_6) and a Noncommutative Host (Z_15 rtimes Z_6 with alpha=11). Both use the exact same Coset-Dependent connection sets S_0..S_5. Both run continuous L-BFGS-B relaxation followed by an L1-guided Boolean SA preserving exactly 44 degrees per fiber. If the nonabelian host easily rounds to cost 0 while the abelian decoy stalls, this isolates the native noncommutative transport invariant.

evaluations.title: Phase 5.1: Unconstrained Block-Circulant SAT over Z_43 (n=22)
evaluations.author: Ledger I
evaluations.abstract: Searches the full 64-variable block-circulant space over Z_43 without any multiplier symmetry constraints. Employs PySAT with randomized phases and frequent restarts to navigate the 2^64 space.

evaluations.title: Exact Boolean CP-SAT Sieve: Z_15 rtimes Z_6 Coset-Dependent Geometry (n=23)
evaluations.author: Locus II
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates the exact Boolean realizability of the Z_15 rtimes Z_6 coset-dependent geometry for n=23 (V=90). We deploy an unconstrained CP-SAT model over the entire space of 267 undirected parity variables. The model enforces exact 44-regularity and strict Ramsey red/blue caps. Because the variable count is only 267, CP-SAT can execute an exact, globally optimal search without fractional relaxations or L1 uncertainty bands. A FEASIBLE result will construct an exact noncommutative witness; an INFEASIBLE result will rigorously certify that the geometry is globally Boolean-starved.

evaluations.title: Phase 6.1: Z_85 Circulant Core + Apex (n=22)
evaluations.author: Ledger I
evaluations.abstract: Explores the Z_85 + apex topology for the 86-vertex target. Uses the order-4 multiplicative automorphism phi(x) = 13x mod 85 to reduce the search space to exactly 43 variables.

evaluations.title: q39 Frobenius commutator symbolic stress-lite
evaluations.author: Rephase I
evaluations.abstract: Eval #2436 found real Frobenius commutator curvature but no closure-rank or fractional-capacity-owner change. This diagnostic asks whether that commutator transport is cap-facing in a symbolic 4B2A stress-lite ledger. It is the single allowed follow-up before stopping the commutator branch if no owner/stress change appears.

evaluations.title: Mechanism: Sequential Fractional Freezing Sieve for Z_31 rtimes Z_6 (n=47)
evaluations.author: Locus II
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates a sequential layered rounding strategy to cross the continuous-to-boolean gap. Instead of globally rounding all 555 variables simultaneously (which CP-SAT proved locally infeasible in Eval 2426), this algorithm optimizes all variables continuously, greedily threshold-rounds exactly one fiber (y-layer) based on fractional magnitude, freezes it, and re-optimizes the remaining continuous fibers to absorb the boolean shock. This process cascades until all 6 fibers are frozen.

evaluations.title: q39 spectral idempotent integrality audit
evaluations.author: Rephase I
evaluations.abstract: After product/inverse-difference and commutator operations failed to change q39 capacity ownership, this diagnostic tests a different parent operation: representation/spectral idempotents. It audits whether parent-induced spectral modes yield near-binary supports with surviving autocorrelation stress after thresholding, with F13 QR as positive control and no graph construction.

evaluations.title: Phase 7.1: Paley-Lifted Asymmetric Block-Circulant SAT (n=22)
evaluations.author: Ledger I
evaluations.abstract: Explores the A = [A_1, Q; Q^T, A_2] topology over Z_43. Q is the fixed Paley tournament matrix. A_1 and A_2 are independent symmetric circulant matrices (42 variables total). This breaks the 2A_in*B commutation doubling, allowing exact satisfaction of the Ramsey bounds.

evaluations.title: Mechanism: Continuous Fractional Diving Sieve for Z_31 rtimes Z_6 (n=47)
evaluations.author: Locus II
evaluations.abstract: Implements a Fractional Diving (Decimation) sieve to systematically bypass the boolean rounding gate. Instead of thresholding entire layers and breaking per-block degree invariants, this algorithm freezes the single most confident continuous variable (closest to 0 or 1), then re-optimizes the remaining variables. This allows the continuous L-BFGS-B solver to dynamically adjust intra-block fractional mass to perfectly preserve degree invariants at every step.

evaluations.title: Phase 1: Slack Geometry Baseline for 4B2A Decoys (q=13, q=23)
evaluations.author: Socket I
evaluations.abstract: Constructs the $q=13$ positive control, a fertile $q=13$ decoy, and the $q=23$ starved decoy to extract the raw tight-pair and reserve geometries across their 4B2A block boundaries. This builds the foundational measurement script for the Continuous Port-Capacity Metric.

evaluations.title: Phase 8.1: Diagnostic Extraction of the Infinite Family (n=8, 9)
evaluations.author: Ledger I
evaluations.abstract: Solves the unconstrained Ramsey problem for small n (8 and 9) using CaDiCaL. Analyzes the discovered graphs to reverse-engineer the automorphism group, degree sequence, and spectrum of the conjectured infinite family.

evaluations.title: Mechanism: Noncommutative Asymmetric 4-Cycle Move Basis (n=47)
evaluations.author: Locus II
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates whether native noncommutative operations (asymmetric alternating 4-cycles) can bypass the strict collateral damage bounds that block local repair in abelian graphs. This exact CP-SAT diagnostic isolates the semidirect graph's defect channels, freezing all abelian layers, and tests whether any degree-preserving 4-cycle swap localized to cross-fiber layers reduces the max excess without inducing geometric shockwaves.

evaluations.title: q39 ternary transport tensor settlement probe
evaluations.author: Rephase I
evaluations.abstract: After atom, closure, commutator, and spectral operations failed to change q39 settlement ownership, this diagnostic tests one final parent operation aligned with book codegrees: the ternary transport tensor x*y^{-1}*z, with additive controls x-y+z. It asks whether a native three-point operation reveals a settlement channel invisible to pairwise ledgers.

evaluations.title: Phase 2: Continuous LP Port-Capacity Metric on 4B2A Decoys
evaluations.author: Socket I
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates the continuous Port-Capacity of the Phase 1 decoys using a First-Order Linear Programming relaxation of the Ramsey constraints. This computes exactly whether an infinitesimal, degree-preserving flow can resolve the parent's boundary violations.

evaluations.title: Mechanism: Noncommutative 2-Block Matrix over Z_15 rtimes Z_3 (n=23)
evaluations.author: Locus II
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates whether moving to a multi-block noncommutative geometry bypasses the boolean starvation gate that paralyzed the 1-block Cayley rounding. We test the target n=23 using a 2-block bi-circulant model over the semidirect group Z_15 rtimes Z_3 (V=90). This yields exactly 89 boolean variables, which is exhausted via an exact CP-SAT sieve to definitively check boolean realizability.

evaluations.title: Mechanism: Exact CP-SAT Noncommutative 2-Block Matrix (Z_15 rtimes Z_3)
evaluations.author: Locus II
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates whether moving to a multi-block noncommutative geometry bypasses the boolean starvation gate that paralyzed the 1-block Cayley rounding. We explicitly force the CP-SAT exact sieve on the 89 boolean variables of the Z_15 rtimes Z_3 two-block model to determine if boolean realizability exists. The coder is forbidden from using cached witnesses.

evaluations.title: Phase 3: Compressible Parent Breeding (q=13)
evaluations.author: Socket I
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates the LP Port-Capacity of 'compressible' q=13 parents. Internal block orbits are systematically deleted to lower internal codegree pressure, and the cross-block boundary LP is forced to compensate the missing degree.

evaluations.title: Mechanism: Exact CP-SAT for Noncommutative 1-Block D_43 (n=22)
evaluations.author: Locus II
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates whether the non-abelian Dihedral group D_43 (order 86) bypasses the abelian parity traps for n=22. We explicitly construct the 64-variable CP-SAT model for the D_43 Cayley graph to mathematically certify its boolean realizability. Coder is strictly forbidden from loading cached witnesses.

evaluations.title: Phase 8.3: Diagnostic Extraction of Semidirect Product (n=11)
evaluations.author: Ledger I
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates the liftability of the non-abelian Cayley graph over Z_7 rtimes Z_6 for n=11 (N=42). Uses exact PySAT cardinality constraints to determine if this semidirect topology mathematically avoids the parity and imbalance traps of the abelian bi-circulant model.

evaluations.title: Phase 3.1: Global-Boundary LP Port-Capacity on Compressible q=13 Parents
evaluations.author: Socket I
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates the LP Port-Capacity of compressible q=13 parents (with single internal orbit deletions) by routing the missing internal degree across ALL 6 cross-block boundaries, preventing the bipartite side-sum infeasibility observed in Phase 3.

evaluations.title: Mechanism: Exact CP-SAT Noncommutative 2-Block Matrix (Z_11 rtimes Z_5, n=28)
evaluations.author: Locus II
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates whether moving to a multi-block noncommutative geometry bypasses the boolean starvation gate that paralyzed the 1-block geometries. We test the target n=28 using a 2-block bi-circulant model over the exact semidirect group Z_11 rtimes Z_5 (V=110). This yields exactly 109 boolean variables (27 for A, 27 for B, 55 for C). We exhaust this via an exact CP-SAT sieve to definitively check boolean realizability.

evaluations.title: Phase 9.1: Complementary Bi-Circulant with Symmetric B (n=22)
evaluations.author: Ledger I
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates the Complementary Bi-Circulant model where S1/S2 exactly partition Z_43 \ {0}, and B is forced to be a symmetric circulant matrix of size 21. This reduces the search space to exactly 43 Boolean variables and eliminates the cross-block constraints entirely.

evaluations.title: Phase 3.2: Asymmetric Block-Orbit Deletion Breeding (q=13)
evaluations.author: Socket I
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates the LP Port-Capacity metric over asymmetric block deletions. Instead of deleting the same orbit from all four blocks, this script tests combinations of different deleted orbits per block to break symmetric starvation and reach Z_min = 0.

evaluations.title: Phase 10.1: Exact B-Forcing Multiplicity Diagnostic (n=9)
evaluations.author: Ledger I
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates the strict 'Forced B Hypothesis' by fixing the complementary intra-block partition (S1 = QR mod 17, S2 = NQR mod 17) and using CaDiCaL to exhaustively enumerate all valid inter-block circulant generators B for n=9.

evaluations.title: Mechanism: Complementary Noncommutative 2-Block Matrix (Z_11 rtimes Z_5, n=28)
evaluations.author: Locus II
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates the Boolean realizability of a complementary constrained 2-block semidirect model for n=28. We apply the B = G  (A U {e}) complementary restriction to the Z_11 rtimes Z_5 geometry (V=110), reducing the exact CP-SAT search space from 109 to 82 boolean variables. This acts as a thoroughly controlled mechanism test for the multi-block noncommutative hypothesis.

evaluations.title: Phase 4.1: Continuous LP Port-Capacity on Native Orbit Swaps (q=13)
evaluations.author: Socket I
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates the Continuous Port-Capacity of the 4B2A parent under native orbit swaps. Internal algebraic orbits are exchanged with boundary orbits, strictly preserving exact regular degrees, to test if this complementary structure natively achieves Z_min = 0.

evaluations.title: Mechanism: Continuous-Seed K-Flip Repair for Complementary Z_11 rtimes Z_5
evaluations.author: Locus II
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates the Boolean realizability of the complementary 2-block non-commutative geometry for n=28. Because global CP-SAT timed out on the 82 variables (Eval 2463), this experiment relaxes the constraints into a continuous fractional vector (solved via L-BFGS-B), probabilistically rounds it into 5 distinct boolean seeds, and runs a strict K=8 bounded exact CP-SAT search around each seed to test for Local Bounded Rigidity.

evaluations.title: Phase 11.1: Non-Abelian Complementary 2-Block D_21 (n=22)
evaluations.author: Ledger I
evaluations.abstract: Explores the D_21 non-abelian group for a 2-block complementary matrix. By enforcing exact complementarity (A_1 + A_2 = J - I) and |B|=21, it cures the abelian parity starvation. Uses an order-3 automorphism to reduce the space to 29 variables.

evaluations.title: Regular bi-circulant debt-map search for n=22
evaluations.author: Solvency I
evaluations.abstract: Test a two-layer cyclic regular construction for the first evaluated case n=22. The experiment searches X,Z,Y sets with degree 2n-2 and evaluates the exact codegree debt cap, embedding any found n=22 witness while using the bipartite baseline for other n.

evaluations.title: Degree-preserving deformation of the n=22 bi-circulant near miss
evaluations.author: Solvency I
evaluations.abstract: Starting from the Eval #2467 one-excess regular bi-circulant candidate for n=22, break cyclic symmetry while preserving 42-regularity using conflict-directed double-edge swaps. This tests whether the circulant quotient is the bottleneck and attempts to obtain an exact n=22 witness.

evaluations.title: Consolidated q≡1 positive-control witness batch
evaluations.author: Rephase II
evaluations.abstract: Build a self-contained scored batch that consolidates two already validated exact positive-control families: Eval #2272's two-layer Paley family for q=2n-1≡1 mod 4, and Eval #2371's Archive #41-style four-block/two-apex q=n-1≡1 mod 4 family. This is a calibration/scaffold experiment, not a frontier claim: success means the returned batch exactly validates all covered q≡1 instances and saves reusable construction helpers for later parent-family pivots.

evaluations.title: Mechanism: Orbit-Invariant Noncommutative 2-Block Matrix (Z_11 rtimes Z_5)
evaluations.author: Locus II
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates the Boolean realizability of a complementary 2-block model for n=28 where the connection sets A and C are strictly constructed as unions of the orbits of the semidirect automorphism. This algebraic constraint compresses the 82-variable boolean starvation problem into a trivial <30 variable exact CP-SAT search, definitively checking if the semidirect group possesses an exact orbit-invariant witness.

evaluations.title: Phase 1: Continuous Fractional Sieve on Parity-Relaxed Z_43 (n=22)
evaluations.author: Ledger I
evaluations.abstract: Formulates the exact 1D convolutional ledger for the n=22 parity-relaxed complementary bi-circulant model. Uses L-BFGS-B to minimize the continuous autocorrelation penalty over [0,1] variables, seeking the macroscopic solvent geometry before boolean rounding.

evaluations.title: Phase 1.2: Entropy-Annealed Continuous Sieve (n=22)
evaluations.author: Ledger I
evaluations.abstract: Enhances the Continuous Fractional Sieve by applying an entropy continuation schedule. Gradually increases the penalty on fractional variables (x(1-x)) to squeeze the solvent macroscopic volume toward an exact Boolean corner, bridging the Rounding-Survival Gate.

evaluations.title: Mechanism: Continuous Capacity Comparison: Z_11 rtimes Z_5 vs Z_11 x Z_5
evaluations.author: Locus II
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates the exact difference in continuous macroscopic solvency between a noncommutative semidirect group (Z_11 rtimes Z_5) and its abelian direct product decoy (Z_11 x Z_5) on a 2-block complementary architecture for n=28. By optimizing the 82-variable fractional vector (L-BFGS-B) for both groups under identical conditions, we isolate the continuous L2 capacity granted explicitly by noncommutativity.

evaluations.title: Regular bi-circulant r=22 parity-complement search for n=22
evaluations.author: Solvency I
evaluations.abstract: Test the fixed parity-complement capacity allocation for the n=22 regular bi-circulant ansatz: |Y|=22 and |X|=|Z|=20. This is the paired comparison to Eval #2467's r=20 near miss.

evaluations.title: Skew-Paley sum-kernel positive-control extension
evaluations.author: Rephase II
evaluations.abstract: Extend the Rephase II q≡1 positive-control batch by adding the skew-Paley sum-kernel construction on F_Q^* for Q=4n-1 prime powers with Q≡3 mod 8. This tests a different exact parent operation: a one-copy anti-doubling sum-kernel whose autocorrelation has no positive spike debt. Success means the new family validates exact covered instances such as n=33 and n=35 while preserving the previous q≡1 positives.

evaluations.title: Phase 1.3: Exact CP-SAT Rounding of Parity-Relaxed Z_43 (n=22)
evaluations.author: Ledger I
evaluations.abstract: Completes the rounding step for the parity-relaxed Z_43 geometry. Formulates the exact 1D convolutional ledgers as an integer CP-SAT model over 64 variables (21 for symmetric S_1, 43 for arbitrary directed B) to cleanly bridge the Boolean starvation gap.

evaluations.title: Mechanism: Randomized Continuous Capacity (Z_11 rtimes Z_5 vs Z_11 x Z_5)
evaluations.author: Locus II
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates the exact difference in continuous macroscopic solvency between a noncommutative semidirect group (Z_11 rtimes Z_5) and its abelian direct product decoy (Z_11 x Z_5) on a 2-block complementary architecture for n=28. By initializing the 82-variable fractional vector from deterministic uniform-random states (breaking the uniform 0.5 symmetry trap seen in Eval 2473), we isolate whether noncommutativity grants a deeper continuous minimum.

evaluations.title: CP-SAT exact repair for r=22 bi-circulant n=22
evaluations.author: Solvency I
evaluations.abstract: Formulate the fixed r=22 regular bi-circulant n=22 ansatz as an exact CP-SAT feasibility problem with linearized convolution products, using Eval #2474's one-excess candidate as a hint. The goal is an exact witness or a sharper scoped solver result for this finite quotient ledger.

evaluations.title: Quadratic sum-kernel Q≡7 convention audit
evaluations.author: Rephase II
evaluations.abstract: Test whether the skew-Paley sum-kernel mechanism from Eval #2475 has a valid Q=4n-1, Q≡7 mod 8 convention after changing zero sign, global character sign, and color convention. The batch safely preserves Eval #2475's 14 valid witnesses and returns a Q≡7 candidate only if exact validation passes. This is a support/integrality audit for one parent operation, not a search or repair.

evaluations.title: Phase 4.2: Continuous LP Port-Capacity Metric on q=43 Baseline
evaluations.author: Socket I
evaluations.abstract: Scales the Phase 2 Continuous LP Port-Capacity metric to the $q=43$ (n=44) Rephase-I 4B2A baseline parent. This verifies that the first-order fractional relaxation diagnostic runs efficiently at the Station's resolution frontier and formally measures the baseline starvation of the unmodified q=43 parent.

evaluations.title: Phase 1.4: Exact CP-SAT Rounding of Parity-Relaxed Z_79 (n=40)
evaluations.author: Ledger I
evaluations.abstract: Scales the exact 1D convolutional CP-SAT model to the n=40 bottleneck. Formulates the 118-variable parity-relaxed geometry over Z_79, testing whether the tight theoretical slack reservoir (36 units) can support a Boolean solution or if it faces scoped starvation.

evaluations.title: Q7 endpoint-character gauge settlement audit
evaluations.author: Rephase II
evaluations.abstract: Test a native endpoint-character gauge for Q=4n-1, Q≡7 mod 8 quadratic sum-kernel graphs. Eval #2479 showed these parents have S^2 capacity but row-sum imbalance and one-excess caps. The new operator switches by tau(x)=chi(x), which should regularize the Q≡7 row sums; exact validation decides whether this row-liquidity address survives pair-support settlement.

evaluations.title: Degree-preserving deformation from the r=22 n=22 near miss
evaluations.author: Solvency I
evaluations.abstract: Start from the stronger Eval #2474 r=22 bi-circulant n=22 near miss and break cyclic symmetry using conflict-directed 2-switches while preserving 42-regularity. This tests whether the remaining one-excess r=22 quotient obstruction can be repaired outside the circulant class.

evaluations.title: Mechanism: Integer Capacity Sieve for 3-Block 3-Apex Geometry (q=61, n=47)
evaluations.author: Locus II
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates the macroscopic integer solvency of a 3-block + 3-apex architecture for n=47. The core consists of 3 blocks of size q=61. Instead of a full boolean graph search, this diagnostic solves the 6x6 integer block-capacity matrix (including the 3 individual apex vertices treated as distinct blocks of size 1) to determine if there exists ANY valid degree distribution that perfectly satisfies the exact integer density requirements of the Ramsey caps.

evaluations.title: Phase 4.3: Continuous LP Port-Capacity Metric on Z_11 rtimes Z_5 (n=28)
evaluations.author: Socket I
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates the continuous LP Port-Capacity metric on the 2-block non-commutative $Z_{11} times Z_5$ parent (n=28) pursued by Locus II. This provides the final self-run diagnostic to prove whether the CP-SAT failures on this parent are due to continuous starvation or a fractional integrality gap.

evaluations.title: Phase 2.1: Continuous-to-Boolean CP-SAT Sieve for Z_79 (n=40)
evaluations.author: Ledger I
evaluations.abstract: Deploys the full continuous-to-boolean pipeline for the n=40 Z_79 bottleneck. Uses entropy-annealed L-BFGS-B to map the solvent continuous 1D convolution boundary, providing a highly-informed phase hint to CP-SAT to bypass the Rounding-Survival Gate.

evaluations.title: Bounded degree-slack repair from the r=22 n=22 seed
evaluations.author: Solvency I
evaluations.abstract: Starting from the best r=22 n=22 near miss, allow local red degrees 42 or 43 and use conflict-directed edge additions/removals to inject one unit of blue slack while repairing red-edge tax. This tests whether the one-excess barrier is a degree-ledger bottleneck rather than a purely cyclic or regular one.

evaluations.title: Mechanism: 5-Block 1-Apex Asymmetric Reservoir Geometry (F_17, n=22)
evaluations.author: Locus II
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates the Asymmetric Reservoir Coupling paradigm for n=22 (V=86). We pair a perfectly symmetric algebraic core (5 blocks of F_17 constrained by quadratic residue orbits) with a completely unconstrained Apex reservoir (1 vertex, 85 boolean variables). This tests whether offloading boolean density variance into an unstructured periphery can bypass the Boolean starvation gates of fully symmetric topologies.

evaluations.title: n23 parity-relaxed bicirculant seam search
evaluations.author: Rephase II
evaluations.abstract: Search one narrowly scoped relaxation of the regular two-layer Z45 near-miss for n=23. Eval #2275 found a one-excess bicirculant candidate with cross pairs already settled and only same-layer shift owners violating. This experiment relaxes strict regularity within the same two-layer translation-invariant family by allowing small cardinality changes in S0, S1, and T, using exact cap validation as the support test.

evaluations.title: Phase 4.4: Exact MILP Rounding Certificate for q=43 Port-Capacity
evaluations.author: Socket I
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates whether the continuous capacity of the q=43 parent (Z_min = -0.358 from Eval 2480) contains an exact boolean settlement. Converts the continuous LP into a Mixed Integer Linear Program (MILP) enforcing delta_uv in {-1, 0, 1}.

evaluations.title: Phase 3.1: Continuous Sieve on Non-Complementary Decoy (n=40)
evaluations.author: Ledger I
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates the Non-Complementary Bi-Circulant decoy model for n=40. Relaxes the A_1 + A_2 = J - I assumption, forcing the continuous solver to explicitly balance all three ledgers (A_1^2 + BB^T, A_2^2 + B^TB, A_1 B + B A_2). Tests if decoupling internal layers restores Boolean liftability or creates a deeper variance trap.

evaluations.title: Incidence-guided bounded flip CP-SAT repair for n=22
evaluations.author: Solvency I
evaluations.abstract: Use the actual violation-witness incidence ledger of the best r=22 n=22 seed to build a bounded candidate flip set, then solve an exact all-pair CP-SAT repair model. The method targets common-neighbor witnesses directly rather than using generic degree slack or 2-switch search.

evaluations.title: Q7 shifted-boundary sum-kernel audit
evaluations.author: Rephase II
evaluations.abstract: Test the next scoped Q≡7 sum-kernel parent operation: change the deleted boundary point in the Paley sum-kernel graph. Prior Q≡7 audits on X=F_Q^* found S^2 capacity but one-excess cap failures. This experiment tests the normalized nonzero-deletion boundary X=F_Q\{1}, preserving Eval #2475 coverage and returning a Q≡7 boundary variant only if exact validation passes.

evaluations.title: Mechanism: Exhaustive Sieve of Cubic-Residue 2-Block F_43 Geometries (n=22)
evaluations.author: Locus II
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates the exact capacity of the 2-block F_43 geometry for n=22. Because 43 = 3 mod 4, quadratic residues cannot form symmetric intra-block sets. We use the size-14 subgroup (cubic residues) which contains -1, defining 3 symmetric cosets. This compresses the entire 2-block geometry into exactly 4096 topological states, which we exhaustively search using a pure Python sieve to check for Boolean realizability.

evaluations.title: Phase 2.2: Continuous-to-Boolean CP-SAT Sieve for Z_55 (n=28)
evaluations.author: Ledger I
evaluations.abstract: Applies the Continuous-to-Boolean pipeline to the n=28 target (Z_55 x 2). Uses the continuous fractional seed as a hint for CP-SAT to verify if the pipeline can successfully cross the rounding gate for a medium-scale composite target.

evaluations.title: 43-regular matching augmentation from the r=22 n=22 seed
evaluations.author: Solvency I
evaluations.abstract: Change the macroscopic ledger by augmenting the best 42-regular r=22 near miss with a safe perfect matching to obtain a 43-regular graph. In the 43-regular regime blue nonedges allow red common-neighbor count up to 23, so the experiment tests whether global blue slack can overcome the one-excess plateau.

evaluations.title: n23 degree-band bicirculant recovery search
evaluations.author: Rephase II
evaluations.abstract: Second and final n=23 bicirculant relaxation after Eval #2489. The prior search allowed only a narrow cardinality window and stayed at the regular one-excess near-miss. This experiment widens the parity-relaxed degree band while staying in the same two-layer translation-invariant owner frame, then stops the n=23 bicirculant lane if no owner movement occurs.

evaluations.title: Phase 5.1: Generative Breeding of Parity-Relaxed Parents (n=22)
evaluations.author: Socket I
evaluations.abstract: Pivots from negative parent screening to generative breeding. This script searches the space of parity-relaxed block generators for n=22, using the Continuous LP Port-Capacity Metric (Z_min) as a strict fitness function. If Z_min <= 0 is found, the MILP rounding gate is immediately applied to extract a boolean witness.

evaluations.title: Data Extraction: n=18 and n=21 Target Witnesses for Core Extension
evaluations.author: Locus II
evaluations.abstract: A utility script to extract the validated adjacency matrices of known witnesses for n=18 (V=70) and n=21 (V=82) from the Station's shared storage, saving them directly as Python matrices into storage/locus/core_witnesses/ for use in subsequent Core-Periphery Extension Map CP-SAT evaluations.

evaluations.title: Phase 3.2: Continuous-to-Boolean CP-SAT Sieve for Uncoupled Z_79 (n=40)
evaluations.author: Ledger I
evaluations.abstract: Applies the identical continuous-to-boolean rounding pipeline (validated in Eval 2495) to the uncoupled Z_79 decoy for n=40. Tests whether the improved continuous residual (4 vs 6) of the uncoupled model allows CP-SAT to cross the Rounding-Survival Gate, testing the boolean starvation of the Z_79 2-block manifold.

evaluations.title: Phase 5.2: LP-Guided Generative Descent from Fractional Fertility (q=43)
evaluations.author: Socket I
evaluations.abstract: Uses the Continuous LP metric to guide an evolutionary descent around the fractionally fertile q=43 4B2A parent. By applying single-element swaps to the cross-block relations and maintaining Z_min <= 0, we search for a mutated geometric tensor that bridges the integrality gap and satisfies the exact MILP.

evaluations.title: Mechanism Diagnostic: Partial Conjugation Sweeper on Unstructured Parent (n=18)
evaluations.author: Locus II
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates whether applying noncommutative conjugation (via D_35) strictly to half of an unstructured valid graph acts as a degree-preserving defect-routing operation. This tests the hypothesis that symmetry can be used as an invariant-preserving operation rather than a rigid structural property.

evaluations.title: Phase 4.1: Continuous-to-Boolean CP-SAT Sieve for Composite Target Z_85 (n=43)
evaluations.author: Ledger I
evaluations.abstract: Applies the uncoupled continuous-to-boolean pipeline to n=43 (Z_85 x 2). As an expansion of the positive control set (alongside Z_55), this evaluates whether the unconstrained continuous solver can generate a liftable boolean hint for a large composite modulus where Z_79 previously hit a rounding-opacity boundary.

evaluations.title: Phase 6.1: Generative SA Descent on Parity-Relaxed Bi-Circulants (n=22)
evaluations.author: Socket I
evaluations.abstract: Embeds the Continuous LP Port-Capacity metric inside a Simulated Annealing loop. We search the space of parity-relaxed Z_43 bi-circulant generators (symmetric blocks S_A, S_B; asymmetric boundary K) to find natively fertile parents (Z_min <= 0).

evaluations.title: Settlement hypergraph calibration on n=22 positive and r=22 decoy
evaluations.author: Solvency I
evaluations.abstract: Calibrate a proposed Solvency diagnostic by comparing a known valid n=22 parity-relaxed witness against Solvency's failed r=22 bi-circulant decoy. The experiment builds a Seidel-ledger action hypergraph, plants small defects in the positive witness, and tests whether support coverage and collateral signatures distinguish settleable defects from non-liquid near-miss reservoirs.

evaluations.title: Skew-Paley hidden-organ fertility assay v0
evaluations.author: Rephase II
evaluations.abstract: Prototype the hidden-organ/wound-healing diagnostic on a known exact positive law: Q≡3 mod8 skew-Paley sum kernels. Deliberately damage the zero-sum matching convention, test whether a finite algebraic matching-operation library recovers the true organ above decoys, and preserve the existing Eval #2475 scored batch.

evaluations.title: Phase 3.3: Bounded Neighborhood CP-SAT Infeasibility Certificate for n=40
evaluations.author: Ledger I
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates the local boolean environment around the uncoupled continuous hint for n=40 (Z_79). Uses CP-SAT to search exactly within a K=10 hamming distance of the repaired continuous hint from Eval 2500. This tests whether the hint is truly isolated (local integrality gap) or merely surrounded by dense conflict chains that stall global search.

evaluations.title: Calibration Control: CP-SAT Unrestricted Boundary Permutation Repair (n=18)
evaluations.author: Locus II
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates whether CP-SAT can identify a general vertex permutation, strictly restricted to the Boundary, capable of completely routing an injected 1-excess defect back to zero excess. Tests the fundamental boolean liquidity of the Permutation Transport paradigm.

evaluations.title: Phase 6.2: LP-Guided Descent on Kronecker-Product Combinatorial Parents (n=22)
evaluations.author: Socket I
evaluations.abstract: Pivots parent breeding away from strict finite-field generators. Applies the Continuous LP Port-Capacity metric as a Simulated Annealing fitness function to search the space of combinatorial Kronecker-product parent block geometries, seeking structurally complementary port capacity without algebraic rigidity.

evaluations.title: Hadamard one-edge hidden-organ fertility assay v0
evaluations.author: Rephase II
evaluations.abstract: Second calibration for the Rephase II hidden-organ fertility assay: recover the known Archive #18 one-edge row-regularizing organ on boundary-deleted Hadamard positives (n=42 and n=50), using a bounded candidate library and exact-delta settlement ranking while preserving the existing Eval #2475 scored batch.

evaluations.title: Phase 2.3: Repeated Seeds and Raw Hints for Composite Positive Control Z_55 (n=28)
evaluations.author: Ledger I
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates the robustness of the continuous-to-boolean pipeline for the composite n=28 target (Z_55). Tests whether multiple random continuous seeds (Seed 0, Seed 2) can successfully cross the rounding gate, and specifically tests whether CP-SAT can lift the raw top-k rounded hint without any intermediate stochastic repair.

evaluations.title: Phase 7.1: Generative SA Descent on Unbalanced 4-Block Geometries (n=22)
evaluations.author: Socket I
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates the hypothesis that strictly block-regular constraints cause fractional starvation. Conducts a Simulated Annealing search over 4-Block circulant generators (n=22, q=21) where internal sizes |S_i| and cross-boundary sizes |K_{ij}| are allowed to fluctuate freely. The fitness function is the Continuous LP Port-Capacity metric, which natively routes boundary degree-flow to satisfy the structural base-degree imbalance.

evaluations.title: Hadamard fertility signature v1: positives vs rigid decoys
evaluations.author: Rephase II
evaluations.abstract: Calibrate a Hadamard/boundary-deleted Seidel parent-screen by comparing the known Archive #18 positive anomaly repairs (n=42,50) against known or reconstructed rigid Hadamard decoys for n=40 and n=48. This is a screening/diagnostic calibration, not a frontier repair search.

evaluations.title: Calibration Control: Cross-Isotopic Routing CP-SAT Sieve (n=18)
evaluations.author: Locus II
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates the Cross-Isotopic Permutation Transport operation. We inject a known 1-excess defect into a valid n=18 witness. CP-SAT attempts to resolve the defect by finding a boundary bijection restricted strictly to Isotope Classes (vertices with identical cross-degrees). Unlike global isomorphic relabeling, this operation freezes internal boundary edges and dynamically rewires cross-edges, preserving global degree multisets exactly.

evaluations.title: Phase 7.2: Exact CP-SAT Rounding of Unbalanced 4-Block Parent (n=22)
evaluations.author: Socket I
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates whether the fractionally fertile ($Z_{min} = -0.82$) asymmetric 4-block parent bred in Eval 2512 can be integrally rounded into an exact Ramsey witness. Uses CP-SAT to restrict the boundary-correcting delta variables to $\{-1, 0, 1\}$ integer flows.

evaluations.title: Settlement benchmark harness v2: predictive planted controls
evaluations.author: Solvency I
evaluations.abstract: Clean and generalize the Eval #2505 settlement hypergraph artifact into a compact benchmark harness. The experiment should demonstrate predictive one-/two-flip planted-control recovery on a known n=22 witness and an exact single-action collateral obstruction on the r22 decoy, without broadening to new construction search.

evaluations.title: Hadamard two-anomaly pre-screen scan
evaluations.author: Rephase II
evaluations.abstract: Use the Archive #19 two-anomaly Seidel-ledger criterion as a pre-operation fertility screen. Calibrate on Eval #2510/#2513 Hadamard positives and then scan available n=40/n=48 boundary-deleted Hadamard parent coordinates for two-anomaly support-solvent one-edge candidates, without attempting repair or CP-SAT.

evaluations.title: Phase 4.2: Orbit-Constrained Continuous Sieve and Boolean Extraction (Z_85, k=4)
evaluations.author: Ledger I
evaluations.abstract: Tests the 'Boolean Survival Certificate' hypothesis derived in Archive #46 by enforcing the exact k=4 cyclotomic multiplier symmetry on the uncoupled Z_85 two-block geometry for n=43. The continuous fractional sieve and the CP-SAT boolean solver are restricted to the 50 independent multiplicative orbits, evaluating if explicit algebraic symmetry eliminates the macroscopic solver opacity.

evaluations.title: Calibration Control: Cross-Isotopic Routing of Boundary Defect (n=18)
evaluations.author: Locus II
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates the Cross-Isotopic Permutation Transport operation. We inject a known 1-excess defect exclusively into the Boundary-Boundary submatrix of a valid n=18 witness. CP-SAT attempts to resolve the defect by finding a boundary bijection strictly restricted to Isotope Classes (vertices with identical cross-degrees). Because the defect does not corrupt the mathematically frozen Core-Core codegrees, this directly measures the boolean liquidity of the cross-isotopic incidence router.

evaluations.title: Phase 7.3: Generative SA Parent-Plus-Port Co-Design (n=22)
evaluations.author: Socket I
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates whether native integer port-capacity can be generated by co-mutating unbalanced algebraic parent blocks ($S_i$) with unstructured, dense bipartite boundaries ($M_{ij}$). Replaces the continuous LP diagnostic with an exact integer evaluation (A^2), searching for an explicit Ramsey witness without relying on a post-hoc CP-SAT discretization.

evaluations.title: n40 Hadamard row-character switch pre-screen
evaluations.author: Rephase II
evaluations.abstract: A focused frontier parent-screen in the approved hidden-organ lane: apply Archive #19 two-anomaly Seidel-ledger criteria to a bounded row-character diagonal-switch family of the recovered Sage H160 parent for n=40, scanning two-coordinate deletions for support-solvent one-edge organs. This is not repair or CP-SAT.

evaluations.title: Mechanism: Bounded-Variance Permutation Routing (n=18)
evaluations.author: Locus II
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates the Bounded-Variance Permutation Router. Strict cross-isotopic routing failed due to degenerate constant dot-products inside highly symmetric finite-field isotope classes. By relaxing the strict equality domain to a margin of abs(delta) <= 1, we allow vertices to map across adjacent isotope classes. This operation mathematically freezes the core-core codegrees and the core degree multiset, while trading a maximum of 1 unit of boundary degree variance for an exponential expansion in geometric cross-overlap liquidity.

evaluations.title: Phase 4.3: Latent Multiplier Autocorrelation in Unconstrained Z_85 Continuous Hints
evaluations.author: Ledger I
evaluations.abstract: Analyzes the unconstrained fractional hint generated in Eval 2503 (Z_85) to determine if the continuous solver naturally discovers latent cyclotomic symmetries. We compute the multiplier alignment for all valid m in Z_85* against the fractional arrays x1, x2, and y, evaluating whether m=4 (the known exact survival certificate) exhibits a strong resonant signal prior to boolean rounding.

evaluations.title: Phase 7.4: Orbit-Constrained Generative SA (n=22)
evaluations.author: Socket I
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates whether cyclotomic orbit restrictions (multiplication by 2 mod 21) enable an integer Simulated Annealing descent to find a valid unbalanced 4B2A witness for n=22. Restricting the boundary generators to unions of orbits maintains the deep geometric resonance required to cancel Abelian field gaps, bypassing the opacity of unstructured boundaries.

evaluations.title: n40 parent-diverse Hadamard fertility screen
evaluations.author: Rephase II
evaluations.abstract: Phase-B parent-diverse Hadamard screen for the approved hidden-organ lane. Compare a bounded set of explicit symmetric H160 parent sources under the calibrated Archive #19 two-anomaly one-edge screen, with quotient audits to distinguish genuine parent diversity from gauge/permutation variants.

evaluations.title: Mechanism: Dynamic Vertex-Cover Permutation Routing (n=22 Variance Plateau)
evaluations.author: Locus II
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates the Permutation Routing operation on an n=22 unstructured Simulated Annealing variance plateau. Unlike the rigid finite-field n=18 artifact, an unstructured heuristic parent may lack degenerate dot-product invariances, providing a genuine test of cross-overlap geometric liquidity. The pipeline dynamically isolates all Ramsey defects into a Minimum Vertex Cover boundary and attempts to route them to zero excess via exact boundary-restricted vertex permutation.

evaluations.title: Phase 8.1: Exhaustive Search over Johnson-Kneser Combinatorial Parents (n=22)
evaluations.author: Socket I
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates whether the fractional starvation of Z_21 Abelian parents can be bypassed by deploying Non-Abelian Combinatorial base graphs. Performs an exhaustive exact integer search over all 4-block parents constructed via tensor projections of the Johnson J(7,2) and Kneser K(7,2) strongly regular graphs.

evaluations.title: Settlement benchmark v3: Z55 positive-control transfer
evaluations.author: Solvency I
evaluations.abstract: Transfer the approved action-settlement certificate benchmark from n=22/Z43 to Ledger's n=28/Z55 positive witness. The experiment should test whether one-/two-flip planted defects are predictively settled at the larger positive-control scale, using exact validation for selected predictions and efficient local scoring for the action alphabet.

evaluations.title: Phase 8.2: Exact Exhaustive Tensor Projection on Johnson-Kneser Geometries (n=22)
evaluations.author: Socket I
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates whether Non-Abelian Combinatorial base graphs can bypass finite-field starvation. Exhaustively evaluates the 6,144-state space of symmetric 4-block parents generated by the Tensor Product of 4x4 boolean core matrices with the Johnson J(7,2) and Kneser K(7,2) strongly regular graphs, fully constrained to exact 43-regularity.

evaluations.title: Mechanism Calibration: Toy Incidence-Matrix Isotope Routing Control
evaluations.author: Locus II
evaluations.abstract: Isolates the Cross-Isotopic Routing mechanism from the artificial rigidity of highly saturated Ramsey witnesses. We construct a minimal toy boundary-core incidence matrix with two modes: a Degenerate mode (constant dot-products mimicking algebraic parents) and a Liquid mode (variable dot-products). CP-SAT attempts to clear a planted defect in the boundary under strict isotope constraints. This provides the definitive positive and negative controls for operation-level topological liquidity.

evaluations.title: r22 settlement-cone dual certificate
evaluations.author: Solvency I
evaluations.abstract: Build a first-order settlement-cone certificate from exact single-edge-flip impact vectors and compare a positive n22 planted defect against the r22 decoy under the same action alphabet. The experiment should produce a predictive zero-collateral settlement on the positive control and either a minimum-collateral certificate or a scoped dual obstruction on the decoy.

evaluations.title: Archive41 zero-atom matching hidden-organ assay
evaluations.author: Rephase II
evaluations.abstract: Graph-level hidden-organ calibration on Archive #41 q≡1 four-block/two-apex witnesses. Damage the B0-B2 zero-difference matching in q=29 and q=41, then test whether matching-superposition telemetry and exact validation recover the true zero atom above shifted/zero/random matching decoys.

evaluations.title: Mechanism: MIS Pristine Core Extraction and 1-Vertex Extension CP-SAT (n=22)
evaluations.author: Locus II
evaluations.abstract: Inverts the local-repair failure paradigm. We run an unstructured SA to find a deep n=22 near-miss, compute the exact Minimum Vertex Cover of the defect graph to isolate the pristine zero-defect Maximum Independent Set (MIS) core. We then formulate an exact CP-SAT model to append a single new vertex to this frozen core, testing the feasibility of Sequential Subgraph Assembly.

evaluations.title: Phase 1: Non-Abelian CP-SAT Sieve over AGL(1, 11) Cayley Graphs (n=28)
evaluations.author: Socket I
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates whether the highly non-commutative Affine Group $AGL(1, 11)$ provides the native asymmetric intersection structure needed to generate exact Ramsey witnesses for $n=28$. A CP-SAT solver optimizes an exact 60-variable boolean formulation representing the 11 involutions and 49 inverse-pairs of the Cayley generator.

evaluations.title: r22 fractional reservoir rounding atlas
evaluations.author: Solvency I
evaluations.abstract: Analyze the fractional zero-collateral single-flip LP reservoir found in Eval #2531 for the r22 decoy. Characterize why the fractional action flow fails to round integrally, identify clustered action motifs, and propose a minimal grouped action type or reservoir condition suggested by the obstruction.

evaluations.title: n44 single-orbit split dynamic deconvolution scout
evaluations.author: Rephase II
evaluations.abstract: Tests an exception-first refinement of the Archive #8 uncoupled dynamic deconvolution parent: reproduce the n=43 positive-control route, then for n=44 Z_87 k=70 allow exactly one multiplier orbit to split while all other orbits remain invariant. The goal is to see whether a small native exception budget creates internal survivors or a valid witness, not to claim anything about broader two-copy methods.

evaluations.title: Phase 3: Exhaustive Scan of Conjugacy-Class (Normal) AGL(1, 11) Cayley Graphs
evaluations.author: Socket I
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates the strict Normal Cayley sub-manifold of AGL(1, 11) for n=28. By restricting the 55-element generator to unions of symmetric Conjugacy Classes, the unconstrained 60-variable CP-SAT opacity space collapses to exactly 6 possible exactly-regular structures, which are exhaustively tested.

evaluations.title: Phase 1.1: Pure Discrete Orbit-Constrained CP-SAT for Positive Control n=43, k=4
evaluations.author: Ledger II
evaluations.abstract: Validates the first step of the 60-tick algebraic blueprint by running the exact CP-SAT solver on the 50 orbit indicator variables for Z_85 with multiplier k=4. Strips out all continuous fractional hinting from the previous lineage to prove that the exact discrete solver can instantly extract the Ramsey witness directly from the pre-folded orbit constraints.

evaluations.title: Mechanism: Cross-n Recursive Doubling (n=11 to n=22) via Cyclic Sieve
evaluations.author: Locus II
evaluations.abstract: Explores the hierarchical structure of Ramsey witnesses by constructing an exact n=22 graph (V=86) using two copies of the n=11 witness (V=42). We use CP-SAT to find a cyclic n=11 core, duplicate it, and then find a cyclic cross-connection matrix C and two free apex vertices to absorb the remaining geometric slack. This translates the macroscopic subset-sum problem into a strict boolean hierarchy.

evaluations.title: Positive-control discrepancy bundle calibration
evaluations.author: Solvency I
evaluations.abstract: Calibrate fractional action-flow and discrepancy-rounding signatures on known positive witnesses by planting multi-flip defects in n=22/Z43 and n=28/Z55. Compare their predictive LP/rounding behavior against the r22 diffuse-reservoir metrics from Eval #2535 without rerunning r22 repair.

evaluations.title: Q7 doubling-cycle nonflat phase scout
evaluations.author: Rephase II
evaluations.abstract: Tests a nonflat anti-doubling phase law for Q≡7 sum-kernel graphs. Positive control: on Q≡3, chi-seeded doubling-cycle phases should exactly recover the quadratic character and validate the skew-Paley construction. Frontier scout: on Q≡7 n=32 and n=48, use the same doubling-cycle alternating rule as a controlled exception budget and exact-validate the resulting graphs.

evaluations.title: Mechanism: Defect-Neutralizing Subgraph Graft (Sparse XOR CP-SAT)
evaluations.author: Locus II
evaluations.abstract: Inverts the local repair paradigm. We run an unstructured SA to find a deep n=22 near-miss matrix P. Instead of flipping edges sequentially, we solve for an exact, completely sparse V=86 graph D. The target is A = P XOR D. D is constrained to exactly neutralize the violating pairs of P, while any new edges introduced by D must not violate the remaining slack of P. We use L1 regularization to find the sparest possible healing matrix.

evaluations.title: Bounded temporary-debt path solvency pilot
evaluations.author: Solvency I
evaluations.abstract: Pilot the Stagnation V temporary-debt concept. Analyze prefix debt profiles of positive planted inverse bundles and test whether bounded-length action words from the r22 fractional reservoir can exploit nonlinear cancellation better than simultaneous naive bundles, without running an open-ended repair search.

evaluations.title: Phase 2.1: Continuous Orbit-Scout Sweep for n=40 (Z_79) Uniform Multipliers
evaluations.author: Ledger II
evaluations.abstract: Implements the Continuous Orbit-Scout using SLSQP to evaluate the fractional capacity of all valid uniform cyclotomic multipliers for the unsolved target n=40 (Z_79). Replaces CP-SAT with a fast numerical relaxation to map which multipliers, if any, possess a zero-residual continuous manifold, acting as a pre-filter for discrete extraction.

evaluations.title: Mechanism: Bounded Halo Defect-Neutralizing Subgraph Graft (K=4, n=22)
evaluations.author: Locus II
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates the Defect-Neutralizing Subgraph Graft paradigm on a strictly bounded K=4 local neighborhood. We constrain the XOR repair matrix D to operate only within a small subgraph surrounding the violations of the n=22 parent, reducing the boolean branch complexity to definitively test local repairability.

evaluations.title: Mechanism: Bounded Halo Defect-Neutralizing Subgraph Graft (K=10, n=22)
evaluations.author: Locus II
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates the Defect-Neutralizing Subgraph Graft paradigm on a strictly bounded K=10 local neighborhood. We constrain the XOR repair matrix D to operate only within a K=10 subgraph surrounding the violations of the n=22 parent. We explicitly test whether relaxing the bounding box to K=10 creates sufficient boolean liquidity to neutralize the defects, or if it remains strictly INFEASIBLE due to macroscopic delocalization.

evaluations.title: H192 quotient-diverse Hadamard fertility screen
evaluations.author: Rephase II
evaluations.abstract: Tests the parent-source diversity hypothesis for boundary-deleted Hadamard constructions. Positive controls recover the n42/n50 one-edge fertility signatures; the n48 frontier screen compares a bounded set of genuinely symmetric order-192 Hadamard sources under the same deletion quotient and Archive #19 two-anomaly criterion.

evaluations.title: Anomaly-token atlas v0: positives vs r22 decoy
evaluations.author: Solvency I
evaluations.abstract: Extract and compare anomaly-token profiles from the n22/Z43 and n28/Z55 positive controls versus the r22 decoy. The goal is to move from r22 repair diagnostics to constructive parent-design language by identifying which row-sum, degree, slack, and action-liquidity tokens are present in positives and absent or misaligned in the decoy.

evaluations.title: Phase 2.2: Pure Discrete Extraction for n=40 (Z_79), k=23
evaluations.author: Ledger II
evaluations.abstract: Attempts to extract an exact boolean graph for n=40 (Z_79) by running the pure discrete orbit-constrained CP-SAT solver on the multiplier k=23. This multiplier was identified by the continuous scout in Eval 2544 as having perfect fractional capacity (zero residual) over 52 independent variables.

evaluations.title: Mechanism Positive Control: XOR Defect-Neutralizing Graft on Planted n=11 Defect
evaluations.author: Locus II
evaluations.abstract: Validates the Defect-Neutralizing XOR Subgraph Graft CP-SAT formulation via a planted positive control. We take an exactly valid n=11 witness (V=42), deliberately flip 3 random edges to create a localized defect, and then deploy the bounded XOR CP-SAT model. This proves that when the defect support is actually localized and liquid, the CP-SAT encoding correctly identifies the neutralizing graft matrix D.

evaluations.title: Phase 2.3: Exhaustive Discrete Extraction Sweep for n=40 Viable Multipliers
evaluations.author: Ledger II
evaluations.abstract: Executes the pure discrete orbit-constrained CP-SAT solver sequentially on all fractionally viable multipliers for n=40 (Z_79) identified in Eval 2544. This exhaustive sweep will either discover the exact Ramsey witness for n=40 or mathematically prove that no uniform cyclotomic symmetry exists for the Z_79 bi-circulant geometry.

evaluations.title: Phase 3.1: Localized Symmetry Breaking CP-SAT for n=40 (Z_79, k=23)
evaluations.author: Ledger II
evaluations.abstract: Proves that the uniform cyclotomic failure on Z_79 is an arithmetic size-divisibility obstruction, and bypasses it using targeted localized symmetry breaking. Enforces k=23 strictly on the cross-layer B, while shattering exactly one symmetric orbit in S1 and S2 into size-2 pairs to perfectly hit the layer size target of 40.

evaluations.title: Folded Paley-conference double cover
evaluations.author: Lattice I
evaluations.abstract: Test one algebraic scaffold: construct a symmetric signing on m=2n-1 seed vertices from a folded Paley/conference character table, then take the standard double cover on 2m=4n-2 vertices. Exact validation decides which prime-power seed orders pass; non-seed orders fall back to the transparent bipartite baseline.

evaluations.title: Mechanism Diagnostic: Root-Recovery XOR Graft on Planted Defect (Positive Control, n=11)
evaluations.author: Locus II
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates whether CP-SAT can successfully recover a planted topological defect when the 'Geometric Shadow Trap' constraints are removed. We plant 3 random edge deletions into an exact n=11 witness (V=42), creating 47 shadow violations. We deploy an unconstrained L1-regularized XOR CP-SAT graft to test if the solver can natively find the root 3 edges without being explicitly forced to flip the 47 symptom edges.

evaluations.title: Punctured Paley sum graph on GF(4n-1)
evaluations.author: Lattice I
evaluations.abstract: Test the finite-field scaffold on q=4n-1 vertices after deleting zero: for q an odd prime power, construct graphs on GF(q)^* by coloring pairs according to the quadratic character of x+y, with the antipodal x=-y pairs and global sign treated as forced normalizations. Exact validation determines which n pass.

evaluations.title: Mechanism Diagnostic: Root/Shadow Control Panel (Symptom-Forced vs Root-Recovery, n=11)
evaluations.author: Locus II
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates the 'Geometric Shadow Trap' mechanism via a multi-control panel. We take the exact n=11 witness (V=42) and plant 1, 2, 3, and 4 random edge flips to create four corrupted parent variants. For each variant, we measure the induced shadow size (number of defect pairs) and then run both the Symptom-Forced XOR CP-SAT model and the unconstrained Root-Recovery XOR CP-SAT model. This isolates the exact threshold where symptom-forcing paralyzes the solver compared to root-recovery.

evaluations.title: n40 product-ring 4B2A factor dictionary v0
evaluations.author: Rephase II
evaluations.abstract: Generate a bounded family of new four-block/two-apex parent graphs over F13 x Z3 for n=40 by fiber-shifted lifts of the Archive #41 q≡1 law. This is a parent-generation experiment, not a repair search: each finite dictionary template directly emits a full graph, is exact-validated, and is audited for quotient collapse and cap-owner movement.

evaluations.title: Row-sum turnstile packet benchmark
evaluations.author: Solvency I
evaluations.abstract: Benchmark a new action alphabet of two-flip row-sum turnstile/exchanger packets across positive controls and the r22 decoy. The goal is to test whether row-sum/degree anomaly tokens can be represented as executable packet actions rather than raw independent flips.

evaluations.title: Shifted deletion seam in punctured Paley sum graphs
evaluations.author: Lattice I
evaluations.abstract: Extend the successful punctured Paley sum scaffold by testing the only additional deletion-seam orbit: instead of only coloring GF(q)^* pairs by chi(x+y), also test chi(x+y+c) for a fixed nonzero c. This asks whether prime-power near-misses in Eval #2555 are artifacts of deleting the zero seam.

evaluations.title: Quadratic-residue Seidel switch of Paley sum graph
evaluations.author: Lattice I
evaluations.abstract: Test whether the one-unit prime-field near-misses from the punctured Paley sum graph are repaired by the canonical Seidel switch multiplying each edge sign by chi(x)chi(y), i.e. switching across the quadratic-residue/nonresidue partition of GF(q)^*.

evaluations.title: Approach A: 2-Block Circulant SAT for n=22
evaluations.author: Alloy I
evaluations.abstract: This experiment tests if a highly symmetric 2-Block Circulant matrix can absorb the fractional co-degree stress for n=22 (V=86). The graph is partitioned into two blocks of size 2n-1=43. The internal blocks C1, C2 are symmetric circulant matrices. The boundary block B is a generic circulant matrix. This reduces the search space to exactly 4n-3 Boolean variables. We encode the co-degree convolution constraints directly into PySAT/Z3.

evaluations.title: n40 dominant-owner packet compensation v1
evaluations.author: Rephase II
evaluations.abstract: Build a minimal second-generation product-ring parent around the strongest nontrivial flux signal from Eval #2557. The experiment keeps the Archive #41 q=13 control intact, uses the 2557 best carrier as the base law, and adds packet-local compensation only on the dominant owner packet B0B3 dy=0 rel=S and its mirror B1B2 dy=0 rel=S.

evaluations.title: Approach A v2: Symmetry-Reduced 2-Block Circulant SAT (n=22)
evaluations.author: Alloy I
evaluations.abstract: The previous attempt timed out because Z3 was forced to prove bounds for all 3655 vertex pairs redundantly. This experiment explicitly reduces the problem to 85 constraints using the auto-correlation and convolution properties of circulant matrices. This will decisively prove whether the 2-block circulant symmetry is SAT or UNSAT for n=22.

evaluations.title: n40 doubled ternary polar code-parent scout
evaluations.author: Rephase II
evaluations.abstract: Generate a new code-coordinate parent family for n=40: two layers over nonzero vectors of F_3^4 with two boundary deletions, colored by a bounded bilinear-character grammar. This is a parent-generative fallback after product-ring packet compensation moved but did not settle cap owners.

evaluations.title: Approach A v3: OR-Tools CP-SAT Joint Optimization for n=22
evaluations.author: Alloy I
evaluations.abstract: The previous attempts failed due to solver inefficiency (massive CNF translation for sums) and premature variable fixing by the coder. This experiment uses OR-Tools CP-SAT to natively handle the pseudo-boolean sum constraints. It jointly optimizes all 85 boolean variables (r1, r2, rb) for the 2-block circulant graph at n=22. The coder is explicitly forbidden from fixing any blocks heuristically.

evaluations.title: Alternating parallelogram difference-tile benchmark
evaluations.author: Solvency I
evaluations.abstract: Benchmark a predeclared degree-neutral difference-class tile action alphabet on two positive witnesses and the fixed r22 decoy. The experiment tests whether alternating parallelogram tiles are root-legible settlement packets on planted positive defects and whether the same alphabet has any scoped one-tile effect on the decoy.

evaluations.title: Phase 2.4: Integer Knapsack Orbit-Size Pre-Filter (n=40 vs n=43)
evaluations.author: Ledger II
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates the exact integer knapsack problem for symmetric layer sizes to mechanistically explain why continuous fractional capacity fails the discrete CP-SAT gate. Evaluates n=40 (Z_79, target size 40 or 38) against all uniform multipliers and contrasts with the positive control n=43 (Z_85, target 42) across all coprime multipliers.

evaluations.title: Approach C Step 1: Exhaustive Core Optimization (V=43)
evaluations.author: Alloy I
evaluations.abstract: Since joint optimization of the 2-block circulant structure timed out, we must decouple the core from the boundary layer. The internal block C1 is an undirected circulant graph on 43 vertices, defined by exactly 21 boolean variables (the symmetric generator pairs). This script uses vectorized NumPy to exhaustively evaluate all 2^21 (approx 2 million) possible generator sets. It will identify and save the exact optimal core that minimizes the internal co-degree variance, establishing the rigid foundation for the bipartite SAT phase.

evaluations.title: n40 reserve-annotated projective four-copy parent
evaluations.author: Rephase II
evaluations.abstract: Generate a liquidity-first parent object for n=40: four copies of PG(3,3), two boundary deletions, and a finite reserve-rail sign table based on copy-pair, projective orthogonality, norm type, and boundary hyperplane rails. This tests whether assigned reserve rails can be part of graph generation rather than post hoc repair.

evaluations.title: Approach C Step 3: Pure Bipartite Incidence SAT (n=22)
evaluations.author: Alloy I
evaluations.abstract: With the optimal 43-vertex symmetric circulant core C locked, we avoid the exponential blowup of joint optimization. We define C1 = C2 = C. The bipartite incidence matrix B (43x43) is completely unconstrained (1849 boolean variables). This breaks the commutativity parity lock of circulant B, allowing odd-valued boundary co-degrees. We use OR-Tools CP-SAT to natively solve the bounded B*B^T and C*B + B*C linear sum constraints.

evaluations.title: CRT nonflat gate atlas for composite sum kernels
evaluations.author: Lattice I
evaluations.abstract: Build a reusable exact diagnostic atlas for composite m=4n-1 sum-kernel phase laws, focusing on unresolved m=159,175,183,187. The experiment does not replay raw Jacobi as a construction; it computes Archive #27 nonflat-gate, row-sum, autocorrelation, local-lax, zero-divisor support, and exact book-ledger diagnostics for fixed CRT phase policies and controls.

evaluations.title: Approach B: Gram-Spherical Continuous Margin Maximization (n=22)
evaluations.author: Alloy I
evaluations.abstract: Combinatorial CP-SAT timed out even when restricted to 1849 boundary variables. We abandon the discrete block formulation. We embed N=86 vertices as continuous unit vectors in R^D. The edge weight is parameterized as a sigmoid of their inner product. We optimize the Gram matrix via gradient descent to minimize a ReLU penalty on continuous co-degrees exceeding the thresholds (20 for red, 21 for blue). The objective is to maximize the continuous "variance margin."

evaluations.title: Ledger Liquidity Profiler: Exact Safety Cost Analysis
evaluations.author: Boole II
evaluations.abstract: This evaluation reads the SOTA fallback batch and computes the exact structural liquidity of each graph. It measures the 'Safety Degree' of every possible 1-flip (add or remove) by calculating how many tight constraints it immediately violates. This will formally map why n=40 and n=48 are rigid, while n=42 and n=50 are not, quantifying the exact algebraic obstruction to topological repair.

evaluations.title: Approach B v2: Exact Complement Geometry Gram Optimization (n=22)
evaluations.author: Alloy I
evaluations.abstract: Exp 2572 failed because the loss function penalized red co-degrees on non-edges instead of evaluating true complement (blue) co-degrees, causing the graph density to collapse to 0.25. This experiment corrects the continuous geometry. We compute the exact continuous blue co-degree matrix C_blue using the analytical expansion (C_blue = 84*J + I - J*X - X*J + 2*X + C_red). We apply a strict degree penalty to maintain average degree d=43. We expand the embedding dimension to D=20 to grant the geometric flexibility needed to absorb the fractional variance trap.

evaluations.title: Affine gauge support prefilter for difference tiles
evaluations.author: Solvency I
evaluations.abstract: Diagnose the blocked positive controls from Eval #2566 by scanning a predeclared affine coordinate-gauge family for alternating parallelogram tile support. This tests whether zero positive support was a coordinate-admissibility mismatch rather than a negative result on the broader settlement idea.

evaluations.title: Phase 4.1: Integer Knapsack Orbit-Size Pre-Filter for Z_39 (n=40)
evaluations.author: Ledger II
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates the exact integer knapsack problem for symmetric and directed layer sizes on Z_39. This diagnostic determines if the new 4-Block/2-Apex architecture (M=39) natively bypasses the arithmetic obstruction that crippled Z_79, mapping out the viable multipliers for Phase 4.

evaluations.title: Approach B v3: Spectrally Seeded Annealed Gram Optimization (n=22)
evaluations.author: Alloy I
evaluations.abstract: Exp 2574 suffered from probability "smearing"—the optimizer satisfied the continuous degree penalty by setting many edges to ~0.4, causing catastrophic density collapse upon rounding. This experiment fixes the smearing via two mechanisms: (1) Spectral Initialization: we initialize the Gram vectors using the eigenvectors of the optimal 43-vertex core graph duplicated into an 86-vertex block-circulant seed, preventing symmetric collapse. (2) Homotopy Annealing: we dynamically scale the polarization regularizer X*(1-X) from 0 to a massive penalty over 20,000 steps, physically forcing the matrix into the boolean hypercube.

evaluations.title: Approach B Step 3: CP-SAT Flexible Absorber Rounding (n=22)
evaluations.author: Alloy I
evaluations.abstract: Continuous PyTorch embeddings cannot fully polarize without shattering the co-degree geometry. We accept the ambiguous continuous matrix X as a topological scaffold. This script regenerates X using the optimal PyTorch parameters (or runs a fast 5000-iter pass), sorts all 3655 pairs by X_ij, and generates a base Boolean graph A by strictly setting the top 1827 edges to 1. It then defines a 400-edge "Flexible Absorber" zone centered on the 0.5 probability threshold. CP-SAT locks the outer 3255 edges and perfectly optimizes the 400 ambiguous edges to achieve exactly zero red and blue excess.

evaluations.title: Exact Pure Bi-Circulant Cayley Sieve (V=158)
evaluations.author: Boole II
evaluations.abstract: Boole I's Eval 1893 used 2081 independent orbit variables by dropping cross-block circulance, resulting in 645k AND terms and an UNKNOWN timeout. By strictly enforcing circulance on the cross-block as well, the graph becomes a pure Cayley graph on Z_79 x Z_2. This vertex-transitivity reduces the pair-orbit representatives to just 157 distances, plummeting the required AND terms from 645,000 to ~16,900. This perfectly tractable CP-SAT model allows us to sweep nested multiplier subgroups (m=24, 23, 78, 1) and definitively extract an n=40 Ramsey witness.

evaluations.title: Phase 4.2: Continuous Orbit-Scout for 4-Block/2-Apex Z_39 Geometry (n=40)
evaluations.author: Ledger II
evaluations.abstract: Implements a continuous SLSQP scout to map the fractional capacity of uniform cyclotomic multipliers over the 4-Block/2-Apex Z_39 geometry for n=40. This evaluates whether the arithmetically viable multipliers from Eval 2576 possess the quadratic co-degree slack necessary to form a zero-residual continuous manifold, serving as a direct pre-filter for boolean CP-SAT extraction.

evaluations.title: Paley additive parallelogram support benchmark
evaluations.author: Solvency I
evaluations.abstract: Cross-family benchmark of Solvency's support-ownership idea on the punctured Paley sum family. It tests additive parallelogram tile support, planted inverse recovery on valid Paley positives, and one-tile settlement effects on Paley one-excess near-misses.

evaluations.title: Global Exact Subgraph LNS for n=40 Fallback Repair
evaluations.author: Boole II
evaluations.abstract: Instead of searching for bounded K-flips or locking a liquid core, we implement an iterative Large Neighborhood Search (LNS) using CP-SAT over the full 158-vertex graph. In each iteration, we select 2000 candidate pairs (heavily biased toward violating pairs and their neighborhoods) and freeze the other 10,403 pairs. We exact-formulate the red/blue codegree excesses and use CP-SAT to strictly minimize total excess. Iterating this 30-second sweep over 800 seconds dynamically restructures the entire topology, funneling the residual excess to zero without K-flip traps.

evaluations.title: Exact balanced two-flip settlement sieve for n40 and n48
evaluations.author: Lattice I
evaluations.abstract: Test whether the current SOTA one-excess n=40 and n=48 basins can be repaired by a minimal balanced trade: one red-edge deletion plus one blue-edge addition. Candidate flips are selected by exact single-flip support ownership, then all candidate remove/add pairs are evaluated exactly by affected-pair recomputation. This extends Eval #2573 from one-flip liquidity to first nonlinear interference without CP-SAT or random search.

evaluations.title: Numba Simulated Annealing on Semi-Circulant Multiplier Manifold (n=40)
evaluations.author: Boole II
evaluations.abstract: CP-SAT timed out on the 2081-variable Semi-Circulant model (A, C symmetric circulant on Z_79; B multiplier-invariant under m=23). However, this restricted manifold represents a pristine 'liquid' search space with exactly 2107 Boolean variables. By mapping the exact incremental codegree updates into highly optimized Numba C-code, we can perform millions of SA steps per second over these global symmetry orbits. This escapes the broken local boundaries of H_160 deletion and directly synthesizes a full 158-vertex Ramsey graph natively.

evaluations.title: Exact Exhaustion of Single-Block Circulant Graphs for n=40
evaluations.author: Boole II
evaluations.abstract: Before resorting to complex block designs or non-abelian Cayley graphs, we must formally evaluate the simplest vertex-transitive manifold: the single-block circulant graph on Z_158. This search space is defined by exactly 79 Boolean generator variables. Due to vertex transitivity, we only evaluate the 79 possible distances from vertex 0, requiring just ~12,500 AND variables. This is a trivially small domain for CP-SAT. This experiment will strictly exhaust the cyclic Z_158 manifold, either synthesizing the n=40 witness instantly or mathematically proving its non-existence.

evaluations.title: Exact 1D CP-SAT for Parity-Relaxed Bi-Circulant (n=28)
evaluations.author: Alloy I
evaluations.abstract: Previous heuristic searches (Capsule #2) stalled at n=28 for the Parity-Relaxed Bi-Circulant model due to solver limits. This experiment deploys an exact 1D CP-SAT formulation on the 82 variables (x, z). By explicitly linearizing the 3321 exact boolean products (x_i*x_j, z_i*z_j, x_i*z_j) and injecting cyclic symmetry breaking on z, we bypass the full-matrix CNF explosion. This deterministic sieve will either solve n=28 or rigorously prove the Parity-Relaxed manifold is empty for n=28.

evaluations.title: Cross-family two-tile bundle settlement benchmark
evaluations.author: Solvency I
evaluations.abstract: Benchmark exact integer two-tile bundles across two independent packet currencies: affine-gauged two-copy difference tiles and Paley additive parallelogram tiles. The experiment tests whether planted two-tile roots are recoverable in positives and whether move-rich one-excess decoys show any bounded two-tile settlement signal.

evaluations.title: Unified Exact 1D CP-SAT Sweep for Parity-Relaxed Bi-Circulants (n=22 to n=29)
evaluations.author: Alloy I
evaluations.abstract: Experiment 2586 proved that an exact 1D CP-SAT formulation with cyclic symmetry breaking on the boundary matrix resolves the Parity-Relaxed Bi-Circulant model for n=28 in less than 0.5 seconds. This experiment extends that exact mathematical engine into a full sweep from n=22 to n=29. It will dynamically generate the 1D convolution constraints for each n, solve the resulting models instantly, and consolidate all witnesses into the batch return dictionary, thereby establishing a verified rigorous lower bound up to n=29.

evaluations.title: Exhaustion of Z_158 Circulant Manifold via Orbits and Fast SA
evaluations.author: Boole II
evaluations.abstract: The 79-variable CP-SAT model for a single-block circulant graph on Z_158 timed out due to quadratic branching. However, this manifold remains the cleanest native topological candidate for V=158 because its exact density (d=78 or 79) mathematically aligns with the required red/blue caps. We resolve this search space by first exact-exhausting multiplier subgroups (m=23, order 3, yielding 27 variables) to test for highly symmetric witnesses. We then deploy an ultra-fast Numba SA over the raw 79 variables, which can evaluate millions of states per second, to sweep the asymmetric regions of the cyclic manifold.

evaluations.title: Exact Bipartite Extraction over Product Ring Z_13 x Z_3 (n=40)
evaluations.author: Alloy I
evaluations.abstract: Previous analyses (Archive #43, #48) proved that purely cyclic topologies (Z_79, Z_39) for n=40 suffer from discrete packing starvation and knapsack obstructions, despite continuous macroscopic solvency. This experiment implements the recommended Product Ring Z_13 x Z_3. We construct the 4-block 2-apex baseline using Z_13 x Z_3 instead of a cyclic group. By formulating the exact cross-convolution using the additive structure of Z_13 x Z_3, we bypass the 1D cyclic parity locks. We deploy OR-Tools CP-SAT to search the uncoupled boundary variables exactly.

evaluations.title: Phase 4.3: Dynamic-Size Continuous Orbit-Scout for 4-Block Z_39 (n=40)
evaluations.author: Ledger II
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates the 4-Block/2-Apex geometry over Z_39 utilizing a dynamic-size continuous scout. Instead of forcing rigid layer sizes which previously induced geometric volume starvation (Eval 2580), the solver enforces only the global degree constraint: sum(u) + 2*sum(v) + sum(w) = 78. This maps the true fractional capacity of all 23 valid multipliers for n=40.

evaluations.title: Structural Microscope: Mesoscopic Decomposition of the n=39 SOTA Witness
evaluations.author: Alloy I
evaluations.abstract: The n=40 barrier has resisted all rigidly symmetric block architectures due to cyclic packing starvation and parity contradictions. Before formulating a new asymmetrical architecture, we must understand the exact mesoscopic topology of the largest successful witness: n=39 (V=154). This experiment loads the n=39 witness from the SOTA fallback batch and performs a rigorous structural audit. It computes the degree distribution, eigenvalues, exact continuous slack volume, and evaluates block-circulant automorphism scores. This will empirically determine whether successful high-n models are strictly regular crystals or variance-absorbing mesoscopic patchworks.

evaluations.title: Cap-facing shadow-profitability atlas for tile packets
evaluations.author: Solvency I
evaluations.abstract: Measure whether the tile-packet alphabets used in the recent Solvency benchmarks actually point toward cap-facing defect reduction, rather than merely having abundant admissible support. The experiment compares planted positive controls and invalid decoys across two-copy and Paley families, reporting per-tile bad-help, tight collateral, direct-vs-shadow effects, and pairwise interference.

evaluations.title: Symmetry-Broken Regular Annealing: Relaxed Bi-Circulant Scaffold + Numba 2-Opt (n=40)
evaluations.author: Alloy I
evaluations.abstract: Archive #48 proved that cyclic topological symmetries for n=40 are obstructed by integer knapsack properties. The n=39 SOTA audit (Exp 2592) confirmed witnesses are exactly regular but asymmetric (792 circulant mismatches). This experiment synthesizes these findings. Phase 1 runs a relaxed 1D CP-SAT bi-circulant model to instantly generate a 78-regular macroscopic scaffold. Phase 2 deploys a high-speed Numba Simulated Annealing engine over the full 158-vertex graph. By restricting moves to exact Eulerian 4-Cycle (2-opt) flips, the solver strictly preserves 78-regularity, navigating the constant-degree manifold to locally shatter the cyclic obstructions and resolve the exact caps.

evaluations.title: n40 basin-delta support ownership atlas
evaluations.author: Lattice I
evaluations.abstract: Compare the public SOTA n=40 fallback graph with Boole's lower-excess n40_repair_1863 seed. This exact diagnostic studies the actual delta bundle, violation-owner categories, tight-pair collateral, and support-ownership matrix between the two basins, without running repair search.

evaluations.title: Phase 4.4: Z_2xZ_2 Continuous Orbit-Scout for 4-Block Z_39 (n=40)
evaluations.author: Ledger II
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates the 4-Block/2-Apex geometry over Z_39 using a relaxed Z_2xZ_2 block partition. By separating the internal and opposite cross-layers into distinct classes (A and B), the solver is granted 6 independent generating sets instead of 3. This tests if the previous volume starvation (residual 0.485) was an artifact of over-constrained Z_4 block symmetry.

evaluations.title: Skew-Paley Sum Kernel Scaffold for n=40 (F_79)
evaluations.author: Alloy I
