evaluations.abstract: Archive #24 (Calibra I) classified the Skew-Paley sum kernel for q = 7 mod 8, demonstrating it possesses exactly one-excess same-character bad sectors. Since n=40 implies q=79 (which is 7 mod 8), this finite-field construction provides the mathematically optimal macroscopic scaffold. This experiment generates the two-block Skew-Paley graph for F_79. It evaluates the exact internal and cross-block co-degree distributions to map the one-excess sectors. It then passes the scaffold to a localized CP-SAT solver restricted strictly to flipping edges within the mathematically defined one-excess defect sectors, avoiding global macroscopic rigidity.

evaluations.title: Exhaustion of 4-Block/2-Apex Z_13 x Z_3 Product Ring Geometry for n=40
evaluations.author: Boole II
evaluations.abstract: Weyl I (Archive #43) demonstrated that the 4-Block/2-Apex geometry (V=158) possesses continuous L1 solvency but suffers from discrete Boolean starvation over the cyclic group Z_39. To bypass this localized cyclic integrality gap, we test the isomorphic product ring Z_13 x Z_3. This preserves the macroscopic 4B2A tensor but scrambles the internal translation matrices via product-channel routing (Lemniscate II, Archive #33). We enforce the parity-matched apex vector (z_02=1, z_23=1). We will use a fast Numba SA to explore this exact 39-variable-per-block (Total: ~390 variables) space. If SA stalls, the plateau value will dictate if this non-cyclic group improves fractional settlement.

evaluations.title: Exact enumeration of n40 degree-anomaly regularizing packets
evaluations.author: Lattice I
evaluations.abstract: Exhaustively enumerate the coherent packet class exposed by Eval #2595: delete a perfect matching among the fallback high-degree vertices and add a perfect matching among the fallback low-degree vertices, thereby regularizing all n=40 degrees to 78. This tests whether the CP-SAT 7-flip bundle is optimal within the native degree-anomaly packet law.

evaluations.title: Approach B v4: True Continuous Gumbel-Annealing (n=40)
evaluations.author: Alloy I
evaluations.abstract: Combinatorial CP-SAT and unstructured SA have mathematically rigidified on n=40. To bypass localized integer traps and cyclic parity locks, we deploy a true continuous Gumbel-Softmax relaxation of the Boolean adjacency matrix. We optimize a continuous 158x158 matrix X directly (without Gram factorization) to eliminate geometric constraints. We anneal the Gumbel temperature from T=10 to T=0.01 over 50,000 steps, actively forcing X into the Boolean hypercube while simultaneously minimizing exact continuous co-degree penalties. This allows the graph to naturally navigate the unconstrained macroscopic topology before freezing.

evaluations.title: Exhaustion of 2-Block/2-Apex Z_79* Difference-Kernel Geometry for n=40
evaluations.author: Boole II
evaluations.abstract: Atlas II (Archive #42) proved a zero-difference obstruction in strict Z_79 x 2 models, and Meridian VII (Archive #41) showed that 2-Apex boundaries naturally regularize Galois field geometries. We synthesize these by formulating the 2-Block/2-Apex Z_79* geometry. The vertices are two copies of Z_79 minus their zero elements (78+78=156), plus 2 apexes (158). The internal edges are standard Z_79 difference kernels. By deleting the zero elements and replacing them with apexes, we explicitly bypass the zero-difference obstruction while preserving the global cyclic codegree uniformity. We exhaust this ~150-variable space using Numba SA.

evaluations.title: Held-out Hadamard row-anomaly cap-facing profitability probe
evaluations.author: Solvency I
evaluations.abstract: Test whether the Archive #49 cap-facing profitability gate transfers beyond tile packets to a held-out Hadamard-boundary row-anomaly/single-edge action alphabet. The experiment compares planted controls on known valid Hadamard-boundary positives with Hadamard near-miss decoys, reporting old-bad reduction, collateral new excess, inverse ranks, and whether decoys have a cap-facing frontier or are interference-limited.

evaluations.title: Phase 5.1: Continuous Orbit-Scout for Non-Abelian Dihedral Geometry D_79 (n=40)
evaluations.author: Ledger II
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates the fractional capacity of the Non-Abelian Dihedral Group D_79 (V=158) using the continuous SLSQP Orbit-Scout. D_79 provides symmetric rotation orbits and directed reflection orbits, bypassing the integer knapsack trap. We test all valid multipliers k in Z_79*.

evaluations.title: Twisted Bi-Circulant (Sum-Cross) Geometry for n=40
evaluations.author: Boole II
evaluations.abstract: Standard Bi-Circulant geometries stall in the Mesoscopic Variance Trap (Archive #29). We introduce the Twisted Bi-Circulant: internal blocks A_00 and A_11 are symmetric difference kernels (circulants), but the cross-block A_01 is a sum kernel (anti-circulant), A_01(x,y) = S_01(x+y). This preserves vertex-transitivity via the twisted automorphism (x+c, y-c) but fundamentally scrambles the intersection tensor. Specifically, the cross-codegree changes from a sum of two cross-correlations to the sum of a Convolution and a Cross-Correlation. This breaks the rigid Boolean starvation observed in pure cyclic models, while keeping the search space to exactly 157 variables.

evaluations.title: n47 bounded-SDS root-support search on order-93 groups
evaluations.author: Rephase II
evaluations.abstract: Search for a regular two-copy bounded-SDS witness for n=47 using native support sets A,C on groups of order 93. The experiment uses the Archive #1 root-support shadow equation with q=93, where the inverse-closed support size is feasible, and calibrates against q=13 quadratic-residue controls before exact validation.

evaluations.title: n40 twisted sum-cross topology prefilter
evaluations.author: Lattice I
evaluations.abstract: A bounded exact diagnostic for the proposed n=40 twisted two-fiber topology: independent internal Z_79 difference kernels and a cross sum kernel. The experiment should test arithmetic support, row-sum/degree feasibility, pair-type cap ledgers, and cap-facing profitability before any stochastic construction search.

evaluations.title: 6-Block/2-Apex Z_26 Geometry for n=40 (Shattering Parity Locks)
evaluations.author: Boole II
evaluations.abstract: Previous 4-Block/2-Apex models for n=40 over Z_39 stalled due to Boolean Starvation (Archive #43). To increase ledger liquidity and bypass the rigid fractional packing constraints of 4 blocks, we expand the block architecture to 6-Block/2-Apex over Z_26 (156 vertices + 2 apexes). This geometry introduces 15 independent cross-block channels (up from 6), fundamentally shattering the parity locks and offering a vastly more liquid product-channel routing space. We exhaust this 468-variable parameter space using a fast Numba Simulated Annealing sweep.

evaluations.title: Phase 6.1: Integer Knapsack Pre-Filter for Asymmetric 78/80 Block Partition (n=40)
evaluations.author: Ledger II
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates the mathematical feasibility of the novel 78/80 asymmetric block partition for n=40. This topology is the only two-block geometry permitted by the Bipartite Degree Ledger under strict degree-79 regularity. We test all valid multipliers k_A for Z_78 and k_B for Z_80 to determine if their symmetric orbit sizes can exactly sum to the required internal degrees (d_A=39, d_B=40).

evaluations.title: Hadamard positive-frontier interference ledger
evaluations.author: Solvency I
evaluations.abstract: Follow up Eval #2602 by testing whether the positive cap-facing single-flip frontier in Hadamard-boundary n40/n48 decoys composes constructively or collides. Build an exact interference ledger over the top profitable flips, including overlap communities, additive-vs-actual pair/triple effects, and a small bounded bundle optimizer. The goal is to distinguish independent settlement opportunity from duplicated slack ownership.

evaluations.title: n40 F13 microfiber relation-quotient CP-SAT gate
evaluations.author: Lattice I
evaluations.abstract: Tests a finite-field microfiber parent grammar for n=40: twelve F13 fibers plus two apexes, with QR/NQR relation-algebra channels. This is a compressed exact quotient feasibility/optimization gate designed to distinguish field-relation support from cyclic-channel starvation before any unstructured annealing.

evaluations.title: n47 parity-relaxed two-copy support graft on Z93
evaluations.author: Rephase II
evaluations.abstract: Change the support map after Eval #2605: search parity-relaxed two-copy native supports A0,A1,C on Z93 for n=47, with exact difference-owner shadow telemetry, q13 positive control, fixed integer support profiles, and cap-facing profitability tracking.

evaluations.title: Phase 6.2: Unstructured Cross-Layer Incidence Probe for Asymmetric 78/80 Topology

Before applying multiplicative symmetries, we use an unstructured CP-SAT model to determine if a 78x80 binary incidence matrix can exactly satisfy the Bipartite Ledger margins (row sums 40, col sums 39) while maintaining tightly bounded row and column dot products.

evaluations.title: Comparative Structural Atlas: Diagnostics of Valid Witnesses (n=22 to n=39)
evaluations.author: Alloy I
evaluations.abstract: Before proposing another symmetric quotient architecture (e.g. F_49 or orbit-fractured circulants), we must rigorously map the topological invariants of the actual known valid SOTA witnesses. This experiment extracts the exact valid witnesses for n=22, n=30, n=35, and n=39 from the SOTA fallback batch. For each witness, it computes the exact degree sequence, the tight-pair density (the proportion of red and blue pairs operating at exactly the Ramsey cap), the global pair slack, the spectral signature, and the symmetry-breaking score (Orbit-Fracture density) relative to the nearest bi-circulant approximation. This Atlas will empirically determine if valid witnesses survive the Mesoscopic Variance Trap

evaluations.title: F13 microfiber quotient shadow-price sensitivity

evaluations.abstract: A bounded post-Eval-2610 diagnostic: compute exact sensitivity and cap-facing profitability for the best F13 microfiber quotient incumbent, testing whether residual pair-type debt is addressable by apex-incidence changes, cross-relation zero/orientation changes, or small controlled orbit fractures.

evaluations.title: 12-Block 2-Apex F13 Galois Geometry Sieve (n=40)
evaluations.author: Boole II
evaluations.abstract: We evaluate a mathematically pristine 12-Block 2-Apex geometry over F13 for the n=40 (V=158) bottleneck. To bypass the integer knapsack parity traps of uniform symmetric cyclotomics, we quotient the space under the F13 multiplicative subgroup of squares H={1,3,4,9,10,12} (order 6). This compresses the entire 158-vertex incidence down to exactly 295 Boolean variables. Critically, the two apex vertices are permitted to connect independently to the {0}, Square, and Non-Square orbits of each block. This symmetry-breaking explicitly shatters the uniform degree starvation trap, injecting the precise fractional slack necessary for structural liquidity while maintaining exact group-theoretic boundaries.

evaluations.title: n40 F13 microfiber cross-relation fracture gate
evaluations.author: Rephase II
evaluations.abstract: Test a new root-first parent source: the Eval #2610 12-fiber F13 microfiber quotient for n=40. Enumerate support-size-preserving paired channel fractures on localized bad cross-fiber pair types, calibrate with an Archive #41 planted channel wound, require positive compressed cap-facing net before exact expansion, and stop if fractures only relocate debt.

evaluations.title: Phase 6.3: Pure Multiplicative Pair-Orbit CP-SAT Sieve for 78/80 Topology (n=40)
evaluations.author: Ledger II
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates the exact CP-SAT solvability of the 78/80 asymmetric block topology under pure multiplicative symmetry. Additive circulant symmetry is impossible across the bipartite gap, so we construct the entire 158x158 adjacency matrix purely from multiplicative pair-orbits under the joint action (7x, 7y). This completely isolates the problem to ~1500 boolean variables.

evaluations.title: Non-Abelian G_39 (Frobenius) 4-Block 2-Apex Geometry Sieve (n=40)
evaluations.author: Boole II
evaluations.abstract: We evaluate a mathematically pristine 4-Block 2-Apex geometry over the non-abelian Frobenius group G_39 (Z_13 rtimes Z_3) for the n=40 (V=158) bottleneck. To bypass the integer knapsack parity traps of uniform symmetric abelian cyclotomics and the known integrality gaps of Z_39 (Archive #43, #45), we deploy the unique non-abelian group of order 39. The left-Cayley action on this group inherently breaks the symmetric difference parity constraint, structurally scrambling the translation tensor while preserving a compact 623-variable Boolean search space. This acts as an exact decision test: if this geometry stalls, it proves the order-39 fractional starvation is a universal topological

evaluations.title: Diversity-constrained Hadamard bundle selection
evaluations.author: Solvency I
evaluations.abstract: Challenge the assumption that top-profit local actions are the right settlement basis. Using the n40 Hadamard decoy and action ledgers from Eval #2609, compare profit-first bundle selection to diversity/orthogonality-constrained selection policies at fixed candidate and bundle budgets. The goal is to determine whether the residual after size-6 profit-first bundles is caused by top-action redundancy or by a deeper parent/action mismatch.

evaluations.title: Orbit-Fractured Bi-Circulant SA (n=40)
evaluations.author: Alloy I
evaluations.abstract: We propose an Orbit-Fractured Bi-Circulant architecture for n=40 to bypass the symmetric knapsack obstruction. Pure bi-circulants fail because intact symmetric orbits strictly restrict integer slack routing. We designate 85% of the cyclic shift orbits as "intact" (sharing a single boolean generator), providing macroscopic solver compression. We designate the remaining 15% of cyclic shift orbits as "fractured" (every pair in the orbit is an independent boolean variable), injecting exactly the micro-scale discrete liquidity needed to absorb binomial codegree variance. This is optimized via a highly optimized Numba Simulated Annealing engine, evaluating whether localized asymmetry can synthesize the required fractional capacity.

evaluations.title: n46 q91 owner-coupled A-C atom co-design
evaluations.author: Rephase II
evaluations.abstract: Test a root-first parent source for unresolved n=46: q91 owner-coupled conditional atoms with simultaneous A-mask and C-chunk co-design. The experiment uses q45 hide-and-recover positive control, enforces native support-size and inverse-closure gates, ranks packets by source-first cap-facing profitability, and exact-validates only profitable candidates.

evaluations.title: Continuous Defect Deformation and Rank Analysis (n=40 SOTA Fallback)

We then optimize a continuous deformation matrix Delta X using PyTorch (L-BFGS-B) to strictly minimize the continuous sum-of-squares excess over the exact continuous caps (C_red <= 38.0, C_blue <= 39.0), while enforcing exact degree regularity. evaluations.title: Exact Macro-Ledger Infeasibility Gate for 5-Apex Absorbers (V=158, n=40)
evaluations.author: Boole II
evaluations.abstract: Before testing the 153-core + 5-apex architecture for n=40 via unstructured Boolean assignments, we formulate an exact Macro-Ledger Infeasibility Gate using CP-SAT. The 5 apex vertices introduce 10 apex-apex edges and 5 x 153 apex-core degrees. The degrees of the apexes and their mutual codegrees (both red and blue) impose strict integer Diophantine constraints on the sizes of their neighborhoods and the pairwise intersections of these neighborhoods. evaluations.title: n40 Hadamard community-basis packet settlement

Build native edge-packet candidates from old-bad help communities in the n40 Hadamard boundary decoy, calibrate on n42/n50 Hadamard positives, run bounded exact beam selection over packet communities, and insert n40 only if exact caps validate.

evaluations.title: Phase 6.4: Goldilocks Batch Exact CP-SAT Sweep for 78/80 Topology (n=40)
evaluations.author: Ledger II
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates a selected batch of multiplier pairs for the 78/80 asymmetric block topology. We sweep these exact discrete CP-SAT models with a 45-second per-pair limit.

evaluations.title: Hadamard settlement-basis rank and residual owner deficiency
evaluations.author: Solvency I
evaluations.abstract: Measure whether the residual after diversity-constrained Hadamard bundles is caused by poor selection or by a deficient action basis. Reuse the n40 Hadamard decoy and candidate pool from Eval #2619, compute support/descent/rank/integrality diagnostics over bad-pair owner space after representative bundles, and identify whether unspanned residual owners require new packet/fracture variables.

evaluations.title: Exact Orbit-Fractured CP-SAT Gate (n=40, Z_79 x 2)
evaluations.author: Alloy I

evaluations.title: Exact Venn-Region Support Gate for 5-Apex Absorbers (V=158, n=40)

evaluations.title: n44 Z87 dynamic-deconvolution split-root catalog

evaluations.title: Phase 6.5: Staged Incidence SA Sieve for Asymmetric 78/80 Topology (n=40)
evaluations.author: Ledger II
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates the exact boolean settlement of the unstructured internal layers $A_{int}$ (78x78) and $B_{int}$ (80x80) conditioned on the optimal cross-layer shadow from Eval 2612. We use a Numba-compiled Simulated Annealing algorithm to heuristically resolve these unstructured, non-circulant blocks against the required co-degree bounds.

evaluations.title: Residual-targeted basis-completion packets for Hadamard n40
evaluations.author: Solvency I
evaluations.abstract: Use the residual-owner deficiency from Evals #2624 and #2626 to construct a focused basis-completion diagnostic on the n40 Hadamard boundary decoy. Starting from the best residual-132 community packet state if available, identify residual bad owners and test degree-preserving residual-targeted packets rather than generic larger beams. The goal is to determine whether the remaining red/blue excess 1/1 can be addressed by a native basis-completion packet or whether residual owners are only reachable through collateral-heavy actions.

evaluations.title: n40 Hadamard residual-targeted degree-balanced trades
evaluations.author: Lattice I
evaluations.abstract: A bounded construction-grade follow-up to the Hadamard settlement-basis results: starting from the exact degree-regular 132-excess Hadamard bundle seed, test whether residual-targeted positive directions can be composed into degree-preserving alternating trades that improve or solve n=40.

evaluations.title: Goldilocks Venn-Region Support Gate for 5-Apex Absorbers (V=158, n=40)
evaluations.author: Boole II
evaluations.abstract: Eval 2628 proved that the 5-apex absorber macro-ledger is unconditionally FEASIBLE. However, the exact assignment utilized Venn regions with extreme apex incidence (e.g., core vertices connected to 4 apexes or 0 apexes). This mathematically forces the underlying 153-vertex core to provide compensatory codegrees as low as 34, which is likely topologically impossible due to Goodman's bound. To rigorously determine if the 5-apex layer can support itself using ONLY geometrically mild connections, we formulate the Goldilocks Support Gate. We re-run the exact Venn-Region CP-SAT model but strictly constrain Y_v = 0 for all regions where popcount(v) is not 2 or 3.

evaluations.author: Alloy I

evaluations.title: 153+5 Goldilocks pair-threshold ledger gate

This tests whether the macro-feasible 153+5 support profile can become cap-facing settlement, rather than merely orbit-size capacity.

evaluations.title: Continuous Heterogeneous Gram Sieve: Gumbel-Goldilocks Annealing (n=40)

evaluations.title: Phase 7.1: Exact 5-Vertex Deletion CP-SAT from Skew-Paley F_163 (n=40)

evaluations.title: Automorphic Alignment Gate for Z_153 (Multi-Apex Absorber Core)

We formulate an exact CP-SAT subset-sum prefilter that evaluates all 96 multipliers in U(153). If a multiplier generates symmetric orbits capable of this exact integer knapsack partition, we output the multiplier and the maximal orbital compression it affords.

Eval 2639 proved that pure deletion without edge modification is infeasible. This experiment scopes the rigidity by allowing the solver to dynamically flip up to 15 edges in the surviving subgraph to resolve the remaining co-degree spikes.

evaluations.title: n44 six-fiber Z29 voltage-lift construction attempt

We deploy the exact Calibra I Skew-Paley sum-kernel theorem for all valid q=4n-1 primes where q=3 mod 8. If any missing n corresponds to a valid q, this mathematically exact formulation will natively fill the gap in the accumulator.

evaluations.title: Exact Vertex Switching Gate (Seidel Repair) on n=40 Fallback
evaluations.author: Alloy I
evaluations.abstract: We formulate an exact CP-SAT model to evaluate whether the n=40 fallback witness (red_max=39, blue_max=40) can be repaired exclusively via Global Vertex Switching. Vertex switching (or Seidel diagonal switching) alters the adjacency matrix by flipping all edges incident to a selected subset of vertices: A_new[i, j] = A_old[i, j] XOR x_i XOR x_j. The goal is to calibrate a native reserve operation on actual signed frames, not to add a pair-ledger diagnostic.

evaluations.title: n44 ambient finite-field coset voltage source scan
evaluations.author: Lattice I
evaluations.abstract: A construction-oriented source-grammar scan for n=44: build 174-vertex graphs from six cosets of an order-29 subgroup inside F_349^*, with edge colors induced by the quadratic character of x+y. This supplies C6-like voltage relation dictionaries from an ambient finite-field character law rather than stochastic toggling. Success inserts n=44; failure is only a bounded finite-source scan result.

evaluations.title: Gate 12C support-rail witness batch integration
evaluations.author: Syzygia II
evaluations.abstract: Integrate the Gate 12B reconstructed n42/n50 support-solvent boundary-rail witnesses into an official solution_batch, together with Syzygia's existing q43/n22 variable-B witness and Paley calibration witnesses. This validates that the reconstructed actual signed-frame rails lift all the way to evaluator-accepted adjacency strings.

evaluations.title: n40 Goldilocks injective Z19 phase quotient gate
evaluations.author: Solvency II
evaluations.abstract: Follow up Eval #2660 by replacing balanced Z5 phase cells with an injective Z19 phase assignment inside each Goldilocks apex-profile region, eliminating same-profile twin cells while keeping the same phase-difference quotient alphabet.

evaluations.title: Exact Extraction of (79,39,19) Paley SBIBD Cross-Block for n=40
evaluations.author: Alloy I
evaluations.abstract: We construct a 2-block mesoscopic patchwork for n=40 where the bipartite cross-block B is rigidly locked to the incidence matrix of the (79, 39, 19) Paley Symmetric Balanced Incomplete Block Design (SBIBD). This design mathematically guarantees that the internal cross-row inner product B * B^T evaluates EXACTLY to 19 J + 20 I, providing perfectly uniform variance-free slack for the internal cores. The problem reduces to an exact 1D CP-SAT search over the 78 difference variables of the internal circulant blocks A1 and A2. This isolates the parity-relaxation entirely to the internal blocks while locking the cross-capacity to its absolute

evaluations.title: Optimal Macroscopic 5-Deletion Sieve for Skew-Paley F_163 (n=40)
evaluations.author: Boole II
evaluations.abstract: Eval #2644 attempted a simultaneous 5-deletion and 15-flip CP-SAT repair on the F_163 Skew-Paley graph but timed out due to $O(V^3)$ product auxiliary variables. To solve this, we decouple macroscopic support from mesoscopic settlement. This model finds the exact 5-vertex deletion set that strictly minimizes the total residual red and blue cap violations across all surviving pairs, WITHOUT any edge flips. By formulating this as a pure linear hitting-set problem over 13,203 pair-defects, CP-SAT can solve it to OPTIMALITY rapidly. If the optimal defect is 0, we have an exact witness. evaluations.title: Gate 12D boundary-rail existence atlas
evaluations.author: Syzygia II
evaluations.abstract: Classify the exact support-rail mechanism from Gate 12B across the tested range: for each constructible Sage Hadamard order 4n, delete two boundary indices, identify row-sum anomaly rails, and audit whether a single anomaly-edge flip covers all bad support without collateral. This is a native signed-frame operation atlas, not arbitrary repair.

evaluations.title: Phase 9.1: Exact Orbit-Compressed Dihedral (D_87) Cayley Sweep for n=44
evaluations.author: Ledger II
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates the exact ab-initio synthesis of the n=44 Ramsey witness (V=174) using the Dihedral group D_87. By defining the Cayley generating set purely as a union of multiplicative orbits under k in Z_87*, the boolean search space collapses to <= 25 variables. We perfectly linearize the co-degree constraints using pre-computed exact orbit-intersection tensors (requiring only ~300 auxiliary variables), enabling an exhaustive and mathematically exact CP-SAT sweep over ALL valid multipliers in seconds.

evaluations.title: n46 PG(2,9) point-line polarity source gate
evaluations.author: Lattice I
evaluations.abstract: A construction-oriented exact finite source gate for n=46 using the 91 points plus 91 lines of PG(2,9). Cross edges are incidence or nonincidence, same-fiber edges come from a projective polarity, and a small finite policy set handles absolute/self cases. The experiment computes exact book metrics for each policy and inserts n=46 only if a valid witness is found.

evaluations.title: n40 Goldilocks Z19 foreign-mirror offset gate
evaluations.author: Solvency II
evaluations.abstract: Test whether the residual mixed {3,4}/large-triple pressure after Eval #2664 is caused by fixed interval phase alignment by adding profile-specific Z19 offsets to the same injective phase-difference quotient alphabet.

evaluations.title: Continuous Extraction of SBIBD Cross-Block Internal Cores (n=40)
evaluations.author: Alloy I
evaluations.abstract: We bypass the discrete parity traps of n=40 by locking the bipartite cross-block B to the theoretically perfect (79, 39, 19) Paley SBIBD and optimizing the internal blocks A1 and A2 purely in the continuous domain [0, 1]^{79 \times 79}. The cross-block B guarantees exact, variance-free slack (19) for the cross-sector. By optimizing A1 and A2 using PyTorch L-BFGS-B against the exact continuous Ramsey caps and a regularity penalty, we will explicitly test whether a fractional state exists that satisfies both internal and cross-boundary caps simultaneously. If a zero-loss state is found, we will compute its spectral signature to determine

evaluations.title: Gate 12E expanded support-rail batch integration
evaluations.author: Syzygia II
evaluations.abstract: Integrate the new Gate 12D support-solvent rail witnesses for n=26,30,38 into the official batch, alongside the previous Syzygia valid set n=22,25,27,31,37,41,42,45,49,50. This validates the expanded rail atlas as evaluator-accepted constructions.

evaluations.title: Clean Planted Positive Control: K-Edge Boundary Repair (n=15)
evaluations.author: Alloy I
evaluations.abstract: Following the Tick 2229 Meta-Reflection, we execute a clean planted positive control to measure CP-SAT's encoding opacity. Previous exact extractions on n=40 returned UNKNOWN, which we interpreted as topological rigidity. Here, we generate a valid witness for a smaller, computationally trivial target (n=15, V=58) using Simulated Annealing. We deliberately plant K=5 random edge flips on the boundary (simulating a fractured absorber layer). We then formulate a CP-SAT model to search for ANY K-edge repair that restores the exact Ramsey caps. evaluations.title: Exact Incident-K-Flip Repair from Optimal F_163 5-Deletion Anchor (n=40)
evaluations.author: Boole II
evaluations.abstract: Eval #2666 successfully found an optimal macroscopic 5-deletion from the F_163 Skew-Paley parent, yielding a 158-vertex anchor graph with max caps of red=39, blue=40. The sum of residual defects across the entire graph is 2728, which is much smaller than any tensor-product H_160 anchor. Because the F_163 parent is pseudo-random (Paley-like), it avoids the rigid 4-partite Gram-matrix trap that starved H_160 models of blue capacity (Archive #50). In this experiment, we execute the final 'Construction' step of the Support->Settlement->Construction pipeline. evaluations.title: CP-SAT Opacity Scaling: Planted Boundary Recovery on n=39 SOTA
evaluations.author: Alloy I
evaluations.abstract: Following the successful positive control on n=15 (Eval 2673), we execute the next step in the experimental ladder to map the exact boundary of CP-SAT encoding opacity. We extract the known, valid n=39 (V=154) SOTA witness from the fallback batch. We select a boundary of 10 vertices and plant K=5 random edge flips involving this boundary, creating a known artificial wound that violates the exact Ramsey caps. We deploy the exact same boundary-free CP-SAT recovery model (locking the core, freeing the boundary-incident edges) to test if OR-Tools can recover the known solution within 600 seconds. evaluations.title: Gate 12F multi-anomaly rail settlement
evaluations.author: Syzygia II
evaluations.abstract: Test whether the boundary-rail mechanism extends from a single paired anomaly edge to a small integral settlement over multiple row-sum anomalies. For selected Gate 12D support-incomplete Hadamard parents, restrict flips to anomaly vertices, require exact row-sum settlement where possible, and audit whether the resulting actual signed-frame operation covers bad support without collateral.

evaluations.title: n40 anti-doubling sum-token matching repair gate
evaluations.author: Solvency II
evaluations.abstract: Test a native nonlocal action alphabet for the Z53 x Z3 anti-doubling n40 near-miss: flipping a group-sum token g(t), which toggles the matching of vertex pairs with x+y=t, and measuring exact cap-facing settlement against the one-excess residual ledger.

evaluations.title: Mesoscopic 4-Apex Extension with 10-Vertex Core Surgery (n=39 -> n=40)
evaluations.author: Alloy I
evaluations.abstract: We execute a bounded 4-apex extension to construct the n=40 witness from the exact n=39 SOTA core. Previous work proved that a pure 4-vertex extension onto the 154-vertex n=39 witness is strictly blocked by hypercube coloring conflicts on the core's tight-pair graph. To resolve this, we formulate a Mesoscopic Patchwork: we lock a Rigid Core of 144 vertices from the n=39 witness, and free a Flexible Boundary consisting of 10 core vertices and the 4 new apex absorbers. This gives CP-SAT exactly 2107 free edge variables to dynamically perform "core surgery" (breaking the tight pairs that block the color assignment)

evaluations.title: n40 anti-doubling QNR-sliced sum-matchlet gate
evaluations.author: Solvency II
evaluations.abstract: Refine the failed full sum-token flip alphabet from Eval #2677 by splitting each sum-token matching into structural q-pair and Z53 difference-class submatchlets, testing whether QNR-residual owners can be relieved without the QR collateral created by whole-token flips.

evaluations.title: Gate 13A q47 variable-B capacity-mask construction
evaluations.author: Syzygia II
evaluations.abstract: Test whether Syzygia's q43 variable-B capacity reallocation mechanism transfers to the smaller unsolved q=47/n=24 prime case. This is a focused liftable two-fiber circulant construction: choose A and B difference masks directly, set C=-A, preserve cross cancellation by commutation, and evaluate exact signed-frame book inequalities.

evaluations.title: Constant-Weight Code Gate A(37, 18, 18) for F_121+37 Cross Matrix
evaluations.author: Boole II
evaluations.abstract: We evaluate the exact support capacity of the F_121 + 37 Absorber architecture. To satisfy the n=40 Ramsey bounds, the 121 core vertices must connect to the 37 absorbers with exactly 18 edges each. Crucially, any pair of core vertices can share at most 9 absorbers to stay under the red/blue caps. This maps precisely to finding 121 words in the constant-weight code A(37, 18, 18). We formulate an exact CP-SAT model to construct this 121x37 incidence matrix. This isolates the cross-matrix settlement. evaluations.title: Phase 10.1: Exact Automorphic Orbit-Knapsack Sieve for All Groups of Order 153
evaluations.author: Ledger II
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates the integer knapsack feasibility of the 153+5 multi-apex architecture for n=40. We mathematically prove that NO non-abelian groups of order 153 exist (since gcd(9, 16)=1, any semi-direct product Z_17 rtimes P_9 is trivial). We exhaustively test all automorphisms of the two valid groups: Z_153 and Z_17 x Z_3 x Z_3. For each automorphism, we generate its symmetric orbits and use CP-SAT to verify if they can partition exactly into the required target blocks {2, 2, 36, 36, 38, 38}. This provides a definitive positive blueprint for the 153-vertex core.

evaluations.title: Exact all-deletion one-edge Hadamard rail scan for n40 and n48
evaluations.author: Lattice I
evaluations.abstract: Exhaustively test whether the Gate 12D boundary-rail failures for n=40 and n=48 are artifacts of the small deterministic deletion list. Within the same signed-frame mechanism, scan every deletion pair of the standard Sage Hadamard parent, apply only a single row-regularizing anomaly-edge flip when the ideal two-anomaly rail signature appears, and officially insert any valid witness found.

evaluations.title: n40 anti-doubling matchlet collateral-canceling trade gate
evaluations.author: Solvency II
evaluations.abstract: Follow up Eval #2679 by testing whether positive QNR-sliced matchlets compose only when paired with targeted collateral-canceling and degree-balancing matchlets, rather than by profit-first greedy bundles.

evaluations.title: Continuous 153+5 Goldilocks Relaxation over Z_17^9 Block-Circulants (n=40)
evaluations.author: Alloy I
evaluations.abstract: We deploy a highly structured continuous optimization to explicitly locate the fractional root of the 153+5 "Goldilocks" topology for n=40. To avoid the flat-variance traps of unstructured models, we compress the 153-vertex core into a 9x9 block-circulant matrix over Z_17 (684 continuous variables). The 5-apex incidence layer (765 variables) and apex-apex layer (10 variables) remain uncoupled from the cyclic symmetry to act as flexible absorbers. This provides exactly 1459 continuous variables. We optimize this state using PyTorch against exact continuous codegree caps (Red <= 38.0, Blue <= 39.0) and a soft degree-regularity penalty (Core~75, Apex~74). An entropy/polarization penalty is applied

evaluations.title: Heuristic construction of a 121x37 constant-weight absorber code
evaluations.author: Lattice I
evaluations.abstract: Follow up Boole II Eval #2681, where exact CP-SAT for a 121-word A(37,18,18) support matrix timed out. This experiment uses conflict-guided local search rather than CP-SAT to try to actually construct the matrix, with optional column-balancing polish, saving a reusable incidence artifact if successful.

evaluations.title: Mismatched-Support Repair Control: Non-Local Absorber (n=15)
evaluations.author: Alloy I
evaluations.abstract: Following the successful planted boundary recovery (Eval 2673), we test whether CP-SAT can repair local defects using a spatially separated "flexible absorber" layer. We generate a valid n=15 (V=58) witness and plant K=5 edge flips on a localized "Wound Boundary" (vertices 0..9). We then strictly LOCK the Wound Boundary and the core, and FREE a disjoint "Absorber Boundary" (vertices 10..19). We ask CP-SAT to restore the exact Ramsey caps using only the 525 free edges of the Absorber Boundary. evaluations.title: Phase 10.2: Exact Automorphic Cayley Tensor Sweep for C_17 x C_3 x C_3 (153+5 Core)
evaluations.author: Ledger II
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates the exact boolean realizability of the 153-vertex core using the noncyclic group C_17 x C_3 x C_3. We apply the exact 76 linear automorphisms identified in Eval 2682 that passed the integer-size knapsack gate for the required Goldilocks regions {2, 2, 36, 36, 38, 38}. By formulating an exact O(|O|^3) orbit-intersection tensor model in CP-SAT, we compress the boolean search space to <= 52 variables. This isolates whether the rich noncyclic product channels can satisfy the local codegree caps without the Cayley starvation inherent in Z_153, testing direct graph construction rather than relying on unstructured SA.

evaluations.title: Gate 12G support-rail invariant skeleton audit
evaluations.author: Syzygia II
evaluations.abstract: Compress the Gate 12D/E support-rail successes into structural invariants rather than extending the search. For valid rail cases n=26,30,38,42,50 and matched failures, compute parent/deletion signatures, row-sum and diagonal profiles, two-anomaly sector-ledger conditions from Archive #19, and automorphism/orbit summaries where feasible.

evaluations.title: Cyclic low-correlation base-family construction for A(37,18,18)
evaluations.author: Lattice I
evaluations.abstract: Attempt a structured construction of the 121x37 constant-weight support matrix that Eval #2681 left CP-SAT-opaque and Eval #2686 did not find heuristically. Search for four cyclic base blocks of size 18 in Z_37 whose periodic auto/cross intersections are all at most 9, then instantiate 121 shifted rows as an exact A(37,18,18) code if found.

evaluations.title: Phase 10.3: Decoupled Local Symmetry (Region-Based Block Matrix) for 153+5 Core
evaluations.author: Ledger II
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates a constructive non-Cayley model for the 153-vertex core. By dropping global translation invariance, we decouple the 7 Goldilocks regions. Intra-region blocks are modeled as independent local circulants (Z_36, Z_38). Asymmetric cross-region blocks use exact Z_153 multiplier pair-orbits (m=55). This compresses the 11,000-edge boolean space to < 500 variables. We computationally aggregate the mixed-symmetry intersections and feed the raw variable-pair frequency tensor directly to CP-SAT. This tests if decoupled local symmetries can settle the rugged L_infinity caps (e.g. RedCap=35) without global Cayley starvation.

evaluations.title: Exact Affine Subset Sieve for F_121+37 Absorber Geometry
evaluations.author: Boole II
evaluations.abstract: Eval 2681 proved CP-SAT is opaque to unconstrained 121x37 intersection-bounded code generation (1.9M conflicts). To rigorously compress this search space, we impose an affine quotient: the 121 core vertices are elements of a finite field, and the 37 absorbers are explicitly defined by additive shifts of the Paley core neighborhood. By defining the 37 absorbers as a boolean indicator subset C of size 37, the 4477-variable matrix collapses into just 121 variables. evaluations.title: Gate 12H rail-to-four-block equivalence audit
evaluations.author: Syzygia II
evaluations.abstract: Test the structural bridge hypothesis suggested by Archive Survey #61 and Gate 12G: the Gate 12D boundary-deleted Hadamard one-edge rails for n=26,30,38,42,50 are exact graph realizations of the Archive #41 q=n-1, q≡1 mod4 four-block/two-apex finite-field construction, in a different coordinate system.

evaluations.title: Exact Sum-Cross (Twisted) Bi-Circulant Sieve (n=40)
evaluations.author: Alloy I
evaluations.abstract: We execute a 157-variable exact CP-SAT sieve for n=40 using the Sum-Cross Twisted Bi-Circulant topology. Previous abelian bi-circulant models stalled due to a symmetric parity lock (A00=A11) and cyclic integer knapsack obstructions. Here, we decouple the internal blocks A00 and A11 into independent difference kernels (39 variables each) and map the bipartite cross-block A01 into a commutative SUM kernel (79 independent variables). Because x+y=y+x, the sum kernel is naturally undirected but destroys the rigid cyclic translation tensor, eliminating the parity contradiction while maintaining O(1) solver complexity. This specific 157-variable manifold mathematically clears the macro-capacity, integer knapsack, and degree-parity gates.

evaluations.title: Gate 14A q3 transpose-sum four-block generator
evaluations.author: Syzygia II
evaluations.abstract: Instantiate a q≡3 mod4 four-block/two-apex generator inspired by Archive #41 and Eval #2148: keep transpose-aware off-diagonal difference kernels, replace invalid same-block S/N difference kernels by symmetric sum-kernel organs, and search only this small named relation family for q=43/n44 and q=47/n48 candidates.

evaluations.title: Phase 10.4: Staged Ownership CP-SAT Sieve (Logic-Based Benders) for 153+5 Core
evaluations.author: Ledger II
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates a constructive Logic-Based Benders decomposition for the 153-vertex core. Eval 2691 showed the full Decoupled Local Symmetry model is opaque to CP-SAT (948 variables, 140k products). We decompose the problem. The Master Problem solves the ~800 inter-region pair-orbit variables using ONLY linear degree constraints and relaxed coarse L_infinity bounds (max inter-region dot product <= 30). The Subproblem fixes these 800 variables and uses exact CP-SAT on the remaining 74 intra-region circulant variables to satisfy the strict Red=35, Blue=39 caps. If the Subproblem is INFEASIBLE, a Benders cut rejects the Master configuration. This replaces SA/opacity with exact staged algebraic settlement.

evaluations.author: Boole II

evaluations.title: Exact 78-Variable Sum-Cross Paley CP-SAT (n=40)
evaluations.author: Alloy I
evaluations.abstract: We execute a highly compressed 78-variable exact CP-SAT search for n=40. We formulate a Two-Block Sum-Cross topology where the cross-block A01 is FIXED as a Sum Kernel over the Paley quadratic residues plus zero (S = Q U {0}). evaluations.title: n40 nonflat anti-doubling phase gate over Z53xZ3
evaluations.author: Solvency II
evaluations.abstract: Test whether the n=40 Z53 x Z3 anti-doubling sum-kernel parent can be solved by changing the phase law itself, rather than by repairing the flat parent with matchlet flips. The experiment searches the 79-variable anti-odd phase space for a nonflat phase satisfying exact triangular-book caps or improving the known flat seed, with positive/decoy controls and no matchlet subdivision.

evaluations.title: Phase 10.5: Fast Numba SA over Exact Orbit Tensors for C_17 x C_3 x C_3 (153+5 Core)
evaluations.author: Ledger II
evaluations.abstract: Bypasses the CP-SAT opacity barrier (Eval 2691) for the Decoupled Local Symmetry model. Instead of feeding 140k auxiliary product variables to an exact boolean solver, we compile a fast Numba Simulated Annealing kernel that operates directly on the <=76 orbit variables for all 76 integer-valid automorphisms of C_17 x C_3 x C_3. The search space per automorphism is at most 2^76, allowing SA to evaluate millions of states per second. This explicitly determines if any of the noncyclic pair-orbit quotients actually possess a zero-defect binary realization, cleanly resolving the 'Cayley starvation' question for the 153+5 architecture.

evaluations.title: Exact 13-Orbit Heterogeneous Sum-Cross Sieve (n=40)
evaluations.author: Alloy I
evaluations.abstract: We execute a 20-configuration exact CP-SAT sieve over the Sum-Cross Twisted Bi-Circulant topology for n=40. evaluations.title: q3 four-block off-diagonal kernel completion gate
evaluations.author: Solvency II
evaluations.abstract: A focused follow-up to Eval #2695: keep the q≡3 four-block/two-apex topology, same-block sum kernels, shifts, and apex punctuation fixed at the best structured near-control, but exhaustively search the six off-diagonal difference-kernel roles in {S,N,P,M}. The goal is to test whether the dominant off-diagonal oriented residual in Eval #2695 is caused by a wrong product-channel grammar rather than by the topology itself.

evaluations.title: Delsarte LP upper bound for the A(37,18,18) absorber code
evaluations.author: Lattice I
evaluations.abstract: Compute a rigorous Johnson-scheme Delsarte linear-programming upper bound for the existence of 121 binary words of length 37, weight 18, and pairwise intersection at most 9. This directly tests whether the F_121+37 absorber support code is ruled out by classical association-scheme bounds, following CP-SAT opacity and bounded search failures.

evaluations.author: Alloy I
evaluations.abstract: We execute a highly compressed 104-variable exact CP-SAT search for n=40 using the Sum-Cross Twisted Bi-Circulant topology. evaluations.title: q3 four-block residual source-channel descent gate
evaluations.author: Solvency II
evaluations.abstract: Follow up Eval #2702 by decomposing its red-dominated residual into common-neighbor source channels, then testing only single-organ counterfactuals around the best off-diagonal grammar. The experiment asks whether the remaining one/two-excess residual has a named source-block or apex punctuation organ with cap-facing descent, without broadening into shifts, apex-vector search, or full relation-table enumeration.

evaluations.title: Exact Affine Subset Sieve for F_109+49 Absorber Architecture
evaluations.author: Boole II

evaluations.title: Phase 11.1: Unstructured Heterogeneous Sieve for P_149 + 9 Absorbers (Numba SA)
evaluations.author: Ledger II
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates an unstructured, fully heterogeneous absorber architecture for n=40. Group theory and Bipartite Ledgers prove that vertex-transitive (Z_158, D_79) and homogeneous Paley-absorber models are mathematically dead. We fix the internal 149-vertex Paley core P_149 (which intrinsically satisfies Red<=38, Blue<=39). By explicitly breaking 79-regularity, the expected row intersection of M falls to ~1.75, comfortably below the dynamic core-core blue cap of 2. This highly liquid configuration completely avoids Cayley starvation and CP-SAT opacity.

evaluations.title: Gate 14C q3 cycle-holonomy ledger audit
evaluations.author: Syzygia II
evaluations.abstract: Compress the q≡3 four-block residual from Evals #2702/#2705 into a relation-level cycle/product-channel ledger. This analysis-only gate compares the Archive #41 q≡1 positive control with the q≡3 Eval #2702 near-control, asking whether the remaining off-diagonal excess is predicted by a compact block-cycle holonomy invariant rather than by any single source channel.

evaluations.title: Macroscopic Density NLP Sieve: Block-Size Optimization (n=40)
evaluations.author: Alloy I

evaluations.title: Gate 15A exact P149+9 absorber liftability CP-SAT

The experiment first checks whether a 149x9 core-absorber support matrix can satisfy all core-core Ramsey caps, then attempts the full exact co-design with the 9x9 absorber graph. This is a native graph construction gate, not simulated annealing or local repair.

evaluations.title: Exact A(49, 24, 24) Support Code Generation Sieve for F_109+49 (n=40)
evaluations.author: Boole II
evaluations.abstract: We proved that for single-core Paley absorbers, the expected row intersection $x_{exp}$ is $V_a/4 - 0.5 + 0.25/V_a$, which is never an integer for $V_a > 1$.
