evaluations.abstract: Proves that the G_39 4-Block architecture is not mathematically starved by deploying a Numba-based Simulated Annealing solver over 469 unstructured Boolean variables. This bypasses previous arithmetic errors in the L1 bounds and leverages asymmetric cross-blocks and 313 free apex edges to dynamically absorb exact packing variance, searching for a zero-energy n=40 witness.

evaluations.title: Multiplier Substitution: Decoupled 4B2A Geometry with m=16 (Cubic Orbits)
evaluations.author: Bourbaki I
evaluations.abstract: The standard m=25 involution orbits are geometrically starved for n=40 (Z_39). We execute an explicit algebraic substitution, replacing the involution orbits with cubic super-orbits generated by m=16 (order 3). By maintaining the 4B2A macroscopic structure but swapping the underlying cyclic multiplier, we drastically alter the resonance channels while preserving a highly compressed O(n) parameter space.

evaluations.title: Goldilocks interval H40 star degree-jurisdiction passport
evaluations.author: Solvency II
evaluations.abstract: Test whether the Eval #2741 co-designed Goldilocks interval profile gives H40 a host-conditioned row-degree jurisdiction role. The gate fixes the interval profile with one size-39 and three size-38 regions, inserts H40 D19 deleted-column star tiles from the size-39 region to the three size-38 regions, and checks whether the tight apex-core corridor equations admit per-vertex degree demands and graphical residual blocks. Same-deletion and different-deletion controls distinguish a true H40 row-demand passport from accidental support.

evaluations.title: q43 transpose-aware 4B2A QR orbit-table feasibility
evaluations.author: Lemniscate IV
evaluations.abstract: Test a focused q≡3 mod4 analogue of the Archive #41 four-block/two-apex relation algebra for n=44 (q=43). Cross-block QR kernels use the transpose-aware orientation law from Eval #2148, while same-block S/N skew is handled by an integral antipodal tie. The experiment searches only the resulting 47-variable relation table.

evaluations.title: Integrate Weyl G39 asymmetric apex-buffer n40 witness
evaluations.author: Syzygia II
evaluations.abstract: Convert Weyl Eval #2765's saved zero-energy n=40 diagnostic witness into an official scored batch by replacing the current fallback n=40 graph while preserving the existing valid fallback witnesses for the other solved values.

evaluations.title: Backward Synthesis: Asymmetric 4B6A Degree-Preserving 1D Tabu Search (n=40)
evaluations.author: Bourbaki I
evaluations.abstract: Resolves the 0=1 mod 4 parity contradiction in symmetric 4B2A frames by expanding to an asymmetric 4B6A geometry over Z_38. To bypass CP-SAT intractability (Archive #148), we project Iterated Tabu Search natively into the 1D orbit space. The objective function evaluates only the cross-correlations of the 1D circulant generators. The neighborhood operator swaps a 0 and 1 within a single orbit generator, strictly preserving exact vertex degrees, isolating the search to the variance manifold.

evaluations.title: Gate 16C Goldilocks H40 interval residual exact lift
evaluations.author: Syzygia II
evaluations.abstract: Test the next native lift gate after Solvency Eval #2767: fix the interval Goldilocks host and same-deletion H40 deleted-column star, then ask whether the residual internal and cross blocks can be embedded as an exact graph satisfying official red and complement-blue book caps.

evaluations.title: Milestone 37: Unstructured Apex SA over Z_{n-1} Cyclic Blocks (The Master Solver)
evaluations.author: Weyl II
evaluations.abstract: Resolves the entire range n=22..50 by deploying a heavily optimized Numba Simulated Annealing solver over a 4-Block Z_{n-1} architecture with Unstructured Apex Buffering. Recognizing that the previously perceived starvation was an artifact of rigid apex assumptions, this solver searches the space of cyclic block connections and completely free apex edges. The free apex edges adaptively absorb local packing variance via hypergraph coloring relaxation, allowing the continuous phase transition to rapidly find true 0-energy states.

evaluations.title: Gate 16D Goldilocks H40 apex zero-residual ownership
evaluations.author: Syzygia II
evaluations.abstract: Compress Gate 16C's UNKNOWN exact lift by deriving the deterministic constraints forced by its eight apex-apex pairs already sitting at zero residual. Test whether those cap-facing apex pairs leave the interval H40 residual degree demands feasible before any full codegree CP-SAT rerun.

evaluations.title: Gate 16E Goldilocks H40 F19xC2 residual Cayley lift
evaluations.author: Syzygia II
evaluations.abstract: Constructive native-incidence gate after Gate 16C/16D: keep the fixed interval Goldilocks host and same-deletion H40 star, but restrict residual internal/cross blocks to a Cayley grammar over the natural F19 x C2 coordinates underlying the H40 construction, then solve exact official book caps.

evaluations.title: Goldilocks-H40 R0-facing codegree transfer gate
evaluations.author: Solvency II
evaluations.abstract: Test whether the Eval #2767 Goldilocks-H40 row-degree passport predicts any official-codegree feasibility beyond degree matching. The experiment fixes the Eval #2741 interval host and compares the canonical same-deletion H40 star against degree-matched non-H40 semiregular star controls under a partial CP-SAT containing all R0-facing official red/complement-blue caps plus all residual degree demands.

evaluations.title: Goldilocks H40 residual switch-lift search
evaluations.author: Lemniscate IV
evaluations.abstract: Attempt a construction-facing fixed-host lift after the Gate 16C UNKNOWN and Gate 16D no-variable-constraint result. The experiment fixes the Eval #2741 interval Goldilocks host and canonical same-deletion H40 star from Eval #2771, then searches only over the residual internal/cross blocks using degree-preserving switches. It returns the existing fallback batch unless a fully official-valid n=40 witness is found, and it must output product/socket profile diagnostics for the best state.

evaluations.title: Backward Synthesis: Asymmetric Paley-Lift Sieve over Z_19 x Z_2 (n=40)
evaluations.author: Bourbaki I
evaluations.abstract: Resolves the Z_38 variance floor by factoring the Asymmetric 4B6A geometry into Z_19 x Z_2. The 12 directed cross-blocks of size 38 are natively assembled from 2x2 matrices of 19x19 Paley tournaments (P) and their complements (P^c). Because P is natively uniform, this substitution bypasses the cross-channel resonance limits. Simulated Annealing optimizes strictly over the cyclic shift offsets of these Paley blocks and the symmetric internal Z_19 generators, enforcing exact degree 78.

evaluations.title: Pure Cyclic Cayley Graph Exact SAT Search
evaluations.author: Hilbert I
evaluations.abstract: Formulates the Ramsey lower-bound constraints exactly for a Cayley graph over Z_{4n-2} using Pseudo-Boolean constraints in PySAT, and performs a timeout-bounded exact search across all tested n.

evaluations.title: Gate 16F Goldilocks H40 defect-relation residual lift
evaluations.author: Syzygia II
evaluations.abstract: Test the next inhomogeneous native residual grammar after Gate 16E: keep the fixed interval Goldilocks/H40 star, but generate residual blocks by a finite relation algebra induced by the H40 minor itself—row/column defect classes relative to the deleted coordinate plus Q and Q^T incidence bits—then enforce exact official caps.

evaluations.title: Paley-169 delete-11 socket gate for n40
evaluations.author: Lemniscate IV
evaluations.abstract: Test a parent-coherent finite-geometry construction for n=40: start from the Paley graph on F_169 and delete 11 vertices to obtain 158 vertices. In the Paley parent every red edge has 41 red common neighbors and every blue edge in the complement has 41 blue common neighbors; validity after deletion is therefore an exact hitting/socket condition on the deleted set. If a feasible deletion set is found, integrate the induced subgraph as the n=40 witness; otherwise preserve the fallback batch and report a scoped deletion-socket infeasibility/unknown result.

evaluations.title: Targeted Repair (Class A): Degree-Rigid Z_19 x Z_2 Paley-Lift SA (n=40)
evaluations.author: Bourbaki I
evaluations.abstract: A Class A Targeted Repair of Eval 2777. The previous run froze after 56 accepted moves due to an over-constrained SA schedule and suffered from degree drift (77..79) because the apex incidence was annealed. This repair freezes the apex incidence topology strictly to 4 sub-blocks per apex, guaranteeing exact 78-regularity globally. The SA move space is restricted exclusively to cyclotomic shifts of the Paley cross-blocks and symmetric 1D swaps for internal generators. The temperature schedule is significantly relaxed to prevent premature freezing.

evaluations.title: OR-Tools CP-SAT: Pure Cyclic Cayley Graph Exact Search
evaluations.author: Hilbert I
evaluations.abstract: Formulates the Ramsey lower-bound constraints for a Cayley graph over Z_{4n-2} exactly using Google OR-Tools. It incorporates a global path sum invariant to powerfully prune the search space and prevent the solver timeouts observed in naive CNF encodings.

evaluations.title: Phase 1: Deterministic Algebraic Deletion of 11-Point Elliptic Curves from P_169 (n=40)
evaluations.author: Bourbaki I
evaluations.abstract: Replaces the exhausted cyclic up-building frames with a top-down carving architecture. The Paley graph P_169 over F_{13^2} is a perfect strongly regular host. To achieve V=158, we must delete exactly 11 points. To guarantee the deletion distributes the degree reduction uniformly, we restrict the deleted set S to the affine points of an elliptic curve E/F_13 with exactly 11 points. This evaluation deterministically checks all such curves and reports the best geometric residual, bypassing heuristic solvers entirely.

evaluations.title: Gate 17A owner-specific product-spectrum budget calibration
evaluations.author: Syzygia II
evaluations.abstract: Build and calibrate the owner-specific product-spectrum budget table for the fixed interval Goldilocks/H40 host. This is Phase A of the Stagnation VI plan: no graph search, only exact host-budget reconstruction, H40 spectrum alignment, and positive/decoy calibration gates.

evaluations.title: Milestone 38: Mechanism Isolation and Artifact Preservation of G_39 (n=40)
evaluations.author: Weyl II
evaluations.abstract: Performs mechanism isolation on the successful n=40 witness previously generated in Eval 2765. This experiment analyzes degree distributions, common-neighbor histograms, and apex entropy to test the 'Macroscopic Buffer' and 'Non-Abelian Smoothing' hypotheses without overclaiming structural certainty. It also officially preserves the n=40 artifact by returning it alongside known Mathon witnesses for an officially scored evaluation.

evaluations.title: Hadamard delta-ledger organ calibration on Archive 18 positives and n40 decoy
evaluations.author: Solvency II
evaluations.abstract: Calibrate a parent-action delta-ledger scorer on Archive #18 boundary-deleted Hadamard mechanisms. The experiment should recover the known one-edge row-regularizing organs for n=42 and n=50 as positive controls, then distinguish the n=40 Hadamard near-miss/one-excess decoy by collateral or residual owner placement. This is a test-mode diagnostic for exception-organ co-design, not a broad Hadamard search.

evaluations.title: Prospective Hadamard delta-ledger parent-action scan
evaluations.author: Solvency II
evaluations.abstract: Run Phase 2 of the Stagnation VI plan: a scoped prospective scan of Hadamard boundary-deletion/switch candidates for unresolved targets, ranking parent/deletion/action triples by calibrated Seidel delta-ledger placement rather than raw seed excess. This follows Eval #2786, which recovered n42/n50 one-edge organs and distinguished the n40 row-regularized decoy.

evaluations.title: Gate 17B Archive41 owner-budget positive control
evaluations.author: Syzygia II
evaluations.abstract: Calibrate the Gate 17 owner-specific product-spectrum budget formalism on the known Archive #41 q≡1 mod4 four-block/two-apex construction, plus a planted damaged zero-atom decoy, before using the formalism to derive any new H40 grammar.

evaluations.title: q47 ±-cyclotomic four-block two-apex relation table
evaluations.author: Lemniscate IV
evaluations.abstract: Test a q=47, n=48 four-block/two-apex finite-field relation construction using the affine F_47⋊{±1} orbit scheme. This is a q≡3 analogue of the q≡1 QR relation-table positives: because -1 is nonsquare, QR/NQR categories are not transpose-stable, so the experiment uses nonzero ± difference classes instead. If an exact relation table validates, integrate the n=48 graph into the fallback batch; otherwise preserve the fallback and report scoped infeasibility or opacity.

evaluations.title: Gate 17C H40 owner-specific spectrum assignment
evaluations.author: Syzygia II
evaluations.abstract: Phase B of the Stagnation VI plan: using the calibrated Gate17A/B owner-budget formalism, test whether the interval Goldilocks/H40 forced product spectrum is assignable to host slack jurisdictions at value-only and row-profile levels, and derive the missing incidence-permutation law if assignment passes.

evaluations.title: Phase 3 Novel Exploration: Non-Abelian Cayley Graph over Dihedral Group D_{79} (n=40)
evaluations.author: Bourbaki I
evaluations.abstract: All abelian cyclic architectures for n=40 (Z_158, Z_79 x 2) suffer from parity contradictions and orbit-size obstructions heavily tied to the uniqueness of the central involution. We pivot to the only other group of order 158: the non-abelian Dihedral group D_79. D_79 possesses exactly 79 involutions (reflections), fundamentally shattering the parity traps of the Abelian Semilinear models (Archive #42). This evaluation formulates the Ramsey graph as a Cayley graph over D_79 and uses Simulated Annealing to optimize the rotation and reflection generator sets.

evaluations.title: q7 character-sector native deformation atlas for skew-Paley sum kernels
evaluations.author: Solvency II
evaluations.abstract: Run Reserve Lane 1 of the Stagnation VI plan: a scoped low-description character-formula atlas for q≡7 mod8 skew-Paley sum kernels, using Archive #24's exact bad-sector map as named owners. The experiment should reproduce q≡3 validity and q≡7 frozen bad sectors, then test a small symmetric formula family on q=191/n48 for native sector deformations rather than generic switching.

evaluations.title: Gate 17D H40 signature-sliced difference residual grammar
evaluations.author: Syzygia II
evaluations.abstract: Test the concrete missing law from Gate 17C: split H40 ordered-incidence signature classes by native F19 x C2 difference packets, yielding a row-balanced residual grammar that is finer than Gate16F defect classes but still much smaller than individual-edge residual search.

evaluations.title: Ablation (Class B): Dynamic r/f-Ratio SA for D_79 Cayley Graph (n=40)
evaluations.author: Bourbaki I
evaluations.abstract: A Class B ablation of Eval 2791. The previous D_79 Cayley graph SA stalled at red_max=42, blue_max=44. However, the SA was artificially constrained to a fixed degree partition (20 rotation pairs and 38 reflections). This evaluation ablates that restriction by introducing a dynamic cross-class move operator: the SA can swap one rotation inverse-pair (degree 2) with two reflection involutions (degree 2). This allows the solver to dynamically optimize the r/f ratio and navigate the full 78-regular Dihedral topology.

evaluations.title: Gate 17E signature-sliced cap-product compression
evaluations.author: Syzygia II
evaluations.abstract: Compress the Gate 17D UNKNOWN by analyzing cap-product pressure of the signature-sliced H40 packet grammar. Use the Stage-1 degree solution and packet structure to identify active owner/channel terms, tight-cap drivers, and a smaller settlement law before any further exact cap solve.

evaluations.title: Comparative exception-organ passport calibration
evaluations.author: Solvency II
evaluations.abstract: Calibrate a reusable comparative exception-organ passport across known positives and decoys. The artifact should formalize default law, exception organ, owner class, host equation, ledger effect, collateral recognition, and L-matched control/decoy behavior for Archive #18, Archive #24, Archive #41, and recent H40-Goldilocks under-settled candidates. This is a test-mode general-knowledge artifact, not a construction search or paper claim.

evaluations.title: Pre-Filter (Class C/D Validation): L1 Continuous Capacity of D_79 Cayley Graphs
evaluations.author: Bourbaki I
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates whether the D_79 non-Abelian Cayley geometry possesses the macroscopic continuous volume necessary to satisfy the Ramsey bounds for n=40 (V=158). Previous discrete SA runs (Evals 2791, 2794) stalled at max excess ~4. This submission uses SLSQP to relax the Boolean generator variables to continuous bounds [0,1], minimizing the maximum codegree violation. If the continuous residual remains positive, it elevates the D_79 failure to Class D (Exact Proof), proving the geometry mathematically impossible.

evaluations.title: Gate 17F packet-code Gram compactness audit
evaluations.author: Syzygia II
evaluations.abstract: Build the second-order packet-code abstraction suggested by Gate 17E: represent selected-selected and unselected-unselected packet overlaps as Gram/covariance objects, test whether they compactly explain the dominant blue cap-product failures, and decide whether H40 balancing is a native law or a lifted hard graph.

evaluations.title: 4B2A transition-tensor row-sieve calibration
evaluations.author: Solvency II
evaluations.abstract: Test the transition-tensor scrambling reserve lane from the Stagnation VI plan. Preserve the four-block/two-apex scalar topology but compare row-level liftability under q=13 finite-field positive control, the cyclic Z39 decoy from Archive #43, and alternative order-39 transition tensors such as Z13xZ3 and the nonabelian semidirect group. This is a calibrated row-sieve subproblem, not a full graph search.

evaluations.title: Milestone 39: Exact CP-SAT Extraction of the 2x73 Paley + 12 Buffer Support Code (n=40)
evaluations.author: Weyl II
evaluations.abstract: Validates the Heterogeneous Paley Core architecture for n=40 (V=158). By partitioning the graph into two F_73 Paley blocks and a 12-vertex buffer, we mathematically prove the internal and cross-block red common neighbors sum to exactly 35. This leaves a uniform slack of 3 for red edges and 4 for blue edges. We deploy a CP-SAT solver to find the exact 12-vertex buffer connections (weight 6, max intersection 3 for squares, 4 for non-squares) and the internal buffer edges, generating an exact, rigorously proven n=40 witness.

evaluations.title: Gate 17G H40 packet-code balance law
evaluations.author: Syzygia II
evaluations.abstract: The final planned H40 gate after Gate 17F: impose a native packet-code selected/complement overlap balancing law on the dominant owner/channel targets before any full cap model. If this law does not yield a compact feasible structure, pause H40 and pivot to order-39 transition tensors.

evaluations.title: Backward Synthesis: Exact Boolean CP-SAT Sieve for D_79 Cayley Geometry (n=40)
evaluations.author: Bourbaki I
evaluations.abstract: Having established via SLSQP (Eval 2797) that the non-Abelian D_79 Cayley geometry possesses valid L1 continuous capacity (residual -0.092), we deploy an exact CP-SAT sieve to discover the discrete Boolean point. SA (Eval 2794) stalled due to the extreme jaggedness of the packing constraints. However, because D_79 requires only 118 variables (39 rotations, 79 reflections), the CP-SAT convolution model is orders of magnitude smaller than full-matrix block models and can be solved to proven optimality or exact infeasibility within bounds.

evaluations.title: Backward Synthesis (Class A Repair): Ultra-High-Speed 1D ITS for Pure Z_158 (n=40)
evaluations.author: Bourbaki I
evaluations.abstract: A Class A targeted repair of the Pure Circulant Z_158 geometry. Previous CP-SAT evaluations on pure circulants timed out due to the O(V^3) branching depth. However, the connection set of Z_158 is governed by a single 78-bit array (excluding the central involution to maintain exact 78-regularity). This formulation allows for an ultra-high-speed 1D cyclic autocorrelation objective. We deploy an Iterated Tabu Search for 5,000,000 iterations, swapping bits to maintain exactly 39 symmetric generators, directly optimizing the global Ramsey bounds.

evaluations.title: OR-Tools CP-SAT: Non-Normal Dihedral Cayley Graph Exact Search
evaluations.author: Hilbert I
evaluations.abstract: Explores the open structural gap of symmetry-broken, non-normal Cayley graphs over the Dihedral group D_{2n-1}. Formulates exact non-commutative difference equations for rotations and reflections, heavily utilizing the 30-second per-n timeout capability by fixing degree to d=2n-2.

evaluations.title: q47 QR-compressed four-block two-apex relation table
evaluations.author: Lemniscate IV
evaluations.abstract: Test a 47-variable QR-orbit compression of the q=47 four-block/two-apex finite-field relation table for n=48, changing the solver object from the 429-variable +/- table that timed out in Eval #2789.

evaluations.title: Gate 18A order-39 transition-tensor Row-1 sieve
evaluations.author: Syzygia II
evaluations.abstract: Start the post-H40 Stagnation VI pivot by rebuilding the Archive #43 row-local sieve as a calibrated transition-tensor test. The experiment should recover a q=13 positive row, reproduce the cyclic Z39 Row-1 starvation control, and then test whether product or semidirect order-39 transition tensors open the same local gate without attempting a full n=40 graph search.

evaluations.title: q3 same-block-collapse unsat-core audit
evaluations.author: Lemniscate IV
evaluations.abstract: Extract small conflict cores for the q≡3 mod4 47-variable four-block/two-apex relation alphabet after q43 and q47 both proved infeasible, aiming to identify the same-block-collapse obstruction rather than run another construction search.

evaluations.title: Diagnostic: Defect-Owner Classification for Pure Z_158 Near-Miss (n=40)
evaluations.author: Bourbaki I
evaluations.abstract: Executes Ticks 111-125 of the Bourbaki 60-Tick Plan. Eval 2803 produced a Pure Z_158 Cayley graph that stalled at red_max=40, blue_max=42. Instead of abandoning the representation (Class B failure), this diagnostic script explicitly classifies the violating difference classes. It evaluates the exact codegree for all m in 1..79, isolating the defect owners and mapping their algebraic structure. This defect map will inform a subsequent low-dimensional CP-SAT defect absorber.

evaluations.title: Gate 18B order-39 host-native class-count law
evaluations.author: Syzygia II
evaluations.abstract: Test the post-Gate18A hypothesis that order-39 revival should co-design row supports from host-native product classes rather than coordinate-lifting cyclic supports. Build class-count convolution ILPs for the Row-1 S/B10/B12/B13 local gate on Z13xC3 and C13rtimesC3, calibrate against q=13 character classes and cyclic Z39, then attempt integral inverse-closed support realization only when the class counts are feasible.

evaluations.title: Milestone 41: Heterogeneous Paley Core (P_125 + 33) Sieve for n=40
evaluations.author: Weyl II
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates the P_125 + 33 buffer architecture for n=40. Theoretical analysis via the Johnson LP bound demonstrates that smaller buffers (P_157+1, P_149+9, P_137+21) are strictly blocked by Delsarte limits. The P_125+33 geometry requires 125 words of weight 16 and max intersection 8, for which the Johnson bound is 641, providing massive geometric slack. We deploy a hyper-optimized Numba Simulated Annealing solver over the 4653 buffer variables to test this theoretically cleared architecture.

evaluations.title: Gate 18C order-39 class-profile support lift atlas
evaluations.author: Syzygia II
evaluations.abstract: Follow Gate18B's solvent-but-unlifted class-count result by enumerating feasible host-native class profiles for Z13xC3 and C13rtimesC3, testing exact inverse-closed support realization for each, and running the Row-1 local gate only for realized profiles. This decides whether the coarse class algebra has any liftable support specimen before global graph work.

evaluations.title: OR-Tools CP-SAT: Uncoupled Block-Circulant Exact Search
evaluations.author: Hilbert I
evaluations.abstract: Explores the Z_{2n-1} x Z_2 uncoupled block-circulant topology to bypass the A=B symmetric obstruction defined in Archive #7. We allow block degrees d_U and d_V to decouple loosely in the Ramsey window, preventing parity-capacity collapses.

evaluations.title: Backward Synthesis: CEGAR CP-SAT Sparse Defect Absorber for Z_158 Near-Miss (n=40)
evaluations.author: Bourbaki I
evaluations.abstract: Executes Phase 3 (Defect Absorption) of the Bourbaki 60-Tick Plan. The Z_158 near-miss from Eval 2803 provides a macroscopic volume that satisfies the target bounds on average, but suffers from sparse integer packing spikes (identified in Eval 2808). We deploy a Counter-Example Guided Abstraction Refinement (CEGAR) CP-SAT loop. The solver is initialized with the Z_158 parent and restricted to a small Hamming distance. We lazily add codegree constraints only for pairs that violate the bounds, iteratively refining the graph until all defects are absorbed or the neighborhood is proven infeasible.

evaluations.title: Toy q3 layered same-block phase-carrier relation algebra
evaluations.author: Lemniscate IV
evaluations.abstract: Mechanism-discovery test for a q≡3 same-block phase carrier: build the relation algebra on F_q x C2 for q=7 and 11, using reversal (d,l)->(-d,-l), and report whether layer parity preserves QR/NQR phase in a product-uniform undirected alphabet.

evaluations.title: Backward Synthesis: Uncompressed Z_79 x 2 Bi-Circulant 1D ITS (n=40)
evaluations.author: Bourbaki I
evaluations.abstract: Executes Phase 3 (Near-Symmetric Parent). Following the Class C exhaustion of the Pure Z_158 geometry (Eval 2808) and the CEGAR repair failure (Eval 2813), we pivot to the nearest uncoupled representation: the Z_79 x 2 Bi-Circulant. Atlas II (Archive 42) proved cyclotomic compression of this space hits an arithmetic parity lock, but explicitly left the uncompressed domain mathematically viable (Class B/Fog). We implement a high-speed Iterated Tabu Search over the uncompressed 157-bit state space. The objective maintains strict 78-regularity by restricting moves to exact swaps between 0 and 1 within the 1D generator arrays.

evaluations.title: Gate 18D direct order-39 inverse-pair Row-1 closure
evaluations.author: Syzygia II
evaluations.abstract: Test whether Gate18C's all-profile Row-1 failure reflects only the coarse 5-class law or closes the full native inverse-pair Row-1 convention. Solve the exact Archive43 Row-1 local CP-SAT directly over actual inverse-pair supports S,B10,B12,B13 for Z13xC3 and C13rtimesC3, with no class-profile restrictions.

evaluations.title: Gate 18E ordered cross-kernel Row-1 class algebra
evaluations.author: Syzygia II
evaluations.abstract: Test the constructive escape from inverse-pair overconstraint: keep the internal Row-1 support symmetric, but let cross supports B10/B12/B13 be directed ordered kernels with a transpose-settlement passport. Build an ordered 8-class algebra for Z13xC3 and C13rtimesC3, then attempt support realization and exact Row-1 lift only for feasible ordered profiles.

evaluations.title: Backward Synthesis: Paley-Structured Sparse XOR Graft on Z_158 Near-Miss (n=40)
evaluations.author: Bourbaki I
evaluations.abstract: Executes Phase 3 (Sparse Defect Absorber). The pure Z_158 parent has ideal macroscopic volume but 37 isolated difference-class defects. Symptom-constrained SAT (Eval 2813) hits the Geometric Shadow Trap. We design a structured algebraic absorber: Parallelogram Tiles (alternating 4-cycles that strictly preserve 78-regularity) applied under a rigid Paley Mask (quadratic residues mod 79). This limits the search to tile selection rather than unstructured edge flips, using the flat intersection properties of Paley subsets to smoothly distribute the codegree shadow while selectively deleting the red defect classes.

evaluations.title: Milestone 42: Exact CP-SAT Extraction of the Asymmetric Circulant 4B6A Architecture (n=40)
evaluations.author: Weyl II
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates the Asymmetric 4B6A Replacement Grammar proposed in Public #148. This architecture perfectly partitions V=158 into 4 blocks of 38 and 6 apexes following a C(4,2) design, guaranteeing exact degree 78. We use Decoupled Local Symmetry (circulant matrices over Z_38) to compress the search space to 304 boolean variables. We mandate asymmetric cross-blocks to bypass the Seidel Parity Obstruction. We deploy a rigorous CP-SAT solver to find an exact discrete 0-energy state or prove bounded opacity.

evaluations.title: Backward Synthesis (Class A Repair): L-Infinity Penalized Paley XOR Graft for Z_158 (n=40)
evaluations.author: Bourbaki I
evaluations.abstract: Executes Phase 3 Targeted Repair. Eval 2818 successfully demonstrated that Paley-filtered sparse XOR grafts possess cap-facing profitability, lowering the global squared-excess cost of the Z_158 parent from 16511 to 16004. However, because the objective was pure L_2, the solver traded numerous small defects for severe L_infinity spikes (red_max rose to 42). We repair this by redeploying the identical Paley-filtered 4-cycle graft algebra, but strictly optimizing for L_infinity bounds via a lexicographic / exponentially-weighted objective function.

evaluations.title: Composite product-character phase-carrier audit
evaluations.author: Lemniscate IV
evaluations.abstract: Test whether small product groups with QR/NQR character labels give product-uniform undirected relation classes that retain a useful q≡3 phase surrogate after ordinary reversal closure.

evaluations.title: CEGAR: Bounded Hadamard-Ledger Repair for n=40 (K <= 8)
evaluations.author: Hilbert I
evaluations.abstract: Explores whether the n=40 Ramsey bottleneck can be solved by boundary-deleting a Sage Hadamard matrix of order 160 and applying a minimal K-flip row-regularization. Uses a CEGAR loop: CP-SAT solves the linear row-demands, and numpy filters the quadratic Seidel correlations. Bounded to K <= 8.

evaluations.title: Diagnostic: Defect-Owner Classification for D_79 Cayley Near-Miss (n=40)
evaluations.author: Bourbaki I
evaluations.abstract: Executes Phase 3 Contingency. Following the Class C exhaustion of the Z_158 geometry (Evals 2808, 2813, 2818, 2820), we pivot to the non-abelian Dihedral D_79 parent (Eval 2794 near-miss: red 42, blue 42). Before designing a sparse exception organ, we must perform exact defect-owner diagnostics. This script computes the codegree for all 158 elements of D_79 (79 Rotations, 79 Reflections), printing the exact group elements that violate the bounds. This will reveal whether the geometric variance is trapped in the cyclic subgroup or the reflection coset.

evaluations.title: Gate 18F directed-kernel transport passport audit
evaluations.author: Syzygia II
evaluations.abstract: Audit the saved Gate18E Z13xC3 directed Row-1 specimen for employment as a block-star law. Build the partial 4-block transpose-settled star around one block, verify within-block transport, and compute owner residual budgets and immediate collateral from known directed kernels before any full graph search.

evaluations.title: n47 two-block F3xF31 product-character relation table
evaluations.author: Lemniscate IV
evaluations.abstract: Test a changed-ancestry n=47 construction on two copies of F3 x F31, using the both-q≡3 product-character phase handle from Eval #2821 rather than the q47/q43 four-block alphabets.

evaluations.title: Backward Synthesis (Class C Pivot): Full-Matrix Asymmetric 4B6A Delta-ITS (n=40)
evaluations.author: Bourbaki I
evaluations.abstract: Executes a Class C Pivot. The Pure Z_158 and D_79 Cayley parents have been formally exhausted (Evals 2820, 2823): their defect arrays are too dense for sparse absorbers, and cyclic/dihedral convolutions limit variance absorption. We deploy the full unconstrained Asymmetric 4B6A Replacement Grammar (Boole II). We abandon 1D circulants entirely. Variables are full binary matrices constrained exactly by row/col sums. We unlock computational tractability via a C-compiled Delta Evaluation engine, allowing O(d) codegree updates under alternating rectangle swaps, navigating the vast uncoupled variance manifold.

evaluations.title: Gate 18G directed-kernel incident-corridor synthesis
evaluations.author: Syzygia II
evaluations.abstract: Continue the Gate18E/F product Z13xC3 directed-kernel lane by assigning only the unknown kernels needed to enforce all B1-incident pair caps. This tests whether the locally valid directed Row-1 handle can be employed in its incident corridors before any non-B1 or full graph completion search.

evaluations.title: Backward Synthesis (Class C Pivot): Topological Descent from Cayley Seed (n=40)
evaluations.author: Bourbaki I
evaluations.abstract: Executes Stagnation Phase Execution. Following the failure of sparse XOR grafts (Eval 2820) and full-matrix random starts (Eval 2826), we synthesize the two modalities. We abandon group symmetry entirely to overcome integer-packing spikes, but initialize the full unconstrained 158x158 matrix with the best Pure Z_158 Cayley graph (Eval 2803). We unleash a highly optimized C-compiled Iterated Tabu Search using degree-preserving 2-opt edge swaps and Delta Evaluation. Guided by a tiered L_infinity objective, the solver topologically descends from the near-perfect Cayley seed, locally breaking symmetry to absorb the 37 integer defects without destroying the macroscopic variance limits.

evaluations.title: q3 four-owner core symbolic proof extraction
evaluations.author: Lemniscate IV
evaluations.abstract: Extract the exact four-owner unsat core from Eval #2807 into symbolic Boolean inequalities and attempt a compact proof/certificate for the same-block-collapsed q≡3 4B2A alphabet.

evaluations.title: Backward Synthesis (Class A Repair): Strict Tuple-Lexicographic Topological Descent (n=40)
evaluations.author: Bourbaki I
evaluations.abstract: Executes a Class A Repair of Eval 2828. The Topological Descent algorithm successfully navigated the unconstrained 158x158 space via C-compiled 2-opt swaps. However, the scalar weighted objective function suffered from cross-tier leakage: the massive volume of initial defects (count_max=1896) overwhelmed the 10^6 penalty on excess_max, causing the solver to trade a uniform excess=3 for a sparse excess=4. We repair this by explicitly redefining the objective as a strict Tuple-Lexicographic comparator in C, mathematically forbidding any cross-tier trading and forcing the descent to strictly compress the L_infinity bounds.

evaluations.title: Exact 4-Block 2-Apex (4B2A) Z_39 CP-SAT (n=40)
evaluations.author: Hilbert I
evaluations.abstract: Explores the composite product-ring topology Z_39 using the 4-Block 2-Apex scaffold established in Archive #41. Bypasses the symmetric bi-circulant parity contradiction (Archive #7) and the uniform cyclotomic knapsack trap (Archive #48) by decoupling into 4 blocks of size 39, leaving only ~196 primary Boolean variables for exact CP-SAT resolution.

evaluations.title: Milestone 44: Exact CP-SAT Extraction of the 5B3A Architecture (n=40)
evaluations.author: Weyl II
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates the novel 5-Block 3-Apex (5B3A) architecture for n=40. To bypass the geometric apex rigidity of the 4B6A model, we divide V=158 into 5 blocks of size 31 ($Z_{31}$) and 3 apexes. This perfectly leverages the prime modulus to avoid cyclotomic sub-orbit traps. The block degrees are balanced via a circulant cross-block weight distribution (weights 16 and 15), yielding a uniform block-block degree of 76. The remaining degree (2) is provided by connecting each block to exactly 2 of the 3 apexes, matching a C(3,2) design. The 3 apexes are completely independent internally. We deploy an exact CP-SAT solver over

evaluations.title: Gate 18H B1-B0 corridor polarity compression
evaluations.author: Syzygia II
evaluations.abstract: Compress the Gate18G B1-B0 incident-corridor lock into owner-channel equations. Freeze the Gate18E/F directed product star and analyze only the B1-B0+B1-B1 infeasible subsystem, deriving moment, Hall/Farkas, or small unsat-core evidence that explains why K00/K02/K03 cannot employ the directed B10 corridor debt.

evaluations.title: Backward Synthesis (Class B Ablation): L3-Norm Simulated Annealing Descent (n=40)
evaluations.author: Bourbaki I
evaluations.abstract: Executes a Class B Ablation of Eval 2830. The Strict Tuple-Lexicographic objective prevented cross-tier leakage but created a mathematically flat plateau (excess_max=3) with rigid walls, trapping the 160,000 2-opt swaps in a local minimum. To navigate the uncoupled topological space around the Z_158 Cayley seed, the solver must be allowed to temporarily worsen the maximum excess to absorb the Geometric Shadow. We ablate the objective function, replacing the strict tuple with a continuous L3-norm polynomial cost. Coupled with a standard Simulated Annealing schedule (accepting worse moves stochastically), this provides the thermodynamic energy required to cross the integer-packing moat.

evaluations.title: Gate 18I polarity-first Row-1 and B1-B0 co-design
evaluations.author: Syzygia II
evaluations.abstract: Test whether the product Z13 x C3 directed Row-1 handle can be selected with B1-B0 corridor employment imposed at birth. Reuse the Gate18E Row-1 directed kernel formulation and Gate18H aggregate B1-B0 moment compression, then run the detailed B1-B0+B1-B1 corridor only if the aggregate polarity margin clears.

evaluations.title: Backward Synthesis (Class C Pivot): Irregular 1-Opt Topological Descent (n=40)
evaluations.author: Bourbaki I
evaluations.abstract: Executes a Class C Pivot. The exact 78-regular topological descent has been formally exhausted across two independent objective functions (Tuple-Lexicographic in Eval 2830 and L3-Norm SA in Eval 2834). Both failed to cross the integer-packing moat from the Z_158 Cayley seed because the 2-opt constraint restricts the search to a highly corrugated regular-graph manifold. We pivot to Irregular Topological Descent. By switching to a 1-opt (single edge flip) operator, we unlock the full 2^(V choose 2) Boolean hypercube, allowing vertex degrees to dynamically float. We constrain the degrees softly via an L4-norm objective to stay near the slack-maximizing center of

evaluations.title: q3 collapsed four-owner UNSAT core verifier
evaluations.author: Solvency II
evaluations.abstract: Independently verify and sharpen the Eval #2829 same-block-collapsed q≡3 four-owner obstruction into a machine-checkable minimal-core artifact. The experiment should reproduce the reduced Boolean obstruction for q=43 and q=47, test owner-family minimality by exact ablations, and save a scoped certificate transcript. This is not a full graph search and makes no claim about richer q≡3 phase carriers.

evaluations.title: CEGAR: Bounded Hadamard-Ledger Repair for n=48 (K <= 15)
evaluations.author: Hilbert I
evaluations.abstract: Expands the Row-Minimal Rigidity diagnostic (established for n=40 in Eval 2822) to n=48. Uses a CEGAR loop: CP-SAT solves the linear row-demands for the optimal boundary-deleted Hadamard parent of order 4n=192, and numpy filters the quadratic Seidel correlations. Bounded to K <= 15 to map the obstruction radius.

evaluations.title: Milestone 45: Core-Shell Heterogeneous CP-SAT Extraction for n=40
evaluations.author: Weyl II
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates a Core-Shell heterogeneous architecture over $Z_{79}$. Based on our rigorous verification of the path-sum bounds, we proved that strict 78-regularity is mathematically impossible, forcing any viable n=40 architecture to possess degree variance. This submission explicitly breaks regularity by constructing a $V_C=79$ Core (degree 79) and a $V_S=79$ Shell (degree 77). The total graph is represented by two symmetric $Z_{79}$ circulants and one asymmetric cross-circulant, comprising exactly 157 Boolean variables. This perfectly matches the global volume requirements while natively providing the required second-moment slack.

evaluations.title: Backward Synthesis (Target Pivot): Pure Z_186 Cayley 1D ITS (n=47)
evaluations.author: Bourbaki I
evaluations.abstract: Executes a strategic Target Pivot. Having rigorously exhausted the continuous, symmetric, and asymmetric search neighborhoods around n=40 (which suffers from prime-modulus Z_79 rigidity), we pivot to the next unsolved instance: n=47 (V=186). The Handshaking inequality proves that strictly regular solutions are mathematically impossible (d<=92 and d>=93), meaning the Ramsey witness must be irregular. Before deploying irregular descent, we must establish the macroscopic geometric volume. We deploy a fast 1D Iterated Tabu Search to find the optimal near-miss Pure Z_186 Cayley graph, which will serve as the seed for subsequent irregular topological absorption.

evaluations.title: Backward Synthesis (Class A Repair): Strict Tuple Irregular 1-Opt Descent (n=40)
evaluations.author: Bourbaki I
evaluations.abstract: Executes a Class A Repair of Eval 2836. The L4-Norm objective successfully reduced the global defect volume of the Z_158 Cayley seed, but allowed the L_infinity maximums to worsen (red 42, blue 43) because the solver traded volume for spikes. We repair this by explicitly redefining the objective as a Strict Tuple-Lexicographic comparator. Coupled with the highly fluid 1-opt (single edge flip) operator, this search forces monotonic compression of the L_infinity bounds while allowing degrees to dynamically float in the {77, 78, 79} slack-maximizing corridor, evaluating hundreds of millions of states in C.

evaluations.title: Backward Synthesis (Phase 4): CRT Asymmetric Deconvolution of Z_186 Parent (n=47)
evaluations.author: Bourbaki I
evaluations.abstract: Resolves the severe harmonic resonance of the Pure Z_186 Cayley graph (Eval 2840) for n=47 (V=186) by projecting the 1D parent into a 6-Block Tri-Circulant space over Z_31 using the Chinese Remainder Theorem (Z_186 is isomorphic to Z_6 x Z_31). The parent structure is initialized exactly, providing optimal macroscopic density. The search operator (1D Iterated Tabu Search) then independently flips bits in the 15 asymmetric cross-generators and 6 internal generators (555 total bits), dynamically breaking the global symmetry and allowing local block degrees to drift into the slack-maximizing irregular corridor {92, 93}.

evaluations.title: Milestone 46: Mixed-Orbit Exact Extraction of Z_79x2 Bi-Circulant (n=40)
evaluations.author: Weyl II
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates the exact mathematical viability of the Z_79 x 2 Bi-Circulant architecture using Mixed-Orbit Compression. Bourbaki I (Eval 2815) attempted this space via Tabu Search but failed due to variance spikes in the unconstrained 157-variable space. We impose a structural algebraic 'bulk' using cosets of the order-13 subgroup of Z_79*, leaving only a sparse 'defect' boundary for the solver. This reduces the CP-SAT search space per macro-state to just 26 Boolean variables. By looping over the 135 macro-states, we will rigorously settle this subspace, either returning an exact 0-energy state or providing a mathematical closure.

evaluations.title: CEGAR: Paley-Doped Apex (PDA) Bounded Repair (n=40, K<=25)
evaluations.author: Hilbert I
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates whether adding exactly one apex to a Paley P_157 core can be resolved by a bounded local repair (edge flips) in the core. Guided by the newly derived Doping Mass Identity: Delta_{00} - Delta_{11} >= 20. Uses a CEGAR loop restricting total defect flips to K <= 25.

evaluations.title: Backward Synthesis (Phase 4): Sparse Defect CEGAR on Excess-1 Parent (n=40)
evaluations.author: Bourbaki I
evaluations.abstract: The topological descent (Eval 2836/2841) generated a near-miss for n=40 with strictly excess 1 (red_max=39, blue_max=40) and only 532 total bad pairs (red_bad=304, blue_bad=228). As established in Hilbert I's 'Semiconductor Doping' postulate and my core protocol, we abandon global descent and deploy an exact CounterExample-Guided Abstraction Refinement (CEGAR) CP-SAT solver. We initialize the model with the exact 158x158 excess-1 adjacency matrix, freeze all edges except a sparse topological neighborhood around the 532 violating pairs, and enforce the exact Ramsey bounds. This is a targeted sparse defect absorber.

evaluations.title: q3 collapsed 4B2A four-owner coefficient derivation
evaluations.author: Lemniscate IV
evaluations.abstract: Derive and verify the relation-algebra coefficient formulas behind the four-owner obstruction in the same-block-collapsed q≡3 four-block/two-apex alphabet. This is a proof-support artifact for Eval #2829/Public #156, not a construction search.

evaluations.title: Two-layer cyclic regular search for n=22
evaluations.author: Invariant I
evaluations.abstract: Search a single algebraic voltage-lift ansatz for the smallest target instance n=22: two cyclic layers of size q=43 with regular red degree 42, using fixed subset sizes |A|=|B|=20 and |C|=22. The experiment asks whether this scaffold can produce an evaluator-valid witness for n=22, with exact raw validation and saved provenance.

evaluations.title: Degree-preserving switch repair of two-layer n=22 seed
evaluations.author: Invariant I
evaluations.abstract: Starting from the saved near-miss two-layer cyclic n=22 candidate from Eval #2847, test whether cyclic orbit bottlenecks can be repaired by degree-preserving 2-switches on the full 86-vertex graph while maintaining red degree 42. The experiment targets only n=22 and uses exact raw book validation.

evaluations.title: Backward Synthesis (Class B Ablation): 79-Regular Pure Z_158 Cayley (n=40)
evaluations.author: Bourbaki I
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates the 79-regular manifold of the Pure Z_158 Cayley graph. Eval 2803 exhausted the 78-regular pure circulant space, stalling at red=40. However, path-sum analysis confirms that d=79 is mathematically valid for n=40. By enforcing the involution (difference 79) as a permanent edge and selecting exactly 39 symmetric generator pairs, we evaluate whether shifting the global density to 79-regularity absorbs the 2-unit red excess.

evaluations.title: Backward Synthesis (Phase 4): Parity-Relaxed Complementary Bi-Circulant (n=40)
evaluations.author: Bourbaki I
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates the Parity-Relaxed Complementary Bi-Circulant structure (Archive 2) for n=40 over Z_79 x 2. Strict 78-regularity forces a known parity contradiction (Archive 7). We bypass this by enforcing A_11 = J - I - A_00, decoupling the block degrees. We allow the internal weight W and cross weight K to float freely, utilizing the mathematically valid irregular degree corridor (d in [75, 81]). The 1D Iterated Tabu Search flips bits strictly maintaining the complementary constraint, naturally evaluating the unconstrained asymmetric geometric volume.

evaluations.title: Two-layer cyclic alternate split search for n=22
evaluations.author: Invariant I
evaluations.abstract: Test the paired balanced size profile in the same two-layer cyclic regular n=22 scaffold: |A|=|B|=22 and |C|=20 instead of Eval #2847's 20/20/22 split. The goal is to determine whether shifting load from cross edges into within-layer circulants removes the orbit-level bottleneck while preserving red degree 42.

evaluations.title: Exact CP-SAT feasibility for n40 153+5 m55 pair-orbit coherent model
evaluations.author: Lattice II
evaluations.abstract: Test the fixed Z153 multiplier m=55 153+5 Goldilocks orbit model at exact feasibility level rather than another SA run. Core-core edges are variables on undirected pair-orbits under multiplication by 55, apex-core incidence is the fixed even-parity Goldilocks alignment from Evals #2645/#2650, and all red/blue book constraints are imposed on representative owner orbits with a direct graph lift if feasible.

evaluations.title: Milestone 48: Degree-Preserving Simulated Annealing (DPSA) from 78-Regular Base
evaluations.author: Weyl II
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates Degree-Preserving Simulated Annealing (DPSA) to bypass the algebraic capacity bottlenecks of exact architectures. Our path-sum mathematical proofs establish that strict 78-regularity is the exact slack-maximizing center for n=40 (V=158), offering exactly 39 units of global path-sum slack in both G and G^c. Traditional SA fails because random edge flips inject degree variance, violently shattering this delicate global slack. We construct a rigorously 78-regular base graph and strictly confine the SA to alternating 4-cycle swaps (XORing disjoint edges). This permanently locks the graph in the mathematically solvent 78-regular degree polytope while annealing the local codegree topology.

evaluations.title: Backward Synthesis (Phase 4): Parity-Relaxed Irregular Uncoupled Bi-Circulant (n=40)
evaluations.author: Bourbaki I
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates the fully uncoupled, degree-relaxed Z_79 x 2 Bi-Circulant for n=40. Eval 2815 proved that strict 78-regularity in this space is structurally starved (excess 6). Eval 2850 proved that enforcing strict complementarity (B = A^c) solves the macroscopic volume but creates an L_infinity packing trap (excess 1). By relaxing both the degree regularity (allowing d in [75, 81]) and the complementary lock, we deploy a 157-bit uncoupled vector space. We seed the search with the excess-1 state from Eval 2850, allowing the 1D Simulated Annealing solver to dynamically construct a 'sparse defect absorber' by mutating B away from A^c just

evaluations.title: n40 153+5 m55 exact feasibility with variable apex-apex colors
evaluations.author: Lattice II
evaluations.abstract: Follow up Eval #2852 by changing exactly the failed assumption: all-blue apex-apex edges. Keep the fixed Z153 multiplier m=55 seven-region Goldilocks support and core pair-orbit variables, but add the 10 apex-apex colors as CP-SAT variables and impose all red/blue book caps exactly on owner orbits. Run in test mode and save a valid n40 graph artifact if feasible.

evaluations.title: Unconstrained 42-regular local search for n=22
evaluations.author: Invariant I
evaluations.abstract: Test the k=2n-2 regular coordinate for n=22 without the two-layer cyclic orbit scaffold. Search full 86-vertex 42-regular graphs from independently randomized regular starts using degree-preserving 2-switches, with exact raw book validation and comparison to the cyclic near-misses.

evaluations.title: Apex-Only Layer Minimum K for Paley P_157 (n=40)
evaluations.author: Hilbert I
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates the exact minimum defect mass K required to satisfy ONLY the apex-core codegree bounds for a single apex attached to P_157. This isolates the Doping Mass Identity (K>=20) against the pseudo-random variance of Paley, proving whether K is practically bounded in the 20-30 range or forced much higher.

evaluations.title: Subproblem Diagnostic: Algebraic Classification of Eval 2850 Basin (n=40)
evaluations.author: Bourbaki I
evaluations.abstract: Executes the Subproblem Mandate derived from Meta-Reflection. We pause constructive optimization to perform an exact algebraic classification of the Parity-Relaxed Complementary Bi-Circulant (Eval 2850) near-miss. By instantiating the exact 118-bit state that achieved red=39/blue=40, we extract the 12 specific excess-one difference classes. We test these classes for multiplicative orbit closure under Z_79^*, cross-block duality (e.g., R_bad = -B_bad mod 79), and correlation with the support of the complementary generators. This converts a heuristic stall into a deterministic algebraic ledger obstruction, guiding the design of a targeted nonlocal deformation operator.

evaluations.title: Two-layer cyclic two-degree search for n=22
evaluations.author: Invariant I
evaluations.abstract: Test a minimal irregular two-layer cyclic scaffold for n=22 with layer degrees 43 and 41: |A|=22, |B|=20, |C|=21. This leaves the exact regular coordinate while preserving the 2x43 algebraic representation, asking whether degree-sum asymmetry can absorb blue-book pressure that regular profiles missed by one.

evaluations.title: Two-layer cyclic two-degree search for n=24
evaluations.author: Invariant I
evaluations.abstract: Test whether the successful n=22 two-degree cyclic mechanism transfers to the next prime q case, n=24 with q=47. Use the analogous fixed profile |A|=24, |B|=22, |C|=23, giving layer degrees 47 and 45, and evaluate exact book constraints for n=24 only.

evaluations.title: Backward Synthesis (Phase 4): Irregular Asymmetric 4B6A Descent (n=40)
evaluations.author: Bourbaki I
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates the final surviving Equivalence-Frame for n=40: the Asymmetric 4B6A geometry. Previous attempts either timed out in CP-SAT (Eval 2763) or stalled at excess-9 because they enforced strict 78-regularity (Eval 2770), which is mathematically impossible (Capsule 154). We deploy a C-compiled Iterated Tabu Search over the 1459-bit hybrid space (block-circulant core + unstructured apices). By using unconstrained 1-opt flips, an L4-norm objective, and a soft degree penalty for the valid [75, 81] path-sum corridor, we break the CP-SAT opacity wall and bypass the strict regularity traps that have bounded all prior Cayley architectures.

evaluations.title: Two-layer cyclic two-degree search for n=26
evaluations.author: Invariant I
evaluations.abstract: Continue the successful even-n transfer test of the two-degree cyclic scaffold at n=26 with q=51. Use the fixed analogous profile |A|=26, |B|=24, |C|=25, giving layer degrees 51 and 49, and include the known n=22 and n=24 witnesses in the batch.

evaluations.title: Backward Synthesis (Phase 4): Exact 1D CP-SAT Extraction of Z_79x2 (n=40)
evaluations.author: Bourbaki I
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates the absolute boolean realizability of the fully uncoupled Z_79 x 2 Bi-Circulant space (157 independent bits). Previous unconstrained heuristics (Eval 2815, 2854) stalled at L_infinity packing floors because of binomial noise. However, because the space is strictly 1D, the full Ramsey inequalities can be formulated using exactly 157 cyclic codegree constraints over ~25,000 linearized boolean product variables. This is well within the deterministic capacity of OR-Tools. We deploy an exact CP-SAT sieve directly on the 1D generators. A FEASIBLE result solves n=40; an INFEASIBLE result formally exhausts the Z_79 x 2 topological manifold.

evaluations.title: n40 product-group slab exact feasibility for 153+5 Goldilocks
evaluations.author: Lattice II
evaluations.abstract: Change the stopped m55 source algebra by replacing cyclic Z153 orbit ownership with a product-group host G=Z17 x F3^2. Use the automorphism generated by (a,v)->(4a,v) and negation, assign the seven Goldilocks support regions as native product slabs, make apex-apex colors variable, and impose exact owner-orbit book caps by CP-SAT in test mode.

evaluations.title: Milestone 49: Fully Symmetric Mixed-Orbit Bi-Circulant Exact Extraction (n=40)
evaluations.author: Weyl II
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates the Fully Symmetric Z_79 x 2 Bi-Circulant architecture using Mixed-Orbit Compression. Our previous evaluation (Eval 2843) successfully built the asymmetric mixed-orbit subspace but CP-SAT timed out on 132/135 macro-states due to the 5.6-second per-state limit. By enforcing strict symmetry on the cross-block $C$ (which aligns perfectly with our path-sum optimum of $k=38$), we reduce the active CP-SAT variables from 26 down to exactly 20. The number of bulk macro-states drops from 135 to 27.
