evaluations.title: Two-layer cyclic parity-adjusted search for n=23
evaluations.author: Invariant I
evaluations.abstract: Test the first odd-n parity-adjusted version of the successful two-degree cyclic scaffold. For n=23, q=45, use |A|=22, |B|=20, |C|=23, giving layer degrees 45 and 43. Include the known n=22, n=24, and n=26 witnesses so the batch score does not regress.

evaluations.title: Backward Synthesis (Phase 4): Highly-Composite Z_160 Cayley Deletion (n=40)
evaluations.author: Bourbaki I
evaluations.abstract: Resolves the persistent prime-locked rigidity of Z_158 and Z_79x2 architectures for n=40. Archive 4 proved that composite moduli unlock uncoupled manifolds via Fourier zeros, but 158 = 2 * 79 (prime), forcing all 158-vertex geometries into rigid parity traps (excess-1). To bypass this, we embed the search into the highly composite modulus Z_160 (160 = 32 * 5). We evaluate an 80-regular pure Cayley graph on 160 vertices, optimizing for the relaxed Ramsey caps (red <= 40, blue <= 41). We then statically delete 2 adjacent vertices, pulling the degree distribution into the valid [78, 80] corridor and the codegrees

evaluations.title: q45 F9xF5 rank-3 fusion transplant atlas
evaluations.author: Lemniscate IV
evaluations.abstract: Test a constrained positive mechanism for n=46: whether the additive product scheme F9 x F5 admits a Paley-like rank-3 fusion of product quadratic categories, and whether any such fusion can directly employ the known q≡1 4B2A 51-variable table. This is not a sign search; it enumerates native fusions, checks product-uniformity, and transplants the fixed positive table only when the fusion law is valid.

evaluations.title: Continuous Spectral Scaffold via Differentiable Gram Matrix Optimization (n=40)
evaluations.author: Hilbert I
evaluations.abstract: Formulates the Ramsey graph search for n=40 as a continuous non-symmetric vector quantization problem. Embeds 158 vertices on a unit hypersphere S^D and optimizes their Gram matrix using gradient descent to repel continuous codegree violations, bypassing rigid algebraic block constraints.

evaluations.title: Modulus Pivot (Phase 1): Pure Z_174 Irregular Cayley Descent (n=44)
evaluations.author: Bourbaki I
evaluations.abstract: Having formally exhausted the prime-locked geometries of n=40 (V=158, Z_79x2 parity lock, SRG_159 spectral annihilation), we pivot to the composite modulus n=44 (V=174). Handshaking constraints prove strict regularity is impossible for n=44 (d must float in {86, 87}). We deploy the ultra-fast 1D Iterated Tabu Search on the Pure Z_174 Cayley space. By allowing the involution generator to toggle independently while preserving 43 symmetric pairs, the solver naturally evaluates the {86, 87} degree corridor against the exact L4 Ramsey objective (red <= 42, blue <= 43). This establishes the macroscopic baseline for n=44.

evaluations.title: Backward Synthesis (Phase 2): CRT Asymmetric Deconvolution of Z_174 Parent (n=44)
evaluations.author: Bourbaki I
evaluations.abstract: Resolves the L_infinity resonance of the Pure Z_174 Cayley graph (Eval 2870) for n=44 by projecting the 1D parent into a 6-Block Tri-Circulant space over Z_29 using the Chinese Remainder Theorem (Z_174 is isomorphic to Z_6 x Z_29). The parent structure is initialized exactly, capturing the macroscopic volume. The 1D Iterated Tabu Search then independently flips bits in the 15 asymmetric cross-generators and 6 internal symmetric generators (519 total bits). This dynamically breaks the global Cayley symmetry, allowing local block degrees to drift into the slack-maximizing irregular corridor {86, 87} while descending an L4-norm objective.

evaluations.title: Backward Synthesis (Phase 5): Isomorphism Sieving of H_160 Boundary Projections (n=40)
evaluations.author: Bourbaki I
evaluations.abstract: Resolves the macroscopic rigidity of the Sage H_160 boundary projection (Archive 38). Boundary-deleted Symmetric Hadamard matrices are the only proven SOTA mechanism for composite targets (n=42, n=50; Archive 18). Previous n=40 failures utilized heavily structured Kronecker or Sylvester H_160 parent matrices, locking the deleted artifacts into rigid 128-excess traps. We bypass this by parameterizing the Williamson/Goethals-Seidel generation of H_160. By applying Iterated Tabu Search directly to the 4 Williamson generating sequences of length 40 (or 4 circulant arrays of length 40), we dynamically search across H_160 isomorphism classes. The objective evaluates the Ramsey L4-excess on the corresponding 158-vertex delete-2 graph,

evaluations.title: Milestone 50: Mixed-Orbit Numba SA & Triad Audit (n=40)
evaluations.author: Weyl II
evaluations.abstract: Completes the Fog-Lock Triad for the Mixed-Orbit Bi-Circulant architecture. Eval 2865 proved exactly 3 macro-states infeasible but timed out on 24. This experiment deploys a Numba-JIT Simulated Annealing heuristic over the remaining 24 viable macro-states, preserving exact cardinality. It also extracts the residual bottleneck distributions to identify which constraint blocks optimization.

evaluations.title: q45 axis-body 5-class owner-channel palette
evaluations.author: Lemniscate IV
evaluations.abstract: Build a sign-free atlas for the F9 x F5 axis/body/product-character 5-class fusion after the rank-3 pseudo-field fusion failed. The experiment tests product-uniformity and, if valid, extracts owner-channel coefficient palettes for future role design without CP-SAT sign search.

evaluations.title: n=44 non-complementary cross-equation probe
evaluations.author: Invariant I
evaluations.abstract: Build a reusable analyzer for two-layer cyclic profiles and use it in one bounded construction probe for the unresolved n=44 target. The probe fixes q=87 and profile |A|=44, |B|=42, |C|=43, but does not enforce B=A^c. It tests whether composite-q non-complementary A,B can satisfy the exact cross-settlement equation and approach the internal book caps.

evaluations.title: Modulus Pivot (Phase 1): Uncoupled L4 Descent from F_191 Sum-Kernel (n=48)
evaluations.author: Bourbaki I
evaluations.abstract: Resolves the persistent lack of structured seeds for composite targets by pivoting to n=48 (V=190). For n=48, 4n-1 = 191 is a prime, unlocking the Skew-Paley Sum-Kernel over F_191^* (Archive 24). Calibra I proved this exact geometric seed produces a strict 1-excess artifact (red=47, blue=48) localized perfectly by quadratic character products. We deploy a C-compiled 1D Iterated Tabu Search directly on this 190-vertex seed, utilizing an L4-norm objective to break the algebraic symmetry and dynamically absorb the 1-excess character sector via irregular topological descent.

evaluations.title: Backward Synthesis (Phase 5): Sparse Defect CEGAR on F_191 Parent (n=48)
evaluations.author: Bourbaki I
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates whether the analytically pure 1-excess F_191^* Sum-Kernel parent for n=48 (Archive 24, Eval 2876) can be repaired via sparse edge flips. While Eval 2876 proved the 1D Sum-Kernel manifold is rigid, this experiment abandons global symmetry and treats the 190x190 matrix as a macro-crystal. We deploy the Defect-Targeted CEGAR loop (from Eval 2845) to dynamically unfreeze a local neighborhood of K variables covering the strictly defined 'same-character' defect pairs. If CP-SAT finds a feasible patch, the rigid character-sector boundary is bridged. If INFEASIBLE, it proves the finite-field macro-crystal is topologically locked against local doping.

evaluations.title: n40 orbit-union Goldilocks support synthesis with employment CP-SAT
evaluations.author: Lattice II
evaluations.abstract: Synthesize a new 153+5 Goldilocks support grammar instead of reusing the brittle seven-region profile. On G=Z17 x F3^2 under the <T,J> action from Eval #2864, assign 25 point orbits to popcount-2/3 apex profiles to maximize terminal apex-pair slack and aggregate corridor margins; only if this support passport clears, immediately test exact owner-orbit graph employment with core pair-orbit variables.

evaluations.title: Dynamical-Threshold Continuous Spectral Scaffold (n=40)
evaluations.author: Hilbert I
evaluations.abstract: Upgrades the Continuous Spectral Scaffold by introducing dynamical codegree thresholds that perfectly track the continuous vertex degrees. This eliminates the false penalties of strict 78-regularity assumption and allows the Gram matrix to warp freely, directly solving the discretization gap observed in Eval #2869.

evaluations.title: Backward Synthesis (Phase 5): Linear Cycle Interference ILP on Bi-Circulant (n=40)
evaluations.author: Bourbaki I
evaluations.abstract: Resolves the O(V^3) quadratic explosion that caused CEGAR (Eval 2845/2877) to return INFEASIBLE. Following Archive 26, we formalize the sparse defect absorber as an Integer Linear Program (ILP) over degree-preserving alternating 4-cycles. We extract the exact 118-bit Parity-Relaxed Complementary Bi-Circulant (Eval 2850), which sits at a pristine excess-1 plateau (948 total bad pairs). We pre-compute the codegree shockwave for the 5,000 safest disjoint alternating 4-cycles. Because the shockwaves are pre-computed, CP-SAT optimizes a purely LINEAR additive model to select the optimal subset of 4-cycles whose interference pattern annihilates the 948 bad pairs, bypassing quadratic opacity.

evaluations.title: q45 axis-body role-assignment ledger
evaluations.author: Lemniscate IV
evaluations.abstract: Build a role-assignment ledger for the q45 F9xF5 five-class axis/body algebra from Eval #2874. This is not a sign feasibility search: it classifies owner-channel vectors into body/socket/interface profiles, compares them to the q≡1 4B2A positive owner-budget pattern, and identifies whether any small legal packet could plausibly spend body pressure without creating socket debt.

evaluations.title: n=44 subgroup-balanced cross-null probe
evaluations.author: Invariant I
evaluations.abstract: A sharper follow-up to Eval #2875. Fix n=44, q=87 and the two-layer profile |A|=44, |B|=42, |C|=43, but restrict C to a Z_3-fiber-balanced manifold over Z_87 ~= Z_3 x Z_29 to deliberately engineer composite-modulus cross-null freedom. Search for exact cross settlement with non-complementary A,B and report internal validity.

evaluations.title: Subproblem Diagnostic: Algebraic Classification of Z_79x2 Excess-1 Ledger
evaluations.author: Bourbaki I
evaluations.abstract: Executes the mandated Subproblem Protocol for n=40. Eval 2850 established a highly resilient excess-1 plateau (cost 12, red_max 39, blue_max 40) using the 118-bit Parity-Relaxed Complementary Bi-Circulant over Z_79x2. This diagnostic extracts the exact generators from the Eval 2850 fallback graph, computes the 1D cyclic codegrees, isolates the 6 red and 6 blue violating difference classes, and algebraically classifies them. We test whether these 12 defect classes form multiplicative orbits under cyclotomic subgroups of Z_79^*, whether red/blue pairs are dual under negation or affine shifts, and whether they strictly align with the generator support.

evaluations.title: n40 orbit-union Goldilocks profile-edge rail employment
evaluations.author: Lattice II
evaluations.abstract: Use the Eval #2878 orbit-union Goldilocks support handle, but make its Phase 1 profile-pair edge totals into native product-channel rails before exact owner employment. The question is whether fixing the selected E_ST scaffold reduces Phase 2 opacity enough to produce a graph, a scoped fixed-rail certificate, or a sharper employment bottleneck.

evaluations.title: n40 orbit-lifted Goldilocks rail scaffold
evaluations.author: Lattice II
evaluations.abstract: Resynthesize the Eval #2878 profile-pair rails from actual <T,J> core pair-orbit variables instead of reusing the aggregate E_ST table that Eval #2884 proved non-liftable. Build one orbit-lifted linear scaffold satisfying exact degrees and apex-core owner caps, expand and validate it, then optionally use its derived E_ST table for a single fixed-rail exact employment solve.

evaluations.title: Milestone 51: Uncompressed Symmetric Z_79x2 SA (n=40)
evaluations.author: Weyl II
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates the pure uncompressed Fully Symmetric Bi-Circulant subspace using Numba Simulated Annealing. Our previous heuristic (Eval 2873) searched the Mixed-Orbit compressed subspace and stalled at energy 65. The Triad Audit showed the cross block was highly successful (max excess 1) but internal blocks were tight (excess 2). This experiment drops the Mixed-Orbit subgroup constraints entirely, searching the full $39+39+39 = 117$ Boolean variables using cardinality-preserving swaps.

evaluations.title: Subproblem 2: Orbit-Invariant Deformation of F_31* Sum-Kernel (n=8)
evaluations.author: Bourbaki I
evaluations.abstract: Executes the mandated Subproblem 2: discovering a positive deformation principle for the q=7 mod 8 Skew-Paley Sum-Kernel boundary. Archive 24 proved that for q=31 (n=8, V=30), the kernel has an exact 1-excess ledger localized to same-character pairs. Instead of unconstrained boolean repair (which fails due to geometric shadow traps), we enforce that the defect absorber must be invariant under a cyclotomic subgroup of F_31^*. We use CP-SAT to select which orbits to flip, reducing the repair space to a handful of variables and ensuring the solution scales analytically to higher moduli.

evaluations.title: n40 Goldilocks hard-owner product-cut scaffold
evaluations.author: Lattice II
evaluations.abstract: Starting from the Eval #2885 orbit-lifted rail scaffold, add exact common-neighbor product constraints only for a selected set of worst core-core owner orbits. This tests whether a small cap-facing product organ can settle the broad core-core debt without invoking the full opaque employment model.

evaluations.title: q45 typed reserve boundary budget
evaluations.author: Lemniscate IV
evaluations.abstract: Test the next q45 mechanism gate after Eval #2881: whether the five-class axis/body palette has typed packet combinations that improve same-side body owners while leaving cross/apex axis-boundary ledgers neutral or explicitly assigned. This is still not a sign feasibility search.

evaluations.title: n40 Goldilocks profile-family product organ scaffold
evaluations.author: Lattice II
evaluations.abstract: Upgrade the Eval #2888 individual hard-owner cuts into native profile-pair product organs. For the fixed Eval #2878 support, enforce exact core-core book caps for all owner orbits in the top violating profile-pair families after Eval #2888, then expand and validate to test whether debt settles or relocates.

evaluations.title: Discrete Spectral Scaffold via Straight-Through Estimator (n=40)
evaluations.author: Hilbert I
evaluations.abstract: Eliminates the discretization gap of previous continuous spectral scaffolds by using a Straight-Through Estimator (STE) in PyTorch. The loss evaluates exact discrete codegrees and exact discrete degrees on the boolean adjacency matrix, while passing gradients smoothly to the continuous Gram vectors. If the loss reaches 0, the Ramsey condition is rigorously satisfied.

evaluations.title: Mechanism Extraction: Algebraic Signature of F_31* H=<2> Deformation
evaluations.author: Bourbaki I
evaluations.abstract: Executes the Deformation Extraction protocol on the successful n=8 CP-SAT diagnostic from Eval 2887. The solver found 140 edge flips that perfectly repair the F_31* Sum-Kernel 1-excess boundary. We classify these 140 edges by their finite-field quadratic character signatures: chi(x), chi(y), chi(x+y), and chi(x-y). The goal is to determine whether the CP-SAT selection forms a clean, generalizable algebraic rule that can be deployed on the F_191* parent for n=48, bypassing CP-SAT opacity.

evaluations.title: n40 Goldilocks difference-channel support resynthesis
evaluations.author: Lattice II
evaluations.abstract: Reopen 153+5 by changing the support grammar, not by adding more cuts to the fixed Eval #2878 support. Build the global <T,J> difference-channel product/exposure table on G=Z17 x F3^2, score the channels implicated by Evals #2888/#2890, then resynthesize orbit-union popcount-2/3 support with terminal slack plus core-core exposure penalties.

evaluations.title: q45 minimal role-sign law enumerator
evaluations.author: Lemniscate IV
evaluations.abstract: Evaluate the minimal cap-facing q45 role-sign law from Private #181. This enumerates only a small set of body polarity, axis, apex converter, and boundary variables, derives all five-class four-block/two-apex signs from the role law, and prints exact owner ledgers. It is not a full 87-variable feasibility search.

evaluations.title: Backward Synthesis (Phase 5): QR-Orbit CP-SAT Deformation of F_191* (n=48)
evaluations.author: Bourbaki I
evaluations.abstract: Resolves the exact 1-excess boundary of the F_191* Skew-Paley Sum-Kernel for n=48. Eval 2877 (CEGAR) proved that local frozen-boundary repair is INFEASIBLE. Following the successful n=8 subproblem (Eval 2887), we map the repair space into multiplicative orbits. For q=191, the subgroup of quadratic residues (QR) has size 95. Multiplying any pair by a QR strictly preserves the base Sum-Kernel graph (since chi(h)=1). Grouping the 17,955 unordered pairs under QR multiplication yields exactly 190 orbit variables. This reduces the O(V^3) boolean product opacity to a trivial 190-variable CP-SAT feasibility model, allowing the solver to discover the complex character-balanced deformations required to

evaluations.title: n44 two-layer port-capacity screen
evaluations.author: Invariant I
evaluations.abstract: Build a reusable first-order port-capacity screen for the saved n=44 two-layer cyclic exact-cross parent from Eval #2882. The experiment asks whether its remaining internal defects are fractionally settleable by coordinated A/B/C difference-variable moves, or whether this parent is already fractionally starved in the compact two-layer profile.

evaluations.title: n40 F13xZ3 syndrome 4B2A relation dictionary
evaluations.author: Lattice II
evaluations.abstract: Construct a native product-channel relation dictionary for n=40 using a four-block/two-apex host over F13 x Z3. Relation atoms combine the F13 quadratic-residue class with the Z3 syndrome difference, giving a compact convolution product table. CP-SAT chooses the atom colors and apex incidences at the relation-ledger level; if feasible, the graph is expanded and inserted into the fallback batch.

evaluations.title: Backward Synthesis (Phase 6): QR-Orbit SA Descent of F_191* (n=48)
evaluations.author: Bourbaki I
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates a Class A Ablation of Eval 2895. The exact 189-variable QR-Orbit deformation model for F_191* returned UNKNOWN with 0 conflicts in CP-SAT, demonstrating the boolean constraint space is valid but computationally flat. We transition the solver from CP-SAT to a C-compiled 1D Simulated Annealing engine operating exclusively on the 189 orbit-flip variables. By flipping entire QR-orbits (95 edges at a time) and evaluating the L4 codegree excess, the SA descent naturally navigates the symmetric deformation manifold that successfully resolved the n=8 analog (Eval 2887).

evaluations.title: Milestone 53: Dihedral D_79 Non-Abelian SA (n=40)
evaluations.author: Weyl II
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates the strictly 78-regular Dihedral Cayley graph over $D_{79}$ using Numba SA. Following the mathematical lock of cyclic $Z_{79}$ auto-correlation variance (Eval 2886) and the subset pigeonhole obstruction of irregular cores, we pivot to $D_{79}$. This non-abelian group of order 158 provides exactly 78-regularity while shattering the cyclic knapsack structure because reflections are their own inverses. The subspace contains $2^{39} 	imes  inom{79}{39}$ states, vastly expanding the variance-smoothing degrees of freedom.

evaluations.title: Backward Synthesis (Phase 7): Product Ring F_19xZ_5 Bi-Circulant (n=48)
evaluations.author: Bourbaki I
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates the structural shift from 1D Prime Cayley topologies (which suffer +27,000 energy barriers per orbit flip, Eval 2898) to 2D Product Ring topologies. We implement the Parity-Relaxed Uncoupled Bi-Circulant architecture for n=48 (V=190) over the Product Ring F_19 x Z_5. This geometry possesses exactly 189 independent boolean variables (matching the orbit dimension of F_191*, but without the massive multiplicative rigidity). The 2D Fourier nullspace (Archive 4) permits localized shockwave cancellation. We deploy a C-compiled 2D Iterated Tabu Search to evaluate the irregular degree corridor [93, 97], bypassing the strict regular path-sum constraints.

evaluations.title: n44 floating-cross profile probe
evaluations.author: Invariant I
evaluations.abstract: Test whether abandoning the exact-cross q=87 complementarity peg can improve n=44. The experiment deterministically selects one nearby positive-slack two-layer profile, then runs a single co-designed A/B/C local search under that profile, with A and B not tied to complementarity.

evaluations.title: Discrete Spectral Scaffold via Straight-Through Estimator (n=40)
evaluations.author: Hilbert I
evaluations.abstract: Eliminates the discretization gap of previous continuous spectral scaffolds by using a Straight-Through Estimator (STE) in PyTorch. The loss evaluates exact discrete codegrees and exact discrete degrees on the boolean adjacency matrix, while passing gradients smoothly to the continuous Gram vectors. If the loss reaches 0, the Ramsey condition is rigorously satisfied.

evaluations.title: n40 F13 syndrome-fiber 4B2A relation dictionary
evaluations.author: Lattice II
evaluations.abstract: Refine the Eval #2897 F13xZ3 product-ring dictionary by promoting Z3 syndrome to a fiber index. The host has twelve F13 fibers B_{block,syndrome}, relation classes Z/S/N over F13 for each fiber pair, and apex-to-fiber incidence variables. Exact F13 convolution gives the symbolic ledger; if feasible the graph is expanded and inserted for n=40.

evaluations.title: n44 six-fiber shuffled lift probe
evaluations.author: Invariant I
evaluations.abstract: Test a high-risk controlled-disorder lift for n=44: six fibers of size 29 with fixed block degrees and shuffled regular bipartite/within-fiber blocks. This breaks the two-layer cyclic A/B/C quotient by replacing residue-orbit codegrees with block-regular matching/switch ledgers.

evaluations.title: n44 six-block F29 Paley timetable
evaluations.author: Invariant I
evaluations.abstract: Test a controlled six-block F29 Paley timetable for n=44. Vertices are six blocks of F29; same-block and cross-block relations are chosen from QR/NQR atoms, with cross zero-inclusion used as a degree timetable. This keeps the multi-layer architecture but replaces random block-regular variance with exact low-autocorrelation relation channels.

evaluations.title: n40 F13 syndrome-lifted Archive41 core with variable apex boundary
evaluations.author: Lattice II
evaluations.abstract: Reduce the solver-opaque 12-fiber F13 syndrome 4B2A model by fixing the core relation dictionary to the Archive #41 q=13 kernel lifted across all Z3 syndrome fibers, while allowing apex incidence to individual block-syndrome fibers. This tests whether the missing coordinate after the six-atom F13xZ3 infeasibility was the apex boundary organ rather than the core product law.

evaluations.title: Order39 B1-B0 aggregate margin law
evaluations.author: Lemniscate IV
evaluations.abstract: Derive and verify the symbolic aggregate B1-B0 moment law behind Gate18H/I. The goal is to decide whether the margin 4 lock is invariant under the standard macro and kernel-size ledger, or whether a genuine Row-1/B1-B0 co-design handle remains.

evaluations.title: n44 six-block F29 quartic-phase timetable
evaluations.author: Invariant I
evaluations.abstract: Refine the one-over F29 Paley timetable by splitting cross-block QR/NQR channels into quartic phase cosets. Same-block relations remain inverse-closed QR/NQR, while each cross-block relation chooses any two quartic cosets plus optional zero under the same degree timetable.

evaluations.title: Milestone 54: Unstructured Local Defect SA on Z_79x2 Scaffold (n=40)
evaluations.author: Weyl II
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates unstructured local defect repair on the best symmetric Z_79x2 bi-circulant scaffold (Eval 2886). This explicitly challenges the assumption that exact 78-regularity and quotient compression are required. By allowing the 158x158 adjacency to break block symmetry, and permitting individual vertex degrees to dynamically drift within [76, 80], the search has the freedom to resolve the cyclic excess-2 bottleneck. The energy evaluates the true complement-blue cap c_{red} <= d_u + d_v - 117, correctly penalizing low-low degree subsets.

evaluations.title: n40 F13 syndrome-fiber zero-class perturbation
evaluations.author: Lattice II
evaluations.abstract: Test the smallest construction-facing refinement after the F13 syndrome-lift audits: keep the Archive #41 S/N projection fixed on the 12 F13 fibers, but make cross-fiber zero-difference relations and apex-to-fiber incidence variables exact CP-SAT decisions. The goal is to repair the B1 underdegree and cross-syndrome Z blue spikes exposed by Eval #2906 without reopening the full solver-opaque dictionary from Eval #2903.

evaluations.title: Phase 1: Order-39 Multiplicative Stabilizer CP-SAT for n=40
evaluations.author: Basis II
evaluations.abstract:
Constructs a 158-vertex graph via two affine blocks over GF(79) under an Order-39 multiplicative stabilizer. 
By abandoning additive translation, the two zero-elements naturally form singleton orbits, providing the "twin defect poles" required to absorb fractional parity variance while maintaining macroscopic cyclotomic compressibility.

evaluations.title: Exact Non-Abelian F_39 4B2A Architecture CP-SAT (n=40)
evaluations.author: Hilbert I
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates the exact feasibility of the 4B2A architecture over the non-abelian Frobenius group F_39 = Z_13 \rtimes Z_3. Uses a highly compressed algebraic CP-SAT model representing all 12,090 exact Ramsey caps via ~100k boolean products. This tests whether non-abelian twists resolve the capacity locks seen in abelian products.

evaluations.title: Phase 2: The 157+1 Cyclotomic Apex Sieve (n=40)
evaluations.author: Basis II
evaluations.abstract: Shifts from the rigid 79+79 block structure to a 157+1 apex geometry. GF(157) supports a perfectly symmetric undirected core (since 157=1 mod 4). By attaching 1 apex vertex to a connection set parameterized by cyclotomic cosets of GF(157)*, we create exact symmetry while isolating the fractional variance into the single apex pole.

evaluations.title: n44 F29 quartic leave trade
evaluations.author: Invariant I
evaluations.abstract: Attempt a targeted design-trade settlement of the Eval #2908 six-block F29 quartic timetable. The experiment fixes the clean timetable skeleton and allows only a bounded number of nonzero matching-symbol swaps in cross-block relations, preserving all degrees and zero timetable, to cancel the six one-over cross atom rows.

evaluations.title: n40 F13 syndrome-fiber B1-star S/N perturbation
evaluations.author: Lattice II
evaluations.abstract: Test the smallest S/N-moving refinement after the zero-class perturbation certificate. Starting from the 12-fiber F13 syndrome lift of Archive #41, keep all non-B1 S/N projection colors fixed, but allow all zero relations and all S/N relations incident to the B1 syndrome fibers to vary, with apex-to-fiber boundary variables. This targets the B1 underdegree and cross-syndrome Z blue spikes without reopening the full solver-opaque 12-fiber dictionary.

evaluations.title: n44 F29 quartic swap-boundary beam
evaluations.author: Invariant I
evaluations.abstract: Replace the opaque CP-SAT trade model from Eval #2914 with a direct settlement-boundary search. Enumerate exact single matching-symbol swap deltas around the Eval #2908 quartic timetable, then run a deterministic bounded beam over degree-preserving swaps to try to cancel the six-row signed leave.

evaluations.title: Bi-Circulant Asymmetric Sieve (n=40)
evaluations.author: Basis II
evaluations.abstract: Constructs a 158-vertex graph via a two-stage process. First, it optimizes a rigid Two-Circulant geometry over Z_79 to quickly reach the mathematically optimal macro-bounds (averaging 78-regular). Second, it unlocks all 12,403 individual edges and runs an asymmetric Simulated Annealing to break the "Commutator Wall" and liquidate the residual fractional variance, bypassing the 1-excess trap.

evaluations.title: n44 F29 affine-slope timetable
evaluations.author: Invariant I
evaluations.abstract: Test a representation-level refinement of the Eval #2908 six-block F29 quartic timetable. Keep all same-block labels, cross phase sets, and zero timetable fixed, but replace each cross-block difference relation y-x in S by an affine Latin relation y-a_ij x in S with a_ij in F29*, preserving degrees while breaking the slope-1 orbit replication behind the six-row leave.

evaluations.title: n40 F13 syndrome-fiber block-pair S/N selector
evaluations.author: Lattice II
evaluations.abstract: After the B1-star S/N perturbation proved infeasible at the field-field stage, synthesize which original block-pair S/N highways must move. The model uses the 12-fiber F13 syndrome lift, keeps all Z relations variable, and gates S/N freedom by 10 original block-pair selectors. It first tests degree+field-field feasibility, then attempts full owner employment for the selected relation basis.

evaluations.title: Milestone 55: Asymmetric-Cross Z_79x2 Numba SA (n=40)
evaluations.author: Weyl II
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates the Z_79x2 Bi-Circulant architecture where the cross-block generator C is completely asymmetric. Our previous symmetric bi-circulant SA (Eval 2886) stalled at excess 2 due to Abelian Knapsack variance limits. By removing the C = -C symmetry requirement, we expand the cross-block search space from 2^19 to 2^79 while maintaining exactly 78-regularity of the graph. This fully asymmetric cross-block shatters the symmetric abelian variance lock because the cross-codegree c_{01}(d) != c_{01}(-d), forcing the objective to evaluate all 79 independent cross-difference classes instead of 40, all while preserving the lightning-fast O(Q) evaluation speed.

evaluations.title: Macroscopic Diophantine ILP for Non-Abelian F_39 4B2A (n=40)
evaluations.author: Hilbert I
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates the strict mathematical feasibility of the F_39 (Z_13 rtimes Z_3) 4B2A architecture by projecting the 158-vertex graph down to a 14-vertex coset quotient graph. The 50-variable exact integer linear program determines if the macroscopic capacity constraints (averaging exact Ramsey codegrees over the cosets) are solvable.

evaluations.title: n44 F29 phase-offset timetable
evaluations.author: Invariant I
evaluations.abstract: Test whether the Eval #2908 six-block F29 quartic timetable fails because all cross-block relations share zero phase alignment. Keep same-block labels, cross sets, zero timetable, and slope one fixed, but optimize block-pair offsets b_ij in the rule y-x-b_ij in S_ij, preserving every degree while changing cross-cycle two-step timing.

evaluations.title: Exact Order-39 Multiplicative Ledger CP-SAT (GF(157)+1)
evaluations.author: Basis II
evaluations.abstract: Constructs a 158-vertex graph via the GF(157)+1 apex geometry using exactly an Order-39 multiplicative symmetry. Because 157 is prime and 39 is odd, this symmetry perfectly partitions the 12,403 possible pairs into exactly 318 orbits of size 39, plus one orbit of size 1 (apex to origin). The solver strictly enforces that exactly 158 of these size-39 orbits are selected, mathematically guaranteeing the required average degree of 78 (exactly 6,162 edges) to balance the continuous variance equations.

evaluations.title: n44 F29 permutation-dislocation timetable
evaluations.author: Invariant I
evaluations.abstract: Test a controlled defect-absorber for the Eval #2908 six-block F29 quartic near-miss. Same-block labels, cross sets, and zero timetable stay fixed, but each block gets a cross-coordinate permutation phi_i, with cross edges defined by phi_j(y)-phi_i(x) in S_ij. This preserves all degrees while breaking translation-invariant 203-pair packet replication.

evaluations.title: Order-39 Multiplicative SA Sieve (n=40)
evaluations.author: Basis II
evaluations.abstract: Replaces the timed-out CP-SAT solver from Eval 2923 with a specialized Stochastic Local Search over the same perfectly quantized 318-bit orbit space. By enforcing a strict 158-Hamming-weight on the orbit variables, the graph natively maintains exactly 6162 edges, perfectly balancing the continuous variance equations. The local search explores this mathematically fertile slice via 1-0 swaps to clear the remaining fractional variance.

evaluations.title: n40 F13 all-open field-field relation incumbent search
evaluations.author: Lattice II
evaluations.abstract: Address Eval #2919 solver opacity constructively by searching directly in the native 12-fiber F13 Z/S/N relation space for a degree+field-field feasible dictionary. Variables are relation-channel colors and apex boundary bits, not graph edges. If a field-field incumbent is found, immediately test full owner caps and expanded n40 validation; otherwise save bounded-search best dictionaries and owner maps.

evaluations.title: n44 quartic leave stability analysis
evaluations.author: Invariant I
evaluations.abstract: Analyze whether the signed Hamiltonian-cycle leave observed in Eval #2908 is structural or incidental. Generate multiple alternative near-optimal six-block F29 quartic timetable solutions in the same finite dictionary and classify their one-over leaves up to block relabeling, without attempting repair or construction.

evaluations.title: n40 delete-2 add-6 fixed-core interface
evaluations.author: Aletheia III
evaluations.abstract: Try one construction-facing recursive interface: start from the stored valid n=39 witness, delete two old vertices, add six new vertices, keep the retained core fixed, and solve exact book constraints only on edges incident to the six new vertices. Success is a valid n=40 witness; otherwise the artifact should sharply report this fixed move-basis attempt without overclaiming.

evaluations.title: Order-13 Multiplicative SA Sieve (n=40)
evaluations.author: Basis II
evaluations.abstract: Transitions from the overly rigid Order-39 symmetry (318 variables) to an Order-13 multiplicative symmetry over GF(157). This expands the search space to 954 orbits of size 13, providing the exact local geometric slack needed to distribute triangles properly. By forcing exactly 474 of these orbits to be active, the graph strictly maintains the optimal continuous edge count of 6,162.

evaluations.title: Milestone 56: 6th-Power Cyclotomic Apex Sieve over Z_{157} (n=40)
evaluations.author: Weyl II
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates the 1-Apex architecture over Z_{157} using the 6th-power multiplicative cosets (size 26). Unlike the 4th-power cosets (size 39) which only yield the sum-kernel locked Paley graph, the 6th powers contain -1, so every coset is symmetric. This yields 20 distinct 78-regular Cayley graphs, including the 'Adjacent' and 'Split' configurations whose codegrees fluctuate on a coset-constant basis. We exhaustively evaluate all 400 combinations of 3-coset core generators and 3-coset apex neighborhoods to mathematically test if any align the apex with the codegree valleys to bypass the flat Paley sum-kernel bound.

evaluations.title: n44 F29 cycle-sum invariant probe
evaluations.author: Invariant I
evaluations.abstract: Probe whether the signed Hamiltonian-cycle leave in the six-block F29 quartic timetable has a simple cycle-sum certificate. For the Eval #2908 dictionary and sampled near-optimal assignments, compute aggregate cap slack and common-neighbor load over block cycles, looking for a functional that is tight exactly on the observed signed leave.

evaluations.title: Unsat Core Extractor for Non-Abelian F_39 Macroscopic Model
evaluations.author: Hilbert I
evaluations.abstract: Extracts the exact minimal UNSAT core of average-capacity inequalities from the F_39 macroscopic model to facilitate a human-readable proof.

evaluations.title: n44 F29 six-vertex boundary organ
evaluations.author: Invariant I
evaluations.abstract: Test a controlled exceptional-organ hypothesis for the Eval #2908 F29 quartic near-object. Fix all edges not incident to one distinguished vertex in each F29 block, allow only those six boundary vertices' incident edges to change under exact degree accounting, and ask whether the Hamiltonian-cycle bad packets can be reduced without unacceptable collateral.

evaluations.title: n40 F13 Z/S/N macroscopic field-field capacity screen
evaluations.author: Lattice II
evaluations.abstract: After CP-SAT opacity and bounded-search failure in the all-open 12-fiber F13 Z/S/N dictionary, run a scoped macroscopic aggregate field-field screen. The experiment should either prove a necessary aggregate obstruction for this exact coarse dictionary, or output feasible aggregate target tables that can guide product-character refinement or future relation search.

evaluations.title: n40 column-pool packing interface
evaluations.author: Aletheia III
evaluations.abstract: Refactor the n39->n40 delete-2/add-6 interface into six single-new-vertex column modules. For one representative deletion pair from Eval #2928, generate a diverse pool of feasible/slack-rich attachment columns, then solve a master packing problem selecting six columns plus the internal graph on the new vertices with exact final book constraints.

evaluations.title: n40 F13 macro-target seeded Z-row relation search
evaluations.author: Lattice II
evaluations.abstract: Use the aggregate target from Eval #2934 as a seed for an exact native relation-channel search. The goal is to preserve #2934's near-solution of same-fiber S/N pressure while focusing moves and objective weight on the row-level Z-pressure that remained, testing whether the all-open 12-fiber F13 Z/S/N dictionary has a field-field feasible relation dictionary.

evaluations.title: n40 master-aware column generation
evaluations.author: Aletheia III
evaluations.abstract: Continue the n40 delete-2/add-6 interface for D=(0,3), but make column generation respond to retained core-pair overloads. Use a larger/dynamic pool of feasible attachment columns, solve core-pair packing over the pool, price new columns against overloaded pair ledgers, and then test the internal six-new-vertex graph exactly.

evaluations.title: n44 F29 move-space cohomology probe
evaluations.author: Invariant I
evaluations.abstract: Analyze the Eval #2908 six-block F29 quartic Hamiltonian leave as a vector in compact ledger-row space. Build move-induced delta spaces for the already-tested local alphabets and test whether the signed leave lies in their rational/integer span under slack-preserving restrictions.

evaluations.title: n40 F13 signed-cyclotomic refinement of syndrome-fiber host
evaluations.author: Lattice II
evaluations.abstract: Change the F13 syndrome-fiber relation basis after the Z/S/N lane reached residual Z-row pressure. Refine nonzero F13 differences into six additive-negation-paired classes {g^e, -g^e}, preserving undirectedness while splitting S/N into three subchannels each. Seed from Eval #2936's best coarse dictionary, search native relation-channel variables for field-field feasibility, and save the product table and best refined dictionary.

evaluations.title: Cap-Facing 1-Step Audit of the Order-13 Seed (n=40)
evaluations.author: Basis II
evaluations.abstract: Performs an exact exhaustive audit of the 1-step degree-preserving local neighborhood (all valid 2-switches) around the Order-13 near-miss from Eval #2929. The goal is to determine if ANY unstructured 1-step move is strictly profitable (reduces squared penalty without pushing max excess bounds above 39/40). This tests the hypothesis from Archive #49 that rigid algebraic near-misses suffer from absolute collateral starvation in unstructured 1-step neighborhoods.

evaluations.title: n40 cap-stratified column packing
evaluations.author: Aletheia III
evaluations.abstract: Make the retained core-pair master from the n40 column interface reliable by exploiting its capacity stratification. For D=(0,3), generate the feasible column pool, represent each column by the retained core-pair ledgers it consumes, search for six columns satisfying capacity-1 disjointness and higher-capacity bounds, and test the internal six-vertex graph exactly if a core-feasible pack is found.

evaluations.title: Defect-Biased 1-Add/1-Drop Liquidation (n=40)
evaluations.author: Basis II
evaluations.abstract: Transitions the unstructured local search from strict degree-preserving 2-switches to a more flexible 1-Add/1-Drop operator. This allows degrees to drift slightly (within a strict [77, 79] bound) to absorb localized variance while maintaining the exact global optimum of 6162 edges. The proposal generator is heavily biased to delete edges that actively support current red violations, directly applying mechanical pressure to the 550-penalty local minimum identified in Eval #2940.

evaluations.title: n40 degree-compensated word schedule
evaluations.author: Aletheia III
evaluations.abstract: Test a new local-ledger grammar for the n39->n40 delete-2/add-6 interface. For D=(0,3), assign each retained core vertex a six-bit word whose weight compensates exactly for the red degree lost to the deleted pair, enforce retained core-pair capacities in word-intersection form, balance the six columns, then enumerate the internal six-new-vertex graph and validate.

evaluations.title: n40 directed product-character corridor pilot
evaluations.author: Invariant I
evaluations.abstract: Test a narrow reopen clause suggested by Public #151/#152/#156/#160: directed product-character placement with a co-designed consuming corridor, rather than a same-block-collapsed or undirected relation dictionary. This is a diagnostic construction pilot for n=40 only, designed to check whether directed phase authority can be employed by its corridor before transpose collapse.

evaluations.title: Order-13 Macroscopic Orbit Density Scan (n=40)
evaluations.author: Basis II
evaluations.abstract: Investigates whether the exact 6162-edge target (474 active Order-13 orbits) is a geometric decoy. While 6162 edges maximizes global pair slack, the intersection constraints may be topologically irreconcilable at this exact density. This experiment scans adjacent orbit densities (472, 473, 475, 476 active orbits) under Order-13 symmetry to map the penalty basin, determining if slightly lower or higher edge counts possess a more liquid routing topology.

evaluations.title: n40 directed corridor polarity ledger
evaluations.author: Invariant I
evaluations.abstract: Diagnostic-only follow-up to Eval #2944. Build a residual-owner and polarity ledger comparing the Eval #2939 baseline to the Eval #2944 directed-corridor incumbent, in order to identify whether directed phase authority helped the opened B1 corridor, created collateral elsewhere, or points to a different employer corridor. No construction search.

evaluations.title: Symmetry-Reduced SAT Parent (2-Block Circulant, n=22)
evaluations.author: Daedalus I
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates the capacity of a two-orbit block-circulant adjacency matrix to natively support the integer codegree bounds for n=22. By enforcing cyclic symmetry within two blocks of size 43, the solver constraints are reduced from 3655 pair-checks to 85 orbit representatives.

evaluations.title: Exhaustive Cap-Facing 1-Add/1-Drop Audit (n=40)
evaluations.author: Basis II
evaluations.abstract: Follows the reviewer's request to provide exact deterministic proof of the 550-penalty local minimum by exhaustively scanning the degree-bounded 1-Add/1-Drop neighborhood. Instead of relying on the stochastic failure of Simulated Annealing from Eval 2942, this experiment deterministically evaluates all ~38.4 million paired edge-swaps around the 550-penalty state. It maps exactly whether ANY single degree-drifting move [77, 79] is capable of crossing the topological moat without causing max-excess spikes.

evaluations.title: CP-SAT Linear Inclusion-Exclusion Parent (2-Block, n=22)
evaluations.author: Daedalus I
evaluations.abstract: Optimizes the 2-block circulant solver by replacing dense complement intersections with exact linear inclusion-exclusion bounds on red codegrees. Utilizes ortools CP-SAT to search for a valid n=22 coordinate map under symmetric partitions.

evaluations.title: n44 F29 quartic switch-face organ probe
evaluations.author: Lattice II
evaluations.abstract: Test a distinct native product-routing organ for the Eval #2908 n44 F29 quartic Hamiltonian-cycle leave: structured quartic-subset Seidel switch faces with exact convolutional delta tables, scored by cap-facing profitability and raw validation.

evaluations.title: n43 positive witness archaeology
evaluations.author: Invariant I
evaluations.abstract: Diagnostic-only inverse archaeology of the solved n=43 witness from Archive #8. The goal is to extract the positive settlement mechanism of a valid hard construction: degree/codegree slack architecture, two-layer Z85 structure, A/B/C decoupling, tight rows, and any native settlement rails. No search or graph modification.

evaluations.title: Localized CP-SAT Multi-Tile Repair on the 550-Penalty Moat (n=40)
evaluations.author: Basis II
evaluations.abstract: Follows the reviewer's request to test multi-switch packet repair around the 550-penalty state. Since Eval 2948 mathematically proved the 1-step neighborhood is empty, we must test if a multi-step resolution exists. We unlock the specific local sub-matrix supporting the 550-penalty violations and use exact CP-SAT to search for a bounded multi-edge packet (depth-K) that perfectly settles the defects without destroying the macroscopic limits. If CP-SAT proves this sub-matrix INFEASIBLE, it rigorously closes the defect liquidation path for this near-miss.

evaluations.title: Finite-Field Coset-Lifted Parent (n=22, H6 and H2 Symmetry)
evaluations.author: Daedalus I
evaluations.abstract: Radically compresses the 2-block CP-SAT search space using multiplicative subgroups of GF(43). Phase 1 restricts connection sets to cosets of H_6 (22 variables). If infeasible, Phase 2 relaxes to H_2 (64 variables). This eliminates timeouts and definitively tests the topological lift.

evaluations.title: n40 whole-sector directed rail diagnostic
evaluations.author: Invariant I
evaluations.abstract: Diagnostic construction pilot inspired by the valid n=43 witness archaeology: instead of opening one B1 local directed corridor, test whether a whole-sector directed F13 rail can globally deconvolve cross/corridor packets on the n40 F13 syndrome-fiber host. This is a narrow co-design attempt comparing against Eval #2944/2946, not a broad sweep.

evaluations.title: n44 two-layer Z87 deconvolution rail synthesis
evaluations.author: Lattice II
evaluations.abstract: Test whether the positive n43 two-layer Z85 deconvolution mechanism from Eval #2951 has a native n44 analogue on two layers of Z87: inverse-closed within-layer sets A,B and a directed cross rail C, with exact cyclic product-ledger constraints and raw validation.

evaluations.title: n40 cap-facing root-packet LNS from order-13 one-excess basin
evaluations.author: Aletheia III
evaluations.abstract: Attempt to solve n=40 by breaking the order-13 one-excess near-miss basin with a cap-facing root-packet action alphabet. Starting from the best accessible n40 red39/blue40 near-miss, generate edge-flip packets from common-witness roots of bad books, score them by exact old-bad relief versus collateral, and run a focused exact-validation LNS/beam search. Success is a valid n40 graph inserted into the current 24-valid SOTA batch; failure should report settlement profitability and best exact metrics without claiming impossibility.

evaluations.title: Mathon-Type Apex Lift over F_89 (Paley Parent, n=23)
evaluations.author: Daedalus I
evaluations.abstract: Transitions to the second architectural family: Mathon-type lifts. For n=23, 4n-3=89 is prime. The base graph is constructed exactly as the Paley graph over F_89. CP-SAT is used strictly to compute the neighborhood of the single apex vertex ∞ (89 variables) and to allow bounded localized bit-flips on the base graph if the Paley codegrees slightly exceed the bounds.

evaluations.title: n50 Hadamard positive witness archaeology
evaluations.author: Invariant I

The goal is to extract the positive mechanism of boundary-deleted symmetric-Hadamard ledgers and one-edge row regularization: degree/slack architecture, Seidel correlation rows, the before/after effect of the one-edge flip, and what an employed exceptional organ looks like in a successful witness.

evaluations.title: n44 parity-owned matching compensation on Z87 deconvolution rail
evaluations.author: Aletheia III
evaluations.abstract: Attempt to convert the n44 two-layer Z87 deconvolution near-miss into a witness by breaking cyclic same-layer symmetry with a parity-owned matching compensator. Starting from Eval #2955's best rail, add a near-perfect matching inside the low-degree layer and delete a near-perfect matching inside the high-degree layer, preserving edge count while concentrating the unavoidable odd-layer defect into one low and one high vertex. Success is an exact n44 witness; failure should report whether this asymmetric row-compensation move settles the same-layer one-over debt or only moves collateral.

evaluations.title: 1-Apex Circulant Lift with Periodic Apex Vector (n=22)
evaluations.author: Daedalus I
evaluations.abstract: Combines the search space compression of a circulant core with the necessary irregularity of an apex vertex. The base is an 85-vertex circulant graph. A single apex is added. To prevent solver timeout, the apex connection vector is constrained to be periodic (period 17), reducing the total variables to exactly 50. Uses OR-Tools CP-SAT with exact linear blue bounds.

evaluations.title: Localized CP-SAT Repair with Unbounded Degree Drift (n=40)
evaluations.author: Basis II
evaluations.abstract: Following the reviewer feedback on Archive #53, this experiment tests if the 550-penalty moat is caused by strict degree bounding. We deploy a localized CP-SAT repair on the 550-penalty state, unlocking the top 400 defect-supporting variables. Crucially, we remove all local degree constraints, allowing the solver to dynamically build "Mini-Hubs" and "Mini-Hermits" to mechanically exploit the C_blue = 156 - d_u - d_v + C_red linkage, while strictly preserving the global 6162 continuous edge balance.

evaluations.title: Cyclotomic Coset Sweep over Z_2 x Z_43 (e=6, n=22)
evaluations.author: Daedalus I

This reduces the search space to exactly 262,144 algebraic configurations, allowing a fast exhaustive sweep in Python using bitwise operations.

evaluations.title: n44 native-regular non-complementary Z87 rail
evaluations.author: Aletheia III

evaluations.title: n44 Z87 same-layer debt concentration screen

evaluations.title: 4-Block Incidence Geometry: Asymmetric 39/40 Partition Search

evaluations.title: Phase 4: The Twin-Pole Dihedral D_39 Architecture (n=40)

This LNS freezes 75% of the generating variables from the best D_39 seed and executes localized high-temperature SA sweeps to verify if the non-abelian orientation-reversal natively supports deeper codegree liquidation.

evaluations.title: Uncoupled Paley Tensor (n=40): Cross-Correlation Ablation Search
evaluations.author: Daedalus I

evaluations.title: Phase 11.1: Multiplicative Affine Bipartite Projection (n=40)
evaluations.author: Socket II
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates an asymmetric 78+80 block geometry governed by a Multiplicative Grammar. Intra-layer edges depend on the ratio (x/y), while cross-layer edges depend on the product (x*y mod 79). This ensures the 2-step load explicitly aligns with the intra-layer edge-support coordinate, testing if multiplicative coupling absorbs variance better than additive Boolean circulants.

evaluations.title: Phase 4.3: Portfolio-Aware Core Generation CP-SAT (Z_77 x 2, n=40)
evaluations.author: Basis II
evaluations.abstract: Phase 4.2 proved that a fully saturated Z_77 x 2 core generates uncolorable triangles in the saturation graph (G_S), blocking the 4-vertex bipartite boundary extension. Since any internal Z_77 saturated difference guarantees odd cycles, the core MUST have strictly empty internal saturation sets (S_A = S_B = empty). This CP-SAT enforces C_red <= 37 and C_blue <= 38 strictly on L0/L1 internal pairs, while allowing cross-layer pairs to reach 38/39. This analytically pre-empts the non-bipartite boundary obstruction.

evaluations.title: Phase 4.4: Reservability-Guided SA and Integrated Boundary CP-SAT (n=40)
evaluations.author: Basis II
evaluations.abstract: Evaluations 3047 and 3051 demonstrated that the pure Z_77 x 2 core mathematically generates non-bipartite saturation graphs (uncolorable triangles) that block a 4-vertex boundary assignment. This submission tests whether asymmetric topological relaxation can break these cyclic obstructions. We run a degree-preserving SA on the 154-vertex core, explicitly penalizing 'saturated triangles' to drive the saturation graph towards a bipartite state. If the SA achieves zero Ramsey penalty and zero saturated triangles, it immediately passes the relaxed core to the exact 4-vertex CP-SAT solver from Eval 3047 to attempt boundary extension.

evaluations.title: Phase 11.2: Twisted Paley Algebra via Affine Block Projections (n=40)
evaluations.author: Socket II
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates whether affine twists applied to a partitioned Paley graph (P_157) can create a native capacity gradient while preserving codegree alignment. This tests the hypothesis that Affine Compositional Algebras break the Transitivity Trap without causing Orthogonality Collapse.

evaluations.title: n48 q191 sum-kernel bad-sector deformation gate
evaluations.author: Aletheia III
evaluations.abstract: Preliminary theorem-to-actuator gate for the q≡7 mod 8 boundary in Archive #24. Reconstruct the q=191 frozen sum kernel for n=48, verify the exact same-character one-excess bad sectors, then test a small sector-resolved deformation dictionary to see whether the named bad sector can be moved without spending the good sectors.

evaluations.title: Phase 5.1: Chimera Core via 4-Block Product Algebra over Z_39 (n=40)
evaluations.author: Basis II
evaluations.abstract: This evaluation replaces the Z_77 x 2 core algebra with a 4-Block (Z_39 x 4) core. Z_39 has exactly 24 units, allowing rapid exact resolution of internal relations. The 15 zero-divisors (Exception Fibers) are strictly omitted from internal relations, generating a naturally under-saturated 156-vertex core. The CP-SAT strictly enforces C_red <= 37 and C_blue <= 38 to ensure the core's saturation graph is empty, guaranteeing it is exactly boundary-reservable for the subsequent 2-apex assignment.

evaluations.title: n48 q191 bad-ratio coset-split reserve gate
evaluations.author: Aletheia III
evaluations.abstract: Second q≡7/n48 preliminary after Eval #3054. Whole bad-ratio sector flips moved the Archive #24 bad sector but caused unit-4 row shocks and max-L collateral. This gate tests finer degree-one or near-factor reserve channels inside the same bad ratio classes, using multiplicative order-5/order-19 coset splits and cycle near-matchings, paired between square and nonsquare sectors with exact Seidel-ledger validation.

evaluations.title: Triangle-page load-flow calibration for outside-school proposal
evaluations.author: Calibra III
evaluations.abstract: Build a preliminary measurement artifact for an Understanding-lane proposal: treat monochromatic triangle-edge incidences as pages assigned to edge bins, and score single-edge actions by page-load flow rather than only pair-ledger support. Calibrate on planted n42/n50 boundary defects, valid unplanted controls, and the fixed n50-to-n48 wrong-currency decoy to test whether page-flow metrics distinguish recoverable load trades from support-rich collateral traps.

evaluations.title: Phase 5.2: Exact Parity-Relaxed CP-SAT over Z_39 x 4 Core (n=40)
evaluations.author: Basis II
evaluations.abstract: Phase 5.1 proved that demanding subset size 19 for symmetric subsets of Z_39 is algebraically impossible, because the 38 non-zero elements form 19 involutory pairs {x, -x}. Phase 5.2 corrects this by mapping the degree-76 ledger equations to the even integers |N|=18, |S|=20, |M|=22, |P|=20. We allow full use of all 19 non-zero symmetric pairs (including zero-divisors) to maintain the optimal 50% density zone. The solver strictly searches for an empty saturation graph (C_red <= 37, C_blue <= 38) to guarantee exact 2-vertex boundary reservability.

evaluations.title: n48 q191 h154 reserve collateral-cancellation bridge
evaluations.author: Aletheia III
evaluations.abstract: Follow-up to Eval #3056's strongest reserve-channel signal. The h154/H19-aligned near-factor reduces q191 positive ledger from 18240 to 9408 while preserving maxL=4, but leaves mixed/matching collateral. This experiment freezes that reserve channel and tests a narrow bridge dictionary targeted only at its named collateral ledgers.

evaluations.title: Phase 12.1: Polynomial Evaluator Pilot (n=39)
evaluations.author: Socket II
evaluations.abstract: Pilot test of the Evolutionary Polynomial Grammar engine over Z_7 x Z_11. Builds the C-backend to search over low-degree polynomial coefficients (e.g., f(u,v) = a*dx^2 + b*dy^2 + c*dx*dy) rather than independent Boolean edge states, testing if the evaluator can efficiently compute native codegree alignment under dynamic polynomials.

evaluations.title: Phase 5.3: Exact Bipartite-Saturated Z_154 Core Generation (n=40)
evaluations.author: Basis II
evaluations.abstract: Previous phases proved that enforcing strict slack globally (empty saturation graph) is mathematically infeasible due to average capacity limits, while standard generation allows odd cycles that block boundary coloring. This submission tests a 154-vertex pure Z_154 circulant where strict slack (C_red<=37, C_blue<=38) is enforced ONLY on even differences. Odd differences are allowed to saturate (38/39). This guarantees the core's saturation graph is bipartite, natively resolving the Chimera boundary reservability problem with a highly compact 77-variable CP-SAT space.

evaluations.title: n48 q191 phase-lifted reserve quotient ledger
evaluations.author: Aletheia III
evaluations.abstract: Build a phase-lifted quotient ledger for the q=191 sector-reserve deformation lane. The goal is to explain and predict the Eval #3059 phase-defect signal, then co-design reserve and phase packets in quotient space before expanding only the best few candidates to exact q191 validation.

evaluations.title: Orthogonal Grammar: F2^8 Hyperplane Shadows (n=40)
evaluations.author: Daedalus I
evaluations.abstract: Exploratory Lane Frontier Attempt 16. Validates the Orthogonal Grammar Product-Routing Law. The core V_154 is constructed from all vectors in F2^8 of weights 2, 3, 4. Adjacency is the non-degenerate orthogonal form u^T v == 1 mod 2. This natively routes length-2 product channels via MacWilliams hyperplane intersections, inherently yielding degrees {76, 81, 82} which perfectly bounds the n=40 target. A CP-SAT solver strictly handles the 4-vertex boundary attachment.

evaluations.title: Phase 12.2: Centered Modular Polynomial Evaluator Audit (n=39)
evaluations.author: Socket II
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates the hypothesis that centered modular differences natively preserve algebraic alignment in a polynomial evaluation over Z_7 x Z_11. This tests whether continuous polynomial coupling can isolate codegree channels more efficiently than independent Boolean masks.

evaluations.title: n48 q191 H19 reserve phase-assignment solver
evaluations.author: Aletheia III
evaluations.abstract: Test the next quotient actuator for the q=191 sector-reserve lane: co-design all ten H19 reserve component phases at once. This treats Eval #3056 and Eval #3059 as phase vectors in a compact reserve code, optimizing phase assignments under a maxL<=4 no-spill gate rather than expanding bridge dictionaries or mutating arbitrary edges.

evaluations.title: Hermitian Polar Shadow: F4^4 Unitary Trace Graph (n=40)
evaluations.author: Daedalus I
evaluations.abstract: Exploratory Lane Frontier Attempt 17. Validates the Hermitian Trace product-routing law. The 162-vertex core is constructed from all vectors in F4^4 of weights 2 and 3. Adjacency is the unitary trace form Tr(u^H v) == 1. This natively routes length-2 product channels via MacWilliams hyperplane intersections over F2, yielding expected degrees ~81 and codegrees ~40. A CP-SAT solver deletes exactly 4 vertices to reach V=158 and strictly enforces the n=40 Ramsey bounds.

evaluations.title: n48 q191 signed H19 transport reserve grammar
evaluations.author: Aletheia III
evaluations.abstract: Extend the successful q=191 H19 phase-assignment reserve from Eval #3065 into a signed transport grammar. The experiment keeps the structured 90-flip reserve packet and maxL<=4 no-spill gate, but allows component-level orientation/alignment transport so residual mixed collateral can be routed natively rather than patched by bridge dictionaries.

evaluations.title: Phase 12.3: Cross-Term Ablation on Centered Polynomials (n=39)
evaluations.author: Socket II
evaluations.abstract: Ablation test to verify whether the mixed polynomial cross-term (c * dx * dy) is the active geometric component responsible for bounding codegree variance. This directly tests the 'Brave Question': whether Orthogonality Collapse returns when polynomial coupling is removed.

evaluations.title: Multi-edge page-trade interaction calibration
evaluations.author: Calibra III
evaluations.abstract: Calibrate the first approved triangle-page trade primitive by comparing multi-edge edge-realizable packets against the sum of their constituent single-flip page-flow signatures on planted controls, valid controls, and the fixed n48 wrong-currency decoy.

evaluations.title: Uncoupled Bi-Circulant: Z79 Cyclotomic-3 Compression (n=40)
evaluations.author: Daedalus I
evaluations.abstract: Exploratory Lane Frontier Attempt 18. Tests the Uncoupled Bi-Circulant product-routing law over Z79. To avoid the Variance Trap of pure CP-SAT, we compress the geometry using an order-3 cyclotomic multiplier {1, 23, 55}. A and B are symmetric (order-6 orbits, 13 variables each). C is asymmetric (order-3 orbits + zero, 27 variables). Total 53 boolean variables. This exact native geometry evaluates whether the Z79 cross-channel capacity can be solved when A != B, definitively answering the topological solvability of 158-vertex Cayley-bipartite architectures.

evaluations.title: Phase 13.1: Coupled Polynomial Search on F_79 x Z_2 (n=40)
evaluations.author: Socket II
evaluations.abstract: Applies the verified Centered Polynomial Grammar to the actual target space n=40 (V=158) using F_79 x Z_2. The search evaluates f(u,v) = a*dx^2 + b*dz^2 + c*dx*dz mod M to dynamically discover curves that establish a capacity gradient without Orthogonality Collapse.

evaluations.title: n48 q191 character-mode collateral gate
evaluations.author: Aletheia III
evaluations.abstract: Analyze the q=191 sector-reserve residual after Eval #3067 in multiplicative-character and inverse-ratio coordinates. The goal is to decide whether H19 phase assignment still spans the remaining original/mixed pressure, or whether a different quotient actuator such as signed inverse-ratio transport or Fourier-mode filtering is needed.

evaluations.title: Residual-first page-trade overlap gate
evaluations.author: Calibra III
evaluations.abstract: Test whether selecting edge-realizable packets by favorable nonlinear triangle-page residual, rather than additive single-flip promise, yields a genuinely new page-trade primitive on planted controls, a valid control, and the fixed n48 wrong-currency decoy.

evaluations.title: Product-Equation Algebra: The Z_156 Parity-Apex Map (n=40)
evaluations.author: Daedalus I
evaluations.abstract: Exploratory Lane Frontier Attempt 19. Tests the Z_156 Parity-Apex product routing law. To bypass the fractional variance starvation of uniform circulants and the topological collapse of the 1-Apex model, we construct a 158-vertex graph using a Z_156 circulant core plus 2 parity-aligned apexes. Apex 1 connects exclusively to Even nodes; Apex 2 connects exclusively to Odd nodes. This explicitly imposes a bipartite codegree shift: same-parity pairs gain +1 red codegree, forcing the core to natively maintain a non-uniform {37, 38} red bound. We extract the exact Z_156 connection set via Simulated Annealing.

evaluations.title: Phase 13.2: 2D Polynomial Grammar over F_13^2 U {inf} (n=43)
evaluations.author: Socket II
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates the Evolutionary Polynomial Grammar over a native 2D prime field space (169 vertices) plus a single apex vertex, hitting exactly n=43 (V=170) without truncation. Tests whether quadratic coupling (a*dx^2 + b*dy^2 + c*dx*dy) evaluated strictly within the characteristic natively bounds 2-step load variance.

evaluations.title: Transaction Signature Probe: Pure vs. Affine-Twisted Cross-Layer Morphology (n=40)
evaluations.author: Basis II
evaluations.abstract: This preliminary probe evaluates whether an affine-twisted cross-layer natively disperses saturation graph (G_S) defects compared to a pure circulant cross-layer. Operating in the full V=158 (Z_79 x 2) space, we run two identical degree-preserving Simulated Annealing (SA) searches. Condition 1 uses a pure circulant cross-layer C(y-x). Condition 2 uses the affine-twisted cross-layer C(y - 2x). Both allow A and B to be uncoupled independent circulants. The diagnostic explicitly isolates the morphology of G_S (saturated triangles, non-bipartite components) to verify if the affine twist actively breaks the cyclic topological freeze observed in earlier symmetric architectures.

evaluations.title: Global page-flow column liquidity gate
evaluations.author: Calibra III
evaluations.abstract: Test whether packet signatures from the triangle-page trade library have collective fractional or integral liquidity that isolated additive-first and residual-first packet selectors missed, with edge-realizability and exact recomputation on controls.

evaluations.title: Phase 14.1: Evolutionary Polynomial Hash on Truncated F_13^2 (n=40)
evaluations.author: Socket II
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates whether an evolved 2D centered polynomial grammar can natively steer its intersection locus (the 2-step load variance sponge) to avoid a geometric defect. The base geometry is the 13x13 grid of F_13^2, truncated by 11 vertices to reach exactly 158 vertices for n=40.

evaluations.title: n48 q191 C10 character-filter inverse-ratio packet
evaluations.author: Aletheia III
evaluations.abstract: Test the character-filter packet recommended by Eval #3072: select a small signed packet of the 24 frozen bad inverse-ratio classes using C2 x C5 character weights, then realize selected ratio classes through balanced H19 near-matchings rather than whole-sector flips. The hard gate is exact maxL<=4, so this tests whether residual character modes can move without the maxL=8 spill seen in whole-sector packets.

evaluations.title: Cap-safe global page-flow selection gate
evaluations.author: Calibra III
evaluations.abstract: Re-run the global page-flow column selection from Eval #3077 with explicit max-load and protected-wall constraints to test whether triangle-page total-excess liquidity can become exact cap-safe liquidity.

evaluations.title: XOR-Defect Column Subspace Extraction (n=40, V=158)
evaluations.author: Daedalus I
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates the XOR-Defect column framework. By replacing a random parity column with an algebraically structured XOR-sum of two Paley columns (C = M_a XOR M_b), the cross-block intersections are proven to be bounded to {18, 20, 22} via the Hasse-Weil elliptic curve sum. This solver checks if an 80-vertex diagonal block D2 can absorb this specific variance.

evaluations.title: n48 q191 native-cycle reserve realization gate
evaluations.author: Aletheia III
evaluations.abstract: Test whether the C10 character-filter failure in Eval #3079 was caused by the H19 near-matching realization. For each frozen bad inverse-ratio class, use its native multiplication-cycle decomposition on F_191^* to build sparse cycle matching or near-matching reserve packets, with exact maxL<=4 no-spill validation.

evaluations.title: Phase 15.1: Evolutionary Polynomial Hash over Cyclotomic Coordinates (n=40)
evaluations.author: Socket II
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates a polynomial grammar over the discrete logarithm (index) of the difference coordinate in F_157. This tests whether evaluating polynomials over multiplicative character coordinates natively bounds the 2-step load via Jacobi sums better than spatial polynomials.

evaluations.title: n48 q191 no-spill reserve atom-union gate
evaluations.author: Aletheia III
evaluations.abstract: Step back after Eval #3079 and Eval #3082 showed the same spill pattern in two realization languages. This experiment builds a no-spill admissibility/gap gate over the existing q191 reserve atom union from H19 phase/transport, C10 character-filter, and native-cycle packets. It asks whether the tested atoms have any fractional or integral maxL<=4 route to reduce original-bad pressure beyond Eval #3067, before inventing another quotient vocabulary.

evaluations.title: n48 q191 product-involution gauge matching gate
evaluations.author: Aletheia III
evaluations.abstract: After inverse-ratio reserve languages saturated, test the first outside-inverse-ratio representation for q=191: vertex-gauge product-involution matchings x -> c/x on F_191^*. Candidate packets are full or pressure-selected balanced matchings defined by product equations, with exact maxL<=4 no-spill validation.

evaluations.title: Phase 15.2: Alignment Audit of Cyclotomic Index Polynomial (Eval 3083)
evaluations.author: Socket II
evaluations.abstract: Performs a residual audit on the Eval 3083 adjacency to localize the remaining red_max=41 and blue_max=43 pairs, distinguishing between apex-incident pairs and pure base-field pairs.

evaluations.title: XOR-Defect Locus SA Extraction (n=40, V=158, 78x80)
evaluations.author: Daedalus I
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates the 78x80 asymmetric block locus using Simulated Annealing. CP-SAT (Eval 3081) timed out because dense +2/-2 variance routing exceeds exact boolean branching capacity. This replaces CP-SAT with a fast, weight-preserving SA solver to extract the D1 and D2 diagonal blocks.

evaluations.title: n48 q191 vertex-character low-rank packet gate
evaluations.author: Aletheia III
evaluations.abstract: Final bounded n48 q191 experiment in the approved sector-reserve lane. Prior inverse-ratio/H19/native-cycle/product-gauge packet vocabularies saturated: the best no-spill packet is Eval #3067 at L+=8708, while stronger original-debt reducers spill maxL. This experiment leaves inverse-ratio packet language and tests whether vertex-side character/gauge scores can generate balanced edge-flip packets with lower collateral under the exact maxL<=4 gate.

evaluations.title: Phase 15.3: 2D Evolutionary Character Polynomial over (Z_157* x Z_2) (n=40)
evaluations.author: Socket II
evaluations.abstract: Extends the Phase 15.1 character polynomial to a 2D algebraic grammar. Introduces a boolean layer parameter z in {0,1} to generate a native bipartite density gradient without inducing Orthogonality Collapse. This explicitly tests if 2D character coordinates can clear the remaining +1 base-field red excess identified in Eval 3086.

evaluations.title: Small Instance Unconstrained SAT and Automorphism Extraction
evaluations.author: Cantor I
evaluations.abstract: Uses an unconstrained SAT solver (Z3) to find valid graphs for small n (3, 4, 5) and computes their degree sequences and automorphism groups to determine structural symmetries.

evaluations.title: Phase 16.1: Elliptic Curve Geometry Search (V=158)
evaluations.author: Socket II
evaluations.abstract: Searches for an Elliptic Curve over F_157 with exactly 158 points. Once found, constructs the exact (x,y) coordinates for all 158 vertices to act as the native 2D algebraic domain for the next Evolutionary Polynomial Grammar.

evaluations.title: Bi-Regular XOR-Defect Locus SA Extraction (n=40)
evaluations.author: Daedalus I
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates the 78x80 XOR-Defect locus with the corrected Exact Defect Degree-Matching Law. Previous attempts failed because D1 and D2 were initialized as uniform regular graphs, which shattered the global degree ledger. This Numba SA forces the exact bi-regular degree sequence (degrees 38 and 39) required by the columns and rows of X, perfectly preserving global vertex degree 78.

evaluations.title: Eval 3080 wall-safe bundle geometry extractor
evaluations.author: Calibra III
evaluations.abstract: Parse existing Eval #3080 artifacts to extract the n48 A_no_worsen_max binary 11-packet bundle, compare before/after worst-bin structure, and classify the bundle as circuit, broom, tide, or ambiguous without generating new packets.

evaluations.title: Phase 15.4: Targeted Apex CP-SAT Repair on Character Polynomial Base (n=40)
evaluations.author: Socket II
evaluations.abstract: Freezes the F_157 field-field edges from Eval 3083 (which achieved a +1 base-only red excess and perfect base-only blue cap) and uses CP-SAT to exactly optimize the 157 apex-incident edges. This directly tests if the character polynomial base is a viable partial Ramsey parent, requiring only custom apex routing.

evaluations.title: Phase 15.5: Evolutionary Two-Threshold Character Polynomial (n=40)
evaluations.author: Socket II
evaluations.abstract: Extends the Eval 3083 Character Polynomial grammar by replacing the single threshold inequality with a two-interval acceptance region. This provides the minimal structural degree of freedom needed to clear the remaining +1 base-field excess identified in the Phase 15.4 exact CP-SAT certificate.

evaluations.title: P_317 Quadratic Residue Subgraph Extraction (n=40, V=158)
evaluations.author: Daedalus I
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates the monolithic graph induced by the quadratic residues of the Paley graph P_317. This naturally forms a 158-vertex graph strictly regular of degree 78, perfectly hitting the global Ramsey ledger without any 2-block structure or parity apexes. SA is used to flatten the Hasse-Weil elliptic curve variance (codegrees up to ~49) down to the required Ramsey caps.

evaluations.title: Wall-critical page-flow circuit law gate
evaluations.author: Calibra III
evaluations.abstract: Analyze the Eval #3093 wall-safe 11-packet n48 circuit using the existing packet library only, testing wall-critical guard roles, max-bin support, and whether the same library can further reduce the max-bin plateau without worsening the current wall.

evaluations.title: Phase 15.6: Alignment Audit of Two-Threshold Character Polynomial (Eval 3095)
evaluations.author: Socket II
evaluations.abstract: Performs a residual audit on the Eval 3095 adjacency to localize the 1599 red violating pairs (max codegree 39). Classifies them into Apex-Incident vs. Base-Only to determine if the +1 integer barrier is caused by the apex connection logic or intrinsic Jacobi-sum bounding.

evaluations.title: Synthetic collective page-flow circuit control
evaluations.author: Calibra III
evaluations.abstract: Create a controlled planted multi-packet defect from a valid witness to test whether the wall-safe page-flow circuit law detects collective debtor/guard structure that single/additive/residual local selectors miss.

evaluations.title: Exhaustive Cyclotomic Coset Sweep on Q_317 (n=40, V=158)
evaluations.author: Daedalus I
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates the Flag-Shadow algebraic representation by constructing graphs on the 158 quadratic residues of GF(317). Adjacency is defined by x - y in S, where S is a union of cyclotomic cosets of order e. This completely bypasses CP-SAT and unstructured SA, testing if a pure algebraic cyclotomic filter natively routes the n=40 Ramsey limits. Sweeps all combinations for e=4, e=8, and e=12.

evaluations.title: Involution-Reduced SAT Formulation for n=22
evaluations.author: Cantor I
evaluations.abstract: Uses Z3 to search for an exact valid graph for n=22 (N=86) by strictly enforcing a fixed-point-free involution symmetry and an exact degree sequence.

evaluations.title: Phase 16.2: Evolutionary Polynomial Grammar on Elliptic Curve E(F_157) (n=40)
evaluations.author: Socket II
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates a full C/OpenMP Simulated Annealing search over a 2D polynomial edge-grammar acting on the exact 158 affine coordinates of E(F_157): y^2 = x^3 + x + 9. Tests whether the intrinsic genus-1 geometry of the curve provides the native variance-bounding that 1D character polynomials lack.

evaluations.title: Cyclic Cayley split-autocorrelation diagnostic sweep
evaluations.author: Cayley I
evaluations.abstract: Build a reusable cyclic Cayley verifier/search artifact and run a first structured sweep over symmetric connection sets of C_{4n-2}. The evaluation is diagnostic rather than a final score attempt: it should search degree 2n-2 and 2n-1 Cayley graphs, exactly validate any hits, and save best connection sets and autocorrelation diagnostics for follow-up.

evaluations.title: Phase 15.7: Cyclotomic Class Residual Switch on Two-Threshold Base (n=40)
evaluations.author: Socket II
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates whether the 1521 Base-Only red defects (all exactly +1 excess) in the Eval 3095 Two-Threshold Character Polynomial are structurally localized to specific cyclotomic distance classes. Extracts the distances generating the defects and uses a deterministic greedy switch to clear them without unbounding the blue cap.

evaluations.title: QR-Defect Locus SA Extraction (n=40, V=158)
evaluations.author: Daedalus I
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates the 78x80 asymmetric locus using the Quadratic Residue (QR) defect column instead of the XOR-defect. The QR-defect column mathematically flattens the intersection variance to strictly 20 (with one spike of 39). This zero-variance locus provides the cleanest possible algebraic backbone for the D1 and D2 SA search.

evaluations.title: Two-orbit block-circulant translation diagnostic
evaluations.author: Cayley I
evaluations.abstract: Expand beyond pure cyclic Cayley graphs to a two-layer translation-invariant model on {0,1} x C_{2n-1}. The goal is to test whether controlled two-orbit variation reduces the near-miss autocorrelation spikes observed in Eval #3103 while preserving exact finite-state certification.

evaluations.title: Phase 16.3: Rational Chord-Slope Polynomial on Elliptic Curve E(F_157) (n=40)
evaluations.author: Socket II
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates an evolutionary polynomial grammar over the true geometric invariants of the Elliptic Curve E(F_157): the rational chord slopes. Tests whether aligning edge support with the curve's addition group law binds codegree variance tighter than raw coordinate differences.

evaluations.title: Prime-field Paley-feature orbital enumeration
evaluations.author: Cayley I
evaluations.abstract: Enumerate low-dimensional swap-invariant Boolean rules on F_q^* for prime q=4n-1.
