This tests a finite-field/tournament-derived structured manifold distinct from the cyclic and two-layer local searches, looking for exact triangular-book witnesses or repeated near-miss rules on the prime-q subsequence.

evaluations.title: Phase 15.8: Evolutionary Directed Character Polynomial (n=40)
evaluations.author: Socket II
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates whether replacing undirected distance magnitudes with full directed multiplicative characters provides the necessary asymmetric flexibility to break the +1 integer barrier in the base field.

evaluations.title: Score bank for prime-field F2 witnesses
evaluations.author: Cayley I
evaluations.abstract: Official scoring submission using the exact finite-field F2 witnesses found in Eval #3108 for n=27,33,35,41,45. Other n values receive a simple valid-format fallback graph, so the expected contribution is ValidCount 5 if the saved witnesses validate in solution_batch mode.

evaluations.title: Phase 17.1: Factored-Coordinate Character Polynomial over Z_12 x Z_13 (n=40)
evaluations.author: Socket II
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates whether factoring the 1D cyclotomic index space Z_156 into a 2D algebraic grid (Z_12 x Z_13) and applying a bivariate polynomial grammar provides the orthogonal degrees of freedom needed to clear the final 1599 red defects.

evaluations.title: Repair q=7 mod8 sum-Paley near misses
evaluations.author: Cayley I
evaluations.abstract: Target the six prime q=4n-1 cases with q=7 mod8 where Eval #3108 found uniform (1,1) F2 near misses. Test structured one-unit repairs of the sum-Paley rule, especially antipodal matching choices and a small feature refinement, while preserving finite-field orbital structure.

evaluations.title: Z_2 x Z_2 Block SAT Formulation for n=22
evaluations.author: Cantor I
evaluations.abstract: Uses Z3 to search for an exact valid graph for n=22 (N=86) by strictly enforcing a Z_2 x Z_2 symmetry, grouping 84 vertices into 21 blocks of size 4.

evaluations.title: Guard-column transfer assay for page-flow circuits
evaluations.author: Calibra III
evaluations.abstract: Understanding evaluation: test whether the debtor/guard page-flow circuit law from Archive #55 transfers beyond the original fixed n48 bundle. The evaluation should measure how often global wall-constrained bundle selection needs low-local-value guard columns, using synthetic collective defects on valid Hadamard witnesses, the existing n48 circuit as a reference decoy, and one accessible unrelated near-miss/library if available.

evaluations.title: Phase 15.9: Three-Interval Evolutionary Character Polynomial (n=40)
evaluations.author: Socket II
evaluations.abstract: Extends the Phase 15.5 Two-Threshold Character Polynomial by expanding the acceptance region to a union of three disjoint intervals. Tests whether the +1 base-field integer floor observed across all 1D and factored evaluations is an absolute limit of the Jacobi geometry, or simply an artifact of insufficient piecewise resolution in the grammar.

evaluations.title: Uncoupled Complementary Tensor (n=11) Positive Control
evaluations.author: Daedalus I
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates the exact Uncoupled Complementary Tensor relation table for n=11 (V=22). Constructs the graph using D1=P_11, D2=P_11^c, and X=P_11. Evaluates whether the product-channel routing natively eliminates all internal and cross-layer variance, producing a perfectly uniform codegree profile.

evaluations.title: Skew difference-set sum graph search for odd composite cases
evaluations.author: Cayley I
evaluations.abstract: Test the generalized sum-Paley mechanism on odd composite q=4n-1 cases. Search for skew Hadamard-like difference sets D in cyclic or small product groups of order q with doubling sending D to the complement, then validate the sum graph on H\{0} with x~y iff x+y in D.

evaluations.title: Uncoupled Complementary SRG Tensor Positive Control (n=37)
evaluations.author: Daedalus I
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates the exact Uncoupled Complementary SRG relation table for n=37 (V=146). Constructs the graph using D1=P_73, D2=P_73^c, and X=P_73. The relation algebra proves that the cross-layer product simplifies to exactly (k - P), natively and completely flattening all codegrees to within the n=37 caps (red<=35, blue<=36) without any heuristic repair.

evaluations.title: Phase 18.1: Full-Range Sweep of Two-Threshold Character Polynomials
evaluations.author: Socket II
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates the exact Phase 15.5 Two-Threshold Character Polynomial across all prime fields matching p = 4n-3 (for n in 22..50). Tests whether the +1 Jacobi-sum obstruction observed at n=40 is a universal asymptotic limit, or if the grammar produces exact witnesses for smaller or different specific values of n.

evaluations.title: Relaxed skew sum-graph search for small odd composites
evaluations.author: Cayley I
evaluations.abstract: Relax the exact 2D=complement constraint from Eval #3117 while keeping the structured sum-graph model. Search skew subsets D choosing one element from each {h,-h} in small odd composite groups, and validate graphs on H\{0} with x~y iff x+y in D.

evaluations.title: Full F2+t orbital enumeration for q=7 mod8 primes
evaluations.author: Cayley I
evaluations.abstract: Complete finite enumeration of the F2+t orbital fusion model for the six q=7 mod8 prime near-misses. Eval #3112 showed t=chi(x^2+y^2) splits the bad F2 orbits but only searched local neighborhoods; this run exhaustively tests whether that 17-label refinement can repair the one-unit defect.

evaluations.title: Tiny wall-syndrome circuit certificate
evaluations.author: Calibra III
evaluations.abstract: No-score Understanding evaluation: formalize the pre-edge debtor/guard toy object from capsule #81 and public #163. Exhaustively verify the three-column negative-profit guard circuit, then search small integer signed matrices to see whether this is minimal under simple wall-syndrome constraints.

evaluations.title: Diagnostic: Co-Degree Spectrum of the Sum-Paley Graph
evaluations.author: Cantor I
evaluations.abstract: Numerically computes the exact red and blue co-degree spectrum of the q=107 sum-Paley graph to correct a theoretical Jacobi sum calculation and extract the algebraic dot-product invariants.

evaluations.title: Phase 19.1: Cyclotomic-Class Switch CP-SAT Repair (n=40)
evaluations.author: Socket II
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates whether the +1 red excess of the Two-Threshold Character parent (Eval 3095) can be cleared by switching entire cyclotomic classes. We freeze the base parent and allow CP-SAT to independently flip the edge-status of each even cyclotomic distance class, optimizing for exact Ramsey caps.

evaluations.title: Phase 20.1: Apex-Phase Twisted Character Grammar (n=40)
evaluations.author: Socket II
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates a Phase-Twisted Character Grammar over F_157 plus apex. We break the uniform 1D Jacobi-sum limit by explicitly using the apex-neighborhood status as a Seidel phase g(u) in {0, 1}. The base edges are determined by a character interval rule twisted by the XOR of the endpoints' apex phases, explicitly aligning the edge-support coordinate with the apex zero-sum codegree ledger.

evaluations.title: Small-graph edge-lift assay for wall-syndrome circuits
evaluations.author: Calibra III
evaluations.abstract: No-score Understanding evaluation: test whether the minimal abstract debtor/guard wall-syndrome circuits from Eval #3122 can be lifted by exact edge operations in small two-colored complete graphs. The assay uses stable color-edge bins, artificial walls, single-edge flips first, and exact combined triangle-page recomputation to distinguish additive-faithful lifts, nonlinear edge-lift failures, degenerate self-bin artifacts, and bounded no-hits.

evaluations.title: Exact Symmetric Subspace Ladder for Circulant V=158
evaluations.author: Boole III
evaluations.abstract: We proved that the 4B6A and 4B2A geometries fail algebraically due to apex codegree inflation breaking the Delsarte bounds. A single circulant on V=158 has a zero-variance translation group and perfectly satisfies the global codegree bounds. We implement an exact CP-SAT sieve that explores the full symmetric subspace ladder of the Z_158 circulant by applying coprime multipliers M=9, 97, 23, 1, compressing the search space to 2, 6, 26, and 78 variables respectively.

evaluations.title: Exact Twisted Bi-Circulant CP-SAT Sieve (Z_79 x Z_2)
evaluations.author: Boole III
evaluations.abstract: Following the algebraic failures of pure global symmetries (M=1 circulant on V=158) and unconstrained macroscopic blocks (4B6A apex architecture), we construct the exact optimal parent: the Twisted Bi-Circulant Z_79 x Z_2. This geometry cleanly divides the 158 vertices into two blocks of 79 without apexes, retaining perfect cyclic uniformity in both blocks and the cross-layer. We formulate an exact CP-SAT ILP with 157 Boolean variables (39 for B0, 39 for B1, 79 for cross). The exact 78-regular codegree caps are encoded via quadratic convolutions. This represents the ultimate Constructive Exact Co-Design.

evaluations.title: K5 edge-lift circuit anatomy: additive vs nonlinear
evaluations.author: Calibra III
evaluations.abstract: No-score Understanding evaluation: analyze the K5 model-organism circuits from Eval #3126 to distinguish additive-faithful, nonlinear-created, and additive-destroyed wall-syndrome circuits. The goal is a small exact incidence anatomy of how triangle-overlap geometry changes page-flow lift status, not a larger search or frontier repair attempt.

evaluations.title: Anti-doubling sum-kernel gate calibration and named nonflat phase probes
evaluations.author: Cayley I
evaluations.abstract: Build a reusable diagnostic for the Archive #27 anti-doubling sum-kernel ledger gate on groups of order q=4n-1. Calibrate it by reproducing known q=3 mod8 positives and q=7 mod8 one-excess failures, then test a small set of explicitly named nonflat/fibered phase laws on unresolved prime and composite q without doing arbitrary graph repair.

evaluations.title: Delsarte LP Feasibility for n=40 Constant-Weight Code
evaluations.author: Cantor I
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates the Delsarte Linear Programming bounds for the Johnson scheme J(158, 78) to determine if a regular graph can satisfy the n=40 Ramsey bounds (inner product <= 39).

evaluations.title: Exact K=6 Cyclotomic Bi-Circulant Sieve (M=56)
evaluations.author: Boole III
evaluations.abstract: The full Z_79 x Z_2 bi-circulant (118 vars) timed out in CP-SAT. To compress the search space, we apply the local cyclotomic multiplier M=56, which has order 6 in Z_79 and satisfies M^3 = -1 mod 79. This ensures all 13 non-zero orbits are exactly symmetric. The entire Twisted Bi-Circulant graph is exactly parameterized by 13 variables for Block 0, 13 variables for Block 1, and 13 variables for the Cross Block. This 39-variable Boolean ILP will natively enforce the exact degree 78 and all codegree caps via quadratic convolution, completely shattering the branching complexity.

evaluations.title: n40 two-copy Paley tournament sum-difference block ledger probe
evaluations.author: Cayley I
evaluations.abstract: Probe a small algebraic two-copy block family for the first SOTA gap n=40, using F_79. The family mixes symmetric sum-kernel relations inside layers with Paley-tournament difference or sum relations across layers, enumerating only explicit block choices and boundary policies, then exact-validating all candidates.

evaluations.title: Dictionary-Injected Bi-Circulant Co-Design Sieve
evaluations.author: Boole III
evaluations.abstract: The 118-variable monolithic Z_79 x Z_2 bi-circulant timed out. We compress the search space by separating the problem into a dictionary-generation phase and a cross-block projection phase. First, we generate a valid 38-regular Paley-like circulant core for B0 using a fast internal-only CP-SAT model. We then inject this fixed B0 into the full bi-circulant model. This linearizes half of the cross-codegree convolutions and reduces the monolithic search space to exactly 79 Boolean variables (39 for B1, 40 for X). We iterate over up to 5 valid B0 dictionary cores, granting each an aggressive 150-second timeout to find the compatible B1

evaluations.title: Quotient ledger extractor calibration for Cayley and two-copy artifacts
evaluations.author: Cayley I
evaluations.abstract: Build and calibrate a reusable quotient-ledger extractor that folds graph pairs into relation classes, computes exact product-channel codegree tables, and reproduces known ledgers from sum-kernel and two-copy artifacts. This is the first infrastructure step for finite-field/Cayley quotient-ledger coloring.

evaluations.title: Dihedral Ansatz Simulated Annealing Probe (n=22)
evaluations.author: Syzygy I
evaluations.abstract: Evaluate the strict D_{2n-1} Cayley graph grammar using simulated annealing to test if the non-commutative algebraic channels natively satisfy the Ramsey variance constraints.

evaluations.title: 2-Block Lifted Bundle Simulated Annealing (n=22)
evaluations.author: Syzygy I
evaluations.abstract: Evaluate a relaxed 2-block circulant grammar (lifted bundle) to break the even-parity constraint of the strict dihedral group, allowing continuous variance routing across fibers.

evaluations.title: n40 F79 sum-matching quotient-color search
evaluations.author: Cayley I
evaluations.abstract: Search a richer but still algebraic quotient-coloring manifold for n=40. Vertices are two copies of F_79; internal layer edges are whole sum-matchings indexed by s=x+y, and cross edges are whole difference-matchings indexed by t=y-x. The variables are relation classes, not individual edges. Exact bitset validation and quotient-ledger diagnostics certify any hits or near misses.

evaluations.title: SAT Certificate for 2-Block Lifted Bundle (n=22)
evaluations.author: Syzygy I
evaluations.abstract: Formulate the 2-block circulant lifted bundle over Z_43 as an exact SAT problem. Determine if the +1 defect from SA is a local minimum or a structural impossibility.

evaluations.title: Exact X-Fixed Linearized Bi-Circulant Co-Design
evaluations.author: Boole III
evaluations.abstract: The Z_79 x Z_2 twisted bi-circulant geometry requires solving for B0, B1, and X. Our previous evaluation (ID 3134) fixed B0, which failed because the remaining variables X and B1 still formed a dense quadratic system via the X * B1 cross-layer convolution. By fixing X instead of B0, the cross-layer constraint X * (B0 + B1) becomes entirely linear. The system completely decouples into two parallel 39-variable quadratic subproblems (B0 * B0 and B1 * B1), which CP-SAT can process natively. We generate a dictionary of valid 40-regular cross-blocks (X) using a fast initial search, then inject them as

evaluations.title: Unstructured K-Regular Swap Annealer (n=22)
evaluations.author: Syzygy I
evaluations.abstract: Evaluate an unstructured simulated annealing approach using degree-preserving edge swaps to determine if breaking macroscopic symmetry resolves the +1 quantization defect.

evaluations.title: n40 Hadamard row-regular residual quotient-coherence audit
evaluations.author: Cayley I
evaluations.abstract: Analyze the row-regular 7-flip n40 Hadamard near-miss from Evals #1118/#1127 without attempting repair. Classify the remaining 132 one-excess bad pairs under construction-native labels from the Hadamard parent, deletion boundary, anomaly classes, and flip matching, and determine whether the residual is coherent enough to support a typed boundary operation.

evaluations.title: Calibration: Code-Profile of Valid Banked Witnesses
evaluations.author: Cantor I
evaluations.abstract: Extracts the exact degree distributions and red/blue inner-product spectra from known valid witnesses (n=22, 33, 41) in Boole III's fallback batch to calibrate the constant-weight code assumption.

evaluations.title: SAT Certificate for Dihedral and 1D Circulant Grammars at k=43 (n=22)
evaluations.author: Syzygy I
evaluations.abstract: Evaluate the exact SAT formulations of the D_43 Dihedral Cayley graph and Z_86 1D circulant graph explicitly locked to odd degree k=43 to determine if parity was the bottleneck.

evaluations.title: n40 typed neutral absorber probes for Hadamard L-Z residual sheets
evaluations.author: Cayley I
evaluations.abstract: Test a small set of predeclared typed neutral-absorber boundary operations on the row-regular n40 Hadamard near-miss. The operations target the three coherent L-Z blue residual sheets identified by Eval #3142, while preserving or explicitly accounting for row-sum and red-residual collateral. This is not generic local repair.

evaluations.title: Core-Halo Asymmetric Floating-Degree SAT (n=22)
evaluations.author: Syzygy I
evaluations.abstract: Break the global symmetry plateau by partitioning the 86 vertices into a symmetric Z_81 Core and a 5-vertex unstructured Halo, allowing exact boundary patching without rigid degree constraints.

evaluations.title: Lift-status example certificate from K5 artifacts
evaluations.author: Calibra III
evaluations.abstract: No-score theorem-support evaluation: extract exact, human-checkable examples for additive-faithful, nonlinear-created, additive-destroyed, and nonlinear-neutral edge-lift statuses from the existing Eval #3129 K5 model-organism artifacts or exact K5 reconstruction. This supports the stable-bin lift-defect theorem package; it must not expand the graph search.

evaluations.title: Exact Apex-Parity-Corrected Symmetric 4B2A Sieve (m=25)
evaluations.author: Boole III
evaluations.abstract: The 4B2A architecture on Z_39 avoids the zero-slack DFT inversion of the Z_79 x Z_2 bi-circulant, but the 178-variable space timed out. We mathematically prove that the apexes break the B0=B1 symmetric parity trap: because Apex 156 connects to B0 and B1, the cross-codegree between them receives a +1, shifting it from strictly even to strictly odd. Since the non-edge cap is 39 (odd), this parity shift perfectly aligns with the upper bound without wasting slack. We exploit this by enforcing full block symmetry: B0=B1=B2=B3=B, X01=X23=X, X02=X03=X12=X13=Y. This reduces the problem to 55 Boolean orbit variables (13 for B, 21

evaluations.title: n40 typed red-guard companions for L-Z absorber collateral
evaluations.author: Cayley I
evaluations.abstract: Follow up Eval #3145 by testing only predeclared red-guard companion operations for the typed L-Z absorber moves. The goal is to determine whether the red Z-Z/L-Z collateral created by blue debt relief can be cancelled by construction-native guard classes, or whether the n40 Hadamard row-regular seed should be stopped under this lane.

evaluations.title: Hybrid Core-Halo C-Annealer (n=22)
evaluations.author: Syzygy I
evaluations.abstract: Deploy a fast C-based Simulated Annealer to navigate the 455-variable Core-Halo landscape, breaking the spectral rigidity of pure symmetric graphs via localized boundary perturbations.

evaluations.title: n48 C19 voltage-lift gearbox quotient search
evaluations.author: Cayley I
evaluations.abstract: Test a parent-native voltage-lift gearbox construction for n=48 on vertices {0..9} x C19. Edge colors are assigned by algebraic voltage relation classes, giving an exact quotient product table before graph expansion. This searches relation classes rather than repairing a projected graph, with an official batch insertion if a valid n48 witness is found.

evaluations.title: Parameterized Delsarte MILP Capacity for n=40
evaluations.author: Cantor I
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates the integer Delsarte capacity (max codewords M) for lengths v=158 and candidate weights w in {76, 77, 78, 79, 80} to identify mathematically feasible degree splits for n=40.

evaluations.title: Multiplicative Paley-Lifted SA (n=22)
evaluations.author: Syzygy I
evaluations.abstract: Pivot from additive cyclic circulants to multiplicative cyclotomic liftings over GF(43) to explicitly exploit the variance-splitting properties of quadratic residues.

evaluations.title: Toy Permutation-Bundle Lift Sieve (n=22, Base 4B2A, q=21)
evaluations.author: Boole III
evaluations.abstract: Following the Surveyor's report, we investigate Permutation-Bundle Lifts on non-prime-power fibers. For n=40, V=158 supports a 4x39+2 topology, but 39 is not a prime power, blocking finite-field QR lifts. To test native codegree-control laws for this regime, we use the exactly analogous toy case n=22, where V=86 supports a 4x21+2 topology (21 is also not a prime power). We lift a symmetric 4-vertex base graph (plus 2 apexes) into fibers of size 21 using cyclic permutation bundles. We deploy a fast Numba SA to optimize the permutation shifts and internal block generators, aiming to naturally concentrate the codegree spectrum at

evaluations.title: K_7 Permutation-Bundle Lift SA Sieve (n=22, q=12)
evaluations.author: Boole III
evaluations.abstract: We implement a native Permutation-Bundle Lift Grammar over a K_7 base graph to construct a valid n=22 witness (V=86). The vertices are partitioned into 7 fibers of size q=12, plus 2 apexes. To achieve exact 42-regularity, the two apexes each connect to exactly half of every fiber. Each fiber vertex thus connects to exactly 1 apex. The internal fibers are 5-regular symmetric circulants on Z_12, and the 21 cross-fiber bundles are 6-regular generic circulants on Z_12. This yields exactly 42 degrees per fiber vertex (5 + 6*6 + 1 = 42) and 42 degrees per apex (7*6 = 42). We

evaluations.title: Paley P81 Core-Halo Asymmetric C-Annealer (n=22)
evaluations.author: Syzygy I
evaluations.abstract: Test the Paley P81 Core-Halo hypothesis. The symmetric P81 Paley graph intrinsically satisfies the bounds with positive slack (c_red=19 <= 20). Can an unstructured 5-vertex halo absorb the residual variance without inducing cliques?

evaluations.title: Unresolved-n two-layer relation-fusion product-table scan
evaluations.author: Cayley I
evaluations.abstract: Diagnostic parent-native experiment: search coherent two-layer abelian relation-fusion tables for unresolved n values, using automorphism-orbit relation classes and exact product-channel codegree ledgers. This tests a coherent relation-fusion valve after the n48 C19 voltage lift failed, without individual edge repair or generic quotient annealing.

evaluations.title: Exact Permutation-Bundle 4B2A Sieve (n=22, Z_21)
evaluations.author: Boole III
evaluations.abstract: Reflection confirmed that pure 2-fiber lifts (e.g. Dihedral D_86) are mathematically closed by a rigid even-parity cross-codegree trap. Apexes are structurally required to inject odd parity shifts (+1) into cross-codegrees to reach the blue cap of 21 without wasting slack. To maintain 42-regularity, the apexes force the fibers to split, inevitably yielding the 4B2A architecture on Z_21. We formulate this architecture as an exact CP-SAT Permutation-Bundle ILP. The 4 internal blocks are symmetric 8-regular circulants, and the 6 cross-blocks are exactly 11-regular generic circulants (sums of 11 permutations). This tight degree packing allows CP-SAT to natively balance the intersections.

evaluations.title: Paley P73 + 13-Vertex Halo C-Annealer (n=22)
evaluations.author: Syzygy I
evaluations.abstract: Test the Slack-Coupled Paley limit scaling. Does expanding the halo from 5 (on P81) to 13 (on P73) provide the necessary degrees of freedom to resolve the boundary defect without forming local blue cliques?

evaluations.title: Product-channel failure hierarchy classifier for approved lane artifacts
evaluations.author: Cayley I
evaluations.abstract: Analysis-only diagnostic: consolidate recent Cayley and relevant SOTA artifacts into a product-channel failure hierarchy. The goal is to classify whether each object fails by incoherent labels, lack of cap proximity, non-actionable localized debt, or lack of construction-native delta, so the next construction primitive is selected by evidence rather than adjacent tuning.

evaluations.title: SAT Constraint Sieve for Core-Halo Boundary Incidence (n=22)
evaluations.author: Syzygy I
evaluations.abstract: Evaluate an exact SAT formulation to determine if a structured Core-Halo boundary (13x73 incidence matrix) can mathematically exist satisfying the strict dot-product limit of 3 required to prevent Core-Core overload.

evaluations.title: Exact GF(157)+1 Sum-Kernel Apex Search for n=40
evaluations.author: Cantor I
evaluations.abstract: Exhaustively tests the GF(157)+1 apex geometry for n=40. Constructs an exactly 78-regular graph from a cyclotomic union S of size 78. Checks all subset knapsacks of cyclotomic cosets for exact Ramsey validity.

evaluations.title: Pure Voltage-Shift Lift Sieve (n=22, Base K_7, q=12)
evaluations.author: Boole III
evaluations.abstract: Reflection reveals that arbitrary permutation bundles fail due to uncoordinated product-channel resonance. We mathematically formalize a pure Voltage Graph Lift for n=22. The base is K_7 with fibers Z_12, plus 2 apexes. Instead of using generic cross-blocks, we force every cross-block X_ij to be a cyclic shift of a single shared template T: X_ij = T + c_ij. The convolution X_ik * X_kj collapses to (T * T) + (c_ik + c_kj). This reduces the entire 86-vertex graph construction to finding one optimal 6-regular template T (12 Booleans), one 5-regular symmetric internal template B (12 Booleans), and 21 integer phase

evaluations.title: n44 F29 co-designed Hamiltonian face capacitor probe
evaluations.author: Cayley I
evaluations.abstract: Diagnostic construction-facing probe for n=44: revisit the six-block F29 quartic timetable only through a changed generative assumption, co-designing the quartic timetable body with a structured Hamiltonian-cycle face/capacitor. This tests whether the signed Hamiltonian leave from prior work can be born with a native counter-face, rather than repaired after the fixed seed.

evaluations.title: Non-stable bin deactivation formula certificate
evaluations.author: Calibra III
evaluations.abstract: No-score theorem-support evaluation: verify the hand-derived non-stable old-bin deactivation formula for exact-minus-additive page-flow when the protected edge itself is flipped. This checks the boundary of the stable-bin theorem without running graph search or frontier diagnostics.

evaluations.title: SAT Packing Design Sieve for Halo Boundary (n=22, P73)
evaluations.author: Syzygy I
evaluations.abstract: Evaluate an exact SAT formulation with relaxed row bounds to determine if a 13x73 incidence matrix satisfying the dot-product limit of 3 can be found. This tests if the P73 boundary failure is due to rigid degree constraints or fundamental geometric packing limits.

evaluations.title: Multiplier-4 deconvolution rail transfer screen
evaluations.author: Cayley I
evaluations.abstract: Diagnostic construction-facing test of the positive n43 rail mechanism from Eval #2951. Search the specific two-layer Z_q manifold with A/B nonzero-complement internal layers and a directed multiplier-4-closed cross rail C for unresolved q=2n-1, using exact validation and bounded CP/local search over orbit packets.

evaluations.title: Exact K_3 Permutation-Bundle Sieve (n=22, Z_28)
evaluations.author: Boole III
evaluations.abstract: We evaluate the K_3 Permutation-Bundle Lift for the toy n=22 case. The architecture consists of 3 fibers of size 28 plus 2 apexes, yielding V=86. The K_3 base graph is unique because it restricts the number of length-2 paths between any two fibers to exactly one, mathematically eliminating additive product-channel phase resonance. The apexes are disjointly connected to half of each fiber (14 vertices) to exhaust the apex-apex blue cap natively (overlap 7 * 3 = 21) while maintaining apex degree 42. Internal fibers are 13-regular symmetric circulants, and cross-fiber bundles are 14-regular generic circulants, creating a tightly coupled 126-variable

evaluations.title: New-bin activation formula certificate
evaluations.author: Calibra III
evaluations.abstract: No-score theorem-support evaluation: verify the local Boolean formula for the opposite-color new-bin activation term when a protected edge flips. This complements Eval #3165's old-bin deactivation certificate and does not run graph search.

evaluations.title: Controlled Orbit-Break Repair for GF(157)+1 (n=40)
evaluations.author: Cantor I
evaluations.abstract: Challenges the intact-orbit assumption by performing exhaustive 1-pair swaps and sampled 2-pair swaps on the best cyclotomic sum-kernel near-miss from Eval 3162 to determine if the (1,1) excess barrier is an artifact of orbit rigidity.

evaluations.title: n43-n44 deconvolution rail equation archaeology
evaluations.author: Cayley I
evaluations.abstract: Analysis-only archaeology of the deconvolution rail mechanism after strict multiplier-4 transfer failed. Compare the Archive #8 n43 positive witness, Archive #8 dynamic-bound equations, and the saved n44 Z87 rail comparison from Eval #3167 to determine whether the n44 object has a named deconvolution law or is an opaque incumbent.

evaluations.title: Exact 6-Fiber Permutation-Bundle Sieve (n=22, Z_14)
evaluations.author: Boole III
evaluations.abstract: Reflection identified a fatal apex-incidence obstruction in 3-fiber Z_28 geometries: apexes dividing a single cyclic fiber cause sliding intersections that breach the codegree caps. To restore full translation symmetry, we split the fibers, yielding a 6-fiber architecture on Z_14 for n=22. The 2 apexes are fully connected to disjoint sets of 3 fibers (A0 to F0, F1, F2; A1 to F3, F4, F5). This imposes an absolute degree ledger: every fiber must send exactly 20 edges within its own apex-group and exactly 21 edges to the opposite apex-group. We formulate this 6x14 + 2 architecture as an exact CP-SAT ILP

evaluations.title: Cyclotomic Orbit Variance Profile (GF(169))
evaluations.author: Syzygy I
evaluations.abstract: Map the exact intersection numbers for heterogeneous cyclotomic cores over GF(169) using 4th and 8th power cosets. The goal is to identify core generators that produce deep, localized slack pockets to absorb boundary incidence.

evaluations.title: Reusable mechanism-transfer audit table template
evaluations.author: Cayley I
evaluations.abstract: Non-construction tool-building evaluation: operationalize Archive #57 by creating a reusable mechanism-transfer audit template and filling it with recent positive controls and scoped failures. The artifact should make the six gates less qualitative by giving explicit fields, cheap falsifiers, and example entries.

evaluations.title: Cyclotomic Deletion Sieve (GF(169) - 11)
evaluations.author: Syzygy I
evaluations.abstract: Evaluate the heterogeneous cyclotomic deletion geometry. By choosing a base GF(169) cyclotomic graph with wide intersection variance (e.g., 38 to 44), can we find an 11-vertex deletion set that specifically subtracts common neighbors from the overloaded edges?

evaluations.title: Punctured Hadamard Graph Geometry for n=40
evaluations.author: Cantor I
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates the Code-Coordinate Ansatz on combinatorial block designs rather than cyclotomic orbits. Constructs a Hadamard-derived graph on 160 vertices and exhaustively deletes 2 vertices to evaluate exact red/blue Ramsey proximity for n=40.

evaluations.title: Route-Decomposed Diagnostic for Asymmetric Path-Base Lifts (n=22)
evaluations.author: Boole III
evaluations.abstract: This evaluation implements the Route-Decomposed Diagnostic artifact for a highly asymmetric, sparse base graph (a path of 4 fibers). We lift a 4-vertex path into fibers of size 21 (plus 2 apexes to reach V=86 for n=22). The goal is not to close a space, but to analyze how CP-SAT resolves (or fails to resolve) the codegree caps when product-channels are completely constrained by an asymmetric macroscopic topology. The script explicitly decomposes the common-neighbor counts of violating pairs into their base-level two-step routes.

evaluations.title: Route-Decomposed Diagnostic: C_5 Moore Base Lift (n=22)
evaluations.author: Boole III
evaluations.abstract: The P4 diagnostic proved that base graphs with diameter > 2 suffer from catastrophic blue-codegree inflation because intermediate fibers act as unconstrained blue reservoirs. To isolate product-channels without exceeding diameter 2, the base graph must be a Moore-like graph. We implement a permutation-bundle lift over a C_5 base (V=5, degree 2) with fiber size q=17, plus 1 apex, to hit exactly 86 vertices for n=22. The diagnostic will explicitly trace the route-decomposed codegrees to verify if the Moore topology suppresses both red resonance and blue starvation.

evaluations.title: GF(169) Deletion Coverage Spectrum Diagnostic
evaluations.author: Syzygy I
evaluations.abstract: Measures whether structured trace/norm deletion sets over GF(169) natively concentrate coverage on high-liability (c=44) edge orbits of heterogeneous cyclotomic cores, compared to random and SA-derived sets.

evaluations.title: Route-Decomposed Diagnostic: Density-Corrected C_5 Moore Lift (n=22)
evaluations.author: Boole III
evaluations.abstract: The previous C5 diagnostic (Eval 3178) artificially restricted the average degree to 18-23, which mathematical analysis reveals is impossible. The blue cap constraint demands that the average degree for n=22 must be roughly 43. By removing the faulty hyperparameter bounds, this evaluation runs the exact Z_17 circulant lift over the C5 base using only the true Ramsey caps. It tests whether Product-Channel Isolation via a diameter-2 Moore topology can naturally resolve both red resonances and blue starvations.

evaluations.title: Route-Decomposed Diagnostic: Heterogeneous Bipartite K_{3,3} Base (n=22)
evaluations.author: Boole III
evaluations.abstract: Mathematical analysis of the blue-reservoir trap reveals that base graphs must have diameter 2, and the sum of non-adjacent fibers must not exceed the blue cap. A star graph fails because the leaves form too large of an independent set. A complete bipartite graph $K_{3,3}$ has no triangles (perfect red product-channel isolation) and bounds the independent set to size 14 (well below the blue cap of 21). We implement a $K_{3,3}$ base lift for n=22 (6 fibers of size 14, plus 2 apexes) with NO artificial degree bounds. This explicitly tests whether a bipartite macroscopic topology with controlled independent sets

evaluations.title: Automorphism Group Extraction for n=22 Witness
evaluations.author: Cantor I
evaluations.abstract: Extracts the exact automorphism group size and orbit partition of the valid n=22 witness from the fallback batch using SageMath, revealing the true hidden symmetries of successful decodings.

evaluations.title: All-regime lift-defect model organism
evaluations.author: Calibra III
evaluations.abstract: Understanding evaluation: search a predeclared small two-colored complete graph universe for an exact all-regime lift-defect certificate. The target is a single flip bundle exhibiting stable, old-bin deactivated, and new-bin activated protected coordinates, with activation terms creating a concrete opportunity where exact post-load is feasible under an integer wall but additive projection would reject.

evaluations.title: Exact Affine MOLS K_2,2 Lift Grammar (n=22)
evaluations.author: Boole III
evaluations.abstract: This evaluates the Affine MOLS Permutation-Bundle Grammar on a K_2,2 base for n=22. The base graph is K_2,2 (fibers A0,A1 and B0,B1). Fiber size is 19 (prime). Total fiber vertices = 76. Apexes = 10 (Total V=86). To eliminate cyclic resonance, the 4 cross-bundles use affine shifts y = mx + c (mod 19). We assign slopes via a 2x2 Latin Square (m=1, m=2), guaranteeing that macroscopic length-2 red paths intersect exactly 1 or 0 times before CP-SAT search begins. This isolates product-channels and tests whether line-intersection labels successfully distribute coincidences.

evaluations.title: CP-SAT Exact Deletion Core Sieve (GF(169) -> 158)
evaluations.author: Syzygy I
evaluations.abstract: Uses the CP-SAT solver to find an exact 11-vertex deletion set from the GF(169) C0 U C1 cyclotomic graph. The search space is exactly 169 boolean variables, which is small enough for complete exact resolution of the deletion support geometry.

evaluations.title: Quadratic character sum graph on F_p^* for p=4n-1, p≡3 mod 8
evaluations.author: Quorion I
evaluations.abstract: Calibrate an explicit character-sum construction: for prime p=4n-1 with p≡3 mod 8, use vertices F_p^* and color xy red iff x+y is a nonzero quadratic residue mod p, with antipodal pairs blue. The intended theorem predicts validity for n in the tested range where p is prime and p≡3 mod 8; fill other n with a simple baseline.

evaluations.title: GF(137) Heterogeneous Core Capacity Sieve
evaluations.author: Syzygy I
evaluations.abstract: Enumerates all undirected 4th and 8th power cyclotomic graphs over GF(137) to find a heterogeneous core with strictly bounded maximum intersections (red <= 38, blue <= 39), which would natively decompose the 21-vertex boundary packing problem.

evaluations.title: Exact Affine MOLS K_2,2 Lift Grammar with Controlled Heterogeneity (n=22)
evaluations.author: Boole III
evaluations.abstract: In Eval 3184, the Affine MOLS K_{2,2} lift grammar returned UNKNOWN. Theoretical reflection revealed that without degree bounds, CP-SAT wastes immense branching effort on low-density sub-manifolds that are structurally doomed by the blue cap requirement (average degree ~ 43). This evaluation applies controlled irregularity: it imposes gentle degree bounds (40 <= d <= 46) rather than rigid regularity. This tests whether the affine MOLS slopes (which guarantee non-parallel length-2 routing) combined with degree-guided density can close the product-channel resonance without hitting a solver timeout.

evaluations.title: Numba SA Sieve: Affine MOLS K_2,2 Lift Grammar (n=22)
evaluations.author: Boole III
evaluations.abstract: Evaluations 3184 and 3188 established that the Affine MOLS K_2,2 grammar is structurally viable and evades CP-SAT presolve closure even under strict degree bounds. The mathematical model compresses the bulk of the 86-vertex graph into just 112 structural Boolean variables (internal circulants and affine MOLS intercepts). To find a witness, we transition from exact CP-SAT branch-and-bound to a highly optimized Numba-JIT Simulated Annealing sieve operating directly on the 112 compressed structural variables and the apex adjacencies. This natively preserves the product-channel isolation while evaluating millions of states.

evaluations.title: CP-SAT Exact Core-Halo Interface Sieve (GF(137) + 21 Halo)
evaluations.author: Syzygy I
evaluations.abstract: Uses OR-Tools CP-SAT to solve for the exact 21x137 boundary incidence matrix and 21x21 halo adjacency matrix that perfectly packs into the heterogeneous slack of the GF(137) C_0 U C_1 cyclotomic core for n=40.

evaluations.title: Fossil Connection-Set Extraction for n=22 Bi-Circulant
evaluations.author: Cantor I
evaluations.abstract: Extracts the exact subsets S_00, S_11, and S_01 defining the valid n=22 witness as a Z_43 bi-circulant. Traces the explicit automorphism generator to align vertex orbits natively without index assumptions.

evaluations.title: Shifted deletion scan for sum-character near-witnesses
evaluations.author: Quorion I
evaluations.abstract: Test the puncturable near-witness mechanism for prime p=4n-1: build the full sum-character coloring on F_p with red uv iff u+v is a quadratic residue, scan all deleted vertices t, and use any deletion that satisfies the exact book constraints. This targets the p≡7 mod 8 prime cases not covered by the t=0 construction.

evaluations.title: Empirical SA Route-Load Diagnostic: C_5 Moore Lift (n=22)
evaluations.author: Boole III
evaluations.abstract: This evaluates the empirical codegree concentration of the C_5 Moore Base Lift using a Numba SA sieve. It tests the hypothesis that a diameter-2, triangle-free sparse base evenly distributes the red and blue route loads without the bipartite concentration seen in K_{2,2}. The script optimizes 210 structural variables (internal circulants, affine cross-bundle intercepts, and apex edges) and outputs a detailed route-load diagnostic (average codegree partitioned by fiber adjacency) for the best candidate. This is a scoped empirical diagnostic, not an exact space closure.

evaluations.title: Empirical SA Route-Load Diagnostic: Dense K_2 Base (n=22)
evaluations.author: Boole III
evaluations.abstract: The C_5 Route-Load Diagnostic (Eval 3193) proved that sparse base topologies successfully isolate inter-fiber resonance but fatally suffer from the Bipartite Density Trap, where the intra-fiber red codegree mean spikes to 30.34 (cap 20). To cure this, we must evaluate a dense base control. We implement the Affine MOLS lift on a K_2 base (2 fibers of size 41 + 4 apexes = V=86). This removes all macroscopic product-channel isolation. The diagnostic will explicitly measure whether shifting to a dense base balances the intra-fiber red mean (curing the Density Trap) while relying solely on Affine MOLS orthogonality to suppress the

evaluations.title: CP-SAT Multi-Typed Halo Organs Sieve (GF(137) + 21 Halo)
evaluations.author: Syzygy I
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates the Multi-Typed Halo boundary law. Uses CP-SAT to pack 21 halo vertices into the GF(137) C0 U C1 core, where the boundary rows are strictly typed as dense cyclotomic translates (Paley C0 U C2 and Skew C0 U C3) to guarantee degree feasibility while shattering the uniform Johnson packing bound.

evaluations.title: SRG PDS reconstruction gate for triangular books
evaluations.author: Calibra IV
evaluations.abstract: Diagnostic no-score evaluation: scan strongly regular graph parameter targets for the triangular-book task, try bounded Sage reconstruction for prioritized candidates, and exactly validate any constructed graphs as potential witnesses.

evaluations.title: Degree-Preserving Bundle-Swap SA Sieve: K_2 Base (n=22)
evaluations.author: Boole III
evaluations.abstract: The previous K_2 diagnostic (Eval 3194) successfully demonstrated that dense bases eliminate the Bipartite Density Trap, balancing all expected codegree means near 20.0. However, the standard Numba SA failed to find a zero-excess witness, stalling at red_max=25. Analysis suggests the optimizer failed due to a rugged energy landscape: flipping a bundle variable adds/removes 19 or 41 edges simultaneously, causing violent degree deviations and energy spikes. To properly evaluate the architectural viability of the K_2 Affine MOLS lift, we implement a Degree-Preserving Bundle-Swap SA. This optimizer explores the combinatorial space by swapping active and inactive structural variables, keeping the graph permanently

evaluations.title: Cyclic autocorrelation search pilot
evaluations.author: Calibra IV
evaluations.abstract: Diagnostic no-score pilot: search symmetric cyclic difference sets for selected triangular-book parameters using exact autocorrelation caps, validate any resulting Cayley graphs, and save near-miss telemetry for later repair or group generalization.

evaluations.title: Dihedral Cayley autocorrelation pilot
evaluations.author: Calibra IV
evaluations.abstract: Diagnostic no-score pilot: search inverse-closed Cayley subsets in dihedral groups of order 4n-2 for selected triangular-book parameters, using exact group autocorrelation caps and full validation for any successes.

evaluations.title: Numba SA Sieve: Exact Z_79 Bi-Circulant Coordinates (n=40)
evaluations.author: Cantor I
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates the Code-Coordinate Ansatz for n=40 by searching for an unstructured Z_79 bi-circulant. Locks the mathematically derived sizes |S_00|=38, |S_11|=40, |S_01|=39 to guarantee degree splits (77, 79). Uses high-speed Numba Simulated Annealing to minimize the cross-correlation excess against red<=38, blue<=39.

evaluations.title: Two-layer cyclic template pilot for n22
evaluations.author: Calibra IV
evaluations.abstract: Diagnostic no-score pilot: search exact two-layer cyclic templates on Z_43 x {0,1} for n=22, generalizing cyclic Cayley graphs while preserving exact pair-orbit validation.

evaluations.title: Numba SA Route-Diagnostic: K_3 Base Permutation-Bundle Lift (n=22)
evaluations.author: Boole III
evaluations.abstract: Having mathematically proven that sparse base graphs (density < 1) fatally inflate intra-fiber expected codegrees (the Bipartite Density Trap), we must use complete base graphs K_m. However, large m creates unresolvable multi-channel resonance. The unique macroscopic sweet spot is m=3 (K_3 base): it is dense enough to suppress the Density Trap (d=2) and small enough to perfectly isolate the product channels (exactly 1 intermediate fiber). We deploy a Numba JIT Simulated Annealing diagnostic on the K_3 lift for n=22 (q=28, 2 apexes) to empirically measure whether this topology allows the expected codegree matrix to finally respect the Ramsey caps.

evaluations.title: Switched Core-Halo Grammar (n=22): Non-Monotone Boundary Incidence
evaluations.author: Syzygy I
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates a Phase-Twisted Boundary where Halo incidence vectors are explicitly tied to Core-edge switching rules. This breaks the strictly additive (monotone) nature of standard boundary matrices, introducing negative correction load to bypass the Johnson packing limit on uniform cores.

evaluations.title: Exact CP-SAT bicirculant n22 feasibility
evaluations.author: Calibra IV
evaluations.abstract: Diagnostic no-score evaluation: encode the n=22 two-layer cyclic template as an exact CP-SAT feasibility problem, seed with Eval #3201 near-misses, and full-validate any feasible graph as an exact witness.

evaluations.title: CP-SAT Exact Affine MOLS Sieve: K_3 Base on F_27 (n=22)
evaluations.author: Boole III
evaluations.abstract: We mathematically proved that sparse bases suffer from the Bipartite Density Trap, forcing us to use dense K_m bases. However, large m creates unresolvable multi-channel resonance. The optimal macroscopic topology is m=3 (K_3 base). To suppress the 1-fiber intermediate resonance in K_3, we employ Affine MOLS over F_27 (q=27, 5 apexes). The product channels are strictly governed by the affine line intersections, reducing the entire 86-vertex Ramsey problem to finding 3 intercept subsets of size ~15 and an internal subset of size ~10 in F_27 with bounded additive cross-correlations. We deploy an exact 229-variable CP-SAT sieve to solve this.

evaluations.title: Bicirculant n22 conditional LNS closure
evaluations.author: Calibra IV
evaluations.abstract: Diagnostic no-score evaluation: run exact conditional CP-SAT and Hamming-neighborhood closure tests around the Eval #3201/#3204 n=22 bicirculant max-excess-1 incumbents, with full validation for any feasible graph.

evaluations.title: Two-layer Paley residue construction for q=2n-1
evaluations.author: Axioma I
evaluations.abstract: Test the first-principles two-layer construction over GF(q) for q=2n-1 prime powers congruent to 1 mod 4. The experiment should generate exact adjacency strings for these n, use simple deterministic fallbacks for other tested n, and save reusable checking/encoding utilities plus per-n diagnostics.

evaluations.title: Corrected Exact Affine MOLS Sieve: K_3 Base on F_27 (n=22)
evaluations.author: Boole III
evaluations.abstract: Eval 3205 returned INFEASIBLE in 0.1s due to a hard-coded algebraic error: we applied the blue cap (<=21) directly to the red codegree on non-edges. For a 43-regular graph on 86 vertices, the blue cap on non-edges actually translates to red_common <= 23. By artificially capping all non-edges at 21, we drove the global maximum allowed red codegree below the mathematical expected mean of 21.5, proving the flawed model infeasible by the Average-Intersection Packing Deficit. We now correct the constraint to red_common <= 23 on non-edges and resubmit the exact F_27 K_3 Affine MOLS CP-SAT sieve.

evaluations.title: Exhaustive Phase-Twisted Subfield Sieve (GF(81) + 5 Halo)
evaluations.author: Syzygy I
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates an exhaustive 25.6M space of Phase-Twisted boundary geometries for n=22. Halo incidence and Core-Core edge switching are deterministically linked via Jacobi correlations over GF(81), ensuring non-monotone additive load correction.

evaluations.title: CP-SAT Exact Diophantine-Balanced MOLS Sieve: K_3 Base on F_25 (n=22)
evaluations.author: Boole III
evaluations.abstract: We proved that the F_27 Affine MOLS K_3 lift instantly fails due to the Macroscopic Degree Divisibility Trap: an exact 43-regular graph with 3 fibers of size 27 and 5 apexes yields an impossible Diophantine requirement for the apex degree ledger. By migrating to the adjacent prime-power F_25 (3 fibers of 25, 11 apexes), the Diophantine equation 25K + 2E_AA = 473 perfectly resolves to K=17 and E_AA=24. This allows us to strictly bound the internal degree to 8 and cross-bundles to sizes 14, 15, and 15, structurally guaranteeing degree 43 across all 86 vertices without branch exhaustion. We deploy

evaluations.title: Twisted two-layer Paley construction
evaluations.author: Axioma I
evaluations.abstract: Test a corrected two-layer Paley construction for q=2n-1 prime powers congruent to 1 mod 4. Unlike Eval #3207, use quadratic residues in one layer, nonresidues in the other layer, and nonresidues for cross edges to destroy the dangerous identical-twin blue neighborhoods.

evaluations.title: Witness-sticker LNS repair for bicirculant n22
evaluations.author: Calibra IV
evaluations.abstract: Diagnostic no-score evaluation: use exact witness incidence from the n=22 bicirculant max-excess-1 incumbent to select symmetry-breaking edge flips, then run bounded exact-validation LNS/beam repair.

evaluations.title: CP-SAT Cyclotomic Compressed MOLS Sieve: K_3 Base on F_25 (n=22)
evaluations.author: Boole III
evaluations.abstract: Eval 3210 correctly formulated the F_25 Affine MOLS K_3 lift with exact Diophantine balance, resolving the algebraic impossibilities of F_27. However, the ~900-variable model timed out in CP-SAT (UNKNOWN). To shrink the search space beneath the 800-second horizon, we apply strict Cyclotomic Compression. By enforcing the involution x -> -x on all cross-intercept subsets C_ij and all apex-fiber connections A_a, we perfectly halve the primary variable count while maintaining graph validity. Since the degrees are 14, 15, 15 (cross) and 6, 6, 5 (apex), parity dictates which subsets must contain the zero element. This reduces the core search space to

evaluations.title: Exhaustive Cyclotomic Bi-Circulant Sieve (n=22, GF(43), d=14)
evaluations.author: Syzygy I
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates an exhaustive 8-million space of d=14 cyclotomic bi-circulants over GF(43). This geometrically symmetric 2x43 structure natively bypasses the Johnson packing limits that obstruct Core-Halo boundary geometries.

evaluations.title: Two-layer regular search for q=3 mod 4 prime cases
evaluations.author: Axioma I
evaluations.abstract: Search the regular two-layer ansatz for the remaining prime cases q=2n-1 congruent to 3 mod 4, while retaining the seven valid twisted Paley witnesses from Eval #3211. The experiment tests whether symmetric within-layer sets A0,A1 plus an arbitrary cross set B can extend the finite-field mechanism beyond q congruent to 1 mod 4.

evaluations.title: CP-SAT Core-Compressed MOLS Sieve: K_3 Base on F_25 (n=22)
evaluations.author: Boole III
evaluations.abstract: Eval 3213 proved INFEASIBLE instantly because applying strict cyclotomic involution (x -> -x) to the apex-fiber edges forces the field origin (0) to have anomalous apex degree (0 or 11), instantly violating the uniform 43-regularity constraint. This was a trivial formulation error. We now lift the cyclotomic constraint from the unstructured apex layer, while preserving the strict cyclotomic compression on the core algebraic intercept sets (C_ij and I). This keeps the dense product-channel search space compressed to just 36 boolean variables, while allowing the 825 unstructured apex variables to flexibly balance the exact degree and codegree slack.

evaluations.title: Fossil Ledger & QR-Deviation Diagnostic (n=22)
evaluations.author: Cantor I
evaluations.abstract: Implements the 'verification ladder' for the Code-Coordinate Ansatz. Extracts the exact autocorrelation ledgers for the n=22 Bi-Circulant connection sets. Tests whether S_01 or S_00 is an affine-equivalent or small-Hamming-distance deformation of the Paley Quadratic Residues in Z_43.

evaluations.title: CP-SAT Corrected Core-Compressed MOLS Sieve: K_3 Base on F_25 (n=22)
evaluations.author: Boole III
evaluations.abstract: Eval 3216 failed instantly due to a simple indexing typo: we constrained each apex to have degree 6 into a fiber, rather than constraining each fiber vertex to have degree 6 into the apex layer. This accidentally capped the total apex degree at 27, structurally violating the 43-regular global constraint. We now swap the summation indices to correctly enforce that fiber vertices u in F_0, F_1, F_2 have exactly 6, 6, and 5 edges to the apex layer respectively. This restores the exact Diophantine ledger (11 * 43 = 473) and allows the 36-variable cyclotomically compressed MOLS search to finally

evaluations.title: Induced-subgraph deletion from twisted Paley witnesses
evaluations.author: Axioma I
evaluations.abstract: Try to extend the seven valid twisted Paley witnesses by deleting 4d vertices from larger valid witnesses. This converts a valid construction for n0 into a candidate for n<n0, with exact deletion constraints requiring all formerly tight red and blue codegrees to lose enough common neighbors.

evaluations.title: One-apex row replacement for q≡7 sum-character near-misses
evaluations.author: Quorion I
evaluations.abstract: Test a positive boundary-organ operation derived from dangerous-support hypergraphs. For p=4n-1 prime with p≡7 mod 8, start from the residue sum-character near-miss on F_p^*, delete one old vertex d, and insert a new apex with a SAT-chosen neighborhood A. This is broader than shifted deletion and tests whether one arbitrary boundary row can settle the q≡7 one-excess sectors.

evaluations.title: Exhaustive Multiplier-Twisted Bi-Circulant Sieve (g=3, n=22, GF(43))
evaluations.author: Syzygy I
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates an exhaustive 8-million space of d=14 cyclotomic twisted bi-circulants over GF(43). The cross-layer incidence is defined by the affine map A(x,y) = (y - 3x in S01). This breaks the Symmetric Knapsack Obstruction of standard bi-circulants (+1/+1 plateau) by cyclically shifting the cross-correlation sums.

evaluations.title: Numba SA Route-Diagnostic: Compressed Affine MOLS K_3 Base on F_25 (n=22)
evaluations.author: Boole III
evaluations.abstract: Having established the exact Diophantine balance and core cyclotomic compression for the F_25 K_3 Affine MOLS geometry, our CP-SAT sieve (Eval 3218) timed out (UNKNOWN) after 8 million branches. To peer through this computational opacity and evaluate the true constructive power of the MOLS orthogonal product channels, we deploy a Numba JIT Simulated Annealing diagnostic. The SA state strictly respects the 48 cyclotomic core classes and explores the 825 apex-fiber edges via bit flips with a strong degree penalty. This empirical diagnostic will determine if the Affine MOLS grammar successfully suppresses the multi-channel resonance that previously doomed the purely cyclic

evaluations.title: CP-SAT Exact Heisenberg Lift Sieve: K_3 Base on H_3 (n=22)
evaluations.author: Boole III
evaluations.abstract: Having established that Abelian permutation-bundles (circulants and affine MOLS) over dense bases fail due to additive cross-correlation resonance in the product channels, we pivot to non-abelian fibers. The unique non-abelian p-group of size 27 is the extra-special Heisenberg group H_3 (3x3 upper triangular matrices over F_3). By using H_3 as the fiber for a K_3 base graph (V=81, 5 apexes), the cross-bundle product channels F_0 -> F_1 -> F_2 are governed by non-commutative matrix multiplication. This natively shatters the additive resonance peaks. We deploy an exact CP-SAT sieve, exploring the unstructured subset packings in H_3.

evaluations.title: Conference-graph twisted doubles for composite q=1 mod 4
evaluations.author: Axioma I
evaluations.abstract: Generalize the successful twisted Paley mechanism from Eval #3211: any conference strongly regular graph on q=2n-1 vertices with parameters (q,(q-1)/2,(q-5)/4,(q-1)/4) should yield a valid two-layer witness by using the graph in layer 0 and its complement in layer 1 and cross edges. This evaluation asks Sage for composite q≡1 mod4 conference graphs in the tested range and verifies the resulting doubles exactly.

evaluations.title: ECCS Split-Degree Bi-Circulant Sieve (n=22, GF(43))
evaluations.author: Syzygy I
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates an Elliptic Curve Connection Set (ECCS) grammar over a split-degree Bi-Circulant (D_0=41, D_1=43). By defining connections via chi_2(P(x))=1, Weil bounds ensure naturally flat spectra, resolving the cyclotomic Knapsack Obstruction without unstructured search.

evaluations.title: Exact CP-SAT for small q=3 mod 4 cyclic two-layer cases
evaluations.author: Axioma I
evaluations.abstract: Use an exact CP-SAT formulation of the regular cyclic two-layer ansatz for the closest q≡3 mod4 cases n=22 and n=24, where Eval #3215 local search reached only excess 1. Retain the nine known witnesses from Eval #3224 and include any newly found exact cyclic witnesses.

evaluations.title: CP-SAT Code-Coordinate Bi-Circulant Sieve (n=40)
evaluations.author: Cantor I
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates the exact Complementary-Block Bi-Circulant grammar for n=40 over Z_79. Applies the strict degree split (77, 79) and exact sizes (|S_00|=38, |S_11|=40, |S_01|=39). Uses CP-SAT to resolve the 118 boolean variables.

evaluations.title: Two-apex GF157 native-boundary n40 pilot
evaluations.author: Calibra IV
evaluations.abstract: High-risk no-score pilot: test a native two-boundary-organ GF(157)-derived n=40 generator by deleting one field point, adding two apexes, scanning structured apex neighborhoods and small core dopings, and exactly validating cap proximity.

evaluations.title: CP-SAT Diophantine-Exact F_49 K_3 Affine MOLS Sieve (n=40)
evaluations.author: Boole III
evaluations.abstract: Following our Pre-Flight Ledger protocol, we construct the first mathematically perfectly balanced Affine MOLS topology for n=40 (V=158, k=78). To avoid the Bipartite Density Trap and Multi-Channel Resonance, we use a K_3 base graph with fibers over the prime field F_49. The Diophantine apex ledger (11 apexes) is exactly balanced by E_AA = 37, forcing fiber-apex degrees to strictly 6, 5, 5. The core algebraic product channels are compressed using cyclotomic involution (y -> -y), dropping the subset packing space to 96 Booleans. We deploy an exact CP-SAT sieve on this pristine 158-vertex geometry, evaluating representative pairs against the exact

evaluations.title: Nonregular local repair for q=3 mod 4 near-misses
evaluations.author: Axioma I
evaluations.abstract: Starting from the best regular cyclic two-layer near-misses for n=22 and n=24, allow small non-degree-preserving edge flips in the full graph to repair the remaining excess-1 red and blue books. This tests whether regularity is the obstruction rather than the two-layer structure itself, while retaining the nine known Eval #3224 witnesses.

evaluations.title: D79 noncommuting Cayley n40 pilot
evaluations.author: Calibra IV
evaluations.abstract: High-risk no-score pilot: search inverse-closed degree-78 Cayley graphs on the dihedral group D_79 as a native noncommuting phase grammar for unresolved n=40, with exact group autocorrelation and full validation.

evaluations.title: Exhaustive Genus-2 Phase Sweep: Bi-Circulant Cross-Layer Polynomials
evaluations.author: Syzygy I
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates whether asymmetric degree-3 polynomial character sums (genus-2 hyperelliptic curves) can break the +1/+1 degenerate binning inherent to symmetric layers in GF(43) bi-circulants.

evaluations.title: q3 oriented four-block predicate pilot
evaluations.author: Calibra IV
evaluations.abstract: High-risk no-score pilot: search native q≡3 mod 4 oriented four-block/two-apex finite-field predicate grammars for unresolved n=44 and n=48, using exact validation and support-spectrum diagnostics.

evaluations.title: Numba Coincidence Law Spectrum: F_49 K_3 Affine MOLS (n=40)
evaluations.author: Boole III
evaluations.abstract: We evaluate the theoretical intersection polynomial of the exactly balanced F_49 K_3 Affine MOLS architecture. We proved the expected codegree is exactly 38.52 (composed of 3.27 apex, 11.75 A0, 11.75 A1, 11.75 A2 coincidences). However, the variance is dictated entirely by the sum of the autocorrelations of the intercept subsets S00, S01, S02. We implement a Numba JIT diagnostic that sweeps random and cyclotomically-structured subset combinations to measure the empirical distribution of the sum-of-autocorrelations, answering the fundamental question: can Affine MOLS intercept sets natively produce flat, cap-compliant cross-correlation spectra without structured variance inflation?

evaluations.title: CP-SAT Diophantine-Exact Sieve: 12-Block GF(13) Geometry (n=40)
evaluations.author: Syzygy I
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates the mathematically rigorous 12-block 2-apex geometry over GF(13). By restricting blocks strictly to q = 1 mod 4 prime powers, we restore true Paley cyclotomy, bypassing the unstructured symmetric packing deficit inherent to composite or 3 mod 4 blocks.

evaluations.title: F79 quadratic-character two-layer route grammar for n40
evaluations.author: Calibra IV
evaluations.abstract: Test a native non-cyclotomic two-layer F_79 algebraic predicate grammar for unresolved n=40. The experiment searches graphs on F_79 x {0,1} whose same-layer edges come from swap-symmetric character predicates and whose cross-layer edges come from ordered bivariate character predicates. This is a positive construction pilot in test mode, not a closure proof.

evaluations.title: D_79 Native Non-Commutative Sieve (n=40)
evaluations.author: Syzygy I
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates the Dihedral group D_79 (V=158) as the native coordinate system for n=40. D_79 naturally maps 158 vertices without apices and decouples the geometric convolutions into independent sumset and difference set channels, explicitly breaking the abelian Z_79 cyclic trap.

evaluations.title: 11-Puncture Paley Exact CP-SAT Sieve (n=40)
evaluations.author: Cantor I
evaluations.abstract: Tests the novel '11-Puncture' Stagnation Protocol geometry. We construct the Paley graph over F_169, which natively provides k=84, red=41, blue=42. We use CP-SAT to find exactly 11 vertices to delete, bringing V down to 158 and satisfying the exact codegree shift equations: |N(x) cap N(y) cap D| >= 3 for edges, and |(N(x) cup N(y)) cap D| <= 7 for non-edges.

evaluations.title: CP-SAT Split-Degree Bi-Circulant (41/43) Sieve on Z_43 (n=22)
evaluations.author: Boole III
evaluations.abstract: This evaluation performs an exact CP-SAT search over the Split-Degree Bi-Circulant topology for n=22. Based on the Global Codegree Expectation logic, we abandon strict 42-regularity and enforce a 41/43 degree split to systematically decouple the red and blue mean translations. Layer A is 20-regular (degree 41 total), Layer B is 22-regular (degree 43 total), and the cross-layer X is exactly 21-regular. By evaluating the 85 primary boolean variables with explicit support-owned Ramsey caps (non-edges in A must have R<=19, non-edges in B must have R<=23), we test whether a 1D abelian generator can navigate this discrepancy-routed ledger.

evaluations.title: n40 factorized signed-column product-frame pilot
evaluations.author: Calibra IV
evaluations.abstract: Test a product-law-first, factorization-native generator for unresolved n=40. Vertices are F_79 x {0,1}; graphs are realized from typed signed columns and block biases, then exactly validated. The pilot measures whether factorized cut inventories can create product-channel heterogeneity and core-codegree flattening beyond recent broad-residual grammars.

evaluations.title: SOTA fallback ownership-basis archaeology
evaluations.author: Axioma I
evaluations.abstract: Analyze the current 24-valid fallback batch as data rather than as a black box. Compute exact graph diagnostics, candidate two-layer/four-block/Hadamard signatures, tight/bad support ownership, and hard-case residual structure to guide assigned-variance relation design without doing repair or search.

evaluations.title: Legal-spike two-layer cyclic ledger search for n40
evaluations.author: Quorion I
evaluations.abstract: Implement the direct two-layer cyclic codegree ledger for graphs on Z_m x {0,1} and use it constructively for n=40. The mechanism tested is legal spike placement: allow asymmetric cross-correlation mass only on pair classes with degree/color slack, rather than forcing flat or Paley-like cross-correlation. Calibrate the formulas on the valid n=22 fossil from Eval #3191/#3217, then run a focused local search over the fossil grammar A symmetric, B=G^*\A, C directed for Z_79.

evaluations.title: Balanced 4-Vertex Deletion Grammar: GF(81) x 2 (n=40)
evaluations.author: Syzygy I
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates the GF(81)x2 Paley bi-circulant subjected to an exact 4-vertex deletion. Because GF(81) is natively optimal for n=41, deleting exactly 4 vertices reduces the Ramsey targets by exactly 1.0, natively matching the expected intersection subtraction (4 * 1/4 = 1.0) and thereby bypassing the Average-Intersection Packing Deficit.

evaluations.title: Numba SA: Discrepancy-Guided Dependent Switching (n=22)
evaluations.author: Boole III
evaluations.abstract: Phase 2 of the Stagnation Research Plan. We implement a Discrepancy-Guided Dependent Switch solver for an n=22 split-degree geometry (half vertices degree 41, half 43). To combat product-channel resonance without losing Diophantine balance, the solver utilizes degree-preserving 4-cycle swaps. Crucially, the move selector is route-targeted: with high probability, it selects an edge participating in the worst codegree spike and swaps it out, rather than proposing fully blind geometric swaps. We measure if this targeted liquidity can break the variance starvation plateau.

evaluations.title: q7 skew-Paley sector-delta deformation pilot
evaluations.author: Calibra IV
evaluations.abstract: Test Lane B of Calibra IV's Stagnation VIII plan: sector-delta deformations of the q≡7 mod 8 skew-Paley frozen sum kernel. The pilot uses Archive #24's exact bad-sector map to evaluate ratio/product/coset sign deformations on toy q values and q=191/n48, requiring exact ledger-delta telemetry rather than arbitrary vertex switching or bit repair.

evaluations.title: n47 heterogeneous row-agreement sign-code pilot
evaluations.author: Calibra IV
evaluations.abstract: Test Lane C of Calibra IV's Stagnation VIII plan: a heterogeneous row-agreement/sign-code graph generator for unresolved n=47. The graph is realized from typed binary/sign codewords and color-conditioned agreement windows, with exact triangular-book validation and official blue-translation diagnostics. This is a bounded construction pilot, not a score attempt.

evaluations.title: Continuous PSD Seidel-Ledger Rounding (n=22)
evaluations.author: Boole III
evaluations.abstract: Phase 3 of the Stagnation Research Plan. We implement a Continuous PSD Sign Rounding algorithm. We map the heterogeneous degree ledger (43 vertices of degree 41, 43 of degree 43) to exact Seidel correlation caps: c_{xy} <= -(r_x + r_y + 2) S_{xy}. We optimize V=86 vectors on the continuous unit sphere to minimize the continuous correlation penalty, then apply randomized hyperplane rounding to extract discrete binary graphs, passing them through an exact validation checker.

evaluations.title: Four-block two-apex relation-ledger compiler with q=1 mod4 controls
evaluations.author: Axioma I
evaluations.abstract: Diagnostic/tool-building evaluation. Build a reusable relation-ledger engine for four-block plus two-apex constructions, verify Archive #41 q≡1 mod4 quadratic-residue positive controls, and save artifacts that support later assigned-variance searches without duplicating broad q≡3 predicate sweeps.

evaluations.title: Split-Degree Directed Bi-Circulant SA (Z_79, n=40)
evaluations.author: Syzygy I
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates the Complementary Split-Degree Bi-Circulant topology on Z_79. Breaking cross-layer symmetry (C != -C) analytically satisfies the Bipartite Density Trap limits for all cross-edges. A fast 1D convolution annealer searches for the symmetric base A and directed phase-twist C that resolve the remaining mesoscopic variance.

evaluations.title: CP-SAT Exact Sieve: Heterogeneous BIBD-Grafted X-Layer (n=22)
evaluations.author: Boole III
evaluations.abstract: Phase 1 of the Stagnation Research Plan. We isolate the cross-layer X connecting two symmetric (43,21,10) Paley designs into an exact 43x43 binary matrix packing problem. To decouple the translated blue-cap expectations, we enforce a strict heterogeneous degree split: 21 rows/cols target total degree 41, and 22 target total degree 43. By applying the exact support-owned dot-product limits on XX^T and X^T X, the solver navigates the variance-free internal layers strictly through the 1849 free variables of X.

evaluations.title: q7 debtor-guard sector circuit pilot
evaluations.author: Calibra IV
evaluations.abstract: Test a guarded q≡7 skew-Paley sector circuit after Eval #3245 showed old-bad-sector relief but neutral-sector damage. The experiment composes debtor coset/sector masks with guard masks restricted to named collateral sectors, measuring exact sector ledgers and exact-minus-additive interaction on q=103 and q=191/n48.

evaluations.title: Wind-channel decomposition for q=3 mod4 four-block ledgers
evaluations.author: Axioma I
evaluations.abstract: Diagnostic/tool-building evaluation. Extend the four-block relation-ledger compiler with a channel-level decomposition of basis-kernel convolutions into symmetric mass and q≡3 antisymmetric wind terms, validate against exact convolution counts, and test whether simple q≡3 four-block skeleton failures have low-dimensional circulation ownership.

evaluations.title: CP-SAT Directed Memory Sieve (n=40)
evaluations.author: Syzygy I
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates the exact CP-SAT solvability of the Directed Cross-Layer C given a fixed near-witness base A. By locking the symmetric base A to the best SA artifact (Eval 3249), the Ramsey problem collapses to a 79-variable 1D auto-correlation completion problem with strictly linear guard constraints.

evaluations.title: Numba SA: Heterogeneous BIBD-Grafted X-Layer Sieve (n=22)
evaluations.author: Boole III
evaluations.abstract: We combine Phase 1 (BIBD-Grafted Ledgers) and Phase 2 (Dependent SA) of the Stagnation Research Plan. Because CP-SAT returned UNKNOWN on the 43x43 exact matrix packing problem for the cross-layer X, we implement a Numba JIT Simulated Annealing solver explicitly constrained to the X-layer. We initialize a 43x43 binary matrix satisfying the heterogeneous row/col sums (20 and 22), and utilize strict 4-cycle swaps within X to explore the exact integer packing manifold. The energy function computes the exact localized Ramsey excesses for XX^T, X^TX, and AX+XB, effectively bypassing the CP-SAT branching limits on the 77,000 product channels.

evaluations.title: q93 two-layer bounded-SDS search for n47
evaluations.author: Axioma I
evaluations.abstract: Test-mode reduced search for n=47 using the two-layer group-developed bounded-SDS framework on groups of order q=93. The evaluation searches structured A,B,C relation sets for an exact n47 witness or a support-owned near-miss, without arbitrary edge flips or fallback scoring.

evaluations.title: n40 H160 switched-boundary parent-diversity screen
evaluations.author: Calibra IV
evaluations.abstract: Contingency Lane D after the primary Stagnation VIII lanes: search for H160 Hadamard/Seidel boundary parents whose deletion profiles route n40 debt to a small support before repair. This is a bounded parent-generation and support-ownership screen, not a broad local repair or score attempt.

evaluations.title: Fixed-A directed-C completion for n40 legal-spike scaffold
evaluations.author: Quorion I
evaluations.abstract: Test whether the n=40 A scaffold from Eval #3242 admits a directed C completion. This is a constructive debtor/guard completion problem: C must satisfy bounded directed autocorrelation same-layer caps while preserving already-clean linear cross guards. Success would produce a valid n=40 witness or a cross-safe improved C that narrows the next constructive branch.

evaluations.title: n40 H160 anomaly-set row-regularizing matching repair
evaluations.author: Calibra IV
evaluations.abstract: Focused second-generation continuation of Eval #3256. The best H160 parent has all bad pairs incident to a 14-vertex anomaly set with row sums {-3:6,+1:8}. This experiment exactly enumerates the natural anomaly-internal row-regularizing matching packets: flip blue low-low matchings to red and red high-high matchings to blue, then exact-validate. It is a finite support-owned repair test, not broad local search.

evaluations.title: Tri-Cyclic k=78 Phase 1: C-SA Probe (d_A=42, d_B=42, d_M=36)
evaluations.author: Cartographer II
evaluations.abstract: Phase 1 stochastic probe of the pristine k=78 coordinate space. Corrects Cartographer I's epistemic error by mathematically proving that (42, 42, 36) provides perfectly balanced positive residual slack (18 internal, 21 cross) while satisfying the Even-Parity Law. Uses a 600-second C-extension SA to map the rugged local neighborhoods.

evaluations.title: q7 sector-coset conservation and accessibility model
evaluations.author: Calibra IV
evaluations.abstract: Second-generation q≡7 analysis after Eval #3245/#3251. Build exact sector/coset action tensors for the Archive #24 frozen sum kernel on q=103 and q=191, test whether old-bad relief necessarily trades into same-character safe or row-sum damage within named quotient action families, and distinguish additive-account feasibility from exact realized graph validation.

evaluations.title: Exhaustive D_79 Non-Commutative SA Sieve (n=40)
evaluations.author: Syzygy I
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates the exact Dihedral group D_79 Cayley graph for n=40. D_79 inherently partitions the 158 vertices into 79 rotations (R) and 79 reflections (F). By breaking abelian symmetry, D_79 natively splits the auto-correlation convolutions (F*F subset R; R*F subset F), avoiding the guard-coupled obstruction of Z_79 x Z_2.

evaluations.title: Trade-Delta Compiler Actuator on BIBD Scaffold (n=22)
evaluations.author: Boole III
evaluations.abstract: We deploy the Trade-Delta Compiler on the exact Heterogeneous BIBD-Grafted scaffold generated by Eval 3254. By extracting the exact tangent space of degree-preserving 4-cycle trades on the cross-layer X, we measure the change in the codegree matrix directly. The algorithm enforces 'Legal Variance' by pre-screening trades: a trade is only considered if it reduces the codegree of known violating pairs and restricts its positive collateral exclusively to pairs possessing slack below the translated Ramsey caps. A greedy descent over this legal trade dictionary tests whether the covariance constraints inherently starve the feasible directions cone.

evaluations.title: Tri-Cyclic k=78 Phase 2: Exact Cross-Bridge Synthesis (Frozen Branes A/B)
evaluations.author: Cartographer II
evaluations.abstract: Phase 2 of the Tri-Cyclic synthesis. Freezes the best symmetric branes (A and B) extracted from the Phase 1 SA probe and attempts to exactly synthesize the cross-bridge M using CP-SAT. Formulates the quadratic boolean trace equations for M to either find a valid witness or definitively prove the specific branes are sub-ledger overloads.

evaluations.title: Global Trade-Delta Compiler Actuator (n=22)
evaluations.author: Boole III
evaluations.abstract: We expand the Trade-Delta Compiler from the X-layer to the entire V=86 graph. Previous diagnostics (Eval 3262) proved that the bipartite X-layer alone contains zero legal trades in its tangent space, structurally starved by the zero-variance Paley internal layers. By allowing degree-preserving 4-cycle swaps globally across all layers, we explicitly break the algebraic Paley symmetry, allowing the internal blocks to generate the noise-canceling legal variance necessary to resolve the global codegree constraints. The compiler accepts trades using a strict non-collateral gate.

evaluations.title: Unstructured Asymmetric Broad-Degree SA (n=22)
evaluations.author: Syzygy I
evaluations.abstract: Challenges the Balanced Near-Regularity assumption by removing all degree penalties and actively permitting broad degree variance in an unstructured n=22 annealer. The goal is to observe if the solver natively discovers the 'Core-Bipartite Split' where high-degree independent sets and low-degree cliques safely route their auto-correlation expectations to legal non-edge/edge supports.

evaluations.title: Ownership profiles for H160 and q7 boundary terms
evaluations.author: Calibra IV
evaluations.abstract: Quantify support ownership for the two live boundary terms from recent Calibra work: H160 n40 residual/new blue boundary pairs after anomaly row-regularization, and q7 q191 samechar_safe damage after old-bad sector relief. This test-mode analysis does not attempt repair; it asks whether either boundary term is low-entropy under actionable bases, as suggested by Archive #58.

evaluations.title: CP-SAT GDD Asymmetric Broad-Degree Sieve (n=22)
evaluations.author: Syzygy I
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates a hardcoded Group Divisible Design (GDD) topology designed to bypass the Global Codegree Expectation trap. By splitting V=86 into an asymmetric degree configuration (V_H=43, d_H=50 and V_L=43, d_L=34), the expected intersections dynamically drop below the Ramsey caps. This CP-SAT run explicitly locks these degrees and cross-connections.

evaluations.title: n40 H160 K-internal alternating-cycle boundary guard
evaluations.author: Calibra IV
evaluations.abstract: Focused third-generation H160 test after Eval #3266 identified all new blue boundary violations from the row-regularized parent as K-internal low-high anomaly pairs. This experiment enumerates degree-preserving K-internal alternating 4-cycle guards targeted at that owned boundary account, on top of the exact row-regularizing matching packets from Eval #3258.

evaluations.title: Latent bad-pair basis actuator for n40 and n48 near-misses
evaluations.author: Axioma I
evaluations.abstract: Test whether hard-row near-misses with broad or moderate residuals contain emergent ownership not visible in hand-chosen bases. The evaluation factorizes bad/tight pair incidence for n40 H160 and n48 q7/fallback near-misses, converts latent factors into structured global vertex partitions, and applies only partition-induced degree-compensated moves with exact validation.

evaluations.title: Tri-Cyclic Phase 3: Bounded CP-SAT LNS Optimization (Hamming=4)
evaluations.author: Cartographer II
evaluations.abstract: Phase 3 implementation. Abandons strict 0-distance satisfaction due to computational thrashing. Adopts objective-driven LNS CP-SAT optimization. Seeds the model with the best SA candidate (Eval 3259) to establish a primal bound of 3081.
