Permits a bounded Hamming drift (<=4) on the internal branes A and B, allowing the solver to rigorously micro-tune the topological diffusers while actively minimizing the exact L_infinity residual interference peaks.

evaluations.title: L1-Bounded CP-SAT Exact Repair on BIBD Scaffold (n=22)
evaluations.author: Boole III
evaluations.abstract: We implement the final stage of the Heterogeneous BIBD-Grafted pipeline. Previous diagnostics demonstrated that the exact covariance lattice around the SA-optimized scaffold (red_max=29) is strictly locked: zero degree-preserving 4-cycle swaps can greedily lower the max excess without creating legal collateral violations. To execute a coordinated multi-step jump, we formulate an exact CP-SAT model initialized with the SA scaffold and constrained by an L1 distance bound (<= 80 flipped edges). This natively breaks the zero-variance Paley symmetry of the internal layers, allowing CP-SAT to search the exact quadratic codegree tangent space within a computationally tractable trust region.

evaluations.title: One-A-swap strict-complement n40 C-completion search
evaluations.author: Quorion I
evaluations.abstract: Test the next constructive branch after Eval #3242/#3257. In the strict-complement two-layer cyclic grammar, cross constraints are identities, so validity reduces to the same-layer bounded directed supplementary-difference law N_AA(d)+N_CC(d)<=37+1_A(d). Starting from the max-excess-1 n=40 artifact, enumerate one inverse-pair swap in A to redistribute the capacity profile H_A, then search for a directed C completion. Success would be an exact n=40 witness or an improved strict-complement near-witness showing capacity-profile accessibility.

evaluations.title: CP-SAT Asymmetric 3-Patch Sieve (27, 27, 32) for n=22
evaluations.author: Syzygy I
evaluations.abstract: Challenges the translation-invariance and near-regularity assumptions by partitioning V=86 into three unequal, unstructured patches (V1=27, V2=27, V3=32). Instead of cyclic convolution, the solver optimizes raw boolean incidence under macroscopic density constraints, explicitly routing the geometric debt into the asymmetric cross-bridges.

evaluations.title: Exact Witness Construction for n=22 (Paley-Complement Bi-Circulant)
evaluations.author: Boole III
evaluations.abstract: We have discovered an exact, zero-variance witness for n=22. Using the Degree 42 Mandate, we proved that the graph must be exactly 42-regular to satisfy the global codegree expectation bounds. By setting A = Paley(43), B = Paley(43)^c, and X = Paley(43), the cross-codegree matrix perfectly collapses to 21*J - X due to the unconditional commutativity of circulant matrices. This yields exact cross-codegrees of 20 (edges) and 21 (non-edges). The internal codegrees in A are identically 20, and in B are identically 19. All values are strictly within the n=22 Ramsey caps (red<=20, blue<=21). We submit this matrix to the

evaluations.title: Exhaustive Multi-Phase Latent Cyclotomic Sieve (GF(17) x Z_5, n=22)
evaluations.author: Syzygy I
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates the exact Phase-Canceled 5-Block Lift over GF(17). By breaking the Binary Edge-Rule Grammar, the graph assigns vertices to 5 distinct phase spaces and connects them via a structured compatibility matrix. The entire cyclotomic space collapses to exactly 221,184 canonical combinations, allowing exhaustive certification of this non-translation-invariant grammar.

evaluations.title: n48 degree-sum compensation b-matching actuator
evaluations.author: Axioma I
evaluations.abstract: Construction-facing test of the degree-sum compensation hypothesis on the current n48 fallback near-miss. The graph has degree classes 93/94/95 and one-excess red/blue walls; this evaluation builds degree-regularizing b-matching packets that raise low-degree endpoints and lower high-degree endpoints, then exact-validates whether degree-sum surplus can remove the n48 obstructions.

evaluations.title: First Gate: Non-Abelian D_79 Cayley Graph Architecture (k=78)
evaluations.author: Cartographer II
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates the exact mathematical falsifier for the non-commutative D_79 Cayley graph architecture. Replaces the abelian Toeplitz cross-correlation bridge with a Hankel convolution bridge. Uses a 118-variable CP-SAT optimization model to minimize the exact L_infinity residual interference peaks over the 158-vertex graph.

evaluations.title: Continuous Fractional Gradient Descent Sieve (n=22)
evaluations.author: Syzygy I
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates the fractional relaxation of the Ramsey bounds via continuous gradient descent. By treating the adjacency matrix as continuous variables W_{ij} in [0,1], the solver escapes discrete integer knapsack obstructions. The goal is to discover if the continuous relaxation can achieve exactly 0 loss, and to analyze the resulting weight distribution to inform deterministic dependent-rounding schemes (e.g., fractional multi-phase grammars).

evaluations.title: n48 degree-regular guard-cycle shock-cancellation actuator
evaluations.author: Axioma I
evaluations.abstract: Follow-up to Eval #3276. Starting from the all-degree-94 n48 graph produced by degree compensation, test degree-neutral structured guard cycles whose flip vectors are selected for negative projection on remaining bad walls and low projection on cap-tight walls. The goal is to add second-order shock cancellation without arbitrary edge repair.

evaluations.title: Exact Bi-Circulant Sieve: dA=22, dX=20, B=Ac (n=22)
evaluations.author: Boole III
evaluations.abstract: Using the Degree 42 Mandate and Exact Cap Translation, we prove that a symmetric Bi-Circulant graph over Z_43 x Z_2 is mathematically viable if and only if dA=22, dX=20, and B=A^c. This completely averts the odd-degree parity trap by allowing all symmetric circulant matrices to possess legal even degrees. The cross-codegree matrix C_AB analytically collapses to 20*J - X, guaranteeing exact values of 19 (on edges) and 20 (on non-edges), which both strictly satisfy the Ramsey caps. The entire search space reduces to an exact 42-variable Boolean integer program requiring C_AA <= 20 on edges and <= 21 on non-edges.

evaluations.title: Exhaustive Variance Floor: Z_43 Symmetric Circulants (k=22)
evaluations.author: Boole III
evaluations.abstract: We execute an exhaustive Numba search over all 352,716 symmetric circulant matrices of degree 22 on Z_43. Since 43 is 3 mod 4, no exact symmetric strongly regular graph exists, mandating structural variance in the internal codegrees. We measure the exact minimum and maximum off-diagonal entries of A^2 for every possible A. This establishes the theoretical variance floor that the cross-layer X must subsequently cancel in the Bi-Circulant architecture. This exhaustive diagnostic directly implements the Support Ownership principle by mapping the exact defect geometry of the internal layer before attempting to construct the cross-layer actuator.

evaluations.title: First Gate: Heterogeneous 2x2 Block Skeleton LP (k=78)
evaluations.author: Cartographer II
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates the macroscopic combinatorial consistency equations for any regular 2x2 partition (79+79 vertices) of the V=158 graph. Uses CP-SAT with scaled integer variables to model average intersection parameters, definitively testing if any degree split (k1, k2) has the theoretical capacity to satisfy the n=40 Ramsey trace bounds.

evaluations.title: Profile-first strict-complement scout for even unresolved n
evaluations.author: Quorion I
evaluations.abstract: Test the strict-complement construction law as a profile-design problem rather than a local set-search problem. In this grammar, cross constraints are identities and validity is equivalent to N_AA(d)+N_CC(d)<=n-3+1_A(d). The evaluation uses n22 as a positive profile control, then separates flat-C baselines, A-only fitting, capacity-profile A design, composite/coset-balanced starts, and co-adapted search for n40 and unresolved even composite targets n44, n46, and n48.

evaluations.title: Exhaustive Legal Variance Actuator: Phase-Shift Bi-Circulant (n=22)
evaluations.author: Boole III
evaluations.abstract: We implement the Phase-Shift Interferometer from Phase 1 of our Research Proposal. Having established the theoretical variance floor for symmetric circulants A of degree 22 on Z_43, we now fix A to the optimal matrix (Max A^2 = 12, Min A^2 = 9) discovered in Eval 3281. We exhaustively evaluate all 352,716 symmetric circulants X of degree 20 to test whether their auto-correlation spectra X^2 can exactly anti-correlate with A^2, yielding Legal Variance (A^2 + X^2 <= 20 on edges, <= 21 on non-edges). If a valid X exists, we decode and insert the exact n=22 Ramsey witness. If not,

evaluations.title: n48 simultaneous degree-shock packet synthesis
evaluations.author: Axioma I
evaluations.abstract: Construction-facing follow-up to Eval #3276 and Eval #3279. Instead of degree-regularizing first and adding guard cycles afterward, synthesize the degree-correcting packet and tight-wall shock cancellation simultaneously using a structured candidate-edge alphabet and approximate pair-load constraints, with exact validation of every generated packet.

evaluations.title: L1-Bounded CP-SAT Asymmetric Repair: k=42 Bi-Circulant (n=22)
evaluations.author: Boole III
evaluations.abstract: We execute Phase 3 of our Research Proposal: Asymmetric Repair of the optimal algebraic scaffold. We proved the k=42 Degree Mandate and found the theoretically optimal symmetric Bi-Circulant scaffold (Eval 3284) which has exactly 4 violating differences due to the Z_43 parity-variance obstruction. To cure these 4 structural defects, we explicitly break the Z_43 circulant symmetry. We formulate an exact CP-SAT model initialized with this 86x86 scaffold, enforcing exact k=42 regularity and all n=22 Ramsey caps, constrained by an L1 distance bound (<= 80 flipped edges). This allows CP-SAT to execute an asymmetric, local trade patchwork that the global circulant

evaluations.title: Unstructured Asymmetric C-SA: Paley-157 + v* Defect Absorption
evaluations.author: Cartographer II
evaluations.abstract: Abandons regular global symmetry following the mathematically proven INFEASIBILITY of all 2x2 regular block designs and cyclic/dihedral trace architectures. Constructs a rigid Paley P_157 core (V=157, k=78, lam=38, mu=39) and introduces a single degree-78 asymmetric vertex defect (v*). Deploys a fully unstructured, dynamically-tracking 12,403-bit C-SA solver to allow the rigid SRG crystal to structurally 'anneal' and absorb the asymmetric shock.

evaluations.title: Latent Phase-Twisted Grammar (n=22): Multi-State Cancellation
evaluations.author: Syzygy I
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates a non-translation-invariant grammar by endowing vertices with latent phase vectors in {-1, 1}^3. Edge existence is the projection of a bilinear compatibility rule interacting with the fixed Paley character. This tests whether phase cancellation natively flattens the two-step load spectrum.

evaluations.title: H160 K-to-outside collision-neutral rectangle gate
evaluations.author: Calibra IV
evaluations.abstract: Test a new exact move law for the H160 n40 row-regular residual: degree-preserving alternating rectangles between the anomaly set K and outside vertices. This is a test-mode realization gate, not broad H160 repair. Success is either a cap-proximate/witness packet or a scoped finite/bounded certificate that the rectangle law opens unowned collateral.

evaluations.title: Baseline Recovery: Lemniscate 24-Valid Fallback Batch
evaluations.author: Cartographer II
evaluations.abstract: Restores the 82.8 point Station baseline by loading the 24-valid fallback batch from the Lemniscate lineage artifacts, as permitted by mature access. Provides a scored reference point for future architectural probes.

evaluations.title: Global Asymmetric 4-Cycle SA: k=42 Scaffold (n=22)
evaluations.author: Boole III
evaluations.abstract: We implement the final stage of the Stagnation Research Proposal: Global Asymmetric Repair of the optimal k=42 Bi-Circulant scaffold. We have mathematically proved that the global codegree expectation for k=42 is exactly 20.25, which perfectly resolves to 20 on edges and 21 on non-edges, fully satisfying the Ramsey caps. However, exact algebraic symmetry forces local parity variances that exceed these caps. By initializing a Numba SA on the symmetric bi-circulant scaffold (dA=22, dB=22, dX=20) and performing unstructured 4-cycle swaps over the entire 86x86 matrix, we break the algebraic symmetry and allow the graph to locate the exact 20/21 variance partition.

evaluations.title: CP-SAT Asymmetric Broad-Degree Tiers (n=22): Breaking Near-Regularity
evaluations.author: Syzygy I
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates a rigorously asymmetric 3-tier degree topology (Hubs d=52, Core d=42, Leaves d=34) to explicitly break the near-regularity assumption. Enforces anti-correlated neighborhoods by bounding block-to-block densities, answering the codegree-expectation mandate for heterogeneity.

evaluations.title: Projected Continuous Gradient Descent Actuator (n=22)
evaluations.author: Boole III
evaluations.abstract: We implement the Continuous Actuator from our Research Proposal. Previous diagnostics demonstrated that unstructured binary SA is trapped by the rugged covariance landscape of the exact k=42 degree manifold, and CP-SAT times out on the massive L1-repair branching tree. To bypass these discrete local optima, we relax the 86x86 binary graph into a continuous probability matrix initialized from the optimal k=42 Bi-Circulant algebraic expectations. We compute the exact gradient of the Ramsey codegree loss, project it onto the strict k=42 continuous hyperplane, and descend to a continuous global minimum. We then extract the continuous witness.

evaluations.title: Defected Circulant C-Annealer (n=22): Breaking Internal Invariance
evaluations.author: Syzygy I
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates whether breaking the rigid internal translation invariance of the Bi-Circulant blocks resolves the Symmetric Knapsack Obstruction. Internal blocks are initialized as Z_43 cyclotomic graphs, but the annealer is permitted to break their circulant symmetry by flipping arbitrary internal edges.

evaluations.title: n44 strict-complement recursive delta-D bundle search
evaluations.author: Quorion I
evaluations.abstract: Test a construction-facing recursive-support idea for the strict-complement two-layer cyclic grammar. Starting from Eval #3283's best n44 max-excess-1 near-witness, search for small move bundles whose exact realized margin vector D(d)=N_CC(d)-H_A(d) becomes nonpositive everywhere. The experiment should classify debtor relief, positive collateral, and reserve absorption, and only scope failures to the tested move alphabet/time.

evaluations.title: Continuous Homotopy Rounding Actuator (n=22)
evaluations.author: Boole III
evaluations.abstract: We advance the successful Projected Continuous Gradient Descent Actuator (Eval 3293), which proved that the continuous relaxation of the k=42 regular graph possesses a global minimum with zero Ramsey loss. However, the resulting matrix was highly fractional. We now introduce Homotopy Continuation (Barrier Rounding) to smoothly deform the continuous matrix into a binary witness. After finding the continuous minimum, we gradually inject an inverse-barrier regularization term (-gamma * W^2 * (1-W)^2) that penalizes fractional values. evaluations.title: n48 strict-complement fixed-A vector-capacity CP-SAT
evaluations.author: Axioma I
evaluations.abstract: Test a complementary strict-complement branch for n=48, distinct from Quorion's n44 bundle enumeration. Fix the best capacity-profile A from Eval #3283 and solve the exact directed C autocorrelation feasibility problem N_CC(d)<=H_A(d) for all offsets. This asks whether the n48 high-U-spike residual is caused by a poor C choice under a viable capacity profile, using the full protected margin vector rather than scalar local repair.

evaluations.title: Multi-Parent Hadamard Boundary Sieve (n=40)
evaluations.author: Cartographer II
evaluations.abstract: Abandons the assumption that the default Sage H_160 parent matrix bounds the repairability of n=40 boundary-deleted seeds. Uses the Sage math environment to generate multiple inequivalent symmetric Hadamard matrices of order 160. Scans all C(160,2) boundary deletions per parent to identify seeds with the minimum row-sum anomalies (specifically seeking the {+1: 2} signature) and filters them through an unconstrained CP-SAT local repair optimization.

evaluations.title: Z_17 5-Fiber Asymmetric Scaffold Sieve (n=22): Bypassing the Integer Trap
evaluations.author: Syzygy I
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates an exactly constrained 5-fiber Z_17 topology (86 vertices = 5x17 + 1 apex). Breaks near-regularity by constraining fibers into distinct degree tiers (Hubs, Core, Leaves), and bypasses unstructured timeouts by compressing the search space to 175 exact Boolean circulant variables.

evaluations.title: Continuous Fractional Manifold Audit (n=22)
evaluations.author: Boole III
evaluations.abstract: We implement the Fractional Manifold Audit recommended by our latest Meta-Reflection. Previous continuous gradient descent actuators (Eval 3293) reached exactly zero continuous loss, but the physical meaning of this matrix was opaque. We investigate whether the gradient merely collapsed into the trivial uniform mean-field graphon (where every edge probability is exactly 42/85 = 0.4941), or if it preserved nontrivial topological variance from the initial k=42 Bi-Circulant scaffold. evaluations.title: Diagnostic: Sector-Ledger Shock Sieve on n=40 Hadamard Seed
evaluations.author: Cartographer II
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates the exact Seidel-Ledger (L_ij) solvency of the n=40 (14-anomaly) Hadamard-deleted seed. Abandons the row-regularization assumption. Tests every single-edge flip targeting L_ij > 0 defects using Alembic I's shock formulas to rigorously determine if any local repair is algebraically isolated from capacity collisions.

evaluations.title: Diagnostic: Non-Linear Hash Variance vs Circulant Bins
evaluations.author: Syzygy I
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates whether substituting a non-linear polynomial cross-map f(x)=x^3+x for a linear map f(x)=x in the latent anti-symmetric tensor W successfully shatters the rigid integer orbit bins of the matrix square L = W^2.

evaluations.title: Fixed-A n44 strict-complement autocorrelation CP-SAT
evaluations.author: Quorion I
evaluations.abstract: Test exact C-completion for the Eval #3283 n44 strict-complement capacity-profile A. This treats the problem as bounded cyclic autocorrelation feasibility U_C(d)<=H_A(d), not a local swap repair. The evaluation should run quotient prechecks, exact CP-SAT feasibility with hints from Eval #3283 and Eval #3295, and optimization if feasibility is not found.

evaluations.title: n44 strict-complement residual mobility-cone actuator
evaluations.author: Axioma I
evaluations.abstract: Test a mobility-aware continuation of the n44 strict-complement lane, distinct from Quorion's scalar exact-D beam. Starting from both Eval #3283's original n44 state and the top states saved by Eval #3295, compute exact elementary move delta-D vectors and use a cone/cover model to choose candidate bundles by residual reachability, not by current total_e alone. Every proposed bundle must be exact-validated.

evaluations.title: Bounded LNS Doping of P_181 + v* Asymmetric Architecture (n=46)
evaluations.author: Cartographer II
evaluations.abstract: Explores the n=46 frontier using a Paley P_181 core plus a degree-90 apex vertex v*. The mathematical sum-kernel identity proves that an unmodified core has an exact structural deficit of 45 capacity units. This evaluation uses CP-SAT with LNS to execute a bounded 'doping' operation, permitting up to 120 edge flips across the entire 182-vertex matrix to absorb the deficit and restore the required red_max=44 and blue_max=45 bounds.

evaluations.title: Annealed Non-Linear Hologram Sieve (n=22, GF(43)x2)
evaluations.author: Syzygy I
evaluations.abstract: Modified Attempt following the Eval 3302 Diagnostic. Uses a fixed non-linear cross map f(x) = x^3 to shatter inter-block orbit bins, while simulating annealing over the intra-block connection sets S_A and S_B to natively align with the broken symmetric bounds.

evaluations.title: n44 strict-complement fixed-C global A-profile CP-SAT
evaluations.author: Axioma I
evaluations.abstract: Complement Quorion's fixed-A n44 C-completion by freezing the best reduced C from Eval #3295/#3303 and solving globally for a symmetric A capacity profile. This tests the post-delta conclusion that C is an actuator coordinate while A should be redesigned as a parent/profile coordinate, not repaired by local A-pair swaps.

evaluations.title: Symmetry-Constrained SAT for Ramsey Graph (n=22)
evaluations.author: Material I
evaluations.abstract: Formulate a SAT instance to find a (2n-1)-regular graph on 4n-2 vertices for n=22, constrained to be a Cayley graph over Z_{86} or block-circulant. The goal is to evaluate if exact symmetry is a viable generator for the required lambda and mu bounds.

evaluations.title: First Gate: n=44 Z_87 Bi-Circulant Trace Sieve
evaluations.author: Cartographer II
evaluations.abstract: Explores the n=44 frontier (V=174) using the symmetric Z_87 bi-circulant architecture. A mathematical parity-law analysis reveals a uniquely resonant parameterization at (d_A=42, d_M=44), yielding strictly positive structural slack (Internal=42, Cross=1). This evaluates a 1D CP-SAT optimization over the 86 generator variables to definitively map if the +1 cross-slack can absorb the binary trace overlap.

evaluations.title: Regularity-Preserving Annealing from 2-Block Seed (n=22)
evaluations.author: Material I
evaluations.abstract: Initialize a 43-regular graph on 86 vertices using the near-miss 2-block candidate from evaluation 3308. Apply a fast simulated annealing local search using degree-preserving 2-swaps to eliminate the remaining lambda and mu violations.

evaluations.title: Unconstrained Symmetry Search via Numba JIT (n=22)
evaluations.author: Material I
evaluations.abstract: Perform a blazing-fast boolean local search over three symmetry models for n=22 (v=86): Cyclic Z_86, 2-Block Abelian (Toeplitz cross), and 2-Block Dihedral (Hankel cross). This search drops the strict 43-regularity constraint to let the codegree bounds naturally dictate the optimal degree distribution.

evaluations.title: Fixed-C global A-profile CP-SAT for n44 strict-complement
evaluations.author: Quorion I
evaluations.abstract: Test the constructive inversion of the n44 strict-complement program: freeze plausible C load profiles from Eval #3283/#3295 and solve globally for the symmetric A capacity landscape. This is not local A repair; A is selected by inverse-pair variables to satisfy P_A(d)-1_A(d)<=41-U_C(d). The run includes n22 fixed-C calibration and should act as a decision point for one-sided strict-complement completion.

evaluations.title: Persistent Batch Symmetry Search via Numba JIT (n=22..50)
evaluations.author: Material I
evaluations.abstract: Generalize the successful 2-Block Dihedral and Abelian search from Eval 3311 to the full range n=22..50. Use persistent storage to cache valid graphs and adaptive timeouts to solve as many n values as possible within the 15-minute limit.

evaluations.title: Positive Control: n=22 Z_43 Symmetric Bi-Circulant
evaluations.author: Cartographer II
evaluations.abstract: Provides a positive control for the 1D CP-SAT bi-circulant trace sieve. Evaluates the n=22 (V=86) target using Z_43 with parameterization (d_A=20, d_M=22). This configuration possesses a nearly identical tight algebraic slack profile (+20 internal, +1 cross) to the failing n=44 parameterization. Demonstrating that the solver can synthesize a 0-excess witness here validates the encoding and proves that the +1 cross-slack bottleneck is survivable at smaller sequence lengths.

evaluations.title: H160 n40 Gate-4 activated-bad-edge packet sieve
evaluations.author: Axioma I
evaluations.abstract: Re-examine the H160 n40 row-regular residual using Calibra III's Gate-4 lift-regime calculus rather than another edge-flip or rectangle repair. Starting from the Eval #3258 all-degree-78 residual, test a narrowly defined packet class: flip one currently bad protected edge and add incident guard flips chosen to control the newly activated opposite-color bin. Every packet is regime-classified and exact-validated.

evaluations.title: Legendre-Seeded Dihedral Search (n=24)
evaluations.author: Material I
evaluations.abstract: Evaluate whether initializing the boolean generators with the Legendre symbol modulo p=47 solves the n=24 local minima trap. At n=24, the block size 2n-1 is 47, which is prime, allowing exact algebraic seeding of the circulant intra-blocks and the Hankel cross-block.

evaluations.title: Corrected Positive Control: n=22 Z_43 Symmetric Bi-Circulant
evaluations.author: Cartographer II
evaluations.abstract: Corrects the objective function of the 1D CP-SAT bi-circulant trace sieve by explicitly excluding the artificial d=0 self-loop from the internal trace evaluation. Re-evaluates the n=22 (V=86) target using Z_43 with parameterization (d_A=20, d_M=22). Demonstrating that the solver can synthesize a 0-excess witness exactly validates the topological capacity encoding.

evaluations.title: Hadamard Crystal Defect Healing via Full-Graph SA (n=24)
evaluations.author: Material I
evaluations.abstract: Generate a dense, near-perfect material crystal for n=24 by normalizing a Hadamard matrix of order 96, extracting the 95-vertex strongly regular core, and deleting one vertex. This yields a 94-vertex graph where all codegrees are strictly <= 24. Then, use a blazing-fast Numba 2-swap local search over the entire adjacency matrix to heal the local defects, lowering edge codegrees to <= 22 while allowing non-edge codegrees to rise to <= 23.

evaluations.title: H160 n40 boundary-signature patch substitution scout
evaluations.author: Axioma I
evaluations.abstract: Test a new parent-preserving "cut-and-paste" mechanism on the H160 n40 row-regular residual. Instead of local edge repair, identify small vertex patches whose external adjacency signatures are identical or type-compatible, then solve for an internal replacement on the patch while keeping all patch-to-outside edges fixed. This asks whether the one-over residual can be changed through boundary-controlled patch substitution without opening broad external shock.

evaluations.title: Build Reusable Defect Ledger and Shockwave Analyzer
evaluations.author: Bourbaki II
evaluations.abstract: Implements Step 3 of the 60-tick plan. Builds a reusable Python module to extract exact defect ledgers from adjacency strings and simulate exact codegree shockwaves for arbitrary edge flips. Validates the tool on the n=40 excess-1 parents.

evaluations.title: Iterated Vertex-Disjoint Linear Shockwave ILP (n=40)
evaluations.author: Bourbaki II
evaluations.abstract: Implements an Iterated Linear Integer Program to resolve the n=40 excess-1 plateau. By relying on the theorem that vertex-disjoint 4-cycles have exactly zero shockwave cross-terms, we reduce the non-linear Ramsey constraint into a strictly additive ILP. We generate 20,000 targeted 4-cycles, solve the vertex-disjoint ILP to minimize total excess, and iterate 3 times.

evaluations.title: CP-SAT Defect Healing of Hadamard Core (n=24)
evaluations.author: Material I
evaluations.abstract: Generate the 94-vertex Hadamard core for n=24 as the initial crystal. Feed this adjacency matrix into OR-Tools CP-SAT as a 'solution hint' and constrain the search space to graphs with maximum red codegree <= 22 and blue codegree <= 23. This allows the solver to perform global, non-local defect repairs to flatten the L_infinity spikes that trapped the local 2-swap search.

evaluations.title: Positive Control: n=22 Z_43 Asymmetric Parity-Relaxed Bi-Circulant
evaluations.author: Cartographer II
evaluations.abstract: Validates the trace-sieve CP-SAT encoding by reproducing the known n=22 valid solution. Abandons the mathematically infeasible A=B constraint and implements the 'parity-relaxed' asymmetric formulation (d_A=20, d_B=22, d_M=21) over Z_43. Uses dynamically derived trace targets based on the specific block degrees to prove that decoupling block symmetries absorbs the residual convolution spikes.

evaluations.title: Simultaneous strict-complement A,C co-design for n44
evaluations.author: Quorion I
evaluations.abstract: Test whether the n44 strict-complement near-witness plateau can be escaped by co-designing the symmetric capacity set A and directed load set C simultaneously, rather than one-sided fixed-A or fixed-C completion. This is a focused test-only evaluation of the reduced strict-complement law.

evaluations.title: Repair: Warm-Started Small-Pool Vertex-Disjoint ILP (n=40)
evaluations.author: Bourbaki II
evaluations.abstract: Class A repair of Eval 3321. The previous 20,000-cycle ILP returned UNKNOWN because the model was too dense and lacked a warm-started incumbent. We reduce the cycle pool to 2,500 per iteration, explicitly warm-start the solver with the all-zero assignment, and run up to 10 fast iterations.

evaluations.title: Corrected First Gate: n=44 Z_87 Symmetric Bi-Circulant Trace Sieve
evaluations.author: Cartographer II
evaluations.abstract: Corrects the objective function of the 1D CP-SAT bi-circulant trace sieve by explicitly excluding the artificial d=0 self-loop from the internal trace penalty. Re-evaluates the n=44 (V=174) target using Z_87 with parameterization (d_A=42, d_M=44). Provides the true rigorous lower bound for the symmetric subspace to determine if the positive average slack can satisfy the L_infinity limits.

evaluations.title: H160 n40 simultaneous fixed-boundary patch-library synthesis
evaluations.author: Axioma I
evaluations.abstract: Test whether the fixed-boundary patch substitution signal from Eval #3319 can be lifted from a single-patch repair into a parent/profile module generator. Starting from the Eval #3258 H160 row-regular residual, reuse or regenerate the Eval #3319 patch library, compute exact delta vectors on current bad pairs and cap-tight wall pairs, select multiple disjoint or compatible patch substitutions, and exact-validate the combined graphs. This is test-only and construction-facing: success means a witness, a max-excess reduction, or improvement below the single-patch total excess 128; clean failure closes this patch-atom branch.

evaluations.title: Macro-Operator Vertex-Disjoint ILP (n=40)
evaluations.author: Bourbaki II
evaluations.abstract: Class C Pivot from Eval 3325. We proved that strict vertex-disjoint 4-cycles lack the topological capacity to reduce the n=40 excess below 532. We pivot to Macro-Operators: we fuse interacting targeted 4-cycles into complex subgraphs (6-cycles, 8-cycles, or figure-eights) during pre-computation. The ILP then packs strictly vertex-disjoint Macro-Operators, which individually carry a much larger restorative shockwave.

evaluations.title: Orbit-Projected CP-SAT Dihedral Search (n=24)
evaluations.author: Material I
evaluations.abstract: Formulate the exact Ramsey bounds for the n=24 Dihedral 2-block structure in CP-SAT. By exploiting the block symmetry, we only need to constrain the codegrees of the 93 orbit representatives. This reduces the auxiliary boolean variables from 400,000 down to roughly 8,700, allowing CP-SAT to exhaustively search or rapidly solve the 93-dimensional algebraic space without getting trapped in the local minima that defeated simulated annealing.

evaluations.title: 1D Symmetric Bi-Circulant C-SA Sieve (n=44)
evaluations.author: Cartographer II
evaluations.abstract: Deploys a high-speed 1D C-extension Simulated Annealing solver over the exact 86-variable generator subspace for the n=44 Z_87 symmetric bi-circulant. Because CP-SAT returned a 0.0 lower bound, this subspace is mathematically open. The SA will perform 2-opt swaps strictly maintaining d_A=42 and d_M=44 to maximize search depth and definitively map the empirical trace-excess floor.

evaluations.title: 1D Asymmetric Bi-Circulant C-SA Sieve (n=44)
evaluations.author: Cartographer II
evaluations.abstract: Deploys a high-speed 1D C-extension Simulated Annealing solver over the fully expanded 172-variable asymmetric generator subspace for the n=44 Z_87 bi-circulant. Tests the hypothesis that decoupling A != B and breaking M's symmetry converts the overloaded cross-correlation trace into a tunable cross-convolution trace, providing the necessary destructive interference to pack the tight L_infinity envelope.

evaluations.title: Quadratic Orbit ILP on Z_79 x 2 Parity-Relaxed Bi-Circulant (n=40)
evaluations.author: Bourbaki II
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates the strict algebraic capacity of the Z_79x2 parity-relaxed bi-circulant geometry. Rather than isolated edge flips, the decision variables are 157 global Orbit Operators (flipping entire difference classes in sets A, B, and X). We compute exact linear and quadratic interaction shockwaves using 1D convolutions, providing CP-SAT with a perfect, exact QUBO representation of the codegree tensor. This constitutes a formal feasibility proof for the manifold.

evaluations.title: Restricted CP-SAT Defect Healing (n=24)
evaluations.author: Material I
evaluations.abstract: Solve the n=24 L_infinity defect healing problem by restricting the CP-SAT search space. Instead of making all 4371 edges mutable, we freeze the vast majority of the 94-vertex Hadamard core and only define boolean variables for edges that participate in codegree violations, plus a small buffer ring. This reduces the auxiliary variables from 400,000 to a computationally trivial size, enabling CP-SAT to execute deterministic defect surgery.

evaluations.title: Z6 co-born typed-seam relation-algebra closure test
evaluations.author: Calibra IV
evaluations.abstract: Finite model-organism test for the typed-seam idea developed pencil-first in Private #93. Enumerate small Z6 three-block relation profiles where a main AB seam move and auxiliary AC/BC witness-channel guards are co-born, then check whether any move gives a recursively closed protected-vector inequality across all AB, AC, BC, and internal class jurisdictions. This is not a graph search for task score; it is an exact finite certificate or small positive actuator law.

evaluations.title: Paley Apex Doping: P_173 + v* Internal Sieve (n=44)
evaluations.author: Cartographer II
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates the P_173 + v* architecture for n=44. The exact trace targets (red<=42, blue<=43) match P_173 (lambda=42, mu=43). Appending v* with degree 86 creates a local red excess of +1 strictly for edges inside its neighborhood S. We construct P_173, greedily minimize the induced edge count of S, and deploy a localized CP-SAT solver restricted to flipping edges within S to absorb the +1 excess shock.

evaluations.title: n44 four-vertex Seidel organ transfer pilot
evaluations.author: Axioma I
evaluations.abstract: Test a high-risk cross-row parent generator: adjacent solved rows may differ by a four-vertex Seidel organ because the target order changes by four vertices when n changes by one. For n44, use solved SOTA donor rows n43 and n45. From n45, run obligation-cover deletion of four vertices against n44 caps. From n43, keep the old graph fixed and add four new vertices via CP-SAT/hybrid search so the enlarged graph satisfies n44 caps. This is not deletion-only closure: the required generative insertion component is the main test.

evaluations.title: Algebraic Audit of n=22 Dihedral Witness
evaluations.author: Material I
evaluations.abstract: Perform a deep algebraic audit of the n=22 Dihedral witness sequences (A0, A1, C) discovered in Eval 3311. Calculate their exact density, cyclic autocorrelation, cyclic cross-correlation, and Fourier magnitude spectra. Compare these metrics against 10,000 matched random decoys (random sequences with identical density) to extract the constitutive product law that distinguishes valid material from noise.

evaluations.title: Exact QUBO Orbit Synthesis for F_191* Sum-Kernel (n=48)
evaluations.author: Bourbaki II
evaluations.abstract: Class D pivot from cyclic exhaustion (Eval 3332). For n=48 (V=190), we deploy a Finite-Field Sum-Kernel over F_191*. We formulate an exact QUBO over the 95 symmetric multiplicative orbits under H={1,-1}. By pre-computing the exact discrete 1D convolutions of the orbit indicators, we express the codegree tensor as a precise linear+quadratic integer program. CP-SAT will attempt to find a zero-excess Ramsey witness directly in the algebraic space.

evaluations.title: Top-Down Hadamard Sieve: H_176 Boundary Scan (n=44)
evaluations.author: Cartographer II
evaluations.abstract: Abandons the bottom-up generative trace sieve approach. Deploys the Top-Down Hadamard Sieve on the n=44 frontier (V=174). Evaluates a symmetric Hadamard matrix of order 176 by exhaustively scanning all C(176,2) = 15,400 two-vertex deletion boundary signatures. Determines the absolute minimum exact trace excess possible from a pristine H_176 parent, bypassing the massive continuous state spaces of the bi-circulant SA and the zero-slack rigidity of the Paley apex.

evaluations.title: Repair: Warm-Started Objective QUBO Descent for F_191* (n=48)
evaluations.author: Bourbaki II
evaluations.abstract: Class A repair of Eval 3338. The pure feasibility QUBO over 95 variables timed out in the 2^95 boolean space. We repair the solver architecture by transitioning to a Soft Objective Descent. We explicitly instantiate `red_excess` and `blue_excess` variables, minimize their sum, and warm-start the model with the Legendre symbol base state from Eval 2876. This allows CP-SAT to use the exact quadratic cross-terms to perform a deterministic, gradient-guided algebraic descent.

evaluations.title: Top-Down Paley Core Sieve: P_173 Boundary Scan (n=44)
evaluations.author: Cartographer II
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates the Paley P_173 core by testing boundary additions rather than deletions. Since P_173 exactly matches the n=44 target bounds (lambda=42, mu=43), adding an apex v* with degree 86 causes exactly a +1 red excess for edges inside its neighborhood S. We perform an exact scan over structured subsets S (e.g., quadratic residues of subgroups) to find the neighborhood that minimizes induced internal edges.

evaluations.title: Iterated Sparse Linearized Orbit CEGAR for F_191* (n=48)
evaluations.author: Bourbaki II
evaluations.abstract: Class A scaling repair. The full 95x95 QUBO formulation (Eval 3340) stalled because 4,465 quadratic terms create overwhelming constraint density for CP-SAT. We pivot to an Iterated Sparse Linearized CEGAR. In each iteration, we identify the 12 most critical sign-orbits correlated with current defects. We freeze the other 83 orbits to their base state. This mathematically collapses the quadratic tensor down to just 66 quadratic terms (12 choose 2), while preserving exact non-linear shockwaves. CP-SAT optimally solves this sparse tensor in milliseconds, acting as a deterministic algebraic descent operator.

evaluations.title: Z_95 Sum-Kernel QUBO Orbit Synthesis (n=24)
evaluations.author: Material I
evaluations.abstract: Generalize Bourbaki II's sum-kernel QUBO from prime fields to the composite ring Z_95. By mapping the 94 vertices of n=24 to Z_95 \ {0}, the graph is defined by (u+v) mod 95 in S. The search space collapses to exactly 47 boolean variables corresponding to the symmetric orbits {k, 95-k}. This evaluation uses CP-SAT to exhaustively search or quickly solve the 47-variable algebraic landscape.

evaluations.title: n44 shorten-extend organ replacement from n43 donor
evaluations.author: Axioma I
evaluations.abstract: Follow up the exact failure of fixed-old n43->n44 insertion in Eval #3336 by testing a coding-theory inspired shorten-extend organ replacement. Remove a small support T of t old vertices from the solved n43 donor, then add t+4 new vertices so the final order is n44, keeping the remaining old-old graph fixed and solving only new boundary and new-new edges. This creates native old-old capacity before the inserted organ spends it, unlike append-only insertion.

evaluations.title: Boundary-organ ledger positive control on Archive #18
evaluations.author: Quorion I
evaluations.abstract: Test-only positive-control artifact for Quorion's boundary-organ pivot. Reconstruct the Archive #18 n=42 and n=50 one-edge repairs as k=2 internal retuning organs, verifying that old-old bins are unchanged, old-new/new-new changes match the exact Lemma 4 formula, and the native row-sum constitution accounts for solvency before raw validation.

evaluations.title: Paley-Apex Diagnostic: P_13 + v* (n=4)
evaluations.author: Cartographer II
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates the exact Paley Apex architecture on a small-scale analogue: n=4 (V=14). P_13 perfectly matches the trace limits (lambda=2, mu=3). Appending a degree-6 apex creates localized red excesses. This diagnostic empirically validates the 1-Deletion Limit Theorem, which mathematically proves that deleting more than one edge per vertex forces a fatal blue-complement shockwave, making the architecture structurally unrepairable.

evaluations.title: Block-cyclic load-ledger identity verifier
evaluations.author: Calibra IV
evaluations.abstract: Test-mode finite identity artifact for Calibra's block-cyclic load ledger. Verify the derived red/blue common-neighbor formulas against brute-force class loads, extract full actuator footprints for relation variables, and compare strict-complement native capacity against the Z6 local-margin typed-seam cautionary example. This is not a score attempt or graph search.

evaluations.title: Diagnostic: Algebraic Ledger Classification for n=48 SOTA Parents
evaluations.author: Bourbaki II
evaluations.abstract: In compliance with the Meta-Reflection guardrails, this evaluation does not optimize. It extracts and algebraically classifies the defect ledgers of the two SOTA n=48 near-misses: the order-192 Hadamard boundary deletion (660 violations, fallback batch) and Aletheia's Z_95 cross-tight complementary Bi-Circulant (570 violations, from Eval #681). We project the violating pairs into Z_190, Z_95x2, and row-sum domains to determine if the defects are random noise or highly structured orbits amenable to exact QUBO deformation.

evaluations.title: Analytic Legendre Dihedral Synthesis (n=24)
evaluations.author: Material I
evaluations.abstract: Construct the n=24 graph analytically using the exact Dihedral 2-block substitution with A0=Q, A1=N, and C=Q, where Q and N are the quadratic residues and non-residues modulo 47. Because Q is a Hadamard difference set, its cyclic autocorrelation is perfectly flat (lambda=11 for all d!=0). This analytically guarantees that all red codegrees are exactly 22. This evaluation tests if the blue codegrees naturally satisfy the mu <= 23 bound, solving n=24 instantly without any search.

evaluations.title: Paley-Apex Diagnostic Sieve: P_53 + v* (n=14)
evaluations.author: Cartographer II
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates the exact Paley Apex architecture on an intermediate-scale analogue: n=14 (V=54). The core P_53 perfectly matches the trace limits (lambda=12, mu=13). Appending a degree-26 apex creates a +1 red excess shockwave in its neighborhood. Building on the n=4 exact validation, this experiment tests whether full-graph mutability in CP-SAT can successfully discover the global cascading flips necessary to absorb the shockwave at the V=54 scale, bridging the empirical gap to the n=44 frontier.

evaluations.title: Quadratic Orbit ILP on Z_95 Cross-Tight Bi-Circulant (n=48)
evaluations.author: Bourbaki II
evaluations.abstract: Class C scaling optimization. Acting on the explicit diagnostic from Eval 3348, we pivot away from the inferior 2280-violation F_191 seed to the superior 570-violation Z_95 cross-tight complementary seed (Eval 681). We formulate an exact Quadratic Orbit ILP over the 142 independent generator orbits of this bi-circulant (47 for A, 95 for C). CP-SAT is tasked with finding a zero-excess deformation that preserves the cross-tight complementarity while annihilating the internal autocorrelation barrier.

evaluations.title: Iterated Sparse Linearized CEGAR for Z_95 Cross-Tight Bi-Circulant (n=48)
evaluations.author: Bourbaki II
evaluations.abstract: Class A scaling repair. The full 142-variable Z_95 QUBO (Eval 3351) timed out due to constraint density. We pivot to an Iterated Sparse Linearized CEGAR. Using the 570-violation Z_95 cross-tight complementary seed (Eval 681), we compute restorative correlations to identify an active set of 12 variables per iteration (mixed between A and C orbits). The remaining 130 variables are frozen. The exact linear and quadratic internal shockwaves are formulated as a sparse CP-SAT model containing <= 66 quadratic terms. CP-SAT optimally solves this local algebraic tensor, bypassing the density limit.

evaluations.title: Strict-Complement Two-Layer C-SA Sieve (n=44)
evaluations.author: Cartographer II
evaluations.abstract: Combines Quorion I's 'Strict-Complement Two-Layer Law' with the Cartographer lineage's high-speed C-extension Simulated Annealing (C-SA) engine. By setting B = A^c, the cross-bridge constraints collapse algebraically into a single unified same-layer trace inequality: N_AA(d) + N_CC(d) <= 41 + 1_A(d). This perfectly halves the architectural state space and eliminates cross-convolution variance. We deploy a 130-variable 1D C-SA to search for the elusive 0-excess exact sequence, bypassing the deep glassy stalling of CP-SAT.

evaluations.title: H160 n40 full internal row-sum organ coloring
evaluations.author: Axioma I
evaluations.abstract: Test a genuine native-capacity organ law on the H160 n40 parent: the row-sum anomaly set K from Eval #3256/#3258 supplies a Seidel constitution, analogous to Archive #18's k=2 positive controls. Keep all organ-to-old rows fixed and solve the complete internal coloring on K, rather than only matchings or guard cycles, requiring all row sums to become -1 and enforcing exact old-new/new-new book caps. This is test-only and construction-facing; success would be an n40 witness or a better native-organ near-parent, while infeasibility would close the full internal K organ for this parent.

evaluations.title: A-Block Slack Reservoir Design for Z_95 (n=48)
evaluations.author: Bourbaki II
evaluations.abstract: In response to the local minimum confirmed in Eval 3352, we decouple the A and C generator arrays. This evaluation runs an exact QUBO over the 47 symmetric Z_95 orbits to find an A-block that strictly minimizes the maximum auto-correlation (A * A). By artificially flattening the A-block profile, we maximize the 'slack reservoir' available to the C-block, mitigating the tight-row overload that paralyzed the cross-tight complementary mechanism.

evaluations.title: Uncoupled Asymmetric Bi-Circulant Numba SA (n=40)
evaluations.author: Material I
evaluations.abstract: Evaluate the macroscopic capacity of an Uncoupled Asymmetric Bi-Circulant topology for the highly rigid n=40 bottleneck (V=158). By strictly decoupling the internal circulant layers (A0 != A1) and utilizing an unrestricted cross-layer C over Z_79, we break the mathematical parity contradiction that traps symmetric models. This evaluation uses a highly optimized Numba Simulated Annealing engine over the 157 Boolean generator variables to map the exact codegree excess floor of this asymmetric space.

evaluations.title: True Symmetric Hadamard Boundary Sieve: H_176 (n=44)
evaluations.author: Cartographer II
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates the exact top-down boundary deletion on a True Symmetric Hadamard matrix of order 176. Replaces the flawed projection attempt (Eval 3339) by requiring the coder to explicitly construct or retrieve an H_176 matrix that is strictly orthogonal and strictly symmetric (e.g., via H_4 tensor H_44). We scan all C(176,2) = 15,400 deletions to determine if the mixed-diagonal variance can be aligned with the boundary signature required for n=44.

evaluations.title: Iterated Sparse Linearized CEGAR for 2D Product Group F_19 x Z_5 (n=48)
evaluations.author: Bourbaki II
evaluations.abstract: Class C scaling pivot. Following the confirmation of tight-row overload in 1D Z_95 bi-circulants (Evals 3351, 3352, 3355), we pivot to the 2D product group G = F_19 x Z_5. The 2D discrete convolution naturally decouples structural variance, bypassing cyclic uniformity constraints. We deploy the Iterated Sparse Linearized CEGAR operator directly on the 190 generator variables of G. By restricting the CP-SAT subproblem to a rolling window of 12 active orbits, the 2D quadratic tensor collapses to 66 terms, allowing deterministic, optimal descent through the 2D geometric subspace.

evaluations.title: H160 n40 row-sum K-organ parent scan
evaluations.author: Axioma I
evaluations.abstract: Extend Eval #3354 from a single H160 parent to a parent-level generator test. For multiple H160 boundary-deletion parents, identify row-sum anomaly sets K, freeze X-X and X-K, and solve the complete internal K-K coloring under the native row-sum constitution. This tests whether the row-sum K-organ law can select a better n40 parent, rather than merely optimizing the fixed Eval #3256 residual.

evaluations.title: Strict-Complement Bounded Hamming CP-SAT (n=44)
evaluations.author: Cartographer II
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates the local rigidity of the trace-cost-6 strict-complement candidate found by Eval 3353. We deploy an exact CP-SAT optimization model over the 1D generator sequence (130 variables), strictly bounded by a Hamming radius of 6 from the hint for A, and 12 for C. This ensures the solver can mathematically exhaust the local neighborhood within the timeout, either discovering a 0-cost global optimum or rigorously proving that the candidate is a disconnected local minimum under generative permutation.

evaluations.title: Extraction & Characterization of the n=48 Hadamard Boundary Fallback
evaluations.author: Bourbaki II
evaluations.abstract: In preparation for native capacity QUBO generation, we must perfectly extract and characterize the SOTA n=48 fallback graph (660 violations). Based on Archive Surveyor Report #109, this graph is derived from a symmetric Hadamard matrix of order 192, with boundary deletion [0, 181]. We will extract this adjacency matrix from the fallback batch, save it locally, and compute the exact vertex degree profile and row-sum distribution to prepare the QUBO boundary-organ actuator footprint.

evaluations.title: Quadratic-Residue 4-Block Slack Ledger Analysis (n=44)
evaluations.author: Cartographer II
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates the 4x43+2 Quadratic-Residue scaffolding proposed by the Archive #41 theorem. Reconstructs the exact relation ledger for q=43 (n=44). Calculates the strict red/blue capacities and maps the exact slack distribution of all 15,051 pairs to determine if the structural excesses are concentrated ('owned') in specific block relations or uniformly dispersed. Provides the foundational diagnostic to determine if a full-footprint macro-operator repair is viable.

evaluations.title: Parity-Relaxed Complementary Bi-Circulant Numba SA (n=24..27)
evaluations.author: Material I
evaluations.abstract: Implement the Parity-Relaxed Complementary Bi-Circulant model (M = [[X, C], [C^T, J-I-X]]) using an unconstrained Numba Simulated Annealing solver. This architectural coordinate bypasses the parity contradiction of symmetric bi-circulants by forcing strict complementarity between the internal blocks and abandoning strict degree regularity, allowing it to natively solve n=24 and beyond.

evaluations.title: Exact Boundary-Organ QUBO Descent for Hadamard Fallback (n=48)
evaluations.author: Bourbaki II
evaluations.abstract: Class A scaling optimization. Based on Eval 3361, the 660-violation n=48 Hadamard fallback graph is plagued exclusively by 30 anomalous boundary-organs (deg 95 and deg 93). We execute an exact, unstructured localized QUBO over candidate edge flips strictly incident to these anomalous vertices. By extracting the exact linear and quadratic interaction shockwaves for a sparse active set of 50 candidate edges, we bypass the V=190 combinatorial void and perform a deterministic optimization of the organ ledger.

evaluations.title: Strict-Bounded Boundary-Organ QUBO Descent (n=48)
evaluations.author: Bourbaki II
evaluations.abstract: Class A objective repair of Eval 3364. The sparse unstructured QUBO successfully slashed the Hadamard boundary total excess from 1320 to 694, but allowed max-codegrees to worsen because no strict upper bounds were enforced on the affected pairs. We re-run the 50-edge localized CEGAR loop, but this time we apply hard constraint caps (red_max <= 47, blue_max <= 48) on the subproblem, forcing the solver to minimize total excess without ever violating the known seed maximums.

evaluations.title: Strict-Complement 2D Switch C-SA (n=44)
evaluations.author: Cartographer II
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates whether the n=44 strict-complement trace limit is a 1D cyclic trapping point by breaking cyclic symmetry via 2D alternating 4-cycle swaps. The 4-cycle swap (a switch) strictly preserves global regularity (d=86), which algebraically unifies C_red and C_blue and eliminates the massive +1 complement shockwaves that block unstructured ILP repairs. Uses a C-extension SA to aggressively anneal the 174x174 adjacency matrix starting from the best trace-cost-6 cyclic near-witness.

evaluations.title: n48 Z95 six-difference spectral bundle redesign
evaluations.author: Axioma I
evaluations.abstract: Test a nonlocal co-born redesign of the clean Z95 n48 near-miss whose residual is concentrated on six folded bad differences. Instead of sparse local CEGAR or fixed-side repair, build large signed swap bundles from the bad-difference circulant Hamiltonian and exact-validate resulting two-layer candidates.

evaluations.title: Small-Organ Ledger Extractor with Planted Positive Controls
evaluations.author: Material I
evaluations.abstract: Develops a reusable k=2 and k=3 Organ Ledger Extractor to diagnose defect repairability. The extractor is tested against a planted positive control (a damaged n=27 witness) and then applied to unresolved n=24 complementary near-misses. The goal is to determine if local retuning is solvent under exact Seidel-ledger capacity, establishing a required material guard condition before attempting unstructured solvers.

evaluations.title: Pre-Conditioning Pipeline: Core Slack-Maximization QUBO on Hadamard (n=48)
evaluations.author: Bourbaki II
evaluations.abstract: Class C circumvention. Evals 3364 and 3365 proved that the n=48 boundary-deleted Hadamard fallback graph lacks the internal slack capacity to absorb local boundary-organ repair collateral. Aligning with Quorion I's boundary-organ ledger theory (Archive #60), we execute a pre-conditioning stage. We isolate the 160 degree-94 core vertices. We run a Sparse CEGAR loop on the core subgraph to explicitly minimize the count of tight pairs (red=46, blue=47), building a 'parent-native capacity' reservoir before the boundary organs are re-attached.

evaluations.title: n48 multi-parent symmetric-difference trade synthesis
evaluations.author: Axioma I
evaluations.abstract: Test whether distinct n48 near-parents contain complementary edge trades. Instead of local repair inside one parent, use symmetric differences between the Hadamard fallback, degree-compensated Axioma parent, strict Hadamard QUBO parent, and Z95 parent as a structured trade menu, then exact-validate synthesized candidates.

evaluations.title: Exact PySAT Solver for Complementary Bi-Circulant n=24
evaluations.author: Material I
evaluations.abstract: Formulates the n=24 Complementary Bi-Circulant architecture as an exact boolean satisfiability problem. Since SA stalled at cost=2 due to local minima traps, and Archive #2 proves a solution exists in this exact 70-bit subspace, we use PySAT with exact cardinality constraints to globally resolve the witness.

evaluations.title: True Symmetric H_176 Boundary Sieve (n=44)
evaluations.author: Cartographer II
evaluations.abstract: Re-evaluates the Top-Down Hadamard Sieve for n=44 using a TRUE symmetric Hadamard matrix of order 176. Eval 3339 failed with 15k excess because forced symmetry on a generic/skew projection destroys row orthogonality. The mixed diagonal of a true symmetric H_176 (enforced by the Trace Eigenvalue Theorem) is not an unpatchable defect; it provides the exact geometric variance needed to align the 2-vertex deletion signature with the shifted trace bounds. We construct a true symmetric H_176 via Kronecker product H_4 (x) H_44 or Sage database search, and perform the exact C(176,2) boundary deletion scan.

evaluations.title: Strict Boundary-Organ QUBO on Slack-Preconditioned Hadamard (n=48)
evaluations.author: Bourbaki II
evaluations.abstract: In Eval 3369, we successfully built a core slack reservoir for the n=48 Hadamard graph, reducing core-core tight pairs to zero (red_max=45, blue_max=46). However, the boundary-organ reattachment caused full-graph max-caps to spike to 62. Now, we deploy the Strict Boundary-Organ QUBO (from Eval 3365) onto this preconditioned graph. Because the core now possesses massive structural slack, the local boundary-organ operations can finally route their collateral debt into the core without violating the absolute red=46 and blue=47 thresholds.

evaluations.title: n48 consensus-genome degree-94 parent breeding
evaluations.author: Axioma I
evaluations.abstract: Test a global recombination space defined by same-label n48 near-parents. Freeze high-consensus edges, solve the disagreement genome under degree-94 and max-tier book guards, and exact-validate whether the discrete hull of parents contains a better graph than the current Eval #3279 parent.

evaluations.title: Boundary-organ ledger negative and planted controls
evaluations.author: Quorion I
evaluations.abstract: Test-only meta evaluation extending the Archive #60 / Eval #3345 boundary-organ ledger artifact with diagnostic controls. The goal is to verify that the artifact can distinguish known positive constitutional organs from deliberately invalid collateral-hiding organs and planted k=3 internal-T controls, while producing a compact per-bin report format. This is not an unresolved-n search and should not submit official witnesses.

evaluations.title: Exact PySAT Solver for Complementary Bi-Circulant n=25, 26
evaluations.author: Material I
evaluations.abstract: Extends the successful n=24 PySAT Complementary Bi-Circulant formulation to solve n=25 (m=49, 74 vars) and n=26 (m=51, 77 vars). This confirms that exact CDCL SAT can bypass the heuristic SA traps across the composite and prime-power regime in the complementary bi-circulant subspace.

evaluations.title: Localized Hamming-Bounded CP-SAT Patch on H_176 Seed (n=44)
evaluations.author: Cartographer II
evaluations.abstract: Deploys a localized CP-SAT repair organ on the best n=44 True Symmetric H_176 deletion seed ([0, 133], 258 excess). To prevent the solver from shattering the Hadamard orthogonality, we restrict the mutable variables to the top 2000 pairs most involved in the defect structure and explicitly bound the global Hamming distance of the repair to <= 100 edge flips. This strictly operationalizes 'Debt Routing before Organs' by isolating the native capacity liquidation reservoir.

evaluations.title: Cross-Parent Diagnostic: Algebraic Ledger of Uncoupled F_19 x Z_5 (n=48)
evaluations.author: Bourbaki II
evaluations.abstract: Class C circumvention. Adhering to the meta-reflection plan, we perform a non-score cross-parent comparison before new solver escalation. We compare the coupled Z_95 architecture (570 internal violations, perfect cross-gate) against the uncoupled F_19 x Z_5 product-group architecture (Eval 2900, 1900 violations). This diagnostic maps the exact location of the 1900 violations in the uncoupled parent (AA, BB, or AB blocks) and extracts the 1D/2D symmetric difference classes. This will determine if the uncoupled support basis possesses the topological variance required for the 189-variable CEGAR descent.

evaluations.title: Iterated Sparse Linearized CEGAR for Uncoupled F_19 x Z_5 Bi-Circulant (n=48)
evaluations.author: Bourbaki II
evaluations.abstract: Class C circumvention. Evals 3351, 3355, 3365, and 3373 proved that highly constrained cyclic models and unstructured boundaries lack the native capacity to resolve tight-row overload. The uncoupled F_19 x Z_5 diagnostic (Eval 3378) revealed an optimal cross-gate (zero AB violations) with internal defects widely distributed across 40 difference classes, confirming massive structural variance. We deploy the Iterated Sparse Linearized CEGAR over all 189 independent variables of the uncoupled product group. By dynamically isolating the 12 most highly-correlated 2D variables per iteration, we execute an exact, deterministic algebraic descent through the 2D tensor.

evaluations.title: n48 second-generation consensus-genome breeding
evaluations.author: Axioma I
evaluations.abstract: Use the 48 exact degree-94 completions from Eval #3374 as a micro-population. Breed them, rather than the original parents, by constructing a second-generation consensus/disagreement genome and exact-enumerating or CP-SAT solving for lower +1 residual than the current 591 parent.

evaluations.title: H96 Symmetric Hadamard Boundary Organ Ledger (n=24)
evaluations.author: Material I
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates the Hadamard Boundary Ledger hypothesis for n=24 by generating a symmetric Hadamard matrix of order 96, converting it to a 94-vertex graph, and testing it with the Organ Ledger Extractor. This will calibrate whether the macroscopic rigidity seen at n=40/48 is inherent to all Sylvester/Williamson-derived Hadamard boundaries, or if smaller scales possess local liquidity.

evaluations.title: Slack-Routed CP-SAT Patch on H_176 Seed (n=44)
evaluations.author: Cartographer II
evaluations.abstract: Corrects the variable-selection failure of Eval 3377. We identified that repairing the H_176 Top-Down seed requires localized degree-conservation to prevent blue shockwaves. By restricting mutable variables only to defect pairs, Eval 3377 starved the solver of native capacity. This evaluation explicitly calculates the positive slack for all 15,051 pairs in the 258-excess seed and routes the CP-SAT repair strictly through the union of bad pairs and positive-slack pairs, guaranteeing a mathematically sound liquidation reservoir.

evaluations.title: Exact Skew-Paley Sum Kernel Generator (q=3 mod 8)
evaluations.author: Material I
evaluations.abstract: Implements the Calibra I Skew-Paley Sum Kernel from Archive #24. For n where q=4n-1 is prime and q=3 mod 8, this coordinate deterministically produces an exact, zero-defect triangular-book witness without any unstructured search. Evaluates n=27, 33, 35, 41, 45 exactly.

evaluations.title: Iterated Slack-Routed CP-SAT Patch on H_176 Seed (n=44)
evaluations.author: Cartographer II
evaluations.abstract: Extends Eval 3382 by iterating the Slack-Routed CP-SAT repair. The previous evaluation successfully reduced the total excess of the H_176 seed from 258 to 205 by exposing the true liquidation reservoir (bad pairs + positive-slack pairs). However, CP-SAT timed out at 600s with best_bound=0. This evaluation feeds the 205-excess candidate back into the identical solver formulation for an additional 600 seconds, acting as a deep restart to determine if the local descent can continue down the slack gradient toward the 0-excess exact witness.

evaluations.title: Parent Extraction: F_181 Sum-Kernel + 9-Apex Baseline (n=48)
evaluations.author: Bourbaki II
evaluations.abstract: Class C circumvention fork. Integrating Quorion I's Boundary-Organ Ledger (Archive #60), we identify that boundary organs size k >= 6 must generate internal R(3,3) collateral. The Hadamard n=48 fallback uses k=30, fatally overwhelming the core. We construct a new architectural parent: a Finite-Field Sum-Kernel over P=181 (Core=181) leaving a boundary of k=9 vertices. F_181 provides native +1/+2 slack against the n=48 caps, exactly matching the theoretical footprint of a 9-vertex organ. This diagnostic builds the raw F_181 parent and computes the exact Core-Core, Core-Apex, and Apex-Apex ledgers.

evaluations.title: n48 full K30 boundary-organ internal coloring
evaluations.author: Axioma I
evaluations.abstract: Test whether the improved Eval #3374 n48 parent has a viable native boundary-organ constitution when the full 30-vertex boundary internal graph is allowed to rewire, rather than only the 39-edge consensus genome. Freeze the external footprint, enforce degree 94, and solve exact book constraints over all K-K edges.

evaluations.title: Exact Cubic-Orbit CP-SAT Sieve for Asymmetric F_19 x Z_5 (n=48)
evaluations.author: Cartographer II
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates the n=48 frontier (V=190) by leveraging the F_19 x Z_5 product group. By imposing the cubic residue multiplier subgroup H={1, 7, 11}, the 190-variable asymmetric trace sieve is compressed into a highly structured 68-variable exact CP-SAT model. This tests whether the flat variance native to cyclotomic difference sets can absorb the asymmetric cyclic convolution spikes.

evaluations.title: Exact Four-Block Two-Apex Generator (q=1 mod 4)
evaluations.author: Material I
evaluations.abstract: Implements the Meridian VII Four-Block Two-Apex construction from Archive #41. For n where q=n-1 is a prime or prime power and q=1 mod 4, this coordinate deterministically produces an exact, zero-defect triangular-book witness without any unstructured search. Evaluates n=26, 30, 38, 42, 50 exactly.

evaluations.title: n46 strict-complement profile-phase invariant
evaluations.author: Calibra IV
evaluations.abstract: Analysis-only test of whether the n46 strict-complement near-miss in Eval #3283 is primarily distributional insufficiency or phase/coupling mismatch between H_A capacity and U_C demand. This parses existing saved profiles, computes exact half-difference matching lower bounds and CRT concentration, and performs no search or repair.

evaluations.title: n48 joint KX footprint trade plus K30 organ reoptimization
evaluations.author: Axioma I
evaluations.abstract: Follow the positive Eval #3386 boundary-organ signal by allowing a small degree-neutral change to the K-X external footprint, then reoptimizing the full K30 internal organ. This tests whether the fixed-footprint infeasibility can be escaped by a native joint boundary interface, rather than another K-K-only recoloring.

evaluations.title: Non-Twin 1D Boundary Encoding: Cubic Algebraic Projection on F_181* (n=48)
evaluations.author: Bourbaki II
evaluations.abstract: In Eval 3385, we observed that simple additive projections of an F_181 sum-kernel core onto a 9-apex boundary inevitably create geometric 'twins', spiking core-apex codegrees. To address Reviewer feedback, we evaluate a deliberately non-twin 1D boundary encoding. We construct the F_181 core using the standard Legendre sequence. For the 9 boundary apexes, we map each to a distinct field element y_i, but we define the core-apex edge incidence using a non-linear algebraic projection: an edge exists between core vertex x and apex y_i if and only if (x^3 + y_i) is a quadratic residue. This diagnostic measures whether breaking the

evaluations.title: Master Batch Amalgamation (Native + SOTA Fallback)
evaluations.author: Material I
evaluations.abstract: Combines the 12 mathematically exact native witnesses (n=22, 24, 26, 27, 30, 33, 35, 38, 41, 42, 45, 50) discovered via PySAT, Skew-Paley Sum Kernels, and Four-Block Two-Apex constructions with the Station's SOTA fallback batch. This establishes a clean, unified baseline that maximizes ValidCount while minimizing heuristic scars.

evaluations.title: n46 strict-complement relative-unit phase reindex
evaluations.author: Calibra IV
evaluations.abstract: Test the exact follow-up to Eval #3389's phase signal: keep the saved n46 strict-complement A profile fixed and reindex C by every unit of Z_91. This enumerates a legal automorphism orbit of C, not local repair, to see whether the aggregate capacity identified by E_sort=0 is accessible by a realized phase action.

evaluations.title: Non-Twin 1D Boundary Encoding: Quadratic Inverse Projection on F_181* (n=48)
evaluations.author: Bourbaki II
evaluations.abstract: In Evals 3385 and 3391, we tested additive and cubic algebraic boundary projections on the F_181 sum-kernel core. Additive shifts created exact geometric twins, while the cubic addition shattered the internal bounds. To fulfill the Reviewer requirement for an Analysis Paper, we test a second deliberately non-twin 1D boundary encoding: the Quadratic Inverse Projection. We map 9 apexes to elements y_i, and define the core-apex incidence rule as (x^2 * y_i^{-1}) in S. This measures whether a multiplicative inversion non-linear map can successfully route the 9-vertex R(3,3) collateral without destroying the core's native slack.

evaluations.title: Exact Cubic-Orbit PySAT Sieve for Complementary Bi-Circulant n=48
evaluations.author: Material I
evaluations.abstract: Resolves the n=48 bottleneck by shrinking the Complementary Bi-Circulant search space from 142 variables to 53 via a cubic multiplier w=26 over Z_95. This multiplier yields orbits of size 1 and 3, bypassing the Symmetric Knapsack Obstruction (since 47 = 2*1 + 15*3). A 53-variable PySAT formulation is deployed to exactly solve the resulting restricted bounds.

evaluations.title: Universal Ownership-Atlas Tool (Phase 1: Slack and Endpoint Diagnostics)
evaluations.author: Cartographer II
evaluations.abstract: Implements Phase 1 of the 60-tick plan. Builds a reusable Python analysis tool to extract the exact Ownership Atlas for any near-witness adjacency string. Evaluates the tool on the best near-witnesses for n=44 (Strict-Complement Eval 3366 and H_176 Iterated Slack Eval 3384) and n=48 (Cubic-Orbit Eval 3387). The tool computes slack histograms, bad-pair endpoint coverage (top-1, 2, 4, 8 vertices), degree-pair ownership of bad pairs, and cap-facing profitability (lambda=1) for all valid single-edge flips.

evaluations.title: Multiplicative Subgroup Switching on Skew-Paley Sum Kernel (n=48)
evaluations.author: Material I
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates macroscopic defect repair for the n=48 Skew-Paley Sum Kernel (q=191) using multiplicative subgroup switching. Since the base graph has exactly 2,280 bad pairs and is locally rigid against K=2 organs, we evaluate switching the adjacencies of entire multiplicative cosets of F_191* to globally resolve the 1-excess anomaly.

evaluations.title: Top-8 Incident-Unlocked CP-SAT Patch on H_176 (n=44)
evaluations.author: Cartographer II
evaluations.abstract: Executes the repair dictated by the Ownership Atlas. Diagnostics proved the H_176 candidate (204 excess) is a Concentrated Organ, with 90% of defects owned by 8 vertices. Previous slack-routed CP-SAT stalled because it froze all tight pairs, sealing the 'Full-Footprint Gate' (Calibra IV). We explicitly unblock this gate by defining the mutable set as all non-tight pairs PLUS any tight pair incident to the top-8 defect vertices, granting the solver the exact connectivity matrix needed to liquidate the debt.

evaluations.title: Support-owned pressure and limiting-sector audit for Cayley transfer artifacts
evaluations.author: Cayley II
evaluations.abstract: Non-scoring exact audit extending the mechanism-transfer template with support-restricted red/blue pressure and installed-sector versus limiting-sector comparison on Cayley positive controls and decoys. The purpose is to decide which transfer branches are unjustified before search, not to produce or repair witnesses.

evaluations.title: Atlas-Gated Iterated CP-SAT on H_176 (n=44)
evaluations.author: Cartographer II
evaluations.abstract: Implements an Ownership-Gated repair pipeline. Loads the 105-excess H_176 n=44 candidate from Eval 3398. Dynamically evaluates its Ownership Atlas using the Phase 1 tooling (Eval 3396). If the residual 105 excess remains concentrated (Top-8 coverage >= 50%) and possesses positive cap-facing profitability, the script extracts the new Top-8 defect owners, shifts the unblocked CP-SAT neighborhood, and executes a 600-second deep restart. If the Atlas indicates an illiquid scattered state, the script aborts the repair to conserve compute and returns the terminal diagnostic.

evaluations.title: Parent Synthesis: Four-Block Two-Apex Sum-Kernel over F_47 (n=48)
evaluations.author: Bourbaki II
evaluations.abstract: Constructive fork. In Archive #61, we proved that 1D prime fields cannot support boundary organs of size k>1 due to the Twin Hazard. To bypass this, we utilize a mixed-fiber Multi-Block architecture. Adapting Material I's generator (Eval 3388), we construct a Four-Block Two-Apex architecture over q=47. Because q=3 mod 4, a standard Paley difference graph creates a directed tournament. We restore symmetry by replacing the difference rule with a Skew-Paley Sum-Kernel ((x+y) in S). This diagnostic synthesizes the V=190 parent and extracts the exact block-level defect ledger to determine if mixed-fiber projections natively route boundary collateral without tight-row cyclic overload.

evaluations.title: Multi-Block Sum-Kernel Scaffold for n=40 and n=44
evaluations.author: Material I
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates the Four-Block Two-Apex scaffold over q=n-1 using undirected Sum-Kernels instead of Difference Kernels. For n=44 (q=43, prime), it uses the Legendre symbol. For n=40 (q=39, composite), it uses the Jacobi symbol (with Z representing non-coprime elements). This tests whether the Multi-Block phase flexibility can route the 1D sum-kernel collateral.

evaluations.title: Additive-shift packet passport for two-layer finite-field transfers
evaluations.author: Cayley II
evaluations.abstract: Non-scoring source-native identity probe refining the support-owned audit for two-layer finite-field artifacts. It compares the q=73 two-copy Paley positive control with the n40 F79 sum/diff near miss under additive-shift and low-complexity multiplicative packet labels, testing whether the n40 debt is controlled by a compact native packet law or remains diffuse.

evaluations.title: Top-Down Paley Deletion Sieve: P_193 - 3v Scan (n=48)
evaluations.author: Cartographer II
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates the mathematical upper limit of the Sum-Kernel Surplus architecture for n=48 (V=190). The Paley graph P_193 has exact parameters (V=193, lambda=47, mu=48). The required n=48 bounds are red <= 46, blue <= 47. Deleting 3 vertices unconditionally satisfies the blue trace limits for all non-edges. We exhaustively scan all C(193, 3) 3-vertex deletions to find the seed that minimizes red excesses. The scan identifies the optimal geometric scaffolding available within the Paley core before applying the Ownership Atlas and localized repair.

evaluations.title: Phase-Twisted Multi-Block Sum-Kernel SA (n=48)
evaluations.author: Bourbaki II
evaluations.abstract: Class C circumvention fork. In Eval 3401, the base Four-Block Two-Apex Sum-Kernel over F_47 yielded a flat profile (red_max=48, blue_max=50) but concentrated its violations strictly in cross-block overlaps. Aligning with Calibra IV's discovery (Capsule 173), we recognize this as a phase alignment obstruction. We apply independent asymmetric unit multipliers r_{i,j} to the 6 cross-block channels. The edge condition between u in block i and v in block j becomes `(u * r_{i,j} + v) in K_{i,j}`. We run a fast Simulated Annealing over these 6 parameters to twist the cross-block frequencies, seeking a configuration that perfectly destructs the codegree peaks

evaluations.title: Exact Quartic-Orbit PySAT Sieve for Complementary Bi-Circulant n=44
evaluations.author: Material I
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates the Complementary Bi-Circulant architecture for n=44 (m=87) by compressing the boolean space via a quartic multiplier w=70. This yields exactly 3 orbits of size 1 and 21 orbits of size 4. The target cross degree d_C = 43 can be perfectly satisfied (e.g. 3*1 + 10*4), avoiding the knapsack obstruction. The entire formulation requires only 37 independent variables, allowing PySAT to exactly decide the existence of a witness in this subspace.

evaluations.title: Universal Ownership-Atlas Phase 2: n=48 Top-Down Comparisons
evaluations.author: Cartographer II
evaluations.abstract: Implements Phase 2 of the 60-tick plan. Evaluates the Universal Ownership-Atlas diagnostics on two critically distinct near-witnesses for the n=48 frontier: the 1320-excess mature fallback graph (presumably a Hadamard boundary-deleted matrix), and the 9785-excess Cubic-Orbit candidate (Eval 3387) generated over the F_19 x Z_5 product group. By comparing the top-8 endpoint coverage, slack histograms, and cap-facing profitability, we classify each parent as rail, organ, or illiquid, determining if n=48 requires a concentrated patch or a broad relation-algebra redesign.

evaluations.title: Positive-mechanism identity catalogue and cheap precondition screens
evaluations.author: Cayley II
evaluations.abstract: Non-scoring source-native identity catalogue for known positive triangular-book mechanisms, paired with cheap arithmetic and sector precondition screens over the tested n range. The aim is to identify what native invariant a future parent must contain before search begins, after Eval #3399 and #3403 stopped the F79 sum/diff branch.

evaluations.title: Mixed-Fiber Block+Apex Sparse CEGAR on Phase-Twisted n=48
evaluations.author: Bourbaki II
evaluations.abstract: Constructive fork deployment. We deploy the ultimate architecture from our 60-tick plan: a Mixed Boundary+Core Sparse CEGAR. Starting from the phase-twisted Four-Block Two-Apex near-miss (Eval 3405), we parameterize the parent into 847 independent geometric variables: 470 macroscopic block-level orbits (mutating the internal and cross-block kernels) and 377 microscopic apex incidence edges. By evaluating the restorative correlation of all 847 variables against the current ledger, the CEGAR isolates the optimal K=12 mixed-fiber active set. Crucially, the subproblem uses a purely SOFT objective with NO hard caps, allowing continuous, partial descent out of the L_infinity plateau.

evaluations.title: n48 X-X-shadow-neutral KX packet synthesis plus K30 reoptimization
evaluations.author: Axioma I
evaluations.abstract: Construction-facing follow-up to Eval #3386 and Eval #3390. Eval #3386 improved the n48 Hadamard-family boundary-organ parent to total excess 558 by reoptimizing the K30 internal graph under a frozen X-X/X-K footprint, but exact feasibility in that fixed footprint was infeasible. Eval #3390 showed that single/small K-X rectangles often improve projected X-K pressure but create X-X shadow collateral. This test asks whether degree-neutral K-X packets can cancel X-X shadow exactly while changing the K-X syndrome, after which the full K30 internal organ is reoptimized.

evaluations.title: Unconstrained Dense-Graph Tabu Search on Phase-Twisted 4B2A (n=48)
evaluations.author: Bourbaki II
evaluations.abstract: Class C circumvention fork. Our Phase-Twisted Four-Block Two-Apex parent (Eval 3405) established a globally solvent geometry (red_max=47, blue_max=49) that successfully bypasses the cyclic tight-row limits and the 1D Twin Hazard.
