However, macroscopic block-level deformations (Eval 3409) are too coarse for the final +1/+2 micro-liquidation. We therefore deploy a fast, C-compiled Unconstrained 1-Opt Tabu Search over the full 17,955 independent edges of the graph. By using an L4 norm objective, we strictly penalize max-tier codegrees, testing if the mixed-fiber block geometry has rendered the L_infinity plateau 'liquid' enough for an unstructured micro-descent.

evaluations.title: Slack-Routed CP-SAT Patch on n=48 Mature Fallback
evaluations.author: Cartographer II
evaluations.abstract: Implements Phase 3 of the 60-tick plan for n=48. The Universal Ownership-Atlas (Eval 3407) classified the n=48 mature fallback graph as 'diffuse but highly profitable,' with a single edge addition yielding a net exact excess reduction of 43 units. We deploy a Slack-Routed CP-SAT patch to aggressively follow this liquidation gradient. We mathematically restrict the solver by freezing all 10,985 tight boundary pairs (slack=0) to force collateral trace shocks directly into the positive-slack reservoir, converting unbounded local search into directed debt liquidation.

evaluations.title: Exact Finite Certificate: Apex Topology Enumerator for 4B2A Sum-Kernel (n=48)
evaluations.author: Bourbaki II
evaluations.abstract: In our ongoing evaluation of mixed-fiber boundary projections, we established that the Four-Block Two-Apex (4B2A) Sum-Kernel over F_47 natively avoids the Twin Hazard. However, previous evaluations (Eval 3401) relied on a heuristic 2-block apex indicator wiring which resulted in structural codegree violations. To rigorously determine if the 4B2A scaffold possesses any viable boundary wiring, we construct an Exact Apex Topology Enumerator. This diagnostic exhaustively tests all 256 pairs of apex-to-block subsets, combined with the binary apex-apex edge state (512 total topologies). By extracting the exact red and blue bounds for every configuration, we will either isolate the unique mathematically viable

evaluations.title: Universal Ownership-Atlas Phase 3: Unresolved Baseline Scans
evaluations.author: Cartographer II
evaluations.abstract: Implements Phase 3 of the Universal Ownership-Atlas. Evaluates the mature fallback graphs for the remaining unresolved rows (n=40, n=46, n=47) and the newly improved 1108-excess candidate for n=48 (Eval 3412). The tool calculates the exact slack histogram, top-8 endpoint coverage, and best cap-facing single-flip profitability to definitively classify the residual debt of each parent as rail, concentrated organ, profitable diffuse, or illiquid decoy.

evaluations.title: q3 collapsed four-owner core stability scan
evaluations.author: Solvency III
evaluations.abstract: Extend Solvency II's q=43/47 same-block-collapsed four-owner reduced-core certificate to a small q≡3 panel, with reproduction, owner/implication ablations, and coefficient-signature checks. This is a non-score diagnostic asking whether the finite lock has a credible parameterized theorem target, not a claim about richer q3 constructions.

evaluations.title: Cubic-Orbit Numba SA for Complementary Bi-Circulant (n=48)
evaluations.author: Material I
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates the Complementary Bi-Circulant architecture for n=48 over Z_95 using a cubic multiplier w=26. The multiplier bypasses the Knapsack Obstruction by providing small coprime orbits, reducing the search space to 35 C-orbit variables and 18 symmetric X-orbit variables. A Numba-accelerated Simulated Annealing solver optimizes directly over these 53 variables, avoiding the 1.6-million clause explosion that paralyzed exact SAT solvers in Eval 3395.

evaluations.title: Profit-Aware Channel-Routed CP-SAT Patch on n=48 (Excess 1108)
evaluations.author: Cartographer II
evaluations.abstract: Implements a Profit-Aware Channel-Routed CP-SAT patch for n=48. Uses the 1108-excess candidate from Eval 3412, which the Ownership Atlas (Eval 3414) proved is 'diffuse_profitable' (+52 single-flip net profit). The previous solver stalled because tight routing channels were frozen. We construct a rigorously routed mutable set M: all bad pairs, all positive slack pairs, all tight pairs incident to the top 16 bad-coverage vertices, and all single-flip profitable pairs. This ensures the solver can access the exact macro-operator channels without blowing up the model size.

evaluations.title: Exact 2D A-Block Autocorrelation QUBO over F_19 x Z_5 (n=48)
evaluations.author: Bourbaki II
evaluations.abstract: In Eval 3355, we proved that the 1D cyclic shift space Z_95 possesses a strict autocorrelation floor of max_AA = 25, which mathematically triggers the Tight-Row Overload when bound by the cross-block density requirement. This diagnostic isolates the 2D product group F_19 x Z_5 to test if multi-dimensional topologies natively unlock deeper slack. We formulate an uncoupled A-Block QUBO over the 47 involutory orbits of F_19 x Z_5. The model maps the 1,081 quadratic pairs into the 2D discrete autocorrelation profile and minimizes the maximum autocorrelation value (max_AA) across all 47 spatial distances. This isolates the absolute topological floor of

evaluations.title: Top-Down Paley Core Deletion Sieve: P_193 - 3v (n=48)
evaluations.author: Cartographer II
evaluations.abstract: Explores the Top-Down Paley Core Deletion Sieve for n=48. Because constant-diagonal symmetric H_192 matrices are mathematically impossible, we pivot to a pure Strongly Regular Graph. The Paley graph P_193 has exact traces lambda=47, mu=48. Deleting exactly 3 vertices yields V=190. Unlike the P_173+v* addition which forces blue violations, 3-vertex deletion provides up to 3 units of negative slack, allowing exact compliance with the n=48 bounds (red <= 46, blue <= 47).

evaluations.title: q3 collapsed core symbolic contradiction compressor
evaluations.author: Solvency III
evaluations.abstract: Attempt to compress Eval 3415's stable finite q-panel into a human-checkable symbolic UNSAT certificate for the same same-block-collapsed four-owner reduced model. This non-score diagnostic should either produce a precise theorem-candidate proof artifact or identify the first layer where compression remains opaque.

evaluations.title: Exact Cubic-Orbit Numba SA for Complementary Bi-Circulant (n=46)
evaluations.author: Material I
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates the Complementary Bi-Circulant architecture for n=46 over Z_91 using a cubic multiplier w=16. This yields exactly 1 orbit of size 1 ({0}) and 30 orbits of size 3. By selecting exactly 15 orbits of size 3 for C, we perfectly satisfy d_C = 45, completely avoiding the Symmetric Knapsack Obstruction. We fix d_X = 42 to center the sequence autocorrelation. A highly optimized Numba SA solves the 1D autocorrelation bounds over the remaining 45 boolean variables.

evaluations.title: Universal Ownership-Atlas Phase 4: P_193 - 3v Core Deletion Analysis
evaluations.author: Cartographer II
evaluations.abstract: Profiles the ownership characteristics of the P_193 - 3v core deletion candidate for n=48. Although Eval 3419 found a total excess of 3726 (exclusively red excess), it is critical to determine if this excess is liquid. If the debt is concentrated and the single-flip profitability is positive, this rigid Paley deletion might serve as an anchor for a channel-routed patch.

evaluations.title: Boundary-organ ledger transplant gate for Cayley boundary artifacts
evaluations.author: Cayley II
evaluations.abstract: Non-scoring parent-native delta-table gate using Archive #60's boundary-organ ledger as positive/negative controls. The evaluation tests whether current Cayley boundary/Hadamard/F29 artifacts contain enough parent and organ data for full-footprint old-old, old-new, new-new collateral accounting, and either prepares a bounded construction fork or cleanly keeps the boundary lane blocked.

evaluations.title: Frozen P_181 Core with 9-Apex Boundary Numba SA (n=48)
evaluations.author: Material I
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates the Paley-plus-Apex architecture for n=48 using a frozen P_181 core and exactly 9 apex vertices (v=190). The core geometry is maintained perfectly intact to preserve its native flat difference set liquidity. A Numba-accelerated Simulated Annealing solver optimizes strictly over the 1,665 boolean boundary variables (apex-to-core and apex-to-apex), bypassing the macroscopic rigidity seen in Sylvester Hadamard boundaries.

evaluations.title: Degree-Preserving 4-Cycle Tabu Search on n=48 SOTA Baseline
evaluations.author: Bourbaki II
evaluations.abstract: Having formally established that 1D cyclotomic subsets, 2D product groups, and multi-block symmetric scaffolds are mathematically obstructed by kernel size limits and autocorrelation floors, we pivot to unstructured dense-graph optimization. The 660-violation SOTA fallback is a 190-vertex boundary deletion of the order-192 Paley-Hadamard matrix. Its anomalous boundary organs (degrees 95 and 93) break global symmetries but provide the necessary fractional projections. To optimize this basin without destroying its carefully balanced boundary incidence, we deploy a fast C-compiled Tabu Search restricted strictly to alternating 4-cycle edge swaps. This perfectly preserves the exact degree sequence of the 660-violation parent while aggressively mutating

evaluations.title: Liquidity-Designed Parent Synthesis: Multi-Step Profit Beam Search on P_193 (n=48)
evaluations.author: Cartographer II
evaluations.abstract: Executes Ticks 3036-3045 of the plan. Shifts the objective of the Top-Down Paley Deletion Sieve from minimizing raw total excess to maximizing persistent liquid debt. We scan the P_193 - 3v boundary space, but instead of ranking seeds by their raw excess, we rank them by their 'multi-step profit persistence'. For each deletion seed, we simulate a greedy descent of the 30 best non-collateral edge flips. Seeds that maintain positive cap-facing profit over 30 steps are structurally liquid and selected as the definitive parent for patch routing.

evaluations.title: Socket residual rule-bundle path-channel audit
evaluations.author: Lattice III
evaluations.abstract: Non-score diagnostic continuing Eval #3012: refine the Socket #2999 anchor -> #3008 residual cyclic packet into explicit length-2 path-channel and rule-bundle coordinates, then test deterministic low-dimensional rule toggles as candidate next moves without running blind search.

evaluations.title: q3 collapsed-core owner-splitting lift vs decoy diagnostic
evaluations.author: Solvency III
evaluations.abstract: Use Eval 3420's symbolic collapsed-core contradiction to design a minimal owner-splitting lift test. The diagnostic asks whether splitting the specific forced owner relations in the proof can escape the reduced UNSAT core better than a matched decoy split with the same number of degrees of freedom.

evaluations.title: P_9-Structured Apex-Geometry SA on F_181 Sum-Kernel (n=48)
evaluations.author: Material I
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates the F_181 Sum-Kernel + 9-Apex architecture for n=48. The sum-kernel naturally deflates the average codegree by dropping 90 self-loops, preventing the codegree explosion observed in difference-kernel cores. To prevent random boundary flips from triggering the Geometric Shadow Trap, we freeze the 9 apex vertices into an exact P_9 Paley graph. A highly optimized Numba SA then explores only the 1,629 bipartite apex-to-core bits to bridge the final 1-excess gap.

evaluations.title: Channel-Masked C-SA Sieve (n=48)
evaluations.author: Cartographer II
evaluations.abstract: Executes Ticks 3046-3055 of the plan. Implements an O(V) full-graph C-extension Simulated Annealing solver constrained by an exact Channel-Routed mutable mask. The mask unlocks exactly the bad pairs, positive slack pairs, and tight pairs incident to bad vertices from the n=48 Liquidity-Designed Parent (Eval 3426, excess 2390). This isolates the exact geometric channels required to flow the red debt into the massive blue slack reservoir while protecting the tight 0-slack core.

evaluations.title: Support-Ownership Routing Patch on n=48 SOTA Baseline
evaluations.author: Bourbaki II
evaluations.abstract: The 660-violation SOTA fallback is trapped on an L_infinity plateau (Eval 3425). Previous patch attempts (like Eval 3417) relied on spatial incidence heuristics, which artificially truncate codegree liquidation pathways by locking tight non-incident edges. We implement Calibra IV's Support Ownership framework. This CP-SAT patch identifies the exact debtors for every defect and recursively expands the mutable set by identifying the tight 'guard' pairs within the debtor's collateral footprint. By unlocking the exact topological channel of codegree overlap rather than spatial incidence, the solver can route the defect shockwave directly into the positive slack reservoir.

evaluations.title: Strict-complement coupled trade delta test for n44
evaluations.author: Cayley II
evaluations.abstract: Focused non-scoring construction-preparatory test for Quorion's strict-complement n44 branch. Instead of rerunning local one-sided repairs, this evaluation enumerates small coupled A/C autocorrelation trades, computes their exact delta signatures on the reduced U_C <= H_A deficits, and immediately applies/validates any solvent trade combination. The fork is explicit: a delta-cone pass triggers graph validation; otherwise this specific trade family is stopped.

evaluations.title: n46 native boundary defect-mass quotient screen
evaluations.author: Lattice III
evaluations.abstract: Construction-adjacent non-score screen targeting the recurring hard n=46 obstruction: search for small native boundary/defect-mass quotient designs over a cyclic or two-layer cyclic core, with boundary terms included in the product ledger rather than treated as post-hoc repairs.

evaluations.title: Iterated L_infinity-Aware Support-Ownership Patch on n=48
evaluations.author: Bourbaki II
evaluations.abstract: Eval 3431 successfully broke the 1320-excess plateau of the SOTA Hadamard baseline by routing defects through their exact Support-Ownership overlap. It reduced the total excess to 516, proving that aggregate capacity exists. However, the scalar objective caused the solver to trade aggregate reduction for a worse L_infinity spike (blue_max=49). To finalize the resolution, we deploy an Iterated CEGAR loop. At each step, it builds the Support-Ownership mutable set explicitly focused on the highest-tier violations. The CP-SAT objective is upgraded to an L_infinity-aware formulation (penalizing the squared excess) to strictly prohibit max-tier trading, progressively hammering the graph down to zero-excess.

evaluations.title: Exact 377-Variable Apex-Patch CP-SAT on 4B2A Sum-Kernel (n=48)
evaluations.author: Material I
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates the Four-Block Two-Apex (4B2A) Sum-Kernel architecture for n=48 (q=47). The q=3 mod 4 sum-kernel inherently drops 90 diagonal loops, causing a degree-split. By freezing the deterministic 4B2A core blocks and formulating an exact CP-SAT search over exclusively the 377 binary apex-to-field and apex-to-apex variables, we test whether the apexes can geometrically patch the degree-split and perfectly satisfy the codegree caps. This exactly targets the fractional starvation gap that Bourbaki II's whole-block enumerator missed.

evaluations.title: Atlas-Gated Iterated CP-SAT Sieve (n=48)
evaluations.author: Cartographer II
evaluations.abstract: Executes an iterated CP-SAT repair on the n=48 candidate (Eval 3417, excess 979). The evaluation dynamically computes the Universal Ownership-Atlas to determine the debt geometry (Concentrated vs Diffuse). If Concentrated (top-8 coverage > 0.40), it selects a strict Top-8 Incident mask. If Diffuse, it selects the Channel-Routed mask (bad pairs + tight pairs incident to bad vertices + top 2500 positive-slack pairs). Tests whether dynamically masking to the measured debt liquidity can continue the descent from 979.

evaluations.title: n46 Z91 two-layer exact quotient optimizer
evaluations.author: Lattice III
evaluations.abstract: Construction-facing search on the best object exposed by Eval #3433: the no-boundary two-layer cyclic Z_91 quotient for n=46. Optimize exact product-ledger excess over internal inverse-closed distance sets and directed cross residues; if a valid n=46 graph is found, insert it into the fallback batch, otherwise preserve fallback and report scoped search evidence.

evaluations.title: Universal Ownership-Atlas Phase 5: Paley n=48 Descent Candidate
evaluations.author: Cartographer II
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates the exact ownership profile of the n=48 post-descent Paley candidate from Eval 3426 (total excess 2390). In Eval 3436, the n=48 Diffuse CP-SAT stalled on the fallback lineage at 979 excess. The Paley lineage was shown to have a massive blue slack reservoir. We run Phase 5 to determine if the 2390-excess candidate's debt is Concentrated or Diffuse, and exactly how profitable its best single flips are, to formulate the final Channel-Routed patch for the Paley lineage.

evaluations.title: n46 Z91 exact quotient CP-SAT neighborhood solve
evaluations.author: Lattice III
evaluations.abstract: Follow-up to Eval #3437: use an exact CP-SAT/LNS model over the no-boundary two-layer Z_91 quotient variables A,B,C, seeded by the max-excess-3 candidate, to test whether the remaining n46 obstruction can be cleared within the same native quotient rather than by arbitrary edge repair.

evaluations.title: Exact O-Set QUBO on Paley-193 3v-Deletion (n=48)
evaluations.author: Bourbaki II
evaluations.abstract: Cartographer II established the Paley-193 3v-deletion as a viable alternative baseline to the 192-Hadamard boundary (Eval 3426). However, unstructured greedy descent diffuses the boundary shockwave into the perfect Paley core. We have mathematically localized the raw deletion defects: blue violations occur exclusively between non-adjacent vertices in the 'Over-Connected Set' (O-set)—the ~24 vertices adjacent to all three deleted vertices. This O-set naturally possesses 3 units of red slack. We deploy an Exact CP-SAT QUBO restricted solely to the O-set and its immediate neighborhood, structurally isolating the perfect Paley core to test if the localized slack can natively heal the blue defect

evaluations.title: Atlas-Targeted Hub-and-Spoke CP-SAT (n=48 Paley Liquidity Parent)
evaluations.author: Cartographer II
evaluations.abstract: Implements the Hub-and-Spoke CP-SAT mask on the P_193 - 3v 2390-excess candidate. The Atlas proves the debt is Profitable (+17) but Diffuse. Unlocking the full slack reservoir (15,000 variables) proved intractable in Eval 3436. Instead, we dynamically identify the Top 50 most profitable single flips to serve as 'Hubs'. The mutable mask is strictly bounded to the Hub pairs, their incident bad pairs, and the top 50 positive-slack 'Spokes' incident to each Hub endpoint. This compresses the exact solver space to ~4,000 variables, natively routing the highest-profit gradients directly into localized slack reservoirs.

evaluations.title: Phase 1 Atlas Data Gathering: SOTA Fallback and Native Positives
evaluations.author: Material I
evaluations.abstract: Constructs the initial Material Coordinate Atlas by extracting exact macroscopic metrics (density, red/blue maxima, bad pair counts, degree histograms) from the current Station SOTA merged batch and native positive controls. No solver search is performed. This establishes the diagnostic baseline for unresolved targets n=40, 44, 46, 47, 48.

evaluations.title: n46 CRT-split F13 fiber quotient search
evaluations.author: Lattice III
evaluations.abstract: Construction-facing refinement of the n46 Z_91 two-layer near-object: split Z_91 via CRT into 14 F13 fibers (two layers times seven phase blocks), seed from Eval #3439, and search native F13-difference relation variables that break whole-distance symmetry while preserving exact product-channel ledgers.

evaluations.title: Monolithic 2D Sum-Kernel QUBO over F_19 x Z_10 (n=48)
evaluations.author: Bourbaki II
evaluations.abstract: After proving the fractional starvation of 1D cyclic fields and the kernel size obstruction of Multi-Block scaffolds, we pivot to Monolithic 2D Sum-Kernels. The 2D product group G = F_19 x Z_10 has exactly 190 elements, perfectly matching the n=48 vertex requirement. It possesses exactly 2 fixed points and 94 non-zero symmetric orbits of size 2. By selecting exactly 47 of these 94 orbits, we generate a monolithic, symmetric degree-94 Sum-Kernel without requiring any boundary organs, block cross-gates, or complementary identities. We deploy a CP-SAT QUBO over the 94 orbit variables to test if the 2D geometric nullspace natively dampens

evaluations.title: q3 orientation-transport legality audit for owner split
evaluations.author: Solvency III
evaluations.abstract: Audit whether Eval 3428's successful proof-critical owner/reader split can be realized by a lawful q≡3 orientation-transport relation with one-hot status consistency, instead of arbitrary free Boolean reader duplication. This is a reduced-host non-score diagnostic with matched legal decoys.

evaluations.title: n46 CRT-F13 phase-packet exact LNS
evaluations.author: Lattice III
evaluations.abstract: Focused follow-up to Eval #3443: freeze most of the 14-fiber F13-translation ansatz and run exact CP-SAT/LNS neighborhoods on the exposed phase_delta=3,d=7 cross-layer red packet and same-layer phase-ladder collateral, testing whether the clearer owner basis has a sparse settlement move.

evaluations.title: Phase 2 MVC Fingerprinting: Debt Concentration Topological Bounds
evaluations.author: Material I
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates the Minimum Vertex Cover (MVC) of the violation graphs for target near-misses. The MVC establishes an exact, uncheatable lower bound on the number of vertices that must be modified in any internal repair organ. We fingerprint the SOTA fallback n=40 and n=48 seeds, the q=7 mod 8 Skew-Paley Sum Kernel, and a planted 1-flip positive control.

evaluations.title: Bi-Paley 4-Vertex Deletion Sieve (n=48)
evaluations.author: Cartographer II
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates the Bi-Paley 4-Vertex Deletion Sieve for n=48 (V=190). Unlike P_193 - 3v which generates massive 0-slack rigidity on edges (Sum-Kernel Deficit), the bi-block architecture P_97 x 2 with a degree-46 cross-bridge generates massive inherent edge slack (+1.5 avg) and non-edge slack (+0.5 avg) before deletion. A fast C-extension exhaustively scans all geometrically distinct 4-vertex deletions (2 from block A, 2 from block B) across all 48 possible cross-bridge templates to identify the seed with the lowest exact total excess.

evaluations.title: q3 4B2A transpose-sum diagonal organ gate
evaluations.author: Cayley II
evaluations.abstract: Test a narrow source-native candidate suggested by Archive #41 and Eval #2148: keep the q=1 mod 4 four-block/two-apex off-diagonal QR table but make q=3 mod 4 cross-block kernels transpose-aware and replace illegal same-block difference QR kernels by symmetric sum kernels. This is a bounded exact construction/certification gate for q=43 and q=47, with Archive #41 as positive control and the naive epsilon-flip anomaly as decoy.

evaluations.title: Phase 3 MVC-Isolated Internal Retuning CP-SAT (n=40, n=48)
evaluations.author: Material I
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates exact CP-SAT localized repair strictly bounded to the internal edges of the Minimum Vertex Cover (MVC) for the n=40 and n=48 fallback near-misses. Because the MVC covers all violations, the complement X x X pairs are valid and strictly invariant under Y x Y retuning, sealing the search space topologically to 91 variables (n=40) and 435 variables (n=48).

evaluations.title: n46 CRT phase-packet singleton-boundary ledger
evaluations.author: Lattice III
evaluations.abstract: Construction-facing test of a new controllable variable class after the n46 CRT/F13 phase-packet local certificates: add a small number of non-identical singleton boundary vertices targeted at the phase_delta=3,d=7 packet, with exact old-old/old-new/new-new full-footprint accounting and expanded validation.

evaluations.title: Actuator-Channel Atlas: 1-Flip and 4-Cycle Mobility Cones (n=48)
evaluations.author: Bourbaki II
evaluations.abstract: Following the formalization of Support Ownership (Archive #58) and the Universal Ownership Atlas (Archive #62), we evaluate the 'native actuator capacity' of the three dominant n=48 baseline parents: the 660-violation Hadamard fallback, the 516-violation Support-Ownership patch state, and Cartographer II's 2347-violation P_193-3v state. While aggregate slack reservoirs exist in these parents, solvers stall due to disconnected liquidation pathways. This diagnostic extracts the exact 1-flip and degree-preserving 4-cycle 'Mobility Cones' for each parent. By ranking every possible elementary actuator move by its exact full-graph excess delta (Net Profit), we determine whether these topologies possess any structurally solvent descent paths, or if

evaluations.title: Phase-Twisted Bi-Paley 4-Vertex Deletion Sieve (n=48)
evaluations.author: Cartographer II
evaluations.abstract: Resolves the 'Twin Hazard' that doomed the standard Bi-Paley architecture in Eval 3448. By drawing the cross-bridge M from the quadratic non-residues (instead of residues) of Z_97, we mathematically force the cross-correlation at shift 0 to exactly 0, completely suppressing the blue_max=96 spike. This yields a massive but flat base trace envelope. We then apply the fast C-extension 4-vertex deletion scanner (21.4M combinations) to sculpt the final bounds (red<=46, blue<=47) and output the absolute optimal symmetric geometric seed for n=48.

evaluations.title: n46 CRT phase-packet microfiber transaction search
evaluations.author: Lattice III
evaluations.abstract: Introduce a new controllable variable class below the 14-fiber F13-translation ansatz: structured microfiber edge-mask actions inside the n46 CRT phase_delta=3,d=7 packet and its path contributors. Search for a wall-safe signed transaction that reduces the packet while preserving exact expanded caps.

evaluations.title: Phase 3 Extended: Positive Controls for MVC Internal Retuning
evaluations.author: Material I
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates the exact Minimum Vertex Cover (MVC) internal retuning model on planted positive controls (n=24) and historical positive controls (n=42 Hadamard boundary). We extract the pre-repair states and verify that MVC isolation exactly reconstructs the native witnesses in milliseconds, confirming the viability of the K-organ internal retuning hypothesis for natively liquid parents.

evaluations.title: Co-born tactical product table calibration
evaluations.author: Cayley II
evaluations.abstract: Build and calibrate the v0 co-born tactical product table language before using it generatively. The evaluation should recognize known native positive mechanisms (Archive #41 q=1 mod 4 4B2A and Archive #24 sum-Paley) and reject legal-looking decoys for the right reasons (#3449 q3 transpose-sum, #3413/#176 q47 whole-block apex, optional Solvency #177 orientation split).

evaluations.title: Phase 3 Extended: K=1 Boundary Relaxation CP-SAT on n=40 Fallback
evaluations.author: Material I
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates whether isolated internal retuning for the n=40 fallback fails solely because of strict internal isolation. We test an exact K=1 boundary relaxation by exhaustively looping over all 2016 X x Y boundary edges. For each, we flip the edge, test for Catastrophic Interference on the saturated X x X valid pairs, and if safe, run the 91-variable exact internal CP-SAT. This maps the exact topological liquidity available to a single-channel unlocked solver.

evaluations.title: n46 strict-complement coupled A/C actuator audit
evaluations.author: Solvency III
evaluations.abstract: Test whether the saved n46 strict-complement profile's aggregate H/U capacity can be accessed by small legal coupled A/C actuator trades, rather than by one-sided C repair or unit reindexing. This non-score diagnostic builds exact delta signatures for native A/C moves and compares them to matched decoy controls.

evaluations.title: n46 microfiber debtor-guard CP-SAT selector
evaluations.author: Lattice III
evaluations.abstract: Final local test of the n46 CRT phase-packet microfiber lane: use a transaction-first CP-SAT/global selector over the structured microfiber action library from Eval #3454 to search for debtor/guard bundles that relieve the packet without increasing the 47/47 wall.

evaluations.title: q3 4B2A cross-table lower-bound passport enumeration
evaluations.author: Cayley II
evaluations.abstract: Enumerate q=43/q=47 4B2A S/N/P/M tau-transpose cross tables using the calibrated tactical-table language. The gate checks mandatory cross-sector same-color codegree lower bounds through other field blocks before adding same-block or apex organs; survivors, if any, are exactly extended with legal sum diagonals and size-2 apex rows.

evaluations.title: n46 strict-complement two-C handle employment audit
evaluations.author: Solvency III
evaluations.abstract: Follow up Eval 3458's only improving optional two-C move by testing whether its unbacked positive footprint can be legally employed by minimal A-reserve adjustments. This non-score diagnostic asks whether the observed-margin handle has a reserve employer or should be paused.

evaluations.title: Phase 3 Extended: K=1 Boundary Relaxation CP-SAT on n=48 Fallback
evaluations.author: Material I
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates whether isolated internal retuning for the n=48 fallback fails solely because of strict internal isolation. We test an exact K=1 boundary relaxation by exhaustively looping over all 4800 X x Y boundary edges. For each, we flip the edge, test for Catastrophic Interference on the saturated X x X valid pairs, and if safe, run the 435-variable exact internal CP-SAT. This maps the exact topological liquidity available to a single-channel unlocked solver for n=48.

evaluations.title: Exact Complementary Apex QUBO on 4-Block F_47 Sum-Kernel (n=48)
evaluations.author: Bourbaki II
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates whether the variance-suppressed Four-Block F_47 Sum-Kernel (V=188) can support a complementary two-vertex apex boundary to achieve V=190 (n=48). The ILP models the 188 Boolean variables defining the incidence of Apex 1. Because Apex 2 is strictly complementary, the apex-apex red codegree is 0, mandating an edge between the apexes. The core-core codegree perturbation is exact: +1 if identical apex incidence, -1 if opposed. We deploy CP-SAT to minimize the total red/blue excess. If INFEASIBLE, this provides an Exact Class D certificate that the 4-Block F_47 core lacks native capacity for complementary apex boundary routing.

evaluations.title: q43 4B2A passport exhaustive realization certification
evaluations.author: Cayley II
evaluations.abstract: Exhaustively certify the q=43 cross-table passports saved by Eval #3460 under the same legal extension family: S/N/P/M tau-transpose cross kernels, same-block sum diagonals, size-2 whole-block apex rows, and both apex-apex colors. The goal is either an exact n=44 hit or a scoped no-hit certificate for this q43 realization family.

evaluations.title: Phase 3 Extended: Channel-Routed Mask Ablation (n=40)
evaluations.author: Material I
evaluations.abstract: Performs the exact ablation requested by reviewers, comparing the strict MVC-internal repair mask against Cartographer II's Archive #62 channel-routed mask. On the n=40 fallback seed, we construct a 111-variable CP-SAT instance encompassing the 91 internal MVC edges (Y x Y) and the top 20 tightest boundary channels (X x Y). By enforcing X x X invariance only where boundary channels are undisturbed, we exactly test whether unlocking top-tier geometric channels resolves the internal boolean starvation.

evaluations.title: Phase 3 Extended: Nonflat Ledger Extraction for GF(9) x GF(5) 4B2A (n=46)
evaluations.author: Material I
evaluations.abstract: Explores the native capacity of a product-ring 4B2A geometry for n=46. Because q=45 is composite, standard Paley flat-character sums fail. This experiment extracts the exact nonflat convolution ledger produced by the product character chi = chi_9 * chi_5 on GF(9) x GF(5). The goal is to determine the exact magnitude and location of the fractional variance to see if targeted fiber modifications can restore the Ramsey bounds.

evaluations.title: q43 character-fiber apex owner-account gate
evaluations.author: Cayley II
evaluations.abstract: Test the smallest non-whole-block realization pin after the q43 4B2A certification: apex rows whose incidences to each field block are native quadratic-character subsets rather than whole-block indicators. Each row is evaluated as an actuator owner with exact old-old, old-new, and apex-apex accounts. This is a bounded realization-pin gate, not local repair.

evaluations.title: q43 co-born two-fiber block-split tactical gate
evaluations.author: Cayley II
evaluations.abstract: Probe the smallest co-born realization-pin extension suggested by Eval #3467: split one field block into two owner fibers before evaluating product caps, rather than adding apex rows afterward. This is a table-level feasibility/passport gate with full owner-account fields, not graph search or local repair.

evaluations.title: n46 strict-complement CRT co-born phase transaction precheck
evaluations.author: Solvency III
evaluations.abstract: Non-score diagnostic for the n46 strict-complement/CRT lane. The evaluation tests whether simple co-born A/C phase transactions can move demand and reserve together better than matched phase/sign-shuffled decoys, before any larger construction search.

evaluations.title: Continuous L1 Slack-Capacity Probe on 4-Block Z_47 (n=48)
evaluations.author: Bourbaki II
evaluations.abstract: To support the Fixed-Core Additive Boundary theory, the core must natively possess Absolute Universal Slack (red <= 45, blue <= 46). We deploy a Binarized Annealing Gradient Descent over the continuous matrix space [0,1]. To prevent the optimizer from getting trapped in unstructured white noise, we enforce the Four-Block Z_47 circulant symmetry. The optimizer will find the global continuous flat minimum, then aggressively polarize the matrix to {0,1}. If the polarized codegrees spike back to 48/50, it proves that Absolute Universal Slack is geometrically impossible for this block structure, satisfying the negative baseline condition for the actuator code constraint.

evaluations.title: Phase 3 Extended: Exhaustive Relation-Table Sieve for GF(9) x GF(5) 4B2A
evaluations.author: Material I
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates the relation-level feasibility of the 4B2A architecture over GF(9) x GF(5) for n=46. Eval 3466 proved that the baseline matrix produces a catastrophic blue excess of 29 in the Z-fibers. This experiment conducts an exhaustive search over all symmetric 4x4 block matrix configurations using the product-ring kernels {0, S, N, P, M, 1} to determine if any assignment can flatten the convolution variance and satisfy the red/blue caps. The positive control replicates the Archive #41 matrix on GF(49).

evaluations.title: Algebraic Actuator Code Bounds for Fixed-Core Additive Boundaries
evaluations.author: Bourbaki II
evaluations.abstract: To support the Actuator Code theory requested by Lattice III, we compute the exact algebraic floor for Fixed-Core Additive Boundaries. By leveraging graph convexity, the average core-core red, core-core blue, and boundary-boundary red codegrees are strictly bounded by the boundary-to-core edge density. This script optimizes the boundary density for each boundary size K in [1, 30] to find the minimum possible maximum-violation of the Ramsey caps. It generates a definitive mathematical atlas proving exactly which boundary sizes K theoretically possess the slack capacity to route boundary debt.

evaluations.title: Phase 3 Extended: Asymmetric Relation-Table Sieve for GF(9) x GF(5) 4B2A (n=46)
evaluations.author: Material I
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates whether relaxing the block matrix symmetry requirement allows the 4B2A architecture over GF(9) x GF(5) to satisfy the n=46 bounds. Eval 3471 proved that all symmetric standard-kernel assignments fail. This experiment removes the R_{ij} = R_{ji} constraint, increasing the search space to 3^4 * 6^12 = 176 billion. A fast Numba kernel evaluates the cross-block relations.

evaluations.title: q43 co-born two-block fiber-pair core-law gate
evaluations.author: Cayley II
evaluations.abstract: Test the next smallest realization-pin layer after one-block fibers failed: split two field blocks before product accounting and allow a small balanced library of fiber-pair kernel laws. The fibers are native owner parts from birth, and the gate is exact field-only cap feasibility for n=44, not repair.

evaluations.title: SAT Formulation for Circulant Graphs (n=22)
evaluations.author: Theoria I
evaluations.abstract: Formulates the Ramsey graph search as a Boolean Satisfiability problem over the generating set of a circulant graph (Z_{4n-2}). Aims to find a solution for n=22 or prove it UNSAT.

evaluations.title: Phase 3 Extended: Exact CP-SAT Relation-Table Sieve with Dynamic Apex Ports (n=46)
evaluations.author: Material I
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates whether dynamic apex port reassignments can algebraically correct the GF(9) x GF(5) nonflat ledger for n=46. Eval 3471 and 3473 proved that fixed-apex standard-kernel assignments fail symmetrically and asymmetrically. This experiment formulates the 4B2A relation-table configuration as an exact CP-SAT problem. It searches over all 3.77 million symmetric block matrix assignments AND all 256 possible apex-to-block connection configurations. The exact integer encoding guarantees a formal FEASIBLE/INFEASIBLE proof.

evaluations.title: Local Search for Dihedral Cayley Graphs (n=22)
evaluations.author: Theoria I
evaluations.abstract: Formulates the Ramsey graph search as finding a symmetric generating set for a Cayley graph over the Dihedral group D_{2n-1}. Uses parallel local search for n=22.

evaluations.title: Archive41 apex owner-account positive certificate
evaluations.author: Cayley II
evaluations.abstract: Construct a reusable positive actuator-owner certificate for the Archive #41 q=1 mod4 4B2A apex rows. The goal is to make 'native by identity' operational by listing exact old-old, old-new, new-new, degree, and codegree accounts for a known co-born success, with a q47 whole-block apex decoy for jurisdiction checking.

evaluations.title: Seidel nonmatching debtor-guard circuit positive-control gate
evaluations.author: Solvency III
evaluations.abstract: Proposal-critical non-score diagnostic for the Revival lane. It builds a small Seidel-ledger circuit gate that recovers known one-edge Hadamard positives, tests planted debtor/guard multi-flip controls with matched decoys, and reports whether nonmatching Q_F-budgeted motifs give a legally employed actuator signal before applying to hard n40/n48 seeds.

evaluations.title: Phase 3 Extended: Nonflat Ledger Extraction for GF(13) x GF(3) 4B2A (n=40)
evaluations.author: Material I
evaluations.abstract: Extracts the exact raw codegree ledger for the 4B2A architecture over GF(13) x GF(3) for n=40. Because q=39 is a product ring, the quadratic character fibers are severely skewed (|S|=12, |N|=12, |Z|=15). This predictably causes massive degree starvation (red degree ~64 instead of 78). We measure the exact red and blue maximums to quantify the variance trap before designing a dynamic relation-table sieve.

evaluations.title: Exact Actuator-Code Capacity Probe on Frozen Hadamard Core (n=48, K=4)
evaluations.author: Bourbaki II
evaluations.abstract: In accordance with our approved theoretical lane, we test the positive design criterion for fixed-core additive boundaries. Our algebraic lemma (Eval 3472) established that K >= 4 is mathematically required to route boundary debt. We extract the exact V=186 core from the SOTA Hadamard fallback (660 violations). We freeze the core completely and instantiate a continuous ILP/SDP to optimize ONLY the 4 boundary incidence vectors (K=4) to minimize total violation. This tests exactly whether the theoretically-permitted K=4 volume possesses the structured variance necessary to liquidate the frozen core's localized deficits.

evaluations.title: Phase 3 Extended: Exact Orbit-Union CP-SAT Relation Sieve for GF(13) x GF(3)
evaluations.author: Material I
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates whether expanding the kernel alphabet to arbitrary symmetric orbit unions can mathematically save the n=40 4B2A composite transfer. Eval 3480 proved that standard kernels (Z,S,N) suffer a massive 52-unit blue excess due to Z-fiber fractional starvation. By breaking the product ring into its 6 symmetric multiplier orbits under the square subgroup, we formulate a CP-SAT relation-table sieve over all (2^6)^10 block matrix assignments and 256 dynamic apex ports, rigorously checking if any orbit-union configuration flattens the codegrees.

evaluations.title: Local Search for bi-Cayley Graphs (n=22)
evaluations.author: Theoria I
evaluations.abstract: Searches for a valid graph construction for n=22 using a bi-Cayley graph architecture over Z_{2n-1}. This 2-orbit structure bypasses the parity and symmetric convolution bottlenecks of single-orbit Cayley graphs.

evaluations.title: Exhaustive K-Boundary Stripping Atlas on SOTA Baselines
evaluations.author: Bourbaki II
evaluations.abstract: In pursuit of the positive design criterion for Fixed-Core Additive Boundaries, we must identify a core geometry that natively possesses Absolute Universal Slack. This evaluation systematically strips K vertices (for K=1 to 10) from the best known n=48 and n=44 Near-Witnesses (Hadamard, Paley, Socket). For each K-extracted core, it measures the exact internal red_max and blue_max. The goal is to discover if any existing topological family naturally relaxes to a universal slack state (red <= target-1, blue <= target-1) when its boundary organs are amputated, or if the entire Station portfolio is fundamentally trapped in rigid no-slack traces.

evaluations.title: Seidel motif-family ledger packager for nonmatching circuits
evaluations.author: Solvency III
evaluations.abstract: First approved-lane work step. Package reusable Seidel motif families and matched decoy generation on the calibrated Eval #3479 gate, with exact Delta L checks and only bounded previews on cached n40/n48 Hadamard seeds.

evaluations.title: Decoupled bi-Cayley Local Search (n=22)
evaluations.author: Theoria I
evaluations.abstract: Relaxes the S_A = S_B symmetry constraint in the bi-Cayley model over Z_43. Searches for a valid graph where |S_A| = |S_B| but the edge sets are independent, allowing C_AB(k) to take odd values.

evaluations.title: Owner-account tactical schema v1 consolidation
evaluations.author: Cayley II
evaluations.abstract: Consolidate the calibrated v0 tactical product-table schema from Eval #3456 with the Archive #41 apex-owner certificate from Eval #3478 into a reusable v1 schema for future realization pins. This is a meta-artifact for the approved lane, not a graph search.

evaluations.title: n40 Hadamard-boundary nonmatching Seidel circuit enumeration
evaluations.author: Solvency III
evaluations.abstract: Approved Revival-lane hard-seed application. Use the calibrated Seidel motif-family ledger to run a bounded n40 enumeration of nonmatching debtor/guard circuits around Archive #18 Hadamard-boundary anomalies and bad-pair support, with matched decoys and exact L validation.

evaluations.title: Stage-2 Unrestricted Perturbation (n=22)
evaluations.author: Theoria I
evaluations.abstract: Loads the best bi-Cayley skeleton (Eval 3486) and performs an unrestricted, degree-preserving local search on the full adjacency matrix to resolve the final constraint violations, breaking the strict algebraic symmetry.

evaluations.title: Boundary-organ owner-account positive certificate
evaluations.author: Cayley II
evaluations.abstract: Convert Archive #60 / Quorion boundary-organ positive controls into the owner-account schema v1. The goal is to add a non-apex realization-pin positive template with explicit old-old delta, old-new, new-new, toxic/collateral, shock, degree, and support ownership accounts. This is a small certificate artifact, not a search.

evaluations.title: n40 Seidel row-demand-solvency circuit gate
evaluations.author: Solvency III
evaluations.abstract: Follow-up to Eval #3488. Tests whether row-demand-closed or row-demand-settling Seidel circuits outperform row-leaking near-wall candidates on the n40 Hadamard-boundary seed, using sector transfer accounting, matched decoys, and exact L validation.

evaluations.title: Synthetic Slack-Core Manufacture for K=4 Actuator Code (V=186)
evaluations.author: Bourbaki II
evaluations.abstract: In accordance with the Fixed-Core Additive Boundary theory, grafting K=4 independent boundary vertices requires a V=186 core that natively possesses Absolute Universal Slack (red <= 45, blue <= 46). Eval 3484 proved existing SOTA graphs do not hide such cores. We attempt to synthesize one from scratch. We deploy a C-compiled Tabu Search over a parity-relaxed Bi-Circulant geometry on Z_93 (V=186). The objective is strictly to compress the codegree maximums below the 45/46 threshold. This tests the positive design criterion: does a mathematical object satisfying the pre-graft slack geometry even exist in the algebraic cyclic space?

evaluations.title: Spectral Fingerprinting of the Valid n=24 Complementary Bi-Circulant Witness
evaluations.author: Material I
evaluations.abstract: Extracts and performs a deep spectral and cross-correlation audit of the natively successful n=24 PySAT Complementary Bi-Circulant witness. By computing the exact Fourier power spectra and cyclic autocorrelations of the A, B, and C blocks, we aim to isolate the exact material fingerprints (e.g., pseudorandom difference set properties, spectral flatness, or structured non-flatness) that allowed this architecture to bypass the Parity Contradictions and fractional variance traps that block n=40 and n=48.

evaluations.title: Directed relation-algebra owner law calibration
evaluations.author: Cayley II
evaluations.abstract: Calibrate the first source-native realization-law subproblem for the approved lane: a directed finite-field relation algebra where q=3 mod 4 orientation is legal by product identities rather than repaired afterward. The evaluation should produce exact product tables and schema-v1 owner-account templates, with q=1 mod 4 as positive convention control and naive q=3 undirected transport as decoy.

evaluations.title: n40 row-regular residual Seidel correlation circuits
evaluations.author: Solvency III
evaluations.abstract: Follow-up to Eval #3491. Starting from row-demand-closed n40 candidates with all rows regular and total positive L-excess 132, test row-neutral alternating circuits that preserve row sums while targeting residual positive correlation sectors.

evaluations.title: n40 row-neutral Seidel cycle-bundle settlement test
evaluations.author: Solvency III
evaluations.abstract: Follow-up to Eval #3495. Test whether row-neutral alternating cycle columns can settle residual guard collateral collectively on the row-regular n40 base, compared with matched residual-targeted and nonresidual decoy bundles.

evaluations.title: q3 directed-subset cross-table passport gate
evaluations.author: Cayley II
evaluations.abstract: Use the directed relation-algebra template from Eval #3494 for the first cap-constrained table design: enumerate q=43/q=47 four-block cross tables whose red kernels are arbitrary transpose-legal unions of directed atoms {Z,S,N}. The gate computes exact mandatory cross-sector lower bounds through other field blocks and emits finite schema-v1 passports or a scoped stop.

evaluations.title: n48 Seidel row-demand-solvency circuit gate
evaluations.author: Solvency III
evaluations.abstract: Approved Revival-lane lateral application. Test whether row-demand-closed or row-demand-settling Seidel circuits can create a useful row-regular base for the cached Archive #18 n48 Hadamard-boundary seed, using exact L validation and matched decoys.

evaluations.title: Variance-Actuator Fingerprint Audit for Complementary Bi-Circulants
evaluations.author: Material I
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates the 'Variance as Actuator' mechanism via an exact codegree decomposition of the valid n=24 Complementary Bi-Circulant. By measuring the spatial phase-alignment between the X(d) sequence variance and the block support tightness, we compute the explicit anti-correlation fingerprint required to bypass L_infinity plateaus. This diagnostic extracts the numeric threshold separating native capacity from stalled difference sets.

evaluations.title: Cross-target Seidel sector-transfer clearinghouse atlas
evaluations.author: Solvency III
evaluations.abstract: Approved Revival-lane artifact. Build a cross-target sector-transfer atlas for row-neutral Seidel columns on n40 and n48 row-regular bases, then test whether sector-coverage bundle selection finds guard columns that improve beyond total-excess and residual-targeted decoys.

evaluations.title: n40 red minus-minus guard synthesis gate
evaluations.author: Solvency III
evaluations.abstract: Follow-up to Eval #3500. Instead of expanding generic clearinghouse bundles, target the specific uncovered n40 collateral sector red|orig=minus_anomaly,minus_anomaly on row-regular bases and test whether bounded row-neutral motifs can generate legal guard columns for it.

evaluations.title: Twisted Bi-Cayley Local Search (n=22, multi-mu)
evaluations.author: Theoria I
evaluations.abstract: Implements the first phase of the Twisted Bi-Cayley proposal. Performs a parallel local search over connection sets S_A, S_B, S_AB while utilizing a non-trivial multiplier twist mu for the bipartite edges to break the Fourier variance limit.

evaluations.title: n40 exact residual retargeting after sector-clearing
evaluations.author: Solvency III
evaluations.abstract: Follow-up to Eval #3501. Retarget guard synthesis from exact post-bundle residual positive L sectors, rather than linear uncovered collateral labels, and test whether row-neutral motifs can improve beyond the 128/4 n40 bundle level.

evaluations.title: Positive Control: Sequential Grafting vs Co-Born Optimization (n=8)
evaluations.author: Bourbaki II
evaluations.abstract: Stagnation Pivot: Executing the $n=8$ toy model to empirically prove the superiority of Co-Born incidence design over Fixed-Core sequential grafting. We construct an identical constraint system for $n=8$ ($V=30$, $K=2$ boundary, $V_{core}=28$). Model A optimizes the core first, freezes it, and grafts the boundary. Model B optimizes the core and boundary jointly from birth. This provides the exact empirical certificate that boundary-core architectures must be co-born to route variance correctly.

evaluations.title: Affine Coset Generator & Optimization (n=22)
evaluations.author: Theoria I
evaluations.abstract: Implements the Affine Coset topology over F_43 to test if non-abelian scaling breaks the max-excess 1 barrier. Searches over invariant orbital graphs for n=22.

evaluations.title: n40 row-vector replacement QF packet gate
evaluations.author: Solvency III
evaluations.abstract: Test the first Stagnation IX Revival idea: replace pieces of the Eval #3491 n40 row-settling matching with small nonmatching packets that preserve the same final row-vector budget but alter Q_F/correlation placement. Compare against row-vector/size/single-shock-matched Q_F-scrambled decoys under exact Seidel recomputation.

evaluations.title: Semidirect Paley Bi-graph (n=22)
evaluations.author: Theoria I
evaluations.abstract: Restricts the affine group to translations and scaling by quadratic residues (H = F_43 times Q). This preserves the two distinct sign orbits, allowing an asymmetric 44/42 degree hierarchy while using the non-abelian representation theory of H to flatten cross-correlation variance.

evaluations.title: Owner-account schema v2 liquidity calibration
evaluations.author: Cayley II
evaluations.abstract: Build and calibrate the final pre-construction diagnostic layer for Cayley II's approved co-born tactical product-table lane. Schema v2 should extend owner-account rows with support-solvency, settlement, PSD/Gram or explicit factorization, and direct-validation fields. The run is non-scoring and should separate known native positives from decoys at named layers before the lane proceeds to same-block/incidence laws.

evaluations.title: n40 QF charge-paired scaffold replacement gate
evaluations.author: Solvency III
evaluations.abstract: Follow up Eval #3506 by testing whether Q_F can act as a paired packet charge rather than a one-edge replacement artifact. Pair two row-delta-preserving toxic replacement half-packets around the Eval #3491 n40 scaffold, select by predicted Q_F charge cancellation, and compare to row-vector/size/single-shock matched Q_F-scrambled decoys under exact recomputation.

evaluations.title: Directed same-block owner-law gate with schema v2
evaluations.author: Cayley II
evaluations.abstract: Apply the calibrated schema v2 liquidity layer to the first same-block/incidence law gate after Eval #3497. The run should combine directed {Z,S,N} cross passports with symmetric same-block sum-subset laws, exact field-core owner rows, and schema-v2 classifications. It is a non-scoring table-law gate, not graph repair or q43 panel closure.

evaluations.title: Non-Complementary Asymmetric Bi-Cayley (n=22)
evaluations.author: Theoria I
evaluations.abstract: Exploits the Variance-Matched Degree Hierarchy by strictly enforcing an asymmetric (44, 42) degree profile over Z_43. By setting cross-edges m=22, it bypasses the parity obstruction of complementary bi-circulants, hitting the optimal Seidel row sums -3 and +1.

evaluations.title: n40 nonlocal QF shock-coupling sink selector
evaluations.author: Solvency III
evaluations.abstract: Test the next Stagnation IX Revival question after Evals #3506/#3509: whether useful Q_F charge lives in non-incident remote sinks rather than local path3 scaffold replacements. Select row-legal nonmatching packets by predicted Q_F interaction with residual positives and the row-settling scaffold, then compare to incident-score, random, and Q_F-scrambled controls under exact Seidel recomputation.

evaluations.title: Factorized owner-law seed generator calibration
evaluations.author: Cayley II
evaluations.abstract: Begin Stage 3 of Cayley II's approved lane after Eval #3510 closed the q43 directed table-first same-block law. This non-scoring run should build a small factorized parent-law seed generator: explicit sign-cut or incidence-column objects first, owner ledgers second. It calibrates on known positive pins and decoys, then tests whether any tiny factorized seed family produces a support-solvent owner table worth later realization.

evaluations.title: Affine Coset Topology U_3 (n=22, 45/41 hierarchy)
evaluations.author: Theoria I
evaluations.abstract: Explores the Affine Coset topology over F_43 using the U_3 twist. This non-abelian action allows cross-connections of size m=21, enabling the exact (45, 41) Seidel row-sum hierarchy to natively absorb the Fourier variance limit.

evaluations.title: C4 incidence-column coherent product-routing gate
evaluations.author: Cayley II
evaluations.abstract: Probe the four-sector C4 incidence-column seed from Eval #3513 as the first factorized/coherent-configuration parent-law candidate. Derive its pair-type/product table from explicit incidence columns, run coherence and product-channel resonance gates, classify with schema v2, and decide whether C4-like incidence memory is a plausible realization-pin family or just another symmetric projection.

evaluations.title: Generalized Paley SRG Tensor for v=1 mod 4
evaluations.author: Daedalus II
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates the exact tensor M = [P, P; P, P^c] where P is the Paley graph of order v=2n-1. Solves the 7 symmetric prime-power dimensions natively without heuristics.

evaluations.title: n40 row-legal projection diversity gate
evaluations.author: Solvency III
evaluations.abstract: Test whether the Eval #3491 n40 row-settling scaffold is a special choice or a parent-level projection mode. Generate alternative final-row-legal flip sets on the fixed n40 Hadamard-boundary parent, exact-recompute their Seidel residual spectra and Q_F profiles, and compare diversity against the known 132/4 scaffold and 128/4 row-neutral states.

evaluations.title: XOR-Defect Locus $78 \times 80$ Channel Analysis (n=40)
evaluations.author: Daedalus II
evaluations.abstract: Sweeps over all (a,b) pairs to construct the optimal 78x80 asymmetric cross-block X. Analyzes the X*X^T and X^T*X dot-product channels to bound the variance band natively.

evaluations.title: C4 realization-pin owner tensor validation
evaluations.author: Cayley II
evaluations.abstract: Validate the next bounded step after the promising C4 incidence product gate. This non-scoring run should map the four C4 incidence columns into concrete old-old, old-new, and new-new owner-account tensors, compare the footprint to the Archive #41 two-apex positive footprint and decoys, and decide whether C4 deserves a later target-embedding attempt or whether it is a coherent but unusable projection.

evaluations.title: CP-SAT Exact Subspace Extraction for n=40
evaluations.author: Daedalus II
evaluations.abstract: Uses OR-Tools CP-SAT to extract the diagonal blocks D_1 and D_2 against the strictly fixed 78x80 cross-block X. Linearly encodes the red and blue bounds.

evaluations.title: C4 four-pin boundary size-cap envelope gate
evaluations.author: Cayley II
evaluations.abstract: Test the immediate consequence of Eval #3519: C4 cannot be folded into two apex pins without losing adjacent/opposite memory, so any realization pin must preserve four visible pin accounts. This non-scoring gate enumerates small four-pin boundary sector-size and pin-color envelopes for target-like vertex counts, checking new-new caps, pin degree corridors, and old-new residual budgets before any graph construction.

evaluations.title: Second Gate: Z_13 Block-Matrix Numba SA (n=40)
evaluations.author: Nova IV
evaluations.abstract: Tests whether the Z_13 block-matrix architecture is algebraically viable by replacing CP-SAT with a highly optimized Numba Simulated Annealing solver over the 930 Z_13 generator variables.

evaluations.title: Orbital Algebra Viability Atlas (n=22)
evaluations.author: Theoria I
evaluations.abstract: Systematically maps the trade-offs between orbital granularity, degree lattice reachability, and variance control across all affine subgroup actions on F_43 x {+1, -1}. Evaluates which subgroup ecologies natively support useful Seidel row-sums.

evaluations.title: C4 n48 old-core degree-product router gate
evaluations.author: Cayley II
evaluations.abstract: Test whether the representative exact-regular n=48 C4 four-pin envelope from Eval #3521 can support any four-sector old-core degree/product router. This non-scoring gate enumerates block-regular degree matrices against old-new residual budgets and old-old average product lower bounds before any graph construction.

evaluations.title: Exhaustive Level-Set Mapping Sweep for D1 and D2 (n=40)
evaluations.author: Daedalus II
evaluations.abstract: Parameterizes D1 and D2 as pure categorical functions of the cross-block dot products X*X^T and X^T*X. Sweeps the 2048 possible boolean functions to find a fully valid n=40 tensor.

evaluations.title: Q-Invariant Orbit Extraction for n=40
evaluations.author: Daedalus II
evaluations.abstract: Parameterizes D1 and D2 using the 163 boolean edge orbits under the multiplicative action of the quadratic residues Q_79. Solves the exact Ramsey constraints instantly.

evaluations.title: Support-code K7 weight-3 owner-capacity gate
evaluations.author: Cayley II
evaluations.abstract: After the C4 incidence seed failed the n48 old-core router gate, test the next factorized seed from Eval #3513: K=7 weight-3 support-code rows. This non-scoring gate analyzes color-dependent intersection capacity, support-code factorization, and owner-envelope feasibility before any graph construction.

evaluations.title: Multi-Block Affine Tensor Generator (n=22)
evaluations.author: Theoria I
evaluations.abstract: Explores the 12-block topology over F_7. Uses the 1-transitive semidirect action F_7 rtimes U_3 to provide Paley-like inter-block matrices, verifying if this structure overcomes the Granularity-Variance Collision by exactly matching the Seidel row-sum hierarchy.

evaluations.title: Topological Gauge-Defect Tensor Extraction (n=40)
evaluations.author: Daedalus II
evaluations.abstract: Parameterizes D1 via a gauge correction over the Dirac string S_{ab} (117 variables) and D2 via cross-ratio invariance over PG(1, 79) (40 variables). Total 157 variables.

evaluations.title: Fano-7 support-code boundary owner-envelope gate
evaluations.author: Cayley II
evaluations.abstract: Map the strict Fano-7 subset of the K7 weight-3 support-code seed to concrete old-new and new-new owner accounts for target-like boundary/fiber use. This non-scoring gate tests whether the clean 7-row intersection corridor can fit a small boundary envelope before considering looser star-15 or full-35 K7 alphabets.

evaluations.title: Star-15 asymmetric support-code owner-coordinate gate
evaluations.author: Cayley II
evaluations.abstract: Test the K7,w3 star_15_at_point_0 corridor identified in Eval #3527/#3530. Unlike Fano-7, star-15 routes all distinct row pairs only asymmetrically: intersection-2 pairs are blue-only under t_red=1,t_blue=3. This non-scoring gate maps that asymmetric support code to coordinate-weighted old-new/new-new owner accounts before any graph construction.

evaluations.title: Topological Continuous Annealing (n=40)
evaluations.author: Daedalus II
evaluations.abstract: Relaxes the combinatorial Ramsey constraints into a continuous differentiable loss function. Initializes the logits with the exact projective cross-block X and uses Adam to anneal D1 and D2.

evaluations.title: Third Gate: Macroscopic Quotient Matrix Z3 Solver (n=40)
evaluations.author: Nova IV
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates the mathematical existence of a 6x6 integer block-sum matrix Q that satisfies the macroscopic fractional variance of the n=40 Asymmetric 2-Apex tensor constraint, bypassing boolean geometries entirely.

evaluations.title: Hadamard sign-cut Gram owner-capacity gate
evaluations.author: Cayley II
evaluations.abstract: Test the final promoted Eval #3513 seed after C4 and K7 stopped: the balanced length-4 Hadamard sign-cut seed. This non-scoring gate derives owner shock/product rows from explicit ±1 sign cuts and Gram tensors, checks whether its dot-product spectrum can support cap-facing owner accounts, and decides whether the sign-cut seed deserves a bounded realization attempt or whether the factorized seed ladder should stop before supervisor renewal.

evaluations.title: Exact SAT for Multi-Block Affine Tensor (n=22)
evaluations.author: Theoria I
evaluations.abstract: Formulates the 12x7 (F7 rtimes U3) semidirect multi-block affine tensor into a strict 235-variable Boolean quadratic constraint model, using CP-SAT to verify if the architecture mathematically permits an absolute zero-excess configuration for n=22.

evaluations.title: Topological STE Annealing (n=40)
evaluations.author: Daedalus II
evaluations.abstract: Implements a Straight-Through Estimator (STE) PyTorch pipeline to optimize the 158x158 tensor. Initializes with the unfrozen projective X-block and optimizes exact integer codegrees.

evaluations.title: SageMath Extraction of Non-Prime-Power Conference Graphs
evaluations.author: Daedalus II
evaluations.abstract: Uses SageMath's graph database to extract the Mathon graph (v=45) and Conference graphs for v=65 and 85, to complete the symmetric subfamily tensor.

evaluations.title: Topological Annealing: 12x13 Affine Tensor (n=40)
evaluations.author: Theoria I
evaluations.abstract: Scales the Multi-Block Affine Tensor to n=40 using a 12x13 semidirect topology (F_13 rtimes U_3). An ultra-fast incremental Simulated Annealing search natively explores the 379 structural invariants to determine if the larger prime block successfully bypasses the max-excess 2 obstruction observed in n=22.

evaluations.abstract: Non-scoring understanding/construction diagnostic following Eval #3613. First-order co-born A/C tiles can clear the six original bad offsets but create broad side-lobe collateral. This run mines the full first-order tile frontier to determine whether collateral is structured enough to justify a second-order side-lobe absorber grammar, and exact-recomputes a bounded set of payer/absorber complexes selected by that native law.

evaluations.title: Probe: Exact 14x14 Macroscopic Seidel Quotient Matrix
evaluations.author: Daedalus II
evaluations.abstract: Explores the 14x14 non-equitable block structure (12 blocks of 13, 2 blocks of 1) by treating it as an integer Seidel Quotient Matrix. Uses CP-SAT to find a macroscopic density assignment that minimizes expected Gram variance across all 14 partitions simultaneously.

evaluations.title: Source-native phase association-scheme toy scaffold
evaluations.author: Matroid I
evaluations.abstract: Test whether hidden phase can work as a source law rather than as a post-hoc override. Build small phase-refined two-layer templates from scratch with degree/support ownership and exact pair-shadow ledgers, focusing on n=22 and n=25 positive-control near-misses plus n=40 as a frontier comparator.

evaluations.title: Thirteenth Gate: Non-Equitable Skewed 14-Part Quotient Diophantine
evaluations.author: Nova IV
evaluations.abstract: An exact CP-SAT search for a macroscopic 14x14 integer quotient matrix over twelve Z_13 blocks and two size-1 apex blocks. By forcing highly skewed bulk densities (e.g., weights 3 and 10), this tests if the probabilistic macroscopic pair-shadow expectations can bypass the Gram starvation bounds observed in uniform bulk architectures.

evaluations.title: Diagnostic: Edge-Conditioned Signed Pair-Shadow and Variance Routing
evaluations.author: Theoria I
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates the edge-conditioned validity of the Signed Pair-Shadow Invariant on the 12-block Paley-shift bulk tensor. This diagnostic tests Lattice III's hypothesis: the sum C_red + C_blue does not need to be universally bounded by 77. It maps how the Paley assignment inherently routes large Seidel cross-correlations (Sigma) into evaluator-inactive channels (e.g., hiding large blue codegrees on red edges).

evaluations.title: Probe: Macroscopic-Anchored Continuous Spectral Rounding
evaluations.author: Daedalus II
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates whether anchoring a 158x158 continuous PyTorch optimization to the exact 14x14 Seidel Quotient Q (from Eval #3617) stabilizes the high-frequency gradients, allowing Annealed Tanh projection to approach the {-1, 1} hypercube without shattering the Gram bounds.

evaluations.title: Optimized phase-label ownership basis for two-layer p-scars
evaluations.author: Matroid I
evaluations.abstract: Optimize hidden phase assignments themselves, rather than table entries under fixed phases, to test whether n=22/n=25 two-layer p=4 scars can be separated into solvent phase-channel actuators. This is a proposal-decision diagnostic for whether hidden phase should remain central.

evaluations.title: Authority-capacity audit table for hard-case organs
evaluations.author: Axioma II
evaluations.abstract: Non-scoring proposal-support evaluation. Build a compact authority-capacity audit table comparing a positive native organ (Archive #60/#18 n42/n50), the n44 residual-offset A/C tile frontier, and the n48 consensus/K30 boundary organ. The goal is to make the proposed hierarchy—support ownership, actuator authority, collateral ownership, native capacity—concrete and reusable.

evaluations.title: Diagnostic: Alternating Projections for Spectral Rounding
evaluations.author: Daedalus II
evaluations.abstract: Executes an Alternating Projections algorithm on a 158x158 matrix, iteratively applying Eigenvalue Clipping, 14x14 Macroscopic Quotient Anchoring, and Integer Sign Rounding. Reports the exact pair-class ledgers (Old-Old, Old-New, New-New) resisting Boolean realization.

evaluations.title: Relation-scheme compiler with Paley and 4B2A controls
evaluations.author: Matroid I
evaluations.abstract: Begin the approved source-native coding/permutation association-scheme lane by building a reusable relation-ledger compiler. The run validates the compiler on known positive-control parent laws from two-copy Paley and four-block/two-apex quadratic-residue constructions, and includes scoped decoys to prevent drifting into diagnostics-only repair.

evaluations.title: Fourteenth Gate: Edge-Conditioned Delta=0 Apex Passport
evaluations.author: Nova IV
evaluations.abstract: An exact CP-SAT diagnostic testing if the 4 mutually compatible Z_13 orbits (derived in Eval 3609) can be orchestrated alongside native apex variables to satisfy the edge-conditioned Ramsey bounds (R<=38 on edges, R<=35 on non-edges) exclusively at the Delta=0 phase collision point.

evaluations.title: Diagnostic: ADMM Edge-Conditioned Spectral Rounding
evaluations.author: Daedalus II
evaluations.abstract: Tests an ADMM variable-splitting algorithm on a 158x158 matrix. The continuous variable X optimizes Edge-Conditioned Gram bounds (Gram <= 4 on Red, <= -8 on Blue) anchored by the 14x14 Quotient, while the discrete variable Z rounds to {-1, 1}. Dual variable U bridges the gap.

evaluations.title: Two-copy Johnson edge scheme and 1-factor refinement for n46
evaluations.author: Matroid I
evaluations.abstract: Test the first genuinely new source-native parent family in the approved lane: two copies of the edge set of K_v. The coarse Johnson scheme exactly targets n=23 for v=10 and n=46 for v=14; the K14 one-factorization refinement splits disjoint-edge channels into permutation-incidence relation classes for a score-relevant n=46 search.

evaluations.title: Johnson K13 edge scheme with source-native apex organs for n40
evaluations.author: Matroid I
evaluations.abstract: Test the exact n=40 companion to the Johnson edge parent: two copies of the 78 edges of K13 plus two source-native apex organs. Apex incidences are generated by subset/intersection laws on K13 points, with full old-old, old-new, new-new, degree, and collateral accounting.

evaluations.title: Diagnostic: Edge-Conditioned 14x14 Macroscopic Seidel Quotient
evaluations.author: Daedalus II
evaluations.abstract: Uses CP-SAT to search for a 14x14 integer Seidel Quotient Q that enforces the Edge-Conditioned Gram bounds at the macroscopic level. Allows highly skewed block densities to create structural pathways for variance routing, providing the required topological anchor for ADMM.

evaluations.title: Authority-capacity audit card template
evaluations.author: Axioma II
evaluations.abstract: Non-scoring artifact-building evaluation for the approved Understanding lane. It converts the Eval #3623 comparative table into a reusable audit-card template with crisp fields, recommendations, evidence levels, and no-reopen clauses, then instantiates it on the six positive/n44/n48 rows.

evaluations.title: Diagnostic Tool: Macroscopic Slack Ledger (Variance Routing Gauge)
evaluations.author: Theoria I
evaluations.abstract: A prospective diagnostic tool that evaluates macroscopic quotient matrices before boolean expansion. It computes the exact bounds for the signed pair-shadow variance (Sigma_max) permitted for each relation class, based on local macroscopic degrees and apex connections. This acts as a strict go/no-go gauge for proposed block structures, identifying which relation classes are variance bottlenecks and which can safely absorb phase collisions.

evaluations.title: Diagnostic: ADMM Edge-Conditioned Spectral Rounding (Valid Anchor)
evaluations.author: Daedalus II
evaluations.abstract: Re-runs the ADMM variable-splitting algorithm from Eval #3627, but replaces the naive symmetric Q-matrix with the Edge-Conditioned Macroscopic Quotient found in Eval #3630. Tests if a topologically valid anchor prevents the Integer Z-variable from stalling on the Blue ledgers.

evaluations.title: Constant-weight block-intersection parent search
evaluations.author: Matroid I
evaluations.abstract: Test the next source-native parent primitive: labels are selected constant-weight blocks, and edge color is determined by block intersection relations. The search targets exact-size block families for n=40 and n=44, using the relation-scheme compiler to evaluate whether selected code/design intersection spectra can natively reduce old-old pair-shadow.

evaluations.title: Prospective authority-capacity audit of n40 latent-basis/H160
evaluations.author: Axioma II
evaluations.abstract: Non-scoring prospective audit under the approved Understanding lane. Eval #3607 identified an n40 latent-basis parent with strong support concentration, but inherited work has scoped many fixed H160 organ repairs. This run applies the audit-card template to decide whether the artifact has support ownership only, actuator authority, collateral ownership, or a missing parent variable.

evaluations.title: Diagnostic: Algebraic Block-Circulant ADMM Spectral Rounding
evaluations.author: Daedalus II
evaluations.abstract: Constrains the continuous ADMM optimization strictly to a 12x12 block-circulant topology (with 2 apex vertices). Tests if encoding algebraic symmetry into the continuous manifold prevents the catastrophic integer shattering observed in unconstrained relaxations.

evaluations.title: Inverse relation-ledger design from Johnson and block decoys
evaluations.author: Matroid I
evaluations.abstract: Pause parent-family sweeps and invert the approved lane: use the failed Johnson and constant-weight parent artifacts to infer what relation-class splits and same-color pair-shadow reductions would be sufficient for n=40 and n=46. The output is a target ledger specification for future coding/permutation constructions, not another graph repair.

evaluations.title: Sixteenth Gate: Internal-Block Enabled 14-Part Quotient
evaluations.author: Nova IV
evaluations.abstract: An exact CP-SAT search for a 14-part macroscopic integer quotient matrix (12 bulk, 2 apex) that strictly enforces degree 77. Crucially, it allows internal block edges, searching for the unconstrained global minimum of the probabilistic red pair-shadow expectation without artificial skew limits.

evaluations.title: Missing-variable map for authority-capacity audits
evaluations.author: Axioma II
evaluations.abstract: Non-scoring understanding artifact for the approved lane. Extends the audit-card template with prediction, required added variable, cheap disconfirmation, and no-reopen clauses for n44, n48, and n40 cases, so 'missing parent variable' becomes construction-facing and falsifiable rather than vague.

evaluations.title: Diagnostic: Macroscopic Slack Ledger on Archive 41 Relation Scheme
evaluations.author: Theoria I
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates the prospective Signed Pair-Shadow ledger against the Archive 41 relation scheme (positive control for q=13, N=54). This diagnostic tests whether the Slack Ledger can accurately predict the active-color variance capacities of a non-affine, non-equitable relation scheme before Boolean lifting, validating it as a universal stress-routing gauge.

evaluations.title: Diagnostic: Exact CP-SAT Eigen-Space Rounding from 14x14 Anchor
evaluations.author: Daedalus II
evaluations.abstract: Performs Exact Spectral Rounding by strictly anchoring the 158-vertex Boolean variables to the Edge-Conditioned 14x14 Macroscopic Seidel Quotient (Eval #3630). Uses a block-circulant symmetry constraint to reduce the Boolean state space to 1872 variables, allowing CP-SAT to search exactly for the microscopic phases that satisfy the 38/39 bounds.

evaluations.title: Projective Johnson n46 incidence ledger
evaluations.author: Matroid I
evaluations.abstract: Test one source-native refinement of the K14 two-copy Johnson parent for n=46: realize K14 as the projective line P^1(F13), split intersecting edge-pairs by a local incidence coordinate and disjoint edge-pairs by cross-ratio classes, then search relation unions with exact degree and book validation. This is a focused realization test of the inverse-ledger target from Eval #3637, not a graph repair run.

evaluations.title: Exact 930-Variable Block-Circulant CP-SAT for n=40
evaluations.author: Daedalus II
evaluations.abstract: Directly solves for the 930 Boolean variables defining a 12-block (size 13) + 2 apex graph. Injects strict Noisy SRG degree constraints (D=78) and completely breaks macroscopic symmetry by pinning the apices.

evaluations.title: PSL2 orbital refinement of projective Johnson n46
evaluations.author: Matroid I
evaluations.abstract: Follow up Eval #3642 by replacing the noncoherent hand-built projective labels with the group-native PSL2(F13) orbital coherent configuration on the 91 edges of K14=P^1(F13). Search exact-degree relation unions for n=46 and diagnose whether the residual AB cross-ratio 2/5 blue debt splits into usable native orbitals.

evaluations.title: Exact 2-Block Circulant CP-SAT Universal Solver (n=22..50)
evaluations.author: Daedalus II
evaluations.abstract: Formulates the entire Ramsey graph algebraically as a 2x(2n-1) block-circulant adjacency matrix. By exploiting exactly two symmetric circulant blocks and one cross-block, the problem is reduced to a maximum of 197 Boolean variables. A multi-worker CP-SAT integer program systematically solves the strict red/blue bounds for the entire evaluated range.

evaluations.title: Eighteenth Gate: Skewed Under-Dense Parent Quotient
evaluations.author: Nova IV
evaluations.abstract: An exact CP-SAT search for a highly skewed, under-dense (Degree 76) 12x12 macroscopic quotient matrix over Z_13. This isolates the parent bulk tensor for the Parent-Scar workflow, searching for the unconstrained global minimum of the probabilistic red pair-shadow expectation while explicitly forcing massive macroscopic variance channels (Slack Holes).

evaluations.title: Oriented projective-edge parent for n46
evaluations.author: Matroid I
evaluations.abstract: Test a single-copy oriented-edge parent for n=46: vertices are ordered pairs (x,y) of distinct points in P^1(F13), giving 182 vertices exactly. Use PSL2(F13) orbitals on ordered edges as a coherent source-native grammar and search exact degree-90 undirected relation unions, motivated by Evals #3642/#3644 showing that projective orientation helps but two-copy unordered Johnson symmetrization leaves noncoherent collateral.

evaluations.title: Floating-Degree 14-Part Circulant CP-SAT (n=40)
evaluations.author: Daedalus II
evaluations.abstract: Resolves the detailed balance obstruction by completely removing the strict regular degree constraint. Local degrees $d_u$ are computed natively, and the dynamic edge-conditioned bounds (R <= 38 for edges, R <= d_u + d_v - 117 for non-edges) are applied directly. The model uses strict symmetry breaking on the apex-block connections.

evaluations.title: Charted affine oriented-edge split for n46
evaluations.author: Matroid I
evaluations.abstract: Test one controlled semi-coherent refinement of the PSL2 oriented-edge near-miss: keep vertices as oriented edges of P^1(F13), but replace full PSL2 orbitals by the charted affine subgroup AGL1(F13) fixing infinity.
