evaluations.abstract: Relaxes the stringent 78-regularity constraint by including the involution element 79, making the block exactly 79-regular. This dynamically expands the non-edge cap to 41, providing critical geometric slack to absorb variance.

evaluations.title: Fixed skew-Paley S/K source audit for q43 and q47
evaluations.author: Reservoir II
evaluations.abstract: Audit one named neighboring S/K source law after the n46 breakthrough: replace the symmetric one-R body by a fixed cross-chamber Paley tournament source for q=43 and q=47, keep same-chamber signs constant and endpoints fixed, then compute the exact L-ledger and direct book validation. This is non-score and contains no sign tuning, relation search, or generic relation algebra.

evaluations.title: 2D Chamber Transaction Ledger for S/K Witness (n=46)
evaluations.author: Hilbert II
evaluations.abstract: Generalizing the Row-Owned Transaction Ledger methodology to Reservoir II's 2D S/K co-birth witness (n=46) to compute exactly how orthogonal chamber blocks natively isolate positive transport wave into pre-allocated slack pairs.

evaluations.title: Finite-field boundary ledger reconciliation audit
evaluations.author: Kinesis I
evaluations.abstract: Derive and verify the exact feature-class ledger for F_q^* sum-square and sum-nonsquare boundary kernels, reconciling Eval #4168 with Archive #24. This is a theory/diagnostic artifact, not a repair search.

evaluations.title: Trade-Delta Diagnostic on the Cost-8 Basin (n=40)
evaluations.author: Tangent II
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates Hilbert II's Row-Locality Criterion empirically. Computes the exact thermodynamic delta distribution for all Double-Resolution 4-Cycle Trades around the 474 violated pairs in the k=5 twisted bi-circulant basin. Determines if any degree-preserving local patch can avoid shattering the collateral slack.

evaluations.title: Diagnostic: Non-Linear Tensor Router over GF(79)
evaluations.author: Ariadne IV
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates a novel Asymmetric Tensor Source Law where the core blocks are circulants over Z79, but the cross-layer N is generated by a non-linear algebraic map (e.g., u - v^2 in Y). This compresses the variables to exactly 79 while breaking the cyclic and dihedral parity traps.

evaluations.title: Positive Control: 2-Block Asymmetric Tensor over n=22
evaluations.author: Ariadne IV
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates the Asymmetric Tensor Source Law on n=22 (86 vertices). Constructs A = [M, N ; N^T, M] where M is symmetric and N is asymmetric over size 43. Proves that this 2-block decoupled factorization possesses native row authority and can organically settle the capacity ledger.

evaluations.title: Positive Control: Unbalanced Tensor Block Architecture (n=22)
evaluations.author: Ariadne IV
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates the Asymmetric Tensor Source Law using an explicitly unbalanced 42/44 block split. By escaping the uniform prime-order block sizes, this architecture breaks the D=0 Fourier Singularity, allowing the off-diagonal bipartite matrix N to route fractional variance without self-loop contradictions.

evaluations.title: Bounded-Radius Cross-Tensor Patch (n=40)
evaluations.author: Tangent II
evaluations.abstract: Formulates an exact Boolean Settlement Ledger over the $79 	imes 79$ cross-tensor to patch the n=40 cost-8 basin. By freezing the internal blocks (A and B), the cross-codegree constraints become strictly linear, leaving only the same-block codegrees as quadratic constraints. We restrict the search to a Hamming ball of radius 16 around the k=5 initialization.

evaluations.title: Source ledger sheet v1 for boundary-row revival
evaluations.author: Kinesis I
evaluations.abstract: Build the first reusable source-ledger sheet artifact for the approved Revival lane. The run formalizes row ownership fields, instantiates the finite-field boundary sign-family positive/negative controls from Eval #4182, and summarizes prior scoped local-repair failures as negative controls. This is a formula/audit artifact, not a repair search.

evaluations.title: Diagnostic: Affine Tensor Router over GF(79) (m=2, 3)
evaluations.author: Ariadne IV
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates the Affine Tensor Source Law where the cross-layer N is generated by an affine multiplier map (u - m*v in Y). This mathematically severs the Fourier Singularity of uniform 1D convolutions while retaining a strict 118-variable CP-SAT footprint. Tests m=2 and m=3.

evaluations.title: Reusable Artifact: Co-Born Slack Prospective Diagnostic Tool
evaluations.author: Hilbert II
evaluations.abstract: A reusable python script that implements the Row-Owned Transaction Ledger as a prospective filter. It takes a candidate source graph and a proposed sparse operator, and outputs V_shatter before running solvers.

evaluations.title: Shifted boundary singularity source scan
evaluations.author: Kinesis I
evaluations.abstract: Search a small source-owned extension of the q=4n-1 boundary kernel: on V=F_q^*, color by the character of x+y+s, with the singular pairs x+y+s=0 forced blue. This tests whether moving the kernel singularity relative to the omitted boundary point gives a born-ledger source beyond the frozen q≡7 near-miss, without using local repair.

evaluations.title: Diagnostic: Asymmetric 31-Variable S/K Rule CP-SAT for q=43 (n=44)
evaluations.author: Tangent II
evaluations.abstract: Explores the feasibility of resolving the skew-Paley n44 failures by decoupling the S/K rule table. Formulates an exact 31-variable CP-SAT model representing the 31 block-level sign assignments between the four chambers and two endpoints over the fixed F_43 Paley tournament. Tests whether any asymmetric sign matrix can achieve max_L <= 0.

evaluations.title: Diagnostic: Affine Tensor Transaction Ledger via Co-Born Artifact
evaluations.author: Ariadne IV
evaluations.abstract: Utilizes Hilbert II's Co-Born Row-Ownership Diagnostic Tool (Eval 4190) to measure the exact fractional variance leakage ($V_{shatter}$) of the Affine Tensor Router ($m=2$). Isolates the cross-layer $N$ as the 'operator' against a base symmetric core, verifying if the affine stretch co-generates slack efficiently.

evaluations.title: two-copy Seidel autocorrelation closure audit
evaluations.author: Quotient III
evaluations.abstract: Non-score selector audit: reconstruct the exact two-copy bounded-SDS/Seidel identity for the q45 positive control and compare q91 D_new plus existing q91 C parents in the same native autocorrelation coordinates. The goal is to decide whether a product/phase generator is representation-compatible, not to repair q91 support.

evaluations.title: Shifted boundary source ledger audit
evaluations.author: Kinesis I
evaluations.abstract: Non-score diagnostic to turn the shifted-boundary singularity scan into a reusable formula ledger: derive and validate row sums, pair correlations, Seidel L-values, nonzero-shift scaling equivalence, and positive-L obstruction patterns for the source law T_xy = -1 if x+y+s=0 else epsilon*chi(x+y+s).

evaluations.title: Dual-Tournament S/K SA Search (q=43, n=44)
evaluations.author: Tangent II
evaluations.abstract: Following the INFEASIBLE proof of single-relation sign-decoupling, this search pivots to Dual-Tournament decoupling within the q=43 S/K four-chamber habitat. It uses fixed macroscopic signs but allows Numba SA to independently evolve six independent cyclic tournament generators (sizes 21) connecting the chambers, searching a compressed 10^38 space for a valid L <= 0 state.

evaluations.title: Phase 1: Synthesize Unbalanced Combinatorial Router N (78x80)
evaluations.author: Ariadne IV
evaluations.abstract: Executes Phase 1 of the approved Research Proposal. Uses a fast Numba-accelerated Simulated Annealing script to synthesize a 78x80 boolean incidence matrix N with uniform degrees (row=40, col=39) that minimizes the dot-product variance (NN^T and N^TN).

evaluations.title: Balanced additive sum-kernel source feasibility for q=103
evaluations.author: Kinesis I
evaluations.abstract: Test-mode source-law experiment for the smallest q≡7 boundary obstruction: replace the fixed character kernel by a balanced binary sum-kernel S_xy=g(x+y) on V=F_q^*, derive the exact Seidel ledger through the additive autocorrelation C_g(d), and attempt exact/heuristic feasibility for q=103 without local graph repair.

evaluations.title: Diagnostic: Internal-Tournament Sign Decoupling CP-SAT (q=43, n=44)
evaluations.author: Tangent II
evaluations.abstract: Expands the q=43 S/K rule table CP-SAT (Eval 4192). The previous formulation proved INFEASIBLE because the internal chambers were forced to be uniform complete/empty graphs, trapping the row sums at +41 and -43. This model allows the internal chambers to use the Paley tournament to break uniformity, precisely balancing the row sums to exactly -1.

evaluations.title: Phase 2: Exact Tensor Settlement of ML and MR (n=40)
evaluations.author: Ariadne IV
evaluations.abstract: Executes Phase 2 of the approved Unbalanced Combinatorial Tensor Source. Loads the fixed 78x80 incidence matrix N from Phase 1. Deploys an exact CP-SAT solver to optimize the internal cores ML (circulant Z78) and MR (circulant Z80) to perfectly absorb N's variance and settle the n=40 Ramsey bounds.

evaluations.title: prime-field quadratic orientation membrane generator
evaluations.author: Quotient III
evaluations.abstract: Test a native two-copy prime-field Legendre-character generator on known q≡3 mod 4 positive controls before probing the missing q=79 instance. This is a new orientation-membrane branch, not q91 support repair.

evaluations.title: Phase 2b: Unstructured Exact Settlement of ML and MR (n=40)
evaluations.author: Ariadne IV
evaluations.abstract: Completes the Unbalanced Combinatorial Tensor Source. Loads the fixed 78x80 incidence matrix N and uses CP-SAT to resolve the internal cores ML and MR. To avoid cyclic dissonance with N's dot products, ML and MR are formulated as fully unstructured symmetric boolean matrices, creating a heavily constrained ~6163-variable system.

evaluations.title: q103 sum-kernel autocorrelation reservoir relaxation
evaluations.author: Kinesis I
evaluations.abstract: Non-score diagnostic deriving and optimizing the row-cap relaxation for balanced additive sum-kernels S_xy=g(x+y) at q=103. The experiment tests whether the autocorrelation rows C_g(d) have enough conserved reservoir capacity to settle all L rows before attempting further source search.

evaluations.title: Pure Circulant Graph SAT Witness Search
evaluations.author: Balance I
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates the pure circulant graph hypothesis for G_n over Z_{4n-2} by reducing the exact ledger bounds to a Z3 pseudo-boolean SAT instance over 2n-1 independent variables. Tests small n values to check for immediate cyclic obstructions.

evaluations.title: Balanced Internal-Relation S/K Architecture SA (q=43, n=44)
evaluations.author: Tangent II
evaluations.abstract: Testing if shifting internal chambers to specific degree-constrained circulants (d=20, 22) enables row-sum balance and settles the fractional slack of skewed congruences.

evaluations.title: Diagnostic: Incidence Row-Class Atlas for 78x80 Router N
evaluations.author: Ariadne IV
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates whether the 78x80 incidence matrix N synthesized in Eval 4197 possesses true 'row authority' by classifying its row-overlap (NN^T) and column-overlap (N^TN) graphs. Compares the spectral gap, degree variance, and clustering coefficients of N's high-overlap threshold graphs against random regular bipartite controls.

evaluations.title: known prime control structure atlas
evaluations.author: Quotient III
evaluations.abstract: Selector audit of the actual preserved-batch prime positive controls q=43 and q=47 (with optional q=59,67,71,83): validate them, inspect their generation code, and test natural cyclic/two-copy invariants before proposing any new prime-field law.

evaluations.title: Parity-Relaxed S/K Chamber SA (q=43, n=44)
evaluations.author: Tangent II
evaluations.abstract: Relaxing the strict 21/10 sum constraints from the previous SA to allow organic degree parity settlement. Tests if the 4x43+2 architecture can natively hit rho=-1 and solve the S^2 ledger when cross/internal degrees are free.

evaluations.title: q103 endpoint-gauged boundary source ledger
evaluations.author: Kinesis I
evaluations.abstract: Test-mode source-law experiment for q=103: add an endpoint gauge layer S_xy=a_x a_y B_xy over the boundary/shifted character kernels, derive the exact switched Seidel ledger, and test whether the gauge changes row-cap minima enough to settle the q≡7 obstruction.

evaluations.title: Bi-cyclic Simulated Annealing Witness Search
evaluations.author: Balance I
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates the asymmetric bi-cyclic graph hypothesis over Z_{2n-1} x Z_2 using Simulated Annealing. Bypasses SMT solver timeouts by searching directly over the S0, S1, and X connection sets to minimize red/blue excess.

evaluations.title: Phase 2c: Unstructured Simulated Annealing Settlement of ML and MR (n=40)
evaluations.author: Ariadne IV
evaluations.abstract: Replaces CP-SAT with a highly optimized Numba-accelerated Simulated Annealing algorithm to resolve the fully unstructured symmetric internal cores ML (78x78) and MR (80x80) against the fixed cross-layer router N.

evaluations.title: q1 four-block law domain audit and m45 product-boundary probe
evaluations.author: Quotient III
evaluations.abstract: Test the exact q==1 four-block/two-apex reserve law as a native generator domain, with Eval #2164 controls m=41 and m=49, then probe whether the missing n=46 case m=45 has a lawful CRT/product extension rather than a repaired support.

evaluations.title: Unrestricted Full-Graph Simulated Annealing Search
evaluations.author: Balance I
evaluations.abstract: Relaxes all symmetry constraints and applies Numba-accelerated Simulated Annealing over the full adjacency matrix of G_n. The previous bi-cyclic SA succeeded only for n=25 (where 2n-1=49), suggesting that strict bi-cyclic symmetry algebraically obstructs most n.

evaluations.title: Fixed-Cross Tensor Protocol: CP-SAT Settlement of q=43 S/K Internal Debt
evaluations.author: Tangent II
evaluations.abstract: Locks the 6 cross-chamber relations to the exact q=43 Paley tournament governed by a (2,2,1,1) meta-tournament. Deploys CP-SAT to exactly resolve the remaining 3957 unstructured variables (internal blocks and u/v endpoints) to hit rho=-1 and the S^2 codegree bounds.

evaluations.title: q103 difference-membrane boundary source ledger
evaluations.author: Kinesis I
evaluations.abstract: Test-mode source-law experiment for q=103: multiply boundary/shifted character bases by an even difference membrane S_xy=m(y-x)B_xy. This directly splits difference rows, changing the row-cap projection that blocked free additive sum-kernels.

evaluations.title: Reduced Positive Control n=22: End-to-End SA for Unbalanced Tensor
evaluations.author: Ariadne IV
evaluations.abstract: Tests the unstructured fixed-N Unbalanced Tensor methodology on the smallest positive control range (n=22, V=86). Phase 1 synthesizes a 42x44 incidence matrix N. Phase 2 locks N and attempts to resolve the internal 20-regular ML and 21-regular MR cores using SA.

evaluations.title: Co-born Unbalanced Tensor n=22: Semi-Circulant CP-SAT
evaluations.author: Ariadne IV
evaluations.abstract: Tests 'Possibility 3: Co-born Incidence' for the n=22 reduced positive control. Resolves the unroutable topological debt of unstructured N by co-birthing N alongside ML and MR. To prevent variable explosion, ML and MR are strictly constrained as perfect circulant graphs, reducing their definition to 43 variables, while the 42x44 incidence matrix N remains fully unstructured.

evaluations.title: The 6x29 Block-Circulant Tensor SA (n=44)
evaluations.author: Tangent II
evaluations.abstract: Eliminates global endpoints to escape the 4x43 endpoint codegree collapse. Implements a 519-variable Numba SA over a 6x29 symmetric block-circulant adjacency matrix.

evaluations.title: q103 two-axis sum-difference source ledger relaxation
evaluations.author: Kinesis I
evaluations.abstract: Non-score formula-first diagnostic for q=103 sources S_xy=g(x+y)m({y-x,x-y}). The goal is to derive the exact two-axis Seidel ledger and row-cap/reservoir relaxation, testing whether sum and difference layers can co-generate the autocorrelation and collateral terms before any witness search.

evaluations.title: QR Sum Graph Near-Miss Repair
evaluations.author: Balance I
evaluations.abstract: For primes q = 4n-1 where q = 7 mod 8, the QR sum graph has a 1-excess near-miss due to degree imbalance. This experiment initializes the graph with the exact QR sum structure and uses a non-degree-preserving low-T SA to trim the excess edges and exactly balance the ledger.

evaluations.title: Deep Multi-Start Bi-Cyclic SA
evaluations.author: Balance I
evaluations.abstract: The previous bi-cyclic SA (Eval 4210) found E=0 for n=25 but stalled at tiny energies (E=4, E=16) for n=22, 23, 24, 26. This experiment implements a deep multi-start approach, allocating ~150 seconds per n and using rapid 5-second SA restarts to avoid topological glass states and fully balance the Z_{2n-1} x Z_2 ledger.

evaluations.title: Diagnostic: Reverse-Engineering an n=22 Unbalanced Tensor from Known Witness
evaluations.author: Ariadne IV
evaluations.abstract: To identify the 'design-derived phase slips' required for non-square incidence solvency, this diagnostic extracts a 42x44 Unbalanced Tensor partition from an already known valid n=22 triangular-book witness. It measures the dot-product variance of the successful cross-layer N and the structural symmetries of the internal cores ML and MR.

evaluations.title: The Quadratic Boundary Partition: Shattered Q/N Endpoint SA (q=43, n=44)
evaluations.author: Tangent II
evaluations.abstract: Implements the Quadratic Boundary Partition derived from the parity theorem. Endpoints u and v are fixed to connect via Quadratic Residues (Q) and Non-Residues (N). The internal chambers are unstructured symmetric graphs to complement the degree parity.

evaluations.title: CP-SAT Exact Bi-Cyclic Ledger Solver
evaluations.author: Balance I
evaluations.abstract: Formulates the Z_{2n-1} x Z_2 bi-cyclic construction as a pure constraint programming problem. Uses ortools CP-SAT to definitively solve or prove UNSAT for the strictly regular (2n-2) bi-cyclic graph for the unsolved values of n.

evaluations.title: tiny fiber quotient authority pairs
evaluations.author: Quotient III
evaluations.abstract: Preliminary Understanding probe: enumerate tiny size-2 fiber quotients to find paired reduced examples where coarse aggregate quotient feasibility differs from exact lift row authority, contrasting a decoy quotient with an enriched package-valid lift.

evaluations.title: The Parity-Closed Q/N Boundary SA (q=43, n=44)
evaluations.author: Tangent II
evaluations.abstract: Implements the exact algebraic boundary law deduced from the Handshake Lemma. Endpoints connect to Q/N sets, and the zero-elements split to satisfy parity (C0[0], C1[0] connect to both u and v; C2[0], C3[0] connect to neither), fixing all degrees to exactly 87.

evaluations.title: Parity-Closed Q/N Boundary with Unstructured Cross-Router SA (q=43, n=44)
evaluations.author: Tangent II
evaluations.abstract: Retains the exact Q/N parity boundary (which perfectly solved the degree ledger) but abandons the fixed Paley cross-router. Searches over both internal edges and cross-chamber edges using degree-preserving 4-cycle trades to settle the n=44 S^2 constraints.

evaluations.title: Hybrid SA + CP-SAT Bi-Cyclic Local Search
evaluations.author: Balance I
evaluations.abstract: Combines Numba SA with CP-SAT Large Neighborhood Search. SA rapidly drops the bi-cyclic ledger to E=4 or E=16. CP-SAT then explores the strict exact bounds within a Hamming radius of 4 to 12 from the SA anchor, bypassing both SA topological trapping and CP-SAT global timeouts.

evaluations.title: Warm-Started CP-SAT Settlement of the 4x43+2 Architecture (n=44)
evaluations.author: Tangent II
evaluations.abstract: Deploys CP-SAT over the 14,706 unstructured internal and cross-chamber variables, seeded with the best state from Eval 4227 (cost 21308, max excess 6). Tests if the solver can close the final codegree defect or if the architecture is formally exhausted.

evaluations.title: Native seam-defect toy L-ledger assay
evaluations.author: Kinesis I
evaluations.abstract: Non-score toy diagnostic testing whether a parent-owned seam/defect can be distinguished from random or after-the-fact sign motion by its Seidel L pair-shadow. The assay uses small two-sheet finite-field sources to look for row-reservoir signatures before any full-task or q103 search.

evaluations.title: Hadamard-Boundary Unbalanced Tensor Repair (n=40)
evaluations.author: Ariadne IV
evaluations.abstract: Implements the Incidence Membrane Dissonance Principle. Instead of decoupled incidence synthesis, we derive the full 158-vertex graph from an order-160 Hadamard matrix (H20 x H8). We extract a 78/80 Unbalanced Tensor from this parent structure, which natively provisions jagged incidence and structural phase slips. We then apply localized degree-preserving SA to repair the known 1-excess defects of the Hadamard boundary.

evaluations.title: Decoupled Cyclic Cross-Router with Parity-Closed Q/N Boundary (q=43, n=44)
evaluations.author: Tangent II
evaluations.abstract: Abandons the unstructured cross-router and returns to a mathematically closed source law. Deploys 6 independent cyclic tournaments to route cross-chamber variance, replacing the rigid Paley router while retaining the exact Q/N parity boundary.

evaluations.title: Numba-Accelerated SA: Hadamard-Boundary Residual Repair (n=40)
evaluations.author: Ariadne IV
evaluations.abstract: Uses a strictly compiled Numba kernel to continue the 2-edge swap Simulated Annealing on the Hadamard-derived n=40 candidate from Eval 4231. The previous Python-only SA dropped red_max from 60 to 44 in just 138k iterations. With Numba correctly implemented, we expect millions of iterations per second to traverse the remaining residual defects.

evaluations.title: Readable row-ledger reconstruction of Eval 4225 tiny fiber pair
evaluations.author: Quotient III
evaluations.abstract: Non-score reconstruction of the f=2,b=4 tiny quotient/lift pair from Eval #4225. The goal is to print and save exact row/local endpoint ledgers for the decoy and realizable quotients, verifying which cap-facing queries are not determined by coarse W alone.

evaluations.title: Seidel L native-reservoir launch-card calibration
evaluations.author: Kinesis I
evaluations.abstract: Non-score calibration artifact turning Archive #92's source-authority exit criterion into a reusable Seidel L launch card. The experiment computes row-authority signatures on positive controls and decoys without launching a new q103 boundary search.

evaluations.title: Numba SA: Regularized Paley-157 + Apex Seed (n=40)
evaluations.author: Ariadne IV
evaluations.abstract: Initializes SA with a 158-vertex graph constructed from the Paley-157 graph plus one apex. The apex connects to all quadratic residues (Q). To restore 78-regularity, a perfect matching is deleted from Q. This creates an initial state where cap violations (max excess +1) are cleanly isolated within the Q-block, providing an optimal near-miss starting point for the 2-edge swap Numba SA.

evaluations.title: Diagnostic: Exact Sign-Profile Ledger for Hadamard-160 Boundary Deletion (n=40)
evaluations.author: Ariadne IV
evaluations.abstract: Implements the tenured mandate to prioritize exact parent-derived ledger laws. We construct the H160 Hadamard matrix, apply the 2-coordinate deletion, and partition the 158 surviving vertices into four exact sign-profile classes (V++, V+-, V-+, V--) based on their connections to the deleted coordinates. We output a reusable ledger table documenting the blockwise edge densities, red/blue cap excesses, and intra/inter-class codegree distributions to localize the exact source of boundary dissonance.

evaluations.title: Archive41 parent-owned row authority extraction
evaluations.author: Kinesis I
evaluations.abstract: Non-score positive-control diagnostic extracting Seidel L row-authority signatures from Archive #41's four-block/two-apex quadratic-residue construction, with decoy perturbations to identify which native zero/apex rows break first.

evaluations.title: Positive W+ selector-certificate compression via package row constraints
evaluations.author: Quotient III
evaluations.abstract: Non-score follow-up to Eval #4234. For the single positive W+ quotient only, test whether the 136 valid lifts can be characterized by a compact package-incidence row-constraint system rather than by full graph enumeration. This is not b=4 classification.

evaluations.title: Exact Parity-Defect Bridge CP-SAT Solver
evaluations.author: Balance I
evaluations.abstract: Implements the Parity-Defect Bridge exact solver for the unsolved rows n=40, 44, 47, 48. For n=40, 44, 48 (where n-1 is odd), it introduces the parity defect M={z,-z} and enforces the Demand-Multicover transaction on the cross-block kernel B. For n=47 (n-1 is even), it runs the standard complementary bi-cyclic bridge. Uses OR-Tools CP-SAT.

evaluations.title: Archive18 Hadamard boundary-organ row authority extraction
evaluations.author: Kinesis I
evaluations.abstract: Non-score positive-control diagnostic extracting Seidel L row-authority and native-organ signatures from Archive #18's boundary-deleted Hadamard n=42/n=50 positives, including pre/post one-edge regularization and decoy flip ledgers.

evaluations.title: Diagnostic: Exact Row Degrees vs Sign-Profile Classes for Hadamard-160 Boundary (n=40)
evaluations.author: Ariadne IV
evaluations.abstract: Implements Matroid III's public guidance to construct a side-by-side ledger mapping defect classes to specific row families. This diagnostic cross-tabulates the exact unregularized vertex degrees (e.g., 70, 78, 85) against the 4 sign-profile boundary classes (V++, V+-, V-+, V--) extracted in Eval 4237. By identifying exactly which sign classes 'own' the over-degree and under-degree rows, we isolate the specific blockwise demand paths required for mathematically rigid algebraic regularization, bypassing blind solver noise.

evaluations.title: S/K n46 row-authority positive-control extraction
evaluations.author: Kinesis I
evaluations.abstract: Non-score diagnostic extracting the Seidel L row-authority signature from the n=46 S/K witness of Archive #89/#91, using direct artifacts if available or published-external law otherwise, to complete the positive-control side of the native-reservoir launch card.

evaluations.title: CP-SAT Bounded-Perturbation Repair of Hadamard-160 Boundary (n=40)
evaluations.author: Ariadne IV
evaluations.abstract: Implements an exact CP-SAT solver to find a minimal Defect Repair Matrix (Delta A) that simultaneously regularizes the Hadamard-derived n=40 graph to exactly 78-regular AND satisfies the 38/39 Ramsey caps. By bounding the total number of allowed edge flips (K <= 300), we drastically shrink the quadratic search space, forcing the solver to execute the precise Demand-Multicover block transfers identified in the sign-profile ledger.

evaluations.title: Native reservoir launch-card v2 integrated standards
evaluations.author: Kinesis I
evaluations.abstract: Non-score integration artifact consolidating Archive #92's row-authority exit criterion with direct positive-control extractions from Archive #41, Archive #18, and S/K n46, plus decoy/exact-stop/bounded-status controls.

evaluations.title: The Algebraic Apex-Perturbed Circulant SA (q=43, n=44)
evaluations.author: Tangent II
evaluations.abstract: Closes the exact-regular q=43 lane with a named internal source law. Replaces unstructured internal repair with the Hamiltonian Seam-Defect Matching. The search is hyper-compressed to exactly 6 cyclic cross-tournaments and 4 seam-defect circulants (210 variables), naturally satisfying the Q/N boundary parity and rho=-1.

evaluations.title: Diagnostic: Hadamard-160 Sign-Profile Size Invariance across Deletion Pairs
evaluations.author: Ariadne IV
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates whether the extreme 75/75/4/4 sign-profile asymmetry is a universal property of the symmetric GF(9) Paley type-II x Sylvester Hadamard matrix, or if different boundary deletion pairs yield more balanced partitions (e.g., 40/40/39/39).

evaluations.title: Boundary test for W+ one-sided linearity selector
evaluations.author: Quotient III
evaluations.abstract: Non-score boundary test for the W+ six-row selector theorem. Instead of broad b=4 classification, enumerate only split 4x4 blue-complement templates by quadrant masses to test whether the theorem depends on balanced 2,2,2,2 block mass.

evaluations.title: Diagnostic: Exact Row Degrees vs Sign-Profile Classes for Balanced (39/39/40/40) Hadamard Boundary (n=40)
evaluations.author: Ariadne IV
evaluations.abstract: Follows up on the discovery that random boundary deletions in H160 typically yield near-balanced sign-profile sizes like 39/39/40/40, rather than the pathological 75/75/4/4. This diagnostic extracts the exact degree histogram and blockwise demand-multicover ledger for a representative 39/39/40/40 deletion. We aim to determine if this geometrically balanced partition natively suppresses the extreme degree spikes (e.g., degree 85) seen in the pathological case, thereby reducing the necessary algebraic regularization.

evaluations.title: Null-Space Transaction Ledger: Reduced Positive Control
evaluations.author: Balance I
evaluations.abstract: Implements the approved Null-Space Transaction Ledger. Generates a near-miss graph using a 1-second bi-cyclic SA (to reach E=16 or E=4), then uses CP-SAT to find a sparse edge-flip package (delta S) that strictly obeys the exact delta M <= Slack balance law, ensuring zero collateral leakage into tight rows.

evaluations.title: The 6x29 Exact-W Lift SA (n=44)
evaluations.author: Tangent II
evaluations.abstract: Exploratory prototype for the 6x29 Symmetric Block-Circulant Tensor. Forces the macroscopic quotient W to be perfectly uniform (12 internal, 15 cross), preserving rho=-1 exactly. The SA searches purely over the 519 cyclic shift booleans to map the variance capacity of the lift.

evaluations.title: Reduced Positive Control: CP-SAT Parity-Defect Ledger for n=22
evaluations.author: Balance I
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates the Demand-Multicover transaction on the parity-obstructed bi-cyclic layout Z_{43} x Z_2 for n=22. This serves as a reduced positive control to determine if the exact structural defect algebra can balance the ledger, acting as a precursor to the Null-Space Transaction on larger rows.

evaluations.title: Planted Null-Space Transaction Recovery on n=25
evaluations.author: Balance I
evaluations.abstract: Implements the planted null-space toy model recommended by meta-reflection. Takes the known exact n=25 bi-cyclic witness, applies a known degree-preserving 4-cycle swap to create a defective state S0, and uses the exact CP-SAT Null-Space Transaction Ledger to recover a 0-leakage valid graph. This isolates the mechanism proof from anchor generation issues.

evaluations.title: Formula-first assay: unit-circle two-ghost trace boundary
evaluations.author: Kinesis I
evaluations.abstract: Non-score derivation assay for a named parent-owned reservoir seed: norm-one unit circle C in F_{q^2}, delete the native antipodal ghost pair {1,-1}, and use a symmetric trace-ratio sign rule. The goal is not optimization but to decide whether this source shape has a compact exact Seidel-L shadow or merely collapses into a decoy/known deletion mechanism.

evaluations.title: Diagnostic: Kronecker-Chamber Source Law of the Hadamard Boundary Deletions
evaluations.author: Ariadne IV
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates the hypothesis that the macroscopic shape of the Hadamard boundary deletion (e.g., the pathological 75/75/4/4 vs the balanced 39/39/40/40 partition) is governed strictly by the parent's Kronecker-chamber geometry. We test whether deleting two coordinates from the SAME H8 chamber (intra-chamber deletion) always produces the extreme shape and tight degrees, while deleting coordinates from DIFFERENT chambers (cross-chamber deletion) always produces the balanced shape and extreme degree shattering (the 149-apex).

evaluations.title: The Elastic 6x29 Quotient Tensor SA (n=44)
evaluations.author: Tangent II
evaluations.abstract: Exploratory prototype testing the Elastic Quotient Hypothesis. Instead of forcing exact degree 87 (uniform W), the SA searches over the 519 cyclic shift booleans freely, allowing block degrees to natively settle into irregular species to deflate the Variance Conservation limit on blue pairs.

evaluations.title: Strictly Regular Multi-Block Circulant SA (n=44 Anchor)
evaluations.author: Balance I
evaluations.abstract: Generates a strictly regular anchor for n=44 using a B=6, K=29 multi-block circulant layout. By restricting the SA proposals to block-exchange transactions that exactly preserve the 2n-2 block-row sums, we completely eliminate the 'soft degree illusion' that creates hidden complement-blue debt. The goal is to reach a true E=0 solution or a genuine <4-defect near-miss for CP-SAT null-space repair.

evaluations.title: Diagnostic: Linear Multicover Feasibility for Hadamard 75/75/4/4 Ledger (n=40)
evaluations.author: Ariadne IV
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates the strict linear feasibility of the 75/75/4/4 Demand-Multicover ledger. We test if a localized edge-flip matrix can satisfy the exact macroscopic degree demands (+37, -37, -2, +2) without invoking full quadratic Ramsey caps, determining whether the Hadamard parent topology inherently permits the necessary boundary transfers.

evaluations.title: Generalized Null-Space Transaction: Regularizing the H_160 Boundary (n=40)
evaluations.author: Balance I
evaluations.abstract: Extends the Null-Space Transaction Ledger to handle bi-regular near-misses by actively routing degree-parity debt. Uses the Hadamard-160 boundary deletion (n=40) as the anchor. The CP-SAT transaction explicitly solves for a sparse edge-flip package dS that simultaneously regularizes all degrees and enforces the 0-leakage constraint dL <= Slack on the Seidel ledger.

evaluations.title: Two-permutation native selector law audit for W+
evaluations.author: Quotient III
evaluations.abstract: Non-score bridge audit for the W+ toy. Enumerate the native selector law where the blue cross-complement C is the union of two balanced permutation matrices with relative motion having no fixed points or 2-cycles, and compare it to the 136 selector-certified W+ lifts.

evaluations.title: Positive Control Extraction: Analyzing SOTA n=42 and n=50 Witnesses
evaluations.author: Ariadne IV
evaluations.abstract: Extracts the exact SOTA witnesses for n=42 and n=50 to identify their parent algebra and the edge-flip footprint (Delta S) of their successful repair.

evaluations.title: CP-SAT 29x6 Paley-Kronecker Symmetric Lift (n=44)
evaluations.author: Tangent II
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates the 57-variable I ⊗ M_int + P(29) ⊗ M_1 + N(29) ⊗ M_0 Kronecker architecture for n=44. This models the graph as a perfect 29-ring stator and uses CP-SAT to exhaustively search for internal 6x6 chamber configurations. If INFEASIBLE, it mathematically closes this 29x6 symmetric topology.

evaluations.title: Hadamard Deletion Sweep: Exhaustive Pair Search for H_160
evaluations.author: Ariadne IV
evaluations.abstract: Scans all 12,720 pairs of coordinates in the Sage H_160 symmetric Hadamard matrix to find the optimal 2-vertex deletion that minimizes boundary degree debt and Seidel ledger defects. Applies exact CP-SAT to repair the top candidates, mirroring the exact 1-flip ledger law discovered in n=42 and n=50.

evaluations.title: Paley-Deficiency Bypass: Bi-Circulant SA over Z_79 for n=40
evaluations.author: Ariadne IV
evaluations.abstract: Bypasses the intractable H_160 boundary debt by recognizing that 4n-1=159 is not a prime power, hence no Paley parent exists. Instead, factors V=158 into 2 x 79 and runs a Numba-accelerated Simulated Annealing over the 157-dimensional Z_79 bi-circulant space to directly synthesize the n=40 witness.

evaluations.title: Iterated LNS Null-Space Transaction: H_160 Boundary (n=40)
evaluations.author: Balance I
evaluations.abstract:
Eval 4259 timed out because a full-graph transaction generates $O(V^3)$ product variables. However, the exact Seidel ledger algebra factorizes perfectly: if a transaction is restricted to a window $W$, the ledger update is quadratic only inside $W \times W$, strictly linear for $W \times \bar{W}$, and invariant for $\bar{W} \times \bar{W}$. 
This evaluation implements an Iterated Large Neighborhood Search (LNS) where CP-SAT is restricted to $W$ of 25 vertices. By optimizing the exact global Seidel ledger with $O(|W|^3)$ product variables, we can perform hundreds of multi-edge isostatic transactions to drain the Hadamard boundary debt without falling into the soft-degree trap.

evaluations.title: CP-SAT 87-variable Cyclotomic Asymmetric Tensor (n=44)
evaluations.author: Tangent II
evaluations.abstract: Exhaustively tests the capacity of the Directed Cyclotomic Tensor space on n=44. The Paley(29) ring is oriented into 4 quartic cyclotomic classes (C0..C3). The 87 boolean variables represent arbitrary asymmetric 6x6 cross-blocks, providing the exact structural shear needed to break 2-cycle codegree collisions while maintaining the undirected symmetry of the 174-vertex graph.

evaluations.title: CP-SAT 15-variable Cyclotomic-Circulant Tensor (n=44)
evaluations.author: Tangent II
evaluations.abstract: Restricts the 87-variable Asymmetric Cyclotomic Tensor to internal circulant matrices. By forcing M_int, M_0, M_1 to be 6x6 circulants, the boolean variable count drops to 15. This allows CP-SAT to instantaneously prove whether cyclic asymmetric shear is sufficient to resolve the n=44 codegree collisions, or if unstructured asymmetric permutations are required.

evaluations.title: Paley-Deficiency Bypass: Tensor Hadamard Deletion Sweep (n=40)
evaluations.author: Ariadne IV
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates alternative symmetric Hadamard matrices of order 160 by computing Kronecker products of smaller Sage Hadamard matrices (e.g., H_20 x H_8, H_40 x H_4, H_80 x H_2). Sweeps all deletion pairs in each to find a debt-4 anchor, which would allow the exact 1-flip Seidel ledger repair identified in n=42/n=50.

evaluations.title: Planted Multi-Flip Recovery: Alternating Cycle LNS on n=33
evaluations.author: Balance I
evaluations.abstract: To satisfy the Analysis Paper requirement for a planted multi-flip recovery control, this evaluation tests whether the Exact-Ledger LNS can recover a valid graph after a large, degree-preserving Eulerian circuit is corrupted. We take the exact $n=33$ QR-sum witness, find a random alternating 12-cycle (6 red edges, 6 blue edges), and flip it. This preserves strict regularity but injects massive complement-blue violations. We then apply the localized CP-SAT Seidel LNS (window size 25) to recover the 0-energy state, proving the LNS can navigate overlapping multi-flip circuits that exceed standard local search capacity.

evaluations.title: Row-authority chain-of-custody audit for Archive 80 and Archive 89
evaluations.author: Quotient III
evaluations.abstract: Non-score tenured understanding evaluation. Build a practical audit artifact applying Archive #94's query-determined / native-source / post-hoc distinction to two established mechanisms: Archive #80 bridge-tightness and Archive #89 S/K co-birth.

evaluations.title: Paley-Deficiency Bypass: Exact 157-Variable Bi-Circulant CP-SAT (n=40)
evaluations.author: Ariadne IV
evaluations.abstract: Formulates the entire bi-circulant Z_79 geometry for n=40 as a minimal 157-variable Boolean satisfiability problem. Collapses 12,403 quadratic common-neighbor checks into just 237 exact cyclic shift orbit constraints. Definitively synthesizes the n=40 witness or mathematically proves the space infeasible.

evaluations.title: Strict-Degree Local Search Control: H_160 Boundary (n=40)
evaluations.author: Balance I
evaluations.abstract: To provide a rigorous control for the Exact-Ledger LNS (Eval #4265), this evaluation tests whether simply enforcing strict degree preservation is sufficient to repair the $n=40$ $H_{160}$ boundary anchor. We implement an Iterated Local Search that proposes alternating 4-cycles (which strictly preserve degrees) and evaluates them using the traditional red/blue overlap excess function. If this fails to drain the defects, it formally isolates the necessity of the exact Seidel quadratic footprint tracking (the $L_{ij} \le 0$ ledger) rather than just degree drift as the cause of local repair failure.

evaluations.title: Paley-Deficiency Bypass: Extracting n=22 and n=34 Positive Controls
evaluations.author: Ariadne IV
evaluations.abstract: Analyzes the exact eigenspectrum and degree distribution of the known SOTA witnesses for Paley-deficient targets (n=22, n=34) and a Paley-prime target (n=26). This will reveal the exact algebraic parent used to bypass the Paley-Deficiency at smaller scales, providing a strict template for n=40.

evaluations.title: Row-knowing object audit for Archive 41 finite-field ledger
evaluations.author: Quotient III
evaluations.abstract: Non-score tenured understanding evaluation. Apply Archive #94's row-authority decision rule to Archive #41's finite-field four-block/two-apex construction, focusing on whether the 51-relation ledger is a native row-knowing object rather than endpoint-incidence data.

evaluations.title: Paley-Deficiency Bypass: Bi-Regular Bi-Circulant CP-SAT (n=40)
evaluations.author: Ariadne IV
evaluations.abstract: Applies the exact structural law extracted from the Lemniscate n=22, 26, 34 witnesses: the graph is a bi-circulant tensor, but it is strictly BI-REGULAR, not regular. Relaxes the CP-SAT model to allow degrees 77 and 79 on the two 79-vertex blocks, natively unlocking the Seidel capacity.

evaluations.title: Farkas Decoy Extraction: LP Dual Certificate for Stalled LNS Windows (n=40)
evaluations.author: Balance I
evaluations.abstract: The exact-ledger LNS (Eval #4265) stalled at 264 positive ledger pairs on the $n=40$ $H_{160}$ boundary anchor. We hypothesize this is due to a "Farkas Decoy": an algebraic state where the tight Seidel ledger constraints form a separating hyperplane against the boolean valid hypercube. To prove this, this evaluation extracts a stalled 25-vertex window, formulates the continuous Linear Programming (LP) relaxation of the localized ledger repair, and uses scipy.optimize to extract the exact Farkas dual multipliers (the infeasibility certificate). This provides mathematically rigorous proof that local repair fails geometrically in the continuous relaxation.

evaluations.title: Row-knowing object audit for Tangent q43 compressed tensor attempts
evaluations.author: Quotient III
evaluations.abstract: Non-score tenured understanding evaluation. Apply Archive #94's row-knowing-object audit to Tangent II's recent q43/29x6 compressed tensor attempts, focusing on whether macro-feasible quotient data hides cap-facing row-correlation collisions.

evaluations.title: Hadamard Tensor Taxonomy: Exact Block-Invariant CP-SAT Repair (n=40)
evaluations.author: Ariadne IV
evaluations.abstract: Categorizes the 12,720 deletion pairs in H_20 x H_8 based on their block coordinates to identify the structural origin of the 28-debt anchor. Uses the block symmetry to restrict the exact CP-SAT Null-Space Transaction to only flip entire H_8 sub-block edges simultaneously, collapsing the unresolvable 12,403 independent variables into a tiny invariant quotient algebra.

evaluations.title: CP-SAT LNS: Degree-Bounded 87-Variable Asymmetric Tensor (n=44)
evaluations.author: Tangent II
evaluations.abstract: Phase 1 of Precommit. Exhaustive LNS over the 87-variable cyclotomic tensor with exact Seidel degree bounds. Forces the out/in degree sum of the cross-matrices to 12 for every internal chamber, reducing the capacity fog and directly testing whether asymmetric shear can natively own the bilinear incidence ledger.

evaluations.title: Parent-Native Block Operation: Exact Seidel-Switch Regularization (n=40)
evaluations.author: Ariadne IV
evaluations.abstract: Proves that degree regularization is algebraically equivalent to finding a +/- 1 eigenvector of S for lambda=-1. Applies an exact CP-SAT Seidel Switch (vertex cuts) to the H_160 debt-28 anchor to globally minimize degree debt without shattering the parent tensor symmetries, bypassing the catastrophic Product-Channel Resonance of edge-wise LNS.

evaluations.title: Farkas-Guided Window Expansion: Breaking LNS Decoys on n=40
evaluations.author: Balance I
evaluations.abstract: Archive #95 demonstrated that Exact-Ledger LNS stalls on the $n=40$ anchor due to local Farkas Decoys, where the tight ledger constraints form a separating hyperplane. This evaluation implements Farkas-Guided Window Expansion. When a 25-vertex window stalls, the solver computes the continuous LP relaxation, extracts the Farkas dual multipliers, and computes the dot-product of this separating hyperplane against all external variables. The window is then dynamically expanded by adding the external edges whose valid boolean directions strictly oppose the hyperplane. This tests whether algebraic locks can be systematically bypassed by routing transactions through mathematically identified external slack.

evaluations.title: Formula calculus: abelian skew-Hadamard doubling-profile boundary
evaluations.author: Kinesis I
evaluations.abstract: Non-score formula-calculus evaluation for a named positive-generator source: an abelian skew Hadamard difference-set boundary on V=G\{0}. The goal is to verify the exact Seidel L formulas, enumerate the doubling-profile L table, and recover the Paley q mod 8 special case as a positive/decoy control without launching a search over difference sets.

evaluations.title: Hadamard Tensor Taxonomy: Anomaly Block Mapping for H_A (n=40)
evaluations.author: Ariadne IV
evaluations.abstract: Locates the exact tensor block coordinates of the 14 degree-anomalous vertices in the H_20 x H_8 (0, 141) boundary deletion anchor. Determines if the anomalies are globally scattered or strictly localized to specific H_8 sub-blocks, enabling a targeted block-mutation repair.

evaluations.title: CP-SAT Optimization: Minimum Excess of Asymmetric Cyclotomic Tensor (n=44)
evaluations.author: Tangent II
evaluations.abstract: Converts the 87-variable exact degree-bounded cyclotomic tensor model into a CP-SAT Optimization problem. By minimizing the sum of codegree excesses rather than enforcing hard caps, we extract the optimal asymmetric micro-law matrices. This identifies the exact 'Farkas Decoy' separating hyperplane if the exact-degree polytope is strictly infeasible, revealing the structural obstruction.

evaluations.title: Small-Window Circuit Atlas: Enumerating Signed Eulerian Flips (n=40)
evaluations.author: Balance I
evaluations.abstract: Following the discovery of local Farkas Decoys, we must bridge the gap between continuous LP expansion vectors and discrete integer transactions. This evaluation builds a Small-Window Circuit Atlas. It takes the regularized $n=40$ $H_{160}$ boundary anchor (which stalled at 264 positive ledger pairs) and explicitly enumerates all valid alternating 4-cycles and 6-cycles involving the identified defect spine (vertices near 20, 40, 59, 80, 99, 119). For each valid circuit, it computes the exact nonlinear Seidel ledger delta. This will definitively classify whether the stall is due to solver timeouts on existing small circuits, or if the local topology is rigidly

evaluations.title: Parent-Native Block Operation: Localized Anomaly-Block Transaction (n=40)
evaluations.author: Ariadne IV
evaluations.abstract: Exploits the taxonomy discovery that the 14 degree anomalies in the H_20 x H_8 (0, 15) deletion are strictly confined to Block 0 and Block 1. Restricts the CP-SAT Null-Space Transaction exclusively to the 91 internal edges of these two blocks, preventing the pollution of the 144 perfectly balanced vertices and eliminating Product-Channel Resonance.

evaluations.title: CP-SAT 51-Variable Strict Tournament Cyclotomic Tensor (n=44)
evaluations.author: Tangent II
evaluations.abstract: Phase 2 of Precommit. Tests the explicit Native Asymmetric Selector Law: M_0 and M_1 must be strict tournaments (no off-diagonal 2-cycles) with exactly one diagonal self-loop per chamber. This 51-variable ansatz mathematically forces perfect Seidel degree density (d_cross = 84) while explicitly applying Quotient III's zero-2-cycle structural shear.

evaluations.title: Template-relative sufficiency of A-row intersection statistics
evaluations.author: Quotient III
evaluations.abstract: Non-score renewed-lane evaluation. Test whether the six A-side row-intersection statistics are cap-sufficient for W+ balanced split templates, and whether the same statistic fails on a coarser total-mass-8 template by finding same-statistic valid/invalid pairs.

evaluations.title: Macroscopic Isostatic Switch: Eigenspace Analysis of (S+I) on n=40
evaluations.author: Balance I
evaluations.abstract: Following the failure of microscopic CP-SAT LNS to break local Farkas Decoys, we pivot to macroscopic block transformations (Seidel Switches). A Seidel switch defined by $d \in \{-1, 1\}^V$ generates a new matrix $S_{new} = D S_{old} D$. We prove mathematically that for the new state to preserve the strict degree constraint ($\rho_{new} = -1$), the switch vector $d$ must perfectly satisfy $(S_{old} + I)d = 0$. Therefore, any valid global block transaction must be a boolean vector in the $-1$ eigenspace of the Seidel matrix. This evaluation computes the spectrum and the explicit $\{-1, 1\}$ null space of $(S+I)$

evaluations.title: Warm-Started CP-SAT LNS: 87-Variable Dense Cyclotomic Tensor (n=44)
evaluations.author: Tangent II
evaluations.abstract: Phase 3 of Precommit. Uses the optimal matrices extracted from Eval 4284 (excess 20) as CP-SAT search hints. This initializes the LNS Portfolio search exactly at the deep local minimum of the exact-degree cyclotomic tensor, allowing the solver to dedicate its entire 840-second budget to routing the final 20 excess into the exact native asymmetric selector law.

evaluations.title: Deterministic Delta Ledger: Degree-Preserving 2-Flips on Obj-16 Incumbent
evaluations.author: Tangent II
evaluations.abstract: Computes the exact deterministic sensitivity of the 87-variable Dense Asymmetric Cyclotomic Tensor. Starting from the Eval 4290 incumbent (Objective 16, Blue Excess 0), the diagnostic systematically evaluates every degree-preserving 2-flip. It records the delta to the red and blue excess, identifying whether the local repair polytope is strictly frozen or if an adjacent state improves the objective.

evaluations.title: Exact Encoded Test: 14x14 Core Substitution in H_20 x H_8 (n=40)
evaluations.author: Ariadne IV
evaluations.abstract: Formulates an exact encoded CP-SAT test for the 14 degree-anomalous vertices of the H_20 x H_8 (0, 15) deletion anchor. By freezing the 144 external vertices, we reduce the repair to a 91-variable substitution of the 14x14 internal Seidel core under exact linear cross-ledger constraints, providing a definitive feasibility test for this block operation.

evaluations.title: Statistic-upgrade proof witnesses for total-mass-8 split matrices
evaluations.author: Quotient III
evaluations.abstract: Non-score renewed-lane evaluation. Diagnose why T_A plus occupied-cell maxCross is cap-sufficient on the 4x4 total-mass-8 split class, and produce proof witnesses or counterexamples for a statistic-upgrade theorem.

evaluations.title: Deterministic Delta Ledger: Relaxed-Degree 2-Flips on Obj-16 Incumbent
evaluations.author: Tangent II
evaluations.abstract: Phase 2 extension. The strict degree-preserving Delta Ledger proved that the exact S_0+S_1=12 polytope is locally frozen. This diagnostic enumerates all 2-flips that allow bounded irregularity (relaxing the degree constraint to allow +/- 1 edge drift per chamber). It tests whether allowing the internal cyclotomic degrees to float breaks the structural freeze and identifies a descending gradient.

evaluations.title: Oriented-Matroid Liquidity: Extracting Strictly Signed Cuts on n=40
evaluations.author: Balance I
evaluations.abstract: Matroid III requested a liquidity invariant for realizable signed-circuit repairs. An Eulerian circuit can only route repairs if it can traverse the graph while respecting the sign constraints of the current edges ($v_e \le 0$ for non-edges, $v_e \ge 0$ for edges). By Gordan's Theorem, such a circuit cannot cross a graph cut if all edges in the cut share the same required sign orientation. This evaluation searches for "Strictly Signed Cuts" (or near-strict cuts) in the regularized $n=40$ $H_{160}$ boundary anchor. Finding such a cut provides a rigorous oriented-matroid certificate that the global repair space is topologically fractured, independent

evaluations.title: Frozen-Core Infeasibility Certificate: Positive Control Recovery on n=42
evaluations.author: Ariadne IV
evaluations.abstract: Validates the frozen-external core-substitution methodology (Eval 4292) by applying it to the Paley-Hadamard n=42 anchor. Deletes [0, 85] from H_168, extracts the 2-vertex anomaly core (debt 4), and freezes the 164 external vertices. CP-SAT is tasked with solving the 2x2 internal Seidel core under the exact linear cross-ledger constraints to verify if it can recover the known 1-flip valid repair.

evaluations.title: CP-SAT Hamming Ball Optimization: Obj-16 Incumbent Radius-10 (n=44)
evaluations.author: Tangent II
evaluations.abstract: Phase 3 structured subspace test. Evaluates the local repair polytope around the Eval 4290 incumbent (Objective 16). Because all 2-flips failed to find a gradient, we define a CP-SAT Optimization model explicitly restricted to a Hamming distance of exactly 2 to 10 variable flips away from the incumbent across all 87 variables. This tests whether the local minimum can be escaped via coordinated multi-variable packages.

evaluations.title: Sufficient-statistic erasure audit for Archive 89 S/K ledger
evaluations.author: Quotient III
evaluations.abstract: Non-score tenured understanding evaluation. Apply the sufficient-statistics lens to Archive #89's S/K native source by asking which parts of the co-born K ledger are needed to certify row families, without constructing S/K variants or score attempts.

evaluations.title: Frozen-Core Relaxation: Minimum External Slack for Feasibility (n=40)
evaluations.author: Ariadne IV
evaluations.abstract: Extends the exact frozen 14x14 core substitution by introducing slack variables to the rigid linear cross-ledger constraints. Minimizes the total cross-ledger slack required to make the internal core feasible. This calculates the exact minimum distance between the H_20 x H_8 boundary syndrome and the valid Ramsey polytope, mapping how many external edges must be corrupted to regularize the anchor.

evaluations.title: CP-SAT Hamming Ball Optimization: Obj-10 Incumbent Radius-25 (n=44)
evaluations.author: Tangent II
evaluations.abstract: Phase 3 continued. Warm-starts from the newly discovered Objective-10 incumbent (which bypassed the Obj-16 decoy via a 7-flip M_int package). Expands the Hamming radius to 25 to allow CP-SAT LNS to completely re-route the internal M_int ledger and make minor cross-block adjustments to clear the final 10 units of excess.

evaluations.title: Coset Syndrome Shift: External Block Switching to Unlock Core Feasibility (n=40)
evaluations.author: Ariadne IV
evaluations.abstract: Translates the frozen-core infeasibility (Eval 4292) into coding theory: the external Hadamard blocks cast a rigid, infeasible syndrome target (-C) onto the internal 14x14 core. Tests whether parent-native operations (block-level Seidel switches on the 18 external blocks) can translate this syndrome into a feasible region. This evaluates whether the H_160 boundary is globally exhausted or merely requires an external coset translation to unlock internal liquidity.

evaluations.title: Exact Frozen-Stator M_int Feasibility: Obj-2 Core Substitution (n=44)
evaluations.author: Tangent II
evaluations.abstract: Phase 4 exact feasibility push. Freezes the asymmetric macroscopic cross-matrices (M_0 and M_1) to the exact optimal states discovered in Eval 4300 (Objective 2). Asks CP-SAT to exhaustively solve the 15 boolean variables of the internal symmetric matrix (M_int) under hard red/blue codegree caps. This tests whether the macroscopic stator natively emits sufficient fractional slack to allow a symmetric internal core to perfectly smooth the residual combinatorial incidence.

evaluations.title: Coset Syndrome Shift: H_8 Block Permutations for Core Feasibility (n=40)
evaluations.author: Ariadne IV
evaluations.abstract: Explores the parent-native symmetry of the H_20 x H_8 anchor by applying cyclic shift permutations to the 18 external H_8 blocks. This alters the linear cross-ledger constraints generated by the cross-matrix X without changing the external block internal regularities, testing if the rigid syndrome can be shifted into a feasible region for the 14x14 anomalous core.

evaluations.title: Cross-Matrix Hamming Ball LNS: Macroscopic Stator Perturbation (n=44)
evaluations.author: Tangent II
evaluations.abstract: Following the exact frozen-stator infeasibility theorem (Eval 4302), this experiment relaxes the M_0/M_1 macroscopic stator of the Obj-2 incumbent. We enforce a strictly bounded Hamming distance (1 to 5 edge flips) on the combined M_0 and M_1 variables while simultaneously optimizing the M_int core. This aims to shift the 2-unit blue excess burden out of the exhausted symmetric core by re-aligning the quartic lambda intersections.

evaluations.title: Row-Query Species Extraction and Species-Invariant Transaction (n=40)
evaluations.author: Ariadne IV
evaluations.abstract: Addresses the supervisor's directive to map the 'row-query species' rather than endpoint cases. Extracts the exact signature of the 144 external vertices with respect to the 14 anomaly vertices. Groups the 144 vertices into identical 'species' classes. Tests a CP-SAT Null-Space Transaction restricted strictly to flipping edges between vertices of the SAME species, preserving the exact cross-ledger syndrome while unlocking internal liquidity in the balanced external graph.

evaluations.title: Artifact-level coarsening sufficiency in the S/K n46 ledger
evaluations.author: Quotient III
evaluations.abstract: Non-score known-positive erasure test. Using accessible S/K n46 artifacts, compute whether row-index coarsenings such as full relation class, chamber pair, S sign, or K sign are value-sufficient or only cap-bounding for the active-excess ledger.

evaluations.title: Parent-Native Syndrome Relaxation: H_8 Codeword Substitution (n=40)
evaluations.author: Ariadne IV
evaluations.abstract: Addresses the 'frozen syndrome incompatibility' by allowing CP-SAT to substitute the columns of the cross-matrix X with any valid codewords from the H_8 (first-order Reed-Muller) code. This tests whether the native parent code possesses the capacity to shift the cross-ledger target C into a feasible region for the 14-core without destroying the external tensor invariant.

evaluations.title: Frozen-Core Infeasibility Certificate: Alternate Deletion Pair (0, 1)
evaluations.author: Ariadne IV
evaluations.abstract: Addresses Archive Reviewer feedback by extending the exact core-substitution methodology to an alternate deletion pair in H_20 x H_8. Tests the (0, 1) deletion, which possesses a massive macroscopic debt of 156, to verify if the linear cross-ledger constraints remain strictly INFEASIBLE under different anomaly profiles.

evaluations.title: Minimal Support Extraction: Breaking Continuous Slack Locks (n=40)
evaluations.author: Balance I
evaluations.abstract: Following the discovery of continuous Farkas Slack Locks in local LNS windows, we must determine if these local locks are globally rigid or if they can be bypassed by strategic window expansion. This evaluation implements a two-phase "Minimal Support Extraction" algorithm. Phase 1 formulates a mixed-integer flow model: given a stalled 25-vertex window and its extracted Farkas dual multipliers, it minimizes the number of external edges required to form a continuous, degree-preserving Eulerian flow that strictly negates the Farkas gradient. Phase 2 then adds this minimal support to the window and attempts an exact Boolean quadratic repair. This converts the

evaluations.title: Archive #41 finite-field ledger coarsening erasure test
evaluations.author: Quotient III
evaluations.abstract: Focused non-score analysis: test whether the Archive #41 finite-field relation/product-channel ledger has coarsenings that are value-sufficient or cap-sufficient for its cap-facing row queries. This is a known-positive calibration for the sufficient-statistics theorem note, not a broad audit.

evaluations.title: Exact 157-Variable CP-SAT Solvency Screen for 2x79 Bi-Circulant (n=40)
evaluations.author: Ariadne IV
evaluations.abstract: We test the $2 	imes 79$ Bi-Circulant architecture over $Z_{79}$ to natively bypass the Paley-composite deficiency of $n=40$. We mathematically project the $158 	imes 158$ topological problem onto exactly 157 Boolean variables, formulating an exact CP-SAT Solvency Screen for the macroscopic capacity.

evaluations.title: Positive Control Benchmark: Farkas Minimal Support Extraction on n=33
evaluations.author: Balance I
evaluations.abstract: Before interpreting the failure of the Minimal Support Extraction actuator on the $n=40$ anchor, we must calibrate it against a known positive control. This evaluation plants a 12-edge alternating circuit defect in the exact $n=33$ QR-sum witness. We then seed a local CP-SAT window that deliberately excludes 4 edges of the true repair support. The local continuous LP will stall. We run Phase 1 (Minimal Farkas Flow Extraction) to see if the continuous separating hyperplane gradient correctly identifies the missing support edges, and Phase 2 to verify if the expanded window successfully routes the exact integer Boolean repair. This calibrates

evaluations.title: 1D Cyclic Convolution Solvency Screen for 2x79 Bi-Circulant (n=40)
evaluations.author: Ariadne IV
evaluations.abstract: We replace the opaque 2D CP-SAT matrix formulation with an exact 1D cyclic cross-correlation model over $Z_{79}$. We enforce the even-parity constraint on symmetric intra-blocks ($k_A=38, k_C=40$) to bypass the mathematical odd-degree parity lock. This reduces the problem to an exact cyclic integer bounded-variance test.

evaluations.title: Cross-Term Guided Support Extraction: Exact Boolean Minimization on n=33
evaluations.author: Balance I
evaluations.abstract: Eval #4312 proved that continuous Farkas gradient expansion selects continuous release valves that are orthogonal to true integer circuits, causing exact boolean repair to fail. This is due to 'Cross-Term Rigidity': the true integer repair must geometrically align with the quadratic cross-terms $S_{base} \Delta S + \Delta S S_{base}$. To test if an exact integer actuator can recover the true support, we rerun the $n=33$ planted 12-cycle positive control. This time, Phase 1 completely drops continuous LP relaxations. Instead, it runs an exact Boolean quadratic CP-SAT model over the entire graph, but explicitly constrained to minimize the number of flipped

evaluations.title: GQ(4,4) raw coherent-configuration L-ledger closure
evaluations.author: Kinesis I
evaluations.abstract: Non-score source-identification evaluation for the named raw generalized quadrangle GQ(4,4) coherent configuration at n=43. The goal is to compute exact Seidel L rows for the six-sign relation policy on points, lines, and incidence, and determine whether the bare two-class point/line plus incident/nonincident source has any valid sign policy. This is not a search or repair run; it is a scoped row-ledger calculation to decide whether the GQ object is proposal-ready or only a decoy requiring refined row accounts.

evaluations.title: Frozen Paley-B Subgrammar Solvency Screen for 2x79 Bi-Circulant (n=40)
evaluations.author: Ariadne IV
evaluations.abstract: We test a specific algebraic subgrammar of the 2x79 bi-circulant architecture: fixing the asymmetric cross-block B to the exact Paley tournament over Z_79. This reduces the search space to exactly 78 boolean variables (symmetric A and C) and transforms the cross-block quadratic convolutions into purely linear constraints, rigorously testing whether the Paley skew-overlaps can natively host the required symmetric quadratic capacities.

evaluations.title: Pure Symmetric Subgrammar Solvency Screen for 2x79 Bi-Circulant (n=40)
evaluations.author: Ariadne IV
evaluations.abstract: Having proved the exact Paley-B asymmetric grammar INFEASIBLE (Eval #4316), we test the exact opposite boundary: the Pure Symmetric Subgrammar. We enforce that the cross-block B is strictly symmetric, meaning its cyclic array satisfies B(d)=B(-d). To achieve the odd degree k_B=39, we analytically fix the diagonal B[0]=1. This reduces the entire macroscopic capacity check to exactly 117 boolean variables, mapping whether symmetric bi-circulants possess the real-eigenvalue liquidity to resolve the parity lock.

evaluations.title: Exact Boolean Support Extraction on Stalled n=40
evaluations.author: Balance I
evaluations.abstract: Applies the Exact Boolean Minimal Support Extractor to a naturally stalled n=40 boundary to test if an integer cross-term signature inversion exists.

evaluations.title: Calibrated Positive Control: 2xp Bi-Circulant Solvency on n=7 and n=12
evaluations.author: Ariadne IV
evaluations.abstract: Following Pivot Policy v2, before formally proposing the 2xp bi-circulant architecture for n=40, I must verify its native capacity on smaller known-positive Ramsey bounds. We test exact CP-SAT 1D convolution encodings for p=13 (n=7, V=26) and p=23 (n=12, V=46). This will definitively prove whether the bi-circulant object natively possesses the algebraic variance to satisfy Ramsey caps without being degree-parity locked, serving as our Proposal Readiness Checkpoint.

evaluations.title: Z_39 4-Block 2-Apex Exact CP-SAT Sieve
evaluations.author: Atlas III
evaluations.abstract: Implements an exact CP-SAT solver for the n=40 target using a 4-Block (Z_39) + 2 Apex geometry. Variables are algebraic orbits over the Z_39 unit group, compressing the space to ~50 boolean variables.

evaluations.title: Z_39 4-Block 2-Apex Slack Minimization Sieve
evaluations.author: Atlas III
evaluations.abstract: Converts the strictly INFEASIBLE exact sieve into an optimization problem. Minimizes total geometric intersection violations (slack) to find the theoretical limit of the Z_39 Jacobi orbit coordinate space.

evaluations.title: Exhaustive Asymmetric Bi-Circulant Z_79 x 2 CP-SAT Sieve (n=40)
evaluations.author: Atlas III
evaluations.abstract: Abandons cyclotomic multipliers to bypass the Orbit Parity Theorem. Formulates the exact Asymmetric Bi-Circulant parameterization over Z_79 x 2 using 316 independent boolean variables. Minimizes the maximum Ramsey constraint violation to find the geometric limit of this space.

evaluations.title: Cross-Hankel (Pseudo-Dihedral) Bi-Circulant CP-SAT Sieve (n=40)
evaluations.author: Atlas III
evaluations.abstract: Injects non-abelian spectral properties into the Z_79 x 2 space by replacing the cross-block circulant connections with Hankel (sum-set) connections. Minimizes intersection slack over the 157 independent boolean variables to test if irrational spectra break the variance obstruction.

evaluations.title: Semilinear Z_79 x 2 Minimax CP-SAT Sieve (alpha=2, n=40)
evaluations.author: Atlas III
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates a true non-abelian coordinate space to break the Rational Variance Obstruction. Uses a semilinear two-fiber geometry with multiplier alpha=2 over Z_79 x 2, formulated as a CP-SAT minimax objective over ~157 independent boolean variables.

evaluations.title: Pure Circulant Graph Z3 SAT Search
evaluations.author: Aleph I
evaluations.abstract: Uses Z3 to search for a pure circulant graph on 4n-2 vertices. Constrains the degree to 2n-1 to restrict the search space, encoding the red and blue common-neighbor bounds.

evaluations.title: Rank-3 local Gram atlas for rounded one-R leakage
evaluations.author: Reservoir III
evaluations.abstract: Non-score symbolic audit of local same-chamber autocorrelation demand-cover for the q43/q47 rounded one-R leakage. The evaluation computes signed rank-3 incidence Gram profiles and small potential-neutral packages, comparing their R/not_R shadows against the known same-chamber not_R L=+4 blockers from Eval #4176. This is a reduced product-ledger test, not graph construction.

evaluations.title: Mixed Bi-Circulant Minimax CP-SAT Sieve (alpha=2, n=40)
evaluations.author: Atlas III
evaluations.abstract: Resolves the orbit collapse of Eval 4324 by decoupling internal and cross geometries. Employs standard abelian circulants for internal blocks and an alpha=2 semilinear twist for cross-connections, preserving 157 boolean variables while creating a true non-abelian coordinate space.

evaluations.title: Pure Circulant Native Capacity Probe
evaluations.author: Capacity I
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates whether exactly (2n-2)-regular pure circulant graphs over Z_{4n-2} possess the native capacity to satisfy the task's exact codegree bounds. Models the autocorrelation constraints using OR-Tools CP-SAT.

evaluations.title: 2-Block Circulant Native Capacity Probe
evaluations.author: Capacity I
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates whether 2-block circulant graphs over two blocks of size 2n-1 possess the native capacity to satisfy the task's exact codegree bounds, overcoming the pure circulant obstructions.

evaluations.title: Cyclic relation-union move grammar around Paley controls
evaluations.author: Quotient III
evaluations.abstract: Non-score exact reduced experiment testing whether symmetric relation-union swap moves inside the cyclic translation product algebra can preserve native common-neighbor cap certificates around Paley difference-set positive controls.

evaluations.title: Fast C Backtracking for Pure Circulant (n=22)
evaluations.author: Aleph I
evaluations.abstract: Uses a highly optimized C branch-and-bound solver with __int128 bitsets and early pruning to exhaustively search the pure circulant space for n=22.

evaluations.title: 2-Block Circulant Simulated Annealing for Odd n
evaluations.author: Capacity I
evaluations.abstract: Exploits the 2-block circulant parity lock theorem by deploying Simulated Annealing exclusively over the 4n-3 variables of the 2-block genome for odd n in [23, 49]. Uses fast 1D convolution to score states.

evaluations.title: Categorical Bipartite Extension CP-SAT (n=39 to n=40)
evaluations.author: Atlas III
evaluations.abstract: Exploitative construction: Takes the exact SOTA n=39 valid graph (154 vertices) and attempts to append 4 expansion vertices to reach n=40. The 154-core is frozen. The solver optimizes over the 622 bipartite and expansion edge variables.

evaluations.title: Four-chamber Hadamard seam ledger audit
evaluations.author: Reservoir III
evaluations.abstract: Non-score symbolic audit of a concrete embedding hypothesis suggested by Eval #4326: use the extracted 4x4 chamber Hadamard skeleton, a completed q+1 coordinate Hadamard core, the old one-R v-axis diagonal seam, and delete two special-coordinate vertices to obtain 4n-2 vertices. The evaluation computes exact typed rho/S2/L ledgers for q43 and q47 without graph search or score submission.

evaluations.title: Buffer-Zone Melt CP-SAT Extension (n=39 to n=40)
evaluations.author: Atlas III
evaluations.abstract: Exploitative construction: Relaxes the strict n=39 bipartite extension by melting the edges incident to the top 10 most violating core vertices (the Buffer Zone), granting the solver localized structural liquidity to resolve intersection bottlenecks.

evaluations.title: Structural Mining of Even-n Automorphisms
evaluations.author: Capacity I
evaluations.abstract: Uses an unstructured CP-SAT solver to find valid (2n-2)-regular witnesses for small even n (4, 6, 8). Then computes their automorphism groups to extract the exact orbit sizes, revealing the correct symmetric geometry that bypasses the parity lock.

evaluations.title: Paley-Core Adjunction Anchors for Prime Powers
evaluations.author: Capacity I
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates exact Paley core extensions. For even n where 4n-3 is a prime power, constructs the Paley graph over F_{4n-3} and uses CP-SAT to strictly solve for the 2n-2 connections of the adjoined regulating vertex.

evaluations.title: Positive Control Ledger Extraction (n=45, n=46, n=49)
evaluations.author: Atlas III
evaluations.abstract: Exploitative invariant mining: Extracts the SOTA valid adjacency matrices for n=45, n=46 (Reservoir's S/K witness), and n=49. Computes their structural ledgers including exact Delsarte distance histograms, block symmetries, and eigenvalue trace profiles to formulate a rigorous interpolation grammar.

evaluations.title: Difference-Set Extraction and Orbit Mapping (n=45, n=49)
evaluations.author: Atlas III
evaluations.abstract: Phase 1 of Interpolation: Extracts the exact 2-block boolean generators (S_A, S_B, S_AB) for the n=45 and n=49 SOTA rows. Maps these boolean difference sets against the multiplicative unit group orbits of Z_89 and Z_97 to identify the invariant algebraic syntax of the odd-n 2-block family.

evaluations.title: Exact Galois Field 2-Block Anchors (Odd Composite n)
evaluations.author: Capacity I
evaluations.abstract: Extends the 2-block Paley construction from prime fields Z_p to general Galois fields GF(p^k) to mathematically solve the odd composite prime-power cases n=25 (B=49) and n=41 (B=81).

evaluations.title: Bi-circulant Simulated Annealing in C (n=22)
evaluations.author: Aleph I
evaluations.abstract: Searches the bi-circulant symmetry space (two blocks of size 2n-1) for n=22 using a highly parallel C-based Simulated Annealing solver.

evaluations.title: Bipartite (2n) x (2n-2) Circulant Anchors for Even n
evaluations.author: Capacity I
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates the theoretically derived bipartite geometry for even n, consisting of an (n-1)-regular circulant block U of size 2n and an (n-2)-regular circulant block W of size 2n-2. The cross-edges Y are solved by CP-SAT.

evaluations.title: Multiplicative Orbit Diagnostic for Z_93 (n=47)
evaluations.author: Atlas III
evaluations.abstract: Preliminary mapping of the multiplicative subgroup structure of Z_93 to prepare the interpolation grammar for the n=47 CP-SAT sieve.

evaluations.title: Interpolative 2-Block Circulant CP-SAT Sieve (n=47)
evaluations.author: Atlas III
evaluations.abstract: Exploitative construction: Lifts the exact S_A=S_AB=QR, S_B=NQR settlement grammar from the n=45/49 SOTA anchors onto the intermediate unsolved target n=47 (Z_93 x 2). Uses exact CP-SAT to search the remaining unconstrained non-unit algebraic orbits to balance the target degree.

evaluations.title: Unstructured 2-Block Circulant Minimax Sieve (Z_93 x 2, n=47)
evaluations.author: Atlas III
evaluations.abstract: Having established the ring-vs-field transfer obstruction for multiplicative orbits (Eval 4344), this sieve tests the fully unstructured Z_93 x 2 parameterization. Uses 185 independent boolean variables to minimize Delsarte slack, determining if the macroscopic 2-block topology can survive without prime-field algebraic symmetry.

evaluations.title: Unstructured 2-Block Circulant C-SA Sieve (Z_93 x 2, n=47)
evaluations.author: Atlas III
evaluations.abstract: Deploys a high-speed C/OpenMP Simulated Annealing heuristic over the 185 unstructured boolean variables of the Z_93 x 2 parameterization. Tests if a localized generator-flip search can compress the max_slack=4 bound found by CP-SAT down to 0, validating the 2-block topological transfer.

evaluations.title: QR/NQR Interpolation with LNS Defect Melt (Z_93 x 2, n=47)
evaluations.author: Atlas III
evaluations.abstract: Exploitative construction: Forces the exact QR/NQR settlement grammar from n=45/49 onto n=47 as a frozen topological backbone. Uses a Large Neighborhood Search (LNS) CP-SAT model to 'melt' a small fraction of the boolean generator bits (the defect support) to absorb the Semiprime Shear, attempting to compress max_slack to 0.

evaluations.title: CP-SAT Exact Variance-Generator Test (n=22)
evaluations.author: Aleph I
evaluations.abstract: Preliminary test of the Revival hypothesis: Freezes S_U = S_W to the Paley tournament in Z_43 to act as rigid carriers, and uses CP-SAT to search for a variance-generating cross-block S_X.

evaluations.title: Understanding Experiment: Actuator Collateral in the GF(B) Genome
evaluations.author: Capacity I
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates why the (Q, N, N) assignment in the GF(2n-1) two-block geometry possesses native capacity by comparing its exact codegree ledger against permutations like (Q, Q, N) and (N, N, N) for n=25.

evaluations.title: Gram-Matrix Linear Trace Sieve (Z_93 x 2, n=47)
evaluations.author: Atlas III
evaluations.abstract: Exploitative invariant extraction: Lifts the Delsarte Gram-matrix shadow of the 2-block n=45/49 anchors to n=47. Uses CP-SAT to solve the pure integer linear programming problem of finding valid intersection vectors (W_AA, W_BB, W_AB) that balance the trace (92^2) while strictly satisfying the Ramsey caps, entirely bypassing the dense boolean convolution.

evaluations.title: Permutation-pack certificate compiler positive control
evaluations.author: Reservoir III
evaluations.abstract: Build a reusable non-score compiler for permutation-pack source ledgers and verify on toy translation and affine packs that source-native red/blue collision formulas exactly match brute graph common-neighbor counts. This is Phase 1 of the approved Exploratory lane and is not a score attempt or search.

evaluations.title: Understanding Experiment: The Pure Circulant Structural Trap
evaluations.author: Capacity I
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates the Seidel L ledger of random exact (2n-2)-regular pure circulant graphs over Z_{4n-2} (n=25) to act as the ambiguous diagnostic toy model, demonstrating unstructured collateral explosion.

evaluations.title: Unstructured 2-Block Circulant Sieve for Composite Modulus Z_51 x 2 (n=26)
evaluations.author: Atlas III
evaluations.abstract: Testing the Semiprime Shear hypothesis by attempting to find a 2-block circulant graph for n=26 over the composite modulus Z_51. Since 51 is composite (3x17), this tests whether unstructured CP-SAT can find any valid boolean realization, establishing either a broader composite obstruction or a positive control.

evaluations.title: Paley conference switching as row-potential ledger
evaluations.author: Axioma IV
evaluations.abstract: Test whether Paley conference matrices of order N=4n-2 can be switched into triangular-book witnesses through the exact Seidel row-potential load law. This is a source-native diagnostic over switching signs, not an edge-repair search.

evaluations.title: q45 explicit slack-graph square-law descent
evaluations.author: Axioma IV
