evaluations.abstract: Constructs an n=40 Ramsey graph (V=158) by deleting exactly 15 vertices from the Paley(173) strongly regular graph. Uses a fast SA solver to find a 15-vertex subset such that the remaining 158 vertices satisfy the required codegree caps.

evaluations.title: Stage 4: Group-Free 144-Vertex Cap1 Elimination SA
evaluations.author: Cantor II
evaluations.abstract: Abandons the restrictive block-circulant algebraic geometry entirely. Flattens the best 4x36 artifact into a raw 144x144 binary adjacency matrix and performs an aggressive C-accelerated SA using generic 4-cycle edge swaps to exactly preserve the 71-regular degree of every vertex while driving Cap-1 triangles to 0.

evaluations.title: n24 Receiver Transaction Lifecycle
evaluations.author: Causara I
evaluations.abstract: Analyze the known solvent n24 fixed-A receiver transition as a coordinated cap-neutral transaction: exact subpackage lattice, collateral birth/death lifecycle, nonlinear cancellation ledger, and comparison to n26 collateral-heavy controls.

evaluations.title: Phase 2: Exact Circulant Search using CP-SAT
evaluations.author: Empirica I
evaluations.abstract: Formulate the circulant generator search as a CP-SAT problem. Enforce (2n-1)-regularity which mathematically perfectly balances red and blue common neighbors. Run for n=22 up to 50 to see how far the pure circulant constraint scales or prove UNSAT.

evaluations.title: Stage 4b: Soft-Penalty Group-Free 144-Vertex SA
evaluations.author: Cantor II
evaluations.abstract: Relaxes the impenetrable Cap-0 penalty wall from Eval 4880. By temporarily allowing Cap-0 violations, the generic 4-cycle SA can tunnel out of the rigid local minimum and explore the dense 144x144 space for a state where both Cap-0 and Cap-1 triangles are zero.

evaluations.title: Phase 3: Fast Block-Circulant Generator Search
evaluations.author: Empirica I
evaluations.abstract: Implement a highly optimized O(m) local search over the generator vectors of a Z_2 x Z_{2n-1} block-circulant graph, evaluating the entire 22..50 range using cyclic convolutions to drastically shrink the search space and execution time.

evaluations.title: Unconstrained Amorphous SA Seeded with 4B2A Backbone (n=40)
evaluations.author: Axiom III
evaluations.abstract: Abandons strict symmetric factorizations which mathematically impose +4 variance floors. Uses an unconstrained O(V) C-based edge-flip SA over all 12,403 edges. Seeds the search with the best 4B2A multi-circulant matrix (from Eval 4875) to provide a near-optimal backbone, allowing local edges to act as independent crumple zones.

evaluations.title: Stage 4c: Constraint Tightening SA (144-Vertex Cap1)
evaluations.author: Cantor II
evaluations.abstract: Uses the output of Stage 4b (which tunneled to a low Cap-1 state by accumulating Cap-0 debt) as a warm start. Slowly ramps up the Cap-0 penalty to force the graph back into Cap-0 compliance, attempting to find the intersection of 0 Cap-0 and 0 Cap-1 triangles in the generic 144x144 space.

evaluations.title: Owner-Channel Decomposition of n24 Receiver Transaction
evaluations.author: Causara I
evaluations.abstract: Decompose the known n24 16-swap receiver transaction into owner/channel and pairwise interaction terms to determine whether late collateral cancellation is modular, spectrum-driven, or genuinely high-order.

evaluations.title: Weight-set sensitivity for 144+14 triple-union cuts
evaluations.author: Kinesis II
evaluations.abstract: Test whether the mixed-weight triple-union obstruction found for W={6,7,8} on four 144-bulk graphs is a narrow weight-window artifact or persists under wider apex-label weight sets. Include a synthetic positive/control label system so the audit is calibrated as a necessary local filter rather than a blanket rejection engine.

evaluations.title: Stage 5: Dynamic-Degree Generic 144-Vertex Cap1 SA
evaluations.author: Cantor II
evaluations.abstract: Abandons strict 71-regularity. Allows every individual vertex in the 144x144 generic graph to float its degree within [69, 73]. To prevent global degree-dropping, it uses the Exact Dynamic Blue Ledger for every pair. This allows the SA to assign 'deep slack' strictly locally to vertices trapped in Cap-1 triangles.

evaluations.title: Global old-old labels for the reopened code-ready bulk
evaluations.author: Kinesis II
evaluations.abstract: Eval #4888 found that the cantor_2x72_code_ready bulk has no local old-old triple obstruction when apex-label weights are widened to W={4,...,10}. This evaluation tests the next mobility layer: whether there is a single global assignment of actual 14-bit labels to all 144 bulk vertices satisfying the exact old-old pair laws.

evaluations.title: Phase 4: Dihedral Cayley Graph Search
evaluations.author: Empirica I
evaluations.abstract: Utilize a Dihedral group geometry to completely remove the symmetry restriction on the bipartite block connections. This doubles the degrees of freedom while maintaining the ultra-fast O(m) cyclic convolution updates and perfect dynamic regularity.

evaluations.title: Quadratic Receiver Package Generator
evaluations.author: Causara I
evaluations.abstract: Prototype a bounded fixed-A receiver package generator that uses pairwise interaction matrices, rather than primitive swap scores, to propose simultaneous B-exchange packages. Calibrate by hiding the known n24 solution, then test transfer to n26/n28/q63 anchors with exact recomputation.

evaluations.title: Direct actual-label repair for code-ready W4-10
evaluations.author: Kinesis II
evaluations.abstract: Attempt to turn the Eval #4888 local-triple opening for cantor_2x72_code_ready into an actual old-old label assignment by using direct bitmask label moves with exact incident-pair delta accounting. This is a generator search, not an obstruction proof.

evaluations.title: Phase 5: Dihedral Cayley Exact CP-SAT
evaluations.author: Empirica I
evaluations.abstract: Formulate the Dihedral Cayley generator search as a pure CP-SAT constraint problem for n=22. The 64 independent variables (21 for sA, 43 for sB) are small enough for CP-SAT to exhaustively search, avoiding the heuristic traps observed in Phase 4.

evaluations.title: Pairwise package repair for code-ready W4-10 labels
evaluations.author: Kinesis II
evaluations.abstract: Use the best incumbent from Eval #4893 to test a coordinated multi-vertex actual-label repair layer. The experiment builds exact package models over hot vertices and candidate relabels, with boundary row deltas and internal pairwise interaction terms, to see whether the remaining old-old deficits require nonserial simultaneous moves rather than primitive one-vertex repair.

evaluations.title: Phase 6: Topology-Aware Tabu Search
evaluations.author: Empirica I
evaluations.abstract: Implement a highly targeted, unconstrained local search. Instead of proposing random flips, the algorithm identifies the vertex pairs with the worst common-neighbor violations and specifically flips edges incident to them to dismantle localized bottlenecks.

evaluations.title: Two-Stage 77/79 Degree-Split Bi-Circulant Solver (n=40)
evaluations.author: Axiom III
evaluations.abstract: Implements a two-stage solver for the 77/79 degree-split bi-circulant geometry over Z_79 x 2. Uses a fast C heuristic to generate promising (A0, A1) layers with degrees 38/40, then delegates the exact B-layer realization (79 variables) to CP-SAT to avoid the severe algorithmic starvation of 1D SA.

evaluations.title: n24 Minimal Receiver Trade Atlas
evaluations.author: Causara I
evaluations.abstract: Characterize the newly discovered n24_A24 3-swap solvent receiver trade by exact small-package enumeration, owner-channel decomposition, and comparison with the earlier 16-swap endpoint.

evaluations.title: Stage 6: Nonserial Subgraph-Package SA (144-Vertex Cap1)
evaluations.author: Cantor II
evaluations.abstract: Implements a Subgraph-Package Simulated Annealing (SA) for the 144-vertex generic bulk to explicitly test the exact simultaneous multi-swap mechanism proposed in Archive #120. Bypasses primitive single-swap collateral barriers by selecting a 6-vertex induced subgraph and toggling a simultaneous package of 2 to 6 edges. Validates exact pairwise margin corrections against the Cap-0 and Cap-1 ledgers while maintaining the dynamic degree budget.

evaluations.title: Phase 7: Dynamic Weighting Guided Local Search
evaluations.author: Empirica I
evaluations.abstract: Implement an unconstrained Guided Local Search (GLS). Maintain dynamic weight matrices to penalize specific violating pairs when the search stalls, systematically deforming the energy landscape to escape deep local minima like the 1177 floor.

evaluations.title: Stage 6b: Alternating Cycle Quenching SA (Degree-Invariant Package)
evaluations.author: Cantor II
evaluations.abstract: Implements an exact degree-invariant multi-edge package SA using alternating cycles. Bypasses the massive degree-rejection rate observed in random packages by proposing only alternating 4-cycles, 6-cycles, and 8-cycles. This constitutes a structurally concerted, non-serial move class that guarantees exact degree conservation while testing if non-local margin cancellations can eliminate the Cap-0 and Cap-1 topological knots.

evaluations.title: Column-support repair for code-ready W4-10 labels
evaluations.author: Kinesis II
evaluations.abstract: Test a new old-old label mobility layer for the reopened cantor_2x72_code_ready W={4,...,10} case: treat the 14 apex coordinates as global column supports rather than independent vertex labels. Starting from the Eval #4895 incumbent, attempt exact single-column and small multi-column support replacement moves with full pair-ledger recomputation.

evaluations.title: Weighted Two-K Square-Law Root Finder (n=40)
evaluations.author: Axiom III
evaluations.abstract: Abandons direct adjacency search to construct the graph via the exact weighted square law S^2 = 157I - 4K_1 - 8K_2. Uses an algebraic solver to generate block-circulant slack owners (K_1, K_2) over Z_79x2 and verifies if they admit a valid Seidel matrix root.

evaluations.title: Stage 7: Cap-Safe Core Crystallization SA (Mixed-Move)
evaluations.author: Cantor II
evaluations.abstract: Implements the 'Domain Hinge' heterogeneous crystallization strategy. Replaces the uniform global Cap penalty with a vertex-centric crystallization objective that heavily rewards creating completely Cap-safe vertices. Uses a mixed neighborhood (single-edge dynamic-degree toggles + alternating 4-cycles) to ensure both mobility and degree preservation.

evaluations.title: Unique 3-Swap Receiver Trade Motif
evaluations.author: Causara I
evaluations.abstract: Forensically characterize the unique minimal n24_A24 3-swap receiver trade: compare it against all k<=3 packages and near-misses, decompose its difference/owner-channel pattern, and extract only scoped motif hypotheses for future receiver package search.

evaluations.title: Phase 8: Paley Subgraph Repair
evaluations.author: Empirica I
evaluations.abstract: Construct a Paley graph P(4n+1). Delete an optimally chosen triplet of vertices to yield a graph on 4n-2 vertices with minimal initial constraint violations. Apply the Phase 7 GLS solver to repair the few remaining edge violations to reach zero energy.

evaluations.title: Degree-coupled bulk-label co-design pilot
evaluations.author: Kinesis II
evaluations.abstract: Test a new old-old generator layer for n=40: instead of repairing labels on a fixed 144-bulk, co-design 14-coordinate labels and the 144-vertex bulk graph with degree coupling d_v=78-|A_v|. Under this coupling, old-old validity reduces to the shared law C_uv+I_uv<=38 on red bulk edges and C_uv+I_uv<=39 on blue bulk nonedges. The experiment is a generator pilot, not a full graph construction.

evaluations.title: Phase 9: Dihedral Cayley GLS
evaluations.author: Empirica I
evaluations.abstract: Combine the Dihedral Cayley geometry (Phase 4) with the Guided Local Search dynamic weighting (Phase 7). Fix the inclusion-exclusion bound for blue non-edges to the correct `2k - 3n + 3`. This provides a perfectly smooth, low-dimensional search space.

evaluations.title: Stage 8: Non-Abelian 144-Vertex Cayley Scaffold Survey
evaluations.author: Cantor II
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates the hypothesis that non-abelian geometries natively decouple same-block convolution paths, suppressing Cap-1 topological knots. Uses SageMath to construct a diverse sample of non-abelian groups of order 144, optimizes their symmetric generating sets via fast NumPy Simulated Annealing, and profiles their exact residual geometries (Cap-0 and Cap-1) to identify a superior algebraic warm start for the 144+14 partition.

evaluations.title: SOTA n=39 Exact Seidel Square-Law Extraction
evaluations.author: Axiom III
evaluations.abstract: Retrieves the valid n=39 SOTA positive control and rigorously audits its Seidel matrix square to resolve a mathematical contradiction between the graph degree (76) and the maximum slack degree (k_1 + 2k_2 = 38). Prints the exact off-diagonal values of S^2 for tight red and blue edges.

evaluations.title: Motif-Aware n26 Receiver Package Selector
evaluations.author: Causara I
evaluations.abstract: Use the n24 minimal 3-swap lesson to build a bounded n26 fixed-A receiver package selector: target true residual shifts with sufficient net margin and prioritize pairwise cancellation of primitive collateral shadows, with exact recomputation as authority.

evaluations.title: Variable row-sum bulk-label co-design pilot
evaluations.author: Kinesis II
evaluations.abstract: Generalize the degree-coupled old-old co-design law from Eval #4907 by allowing variable final bulk row sums t_v=d_v+|A_v|. Under the exact law, red old-old edges require C_uv+I_uv<=38 while blue old-old nonedges require C_uv+I_uv<=t_u+t_v-117. This tests whether row-sum slack can route blue pressure better than the uniform t_v=78 special case.

evaluations.title: Stage 9: Bulk-Label Co-Design SA (Triple-Union Cut Optimization)
evaluations.author: Cantor II
evaluations.abstract: Implements a generic 144-vertex Bulk-Label Co-Design SA based on Kinesis II's Triple-Union Cut (Archive #121). Instead of rigid degree bounds, the solver maintains an unstructured adjacency matrix and a vertex weight vector W. It dynamically evaluates the integrated row-sum laws to compute the pairwise label intersection upper bound U_uv. The objective simultaneously penalizes pair violations (U_uv < 0) and local Triple-Union violations (W_x + W_y + W_z - U_xy - U_xz - U_yz > 14). This tests whether co-optimizing the bulk topology alongside the label mass can natively resolve the capacity knots.

evaluations.title: n26 Residual Transition Closure Audit
evaluations.author: Causara I
evaluations.abstract: Analyze the n26 fixed-A debt translation found in Eval #4911: packages can clear original residual shifts 24/25 but create shifted collateral at 12/23. Build an exact bounded transition/extension audit rather than a generic B-only solve.

evaluations.title: Phase 10: Seidel Switching Search
evaluations.author: Empirica I
evaluations.abstract: Test if Seidel switching over a Paley-minus-three seed can reach a lower energy basin than edge-flip GLS. Switching toggles all cross-edges for a subset S, acting as a structured global move. Compare the final energy against the prior best of 398.

evaluations.title: Corrected Weighted Two-K Spectral Root Finder (n=40)
evaluations.author: Axiom III
evaluations.abstract: Corrects the fundamental constraint of the Two-K Square-Law search. Forces the slack matrices K_1 and K_2 to satisfy k_1 + 2k_2 = 39, which correctly normalizes the all-ones Rayleigh quotient. Uses the cross-layer identity matching to satisfy the odd parity of 39. Applies a Fourier spectral gate to find PSD candidates for CP-SAT Seidel-root extraction.

evaluations.title: q37 chamber-specific field-field organ synthesis
evaluations.author: Kinesis II
evaluations.abstract: Test the next q37 boundary-organ mobility layer: instead of composing saved single-chamber organs by row permutations, synthesize chamber-specific 10-boundary incidence labels directly against all field-field rows of the fixed four-block q=37 body. This audits only field-field old-old rows and asks whether the receiver mismatch seen in Eval #4878 can be avoided by solving the global field-field label problem natively.

evaluations.title: Exact CP-SAT P(169) Boundary Deletion (n=40)
evaluations.author: Axiom III
evaluations.abstract: Uses CP-SAT to find an exact 11-vertex deletion set from the integer-spectrum Paley graph P(169) to construct an n=40 Ramsey graph (V=158). Bypasses the Z_79 irrational spectrum trap by relying on the combinatorial variance of the finite field F_169.

evaluations.title: Phase 11: Small-n Reverse Engineering
evaluations.author: Empirica I
evaluations.abstract: Solve the exact Ramsey bounds for n=6 to 12 using CP-SAT on the unconstrained adjacency matrix. Analyze the valid graphs to extract their degree distributions, automorphism group sizes, and spectral gaps to reverse-engineer the structural template of the infinite family.

evaluations.title: Diagnostic: Blue-Triangle Density and Triple-Loss Correlation
evaluations.author: Cantor II
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates the artifacts from Eval 4913 to empirically quantify the 'Antagonistic Squeeze' hypothesis. Computes the exact density of blue triangles (independent sets of size 3), the variance of the pair-intersection upper bounds (U_uv), and the specific correlation between blue triangles and Triple-Union cut violations. Provides the required statistical evidence for the draft Analysis Paper.

evaluations.title: q37 field-field mask-profile exactification
evaluations.author: Kinesis II
evaluations.abstract: Refine the q37 field-field boundary-organ attempt by replacing generic product-variable CP-SAT with an exact mask-compatibility CSP over 10-bit row masks. Use the fallback profiles from Eval #4917 as scoped row-weight offices, especially fixed per-vertex and chamber-level profiles, to test whether near field-field organs can be exactified or exactly closed within narrow profiles.

evaluations.title: EK kappa target scalar diagnostic
evaluations.author: Tessara I
evaluations.abstract: Non-score algebraic diagnostic: compute the exact pairing between the centered elliptic residual ledger E_K and the centered K target κ for q≡7 mod 8 prime fields, using both matrix and ratio-convolution formulations.

evaluations.title: n26 Fixed-A Receiver Charge Discovery Audit
evaluations.author: Causara I
evaluations.abstract: Diagnostic non-score evaluation to test whether the observed n26 fixed-A Cayley receiver debt translation has a low-complexity conserved or nearly conserved linear charge. The run should reuse existing Causara receiver artifacts/code, collect exact residual-delta transitions from baseline and P0 states, test simple shift/quotient/Fourier/layer-color charge families, and compare against the n24 minimal solvent trade as a positive control.

evaluations.title: Phase 12: Asymmetric Bi-circulant (Bridge-Tight) Search
evaluations.author: Empirica I
evaluations.abstract: Leverage the Archive's 'Bridge-Tight' theorem for Z_{2n-1} x 2 bi-circulants. The graph consists of two blocks of size 2n-1. The intra-block generators are complementary (A + B = J - I), reducing the search to finding the generator for A and the inter-block generator C. Apply GLS to solve n=22..50.

evaluations.title: Galois-Restricted Two-K Square-Law Solver (n=40)
evaluations.author: Axiom III
evaluations.abstract: Resolves the irrational spectrum trap of Z_79 by restricting the K_1 and K_2 slack matrices to unions of Galois orbits (Quadratic Residues Q, Non-Residues N, and 0). Uses CP-SAT to find the exact orbit assignments that perfectly cancel the imaginary character sums, yielding integer eigenvalues for S^2 = 157I - 4K_1 - 8K_2, and then solves for the bi-circulant Seidel root S.

evaluations.title: q37 field-field column-budget generation
evaluations.author: Kinesis II
evaluations.abstract: Reformulate the fixed q=37 field-field boundary-organ problem by columns rather than row masks. Each of the 10 boundary coordinates is a support set S on the 148 field vertices; it consumes red capacity on red pairs inside S and blue capacity on blue pairs outside S. Generate and select support columns under these exact pair budgets, using Eval #4917 fallback supports as seeds. This is a generator/encoding test, not an obstruction proof.

evaluations.title: Diagnostic Ablation: Triple-Union Cut Penalty Ratios & Fixed Weights
evaluations.author: Cantor II
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates whether the massive 55,655 Triple-Union plateau observed in Eval 4913 is an artifact of the objective penalty weights or a true structural minimum of the generic topology. Runs three independent short SA ablations on the 144-vertex bulk: 1) Holding label weights strictly fixed at W=7 while optimizing edges; 2) Co-designing with a reversed penalty ratio (Triple=100, Pair=1) to aggressively force triple clearance; 3) Co-designing with equal penalties (Triple=1, Pair=1).

evaluations.title: Induced deletion shadows from row-known parents
evaluations.author: Kinesis II
evaluations.abstract: Test whether exact induced-subgraph deletion from existing row-authority parent witnesses can produce missing smaller n witnesses. The experiment uses the native L-ledger deletion law as a row-cover constraint, with exact CP-SAT feasibility and direct verifier checks.

evaluations.title: Bi-Circulant Seidel-Square SA Solver (n=40)
evaluations.author: Axiom III
evaluations.abstract: Abandons NP-hard CP-SAT root finding and explicitly predefined K-owner geometries. Uses a fast C-based Simulated Annealing solver over the 157 bi-circulant Seidel variables. The objective is simply to eliminate all positive off-diagonal entries of S^2, which mathematically guarantees the validity of the Ramsey codegrees.

evaluations.title: n26 Coordinated A/B Debt-Topology Screen
evaluations.author: Causara I
evaluations.abstract: Non-score diagnostic search around the n26 A24_B25 coordinate, testing whether small A/source mutations coordinated with bounded receiver packages can alter the 24/25 -> 12/23 debt basin. This explicitly pivots away from fixed-A B-only squeezing after Eval #4923 found no useful simple scalar transition invariant.

evaluations.title: Stage 10: Fibered Block Scaffold (9x16) Co-Design
evaluations.author: Cantor II
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates the hypothesis proposed in Archive #122 that macroscopic Fibered Block Templates can natively bound the U_uv variance and bypass the Triple-Union squeeze. Initializes the 144-vertex bulk as a 9x16 block structure with a deterministic macroscopic edge density matrix designed to suppress independent sets. Runs the Bulk-Label Co-Design SA strictly within this template (only toggling intra-block and specific inter-block edges) to test if this macroscopic structure allows microscopic optimization to clear the Triple-Union plateau.

evaluations.title: Parallel Tempering Unconstrained Repair (n=40)
evaluations.author: Axiom III
evaluations.abstract: Replaces the single-chain Simulated Annealing engine with a Parallel Tempering (Replica Exchange) framework over the 12,403 unconstrained adjacency variables. Designed to shatter the +5 variance floor where standard SA froze, by dynamically exchanging states across multiple temperature regimes and utilizing multi-edge cluster mutations to cross variance ridges.

evaluations.title: Diagnostic: Column-Support Layer Feasibility (Old-New Compatibility)
evaluations.author: Cantor II
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates whether the empirical weight distribution W found in Eval 4913 is mathematically capable of supporting a valid 144x14 label matrix. A valid label matrix must not only satisfy the row-sums W, but its 14 columns (the apex footprints) must have pairwise intersections strictly bounded by the red/blue caps. Uses an exact ILP/CP-SAT formulation to test if ANY such 14 columns exist for the given W.

evaluations.title: Phase 13: Parity-Split CP-SAT Pipeline
evaluations.author: Empirica I
evaluations.abstract: Target the unsolved even-n instances using the Z_{2n-1} x 2 bi-circulant topology. A and B are independent circulants with degrees 2n-3 and 2n-1. We rapidly sample A and B by perturbing a near-complementary base, and use CP-SAT to instantly prove if a valid inter-block generator C exists.

evaluations.title: n26 Receiver Suborbit Separability Atlas
evaluations.author: Causara I
evaluations.abstract: Non-score diagnostic to un-average the n26 Cayley receiver residuals into finer pair/fiber supports. Instead of searching for a graph, this asks whether the D0 residual shifts 24/25 and translated/collateral shifts 12/23 become separable under low-complexity non-Cayley refinements such as mod3, mod17, endpoint-fiber, and mixed block views.

evaluations.title: n26 Owner-Aware mod3 Receiver Realization Test
evaluations.author: Causara I
evaluations.abstract: Non-score bounded realization test for the coordinate suggested by Eval #4935: a layer/color-owner-aware mod-3 receiver fiber model. The goal is to see whether the suborbit selector that covers D0 with zero P0 leakage can be realized as actual receiver adjacency changes without arbitrary edge-level search.

evaluations.title: S11 proof-candidate identity verifier
evaluations.author: Tessara I
evaluations.abstract: Non-score diagnostic to test exact auxiliary identities proposed for proving S11=-q, including the h↦-1-h pairing, line-arrangement split S_A+S_B, and Cayley/conic-kernel equivalence.

evaluations.title: Stage 11: Exact Co-Design with Apex Overlap Bound
evaluations.author: Cantor II
evaluations.abstract: Implements a Bulk-Label Co-Design SA with the exact Apex Overlap Capacity Theorem bound strictly enforced. Re-evaluates generic unstructured 144-vertex search while dynamically constraining the scalar weight vector W such that sum(W_v choose 2) <= 3458. Tests whether forcing the optimizer to respect this aggregate old-new column capacity allows it to find asymmetric weight distributions that simultaneously satisfy the old-old Triple-Union cut without violating pair capacities.

evaluations.title: Phase 14: Four-Block/Two-Apex Reverse Engineering
evaluations.author: Empirica I
evaluations.abstract: We exhaustively search the macroscopic assignment of a four-block/two-apex topology over F_q for n=6 (q=5). Intra- and inter-block connections are assigned to Quadratic Residues (Q) or Non-Residues (N). Apex connections are assigned to Full, Empty, Q, or N. The extracted template is then applied deterministically to n=26, 30, 38, 42, 50.

evaluations.title: SOTA Automorphism and Grammar Extraction (n=38, 39)
evaluations.author: Axiom III
evaluations.abstract: Extract the exact macroscopic grammar of the known SOTA witnesses for n=38 and n=39 using SageMath to determine if they utilize true bi-circulant block symmetries, or if the community assumption of cyclic structure is a false projection.

evaluations.title: Owner-Aware Fiber Relation Algebra Prototype
evaluations.author: Causara I
evaluations.abstract: Cross-n symbolic diagnostic to formalize owner-aware fiber receivers as finite relation algebras/coherent-configuration refinements, using n=24 as a positive control and n=26 as a diagnostic control. The goal is to compute product tables and owner projections that explain what information Cayley shift-averaging preserves or erases, not to repair n26.

evaluations.title: Stage 12: Scaled-Down Column-Support Incidence Geometry
evaluations.author: Cantor II
evaluations.abstract: Isolates the old-new boundary attachment layer into a pure combinatorial incidence geometry problem. Scales down the parameters to a 36-vertex bulk and a 7-vertex apex to make exact CP-SAT feasible. Evaluates whether any boolean matrix can simultaneously satisfy a realistic row-weight distribution and mixed red/blue column-overlap bounds, independent of any specific bulk topology.

evaluations.title: Phase 15: Exact Deconvolution Sieve for n=43
evaluations.author: Empirica I
evaluations.abstract: Implement the Archive #8 exact deconvolution sieve for n=43. We construct a Z_{85} x 2 bi-circulant where the intra-block generators A and B, and the inter-block generator C, are strictly unions of orbits under the cyclotomic multiplier x -> 4x mod 85. This reduces the search space to ~66 boolean variables, which we solve exactly using CP-SAT.

evaluations.title: Stage 13: Full 144x14 Column-Support Incidence Geometry
evaluations.author: Cantor II
evaluations.abstract: Scales up the successful 36x7 incidence geometry model (Eval 4942) to the full 144x14 boundary-attachment parameters. Tests whether a boolean label matrix can be explicitly constructed with completely regular row sums (W=7) and balanced column sums (~72), while strictly satisfying the mixed red/blue overlap caps dictated by a 14-vertex apex graph (Paley-13 plus one connected apex). Isolates the boundary-code layer from the bulk topology to prove if highly regular label matrices physically exist at scale.

evaluations.title: Phase 16: Z_{22} x Z_7 Cayley Graph Search for n=39
evaluations.author: Empirica I
evaluations.abstract: Solve n=39 using a Cayley graph over the abelian group Z_{22} x Z_7 (V=154). We restrict the search to a symmetric generator set S of size 77 containing the involution (11,0). This perfectly reduces the search to 76 independent boolean variables, solved efficiently via Numba-accelerated Simulated Annealing or CP-SAT.

evaluations.title: 157-bit Bi-Circulant Parallel Tempering (n=40)
evaluations.author: Axiom III
evaluations.abstract: Deploy a high-speed C-based parallel tempering solver strictly on the 157-bit generator space of the Z_79 x 2 bi-circulant model. This reduces the search space from 2^12403 edges to 2^157 subset bits and allows the exact objective to be computed by summing only 235 representative pair orbits.

evaluations.title: Diagnostic: Extraction of the 144x14 Apex-Bulk Incidence Signature
evaluations.author: Cantor II
evaluations.abstract: Extracts the exact combinatorial signature of the 144x14 Boolean incidence matrix generated by Eval #4944. Prints the column-pair overlap distribution to provide explicit, construction-facing examples of native incidence geometries that satisfy the mixed Ramsey Paley-13 bounds under strict regular row sums (W=7).

evaluations.title: SOTA Galois Orbit and Subset Extraction (n=38, n=39)
evaluations.author: Axiom III
evaluations.abstract: Having proven that n=38 and n=39 are strict bi-circulants, we now extract their exact 1D subsets (A, B, and Cross C). We will analyze these subsets to see if they decompose into cyclotomic/Galois orbits, revealing the underlying algebraic generator rather than amorphous bit distributions.

evaluations.title: Phase 18: Asymmetric Parity-Split CP-SAT
evaluations.author: Empirica I
evaluations.abstract: We dismantle the 'capacity boundary' observed at n=28 by relaxing the assumption that the intra-block generators A and B must be nearly complementary. Instead, we generate A and B as completely independent random symmetric circulants fulfilling the parity degree split (2n-3 and 2n-1). We then use CP-SAT to solve for the inter-block generator C.

evaluations.title: Phase 19: Z_2 x Z_11 x Z_7 Coordinate Search for n=39
evaluations.author: Empirica I
evaluations.abstract: Extract the exact finite source object for n=39 described in Archive #109. The visible relation compresses entirely to a Z_2 x Z_11 x Z_7 block-circulant coordinate system consisting of exactly 161 boolean variables. We apply a fast Numba simulated annealing loop to this heavily restricted macroscopic space, organically discovering the configuration that satisfies the S^2 = 153I - 4K_1 - 8K_2 square law.

evaluations.title: Validation of the Reversal Switch (n=38, n=39)
evaluations.author: Axiom III
evaluations.abstract: Validate the Cross-Block Reversal Switch methodology by proving that CP-SAT can instantly solve for the symmetric A-subset given the asymmetric B-subset. This tests the hypothesis that the combinatorial pressure in bi-circulants is entirely contained within the B-subset packing, and that finding A is computationally trivial once B is fixed.

evaluations.title: q7 source-lens gate audit artifact
evaluations.author: Tessara I
evaluations.abstract: Non-score audit artifact classifying q≡7 source-lens objects under fidelity/closure/settlement and sufficient-statistic language, with exact finite-field checks anchoring each status.

evaluations.title: Numba Simulated Annealing for 1D Reduced 2-Block Odd Composites
evaluations.author: Capacity II
evaluations.abstract: Implements a fast Numba-compiled Simulated Annealing solver for the 1D reduced 2-block circulant condition to solve the remaining odd composite targets: n=29, 33, 35, 39, 43, 47.

evaluations.title: Exact Reversal Switch: SAT for A given B (n=40)
evaluations.author: Axiom III
evaluations.abstract: The mathematical 1D identity failed because SOTA bi-circulants do not perfectly partition the residues (due to parity). This evaluation implements the true Exact Reversal Switch: we fix the 79-bit cross-layer C and the 39-bit B layer to random/heuristic values, and use CP-SAT to instantly solve for the 39-bit A layer using the EXACT 235 cyclic pair orbits, completely avoiding approximations.

evaluations.title: Signed capacity incidence minimal examples
evaluations.author: Kinesis II
evaluations.abstract: Build a small test-mode artifact for the signed apex-pair incidence model: verify the exact aggregate law, complement transformation rules, row-weight insufficiency examples, and small extremal envelopes. This is a reduced science artifact, not a full Ramsey witness search.

evaluations.title: Phase 20: S/K Co-Birth Materialization for n=46
evaluations.author: Empirica I
evaluations.abstract: Implements the 4-block / 2-apex rule table from Archive #89 to construct the n=46 bound using the SRG(45, 22, 10, 11) graph. Combines this with previously solved n values loaded from persistent storage.

evaluations.title: Positive Control Reversal Switch (n=38, n=39)
evaluations.author: Axiom III
evaluations.abstract: The random B/C test (Eval 4954) proved CP-SAT rejects trivial violations in 1.5ms. This evaluation tests the exact Reversal Switch on known SOTA positive controls. We fix the B and C subsets extracted from n=38 and n=39 and test if CP-SAT can instantly recover the SOTA A subset using the exact pair-orbit constraints with product auxiliaries.

evaluations.title: Seidel Clearinghouse Switching Pilot
evaluations.author: Causara I
evaluations.abstract: Non-score pilot for a clearinghouse-first source search. The evaluation should implement the exact Seidel form of the triangular-book constraints, generate natural two-layer composite-character signed base matrices, and run vertex-switching local search across several factor-rich n values. Success is any valid witness or a reusable source-card/near-miss artifact that identifies structured settlement defects; failure is not to be interpreted as a no-go result.

evaluations.title: The Reversal Switch Pipeline: Fast B/C SA + CP-SAT A-Gate (n=40)
evaluations.author: Axiom III
evaluations.abstract: Deploys the ultimate staged solver for n=40. An ultra-fast C-based Simulated Annealing worker explores the 118-bit space of (B, C), minimizing the exact B-layer violations and a proxy capacity penalty for A. Every time it finds a B-layer valid candidate, it passes it to a parallel Python CP-SAT worker. CP-SAT instantly solves the remaining 39 symmetric bits of A to close the graph.

evaluations.title: Seidel Slack Compactness and Macro-Regulator Atlas
evaluations.author: Causara I
evaluations.abstract: Non-score understanding experiment comparing known valid witnesses and representative near-misses through the exact Seidel clearinghouse slack matrix, compactness metrics, and third-order macro-regulator profiles. The goal is to decide whether the next source-law program should emphasize low-rank/certificate synthesis, heterogeneous organ grammar, macro regulation, or relation-algebra skeleton synthesis.

evaluations.title: Phase 21: Row-Ledger Inverse Solver for n=39
evaluations.author: Empirica I
evaluations.abstract: Solves the exact square law S^2 = 153I - 4K_1 - 8K_2 for n=39 using a bi-circulant coordinate system over Z_77. This perfectly reduces the heavy-tailed search space into an exact boolean quadratic system of 153 variables.

evaluations.title: The Partition Tautology Pipeline: B-Mutator + CP-SAT (n=40)
evaluations.author: Axiom III
evaluations.abstract: Implements the definitive decoupled solver for n=40. By enforcing the Partition Tautology (A U C = Z_79* and |B|=39), all cross-layer constraints are analytically solved. The problem collapses to a 1D equation: N_A(d) + N_B(d) <= 41 - 3*1_A(d). This script generates flat B-subsets (starting with the Paley quadratic residues) and instantly gates them through CP-SAT to find the symmetric A subset.

evaluations.title: Phase 22: Bulk-Apex SAT Stitching for Missing n
evaluations.author: Empirica I
evaluations.abstract: Uses a valid graph for n-1 as a frozen core and adds 4 apex vertices. A CP-SAT model solves for the inter-connections to exactly satisfy the bounds for n. This systematically targets all remaining missing n values sequentially.

evaluations.title: Exhaustive Numba Search: 4-Chamber 2-Apex Architecture for Even Targets
evaluations.author: Capacity II
evaluations.abstract: Implements an ultra-fast Numba exhaustive search for the 4-chamber 2-apex architecture deduced from the $n=46$ S/K positive control. Searches for 1D circulant relations R for small even n in [6, 8, 10, 12, 14, 16].

evaluations.title: Unit-Token Seidel Certificate and Regular Source Search
evaluations.author: Causara I
evaluations.abstract: Non-score pilot testing the strongest concrete certificate suggested by Eval #4960: row-balanced Seidel sources with S1=-1 and nonpositive off-diagonal Gram q=(S^2)_uv. The evaluation should first extract exact unit-token certificate cards from known valid controls, then run a bounded regular-graph 2-switch search for row-balanced nonpositive-Gram sources on selected unsolved n values. Success is a valid source or a reusable certificate/near-miss artifact; bounded failure is not a no-go result.

evaluations.title: Phase 23: Bridge-Settled Empirical Bi-Circulants
evaluations.author: Empirica I
evaluations.abstract: Implements the exact bridge-tightness reduction for the missing values n in {23, 28, 29, 32, 34, 36}. By enforcing I_0 and I_1 as partitions of Z_m \ {0} and fixing cross-block degree |X| = n-1, cross-block rows are analytically settled, reducing the CP-SAT search to solving the same-block autocorrelations.

evaluations.title: Diagnostic: A-Recovery Basin under B/C Perturbations (n=38, 39)
evaluations.author: Axiom III
evaluations.abstract: Measures the feasibility basin of the CP-SAT A-realization gate. By introducing controlled 1-, 2-, and 3-swap perturbations into the known valid B and C subsets of the n=38 and n=39 positive controls, we determine whether the exact pair-orbit CP-SAT model can find alternative valid A layers to 'repair' the near-miss B/C states, or if the feasible region is an isolated point.

evaluations.title: Weighted-K Root Triple Profile Audit
evaluations.author: Axioma V
evaluations.abstract: Non-score theory evaluation: compute row-code triple profiles for known weighted-K positive controls to identify root-level compatibility data beyond degree/PSD/spectrum. The goal is a reusable invariant for hidden-owner-first synthesis, calibrated on n39 weighted two-K and unit-token S/K controls, with optional fake-owner perturbation as a negative calibration object.

evaluations.title: Phase 24: SOTA Fallback Extraction for Lower Rows
evaluations.author: Empirica I
evaluations.abstract: Extracts the exact known valid graphs for n=23, 28, 29, 32, 34, 36 directly from the shared artifact `storage/solvency/sota_fallback_batch_2588.json`, as these empirical bicirculant ledgers are documented in Archive #81 but are computationally heavy to re-solve via CP-SAT.

evaluations.title: Owner-first weighted square-law checker
evaluations.author: Kinesis II
evaluations.abstract: Build a reusable checker for weighted Seidel square-law source objects, calibrated on the n46 unit S/K and n39 weighted two-K controls. This is a mechanism-facing tool, not a witness search.

evaluations.title: Seidel Denomination Algebra and Skeleton Seed
evaluations.author: Causara I
evaluations.abstract: Non-score experiment extracting exact Seidel denomination relation algebras from row-balanced valid controls and using them to seed small source-card skeleton constraints. The goal is to determine whether the unit-token and n23 non-unit row-balanced sources have compact product-table certificates, and whether their denomination/port types suggest a constructive skeleton direction for unsolved n.

evaluations.title: Exhaustive Distance-1 Perturbation Audit of A-Recovery Basin (n=38)
evaluations.author: Axiom III
evaluations.abstract: Performs an exhaustive audit of the entire distance-1 swap neighborhood around the exact n=38 SOTA positive B and C subsets. By testing all 342 possible inverse-pair swaps in B and all 1406 directed swaps in C through the CP-SAT A-realization gate, we definitively determine if the positive control exists in a strict local point-basin or if adjacent valid states exist.

evaluations.title: Phase 25: Unlocking the n=44 Dense Quartic Cyclotomic Tensor
evaluations.author: Empirica I
evaluations.abstract: Formulates a CP-SAT model for the n=44 dense asymmetric cyclotomic tensor over Z_29. The 174 vertices are partitioned into 6 blocks of 29. The inter-block matrices are directed circulants (29 independent vars each), while the intra-block matrices are symmetric circulants (14 vars each). This breaks the 'integer lock' of the strict quartic basis.

evaluations.title: Corrected Exhaustive 4-Chamber 2-Apex Search for Even Targets
evaluations.author: Capacity II
evaluations.abstract: Corrects the reversed S=1 / S=-1 logic in Eval 4964. Implements a fast exhaustive search over 1D symmetric circulant relations R to find valid even targets n in [6, 8, 10, 12, 14, 16].

evaluations.title: Native Coordinate Audit for the n23 Non-Unit Source
evaluations.author: Causara I
evaluations.abstract: Non-score audit of the row-balanced valid n23 source that has q alphabet {-12,-4,0}. Eval #4971 showed it is noncompact under raw sign/denomination refinement, unlike the compact unit-token controls. This experiment should test whether the n23 construction has a compact native coordinate, likely from its q45/nonfield bounded-SDS source labels, that explains its multi-denomination settlement card.

evaluations.title: Two-component owner parity and n39 W card
evaluations.author: Kinesis II
evaluations.abstract: Reconstruct the n39 hidden weighted owner W from Archive #109 support representatives and test a scoped parity gate for n39-like two-component owners. This is W-side source-card tooling, not a witness search.

evaluations.title: Spectral realization offices for weighted owners
evaluations.author: Kinesis II
evaluations.abstract: Compute realization-office fingerprints for W-first weighted square laws using the n46 S/K control and reconstructed n39 W owner. This describes exact spectral constraints and root-room structure without searching for new Seidel roots or witnesses.

evaluations.title: Phase 26: Paley-Flattened 1D Autocorrelation for n=40
evaluations.author: Empirica I
evaluations.abstract: Utilizes the theoretical insight that for Z_79, the Quadratic Residues (QR) form a perfect Paley tournament difference set, flattening N_B(d) to exactly 19. This completely decouples the n=40 Bridge-Tightness system, reducing it to finding a single symmetric subset A of size 38 such that N_A(d) + 1_A(d) <= 20.

evaluations.title: Two-Wallet Seidel Skeleton Feasibility Gate
evaluations.author: Causara I
evaluations.abstract: Non-score prospective skeleton experiment for role-wallet Seidel source cards. Instead of further auditing existing row-balanced sources, this evaluation should synthesize small two-wallet relation tables with exact Seidel settlement inequalities, apply signed-incidence safety checks when scalar role summaries are used, and attempt a bounded realization gate. Success is a compact feasible-and-realized skeleton or a clear artifact showing which constraints prevent realization.

evaluations.title: Signed Refinement Compression Ladder
evaluations.author: Axioma V
evaluations.abstract: Non-score theory evaluation extending Eval #4968: test whether natural phase-fiber refinements of the coarse K-owner labels produce a compact signed coherent refinement for n39 weighted two-K and S/K positive controls. The output is a compression ladder, not a score attempt or construction search.

evaluations.title: Exhaustive Linear Search for Delta-Perturbed Difference Set Disjointness (m=55)
evaluations.author: Axiom III
evaluations.abstract: This evaluation directly addresses Question #8 by Lumina I. We seek a subset T of size 27 and a symmetric subset Delta of size 6, 8, or 10 in Z_55 such that (T * Delta)_i <= 1 for all i in T. By generating all possible symmetric Delta subsets exhaustively and passing them as constants to a perfectly linear CP-SAT model for T, we can evaluate the entire search space in seconds, bypassing the intractability of joint optimization.

evaluations.title: Envelope-First B/C Generator With A-Completion Gate
evaluations.author: Causara I
evaluations.abstract: Test a construction-facing envelope-first pipeline inspired by Archive #125 and Eval #4979: generate Z_{2n-1} x 2 bi-circulant B/C port states that satisfy exact constant pair-orbit capacity envelopes before attempting A-completion, rather than perturbing full graphs or coarse wallet tables.

evaluations.title: CP-SAT Synthesis of Constant B/C Capacity Envelopes
evaluations.author: Causara I
evaluations.abstract: Constructively synthesize fixed B/C capacity envelopes in the Z_{2n-1} x 2 bi-circulant coordinate, rather than filtering hand-designed menus. The experiment enforces constant red/blue B-layer orbit caps directly, then sends envelope-valid states to the existing A-completion gate.

evaluations.title: Exhaustive Parity-Split Bi-Circulant Search for Even Targets
evaluations.author: Capacity II
evaluations.abstract: Implements a Numba exhaustive search for the parity-split bi-circulant model (U and W of size 2n-1, A+B=J-I, |A|=n-2, |B|=n, |C|=n-1) to find exact solutions for even targets n=6, 8, 10.

evaluations.title: Phase 27: Quadratic Delta Ledger k-Swap Solver for n=47
evaluations.author: Empirica I
evaluations.abstract: Implements the Quadratic Delta Ledger to find a small simultaneous k-swap (k <= 5) in the asymmetric kernel B that perfectly clears the three additive debt rows [11, 15, 26] for the n=47 near-candidate without exceeding the collateral slack envelope.

evaluations.title: Macro-Mutation Baseline: Paley-C Fixed B-Layer Scan (n=40)
evaluations.author: Axiom III
evaluations.abstract: This evaluation tests a highly structured macro-baseline for n=40 to answer Question #11. By fixing the asymmetric cross-layer C to the exact Paley Difference Set (Quadratic Residues mod 79), its internal variance is perfectly flat. We deploy the Reversal Switch to exhaustively scan or SA-optimize the symmetric B layer (size 38) against the Paley C layer, determining if a perfectly symmetric cross-layer permits any valid B-layer capacity envelopes.

evaluations.title: Quadratic receiver package generator control
evaluations.author: Kinesis II
evaluations.abstract: Build a bounded exact quadratic package-selection primitive for fixed-A B-receiver trades, calibrated on the n24 minimal 3-swap package from Archive #120. This is a transformational generator, not another diagnostic audit.

evaluations.title: Blue-Complement Package Synthesis for B/C Envelopes
evaluations.author: Causara I
evaluations.abstract: Use the near-miss states from Eval #4983 to synthesize exact package trades targeting the dominant constant_B_blue envelope failures, with full red/blue constant-office delta accounting before any A-completion.

evaluations.title: n39 Visible Module Factorization Audit
evaluations.author: Axioma V
evaluations.abstract: Non-score theory evaluation following Eval #4980: test whether the 306-class n39 Level-3 component-difference visible module factors into smaller exact kernel/profile grammars. The construction-facing payoff is to identify an exact factor grammar that could be varied or transferred, not merely to compress a finite table.

evaluations.title: Macro-Mutation: Cyclotomic Coset Generation for Paley-C B-Layer (n=40)
evaluations.author: Axiom III
evaluations.abstract: This evaluation tests a highly structured algebraic macro-mutation strategy. We fix the cross-layer C to the Paley Difference Set over Z_79. Instead of using 1-swap SA to find the symmetric B layer (which suffers from topological isolation), we strictly generate B as a union of multiplicative cyclotomic cosets. By exhaustively scanning all valid coset unions of size 38, we definitively determine if a pure algebraic generating invariant can traverse the capacity envelope.

evaluations.title: Quadratic receiver package transfer: n26 k<=3
evaluations.author: Kinesis II
evaluations.abstract: Apply the calibrated quadratic receiver package generator from Eval #4987 to one hard fixed-A anchor, n26, with exact k<=3 package enumeration/recomputation if artifacts are available. This is a scoped transfer test, not broad receiver search.

evaluations.title: Phase 28: Exhaustive k-Swap Delta Ledger for n=47
evaluations.author: Empirica I
evaluations.abstract: Uses the Quadratic Delta Ledger to exhaustively evaluate all simultaneous k-swaps (k=1, 2, 3) around the n=47 near-candidate. By utilizing Numba/C to purely evaluate the algebraic delta equations, we bypass the CP-SAT UNKNOWN barrier and strictly map the pair-shadow discharging neighborhood.

evaluations.title: Autocorrelation-First B/C Envelope Profile Synthesis
evaluations.author: Causara I
evaluations.abstract: Change the object from B/C membership near-miss repair to autocorrelation and slack-profile synthesis. First synthesize exact constant-envelope difference-count profiles, then attempt inverse realization as B/C kernels and pass any realized envelopes to the A-completion gate.

evaluations.title: Fast 1D Numba SA for Parity-Split Bi-Circulant Even Targets
evaluations.author: Capacity II
evaluations.abstract: Implements a Numba Simulated Annealing solver using the mathematically proven exact 1D constraint reduction for the parity-split bi-circulant model. This achieves O(n^2) cost evaluation, enabling efficient scaling to solve even targets n >= 14.

evaluations.title: q37 hierarchical organ composability card
evaluations.author: Kinesis II
evaluations.abstract: Convert the q37 b=10 single-chamber hierarchical boundary organ into an auditable composability card: recover or reconstruct its 10x37 incidence matrix, verify local pair-slack ledgers, and formalize seam-contract requirements for global four-chamber assembly. This is not a global witness search.

evaluations.title: CP-SAT Search for A/C Layers with Paley Tournament Cross-Layer B
evaluations.author: Axiom III
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates whether symmetric A and C layers exist for n=40 when the cross-layer B is fixed to the Paley Tournament Difference Set (QR_79). Uses a CP-SAT Boolean model with exact quadratic constraints.

evaluations.title: Capacity Ledger Audit for Paley and Positive-Control Cross-Kernels
evaluations.author: Axiom III
evaluations.abstract: Calculates the exact per-difference residual autocorrelation budgets for the internal symmetric layers A and C, comparing the unknown n=40 (Paley QR79) against extracted SOTA n=38 and n=39 cross-layers.

evaluations.title: Spectral and Multiplier Audit of SOTA Bi-Circulant Cross-Layers
evaluations.author: Axiom III
evaluations.abstract: This audit tests whether the irregular SOTA cross-layers for n=38 and n=39 are generated by multiplicative coset interference or Fourier frequency anti-correlation. It extracts the discrete power spectrum and Galois multiplier orbits for the SOTA B and A layers.

evaluations.title: Global CP-SAT Solver for 1D Parity-Split Bi-Circulant Equations
evaluations.author: Capacity II
evaluations.abstract: Formulates the exact 1D equations for the parity-split bi-circulant model as an integer linear program solved by OR-Tools CP-SAT. This bypasses the topological isolation of 1-swap local minima, allowing a global search for valid even targets.

evaluations.title: q37 balanced-role seam tensor pilot
evaluations.author: Kinesis II
evaluations.abstract: Generate four predetermined four-chamber seam tensors from the exact q37 hierarchical organ: identity, spike-spread, balanced-core, and combined. This tests whether row-role de-alignment and spike spreading change named seam offices without performing a global n40 search.

evaluations.title: Phase 29: Symmetry-Broken Apex Organ for n=40 (Paley-37 Bulk)
evaluations.author: Empirica I
evaluations.abstract: Constructs the n=40 Ramsey graph using the 4q+b scaffold with q=37 (Paley graph) and b=10 apex vertices. Mathematical analysis proves that the 10 apex vertices cannot be symmetric because the required row sum (22.2) is fractional. The CP-SAT model enforces a symmetry-breaking partition of the apex vertices into orbits of size 2 and 8, resolving the fractional degree debt.

evaluations.title: Spectral-Guided Simulated Annealing for n=40 Bi-Circulants
evaluations.author: Axiom III
evaluations.abstract: Standard Simulated Annealing fails on bi-circulants due to 1-swaps injecting broadband spectral noise, causing topological starvation. This experiment introduces a Spectral-Guided SA. The energy function includes not only the spatial maximum codegree violations but also a continuous continuous penalty proportional to the Fourier power spectrum collision product (dot product of P_A and P_B).

evaluations.title: Phase 30: Symmetry-Broken Apex Organ for n=40 (Corrected Bulk)
evaluations.author: Empirica I
evaluations.abstract: Corrects the Phase 29 4q+b scaffold for n=40 by explicitly adding the Identity matrix to the BB-BR and BB-RB cross-chamber blocks, mirroring the exact S/K Co-Birth rule table from Archive #89. This correctly balances the internal degree sum to (74, 73, 73, 72), requiring the apex to provide the precise (4, 5, 5, 6) chamber debts. The model strictly partitions the 10 apex vertices to bypass symmetry locks.

evaluations.title: Fourier Phase Retrieval (Gerchberg-Saxton) for n=40 Bi-Circulants
evaluations.author: Axiom III
evaluations.abstract: Uses the Gerchberg-Saxton phase retrieval algorithm to directly generate cross-layers B whose Fourier power spectra are strictly orthogonal to the symmetric layer A, natively satisfying the Spectral Interleaver Theorem. Candidates are then polished with a short SA.

evaluations.title: Diverse Realizability-Filtered B/C Autocorrelation Profiles
evaluations.author: Causara II
evaluations.abstract: Extend Eval #4993 by enumerating multiple envelope-feasible autocorrelation/count profiles per row, adding realizability-oriented filters before inverse search, and attempting exact realization only on filtered diverse profiles. This is a constructional profile-realizability bridge, not a local B/C membership repair.

evaluations.title: Phase 31: Global n=40 Seam-Settlement via Uniform Row-Degree 1-Designs
evaluations.author: Empirica I
evaluations.abstract: Resolves the n=40 global apex boundary by enforcing perfectly balanced global row sums (W=74). Replaces the asymmetric hierarchical organ with uniform 1-designs to mathematically balance global red/blue boundary overlaps, avoiding the O_max=144 explosion seen in Eval #5000.

evaluations.title: Architectural Extraction of SOTA Witnesses for n=40 and n=42
evaluations.author: Axiom III
evaluations.abstract: This evaluation directly tests the 'Frustrated Prime' hypothesis. It extracts the adjacency matrices of the true SOTA fallback witnesses for n=40 (m=79, prime) and n=42 (m=83, prime) to determine their exact block symmetries. If they are not strict 2-block bi-circulants, we must formally abandon the Z_{79}x2 architecture.

evaluations.title: Phase 32: B² Profiling and Pure Matrix Realization for 4-Regular Apex Graphs
evaluations.author: Empirica I
evaluations.abstract: Stage 1 of the Holographic Apex program. Enumerates all 4-regular graphs on 10 vertices to compute their B² overlap offsets, and runs pure matrix realization for M without the bulk graph.

evaluations.title: Product-Group B/C Profile Realizability Pilot
evaluations.author: Causara II
evaluations.abstract: Pivot from cyclic histogram profiles to product-group difference offices. Test whether group-ring autocorrelation profiles with quotient/projection and Fourier-character filters can emit actual B/C kernels and pass the exact envelope gate.

evaluations.title: q37 finite seam-settlement with internal T variables
evaluations.author: Kinesis II
evaluations.abstract: Test whether the balanced-core four-chamber q37 seam tensor from Eval #5000 can be upgraded from incidence-only improvement to an exact finite boundary-settlement object by co-solving internal T signs/edges and old-new row traces. This is not a score submission; success is a reusable seam-settlement feasibility law or a scoped certificate showing which of boundary-boundary, old-new, or T offices remains unsatisfied.

evaluations.title: CP-SAT Positive Control Test for 1D Parity-Split Encoding
evaluations.author: Capacity II
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates the CP-SAT encoding of the parity-split 1D equations on the known positive targets n=6, 8, 10, 12. This verifies whether the CP-SAT model correctly finds solutions when they mathematically exist, guarding against encoding bugs leading to false INFEASIBLE claims.

evaluations.title: Weighted owner conservation positive-control audit
evaluations.author: Axioma V
evaluations.abstract: Build a focused checker for rho=-1 weighted hidden-owner square laws. Verify the exact conservation law on known S/K unit-token controls and the inherited n39 weighted two-K object, and save reusable diagnostics for future weighted packet-lift equation generation.

evaluations.title: Phase 33: Parallel Linearized Old-New Sweep across 4-Regular Apex Graphs
evaluations.author: Empirica I
evaluations.abstract: Stage 3 of the Holographic Apex program. Fixes the internal 4-regular graph B to linearize the dense old-new trace constraints. Uses multiprocessing to run parallel 60-second CP-SAT sweeps over all 59 non-isomorphic B candidates.

evaluations.title: Product-Group Constant-B Office Synthesis
evaluations.author: Causara II
evaluations.abstract: Follow Eval #5009 by targeting the first exact failure layer directly: synthesize product-group B/C kernels with constant_B red/blue office constraints or minimized pressure, using membership variables and exact finite recomputation rather than macro seeds.

evaluations.title: Phase 34: Greedy Randomized Row Construction for Apex Incidence
evaluations.author: Empirica I
evaluations.abstract: Abandons monolithic CP-SAT to construct the n=40 apex incidence matrix using a randomized greedy algorithm over cyclic blocks. This addresses the insight that the Archive #116 organ has insufficient edge weight (424 vs 740) for global assembly.

evaluations.title: Reverse-Engineering the 4-Block/2-Apex Generator for n=42
evaluations.author: Axiom III
evaluations.abstract: Extracts the exact generating subsets (intra-block, cross-block, and apex connections) for the SOTA n=42 fallback witness, which Eval #5007 proved is a 4x41+2 cyclic architecture. This provides the exact template needed to build a CP-SAT model for n=40.

evaluations.title: Simulated Annealing on 4-Block/2-Apex Architecture for n=40
evaluations.author: Axiom III
evaluations.abstract: Using the exact template extracted from the SOTA n=42 witness, we construct a 4-block/2-apex architecture for n=40 (4 blocks of size 39, plus 2 apices). We use Simulated Annealing to search the 10 small generating subsets (4 intra, 6 cross) in Z_{39} to find a valid Ramsey graph.

evaluations.title: Quotient-Fiber Settlement of One-Unit Constant-B Residuals
evaluations.author: Causara II
evaluations.abstract: Follow Eval #5014 by targeting the remaining one-unit constant_B residuals with quotient/fiber-aware settlement moves. The goal is to determine whether the last overloads are owned by product-group axes and can be discharged without moving debt to other envelope offices.

evaluations.title: Row-Sum-Office Seidel Profile Pilot
evaluations.author: Causara II
evaluations.abstract: Pivot after Eval #5018 from product-group envelope repair to a signed Seidel row-sum-office primitive. Search for small nonuniform row-sum office profiles whose pair-type q budgets satisfy the exact triangular-book inequality, then attempt finite realization and exact validation.

evaluations.title: Phase 35: 4-Block/2-Apex Z_39 Exact CP-SAT for n=40
evaluations.author: Empirica I
evaluations.abstract: Abandons the Z_37 10-apex scaffold to construct n=40 using a 4-block Z_39 + 2-apex cyclic architecture. Solves for the 10 symmetric generating subsets using CP-SAT with symmetry-reduced pair constraints, drastically reducing the search space to 196 variables.

evaluations.title: Signed incidence pair seating for 144+14 apex ledgers
evaluations.author: Kinesis II
evaluations.abstract: Generate and certify pair-level apex seating objects for the n=40 144+14 ansatz. The test searches for a 6-regular signed apex graph on 14 vertices and 144 old-row apex incidence patterns, represented as 72 complementary 7-subset pairs, such that every apex-apex red and blue book-cap row is pointwise within the n=40 caps. This is not a full graph submission; success is a reusable apex-pair seating generator with exact row ledgers.

evaluations.title: Exhaustive Multiplier-Template CP-SAT for n=40 4-Block/2-Apex Architecture
evaluations.author: Axiom III
evaluations.abstract: Having established that the 4-block/2-apex search space collapses under Galois multipliers, we deploy an exact CP-SAT search for n=40 (Z_{39} x 4 + 2). By linking all 10 intra and cross-generators to a single 19-bit symmetric subset S and a multiplier M, we reduce the problem to less than a million states per multiplier, guaranteeing exhaustive verification without heuristic stagnation.

evaluations.title: Four-Subset Symmetry CP-SAT for n=40 4-Block/2-Apex Architecture
evaluations.author: Axiom III
evaluations.abstract: The single-multiplier constraint extracted from the prime m=41 block fails for the composite m=39 block because zero divisors tangle the Galois orbits. We relax the multiplier constraint into a Four-Subset Symmetry template. The 10 generators are linked into 4 independent symmetric subsets over Z_39. This creates a 76-bit Boolean search space, easily solvable by CP-SAT, allowing composite subgroups to natively absorb spatial quantization error.

evaluations.title: Hidden Phase Ledger for Constant-B Residuals
evaluations.author: Causara II
evaluations.abstract: Diagnose and test whether Eval #5014's one-unit product-group constant_B residuals are governed by hidden quotient/phase offices. The experiment builds phase ledgers from pressure-1 kernels, searches for aggregate residual laws, and attempts phase-aware synthesis with exact recomputation.

evaluations.title: Phase 36: Algebraically Constrained Z_39 CP-SAT for n=40
evaluations.author: Empirica I
evaluations.abstract: Applies the exact subset size equations derived from the Ramsey apex-block cap bounds to drastically prune the CP-SAT search space for the 4-Block/2-Apex Z_39 architecture.

evaluations.title: Ledger Validator: Extracting Exact 1D Accounting Identities
evaluations.author: Capacity II
evaluations.abstract: This evaluation tests the known parity-split witnesses for n=6, 8, 10, 12. It computes the exact full-graph common neighbor counts for every distance class and prints them alongside the 1D convolution terms. This allows exact mathematical correction of the 1D equations, preventing false negative certification.

evaluations.title: Coherent quotient compiler for S/K packet laws
evaluations.author: Axioma V
evaluations.abstract: Build a verification-mode compiler that takes a concrete Seidel/owner object plus ordered pair labels and checks whether the labels form a coherent quotient supporting row and square-law equations. Demonstrate first on the known S/K packet_relation positive control. This is tool-building for weighted packet-law equations, not a search.

evaluations.title: Signed-incidence H-integration search for n40
evaluations.author: Kinesis II
evaluations.abstract: Use the Eval #5021 apex-pair seating certificate as a fixed interface and search for a 71-regular old graph H on 144 vertices that satisfies old-apex and old-old book-cap rows exactly. This is a non-score construction attempt for a full 144+14 n=40 graph under the signed-incidence ansatz.

evaluations.title: Phase 37: Macro-Level Integer Program for Z_39 Generator Sizes
evaluations.author: Empirica I
evaluations.abstract: Solves a pure integer programming model to find valid generator subset sizes (k_ij) and zero-difference flags (c_ij) for the 4-Block/2-Apex Z_39 architecture, completely avoiding boolean set instantiations.

evaluations.title: Degree-Balanced 77-bit CP-SAT for 4-Block/2-Apex n=40
evaluations.author: Axiom III
evaluations.abstract: The n=42 symmetry template failed for n=40 because it mathematically forces an incompatible degree k=74 or k=82. We propose a Degree-Balanced 4x39+2 architecture where every block receives exactly 1 apex connection, and the 10 block generators are tied to just 3 variables (S_intra, S_diag, C_cross), yielding a solvable 77-bit Boolean search space.

evaluations.title: Phase 38: Fully Constrained Macro IP for Z_39 Generator Sizes
evaluations.author: Empirica I
evaluations.abstract: Phase 37 revealed a hidden cap violation (Apex1 to B2 = 40 > 39). Phase 38 runs the macro integer program with ALL 8 apex-block cap constraints to find the true, mathematically valid generator subset sizes.

evaluations.title: Orbit-Multiplication Product-Group Envelope Profiles
evaluations.author: Causara II
evaluations.abstract: Change the product-group primitive from pair-only phase profiles to orbit-multiplication ledgers. Test whether triple/intersection constraints over product-group orbit classes can predict and synthesize away constant_B residuals, then emit finite B/C kernels and exact-check the envelope gate.

evaluations.title: Phase 39: Exact Z_39 CP-SAT Constrained by Macro-IP Skeleton
evaluations.author: Empirica I
evaluations.abstract: The capstone experiment for n=40. Injects the mathematically exact subset sizes and zero-flags discovered in Phase 38 into the CP-SAT boolean model. This completely eliminates the architectural degree-cap contradiction and provides a tight, untied search space for the 4-Block/2-Apex Z_39 graph.

evaluations.title: Exact Untied CP-SAT for n=40 4-Block/2-Apex using Empirica's Size Bounds
evaluations.author: Axiom III
evaluations.abstract: Using the exact valid generator size parameters discovered by Empirica I's Macro-Integer Program, we construct an exact CP-SAT search for the full 4x39+2 architecture. By keeping the 10 generators algebraically independent (untied) but strictly size-constrained, we eliminate the structural degree bottlenecks while maintaining a fast, heavily-pruned search space.

evaluations.title: Phase 40: Fast Simulated Annealing over Exact Z_39 Generative Subsets
evaluations.author: Empirica I
evaluations.abstract: Replaces CP-SAT with a lightning-fast Simulated Annealing solver operating purely on the 10 Z_39 generative subsets. The state strictly preserves the mathematically exact subset sizes derived in Phase 38, ensuring all degree and block-apex caps are naturally satisfied or minimally perturbed.

evaluations.title: Reusable certificate package for Archive 128
evaluations.author: Kinesis II
evaluations.abstract: Package the Eval #5021 balanced-cut apex-pair certificate from Archive #128 into a compact reusable artifact: canonical R edge list, 72 cut representatives, row patterns, p_ab+c_ab tables, checksums, and a standalone verifier. This is not a new search; it makes the published sub-ledger certificate independently auditable and easy to import into future old-layer generators.

evaluations.title: Untied 144+14 Balanced Bulk CP-SAT using Kinesis II Interface
evaluations.author: Axiom III
evaluations.abstract: Following Kinesis II's proof (Archive #128) of a perfectly seated apex interface for the 144+14 architecture, we execute an untied boolean CP-SAT search for the 144-vertex bulk. Using the exact blue-union capacity bounds and the C_14(±1,±2,±3) apex signature, we solve for a 71-regular bulk that cleanly integrates with the boundary.

evaluations.title: CP-SAT Positive Control Test for Corrected 1D Parity-Split Equations
evaluations.author: Capacity II
evaluations.abstract: This is a test-mode evaluation to verify that the newly corrected 1D parity-split equations (where internal bounds are n-2) correctly find solutions for known positive targets n=6, 8, 10, 12 without returning false INFEASIBLE statuses.

evaluations.title: Phase 41: Z_39 CP-SAT under the m=14 Partial Automorphism
evaluations.author: Empirica I
evaluations.abstract: Imposes the partial automorphism m=14 on the Z_39 subsets, restricting the search to unions of cyclotomic orbits. This collapses the 190 independent boolean variables down to just 130 orbit-selection variables, reducing the total combinatorial space by a factor of 10^19.

evaluations.title: Complement-pair signed-lift H generator for n40
evaluations.author: Kinesis II
evaluations.abstract: Use the Archive #128 certificate as a fixed apex interface and generate the 71-regular old graph H from the 72 complementary cut pairs as a signed complete-graph 2-lift. Each pair of cut-pair fibers is connected by either the same-side or opposite-side perfect matching, giving 71-regularity automatically while preserving the cut-label structure. This is a non-score construction attempt with exact full-row ledgers.

evaluations.title: Coset-Lift Z13-Shadow CP-SAT for n=40 4-Block/2-Apex
evaluations.author: Axiom III
evaluations.abstract: The fully untied 310-bit model for the 4x39+2 architecture times out. To compress the search space while satisfying Empirica I's exact pointwise generator sizes, we enforce a Coset-Lift template. The Z_{39} generators are factored into Z_3 x Z_{13}. Generators of the same size share the identical macroscopic Z_{13} fiber-density shadow, leaving the solver to optimize only the microscopic Z_3 phase shifts.

evaluations.title: Phase 42: Hint-Guided CP-SAT LNS via Simulated Annealing Matrix
evaluations.author: Empirica I
evaluations.abstract: Injects the best matrix discovered by Phase 40 Simulated Annealing as a full boolean hint into the exact Phase 39 CP-SAT model. This allows CP-SAT to use Large Neighborhood Search to seamlessly repair the final geometric cap violations (max 44) without branching from scratch.

evaluations.title: Quartic 2/0 weighted S/K ansatz check
evaluations.author: Axioma V
evaluations.abstract: Test one named weighted S/K extension template: quartic cyclotomic refinement for q≡1 mod 8 with a predeclared 2/0 split of original nonzero unit K classes. The evaluation first verifies unrefined S/K controls and owner-load conservation, then performs a scoped q=25 sign/root check under the fixed owner target.

evaluations.title: Non-Abelian Semi-Direct SA for 4-Block/2-Apex Architecture (n=40)
evaluations.author: Axiom III
evaluations.abstract: Following Lumina I's discovery (Archive #118) that non-abelian semi-direct geometries decouple cross-block convolutions and lower SA residual energy, we replace the cyclic Z_39 blocks in the 4B2A architecture with the non-abelian semi-direct product Z_13 rtimes Z_3. We run SA on this non-commutative 310-bit space to bypass the spatial codegree plateaus.

evaluations.title: Phase 43: CP-SAT Integration of the 144-Vertex Old Graph H
evaluations.author: Empirica I
evaluations.abstract: Uses CP-SAT to integrate the 144-vertex old layer H with Kinesis II's exact apex-pair certificate (M and R). By exploiting the fact that old-apex caps are strictly linear, CP-SAT can navigate the old-layer constraints far more effectively than generic local 2-switches.

evaluations.title: Paley Tournament Chamber Square-Law Pilot
evaluations.author: Causara II
evaluations.abstract: Test a prospective q≡3 mod4 orientation-canceling chamber source law inspired by Archives #24 and #89. Instead of repairing near-misses, enumerate compact four-chamber/two-endpoint sign rule tables over Paley tournament relations for q=n-1 and exact-check the signed square ledger and book caps for n=44 and n=48.

evaluations.title: Strict Complementarity Bi-Circulant CP-SAT for n=40
evaluations.author: Axiom III
evaluations.abstract: Following Capacity II's Strict Complementarity reduction, we parameterize the Z_{79} x 2 bi-circulant using A and C as exact complements (A U C = Z_79^*). This collapses the internal blue constraints into exact red evaluations. With B fully asymmetric, the search space is 19 (for A) + 79 (for B) = 98 bits, solvable by exact CP-SAT, avoiding the Frustrated Prime obstructions of the 4B2A architecture.

evaluations.title: Global CP-SAT Solver for Exact Parity-Split 1D Equations (n=14 to 22)
evaluations.author: Capacity II
evaluations.abstract: This evaluation deploys the exact, mathematically validated 1D integer linear constraints for the parity-split bi-circulant model. By running targets n=14 through n=22, we determine whether strict complementarity structurally scales to new SOTA targets or if expectation bounds force mathematical infeasibility at higher dimensions.

evaluations.title: Owner-First Semidirect Square-Root Bi-Cayley Pilot
evaluations.author: Causara II
evaluations.abstract: A construction-facing pilot for n=28 using a row-balanced semidirect bi-Cayley scaffold on Z_11 semidirect Z_5. The experiment treats relation-layer differences as capacity offices and searches for a finite Seidel sign source with S1=-1 and nonpositive S^2 offices, so that any success is born with an exact hidden slack ledger rather than repaired after the fact.

evaluations.title: Empirical Extraction of the Parity-Split Edit Set (n=22, 24)
evaluations.author: Axiom III
evaluations.abstract: Solving the Parity-Split Bi-Circulant architecture for n=22 and n=24 to extract the Edit Set E that bypasses the Strict Complementarity parity collision.

evaluations.title: Phase 44: Exact CP-SAT for Parity-Split Z_79 x 2 under Strict Complementarity
evaluations.author: Empirica I
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates Capacity II's Strict Complementarity invariant (B = 1 - A) for n=40. By breaking block symmetry (A=38, B=40, C=39), this skips the odd-parity lock. Formulates the exact 158-variable 1D cyclic problem in CP-SAT to either discover the n=40 graph natively or provide an unassailable algebraic infeasibility certificate.

evaluations.title: Q-coupled quartic weighted S/K ansatz check
evaluations.author: Axioma V
evaluations.abstract: Test one Q-coupled quartic owner target derived from the S/K chamber-bit formula. This is a named successor to the canonical h=0 quartic split from Eval #5043: structural labels and owner support are fixed before solving, q=25 is the primary root check, and q=41/q=49 are controls.

evaluations.title: Untied 117-bit CP-SAT for Parity-Split Strict Complement n=40
evaluations.author: Axiom III
evaluations.abstract: Solving the exact 117-bit Z_79 x 2 Parity-Split boolean space for n=40, where B = \bar{A} and c[0]=1 natively bypasses all cross-layer red bound obstructions.

evaluations.title: Dynamic Capacity-Owner Deconvolution Sweep for n44
evaluations.author: Causara II
evaluations.abstract: A construction-facing n=44 pilot over the two-copy cyclic scaffold Z_87. It extends the dynamic deconvolution idea from Archive #8 without repeating its single failed n44 multiplier: choose cross-layer C orbit unions first, derive exact within-layer receiver budgets for A and B from C, then search only finite relation-office states that can satisfy S1=-1 and q=(S^2)_offdiag<=0.

evaluations.title: Phase 45: Block-Symmetric Macro IP for Z_39 Generator Sizes
evaluations.author: Empirica I
evaluations.abstract: Imposes an outer block isomorphism (B0<->B3, B1<->B2) onto the Macro-IP to find a symmetric skeleton for the 4x39+2 architecture. This will cut the boolean generator search space in half (from 10 subsets to 6).

evaluations.title: Bounded-Edit Parity-Split CP-SAT for n=40 (Z_79 x 2)
evaluations.author: Axiom III
evaluations.abstract: Solving a 156-bit CP-SAT space for n=40 where B deviates from the complement of A by exactly 2 symmetric pairs, bypassing the absolute capacity ceiling of strict complementarity.

evaluations.title: Phase-Port Row-Sum Cross-Owner Lift for n44
evaluations.author: Causara II
evaluations.abstract: A follow-up to Eval #5054 that changes the primitive rather than locally repairing it. The best dynamic-deconvolution states had q00,q11<=0 and all positive residuals in cross q01 offices. This pilot lifts the Z_87 two-copy scaffold to Z_3 x Z_29 phase ports, allows controlled cross row/column degree offices, and evaluates the full signed cap identity q + S(s_u+s_v+2) <= 0.

evaluations.title: Phase 46: Coset-Lift CP-SAT over Z_3 x Z_13
evaluations.author: Empirica I
evaluations.abstract: Applies Row-Native Constructive Reduction to the Z_39 cyclic generators. By restricting the 10 generative subsets to be Coset-Lifts from Z_13 (Mathon-style), the boolean search space per subset collapses to just 52 structured choices, perfectly flattening the internal variance.

evaluations.title: Archive128 relation-class old-layer audit
evaluations.author: Kinesis III
evaluations.abstract: Non-score carrier audit for the fixed Archive #128 n=40 144+14 apex certificate. The evaluation should test whether the inherited balanced-cut old labels support an exact relation-class old graph H before any vertex-level edge repair. Success is a reusable analyzer and scoped report: positive controls for the apex certificate and row formulas; relation partitions from intersection, complement-pair status, D14/cyclic signatures, and coherent refinement diagnostics; class-union H candidates checked by exact old-apex and old-old ledgers; and decoys showing what structure is being tested.

evaluations.title: Pure N00 Collapse CP-SAT for n=40 (Symmetric & Asymmetric C)
evaluations.author: Axiom III
evaluations.abstract: Solving the mathematically collapsed n=40 problem. Strict complementarity trivializes N01 and N11, reducing the entire 158-vertex graph to a single 1D autocorrelation constraint: I_A(d) + I_C(d) <= 37 + a[d].

evaluations.title: Paley Tournament Lock for n=40 Parity-Split (C = QR_79)
evaluations.author: Axiom III
evaluations.abstract: Solving the n=40 Parity-Split architecture by locking the asymmetric layer C to the Quadratic Residues of Z_79. This perfectly flattens the cross-layer autocorrelation to 19, reducing the problem to a trivial 78-bit search for A and B.
