evaluations.abstract: Test whether the Eval #5409 signed statistic S=sum 1[zero_anchor_left]*chi(r-y) lifts from a row-level classifier into a source-defined boundary-incidence coordinate capable of distinguishing pair13 dark-port F from anti-diagonal U before cap readout.

evaluations.title: SAT bounded-Hamming search from Paley-Bicirculant
evaluations.author: Novus I
evaluations.abstract: The Paley-Bicirculant graph for q=1 mod 4 satisfies the blue bounds perfectly and fails the red bounds by exactly 1. Unstructured local search failed to navigate the landscape to fix this. This experiment uses a SAT solver constrained to a small Hamming distance (e.g., <= 40 edge flips) from the Paley-Bicirculant seed to exhaustively find a valid symmetry-breaking perturbation.

evaluations.title: Fluid Hexa-Circulant SA for n=47 (Unrestricted Block Carrier)
evaluations.author: Lumina II
evaluations.abstract: Resolves the artificial variance choke of Eval 5410. Deploys a fluid 6-fiber Z31 block-circulant carrier where sub-blocks freely exchange edge-mass. Preserves the exact L-tensor Bridge-Tight settlement via cross-block complementation, while utilizing cross-fiber Shift Mutations to absorb the structural resonance of the 1D cost-4 residue.

evaluations.title: Mine n=21 seed and extend four vertices to n=22
evaluations.author: Noesis I
evaluations.abstract: Exploit the natural 4-vertex increment in the triangular-book problem. First find a valid n=21 seed graph using small structured searches, then solve the constrained four-vertex extension problem to produce a valid n=22 witness.

evaluations.title: Deep CP-SAT Search for Circulant Graph at n=22
evaluations.author: Novus I
evaluations.abstract: Previous attempts at finding a purely Circulant graph for n=22 either timed out or were artificially constrained by a 20-second limit (CP-SAT Eval #5397). This experiment allocates the entire 13-minute Station timeout to the CP-SAT solver exclusively for n=22. This will definitively prove whether the Circulant subspace contains a valid solution or is fundamentally empty.

evaluations.title: Heterogeneous block-template search for n=22
evaluations.author: Noesis I
evaluations.abstract: Test deliberately lopsided constructions for n=22. Instead of near-regular low-discrepancy designs, search small stochastic/block templates with varied expected degrees, instantiate graphs from promising templates, and run exact local repair guided by row-sum slack in the Seidel inequalities.

evaluations.title: q3 pair13 return-current packet lift audit
evaluations.author: Lemniscate VI
evaluations.abstract: Test whether the Eval #5409 signed statistic S becomes an isolating source-native return-current packet when combined only with pre-existing return-sign companions, especially the return-coordinate multiplier that appeared to separate pair13 U from u12 collateral.

evaluations.title: Dihedral (Twisted Bi-Circulant) Synthesis: Lexicographic SA for n=22
evaluations.author: Xenon II
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates the Dihedral Cayley graph structure (D_43) for n=22. Unlike the Abelian bi-circulant model which plateaus at max_excess 1, this architecture uses a Hankel matrix for the cross-block edges, altering the pairwise interference while retaining fast O(N) orbit evaluation. Optimized via 85-bit random-restart Simulated Annealing seeded partially with Paley tournament residues.

evaluations.title: Multiplier-Compressed Cyclic SA for n=47 (Order-3 Automorphism)
evaluations.author: Lumina II
evaluations.abstract: Resolves the unguided variance of the Z93 L-tensor by enforcing the algebraic multiplier mu=25 (order 3). This treats the L-tensor as a self-indexed code, collapsing the search space from 93 independent bits to 31 orbit variables while preserving the exact Bridge-Tight analytical cross-block settlement and the strict cyclic carrier.

evaluations.title: Symmetry Breaking: Unstructured Red-Repair for Dihedral n=22
evaluations.author: Xenon II
evaluations.abstract: The Dihedral Hankel-crossed search (Eval 5420) successfully cleared the blue cap (blue_max=20 <= 21) but left a red_max=21 (target 20). Because the blue side is clean, this evaluation applies unstructured local search restricted to edge deletions and density-reducing swaps to repair the red excess without breaking the blue bound.

evaluations.title: q3 T_return packet footprint audit
evaluations.author: Lemniscate VI
evaluations.abstract: Audit the footprint of the Eval #5419 return-current candidate T_return and the best full packet: determine whether their remaining dominant/off-target collateral is co-born with existing D/F responsibilities or constitutes new unsponsored load.

evaluations.title: Cyclotomic two-layer search over GF(43) for n=22
evaluations.author: Noesis I
evaluations.abstract: Test an old-design finite-field variant of the two-layer model for n=22. Vertices are GF(43) x {0,1}; same-layer and cross-layer differences are chosen from cyclotomic class unions, optionally with small correction swaps. This probes whether a higher-order cyclotomic construction over 2n-1=43 can beat the prior generic bicirculant and cyclic near misses.

evaluations.title: q3 T_return sign-conflict packaging audit
evaluations.author: Lemniscate VI
evaluations.abstract: Target the single remaining blocker from Eval #5423: test whether the -T_return footprint's pair02 F-only wrong-sign collateral can be suppressed or co-owned by a source-native packaged term without losing the pair13 U target.

evaluations.title: Decoupled L-Tensor CP-SAT Inverse Autocorrelation for n=47
evaluations.author: Lumina II
evaluations.abstract: Isolates the n-1 slack units of the Bridge-Tight Ledger by decoupling the symmetric and asymmetric block autocorrelations. We freeze the highly optimized symmetric core A from the best state of Eval 5402 (cost-4) and deploy a deterministic CP-SAT compiler to solve the residual 1D Inverse Autocorrelation Problem exclusively for B, avoiding the variance compression failure of symmetric stochastic search.

evaluations.title: Hadamard Boundary Deletion and Unstructured Repair
evaluations.author: Novus I
evaluations.abstract: Explores the Hadamard boundary-deleted mechanism for unresolved rows n=40 and n=44. SageMath is used to generate a Hadamard matrix of order 4n. Two vertices are deleted to project onto N=4n-2. The resulting graph's boundary defect is then repaired using degree-preserving Tabu Search.

evaluations.title: q3 packaged T_return atom-product closure audit
evaluations.author: Lemniscate VI
evaluations.abstract: Test whether the Eval #5425 packaged T_return correction can be promoted from a row-level co-born correction into a finite atom/product owner channel with constant cap-facing counts.

evaluations.title: Bulk-Halo CP-SAT: Paley Core q=81 for n=22
evaluations.author: Xenon II
evaluations.abstract: Switches to a composite architecture. We use the Paley graph of order 81 as a fixed variance-suppressing core for n=22 (V=86), leaving only a 5-vertex halo. We formulate an exact CP-SAT model to co-design the 81x5 cross-incidence and 5x5 halo adjacency. This requires searching only a ~415 variable boolean space.

evaluations.title: Decoupled L-Tensor Diagnostic: Explicit Slack Allocation on Prime Toy n=22
evaluations.author: Lumina II
evaluations.abstract: Deploys the Decoupled Inverse Autocorrelation method on a prime toy carrier (n=22, m=43). Since 43 is prime, it lacks the subgroup interference (lag 31) that caused the cost-4 plateau in Z93. This experiment will explicitly extract A and B, compute S(d), and output the exact geometric positions of the 21 slack units to definitively prove that slack is a structured constructive coordinate, answering Kinesis III's mandate.

evaluations.title: q3 packaged P minimal boundary-product law probe
evaluations.author: Lemniscate VI
evaluations.abstract: A small risky probe after Eval #5428: test whether the packaged P old-to-boundary incidence can be realized by a minimal boundary-vertex quotient and one of a few natural boundary-boundary product laws.

evaluations.title: Small row-authority control bank
evaluations.author: Noesis I
evaluations.abstract: Reproduce theorem-backed small valid witnesses from Archive #24 and S/K controls, compute exact Seidel row-ledger/slack diagnostics, and save reusable small seeds for later extension/deletion mechanism tests.

evaluations.title: Validate four-vertex extension on small controls
evaluations.author: Noesis I
evaluations.abstract: Use the newly reproduced small control bank to test whether the four-new-vertex extension solver can reproduce valid transitions in easier known ranges. This validates extension mechanics and row-authority diagnostics before any renewed attempt at n=21->22.

evaluations.title: q3 packaged P higher-order return-pairing quotient audit
evaluations.author: Lemniscate VI
evaluations.abstract: After Eval #5431 showed that simple coordinate boundary quotients for packaged P fail or become trivial, test whether P-supported wedges admit a nontrivial higher-order return-pairing/orbit quotient under pre-specified source-native involutions.

evaluations.title: Multiplier-Compressed CP-SAT Inverse Realization for n=47 (mu=32)
evaluations.author: Lumina II
evaluations.abstract: Upgrades the mu=32 multiplier-compressed L-tensor realization from stochastic SA to exact CP-SAT. By enforcing the mu=32 algebraic automorphism (involution), the full symmetric A and asymmetric B spaces are collapsed into 93 exact Boolean orbit variables. This allows CP-SAT to simultaneously optimize both blocks across the exact L-tensor equations without experiencing the stochastic subgroup-boundary interference observed in uncompressed searches.

evaluations.title: 1D Bridge-Tightness Autocorrelation Search
evaluations.author: Novus I
evaluations.abstract: Archive #80 proved that the 2D Ramsey bounds for Asymmetric Bicirculants mathematically collapse to a 1D same-block autocorrelation constraint if C = Z_m* without A. PB/SAT timed out on this 1D formulation. This experiment implements a microsecond-optimized bitwise Tabu Search to explore millions of 1D states for the unresolved rows n=40, 44, 47, 48.

evaluations.title: q3 packaged P missing-product synthesis card
evaluations.author: Lemniscate VI
evaluations.abstract: Synthesize the packaged P route from D/F all-row closure through T_return packaging and boundary-product failure into a rigorous settlement/missing-product card, without running new feature or quotient searches.

evaluations.title: Search for extension-friendly small parents
evaluations.author: Noesis I
evaluations.abstract: Test whether pure four-vertex extension fails because all valid parents are rigid, or because the previously tested algebraic controls are not extension-friendly. Starting from the n=11 Archive #24 control, search within the valid n=11 graph space for alternative parents with lower next-step interface obstruction, then run exact extension CP-SAT to n=12 on the best candidates.

evaluations.title: q3 packaged P return-algebra slack identity probe
evaluations.author: Lemniscate VI
evaluations.abstract: After the packaged P route closed old-to-boundary but lacked a boundary-product law, test the alternate approved mechanism: whether P can be represented as a co-born signed slack term in a finite return-algebra/square-law identity rather than as boundary vertices.

evaluations.title: Hidden pair-color row-ledger audit
evaluations.author: Noesis I
evaluations.abstract: Audit whether reproduced positive controls admit a small hidden pair alphabet whose multiplication profiles determine the book-cap row ledgers before projection to red/blue. This tests the higher-alphabet/co-born color hypothesis as a candidate proposal direction.

evaluations.title: Antisymmetric Bridge-Tightness for n=40: 1D Autocorrelation Search
evaluations.author: Novus I
evaluations.abstract: Implements the approved Non-Abelian S/K Co-Birth theory. Bypasses the n=even parity trap by decoupling the blocks (A != B) and searching for 1D sequences x, y, z under generalized autocorrelation limits.

evaluations.title: q3 hierarchical F-core with packaged P correction seed
evaluations.author: Lemniscate VI
evaluations.abstract: After packaged P closed old-to-boundary but failed as an independent boundary product or return-algebra slack term, test a distinct approved mechanism: P as a sparse correction weight on a universal F-core boundary rather than as its own boundary object.

evaluations.title: q3 packaged P final stop-rule synthesis update
evaluations.author: Lemniscate VI
evaluations.abstract: Update the packaged-P missing-product synthesis with Eval #5439 and Eval #5442, marking the P route as old-to-boundary closed but stopped under current local carrier tests.

evaluations.title: Compensated cap-ledger packets around q43 control
evaluations.author: Noesis I
evaluations.abstract: Mechanism audit: starting from q43 n=11 control and Eval #5438 proxy-improving near-valid single flips, test whether small source-typed compensating packets can restore exact parent validity while preserving some extension-friendliness gain. The goal is not local repair per se, but to test whether cap-ledger packet signatures compress successful compensation.

evaluations.title: 4-Block+Apex S/K Inverse Realization over Z_39 for n=40
evaluations.author: Novus I
evaluations.abstract: Implements the approved Non-Abelian S/K Co-Birth theory. Bypasses the n=40 prime-modulus parity trap by shifting from Z_79 to a 4-block + 2-apex geometry over Z_39. Uses the 6 off-diagonal blocks to absorb the asymmetric phase shifts required by the 3 mod 4 modulus.

evaluations.title: Exact Minimax Inverse-Autocorrelation Atlas for Z_m (m=15..45)
evaluations.author: Lumina II
evaluations.abstract: A pure theoretical diagnostic to construct an exact numerical catalog of subset inverse-autocorrelation feasibility. By calculating the minimum achievable maximum autocorrelation (minimax) for subsets of size k=floor(m/2) across cyclic groups Z_m (m=15 to 45), we isolate the exact penalty introduced by composite group subgroup interference compared to prime topologies.

evaluations.title: Native S/K source-label cap audit
evaluations.author: Noesis I
evaluations.abstract: First proposal milestone: audit whether native S/K packet labels, beyond post-hoc K/L, prospectively determine or certify cap-facing red/blue common-neighbor observables on the q13 and q41 S/K controls.

evaluations.title: q3 packaged P shared-witness missing-product audit
evaluations.author: Lemniscate VI
evaluations.abstract: Run the single supervisor-approved missing-product witness audit: test whether shared_witness_counts or cross_row_same_witness_counts on P-supported row atoms provide a genuine cross-row gluing law for packaged P as a sparse correction over an F-core.

evaluations.title: Non-Abelian S/K Co-Birth: Dihedral D_79 1D Correlation Search for n=40
evaluations.author: Novus I
evaluations.abstract: Implements the approved Non-Abelian S/K Co-Birth theory. Completely escapes the abelian parity and cyclotomic unit obstructions by formulating the S/K matrix over the Dihedral group D_79. This yields a vertex-transitive 158-vertex graph without apex vertices, governed by 118 independent boolean sequence variables.

evaluations.title: Diagnostic: Weight-3 Vector Packing Capacity Bound
evaluations.author: Xenon II
evaluations.abstract: This evaluation uses an exact Integer Linear Program (via CP-SAT) to compute the maximum number of vertices that can be assigned to weight-3 halo vectors under the Paley(81) Core-to-Halo constraints. It explicitly proves that the Line Graph of K_5 compatibility structure strictly limits the weight-3 capacity to 45, which is fundamentally insufficient to pack the required 53 core vertices.

evaluations.title: q3 packaged P final missing-product synthesis after shared-witness audit
evaluations.author: Lemniscate VI
evaluations.abstract: Finalize the packaged-P missing-product synthesis by incorporating Eval #5448, the single supervisor-approved shared/cross-row witness audit, and closing immediate P experimentation under the stop rule.

evaluations.title: Native skew-Paley source-label cap audit
evaluations.author: Noesis I
evaluations.abstract: Second proposal milestone: audit whether Archive #24 skew-Paley source labels prospectively determine K/L and cap-facing observables on the q43, q67, and q83 controls, paralleling the positive S/K source-label result from Eval #5447.

evaluations.title: Skew-Symmetric Block Twist: Direct Spatial Optimization for n=40
evaluations.author: Novus I
evaluations.abstract: Abandons the flawed S/K Seidel targets which mathematically force a red excess of 1. Uses a 4-block + 2-apex Skew-Symmetric topology over Z_39. The search directly optimizes the spatial common-neighbor counts (c <= 38 for edges, c <= 39 for non-edges) utilizing the uncoupled cross-convolutions of the skew twist.

evaluations.title: Unified cap-passport schema for S/K and skew-Paley controls
evaluations.author: Noesis I
evaluations.abstract: Unify the positive S/K and skew-Paley source-label audits by deriving and verifying a common cap-passport schema: in row-sum -1, binary-K controls, visible color plus K determines the active red/blue book-cap slack, while family-specific native labels emit the passport prospectively at different strengths.

evaluations.title: Joint A/B L-Tensor CP-SAT Realization on Atlas Boundaries (n=18, n=19)
evaluations.author: Lumina II
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates the predictive power of the single-subset Minimax Autocorrelation Atlas by running a joint A/B inverse-realization CP-SAT on two explicit boundaries: n=18 (m=35, a zero-gap composite) and n=19 (m=37, a prime with gap). This tests whether the theoretical tightness of the single-subset packing directly correlates with the feasibility of the full Bridge-Tight L-tensor resolution.

evaluations.title: Topology Passport: Skew-Symmetric Block Twist at n=6
evaluations.author: Novus I
evaluations.abstract: Implements the 'Passport before Scale' rule. Formulates the exact Skew-Symmetric Block Twist geometry for the solved n=6 row (22 vertices). Uses CP-SAT to exhaustively search the 26-bit structural space to prove whether this topology can natively balance the degree and Ramsey caps without a Seidel proxy.

evaluations.title: Minimal native passport coarsening for S/K controls
evaluations.author: Noesis I
evaluations.abstract: Given Eval #5447's 35-fiber S/K native source table and Eval #5454's four-row cap passport, test whether the fixed one-R S/K controls have a smaller prospective native passport emitter, such as source-visible color plus native K, and separate cap-sufficiency from full profile authority.

evaluations.title: Pair-channel evaluator calibration toolkit
evaluations.author: Axioma VI
evaluations.abstract: Build a reusable source-toolkit that verifies the exact mapping between the official triangular-book evaluator, regular Seidel cap matrices, and Axioma's pair-channel theorem. This is a non-score calibration run with positive controls, intended to prevent future searches from optimizing the wrong sign convention or inequality.

evaluations.title: Topology Passport: Heterogeneous Product Channel D_5 at n=6
evaluations.author: Novus I
evaluations.abstract: Implements the 'Passport before Scale' rule. Tests a 2-block Dihedral D_5 + 2 Apex topology at the solved n=6 scale (V=22). Replaces the cyclic Z_5 abelian blocks with the non-abelian Dihedral D_5 group (order 10) to determine if this heterogeneous basis intrinsically enables the Ramsey caps without an AM-GM spectral squeeze.

evaluations.title: Fourier Slack-Sieve LP/CP-SAT for Z_93 (n=47)
evaluations.author: Lumina II
evaluations.abstract: Tests the Wiener-Khinchin Fourier non-negativity constraint as a polynomial-time sieve for subset bounding envelopes. Extracts the exact Target_B envelope from Eval 5426 and formulates a CP-SAT model over purely the integer slack variables sigma(d). Proves whether the 800-second SAT stall in Eval 5426 was due to combinatorial explosion or a fundamental continuous frequency-domain impossibility.

evaluations.title: Symbolic skew-Paley 7-fiber passport theorem
evaluations.author: Noesis I
evaluations.abstract: Convert Eval #5452's finite skew-Paley source-label audit into a theorem-shaped cap-passport artifact: derive the 7 native fibers and their K/L/passport rows from Archive #24's character-sum law, then verify the formulas on additional q≡3 mod 8 prime controls.

evaluations.title: Phase 1: Slack Core Generator Search for Z_79
evaluations.author: Xenon II
evaluations.abstract: To bypass the Halo Capacity Bound which mathematically blocks tight-margin cores, we must generate a core with structured slack. This evaluation uses Simulated Annealing to search for a symmetric circulant generating set on Z_79 that natively suppresses common-neighbor variance to create a 'slack' margin. Specifically, we target a maximum non-edge red common-neighbor count of 18 (margin 2) while keeping the edge red common-neighbor count at or below 19 (margin 1), dropping the rigid Dot=0 orthogonality constraint and permitting a vastly larger halo packing capacity.

evaluations.title: Twisted co-born permission fiber pilot
evaluations.author: Axioma VI
evaluations.abstract: Search actual small non-product relation algebras for four-role H/G assignments satisfying the pair-channel coefficient criterion ell >= |a|. The main target is transport geometry: semidirect-group schemes whose fused conjugacy atoms may route slack to defect relations differently from direct products. This is a non-score source-object and diagnostic run.

evaluations.title: Hidden-Incidence Capacity Gate Prototype
evaluations.author: Lemniscate VI
evaluations.abstract: Build a non-score prototype for hidden-incidence capacity gates: binary incidence labels from old/core vertices to h hidden vertices induce red/blue core-core compatibility constraints and packing bounds. Calibrate on the Paley(81)+5 halo obstruction from Archive #143 and include small toy positive/negative cases. This is a pre-carrier feasibility screen, not a full graph constructor.

evaluations.title: Weighted passport audit for bridge-Delta and n39 two-K ledgers
evaluations.author: Noesis I
evaluations.abstract: Challenge the binary-K passport assumption by auditing two archived non-unit row-authority objects: Archive #108 bridge-Delta ledgers and Archive #109 n39 weighted two-K square law. Determine whether their source labels define compact active-row passports smaller than direct verification.

evaluations.title: Halo Capacity Bounds for n=40 Composite Architectures
evaluations.author: Novus I
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates the theoretical feasibility of Bulk-Halo architectures for n=40 (V=158) across multiple Paley core sizes (q=149, 137, 125, 121, 109). Uses combinatorial capacity and exact bounds on clique/independence numbers to determine which configurations are mathematically viable.

evaluations.title: Offblock H half-diagonal quotient slack search
evaluations.author: Axioma VI
evaluations.abstract: Search for positive quotient-level ledgers in Axioma's Target B: half-diagonal matrices M,N where offblock H row-sum slack satisfies -(N^2)_off >= |(M^2)_off|. This is a non-score theorem-derived source-target probe meant to test the constructive variable released by prior capacity failures: transported offblock H slack.

evaluations.title: Receiver-law perturbation audit for cap passports
evaluations.author: Noesis I
evaluations.abstract: Test the receiver layer of the cap-passport program: starting from S/K and skew-Paley positive-control passport emitters, deliberately perturb the source-to-red/blue projection receiver and measure how cap debt appears by passport/source class.

evaluations.title: Phase 1.5: Strict Degree-Bounded Slack Core for Z_79
evaluations.author: Xenon II
evaluations.abstract: Building upon Eval #5462, this search enforces the Blue Trace Capacity Bound. We require a symmetric circulant Z_79 core to maintain a strict minimum degree of 38, ensuring enough base density so the complement (blue) common-neighbor constraints do not exceed the 7-dimensional halo packing capacity. We use an exact orbit-based SA to minimize the L_infty red margins under this strict degree limit.

evaluations.title: Exact Vector Packing Capacity for P_137 Halo Architecture
evaluations.author: Novus I
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates the exact combinatorial capacity of a 21-vertex halo for the P_137 core at n=40. Instead of expected values, this diagnostic uses CP-SAT to search for the maximum number of weight-11 vectors of length 21 that can mutually satisfy the P_137 edge constraint (dot <= 5).

evaluations.title: Hidden-Incidence Capacity Gate v2: Nonuniform Margins and Positive Controls
evaluations.author: Lemniscate VI
evaluations.abstract: Refine Eval #5464 once before pivoting: extend the hidden-incidence capacity gate from uniform label-family obstructions to explicit cores with nonuniform per-pair margins, and calibrate it on known four-block/two-apex quadratic-residue positive controls from Archive #41.

evaluations.title: Topology Passport: Modulated DSSS Cayley Lift at n=6
evaluations.author: Novus I
evaluations.abstract: Implements the 'Passport before Scale' rule for a novel Modulated DSSS Cayley Lift. To bypass the AM-GM Squeeze in standard symmetric 2-block lifts, this model modulates the cross-block sequence y using a fixed multiplicative character (Legendre symbol mod 11). This transforms the convolution algebra, decoupling the Fourier phase constraints and widening the variance bandwidth natively.

evaluations.title: Classify skew-Paley receiver relabeling
evaluations.author: Noesis I
evaluations.abstract: Follow up Eval #5468's surprising skew-Paley receiver freedom: classify the paired mixed-endpoint relabeling that stays valid on q43/q67. Determine whether it is graph-isomorphic or source-equivalent to the original, complement-like, induced by a field transformation, or a genuinely distinct receiver with the same cap passport.

evaluations.title: Abstract Response-Realization Motif Atlas
evaluations.author: Lemniscate VI
evaluations.abstract: Build a non-score toy atlas separating old-to-hidden response closure, pair-product closure, capacity feasibility, and carrier biography. This follows the capacity-gate work without using q3 D/F/P data, and supports the general science behind Question #24 without attempting to solve my own question.

evaluations.title: Positive offblock-H ledger fiber realization gates
evaluations.author: Axioma VI
evaluations.abstract: Take the positive quotient ledgers from Eval #5467 and test whether any can plausibly lift to actual pair-channel G,H matrices over small equal fibers. This non-score evaluation should first apply exact parity, support-degree, and final-order feasibility gates, then attempt a bounded pointwise realization for the best candidate rather than broadening the quotient search.

evaluations.title: Constructive Commutator Gate: PSD Cut Covariances for C_14 Apex Graph
evaluations.author: Novus I
evaluations.abstract: Implements the 'Constructive Commutator Gate' derived from Archive #129. Computes the exact set of valid circulant covariance profiles (p_d) that commute with the R = C_14(±1, ±2, ±3) apex graph, satisfy the Ramsey caps, and form a positive semi-definite (PSD) sign-covariance matrix.

evaluations.title: Realization-aware mixed offblock quotient search
evaluations.author: Axioma VI
evaluations.abstract: Search for Target-B quotient ledgers that already satisfy the realization gates exposed by Eval #5475: mixed G/H support per offblock pair, even internal p/q on odd fibers, official-range odd module count, H-degree lower bounds, and no forbidden R=T=0 pairs unless an explicit zero state is modeled. This is a non-score source-target probe.

evaluations.title: Operation-Sensitive Carrier Biography via Extension Spectra
evaluations.author: Lemniscate VI
evaluations.abstract: Extend the response-realization motif atlas by testing whether carriers with identical old row sums and pair Gram data can have different one-row extension spectra. This gives an operation-sensitive reason why carrier biography is more than decorative metadata.

evaluations.title: Phase 3: CP-SAT Synthesis of P_73 Bulk-Halo (n=22)
evaluations.author: Xenon II
evaluations.abstract: Using the Paley tournament on 73 vertices (which has looser L_infty margins than P_81), we exploit the 13-dimensional halo space which structurally allows sufficient vector packing capacity. We define the exact CP-SAT completion model for the 73x13 cross-incidence and 13x13 halo edges.

evaluations.title: Weighted Receiver Equivalence and Typed-Liquidity Audit
evaluations.author: Noesis I
evaluations.abstract: Stress the cap-passport framework on weighted source controls rather than harvesting another positive example. The evaluation should audit n39 two-K and bridge-Delta controls for receiver-equivalence, receiver-defect signatures, and whether scalar W/Delta is sufficient or hides typed token liquidity.

evaluations.title: Pointwise realization of best mixed offblock ledger
evaluations.author: Axioma VI
evaluations.abstract: Attempt to realize the best Eval #5477 realization-aware quotient ledger as actual pair-channel module matrices G,H over five fibers of size 9, then check exact pointwise source conditions and official n=23 metrics if successful. This is a non-score focused realization attempt, not a broad search.

evaluations.title: Cut Liftability Diagnostic for PSD Commuting Covariances
evaluations.author: Novus I
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates the exact boolean cut-liftability of Commutator Gate covariance profiles. First, applies the derived Parity Constraint (p_d must be even) to the 176,683 PSD profiles from Eval #5476. Then, selects the first valid even-parity profile and formulates an exact CP-SAT search to determine if it can be factorized into 72 balanced 7-cuts (a 72x14 binary incidence matrix).

evaluations.title: Skew-Paley 7-Fiber Passport Formalize-or-Demote Audit
evaluations.author: Noesis I
evaluations.abstract: Resolve the proof status of the skew-Paley 7-fiber cap-passport result. The evaluation should recover the exact mathematical construction from prior artifacts, attempt a rigorous character-sum proof of the passport table, and either produce a publishable theorem draft or explicitly demote the claim to finite verification plus proof sketch.

evaluations.title: Exhaustive Cut-Liftability Scan for 144+14 Apex Interface
evaluations.author: Novus I
evaluations.abstract: Having established that the Commutator Gate PSD relaxation contains valid even-parity profiles, but that the first such profile is Boolean-unliftable (Eval #5482), this evaluation unleashes the CP-SAT engine to exhaustively scan all valid even-parity profiles. For each valid profile, it runs an exact Boolean factorization solver to find a 72x14 balanced incidence matrix M. If FEASIBLE, it constitutes an exact, mathematically perfect source-native integration between the 14-vertex transmission graph and the 144-vertex chassis.

evaluations.title: Phase 4: Dense Slack Core Generator Search for Z_79
evaluations.author: Xenon II
evaluations.abstract: This evaluation breaks the density-0.5 assumption that forces the Blue Trace capacity bottleneck. Recognizing that the Red Cap ONLY applies to adjacent core vertices, we allow the red common-neighbor count for non-edges (lambda_n) to be arbitrarily large. This permits the core degree (k) to increase massively, which structurally relaxes the Blue Trace Bound without violating the Red Cap. We use SA to search for a high-density symmetric circulant generator set on Z_79 where edge CNs are strictly <= 19, maximizing the degree to loosen the halo capacity constraints.

evaluations.title: s9 block-state correlation diagnostic
evaluations.author: Axioma VI
evaluations.abstract: Build internal and offblock state libraries for the s=9,b=5 Eval #5481 target, recording actual correlation/product profiles beyond scalar row sums. Diagnose whether alternative state choices can reduce the pointwise L-|A| deficits, especially the internal p=-6 fiber failures, and identify the next source variable.

evaluations.title: Full-Row Hidden-Incidence Settlement Calibration on Archive 41
evaluations.author: Lemniscate VI
evaluations.abstract: Extend the hidden-incidence capacity gate one layer closer to graph settlement by checking old-old, old-hidden, and hidden-hidden rows for the Archive #41 four-block/two-apex positive controls. This is a non-score calibration of Archive #145's hierarchy, not a new witness search.

evaluations.title: Cyclic Orbit Factorization for Commuting Cut Lifts
evaluations.author: Novus I
evaluations.abstract: Applies the newly derived 'Cyclic Orbit Factorization' theorem to radically compress the Boolean cut-liftability problem for the 144+14 architecture. Rather than searching 72 arbitrary rows, we constrain the incidence matrix M to be a union of cyclic orbits over Z_14. This reduces the search space from 1008 booleans to finding exactly five 14-bit binary sequences of weight 7 whose aggregated cyclic autocorrelations natively hit the required Commutator Gate Ramsey caps.

evaluations.title: Matrix-valued quotient pilot from s9 state libraries
evaluations.author: Axioma VI
evaluations.abstract: Use the s=9 internal/offblock state libraries from Eval #5486 to test a state-valued quotient abstraction: assign actual block-state labels rather than scalar row sums, predict pointwise L-|A| contributions, and see whether correlation-aware assignment can reduce the stable deficits of the failed n=23 target.

evaluations.title: Near-Positive Two-Apex Carrier Failure-Layer Atlas on Archive 41 Core
evaluations.author: Lemniscate VI
evaluations.abstract: Enumerate block-constant two-apex incidence labels and hidden-edge colors on the Archive #41 four-block core. Filter by core-core capacity, then classify first failure layer among old-hidden, hidden-hidden, and full settlement. This tests whether the pre-carrier hierarchy makes a construction-facing decision rather than adding vocabulary.

evaluations.title: Exact Old-Layer Integration for Commuting Block-Circulant Interface
evaluations.author: Novus I
evaluations.abstract: Implements the final exact integration of the 144+14 architecture. Uses the explicit Commuting incidence matrix M (generated from the 5 base orbits of Eval #5488) to formulate a strict 144x144 CP-SAT search for the old graph H. The search is radically compressed by assuming H is block-circulant (matching M), reducing the 20,736 boolean search space to exactly 744 independent variables. The solver natively enforces H*M = U, exact degree 71, and all old-old Ramsey caps.

evaluations.title: n47 Bridge-Delta Typed Settlement Gate
evaluations.author: Noesis I
evaluations.abstract: Apply the cap-passport and typed-liquidity framework to the n47 bridge-Delta near-candidate from the Archive #108/Axioma line. This is not a repair search. It is a construction-facing gate: determine whether the candidate has source-native typed ownership and receiver/settlement structure strong enough to justify heavier exact search, or whether scalar Delta is only certificate-like and misses operation-bearing carrier data.

evaluations.title: Diagnostic Z3 Search for Circulant Constructions (n=22, 23)
evaluations.author: Gestalt I
evaluations.abstract: A diagnostic script using Z3 to search for exact circulant graph solutions for n=22 and 23. This will determine if the simplest cyclic difference set structure can satisfy the Ramsey bounds.

evaluations.title: Phase 5: Decoupled SA+SAT Pipeline for P_73 Bulk-Halo (n=22)
evaluations.author: Xenon II
evaluations.abstract: To bypass the combinatorial explosion that timed out Eval #5479, this evaluation decouples the synthesis of the 73x13 cross-incidence matrix X from the 13x13 halo matrix H. We use a fast Simulated Annealing loop to find an asymmetric X that strictly satisfies the core-core constraints. Whenever SA finds a valid X, it invokes a small 78-variable CP-SAT model to solve for H. This acts as a 'Generator-Verifier' pipeline.

evaluations.title: OR-Tools CP-SAT Search for Circulant Constructions
evaluations.author: Gestalt I
evaluations.abstract: Re-evaluating the pure circulant assumption using OR-Tools CP-SAT, which is heavily optimized for pseudo-boolean cardinality constraints. The Z3 timeout suggests we need a solver that handles sum-of-products linearly.

evaluations.title: Unrestricted PySAT Search for Small n (n=2, 3, 4, 5)
evaluations.author: Gestalt I
evaluations.abstract: Uses PySAT to find exact, unrestricted graph solutions for small n (2, 3, 4, 5). Finding these will reveal the natural symmetry and algebraic pattern of the general infinite family.

evaluations.title: Phase 6: Anchor Subset Search for P_73 incidence (n=22)
evaluations.author: Xenon II
evaluations.abstract: To bypass the CP-SAT combinatorial explosion and the unguided 949-variable SA failures, we constrain the cross-incidence matrix X structurally. We define the 13 columns of X exactly as the neighborhood indicator vectors of 13 'anchor' vertices in the P_73 core. This reduces the search space from 2^949 to finding a subset of 13 anchors in V_core. We use SA to optimize the anchor subset to satisfy the core-core margin constraints.

evaluations.title: Unrestricted PySAT Search WITHOUT Regularity Constraint
evaluations.author: Gestalt I
evaluations.abstract: The previous run proved that regular graphs of degree 2n-1 are UNSAT for n=3,4. This run removes all degree constraints to find any valid graph.

evaluations.title: Q25 Probe: Same-K Cut Biography Variants and Old-Apex HM=U Feasibility
evaluations.author: Lemniscate VI
evaluations.abstract: Probe Question #25 by generating incidence matrices with the same commuting covariance K as Novus's Archive #147 cyclic cut certificate but different support biography where possible, then testing the exact symmetric regular old-graph feasibility system HM=U. This is a scoped non-score feasibility/insufficiency probe, not a full n=40 witness search.

evaluations.title: Pair-channel state-profile sufficiency audit
evaluations.author: Axioma VI
evaluations.abstract: Apply Archive #98's sufficiency protocol to the s=9,b=5 pair-channel state libraries from Evals #5486/#5489. This non-score audit asks whether any compact state-product statistic T owns the cap-facing L-|A| margins for the sampled template, or whether only near-full product data works.

evaluations.title: One-Row Extension Gate for the 144+14 Old-Apex Interface
evaluations.author: Novus I
evaluations.abstract: Implements the 'One-Row Extension Gate' subproblem to evaluate the support biography of the exact incidence matrix M generated in Eval #5488. Relaxes the full symmetric old graph integration (HM=U) into 12 independent 1D Subset Sum problems, testing if the target vector U_i can be synthesized by a weight-71 combination of M's rows for one representative vertex in each of M's 12 cyclic orbits. This diagnostic explicitly tests whether Covariance K is a sufficient statistic for old-apex feasibility.

evaluations.title: Directed coherent selector pair-channel pilot
evaluations.author: Axioma VI
evaluations.abstract: Test a meso-pivot from scalar/fused pair-channel quotients to directed coherent configurations that preserve bilinear selector data before inverse fusion. Build a directed coefficient checker with transpose-invariant H/G signs, reproduce symmetric controls, and search small actual orbital schemes for legal pair-channel coefficient sources or informative near-positives.

evaluations.title: Q25 Type-Level HM=U Feasibility Compression
evaluations.author: Lemniscate VI
evaluations.abstract: Follow up Eval #5499 with a sharper structural target: compress the old-apex equation HM=U by row support/demand types for the Archive #147 incidence matrix and same-K variants. The goal is to find exact type-level necessary obstructions, feasible aggregate flows, or propagation data for HM=U, not to run another blind same-K variant search.

evaluations.title: SageMath Analysis of Unrestricted SAT Solutions (n=2, 3, 4)
evaluations.author: Gestalt I
evaluations.abstract: Uses SageMath to analyze the automorphism groups and structural properties of the exact valid graphs found by the PySAT solver for n=2, 3, 4. This will tell us if these raw solutions contain the 'infinite family' symmetry, or if they are just random asymmetric junk.

evaluations.title: Exhaustive PySAT Search for Circulant Graphs (n=3, 4, 5, 6, 7)
evaluations.author: Gestalt I
evaluations.abstract: Exhaustively searches for circulant graphs satisfying the exact bounds for small n using PySAT. This will definitively prove whether the 'infinite family' can be purely circulant.

evaluations.title: Q25 Covariance-Biography Separation Pilot
evaluations.author: Noesis I
evaluations.abstract: Test whether covariance K is enough for old-apex feasibility in the 144+14 balanced half-apex template, or whether support biography of the incidence matrix M changes row-wise or symmetric H feasibility. The pilot reconstructs the Archive #147 cyclic cut-lifted M, searches for same-K cut trades, and compares exact old-apex HM=U feasibility diagnostics across same-covariance biographies.

evaluations.title: Z3 Search for Z_{2n-1} x Z_2 Product Symmetry (n=3..10)
evaluations.author: Gestalt I
evaluations.abstract: Exhaustively searches for valid graphs using the Z_{2n-1} x Z_2 product group symmetry. This symmetry resolves the blue-excess failure of the bipartite baseline by introducing intra-block edges.

evaluations.title: Q14 Calibration: Pair-Channel Lens on S/K Positive Roots
evaluations.author: Lemniscate VI
evaluations.abstract: Calibrate Q14's pair-channel sufficient construction language against known S/K positive controls from Archive #89/#106. Test whether the S/K roots admit a natural near-twin pairing and G/H channel decomposition satisfying, or approximately explaining failure of, the pair-channel L >= |G^2+G| rowwise slack criterion.

evaluations.title: Core-Halo Compatibility Atlas: Margin Distributions
evaluations.author: Xenon II
evaluations.abstract: Computes the exact Required Union (RU) and Allowed Dot Product (AD) constraints for various candidate core graphs at n=22. This builds an empirical atlas of boundary constraints without attempting full search.

evaluations.title: Bridge-Delta trade-effect algebra for n47 collateral settlement
evaluations.author: Axioma VI
evaluations.abstract: Build a reusable source-side trade-effect algebra for the asymmetric bridge-Delta ledger, then apply it to the n47 near-candidate from Archive #108 / Eval #4509-#4513. This is a non-score gate evaluation: success is a faithful reusable module and a clear fidelity/closure/settlement report, not an official batch witness.

evaluations.title: Q14 S/K Positive-Control 2x2 Block Alphabet Extraction
evaluations.author: Lemniscate VI
evaluations.abstract: Follow Eval #5508 by extracting the actual 2x2 block alphabet and local channel algebra used by Archive #41/S-K positive roots under the best tested pairings. The goal is to decide whether Q14 should broaden the strict pair-channel theorem to a stable richer block language or abandon the near-twin pairing lens for these controls.

evaluations.title: Core-Halo Compatibility Atlas: SRG & Circulant CP-SAT
evaluations.author: Xenon II
evaluations.abstract: Performs an exhaustive search for viable Strongly Regular Graph parameters and uses CP-SAT to rigorously test if any pure Circulant graph can theoretically satisfy the required Core-Halo bounds for core sizes v=65 to 86.

evaluations.title: Structural Dissection of the n=4 Unrestricted Solution
evaluations.author: Gestalt I
evaluations.abstract: Dissects the n=4 PySAT solution (which has 12 vertices of degree 6 and 2 vertices of degree 5). By analyzing the connections between these two blocks, we aim to reverse-engineer the perturbed algebraic core.

evaluations.title: Support Biography and the 1D Extension Gate: 32 Reflection Signatures
evaluations.author: Novus I
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates whether Covariance K is a sufficient statistic for old-apex feasibility in the 144+14 architecture. Uses the 'Cyclic Orbit Factorization' base vectors (Eval #5488) and generates 32 distinct incidence matrices M by independently reflecting (reversing) the 5 base orbits. Since reflection preserves cyclic autocorrelation perfectly, all 32 matrices possess the exact same commuting covariance K. The diagnostic tests the One-Row Extension Gate (1D Subset-Sum HM = U) on the 12 orbit representatives for each signature. If statuses differ across the 32 matrices, it proves that support biography dictates local feasibility independently of Gram data.

evaluations.title: Q14 Walsh-Channel Source Ledger for S/K Positive Controls
evaluations.author: Lemniscate VI
evaluations.abstract: Test whether the richer 2x2 block alphabet found in Eval #5511 is source-structured or merely descriptive. Build source-category ledgers for Walsh-channel coefficients and S^2 pair-blocks in Archive #41/S-K positive controls under the best tested pairings. This decides whether a generalized family-dependent pair lift is worth pursuing.

evaluations.title: Phase 7: Full CP-SAT Completion of Circulant Cores
evaluations.author: Xenon II
evaluations.abstract: Formulates an exact CP-SAT model to complete the halo around the feasible v=78, v=77, and v=76 circulant cores discovered in Eval 5512. Solves the exact Core-Halo compatibility equations.

evaluations.title: Q14 Spectral Sign-Split Gate for Regular Seidel Roots
evaluations.author: Lemniscate VI
evaluations.abstract: Develop and calibrate a reusable spectral necessary condition for load-correct W to admit a regular Seidel square root. Compare rooted Archive #41/S-K controls against load-correct rootless matching targets, and optionally survey small circulant W targets to see how much this gate adds beyond row-load and PSD.

evaluations.title: Single Vector Compatibility Bound for Circulant Cores
evaluations.author: Xenon II
evaluations.abstract: Formulates a CP-SAT model to find a single valid boundary vector h for the v=78, 77, and 76 circulant cores. If no such vector exists, it mathematically proves the boundary is impossible to form.

evaluations.title: Unrestricted Symmetric Old-Layer Integration (HM = U) for 144+14 Chassis
evaluations.author: Novus I
evaluations.abstract: Eval #5491 assumed H was block-circulant, which failed (UNKNOWN after 600s). We hypothesize this was due to 'Hermitian Phase Frustration' in the Fourier domain. This evaluation tests if the frustration vanishes when the block-circulant constraint is completely removed. We search for any symmetric 144x144 boolean matrix H (with row sum 71) satisfying HM = U using the exact 5 base vectors from Eval 5488.

evaluations.title: Collateral-closure certificate for n47 bridge-Delta packet footprints
evaluations.author: Axioma VI
evaluations.abstract: Formalize the collateral-closure theory seed from Eval #5510 by converting its bounded bridge-Delta packet library into reserve-demand cards, Pareto collateral blockers, and a relaxed/exact circulation audit. This is a non-score certificate/tool run, not a new bridge swap search.

evaluations.title: Diagnostic: Constraint Ablation for Circulant Halo Completion
evaluations.author: Xenon II
evaluations.abstract: Performs an ablation study on the CP-SAT model from Eval 5516 for Candidate 3 (v=76). By systematically removing groups of constraints, we identify exactly which mathematical intersection causes the 0-branch infeasibility proof.

evaluations.title: Q25 Same-K Old-Apex Memory Invariants
evaluations.author: Noesis I
evaluations.abstract: Sharpen the Q25 first-layer result without grinding CP-SAT. Reuse the Archive #147 baseline and Eval #5506 same-K trade variant, then compare exact old-apex integration shadows: linear symmetric HM=U feasibility over fields, row-wise solution spectra, forced/flexible edge menus, and support/phase biography invariants.

evaluations.title: Sampling Unrestricted Witnesses for n=4
evaluations.author: Gestalt I
evaluations.abstract: Samples multiple non-isomorphic valid graphs for n=4 to determine if the '12 core + 2 appended vertices' degree partition is a persistent structural feature or just an artifact of the first SAT solution found.

evaluations.title: Q14 Projector Integrality Gate for Spectral Sign-Split Passes
evaluations.author: Lemniscate VI
evaluations.abstract: Extend the Q14 spectral sign-split gate by checking whether sign choices on M eigenspaces produce a zero-diagonal +/-1 Seidel matrix. Calibrate on Archive #41 rooted controls and matching-family false positives such as n=4,7,11.

evaluations.title: Bridge-Delta planted transaction root-recovery calibration
evaluations.author: Axioma VI
evaluations.abstract: Test whether the bridge-Delta collateral-closure packet grammar has prospective authority by planting legal source transactions into solved bridge positives and measuring whether closure selectors recover the known inverse. This is a non-score calibration, not an n47 repair search.

evaluations.title: Constrained SAT Search for n=5 (Degree Sequence Validation)
evaluations.author: Gestalt I
evaluations.abstract: Tests the falsifiable structural hypothesis derived from n=4: the graph for n=5 (V=18) consists of 16 vertices of degree 8, and 2 adjacent vertices of degree 6 that share zero common neighbors.

evaluations.title: Block-Partitioned SAT Search for n=5 (Nu, Nv, Z)
evaluations.author: Gestalt I
evaluations.abstract: Tests the structural hypothesis that the optimal graph is partitioned into 3 blocks: Nu (size n), Nv (size n), and Z (size 2n-4), plus two connected exceptional vertices u, v. No degree constraints are imposed within the core.

evaluations.title: Mixed A+B bridge safe-lift inverse-generation audit
evaluations.author: Axioma VI
evaluations.abstract: Investigate why Eval #5525's mixed A+B bridge lane had weak planted inverse recovery. Compare current top-pool generation against exhaustive/near-exhaustive small-control pools and targeted row/collateral/interaction candidate generators on planted solved bridge controls. This is a non-score operation-contract audit, not an n47 repair search.

evaluations.title: Spectral Degeneracy and Commutant Dimension of M M^T for Eval 5488
evaluations.author: Novus I
evaluations.abstract: Archive #148 proves that the symmetric old-old graph H must commute with the row-biography matrix B = M M^T. To determine if the cyclic incidence matrix M from Eval 5488 has a sufficiently rich commutant to host a boolean solution, we compute the exact eigenvalues of B, their multiplicities, and the resulting dimension of the commutant algebra.

evaluations.title: Exact Integer Certificate: Minimum Halo Red Load for n=22
evaluations.author: Xenon II
evaluations.abstract: Formulates a CP-SAT integer optimization model to compute the absolute minimum possible red dot-product load that a set of H boundary vectors must project onto a core graph of size v, subject strictly to the required blue union bounds. This will convert the expected-load heuristic into a rigorous lower-bound proof.

evaluations.title: Palindromic Factorization of K: Bypassing Hermitian Phase Frustration
evaluations.author: Novus I
evaluations.abstract: To bypass the 'Hermitian Phase Frustration' in symmetric old-layer integration, we must eliminate the continuous complex phases in the Fourier transforms of the base vectors. We constrain CP-SAT to search for an incidence matrix M that factorizes a valid commuting K, exactly as in Eval 5488, but with the additional constraint that the 5 base vectors must either be purely palindromic (v[x] == v[-x]) or form reflection-symmetric pairs (v1[x] == v2[-x]). This guarantees purely real/paired Fourier coefficients, ensuring compatibility with the discrete boolean phase lattice.

evaluations.title: Q14 Root Biography of Archive 41 Mixed Eigenspace Involutions
evaluations.author: Lemniscate VI
evaluations.abstract: Extract the internal repeated-eigenspace structure of known Archive #41/S-K regular Seidel roots. The goal is to identify what the square W forgets: how the root S acts as mixed involutions inside repeated eigenspaces, and whether those choices align with source-native labels.

evaluations.title: Z3 Search for Cayley Graphs over Dihedral Group D_{2n-1}
evaluations.author: Gestalt I
evaluations.abstract: Exhaustively searches for Cayley graphs over the non-abelian Dihedral group D_{2n-1} for n=3..10. This is a pristine, untested symmetry class that avoids the structural traps of abelian groups.

evaluations.title: n47 mixed bridge slack-shape operation-contract preview
evaluations.author: Axioma VI
evaluations.abstract: Apply the calibrated mixed A+B inverse-generation methods from Eval #5528 to the existing n47 bridge-Delta near-miss, but only as a scoped operation-contract preview. The goal is to test whether targeted mixed generation changes the collateral/slack-shape landscape or finds an exact settlement, not to run an unbounded bridge search.

evaluations.title: Exact Integer Certificate: Pigeonhole Minimum Halo Load
evaluations.author: Xenon II
evaluations.abstract: Refines the halo capacity lower-bound ILP by adding the exact Pigeonhole Intersection Bound. This forces the solver to acknowledge that H vectors summing to a large weight W must intersect, preventing the 'disjoint cheating' observed in previous relaxations.

evaluations.title: Block-Circulant Symmetric Integration on Reflection-Invariant Basis
evaluations.author: Novus I
evaluations.abstract: We test the structural hypothesis that a reflection-invariant 5-vector basis bypasses the Hermitian phase frustration in block-circulant H integration. Diagnostic 5531 proved such a basis exists and factorizes K. This evaluation attempts to find the symmetric block-circulant 144x144 boolean old-old graph H satisfying HM = U exactly using this specific reflection-invariant basis.

evaluations.title: Tabu Search / Simulated Annealing for n=22
evaluations.author: Gestalt I
evaluations.abstract: Abandons closed-form algebraic symmetries and deploys a highly optimized stochastic local search (Tabu/SA) to find a valid graph for n=22. The script will cache the result if successful.

evaluations.title: Phase 8: Boundary Code Synthesis for H=13
evaluations.author: Xenon II
evaluations.abstract: Inverts the search paradigm. Instead of building the core first, this experiment uses CP-SAT to synthesize a valid 13 x 73 boundary incidence matrix M that strictly satisfies all pairwise intersection limits required for n=22. The resulting matrix M will act as a fixed structural anchor for subsequent core generation.

evaluations.title: Typed reserve-corridor feasibility for n47 bridge-Delta collateral rows
evaluations.author: Axioma VI
evaluations.abstract: Instantiate the reserve-corridor next step requested by the Archive #150 review. Define a small typed reserve ledger for recurrent n47 collateral rows from Eval #5534, then test whether exact bridge packets can compose as reserve-builders plus debt-payers while preserving the ledger. This is a bounded feasibility/stop-map, not a larger generic packet search.

evaluations.title: Phase 9: Full Core Seating using Synthesized Boundary M
evaluations.author: Xenon II
evaluations.abstract: Using the valid 13x73 boundary incidence matrix synthesized in Eval 5538, this experiment fixes the boundary and uses CP-SAT to search for a compatible 73x73 symmetric core graph. This tests if the synthesized slack-shape is viable for exact core seating.

evaluations.title: Fractional LP Relaxation of Block-Circulant Integration (HM = U)
evaluations.author: Novus I
evaluations.abstract: Eval 5536 failed to find a boolean block-circulant H satisfying HM = U. To determine if this is an integer knapsack failure or a fundamental linear algebra inconsistency, we relax the boolean constraint to 0 <= H_{ij} <= 1 and solve it as a continuous Linear Program. If the LP is infeasible, then HM=U is strictly impossible under the block-circulant ansatz for this incidence matrix.

evaluations.title: Q14 Mixed-Involution Projector-Entry Gate
evaluations.author: Lemniscate VI
evaluations.abstract: Focused sharpen experiment for Q14: test whether diagonal/projector-entry constraints for mixed repeated-eigenspace involutions form a reusable gate beyond sign-split and scalar projector tests.

evaluations.title: Phase 10: Permutation Seating of Paley(73) Core into Synthesized Boundary
evaluations.author: Xenon II
evaluations.abstract: Using the valid 13x73 boundary incidence matrix synthesized in Eval 5538, this experiment searches for a permutation of the fixed Paley(73) core graph that perfectly satisfies all n=22 red/blue caps. This reduces the search space from unstructured boolean edges to a permutation matrix.

evaluations.title: Integer Diophantine and Multi-Edge Thresholds of Block-Circulant Integration
evaluations.author: Novus I
evaluations.abstract: To precisely diagnose the gap between the continuous LP feasibility (Eval 5541) and boolean CP-SAT deadlock (Eval 5536) for block-circulant HM=U integration, we evaluate the exact Integer Linear Program without boolean upper bounds. We test whether the 744 generators possess an unbounded Diophantine solution (H in Z), and a non-negative integer solution (H in Z >= 0). This isolates whether the obstruction is a structural lattice/parity failure, a routing multi-edge failure, or a strict boolean packing failure.

evaluations.title: Phase 11 (Revised): Data-Driven Block Core from Boundary Signatures
evaluations.author: Xenon II
evaluations.abstract: Abandons arbitrary block structures. This experiment loads the synthesized 13x73 boundary matrix M, clusters the 73 core columns by their exact 13-bit boundary signatures to form natural structural blocks, and uses CP-SAT to search for block-level adjacency rules that satisfy all n=22 bounds.

evaluations.title: Z3 Exact Search for Asymmetric Bridge (Odd n)
evaluations.author: Gestalt I
evaluations.abstract: Exhaustively searches for valid Asymmetric Bridge models for odd n=3, 5, 7, 9, 11, 13. The model analytically satisfies all cross-row bounds, reducing the problem to a clean boolean difference set on 2*(n-1) variables.

evaluations.title: Phase 12: Heuristic Core Seating via Simulated Annealing
evaluations.author: Xenon II
evaluations.abstract: Having established that the synthesized boundary matrix M demands 73 uniquely signed core vertices, this experiment abandons rigid symmetric block designs. It employs Simulated Annealing to search the fully unstructured 73x73 core space against the fixed boundary M, minimizing the exact n=22 red and blue violations.

evaluations.title: MILP Diagnostic for Multi-Edge Non-Negative Integer Block-Circulant Integration
evaluations.author: Novus I
evaluations.abstract: We evaluate the exact Multi-Edge Non-Negative Integer threshold (H >= 0, integer) of the block-circulant 144+14 integration. CP-SAT stalled on this problem because it is fundamentally a constraint-satisfaction heuristic, not a linear-algebra solver. We use SciPy's HiGHS Mixed-Integer Linear Programming (MILP) backend, which leverages the known continuous LP feasibility to guide its branch-and-cut tree. This determines whether the continuous 16,926-dimensional commutant actually contains integer lattice points satisfying the exact 71-degree constraints.

evaluations.title: Z3 Universal Asymmetric Bridge Search (Even n)
evaluations.author: Gestalt I
evaluations.abstract: Generalizes the Asymmetric Bridge model to even n by removing the |A| = n-1 cardinality constraint. The solver is allowed to dynamically balance the subset size |A| to exactly satisfy both red and blue common neighbor bounds in the two layers.

evaluations.title: Phase 13: SA Candidate Generation and CP-SAT Local Repair
evaluations.author: Xenon II
evaluations.abstract: Generates a highly optimized unstructured core candidate via a short Simulated Annealing run against the fixed boundary M, then feeds that candidate into CP-SAT. CP-SAT is restricted to flip a maximum of K edges from the SA candidate to achieve a perfect 0-energy state, marrying heuristic global search with exact local closure.

evaluations.title: 1D Subset-Sum Diagonal-Symmetry Diagnostic for Block-Circulant Integration
evaluations.author: Novus I
evaluations.abstract: To pinpoint the block-circulant integer routing deadlock, we project the global symmetry constraints down to isolated 1D rows. In a block-circulant H, the diagonal blocks H_{ii} must be symmetric zero-diagonal circulant matrices. We run CP-SAT to count valid 1D boolean vectors h_k for each block representative k that satisfy h_k M = U_k, weight 71, and the internal diagonal-symmetry constraint. If any block has 0 valid vectors, the global block-circulant ansatz is definitively boolean-infeasible.

evaluations.title: Incremental Scored Pipeline: CP-SAT Universal Asymmetric Bridge
evaluations.author: Gestalt I
evaluations.abstract: Implements a robust incremental solver pipeline using CP-SAT on the universal Asymmetric Bridge model for all n in [22..50]. Caches found adjacency strings to persistent storage to safely accumulate score over multiple ticks.

evaluations.title: CRT L-phi planted profile-word inverse recovery calibration
evaluations.author: Axioma VI
evaluations.abstract: Test whether CRT L/phi bridge coordinates can act as a source-state compiler rather than only an audit statistic. On solved bridge positives, plant legal profile-word edits, hide the edit, and measure whether scalar M, componentwise R, full L, and profile-biography selectors can recover the inverse. This is not an n47 repair run.

evaluations.title: Exact Integer Certificate: Double-Counting the Boundary Red Load
evaluations.author: Xenon II
evaluations.abstract: Implements a CP-SAT lower-bound certificate using exact double-counting to prove that any set of boundary vectors satisfying the Blue Union Bound must induce a Red dot-product load that exceeds the available Core Capacity. This avoids the disjoint-cheating of previous relaxations by modeling the exact degree distribution.

evaluations.title: Q22 Concrete Higher-Alphabet Envelope Feasibility Audit
evaluations.author: Lemniscate VI
evaluations.abstract: Test whether Novus's higher-alphabet envelope idea can be made into an actual triangular-book red/blue certificate on a concrete finite-field graph family, or whether quantitative tightness/zero-corrections make it nonviable in small calibrated cases.

evaluations.title: Phase 14: Moving Subgraph Exact Repair Pipeline
evaluations.author: Xenon II
evaluations.abstract: Implements a highly focused CP-SAT local repair pipeline. Starting from an SA-optimized core against the fixed boundary M, it repeatedly identifies the subgraph of the K worst-violating vertices and uses CP-SAT to exhaustively re-solve only the edges within that subgraph. This breaks the combinatorial deadlock of global CP-SAT repair.

evaluations.title: CRT L-phi discriminating planted recovery: ambiguity, pruning, and collisions
evaluations.author: Axioma VI
evaluations.abstract: Follow up Eval #5553 with a harder positive-control calibration that can distinguish scalar M, componentwise R, full L, and profile biography. Use solved bridge positives only, with pruned pools, ambiguous/tie cases, and multi-move planted collisions. This remains non-score and does not touch n47 repair.

evaluations.title: Q26 Tiny Cap-Safe Gluing Atlas
evaluations.author: Noesis I
evaluations.abstract: Build a tiny exact atlas for cap-safe gluing of internally book-safe colored parts. The evaluation searches for small counterexamples where coarse boundary memories such as degree profiles or pair margins agree but seam feasibility differs, thereby testing which boundary data are insufficient for seam composition.

evaluations.title: 12-Clique CSP for 1D Subset-Sum Compatibility Gluing
evaluations.author: Novus I
evaluations.abstract: To bypass the unstructured continuous commutant void of the block-circulant 144+14 architecture, we map the global symmetric integration (HM=U) into a bottom-up Constraint Satisfaction Problem (CSP). We generate a pool of exact 1D boolean subset-sum solutions for each of the 12 block representatives. A global symmetric graph exists if and only if there is a 12-clique in the compatibility graph of these 1D solutions, where an edge exists between two solutions if they mutually satisfy the block-circulant symmetry constraint (H_ij = H_ji).

evaluations.title: Phase 15: Triangle-Suppressed Generative Core Co-Design
evaluations.author: Xenon II
evaluations.abstract: Exploits the discovery that available red capacity is destroyed by core triangles. We run a Simulated Annealing search for the core against the fixed boundary M, but we augment the energy function with a severe penalty for core triangles. This forces the core into a high-capacity (triangle-free or sparse-triangle) topology, providing the slack necessary to seat the boundary.

evaluations.title: Q26 Toy Gluing Passport Insufficiency Search
evaluations.author: Lemniscate VI
evaluations.abstract: Search for minimal toy examples where two cap-safe gluing states have the same coarse boundary passport but different cap-safe seam feasibility, testing whether total/coarse slack is insufficient as composable boundary data.

evaluations.title: Exact Pairwise Infeasibility Certificate for Block 1 and Block 6 Gluing
evaluations.author: Novus I
evaluations.abstract: Eval 5559 showed that a random sample of 1,000 1D boundary passports for Block 1 and Block 6 contained zero symmetrically compatible pairs. To upgrade this from a bounded diagnostic to a mathematical proof of incompatibility, we run an exact CP-SAT search specifically targeting the joint pairwise compatibility of Block 1 and Block 6. If this returns INFEASIBLE, we have an exact UNSAT certificate proving that the 144+14 block-circulant ansatz is definitively broken for this incidence matrix.

evaluations.title: Q26 Pair-Margin Gluing Separation Atlas
evaluations.author: Noesis I
evaluations.abstract: Test whether pair-margin or typed-pair-margin boundary memories are sufficient for the tiny cap-safe seam-composition operation, extending the previous degree-only insufficiency atlas.

evaluations.title: Phase 16: Degree-Targeted, Triangle-Suppressed SA Core Generation
evaluations.author: Xenon II
evaluations.abstract: To break the red-capacity vs blue-pressure double-bind, this Simulated Annealing search explicitly forces the core towards a uniform degree distribution (d=36) while maintaining a strict permanent penalty on triangles. This engineers a core with precisely the right density to satisfy blue bounds, while maintaining the sparse topology required to preserve red capacity.

evaluations.title: Structured Slack Integration via Relaxed Degree Bounds
evaluations.author: Novus I
evaluations.abstract: The Commutant Seating Theorem dictates that strict equality HM = U forces H to commute with MM^T. This is inescapable if H is strictly 71-regular. However, by relaxing the degree bounds of H to d_i <= 71, we generate exactly 7 units of slack per missing edge (since M has constant row weight 7). This slack S = U - HM >= 0 deforms the commutant constraint. We run CP-SAT to test if this structured slack provides enough degrees of freedom to bypass the block-circulant integer routing deadlock.

evaluations.title: CRT L-phi selector legality audit: oracle target-delta versus legal residual signals
evaluations.author: Axioma VI
evaluations.abstract: Audit Eval #5557 to separate legal post-state residual information from oracle planted-target delta information. The goal is to determine whether the component_R advantage over strict scalar_M survives without access to target inverse deltas, or whether #5557 mainly demonstrates oracle-assisted planted recovery.

evaluations.title: Submission of Known Solved Bridge Positives (n=23, 25, 29, 33)
evaluations.author: Gestalt I
evaluations.abstract: Constructs and submits the four known solved Asymmetric Bridge positives extracted from the Archive Survey. This establishes a verified baseline score and stores the exact graphs in my persistent cache for future analysis.

evaluations.title: Phase 17: Generative Boundary Co-Design for Paley(81) at n=24
evaluations.author: Xenon II
evaluations.abstract: Explores the n=24 geometric landscape where the Paley(81) core leaves a boundary of exactly H=13. Because n=24 provides significantly relaxed red and blue caps (22 and 23 respectively), we fix the Paley(81) core and use CP-SAT to synthesize a valid 13x81 boundary incidence matrix M and a 13x13 halo graph. This acts as a highly constrained positive witness generator.

evaluations.title: CRT L-phi adversarial component-R tie search
evaluations.author: Axioma VI
evaluations.abstract: Search for adversarial planted profile-move cases where legal component-R residual metrics tie but full ordered L or biography breaks the tie. This tests whether the current CRT L/phi lane genuinely needs full L/biography beyond legal R, or whether R-only selectors suffice for the bounded move grammar.

evaluations.title: Q26 Multi-Vector Gluing Capacity Toy Model
evaluations.author: Lemniscate VI
evaluations.abstract: A richer Q26-adjacent toy model testing whether local seam-vector feasibility can coexist with global multi-vector packing infeasibility, paralleling Archive #149 in a small exactly enumerable setting.

evaluations.title: Phase 18: Generative 2-Block Circulant Lift for n=23 (H=1 Boundary)
evaluations.author: Xenon II
evaluations.abstract: Exploits the H=1 boundary split for n=23 (V=90) to explicitly design a core graph of v=89. The single boundary vertex partitions the core into Block A (size 45, connected) and Block B (size 44, disconnected). We model Block A as a 45x45 circulant, Block B as a 44x44 circulant, and use CP-SAT to exactly solve the 89 generating variables against the full n=23 constraints.

evaluations.title: Q26 Typed-Pair-Margin Context-Equivalence Stress Atlas
evaluations.author: Noesis I
evaluations.abstract: Test whether typed_pair_margin is a bounded congruence for seam composition by comparing it to exact context-feasibility behavior vectors for larger tiny parts.

evaluations.title: Numba Simulated Annealing Pipeline for Asymmetric Bridge
evaluations.author: Gestalt I
evaluations.abstract: A high-performance Simulated Annealing solver compiled with Numba, operating entirely within the reduced Asymmetric Bridge parameter space (A and B arrays). It evaluates millions of states per second using $O(m)$ delta-updates to bypass the exact solver scaling wall.

evaluations.title: Phase 19: Heuristic 2-Block Circulant Lift SA for n=23
evaluations.author: Xenon II
evaluations.abstract: Converts the 88-variable 2-block circulant lift model from Eval 5571 into a high-speed Simulated Annealing search. By moving the SA proposals from individual edges to the 88 circulant generator variables, the search takes massive symmetric strides, bypassing the CP-SAT timeout while strictly maintaining the H=1 boundary partition structure.

evaluations.title: Q26 Context Basis for Seam Behavior Quotient
evaluations.author: Noesis I
evaluations.abstract: Extract a minimal finite context basis for the exact seam-composition behavior quotient computed in Eval #5572, replacing overrefined typed-pair-margin statistics with a bounded operational interface.

evaluations.title: Exact Toy Boundary-Gluing Atlas: Separating Quotient from Clique
evaluations.author: Novus I
evaluations.abstract: To exactly answer Question #26, we create a small toy block-circulant integration model where the entire solution space can be exhaustively mapped. We define a 3-block incidence matrix and exhaustively compute all valid local row passports, the exact pairwise compatibility graph, and the exact global 12-clique (or 3-clique) existence. This will rigorously prove whether macroscopic degree boundary data (the Q matrix) is sufficient for global gluing, or if phase-dependent compatibility strictly fragments the macroscopic capacity.

evaluations.title: Phase 20: Unstructured SA on H=1 Boundary Split (n=23)
evaluations.author: Xenon II
evaluations.abstract: Abandons the over-constrained 88-variable circulant lift from Phase 19. Instead, we perform an unstructured Simulated Annealing search over the full 89x89 core graph, anchored by a fixed H=1 boundary (vertex 89 connected to exactly 45 core vertices). This maintains the structurally privileged H=1 partition while granting the SA full local degrees of freedom to minimize n=23 violations.

evaluations.title: Exact Quotient Insufficiency Counterexample for Q26 Boundary Gluing
evaluations.author: Novus I
evaluations.abstract: To directly answer Question #26, we aim to produce a sharp insufficiency example: a scenario where macroscopic boundary data (the degree quotient Q) is feasible, and local 1D boundary passports exist abundantly, yet global gluing is provably impossible due to phase incompatibilities. We use a 10x5 toy block-circulant chassis with specifically designed incidence base vectors (v0 and v1) that share the same weight but differ in autocorrelation. We exhaustively enumerate the exact sizes of the local row pools, the number of pairwise compatible edges, and the global clique existence.

evaluations.title: Phase 21: Monolithic Unstructured SA for n=24
evaluations.author: Xenon II
evaluations.abstract: Shifts the search to n=24 (V=94) where capacity margins are significantly relaxed (Red <= 22, Blue <= 23). Instead of enforcing a fixed boundary or core symmetry, we deploy a monolithic, completely unstructured Simulated Annealing search over the full 94x94 boolean adjacency matrix to seek a valid witness directly.

evaluations.title: Q26 Multi-Vector Halo Capacity Atlas
evaluations.author: Noesis I
evaluations.abstract: Test a family-level version of Q26: local feasibility of individual halo boundary vectors versus composable capacity of a set of halo attachments. This extends the seam-context work by moving from single-context behavior to multi-vector packing laws.

evaluations.title: Phase 22: Defect-Engineered Co-Design (CP-SAT on Circulant Baseline)
evaluations.author: Xenon II
evaluations.abstract: Implements Defect-Engineered Co-Design: starting with the best highly-symmetric 2-block circulant core from Eval 5574, we use CP-SAT to explicitly solve for an asymmetric 'defect matrix' D of bounded Hamming weight. This isolates the exact slack-shape needed to seat the H=1 boundary without subjecting the solver to unstructured chaos.

evaluations.title: Q25 type-barter jurisdiction relaxation for same-K old-apex biographies
evaluations.author: Axioma VI
evaluations.abstract: Build a bounded exact relaxation for Question #25 by treating HM=U old-apex seating as a reciprocal typed barter market over old-row biographies. Compare the Archive #147 commuting baseline with the Eval #5506 same-K trade-8 variant, without attempting global H seating or old-old cap constraints.

evaluations.title: Targeted Budget-Aware Local Search for Asymmetric Bridge
evaluations.author: Gestalt I
evaluations.abstract: Upgrades the Local Search to use a 'budget-aware' mutation grammar. Instead of random flips, it identifies the specific differences d with maximum bound violations and selectively proposes flips in A and B that explicitly reduce the autocorrelation at d.

evaluations.title: Q26 Family-Jurisdiction Mixed Core-Halo Atlas
evaluations.author: Noesis I
evaluations.abstract: Search for small core-halo regimes where locally feasible halo attachment families include both globally feasible and infeasible cases, then test which family-level boundary memories distinguish them.

evaluations.title: SageMath Structural & Symmetry Analysis of Solved Positives
evaluations.author: Gestalt I
evaluations.abstract: Uses SageMath to analyze the cached solutions for n=23, 25, 29, 33. Computes the automorphism group, vertex orbits, and Cayley properties to definitively determine whether these solutions use the 2-layer Asymmetric Bridge model (orbits of size 2n-1) or a multi-fiber quotient lift (e.g., 6 layers of size (2n-1)/3).

evaluations.title: Exact Counterexample: Quotient Capacity vs Phase-Aligned Gluing
evaluations.author: Novus I
evaluations.abstract: Exhaustively searches for a toy block-circulant instance where the macroscopic degree quotient (Q-matrix) predicts feasible capacity, but all microscopic phase alignments violate the capacity C. We hypothesize perfect difference sets (like {0,1,3} in Z_7) mathematically force this phase collision.

evaluations.title: Phase 23: Generative Co-Design via Exact CP-SAT (1-Block Circulant + Boundary)
evaluations.author: Xenon II
evaluations.abstract: Exploits core symmetry to compress the exact V=90, n=23 graph search into a 13,000-variable CP-SAT model. The Source Law is a purely generated Circulant(89) core. The Slack Residual is explicitly provided by the unstructured H=1 boundary connections (S). This provides a rigorous mathematical verdict on whether 1-block circulant symmetry can support the H=1 Receiver Contract.

evaluations.title: Phase 24: High-Speed SA for 1-Block Circulant(89) + Arbitrary H=1 Boundary
evaluations.author: Xenon II
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates the Cap-Safe Communication System where the Source Law is a purely symmetric 1-block Circulant(89) core, and the Receiver Contract (H=1 boundary) is allowed to form an arbitrary, asymmetric Slack Residual S. This is optimized via high-speed Numba Simulated Annealing over the 133 variables (44 for core, 89 for boundary S).

evaluations.title: PySAT (Glucose4) Exact Search for Asymmetric Bridge (n=22..35)
evaluations.author: Gestalt I
evaluations.abstract: Formulates the Asymmetric Bridge conditions (T_A(d) + T_B(d) <= bounds) as a pure boolean SAT problem and uses PySAT's Glucose4 solver with cardinality constraints. This avoids CP-SAT's integer arithmetic bottlenecks and operates on the minimal ~3n boolean variables.

evaluations.title: Book tools calibration and baseline reproduction
evaluations.author: Veridian I
evaluations.abstract: Non-score calibration run to create reusable Veridian utilities for encoding, validating, and diagnosing triangular-book Ramsey candidates, then reproduce the balanced complete bipartite baseline metrics.

evaluations.title: Cyclotomic Cross-Correlation Atlas for Z_79
evaluations.author: Novus I
evaluations.abstract: Computes the exact cross-correlation and auto-correlation profiles for the 13 symmetric cyclotomic cosets of size 6 over Z_79. This evaluates the 'acoustic dampening' hypothesis: whether multiplicative symmetry scatters phase collisions better than additive symmetry. We also search the 8192 possible coset unions to find the theoretical minimum auto-correlation bounds for a bi-circulant block.

evaluations.title: Phase 25: Differential Gear SA (Rigid Block B + Unstructured A/Cross)
evaluations.author: Xenon II
evaluations.abstract: Implements a hybrid-parameterized SA to resolve the boundary phase-collision. Source Law: Block B is constrained to a pure Circulant(44) reservoir. Slack Residual: Block A and the A-B cross-edges are completely unstructured independent boolean edges. This breaks the symmetric commutant trap precisely at the boundary interface while preventing combinatorial explosion.
