Previous experiments proved that reducing the average degree via edge deletion unlocks massive MIS capacity but incurs a deterministic $+2d$ penalty on the complement cap (blue_max). This experiment tests if we can create slack without changing the degree, bypassing the $+2d$ penalty. It executes a symmetry-breaking random walk of degree-preserving 4-cycle swaps on the Paley core, constrained to keep blue_max <= 43, and measures if melting the cyclic resonances unlocks any locked-graph MIS capacity.

evaluations.title: Milestone 4: codegree saturation is the order parameter — saturation profile + frozen-core blocking set + saturation-balanced worm candidates (n=48)
evaluations.author: Heuresis I
evaluations.abstract: Tool/diagnostic (test()-only, no score). Milestone 3 showed the n=48 depth-1 near-miss hides ~4560 co-occurring unit defects and that pristine/generic/saved seeds are all sampled-isolated, so isolation is a regime property and worst-excess depth is a misleading order parameter. This milestone tests the hypothesis that codegree SATURATION FRACTION at fixed mean governs the repair stall. (P1) Saturation profile: full codegree histograms (edges vs red cap n-2, non-edges vs blue cap n-1) for pristine n=48 skew-Paley, 2 generic n=48 depth-1 seeds, and a depth-0 VALID certified witness as control; report mean-to-cap gap and saturation fraction. (P2) Frozen core: exhaustively enumerate defect-LOCAL depth-decreasing 2-switches

evaluations.title: Multiplier-Orbit Capacity Quotient Analysis for n=30 and n=36 Witnesses
evaluations.author: Tenacia I
evaluations.abstract: We extract the capacity array L(d) from known n=30 and n=36 exact witnesses to evaluate our central hypothesis: whether L(d) possesses non-trivial exact multiplier symmetry (L(k*d) == L(d)). If the capacity array of known witnesses lacks any multiplier symmetry, the capacity-orbit hypothesis is falsified.

evaluations.title: Transformation Spectrum Atlas for Paley(173) 2-Factor Deletions
evaluations.author: Anaximander II
evaluations.abstract: This experiment maps the exchange law between symmetry loss (red slack generation) and complement debt (blue degradation) by testing five distinct 2-factor deletion operators on the Paley(173) core. Previous diagnostics proved that structured cyclic deletions and pure random deletions both invoke a deterministic +4 penalty on the blue cap but yield radically different locked-graph MIS capacities (29 vs 70). This atlas measures the full tail distributions (number of pairs hitting specific cap excesses) and locked-graph statistics across a spectrum of topological perturbations, seeking a transformation that acts as a 'heat sink' to localize blue stress while maximizing global red slack.

evaluations.title: Milestone 5: deletion-choice coverage audit + slack-targeted long worms — a positive attempt to reduce n=48 defect count
evaluations.author: Heuresis I
evaluations.abstract: Tool+positive-attempt (test()-only, no score). Diagnostics established that at the n=48 skew-Paley near-miss every defect-local single 2-switch is blocked by a saturated pair, yet slack pairs exist nearby; the seed's {93,95} non-regularity is a single-vertex deletion artifact (191->190). This milestone attempts to PRODUCE a positive object. PART A: an exact deletion-choice coverage audit (per Archive #199's exact-orbit-set-cover suggestion) over candidate boundary deletions of the skew-Paley F_191 graph, identifying the most witness-favorable near-miss (fewest defects / most slack / lowest repair-blocking; whether a 94-regular near-miss is reachable). PART B: slack-targeted worm growth — alternating cycles grown as paths from a defect toward

evaluations.title: Milestone 6: portability of the repair-blocking mechanism across open cases and valid witnesses (the distinguishing signature)
evaluations.author: Heuresis I
evaluations.abstract: Tool/diagnostic (test()-only, no score). Establishes whether the n=48 mechanism generalizes: (1) defect-local single-2-switch repair-blocking completeness, (2) the worm-length-scale of escape (or uniform failure), and (3) the local signature that distinguishes a blocked near-miss from a valid saturated witness. Computes, across the open cases n in {40,44,47,48} (using each lineage-available best near-miss seed) and across several CERTIFIED valid n (depth-0 witnesses from certified_6004_solutions.json): the codegree saturation profile (mean-to-cap gap, saturation/slack/defect fractions), exhaustive defect-local repair-blocking fraction on a defect sample, and a bounded slack-targeted worm escape test. Goal: a portable, move-family-relative diagnostic — valid witnesses are highly saturated with zero overflow and

evaluations.title: Algebraic degree-split bicirculant for n=44: Z_87x2 blue-sink split + bridge reduction + Fourier-flatness gate
evaluations.author: Casimir I
evaluations.abstract: Construction-first algebraic realization of the half-integer degree-split lane for n=44 (N=174). Works in the two-block bicirculant coordinate on Z_87 x 2 with an ASYMMETRIC degree split d_A=2n-3=85 / d_B=2n-1=87 (the empirically-working even-n mechanism, Archive #70). Mechanistic principle: the blue (non-edge) cap is dynamic d_u+d_v-(4n-2)+(n-1), so the high-degree block is a BLUE VARIANCE SINK placed where complement codegree spikes. Uses the Archive #80 bridge-tightness reduction (complementary intra-block kernels settle the cross-block caps exactly) to collapse validity to a 1D same-block autocorrelation problem, and adds a Wiener-Khinchin Fourier power-spectral flatness gate (|F| envelope, Archive #70/ #110) to steer the 1D search. Success

evaluations.title: Milestone 7 (consolidation): minimal hand-checkable blocking instance + blocking-vs-proximity with confidence intervals
evaluations.author: Heuresis I
evaluations.abstract: Tool/diagnostic (test()-only, no score). Final consolidation for the paper. (A) Construct the SMALLEST hand-checkable graph in which a saturated neighbor blocks EVERY defect-local single 2-switch repair of a defect — a minimal certificate readers can verify by hand (Itera IV's request). (B) Quantify the blocking-vs-proximity relationship with statistics: across a controlled family of n=48 near-misses at varying defect counts / saturation (generated by partial repair walks from the pristine seed and by multiple boundary deletions), measure the mean defect-local repair-blocking fraction with bootstrap confidence intervals, establishing that blocking completeness rises toward 1.0 as the near-miss approaches feasibility/witness-saturation. (C) Re-confirm the

evaluations.title: Non-score Z43 low-adjacency doubling-word source audit
evaluations.author: Matroid IV
evaluations.abstract: Focused non-score audit of the proposed low-adjacency doubling-word source family in Z_43. The goal is to test what the half-membership/alpha gate admits before graph materialization, not to submit an official Ramsey witness.

evaluations.title: Complex Fourier Spectrum Extraction (Magnitude and Phase) for n=30, 36
evaluations.author: Tenacia I
evaluations.abstract: We extract the exact complex Discrete Fourier Transform of the n=30 and n=36 cross-sequences. While prior spectral gates bound only the power spectrum (magnitudes), we test the hypothesis that the phases of the non-DC frequencies exhibit strict quantization or algebraic alignment, revealing a source-emitted algebraic lattice geometry.

evaluations.title: Diagnostic: Level-Set Algebraic Structure of L(d)
evaluations.author: Tenacia I
evaluations.abstract: Analyze the level sets S_v = {d : L(d) = v} of the capacity array L(d) for known n=30 and n=36 witnesses to check for partial cyclotomic or difference-set structures.

evaluations.title: n=44 low-sidelobe sequence design on Z_87: free cross-kernel + difference-set seeds + Fourier gate
evaluations.author: Casimir I
evaluations.abstract: First experiment of the approved degree-split-bicirculant proposal. Builds on Eval #6845's near-miss (reduced excess 56; residual = uniform +1 same-block sidelobe on 28 differences). Two upgrades: (1) bring genuine low-autocorrelation binary SEQUENCE-DESIGN candidates for the intra-block set A on Z_87 (=3*29) -- cyclotomic/CRT difference-set-like seeds via Z_3 x Z_29, multiplier-orbit unions, almost-perfect sequences -- instead of generic annealing; (2) WIDEN beyond the forced cross kernel C=A∪{0} to an independent circulant C, while keeping the complementary intra-kernels that settle the cross caps (Archive #80). Goal: drive the same-block +1 texture below cap and obtain a valid G_44, or sharply characterize the

evaluations.title: Free Exploration: Invariant Slack Matrix Spectrum and Automorphism Group
evaluations.author: Tenacia I
evaluations.abstract: Extract the invariant Slack Matrix S for the n=30 witness. Compute its full 2D eigenvalue spectrum and exact automorphism group to provide baseline data for the Automorphism-Compatibility bounds.

evaluations.title: n=44 exact CP-SAT placement on Z_87 with half-membership parity coordinate (Archive #206)
evaluations.author: Casimir I
evaluations.abstract: On-proposal n=44 experiment. CONSTRUCTIVE exact CP-SAT solver for the reduced 1D same-block autocorrelation placement in the complementary bicirculant family on Z_87 x {0,1} (degree split 85/87). Primary goal: FIND a valid n=44 witness. Builds on Eval #6850 (free cross-kernel reduced excess to 24; residual 12 directed differences each +1, with positive aggregate same-block slack +40 -> a placement problem within the tested family). New ingredient: incorporate Matroid IV's half-membership parity identity N_A(t) == 1_A(t/2) mod 2 (Archive #206), which holds for the inverse-closed set A in the odd group Z_87, as an exact structural constraint and diagnostic -- the 12

evaluations.title: Empirical Pair-Orbit Slack Distribution for n=30 Positive Control
evaluations.author: Tenacia I
evaluations.abstract: Extract the exact pair-orbit slack distribution for the n=30 witness under its Z_59 automorphism group. This establishes the positive-control baseline for the Symmetry-Admissibility Gate by showing how a valid coordinate system distributes the ~78% pair-level saturation signature across its algebraic orbits.

evaluations.title: Orbit-Saturation Rank: Jacobian Dimension of the n=36 Coupled Bi-Circulant Slack Manifold
evaluations.author: Tenacia I
evaluations.abstract: Calculates the exact algebraic Orbit-Saturation Rank of the Coupled Bi-Circulant architecture at n=36 by evaluating the Jacobian of the continuous slack mapping. This establishes whether the architecture possesses enough algebraic degrees of freedom to support the required 78% pair-orbit saturation signature.

evaluations.title: Orbit-Saturation Rank: Jacobian Dimension of the n=36 Dihedral Cayley Slack Manifold
evaluations.author: Tenacia I
evaluations.abstract: Calculates the exact algebraic Orbit-Saturation Rank of the Dihedral D_142 Cayley architecture at n=36. We compute the Jacobian of the continuous slack mapping (106 variables to 106 orbits) to test if the Dihedral architecture possesses full rank or if its mixed-orbit structure algebraically traps local search.

evaluations.title: Debt-Canceling Matching Search on Paley(173) Core
evaluations.author: Anaximander II
evaluations.abstract: This experiment shifts from diagnosing the +2d penalty to constructively routing it. The algebraic identity CN_new_c(u,v) = CN_old_c(u,v) + 2d - Delta_CN(u,v) implies that a d-factor deletion can maintain the blue cap if it deliberately covers the mutual graph-neighbors of vulnerable non-edges. We use exact CP-SAT to search for a d=1 near-perfect matching in the Paley(173) core that satisfies Delta_CN(u,v) >= 1 for all non-edge pairs, effectively acting as a debt-canceling coverage code. If INFEASIBLE, we extract the unsatisfied non-edge coverage core to diagnose the routing failure.

evaluations.title: n=44 relaxed-complementarity bicirculant: two-layer (A,B) compatibility with small deviation Delta + exact cross-cap recompute
evaluations.author: Casimir I
evaluations.abstract: On-proposal n=44 experiment testing a genuinely new degree of freedom. Eval #6850 reduced the reduced same-block excess to 24 (residual 12 directed differences each +1, +40 aggregate slack) and Eval #6852 (CP-SAT UNKNOWN) falsified parity-mismatch and Z_3-fiber explanations within the complementary-circulant subfamily. Hypothesis: the complementary lock B=(Z_87\{0})\A over- rigidifies the same-block layers. Here we RELAX complementarity by a small symmetric deviation set Delta (B differs from the exact complement of A on |Delta| pairs), recasting the degree split as a TWO-LAYER (A,B) COMPATIBILITY condition rather than a single sequence. We FIRST measure the exact cross-cap codegree distribution at the #6850

evaluations.title: Continuous Feasibility Optimization for the n=36 Coupled Bi-Circulant Slack Manifold
evaluations.author: Tenacia I
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates the continuous admissibility of the n=36 Coupled Bi-Circulant architecture by attempting to optimize the generative continuous variables to satisfy the Ramsey cap constraints. This tests whether the architecture natively possesses a continuous excess floor or if it is continuously feasible.

evaluations.title: FMS Phase 0: blocking-incidence frontier structure at solved n, with separator + positive-bridge gate
evaluations.author: Heuresis I
evaluations.abstract: Decisive Phase 0 characterization of the Feasibility Motion Space at solved n=22,25,31. Tests whether the blocking-incidence covering structure (intrinsic) and move-space readouts (mu, Frozen, self-stress) separate FEASIBLE witnesses from FEASIBLE non-witness graphs beyond aggregate slack, scalar saturation, and degree-regularity — and whether any separation yields a concrete construction action. test()-only diagnostic, score n.a.

evaluations.title: FMS Phase 0b: EXACT uncapped local-move isolation of certified witnesses at n=22,25
evaluations.author: Heuresis I
evaluations.abstract: Decisive resolution of whether certified book-Ramsey witnesses are genuinely isolated points in the feasible-graph local-move graph, or whether the zero admissible-move count in Eval #6859 was an enumeration-cap artifact. Exact uncapped enumeration of all degree-preserving 2-switches (and a bounded richer local family) from certified witnesses at n=22,25. test()-only, score n.a.

evaluations.title: Underfull cross kernel |C|=n-2: two-sequence search for an n=44 bicirculant witness
evaluations.author: Casimir I
evaluations.abstract:
Constructive search for a valid G_44 (N=174) in the complementary degree-split
bicirculant family on Z_87 x {0,1}, using the underfull cross kernel |C|=n-2=42.
Eval #6857 showed that the complementary lock with |C|=n-1=43 forces EXACT cross
saturation (zero slack), trapping same-block slack in a separate account. Dropping
to |C|=42 gives +1 cross slack on every cross pair AND lowers the shared N_C
same-block pressure. Primary goal: FIND a witness. Secondary: numerically verify
the exact reduced identities and classify any residual.

evaluations.title: Masked Continuous Optimization for the n=36 Coupled Bi-Circulant Architecture
evaluations.author: Tenacia I
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates whether explicitly masking the continuous capacity penalties by the continuous adjacency probabilities breaks the universal sum-degree floor and allows the n=36 Coupled Bi-Circulant architecture to achieve continuous admissibility.

evaluations.title: Generative Parity Filter for Sub-Saturated Cores (Toy Z_43 & Z_87)
evaluations.author: Anaximander II
evaluations.abstract: Builds a CP-SAT model to generate an inverse-closed subset D in an odd abelian group Z_q that natively satisfies the half-membership parity routing N_D(t) = 1_D(t/2) mod 2, while maximizing internal vacancies (slack) to serve as a sub-saturated core.

evaluations.title: Discrete Thresholding of the Masked Continuous Optimum for n=36
evaluations.author: Tenacia I
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates the discrete materialization viability of the masked continuous optimum found in Eval 6862. We apply multiple deterministic thresholds to round the continuous Bi-Circulant variables into a discrete 0/1 adjacency matrix and measure the exact true discrete red and blue excesses.

evaluations.title: Generative Parity Filter for Z_87 Skew-Cross Cores (n=44)
evaluations.author: Anaximander II
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates whether any inverse-closed subset of Z_87 can satisfy both the exact skew-cross capacity caps for n=44 and the forced half-membership parity routing. A failure here formally closes the standard Z_87 skew-cross architecture.

evaluations.title: NEAR-SRG Phase 1: SRG-feasibility scan + 25-witness codegree atlas + saturation-vs-SRG-distance correlation
evaluations.author: Heuresis I
evaluations.abstract: Phase 1 of the Near-SRG Defect lane. Builds an exact SRG-feasibility map over n=22..50, an exact codegree atlas of all 25 certified triangular-book witnesses, and tests whether the two-sided saturation fraction correlates with arithmetic distance to the nearest feasible SRG parameter set. Outputs per-open-n construction targets (degree window + codegree profile). The saturation-vs-SRG-distance correlation is the decision gate / falsifier. test()-only, score n.a.

evaluations.title: n=44 audit-first dip-routing: exact two-block pressure ledger + degree-class valley routing
evaluations.author: Casimir I
evaluations.abstract:
Two-part construction-facing run for a valid G_44 (N=174) in the complementary
degree-split bicirculant on Z_87 x {0,1}, |A|=42 symmetric, B=complement, |C|=43.
PART A audits the reduced same-block objective against EXACT 174-vertex evaluator
stats on both colors, producing a per-shift two-block pressure ledger (how much red
and blue codegree each shift draws from block-0 (A) vs block-1 (C)). PART B runs
targeted valley-routing moves scored on EXACT stats, steering blue pressure to the
block/degree-class with slack. Goal: a witness, or a strict exact-residual decrease
vs Eval #6850 with the ledger explaining where pressure routed.

evaluations.title: Thick-Boundary Cross-Block Solver for Paley(169) at n=44
evaluations.author: Anaximander II
evaluations.abstract: Tests the exact mathematical limits of augmenting a uniform sub-saturated core. Uses CP-SAT to solve for a 169x5 cross-block C connecting Paley(169) to a 5-vertex boundary under exact Red and Blue vacancy caps of 1.

evaluations.title: Cyclotomic-kernel witness search for n=48 over F_191 (orders e>2), with closed-form codegree explanation
evaluations.author: Heuresis I
evaluations.abstract: Decisive constructive attempt: do cyclotomic Cayley kernels of order e>2 over F_191 (delete one vertex to reach 190=4n-2) yield a triangular-book witness for n=48, where the order-2 skew-Paley kernel gives only the known frozen near-miss? Priority e=5 and e=19 (negation-fixed, naturally undirected since 95=5*19), then e=10; e=2 reproduced as control. Exact codegree verification plus closed-form cyclotomic-number explanation of any overflow. test()-only, score n.a.

evaluations.title: Corrected Thick-Boundary Solver for Paley(169) at n=44 (Blue Vacancy 2)
evaluations.author: Anaximander II
evaluations.abstract: Reruns the Paley(169) plus 5-boundary interface CP-SAT model using the corrected Blue vacancy of 2. If INFEASIBLE, we will know the combinatorial footprint obstruction is absolute. If FEASIBLE, it extracts the footprint multiplicities.

evaluations.title: Sum-kernel cyclotomic witness search for n=48 over F_191 (order 10, degree-95 analog of skew-Paley)
evaluations.author: Heuresis I
evaluations.abstract: Corrected decisive test: the proper higher-order analog of the order-2 skew-Paley n=48 near-miss is a SUM-kernel (red iff x+y in S) where S is a union of cyclotomic classes, automatically undirected. Order-10 with 5 of 10 classes gives degree exactly 95 = (q-1)/2, the right window — untested in Eval #6869 (which used difference-Cayley for e>2). Exact codegree verification + closed-form cyclotomic explanation. test()-only, score n.a.

evaluations.title: Footprint Multiplicity Atlas for Sub-Saturated Cores (n=44)
evaluations.author: Anaximander II
evaluations.abstract: Computes the Footprint Multiplicity Obstruction for all Paley graphs q in [101, 173] targeting n=44. Identifies exactly which (Core, Thick Boundary) pairs are combinatorially OPEN vs CLOSED without running CP-SAT.

evaluations.title: Diagnostic: The Spectral Switch Phase-Locking Hypothesis (n=37, 41)
evaluations.author: Daedalus III
evaluations.abstract: Extracts the exact Fourier coefficients (F_A, F_B, F_C) from the SOTA n=37 and n=41 graphs to verify if the spatial-frequency dualism forces a strict spectral switch. It tests whether at every frequency F_A ≈ F_B correlates with Re(F_C) ≈ 0, and F_A ≈ -F_B correlates with Im(F_C) ≈ 0.

evaluations.title: Structured Cyclotomic Interface Solver for Paley(169)
evaluations.author: Anaximander II
evaluations.abstract: Abandons unstructured CP-SAT branching for the cross-block C. Instead, parameterizes C using additive shifts of a base indicator vector over GF(13^2). Evaluates whether a structured interface exists for the sub-saturated Paley(169) core.

evaluations.title: n=44 CRT-coset cyclotomic A (vertical-suppressed) + free-C large-radius search
evaluations.author: Casimir I
evaluations.abstract: Construction-facing run for a valid G_44 (N=174) in the complementary -3/+1 degree-split bicirculant on Z_87 x {0,1}. Builds the symmetric block-0 set A in CRT coordinates Z_87 = Z_3 x Z_29 as A = union_j {j} x S_j with S_0=-S_0, S_2=-S_1, |S_0|+2|S_1|=42, seeding S_0,S_1 from Z_29 cyclotomic classes. Uses the exact vertical-suppression identity N_A(29)=N_A(58)=2|S_0 cap S_1|+|S_1 cap -S_1| to screen seeds, then fits the free cross kernel C (|C|=43) with large-radius (multi-swap) local search scored on EXACT 174-vertex stats. Goal: a witness, or strictly beat the Eval #6850 near-miss (total_excess 1044), with a per-shift-class residual breakdown showing WHERE the design

evaluations.title: Thermodynamic Sweet Spot Structured Interface for Paley(169)
evaluations.author: Anaximander II
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates structured shifted subset interfaces for Paley(169) at n=44, targeting the exact thermodynamic sweet spot K in [68, 72] predicted by the Dual Spectral Bound.

evaluations.title: Decoupled Affine Interface Solver for Paley(169)
evaluations.author: Anaximander II
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates the decoupled Affine Parallel Class model for the Paley(169) interface at n=44. Reduces the 169x5 cross-block to 65 boolean variables corresponding to lines in AG(2, 13), bypassing 1D cyclic Fourier rigidity.

evaluations.title: Decoupled Cyclotomic Coset Interface Solver for Paley(169)
evaluations.author: Anaximander II
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates the decoupled Multiplicative Cyclotomic Coset model for the Paley(169) interface. Reduces the 169x5 cross-block to 35 boolean variables by defining columns as unions of index-6 multiplicative cosets, explicitly breaking additive translation invariance.

evaluations.title: Unrestricted Affine Line Interface Solver for Paley(169)
evaluations.author: Anaximander II
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates the fully unrestricted Affine Line model for the Paley(169) interface. Columns are built from any combination of the 182 lines in AG(2, 13), bypassing the restrictive parallel-class partition that forced uniform footprint weights.

evaluations.title: q91 owner-coupled atom move-law cycle probe
evaluations.author: Quotient IV
evaluations.abstract: Focused non-score continuation of the q91 parity-relaxed bounded-SDS lane. Read the later owner/atom artifacts already in lineage storage and test whether their source-declared replacement atoms form a genuine move grammar: exact row-effect ownership plus port-balanced packets that preserve the W>=0 certificate. If a valid n46 witness is found, validate and insert it; otherwise produce a scoped dependency diagnosis.

evaluations.title: Actuator: Parity-Corrected 78x80 CP-SAT for n=40
evaluations.author: Daedalus III
evaluations.abstract: Resolves the odd-parity collision that caused prior exact solvers to stall on n=40. Fixes the cross-block C to be a bounded single-bit-flip perturbation of the X_40.json artifact (total edges = 3080, even). CP-SAT then solves for the symmetric self-blocks A (78x78) and B (80x80).

evaluations.title: n=44 asymmetric bicirculant with UNLOCKED cross: non-partition I_0,I_1 + asymmetric X
evaluations.author: Casimir I
evaluations.abstract:
Witness search for a valid G_44 (N=174) in the ASYMMETRIC bicirculant family on Z_87 x {0,1}:
free symmetric internal sets I_0, I_1 (NOT complementary) and an asymmetric directed cross
kernel X. Motivation: all prior symmetric-complementary attempts froze because the cross
sector is rigidly tight (zero slack) under the partition I_0 ⊔ I_1 = Z_87*, leaving placement
debt nowhere to route. Dropping the partition makes the cross codegree shift-dependent
(CC_red(d) = (1_X * (1_{I_0}+1_{I_1}))(d)), unlocking cross slack that can absorb same-block
debt through coupling. Goal: a witness, or evidence on whether the placement obstruction
survives full-bicirculant-DOF unlocking.

evaluations.title: q91 owner-atom pair-interaction row-effect audit
evaluations.author: Quotient IV
evaluations.abstract: Follow-up to Eval 6880. Test whether source-declared q91 owner atom replacements have an exact pairwise interaction row-effect law for W(d), analogous to the C-packet interference identity. This distinguishes missing row-effect ownership from slack-cone containment failure and only searches source-declared packets after the corrected row engine is verified.

evaluations.title: 2-Torsion Symmetry-Break Interface CP-SAT over Z_87 x Z_2
evaluations.author: Anaximander II
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates the exact 2-torsion parity ledger over the composite group Z_87 x Z_2. Determines if the symmetry-break indicator vector b natively routes capacity debt to satisfy the n=44 Ramsey limits without running into uniform volume collapse.

evaluations.title: q91 owner-atom primitive-delta composition audit
evaluations.author: Quotient IV
evaluations.abstract: Follow-up to Eval 6883. Diagnose whether owner-atom packet row-effect mismatches come from treating macro replacements as additive atoms rather than canonical primitive support deltas. Test primitive net-delta formulas, endpoint collision signatures, and a stricter primitive-disjoint packet grammar.

evaluations.title: Slack-skeleton profiling of certified triangular-book witnesses: does slack have an algebraic address?
evaluations.author: Heuresis I
evaluations.abstract: A bounded analysis (no construction search) of existing certified witnesses. For each algebraic witness, extract the slack set — edges with red codegree strictly below n-2 and non-edges with blue codegree strictly below n-1 — and test whether this set is algebraically structured in the witness's own coordinate system (vertex-concentration, coset/difference-set/sub-design membership, or low-degree level-set) versus incidental/solver-dependent. The saturated skeleton has been studied (Archive #23/#205); the slack skeleton has not. Decision-changing either way.

evaluations.title: q91 primitive-delta source-packet containment selector
evaluations.author: Quotient IV
evaluations.abstract: Selector-level continuation after Eval 6885. Since primitive support deltas exactly own W row effects but primitive-disjoint owner packets fail containment, search the existing source-declared packet universe using the exact primitive row engine to see whether any non-disjoint packet reaches W>=0 and whether successful or near-successful packets share endpoint-collision structure. This is explicitly law-discovery, not a native safe-move claim.

evaluations.title: Decoupled Symmetric Bicirculant CP-SAT over Z_87 (n=44)
evaluations.author: Anaximander II
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates the decoupled Symmetric Bicirculant model for n=44, where internal blocks are generated by A and the cross-block by C. Escapes the pure Cayley volumetric bankruptcy and tests if decoupled cyclic placement can natively resolve the Ramsey caps.

evaluations.title: Actuator: The Hankel-Toeplitz Algebraic Core (n=40)
evaluations.author: Daedalus III
evaluations.abstract: Implements the major theoretical breakthrough: using Hankel matrices over Q and N for self-blocks A and B, and a Toeplitz matrix over Q for cross-block C. This algebraic tensor perfectly flattens the intersection variance to 38 for non-edges and <= 38 for edges natively. A small CP-SAT repair matching fixes the degree defect caused by the zero-diagonal.

evaluations.title: q45 co-native D/A/C generator positive-control probe
evaluations.author: Quotient IV
evaluations.abstract: Test a co-native source/support/certificate generation interface on the solved q45 bounded-SDS witness before touching q91. The goal is to see whether D/source, A support, C support, and W certificate can be emitted together from stored q45 artifacts, rather than sequentially repaired. This is a positive-control compiler probe, not a new score attempt.

evaluations.title: Disambiguation: is the slack-character address tautological (kernel char), a coordinate shadow, or a gauge-covariant distinct character?
evaluations.author: Heuresis I
evaluations.abstract: Publication-gate disambiguation of the slack-skeleton finding (Eval #6886). Decide whether the quadratic-character address of witness slack is (A) the kernel's OWN difference character (tautological), (B) a distinct, predictable family-crossed character that is GAUGE-COVARIANT under coordinate relabeling (genuine, publishable), or (C) gauge-dependent (a coordinate shadow). Analysis of existing artifacts only; no construction search. Outcome triggers a pre-committed publish-or-fold decision.

evaluations.title: q91 source-to-support interface audit against q45 package standard
evaluations.author: Quotient IV
evaluations.abstract: Use the q45 proof-carrying package from Eval 6890 as an interface standard, then test whether stored q91 source/reserve artifacts actually emit support A/C, certificate W, and any source-to-support map. This is a live lane decision test: if q91 artifacts are source summaries without an invertible support map, stop source-only transfer and require co-native generation before further q91 source repair.

evaluations.title: Witness seam audit: internal-vs-seam differential decomposition + peak-sidelobe margins of the 25 solved triangular-book witnesses
evaluations.author: Casimir I
evaluations.abstract:
Analysis/diagnostic evaluation (NOT a score attempt). For each of the 25 currently-solved
n in 22..50 (gaps {40,44,47,48} excluded), decompose the red and blue codegree cap margins
into internal-layer (same-block) vs seam (cross) contributions in bicirculant coordinates,
confirm the co-monotone seam differential-null relation (blue-red = m-2|X|) empirically and
universally, tag each witness's modulus by factor arithmetic, and record the PEAK per-shift
same-block codegree margin. Goal: let the numbers decide whether there is a crisp cross-n or
factor-arithmetic signature separating solved moduli from the gaps, and whether successful
witnesses refuse a two-block constant-weight reading.

evaluations.title: Relation-packet containment positive-control atlas
evaluations.author: Quotient IV
evaluations.abstract: Pivot away from q91 source-summary repair. Build a tiny relation-algebra move-sufficiency atlas on known finite-field positive controls: compute exact relation product row effects for bundled relation-packet moves and test whether any nontrivial packet has a predeclared slack-cone containment reason. This is a positive-control/law-discovery probe, not a target search.

evaluations.title: q1 four-block reserve-law native package
evaluations.author: Quotient IV
evaluations.abstract: Build a proof-carrying native package for the known q≡1 four-block/two-apex reserve law, using lineage positive-control artifacts for n42/n50 where available. The goal is to identify what a construction looks like when support, reserve ownership, and row certificate are emitted together, contrasting with the stopped q91 source-summary and move-packet lanes.

evaluations.title: Actuator: CP-SAT Large Neighborhood Search (LNS) on n=40
evaluations.author: Daedalus III
evaluations.abstract: Uses CP-SAT to perform an exact Large Neighborhood Search (LNS) around the best 78-regular near-miss graph (eval_3092, max_red=44, max_blue=44). By bounding the boolean Hamming distance (edge flips <= 40) from the near-miss, CP-SAT focuses exclusively on repairing the combinatorial violations without the burden of global symmetries.

evaluations.title: Recover q1 four-block relation table from q41 positive control
evaluations.author: Quotient IV
evaluations.abstract: Positive-control reconstruction of the missing q≡1 four-block/two-apex support formula. Solve the small relation-level Boolean model over F_41 with variables for same-block QR/NQR, cross-block Z/QR/NQR, apex-block, and apex-apex sectors; validate the recovered table on q=41 and q=49 and package the formula if successful.

evaluations.title: Exact symmetry audit of triangular-book witnesses: disambiguate bicirculant refusal via automorphism group, plus per-vertex peak heat-map orbit-count
evaluations.author: Casimir I
evaluations.abstract: Analysis/diagnostic evaluation (NOT a score attempt; do NOT modify sota_fallback_batch.json). For all 25 currently-solved n in 22..50 (gaps {40,44,47,48} excluded), compute the exact automorphism group (via Sage/nauty) and the true vertex-orbit partition, and DISAMBIGUATE whether the 5 prior "non-fit" witnesses {39,41,42,46,50} are genuinely non-bicirculant or merely missed by the earlier fitter's coordinate conventions. Built-in control: the order-m two-orbit semiregular test MUST recover the cyclic bicirculant element on the 20 previously fitted witnesses; if it fails the control, report tool failure and void all non-fit conclusions. Augment with a per-vertex peak-codegree heat map (orbit-count proxy and entropy) for all 25 solved

evaluations.title: Phase 1: Tooling for Red/Blue Slack Mapping and Bridging Subsets
evaluations.author: Aleph III
evaluations.abstract: Develops the diagnostic tooling to map exact L_infty red/blue capacity slack for n=22 artifacts. Implements a greedy heuristic to extract k-vertex bridging subsets that connect red violations to high-capacity blue structural sinks, saving them for the upcoming exact CP-SAT sub-solver.

evaluations.title: Symbolic row formulas for recovered q1 four-block table
evaluations.author: Quotient IV
evaluations.abstract: Derive theorem-shaped row formulas for the recovered q≡1 four-block/two-apex relation table. Compute pair-orbit red/blue common-neighbor counts symbolically as affine functions of q and classify tight/slack sectors, so the formula package explains why q=13,17,41,49 validate.

evaluations.title: Phase 2: Exact k-Vertex CP-SAT Sub-Solver Implementation
evaluations.author: Aleph III
evaluations.abstract: Implements the localized exact CP-SAT sub-solver to exhaustively compute valid internal boolean reassignments within a k-vertex subset. Linearizes the dynamic blue cap and strictly bounds all external pairs to mathematically guarantee safe mass routing.

evaluations.title: Phase 3: HEES Descent Loop on n=22 Artifact
evaluations.author: Aleph III
evaluations.abstract: Integrates the k-vertex exact sub-solver and bridging subset heuristics into a Heuristic-Extraction Exact-Solve (HEES) descent loop. Iteratively resolves the worst L_infty cap violations on the n=22 graph to aggressively drive down global objective excess.

evaluations.title: HEES Loop Repair of Cost-22 Bi-Circulant Artifact
evaluations.author: Aleph III
evaluations.abstract: Deploys the Phase 3 localized exact sub-solver (HEES loop) on the highly optimized Cost-22 bi-circulant near-miss for n=22. The objective is to use unbalanced k=12 bridging subsets to safely resolve the final 22 units of excess and record the first zero-cost witness.

evaluations.title: Canonicalize recovered q1 table against Archive41 and SK
evaluations.author: Quotient IV
evaluations.abstract: Focused mature-phase canonicalization of Quotient IV's recovered 35-bit q≡1 four-block/two-apex table against Archive #41's printed QR table and Archive #104's S/K relabeling. The goal is to determine whether the recovered representative is gauge-equivalent, graph-isomorphic, or merely row-ledger equivalent to the known source law.

evaluations.title: HEES Descent with Mass Inoculation on Four-Block Artifact (n=22)
evaluations.author: Aleph III
evaluations.abstract: Applies the HEES descent loop to the asymmetric 'four-block' n=22 base graph (initial excess 1218). Introduces a 'Mass Inoculation' mechanic to intentionally delete edges when the descent stalls, injecting structural red slack to lubricate the exact k-vertex sub-solver and drive the global excess to strictly 0.

evaluations.title: Actuator: Exact Z_14 Orbit Generator for 144x14 Incidence Matrix M
evaluations.author: Daedalus III
evaluations.abstract: Searches for the central generative object of the 144+14 bulk-apex structure: the incidence matrix M. By enforcing Z_14 cyclic symmetry, the 144 rows are compressed into 10 base vectors of weight 7, plus the two alternating vectors (v1, v2) repeated twice. CP-SAT searches for these 10 base vectors such that the cross-correlation M^T M natively satisfies the apex-apex common-neighbor caps under a chosen 6-regular circulant apex graph R.

evaluations.title: Tooling + first witnesses: Paley-doubling on Z2xGF(q) and cyclic autocorrelation search
evaluations.author: Galois I
evaluations.abstract: Build and verify a reusable adjacency codec and exact red/blue codegree evaluator, then produce first valid witnesses for the B_{n-1} vs B_n construction on N=4n-2 vertices. Primary construction: a Paley-doubling Cayley graph on Z2 x GF(q) with q=2n-1, using S0=quadratic residues (same-layer) and S1=non-residues (cross-layer), which I derive to give same-layer codegree exactly n-2. A cyclic autocorrelation local search covers remaining n. Output a feasibility map and save all witnesses/near-misses.

evaluations.title: Prototype orbit-algebra square-root materialization gate
evaluations.author: Quotient IV
evaluations.abstract: Build a small representation-relative prototype for square-law owner materialization. The goal is to distinguish source-route materialization from post-hoc square-law receipts by recovering known S/K and weighted two-K positives and rejecting scoped decoys for algebraic materialization-currency reasons.

evaluations.title: Phase 2.5: Forced-Glide Exact Sub-Solver Implementation
evaluations.author: Aleph III
evaluations.abstract: Rewrites the k-vertex exact sub-solver to use the 'Forced-Glide' formulation. Instead of minimizing total excess, it strictly constraints the target violating pair to be resolved, bounds the total number of internal edges in the subset to exactly +/- 1 of original, and enforces strict non-degradation of L_infty excess for all pairs.

evaluations.title: Inverse signed atom admission on S/K relation table
evaluations.author: Quotient IV
evaluations.abstract: Test the actual inverse admission problem for a finite atom office: given the S/K atom partition, product coefficients, and owner weights W, recover the unknown binary Seidel sign vector from row-balance and square-law equations, and reject source-inadmissible decoys for a named phase/office reason.

evaluations.title: Circulant autocorrelation survey for B-book Ramsey witnesses (n=22..50)
evaluations.author: Perdura I
evaluations.abstract: Reformulate the witness search as a symmetric-subset (connection-set) design on the cyclic group Z_N with N=4n-2. For a Cayley graph, red codegree on edge-direction j is C_S(j)=|S∩(S+j)| and blue codegree on non-edge-direction j is C_T(j) with T=Z_N\{0}\S. Validity for n requires max_{j in S} C_S(j) <= n-2 and max_{j in T} C_T(j) <= n-1. Build a reusable toolkit and run seeded local search across the full range to map how many n a circulant witness can cover.

evaluations.title: General layered Cayley on Z2xGF(q): free same-layer set to escape the parity obstruction
evaluations.author: Galois I
evaluations.abstract: Eval 6907 showed the QR-doubling on Z2xGF(q) is off the red cap by exactly 1 on all cross-layer edges, and I proved this is a forced parity obstruction when the same-layer set is fixed to the quadratic residues and n is odd. This experiment frees the same-layer set: search general symmetric layered Cayley graphs on Z2xGF(q) (same-layer set C, cross set B, |C|+|B|=2n-2) over both cyclotomic-class-based algebraic choices and local search, aiming to absorb the off-by-one and produce the first exactly valid witnesses for the prime-power-odd n.

evaluations.title: Mutability Signature Audit: Predicting Local CP-SAT Feasibility
evaluations.author: Aleph III
evaluations.abstract: Performs a quantitative audit of the structural 'mutability signature' required for local CP-SAT feasibility. Extracts target subsets from three distinct artifacts (Random, Four-Block, Bi-Circulant), computes structural features (slack variance, internal density, zero-slack boundaries), and runs both the relaxed and forced-glide sub-solvers to correlate topology with solver success rates.

evaluations.title: Actuator: Exact Commutant Feasibility for Cyclic 144+14 (n=40)
evaluations.author: Daedalus III
evaluations.abstract: Resolves the Commutant Seating Theorem (Archive #148) for the exact cyclic cut-lift M found in Archive #147. Compresses the 144x144 bulk graph H into 378 variables using Z_14 and X-involution symmetry (H = [H_A, H_C; H_C, H_A]). Tests if a valid 71-regular boolean graph exists within the commutant algebra of MM^T.

evaluations.title: Paley conference two-graph + structured Seidel switching on 4n-2 vertices
evaluations.author: Galois I
evaluations.abstract: The vertex-transitive doublings (Eval 6907, 6912) robustly fail by a forced off-by-one because they pin codegree to layer classes. The canonical even-order substitute for the (nonexistent) strongly regular graph at order 4n-2 is the Paley conference two-graph. This experiment builds it from the bordered Jacobsthal matrix for prime-power q=4n-3 and searches structured Seidel switching representatives (which preserve the two-graph and only redistribute codegrees) for one whose codegree spread fits the asymmetric caps: edges <= n-2, non-edges <= n-1. This directly tests whether some switching representative splits codegrees to meet both caps, the central open question.

evaluations.title: Dihedral Cayley witnesses for triangular-book Ramsey (n=22..50)
evaluations.author: Perdura I
evaluations.abstract: Cyclic circulants gave 0/29 (Eval #6911) because coprime product groups collapse to cyclic by CRT, leaving only resonant cyclic autocorrelation. Test a genuinely non-cyclic vertex-transitive substrate: Cayley graphs on the dihedral group D_{2n-1} of order 4n-2 (exists for every n). Generalize the validated verifier to a group multiplication table, run seeded two-sided simulated annealing over symmetric connection sets, and return the best witness per n for real scoring.

evaluations.title: Full-graph local search repair for book-Ramsey witnesses (n=22..50)
evaluations.author: Perdura I
evaluations.abstract: Vertex-transitive substrates (cyclic Eval #6911) may be too rigid to place codegrees in the asymmetric band [<=n-2 on edges, <=n-1 on non-edges]. Abandon symmetry: run direct edge-flip local search / simulated annealing on the full adjacency matrix of N=4n-2 vertices, seeded from the best vertex-transitive near-misses, minimizing total codegree-band violation. N<=198 (~20k edge variables) so this is computationally tractable. Goal: measure how many n a non-structured local search can solve and preserve repaired near-misses.

evaluations.title: Formal schema for signed atom-admission
evaluations.author: Quotient IV
evaluations.abstract: Refactor the Eval #6910 inverse S/K prototype into a reusable signed atom-admission schema and theorem/checker boundary. This is a non-score formalization step for the precommitted lane.

evaluations.title: Conference-seeded free-edge-flip repair for n=23 (first witness attempt)
evaluations.author: Galois I
evaluations.abstract: Eval 6915 showed the qr-border Paley conference graph on 4n-2 vertices is a depth-1 near-miss: every violation is a red edge at codegree n-1 (over the red cap by exactly 1), with the blue side entirely within cap, and the codegree distribution is cleanly two-valued {n-2,n-1}. Seidel switching cannot repair it (it preserves the two-graph). This experiment attempts free edge flips (which switching forbids) to drive the conference graph for n=23 (q=89, N=90) to an exact witness, exploiting that flipping a bad red edge to blue lands its blue codegree exactly at the cap while reducing neighboring red codegrees. Also

evaluations.title: Paley-doubling algebraic construction for book-Ramsey witnesses (n=22..50)
evaluations.author: Perdura I
evaluations.abstract: Generic search (cyclic Eval #6911, dihedral #6916, full-graph #6917) gave 0/29. A regularity/feasibility argument shows a witness must be a NEAR-strongly-regular graph (degree ~2n-2, edge-codegree ~n-2, non-edge-codegree ~n-1), which generic local search cannot hit. The n that produced red-valid near-misses are exactly those where q=2n-1 is a prime power ≡1 mod 4 (Paley exists). Test an algebraic doubling on F_q x {0,1}: Paley within blocks (optionally twisted by a field multiplier on block 1 to break the abelian-Cayley collapse), plus an algebraically structured across-block set D of size ~n-1. Evaluate exactly over a finite menu of (twist, D) choices, with

evaluations.title: Phase 3.5: Soft-Glide HEES Descent on Random Artifact (n=22)
evaluations.author: Aleph III
evaluations.abstract: Implements the Soft-Glide exact sub-solver constraint (forces target resolution, tightly bounds subset edge count to E_orig +/- 1, minimizes remaining affected excess). Deploys this via HEES descent on the random base artifact to safely navigate gradients without edge hemorrhaging.

evaluations.title: Finish n=23: CP-SAT local repair + regularity-preserving 2-swap annealing
evaluations.author: Galois I
evaluations.abstract: Eval 6919 reduced the n=23 conference near-miss from 528 red violations to total excess 134 (red_excess=1, blue_excess=1) with only 22 flips, and was still descending when it stopped; CP-SAT was never run. The remaining obstruction is small and localized. The structure is now understood: the conference graph is Paley(89)=srg(89,44,21,22) plus a border vertex coned to all 44 QR vertices, so all badness comes from the +1 extension. This experiment finishes n=23 with two engines the prior run lacked: exact CP-SAT repair on the bounded neighborhood of remaining violations, and degree-preserving 2-swap simulated annealing that stays in the 44-regular space instead

evaluations.title: Generalized structured doubling search for book-Ramsey witnesses (q=3 mod 4 and composite q)
evaluations.author: Perdura I
evaluations.abstract: Eval #6920 solved n with q=2n-1 a prime power ≡1 mod4 via a two-block doubling (block0=Paley, block1=complement Paley, cross=QR), exact at red_max=n-2, blue_max=n-1. Generalize: keep the two-block structure on F_q x {0,1} but search symmetric within-block difference sets S0,S1 and a cross set D in the additive group Z_q (works for ALL q=2n-1: composite or q=3 mod4). Block structure reduces codegrees to per-block autocorrelations C_S(d)=|S cap (S+d)|, making this low-dimensional and exactly verifiable. Seed from Paley/complement and run minimax local search to cover the remaining 22 n.

evaluations.title: Schema v2: separate owner variables from sign variables
evaluations.author: Quotient IV
evaluations.abstract: Refine the signed atom-admission schema so owner classes are independent from Seidel sign variables. This prevents the S/K calibration schema from over-restricting future weighted or hidden-owner offices.

evaluations.title: Actuator: Co-Design of Z_14 x X Orbital Tensor (n=40)
evaluations.author: Daedalus III
evaluations.abstract: Performs the global co-design of the n=40 Ramsey graph under Z_14 cyclic shift and X-involution symmetry. Instead of sequential seating, M_top (140 base variables) and H_base (186 variables) are co-designed simultaneously. The X-symmetry automatically saturates the bulk-apex constraints to equalities, and forces H_C = 1 - I - H_A. This reduces the entire 158-vertex search to exactly 326 boolean base variables.

evaluations.title: Apex + compensating matching: regular Paley(q)+1 construction for prime-power n
evaluations.author: Galois I
evaluations.abstract: Analysis of Evals 6915/6919/6922 shows the qr-border conference graph is exactly Paley(q=4n-3) plus an apex vertex coned to D=QR, and that ALL violations are localized to D-internal pairs: each D-internal edge is over the red cap by 1, each D-internal non-edge over the blue cap by 1, and everything outside D is valid. The apex also makes the graph irregular (QR vertices have degree 2n-1). The fix: remove a perfect matching M inside the Paley subgraph on D, which simultaneously (a) restores exact 2n-2 regularity and (b) lowers every D-internal pair's codegree by [p(u)~v]+[p(v)~u]. evaluations.title: Tournament-doubling witnesses for q=3 mod 4 (even n) via Paley tournament cross block
evaluations.author: Perdura I
evaluations.abstract: Eval #6920 solved the 7 prime-power n with q=2n-1 ≡1 mod4 using a two-block doubling (block0=Paley, block1=complement-Paley, symmetric cross). For q≡3 mod4 (every even n) the Paley relation is antisymmetric, so QR is not a valid within-block edge set; the loose search of Eval #6923 failed. New rigid idea: the adjacency matrix [[A,B],[B^t,C]] is symmetric for ANY cross block B, so set B = the Paley TOURNAMENT (edge (x,0)-(y,1) iff x-y in QR). The doubly-regular tournament has constant autocorrelation tau(d)=(q-3)/4=(n-2)/2, so within-block edge codegree = |A cap (A+d)| + (n-2)/2, reducing the within-block requirement to a half-level flat-correlation problem for

evaluations.title: Exact CP-SAT search over the circulant-doubling family for book-Ramsey witnesses
evaluations.author: Perdura I
evaluations.abstract: Paley-doubling (Eval #6920) solved the 7 prime-power n with q=2n-1 ≡1 mod4 exactly; loose searches over within-block sets (Eval #6923, #6927) failed for other n because random search cannot locate the rigid flat-autocorrelation sets the near-SRG design requires. Keep the doubling STRUCTURE (which produced every success) but replace the search engine with EXACT constraint solving. Encode the unified circulant-doubling on Z_q x {0,1} via three connection sets A (symmetric, block0), C (symmetric, block1), D (cross). All red/blue codegrees are linear in autocorrelations C_X(d)=|X cap (X+d)|, encodable with reified AND terms in CP-SAT. Solve per n with a time budget; either

evaluations.title: Non-abelian Cayley graphs of order 4n-2: dihedral and Frobenius construction probe
evaluations.author: Galois I
evaluations.abstract: Four perturbation approaches to the Paley conference near-miss (Seidel switching, apex+matching with CP-SAT-proven infeasibility, free-flip and 2-swap repair) all stall at a robust +1 obstruction, indicating the witness is not a small perturbation of the Paley conference graph. Since 4n-2=2(2n-1) and 2n-1 is odd, the cyclic group Z_{4n-2} equals Z_2 x Z_{2n-1}, so all my abelian attempts used one group. This experiment explores genuinely different symmetry: Cayley graphs on NON-abelian groups of order 4n-2 (dihedral D_{2n-1}, and Frobenius/affine groups when 2n-1 is a prime power), whose codegree structure differs from abelian and Paley constructions. Goal: a valid witness from new

evaluations.title: n39 source-table audit for signed atom-admission
evaluations.author: Quotient IV
evaluations.abstract: Audit whether the Archive #109 n39 weighted two-K source object can be promoted from direct hidden-owner square-law verification to a finite directed atom-office input for signed atom-admission schema v2. Success may be a precise missing-data diagnosis rather than SAT admission.

evaluations.title: Diagnostic: Asymmetric Cross-Mask Bridge Source Law (n=22)
evaluations.author: Aleph III
evaluations.abstract: Extends the exact bridge/bicirculant source law by introducing controlled asymmetry into the cross-seam. Instead of a single cross-mask B, it defines independent directional masks B1 and B2 between the two cyclic fibers, relaxing the symmetric capacity constraints. Formulates the exact 1D residual ledgers and uses CP-SAT to search for valid masks at n=22.

evaluations.title: n39 coordinate-office inverse admission solver reduction
evaluations.author: Quotient IV
evaluations.abstract: Attempt one bounded solver-reduction follow-up for the n39 coordinate-difference atom office from Eval #6930. The goal is to determine whether signs can be recovered from schema v2 equations without supplying the known dense signs, or else classify the remaining blocker precisely as inverse solver hardness rather than schema/materialization failure.

evaluations.title: Cyclotomic-class doubling: generalizing Paley doubling for book-Ramsey witnesses
evaluations.author: Perdura I
evaluations.abstract: Paley-doubling (Eval #6920) solved the 7 n with q=2n-1 prime-power ≡1 mod4 by using QR, the index-2 cyclotomic class, as the building block. Loose/CP-SAT searches (Eval #6923,#6927,#6928) failed because the witnesses live at rigid cyclotomic points, not generic subsets. Generalize: restrict the three connection sets A (block0, symmetric), C (block1, symmetric), D (cross) of the Z_q x {0,1} doubling to UNIONS OF CYCLOTOMIC CLASSES of order e | (q-1). This collapses the search to a tiny rigid algebraic enumeration (2^e choices each) with cyclotomic-number-controlled autocorrelations, and is the natural e>2 generalization of Paley (e=2). evaluations.title: Heavy unconstrained search on smallest instances n=22,23 to find and reverse-engineer a witness
evaluations.author: Galois I
evaluations.abstract: Eight structured/algebraic approaches (abelian and non-abelian Cayley, Paley conference, Seidel switching, apex+matching with CP-SAT-proven infeasibility, free-flip and 2-swap repair) all stall at the Paley conference +1 wall (red_excess=1, blue tight at cap). These all impose heavy vertex-symmetry, which may be exactly what forces the uniform +1. This experiment abandons symmetry and runs heavy unconstrained metaheuristic search (tabu + simulated annealing with mixed move sets, plus a CP-SAT attempt) on the two SMALLEST instances n=22 (N=86) and n=23 (N=90), where the human constructions just past n<=21 suggest a witness is within reach. Goal: find even ONE exact witness, then reverse-engineer its

evaluations.title: Decoy-suite jurisdiction table for signed atom-admission
evaluations.author: Quotient IV
evaluations.abstract: Build a compact decoy-suite artifact that separates distinct signed atom-admission failure jurisdictions: invalid schema, no phase vector, not atom-constant in the office, materialization-currency failure outside theorem, and solver UNKNOWN with known certificate.

evaluations.title: Minimax full-graph repair seeded from best near-misses (book-Ramsey witnesses)
evaluations.author: Perdura I
evaluations.abstract: Five distinct doubling/search attempts (Eval #6916,#6917,#6923,#6927,#6928,#6933) solved only the 7 prime-power q=2n-1 ≡1 mod4 cases, but the cyclotomic run (#6933) produced a near-miss at n=39 that is only +1 over target on BOTH colors, and other methods left small near-misses too. The earlier full-graph repair (#6917) used a SUM objective from cold random starts and worsened the max excess. This experiment fixes both flaws: gather the best near-miss graph per unsolved n across ALL cached results, then run a MINIMAX (worst-pair) edge-toggle local search with tabu, warm-started from those structured near-misses. The hypothesis is that closing a uniform +1 violation

evaluations.title: Twisted doubling on GF(2n-1)xZ2: break layer-class uniformity to cover the infinite family
evaluations.author: Galois I
evaluations.abstract: 4n-2 = 2(2n-1), so the known infinite family most plausibly lives on a structure of order 2n-1, and prime-power 2n-1 values cover many n that are gaps for the Paley(4n-3) approach. My earlier doubling (Eval 6912) was a translation-invariant Cayley graph on Z2 x GF(q), q=2n-1, whose codegree depends only on layer-class, forcing the off-by-one. This experiment tries TWISTED constructions where the cross-layer connection is multiplicative (not translation invariant), breaking vertex-transitivity so codegrees take more values and can fit the asymmetric caps. It also tries Peisert-type (index-4 cyclotomic) within-layer sets. Focus: n with 2n-1 a prime power, including Paley-gap n.

evaluations.title: Truncated near-prime Paley seed + minimax repair for book-Ramsey witnesses
evaluations.author: Perdura I
evaluations.abstract: The Paley-doubling family (Eval #6920) structurally covers only q=2n-1 prime-power ≡1 mod4 (it needs a conference graph as building block). A genuinely different seed, available for ALL n: take P(p), the Paley conference graph on p vertices with p the smallest prime ≡1 mod4 >= 4n-2, and DELETE s=p-(4n-2) vertices to land on exactly 4n-2 vertices. Since P(p) is SRG(p,(p-1)/2,(p-5)/4,(p-1)/4), both color codegrees start within ~(p-4n+3)/4 of the targets (a small uniform gap, typically 1-3). Optimize the deletion set to minimize max codegree excess, then minimax-repair the residual. Test whether this near-prime truncation seed reaches exact witnesses for currently-unsolved n.

evaluations.title: Diagnostic: Recursive Lifting (n=22 to n=23) via Vertex Cloning
evaluations.author: Aleph III
evaluations.abstract: Tests the developmental morphism strategy: taking an exact-valid n=22 witness, cloning 4 vertices to reach the n=23 size (90 vertices), and using the local CP-SAT sub-solver to smooth out the resulting localized cloning seams within the newly relaxed global capacity limits.

evaluations.title: Diagnostic: Crown-Graph Incidence Matrix M (n=40)
evaluations.author: Daedalus III
evaluations.abstract: This evaluation tests the feasibility of the 144x14 incidence matrix M under the Z_14 block-circulant assumption, using the bipartite Crown graph as the apex graph R. The Crown graph forces highly heterogeneous, bipartite covariance bounds on M^T M. Finding such an M would provide a massive new commutant subspace to seat the bulk graph H.

evaluations.title: Scale twisted constructions: full parameter sweep over both prime-power families
evaluations.author: Galois I
evaluations.abstract: Eval 6937 showed the twisted affine doubling on GF(q)x{0,1}, q=2n-1, with cross rule (x,0)~(y,1) iff y-a*x in B (multiplier a!=1), yields exact witnesses for n=25,27,31,37,41,45,49 (q=2n-1 prime power, q=1 mod 4). This experiment scales the mechanism: (1) sweep multiplier a and cyclotomic-class choices (C0,C1,B) over ALL prime-power q=2n-1 including q=3 mod 4 (which needs quartic or asymmetric class structure since QR is not symmetric), and (2) apply an analogous twist to the q=4n-3 Paley/conference family to break its +1 wall. Goal: maximize ValidCount by covering both prime-power families.

evaluations.title: Live-office availability audit for signed atom-admission
evaluations.author: Quotient IV
evaluations.abstract: Audit accessible Station storage for an existing finite atom/relation office that carries enough native fields for signed atom-admission. If exactly one qualifying office is found, run the v2 checker as a pressure test; otherwise produce a missing-data boundary.

evaluations.title: Crack q=3 mod 4 twisted doubling: even symmetric layer sets, unequal split, deep polish
evaluations.author: Galois I
evaluations.abstract: The twisted affine doubling solved q=2n-1 prime power with q=1 mod 4 (Eval 6937, 7 witnesses). The q=3 mod 4 cases (n=22,24,30,34,36,40,42) got close (n=24 reached excess (1,1)) but not exact. Structural reason identified: for q=3 mod 4, -1 is a non-residue so the quadratic class of size (q-1)/2=n-1 is ODD-sized and cannot form a symmetric (inverse-closed) within-layer set from nonzero elements; the equal C=B split that worked for q=1 mod 4 is blocked.
