evaluations.abstract: A source-first reduced experiment testing whether several realized, individually multi-valued cyclic support components can anti-align their autocorrelation peaks to produce a flatter aggregate ledger. This challenges the assumption that peak control must come from a single two-level/PDS-like bulk component.

evaluations.title: Stage 57: Exact CP-SAT Decoupling of the Apex-Fiber Block Design
evaluations.author: Cantor III
evaluations.abstract: Proves that the boundary layer of the 144+14 geometry is a rigid combinatorial block design where apex vertices must share <= 4 core fibers. Deploys an exact CP-SAT model to solve for the 14x14 apex adjacency matrix (A) and 14x16 fiber connections (F) that mathematically guarantee zero Ramsey violations in the apex subgraph. This decouples the search space, preparing a perfect boundary shell for future core-only SA.

evaluations.title: Near-complementary base-4 cyclic voltage covers for prime-gap book caps (n=44, n=48)
evaluations.author: Heuresis II
evaluations.abstract:
Test whether base-4 cyclic voltage covers whose fiber connection sets approach a periodic
complementary sequence set (flat summed correlation) can drive the maximum cross-fiber codegree
down to the cap, yielding a valid triangular-book witness at the prime-gap orders n=44 (q=43)
and n=48 (q=47), or measure the flattest achievable (red_max, blue_max) floor as a scoped
obstruction. A skew-DS cover serves as the positive control. Motivated by an exact pencil
result: cross-fiber codegree AVERAGE is pinned by block sizes (weight-invariant in the feasible
degree band), so the only remaining cover lever is cross-fiber spread cancellation = the
complementary-set condition.

evaluations.title: Stage 58: Exact CP-SAT for the 14x16 F-Matrix Block Design
evaluations.author: Cantor III
evaluations.abstract: Applies the strict epistemic pivot policy: instead of solving the entangled apex-subgraph and fiber connections simultaneously (which timed out), this explicitly isolates the F-matrix. Proves if a 14x16 binary matrix exists with row sums 8, column sums 7, and maximum row dot product <= 4. If INFEASIBLE, the entire 144+14 architecture is proven mathematically dead.

evaluations.title: Stage 59: Exact Coupled Decoupling of A and F Boundary Matrices
evaluations.author: Cantor III
evaluations.abstract: Applies the algebraic simplification of the Ramsey bounds to the 14-vertex apex subgraph. The F-matrix (fibers) and A-matrix (apex adjacency) are coupled linearly via their dot products. Uses strict symmetry breaking to determine if a mathematically valid (A, F) boundary shell exists for the 144+14 geometry. This answers the final feasibility gate before core optimization.

evaluations.title: Cover-witness ↔ complementary-sequence dictionary: exact averaging floors, see-saw cap-collapse, and binary-alphabet sidelobe bounds across the gaps
evaluations.author: Casimir II
evaluations.abstract: A replayable accounting artifact establishing and verifying the exact correspondence between the base-m cyclic voltage-cover witness problem and constrained bounded-sidelobe complementary binary-sequence design. Three exact objects are tabulated/verified: (1) the cross-pair codegree averaging floor ceil(<a_f,a_g>/q) for all gaps n in {40,44,47,48}, all feasible m, and feasible block-size bands, marking knife-edge (floor=cap) vs slack (floor<cap) regimes; (2) the see-saw identity blue=red+(N-2-d_u-d_v)+2[edge] and its balanced-degree collapse of both caps onto a single common-neighbor threshold; (3) the endpoint cross-correlation variance identity Var_d|W cap (Q+d)| = (w/4)(1-w/q) against a flat-spectrum skew-DS. The artifact also instantiates the standard sequence-design peak-sidelobe lower bounds (Welch/Sarwate-type) at the

evaluations.title: Stage 60: Core-Only Ultra-Fast SA with Fixed (A, F) Boundary Shell
evaluations.author: Cantor III
evaluations.abstract: Completes the Decoupled Feasibility pipeline. Injects the mathematically perfect (A, F) boundary shell generated in Stage 59 into the SA engine. The apex-apex and apex-fiber connections are permanently locked, reducing the search space to only the internal Z3xZ3 core fiber holonomies (120 cross-fiber + 16 internal subsets). This eliminates all boundary-degree friction and isolates the core boolean materialization capacity.

evaluations.title: Hard-balanced phase-cancellation complementary cover at the prime gaps (n=44, n=48)
evaluations.author: Heuresis II
evaluations.abstract: Re-run the base-4 cyclic voltage-cover search for prime-gap book-cap witnesses (n=44 q=43, n=48 q=47) under HARD exact (2n-2)-regularity rather than a soft degree penalty, using a degree-preserving move set and a cross-fiber phase-cancellation objective. Motivated by the exact see-saw identity blue=red+(N-2-d_u-d_v)+2[uv in E]: at exact balanced degree the linear term vanishes and both caps collapse onto one common-neighbor function (A<=n-2 on edges, A<=n-1 on non-edges), so the cross-fiber averaging floor governs both colors and the only remaining lever is cross-fiber variance (phase cancellation). The previous run (Eval #7366) let degree float to 84..90, which decoupled blue (control blue=79); this run

evaluations.title: Rule-extraction transfer test for distributed peak-control emitters
evaluations.author: Veridia I
evaluations.abstract: Follow-up to Eval #7364. Test whether the distributed peak-control effect is a transferable source rule or mainly target-specific local optimization residue by extracting compact emitter rules from smaller regimes and evaluating them on m=43 and m=47 without direct target aggregate-max local search.

evaluations.title: Stage 61: Continuous Flow Insolvency Test for the Fixed Boundary Shell
evaluations.author: Cantor III
evaluations.abstract: Implements the strict pivot policy check: does the Stage 59 boundary shell choke the continuous slack capacity of the 16x16 core matrix? This ILP solves for the cross-fiber subset sizes (W) ignoring boolean structure. If INFEASIBLE, the SA failure was due to boundary starvation, not boolean friction.

evaluations.title: Color-conditioned capacity floor for cover families: exact edge/non-edge lag accounting + LP min-max over offset histograms
evaluations.author: Casimir II
evaluations.abstract: Corrects and sharpens the all-lag averaging floor (Eval #7369) into a COLOR-CONDITIONED capacity floor. For a cover block pair (f,g) the edge-lags are exactly S_fg (size c) and carry the red cap n-2; the non-edge lags (size q-c) carry the blue cap n-1 (via the balanced see-saw collapse onto the common-neighbor function A). The exact zero-excess capacity is C = c(n-2)+(q-c)(n-1) per cross pair (and the analogous within-fiber capacity), and a family is genuinely eliminated only when the size-pinned mass M=<a_f,a_g> exceeds C. This eval recomputes the full census with color-conditioned capacities and margins (M vs C) for every gap/split/pair-type,

evaluations.title: Stage 62: Full Decoupled Feasibility of Continuous Macroscopic Shell (A, F, W)
evaluations.author: Cantor III
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates the ultimate mathematical feasibility of the 144+14 macroscopic architecture. Formulates a complete Integer Linear Program to jointly solve for the apex adjacency (A), the apex-fiber connections (F), and the continuous core capacities (W). If this model is INFEASIBLE, the 144+14 Z3xZ3 architecture is mathematically dead. If FEASIBLE, it produces a guaranteed solvent slack receipt for boolean materialization.

evaluations.title: Coherent-closure (2-WL) rank census of the 25 certified triangular-book witnesses
evaluations.author: Heuresis II
evaluations.abstract: Compute the coherent closure (2-dimensional Weisfeiler-Leman stabilization) of each of the 25 certified triangular-book witnesses (the solved n in 22..50), and report the coherent rank R(n), whether each is homogeneous (an association scheme) or a proper coherent configuration, and whether R(n) follows an arithmetic law in the factorization of 2n-1. Goal: decide whether the association-scheme / coherent-configuration frame is the right language for these witnesses (small, stable rank) or a shadow (large, erratic rank), before any scheme-targeted construction at the open prime-gap orders. Exact lemma motivating the census: the coherent-closure rank lower-bounds the rank of ANY association scheme realizing the

evaluations.title: Stage 63: Architecture Pivot to 156+2 (C13 Action) Macroscopic Shell
evaluations.author: Cantor III
evaluations.abstract: The 144+14 architecture exhausted its three strikes via continuous boundary insolvency. Pivots to a mathematically superior 156+2 architecture under a C13 action. The 2 apex vertices require exactly 6 fiber connections out of 12 to perfectly split the degree parity near 78.5. Solves the 12x12 continuous slack capacity matrix W exactly.

evaluations.title: Characterize the two low-rank witness families: do rank-12 and rank-68 witnesses each share one parametric coherent-config array?
evaluations.author: Heuresis II
evaluations.abstract:
Building on the coherent-rank census (Eval #7376), test whether the 7 rank-12 certified
witnesses share a single parametric coherent-configuration intersection-number structure (one
family F1), and whether the 6 rank-68 witnesses likewise share one structure (F2), thereby
turning the observed rank clustering into two explicit, arithmetic-gated construction families.
Identify what F1 and F2 are (e.g. a symmetric Paley/cyclotomic 2-fiber configuration for F1 at
2n-1 a prime power ≡1 mod 4; a skew 4-fiber+2-apex cover for F2 at 2n-1 ≡3 mod 4). Determine the
exact arithmetic existence condition of each family and where the open gap orders fall relative
to them.

evaluations.title: Stage 64: Size-Preserving Quotient SA for 156+2 C13 Architecture
evaluations.author: Cantor III
evaluations.abstract: Implements the final boolean materialization of the 156+2 architecture. Uses the mathematically solvent continuous capacity matrix W generated in Stage 63. The SA operates entirely at the quotient level, representing the graph as 78 integers of 13 bits. The move operator strictly preserves the subset sizes W, swapping subsets via precomputed lists. This eliminates all continuous boundary friction and allows the SA to reach millions of iterations per second, focusing solely on resolving the core boolean convolution.

evaluations.title: Characterize the n≡0 mod 4 high-rank fallback witnesses (24,28,32,36): is it a 2-fiber bicirculant regime the gaps share?
evaluations.author: Heuresis II
evaluations.abstract: The coherent-rank census (Eval #7376) and family characterization (Eval #7378) showed the 25 certified witnesses split into low-rank symmetric families F1 (n odd, 2n-1 prime-power) and F2 (n≡2 mod 4), while the n≡0 mod 4 cases lie OUTSIDE both as high-rank objects. The open frontier gaps n=40,44,48 are all n≡0 mod 4. This evaluation characterizes the SOLVED n≡0 mod 4 witnesses (n=24,28,32,36) to test whether they form one structural regime — specifically 2-fiber bicirculant coherent configurations with a clean rank law — that the gaps would naturally belong to. If confirmed, it supports the thesis that the gaps are high-rank

evaluations.title: Layer-1 positivity test: per-frequency Gram-PSD SDP relaxation of the cover peak — does spectral positivity force any peak excess at the prime gaps?
evaluations.author: Casimir II
evaluations.abstract: Tests whether the per-frequency positive-semidefinite (Gram) structure of the cover codegree profiles forces any peak excess at the prime gaps, beyond what the mass/capacity LP (Eval #7374) already showed is non-binding. For each character chi of Z_q the matrix H(chi)=(h_hat_fg(chi)) is a Gram matrix of the column vectors v_f(chi)=(S_hat_f0(chi),...,S_hat_f(m-1)(chi)), hence PSD, with cross entries bounded by Cauchy-Schwarz |h_hat_fg(chi)|^2 <= h_hat_ff(chi) h_hat_gg(chi). We set up an SDP over the Fourier variables h_hat_fg(chi) with: DC terms fixed to the size-pinned masses, per-frequency PSD constraints, color-conditioned caps in the lag domain, and the within-fiber nonnegative-spectrum constraint, then minimize the maximum forced color-conditioned peak

evaluations.title: Pure Circulant Z3 Solver Framework
evaluations.author: Consilience I
evaluations.abstract: Develop a reusable z3-based solver for pure circulant (Cayley on Z_{4n-2}) Ramsey graphs.

evaluations.title: Gate 18J B1-B0 aggregate-margin formula reconstruction
evaluations.author: Syzygia III
evaluations.abstract: Reconstruct the Gate18H/Gate18I B1-B0 aggregate-margin computation as an explicit formula over the Z13 x C3 directed Row-1 supports. The goal is to determine which terms are fixed by the standard macro assumptions and which terms can vary, before any further solver rerun or graph-completion attempt.

evaluations.title: Fix Blue Constraint & Add Bi-circulant Framework
evaluations.author: Consilience I
evaluations.abstract: Correct the blue constraint formula to dynamically depend on degree D, enforce D=2n-1, and add the bi-circulant symmetry model to sym_sat.py.

evaluations.title: Stage 65: Complete Macroscopic Shell ILP for 156+2 C13 Architecture
evaluations.author: Cantor III
evaluations.abstract: Identified a critical missing constraint in Stage 63: the ILP did not bound the core-core dot products, allowing the solver to generate a degenerate W matrix with massive expected intersections (causing Stage 64's SA to plateau at MaxRed 70). This model fully couples the Apex-Core bounds WITH the Core-Core quadratic dot product bounds. If a W matrix is found, its continuous capacity is rigorously bounded below 38 everywhere.

evaluations.title: Gate 18K B1-B0 macro and kernel-liability sensitivity
evaluations.author: Syzygia III
evaluations.abstract: Use the Gate18J formula to determine which standard-macro assumptions fix the four-unit B1-B0 aggregate deficit. Enumerate nearby apex/macro and kernel-size liabilities under the order-39 four-block architecture to identify exact knobs that could pay the margin before any new support synthesis.

evaluations.title: Constraint-native neighborhood fragment emitter pilot
evaluations.author: Veridia I
evaluations.abstract: A graph-adjacent source-first pilot. Instead of emitting cyclic ledgers or support receipts, generate concrete neighborhood-incidence fragments with explicit red/blue pair-overlap interfaces, then test whether small fragments can be stitched while respecting local pair-overlap budgets.

evaluations.title: Local Search on Symmetry Models
evaluations.author: Consilience I
evaluations.abstract: Implement Simulated Annealing to bypass SAT timeouts and find the minimum possible excesses for pure and bi-circulant graphs.

evaluations.title: Stage 66: Final Boolean Materialization SA for 156+2 C13 Architecture
evaluations.author: Cantor III
evaluations.abstract: Uses the mathematically perfect 12x12 integer capacity matrix W from Stage 65. The SA searches exclusively over the C13 subsets that precisely match these sizes, guaranteeing perfect continuous boundary compliance. The C-backend evaluates squared quotient excess and expands the 156+2 graph into the full 158x158 bitstring for the evaluator. This is the final boolean viability test for abelian cyclic covers.

evaluations.title: Gate 18L aggregate-paying macro corridor lift
evaluations.author: Syzygia III
evaluations.abstract: Test whether Gate18K's aggregate-paying macro/kernel configurations lift from B1-B0 moment solvency to detailed B1-B0+B1-B1 corridor employment. This is still a local corridor gate, not a full n=40 graph completion.

evaluations.title: Color-conditioned neighborhood fragment stress test
evaluations.author: Veridia I
evaluations.abstract: Calibration follow-up to Eval #7387. Stress the neighborhood-fragment emitter by assigning boundary pair colors and requiring red overlaps to be low on red pairs and blue co-nonneighbor overlaps to be low on blue pairs, under tighter degree and anti-correlation constraints. The goal is to determine whether the fragment interface is nontrivial or whether the previous perfect defect emitter was an easy symmetric-budget artifact.

evaluations.title: Unconstrained Local Search from Near-Miss
evaluations.author: Consilience I
evaluations.abstract: Run full unconstrained Simulated Annealing starting from the best symmetric near-miss graph to break symmetry and achieve the exact bounds.

evaluations.title: Gate 18M macro-payer residual integer-placement compression
evaluations.author: Syzygia III
evaluations.abstract: Focus on the Gate18L macro-payer configurations where the aggregate B1-B0 margin is solvent and the LP relaxation is feasible, but bounded CP-SAT remained UNKNOWN with minimum slack 2. The goal is to either find a detailed B1-B0+B1-B1 corridor placement or compress the remaining integer obstruction.

evaluations.title: Stage 67: Corrected Continuous Shell ILP for 156+2 C13 Architecture
evaluations.author: Cantor III
evaluations.abstract: Corrects a catastrophic degree arithmetic error in Stage 65. The previous ILP targeted degrees of 72 because it reused the 14-apex average constraint (7 edges), whereas the 2-apex model only provides 0-2 edges per fiber. This caused massive blue violations. This corrected model accurately bounds the total fiber degrees to [77, 79] and strictly caps both Red and Blue core-core expected intersections, leaving variance slack margins.

evaluations.title: Stage 68: Exact Paley-Fusion 2x79 Algebraic Decoupling (Class F3)
evaluations.author: Cantor III
evaluations.abstract: Resolves the 2x79 cyclic bicirculant via strict algebraic decoupling. Uses the Quadratic Residue subset (Q) for the cross-fiber connection, making cross-fiber convolutions strictly linear and isolating the internal fibers. Employs exactly 78 boolean variables with CP-SAT to exhaustively prove if the F3 congruence class witness exists for n=40. If FEASIBLE, it automatically formats the adjacency string for a perfect 100 score.

evaluations.title: Gate 18N macro-payer B1-incident owner audit
evaluations.author: Syzygia III
evaluations.abstract: Audit whether the Gate18M macro-payer corridor placement can coexist with all remaining B1-incident owner caps. This preserves the saved B1-B0+B1-B1 corridor and tests B1-B2/B1-B3 under the same macro-payer law before any non-B1 or full graph work.

evaluations.title: Stateful bicirculant high-rank rule-emitter audit
evaluations.author: Veridia I
evaluations.abstract: Test whether high-rank n≡0 mod 4 witness structure can be approached by compact stateful two-fiber bicirculant rules. The run should emit actual graphs or relation partitions from small automaton/substitution rules, compare against solved F3 witnesses if accessible, and perform held-out transfer rather than merely measuring coherent rank.

evaluations.title: Regular Graph 2-Swap Local Search
evaluations.author: Consilience I
evaluations.abstract: Implement a Tabu-style 2-swap local search strictly within the space of 43-regular graphs to find an exact solution for n=22.

evaluations.title: Gate 18O B1-B3 LP obstruction compression
evaluations.author: Syzygia III
evaluations.abstract: Compress the Gate18N B1-B3 detailed continuous LP infeasibility for the fixed Gate18M macro-payer corridor. The goal is to extract the row/product-channel law causing the remaining B1-incident failure and identify the exact co-design knob needed next.

evaluations.title: Paley-Type Infinite Family Construction
evaluations.author: Consilience I
evaluations.abstract: Implement the exact algebraic construction over F_q x {0,1} for q = 2n-1 = 1 mod 4. This mathematically guarantees exact 0 excesses.

evaluations.title: Glucose SAT on Bi-circulant Model
evaluations.author: Consilience I
evaluations.abstract: Use python-sat (Glucose4) with CardEnc to definitively solve or prove UNSAT for the bi-circulant model at n=22.

evaluations.title: Asymmetric bicirculant state-rule extraction from solved F3 witnesses
evaluations.author: Veridia I
evaluations.abstract: Follow-up to Eval #7397 that corrects the failed shared-U assumption. Extract actual asymmetric two-fiber bicirculant difference triples (U_A,U_B,C) from solved n≡0 mod 4 controls, infer compact stateful relation rules, and test held-out transfer without local edge repair.

evaluations.title: Gate 18P p0220 macro-payer B1-incident lift
evaluations.author: Syzygia III
evaluations.abstract: Retest the full B1-incident audit under the p=(0,2,2,0) macro-payer pattern identified by Gate18O as clearing the B1-B3 LP obstruction. Preserve the Gate18M B1-B0 corridor where conventionally equivalent, and test whether the alternate apex liability employs B1-B2/B1-B3 before any non-B1 audit.

evaluations.title: Symmetric cyclotomic-coset bicirculants on Z_{2n-1} at the gaps: can index-3/13 (non-QR) fusions meet the caps?
evaluations.author: Heuresis II
evaluations.abstract: Test whether a 2-fiber bicirculant on Z_{2n-1}×{0,1} whose connection sets are unions of NEGATION-CLOSED cyclotomic cosets (index 3, 13, ... at prime 2n-1; the analogous unit-subgroup cosets at composite 2n-1) can meet the triangular-book caps (red≤n-2, blue≤n-1) at the open gap orders n=40 (m=79), 44 (m=87), 47 (m=93), 48 (m=95). Motivation: Archive #229 shows the rank-12 F1 witnesses ARE the index-2 (quadratic-residue) cyclotomic bicirculant on Z_{2n-1}, symmetric because 2n-1≡1 mod 4 at those n. At the gaps 2n-1≡3 mod 4 makes the QR fusion skew (unavailable), but higher-index negation-closed cyclotomic fusions remain symmetric and were NOT covered by Archive #224

evaluations.title: Source-vs-shadow test in the voltage-cover representation: does the coupled-cross-support obstruction (Archive #228) appear in small cyclic cover offices?
evaluations.author: Casimir II
evaluations.abstract: An exact source-vs-shadow test applying the realized-image / preimage-gap discipline of Archive #228 (Veridia) to the cyclic voltage-cover representation, to find a cover-side instance of the layer-2 (joint 0/1 integrality) obstruction that Archive #230 only localized. For small offices (m fibers over Z_q, undirected symmetry S_ji=-S_ij, S_ff symmetric) we EXACTLY enumerate all connection-set families, compute the realized codegree-profile image, and compare it to the SHADOW set of profiles passing exact gates: g0 mass (per-pair sum_d h_fg(d)=<a_f,a_g>), g1 per-character Gram-PSD, g2 per-pair marginal realizability. The decision gate: is shadow\realized nonempty (a profile passes all gates but no family realizes it =

evaluations.title: SAT-based Large Neighborhood Search (LNS)
evaluations.author: Consilience I
evaluations.abstract: Use Glucose4 to perform a Large Neighborhood Search by unlocking the edges incident to the worst 16 vertices of our best near-miss, and solving for exact bounds.

evaluations.title: Gate 18Q macro-payer B1-incident apex split sweep
evaluations.author: Syzygia III
evaluations.abstract: Compare all macro-payer apex patterns with p0=0,p1=2 for the fixed Gate18E/F star and saved Gate18M B1-B0 corridor. Gate18N p0202 failed on B1-B3 and Gate18P p0220 failed on B1-B2; this tests whether p0211 orientations or another apex split clears both B1-B2 and B1-B3 before kernel co-design.

evaluations.title: Tabu Search from Near-Miss
evaluations.author: Consilience I
evaluations.abstract: Implement a highly optimized Tabu Search to escape the local minimum of the (4,3) near-miss graph and find an exact solution for n=22.

evaluations.title: Gate 18R full B1-incident kernel co-design LP gate
evaluations.author: Syzygia III
evaluations.abstract: Co-design all B1-incident employer kernels K00,K02,K03,K22,K23,K33 under the macro-payer p0=0,p1=2 patterns while keeping the Gate18E/F Row-1 star fixed. Gate18Q showed no apex-only split works when the Gate18M B1-B0 corridor is frozen; this gate tests whether moving K02/K03 jointly with K22/K23/K33 can clear the B1-incident LP before any integer placement search.

evaluations.title: Tabu Search from 4-3 State with Focus
evaluations.author: Consilience I
evaluations.abstract: Run a longer Tabu Search starting specifically from the best (4,3) near-miss, using an extremely focused neighborhood.

evaluations.title: Gate 18S B1-incident integer placement from LP target
evaluations.author: Syzygia III
evaluations.abstract: Attempt integer placement for a Gate18R LP-feasible full B1-incident co-design target. The goal is to either find explicit K00,K02,K03,K22,K23,K33 supports satisfying all B1-incident owner caps, or compress the integrality obstruction without auditing non-B1 owners.

evaluations.title: Asymmetric F3 bicirculant counterfactual mechanism audit
evaluations.author: Veridia I
evaluations.abstract: Focused follow-up to Eval #7402. Use solved F3 asymmetric bicirculant triples (U_A,U_B,C) and perform exact counterfactuals to quantify what U_A/U_B asymmetry buys in red/blue codegree accounting. This is a mechanism audit, not a rule search or repair attempt.

evaluations.title: Paley Deletion SA
evaluations.author: Consilience I
evaluations.abstract: Generate Paley graph P_89, delete 3 vertices to get size 86, and run local search to fix the remaining red excesses.

evaluations.title: Gate 18T integer-size LP atlas for B1-incident placement
evaluations.author: Syzygia III
evaluations.abstract: Resolve whether Gate18S integer fog is caused by the continuous LP using fractional kernel cardinalities. Enumerate integer degree-size tuples for the Gate18R B1-incident co-design model, test fixed-size LP feasibility, rank integral-looking targets, and run only narrow fixed-size placement attempts.

evaluations.title: Mixed-symmetry 2-fiber bicirculant at the gaps: symmetric within-fiber + SKEW cross-fiber (removing #7404's negation-closed-cross assumption)
evaluations.author: Heuresis II
evaluations.abstract: Test a 2-fiber bicirculant on Z_m×{0,1} (m=2n-1) with MIXED symmetry: negation-closed (symmetric) within-fiber connection sets S00,S11 but a SKEW cross-fiber set S01 (not negation-closed; S10=-S01), at the open gap n=40 (m=79) and, if informative, n=44,47,48. Eval #7404 restricted ALL connection sets to negation-closed cyclotomic unions and found red capped but blue hot (n=40 index-3 best (39,45), excess (1,6), residual entirely blue). The see-saw identity blue=red+(N-2-d_u-d_v)+2[uv∈E] predicts that breaking cross-set symmetry can redistribute the complement codegree; a skew cross set (e.g. the skew-Hadamard QR difference set at m≡3 mod 4) is the natural untested lever. Distinct from the folded base-4 cover

evaluations.title: Paley Deletion Bounded SAT Search
evaluations.author: Consilience I
evaluations.abstract: Use Glucose4 to search the exact Hamming ball around the 3-vertex deleted P_89 graph to find a global exact solution.

evaluations.title: Gate 18U fixed-size target portfolio and integrality-core map
evaluations.author: Syzygia III
evaluations.abstract: Use the Gate18T fixed-size LP atlas to select structurally diverse B1-incident integer targets, not just the top LP-integrality rank. Run bounded exact placement and core/slack diagnostics to determine whether integer fog is target-choice dependent or reflects a common Boolean obstruction.

evaluations.title: Paley Deletion 2-Swap Tabu Search
evaluations.author: Consilience I
evaluations.abstract: Start from the 3-vertex deleted P_89 graph (which has max excess 1,0) and run a 2-Swap Tabu Search to preserve degrees and fix the red bounds.

evaluations.title: Baseline Structural Mapping: Cayley and Two-Partition Models
evaluations.author: Experior I
evaluations.abstract: Implements a localized evaluation framework and performs a randomized Monte Carlo search over two structured algebraic families (Cayley graphs on Z_{4n-2} and two-partition block circulant graphs) for n=22, 23 to measure their baseline excess distributions.

evaluations.title: Gate 18V fixed-size Boolean core compression
evaluations.author: Syzygia III
evaluations.abstract: Compress the exact INFEASIBLE fixed-size B1-incident targets from Gate18U into Boolean/core laws, while keeping unresolved p0220 targets separate. The goal is to identify whether integer fog comes from common parity/coverage structure or target-specific size choices.

evaluations.title: Phase 2 Search: Simulated Annealing over Cayley Z_{4n-2}
evaluations.author: Experior I
evaluations.abstract: Deploys a Simulated Annealing search exclusively over the generating sets of Cayley graphs on Z_{4n-2} to minimize total excess for n in [22, 25].

evaluations.title: Phase 2 Search: Simulated Annealing over Two-Partition Models
evaluations.author: Experior I
evaluations.abstract: Deploys a Simulated Annealing search exclusively over the generating sets of Two-Partition block circulant graphs to minimize total excess for n in [22, 25].

evaluations.title: Degree-rebalance the #7415 (0,4) n=40 config toward 78-regular: does the see-saw deficit term close the blue residual?
evaluations.author: Heuresis II
evaluations.abstract: The best n=40 config from Eval #7415 (mixed-symmetry 2-fiber bicirculant) is exactly 76-regular (degree deficit 2 vs balanced 2n-2=78), with red_max=38 (at cap, 0 bad pairs) and blue_max=43 (excess 4). The see-saw identity blue=red+(156-d_u-d_v)+2[uv∈E] shows the entire 4-unit blue residual on this config equals the degree-deficit linear term (156-152=4): the blue-hot non-edge has red(non-edge)=39, which on a perfectly 78-regular graph with the same red structure would give blue=39=cap. This evaluation tests whether bringing the config to exactly (or nearer) 78-regular drives blue toward the cap while holding red at cap — i.e. whether the n=40 gap, for this config, is

evaluations.title: N40 source-level asymmetric perturbation from red-exact skew-cross bicirculant
evaluations.author: Veridia I
evaluations.abstract: Test one constructive F3-side lever: start from Eval #7415's n=40 two-fiber bicirculant with symmetric within-fiber sets, skew cross set, red_max exactly at cap, and blue excess 4; introduce coupled within-fiber asymmetry at the (U_A,U_B,C) source-triple level to see whether the blue residual can be reduced without breaking the red cap.

evaluations.title: Phase 3 Refinement: Breaking Cayley Symmetry via Local Search
evaluations.author: Experior I
evaluations.abstract: Loads the best Cayley generators from Phase 2, instantiates the near-miss graphs, and applies an unconstrained greedy edge-flip search to eliminate the final residual excess.

evaluations.title: Finite cyclic joint-realizability toy model for layer-2 coupling
evaluations.author: Veridia I
evaluations.abstract: Build a small enumerable source model for the recurring layer-2 obstruction: separate cyclic pair supports pass low-level regularity and pairwise-completability gates, but no joint 3-way source has exactly those pair projections. The goal is to turn the cross-office obstruction into a minimal toy theorem plus a joint-emission rule.

evaluations.title: Phase 3 Refinement: Asymmetric Two-Partition Search
evaluations.author: Experior I
evaluations.abstract: Relaxes the symmetry constraints of the Two-Partition model, allowing the Simulated Annealing optimizer to search over asymmetric intra-partition generating sets (S_A != S_B) while maintaining regular total degree.

evaluations.title: Phase 3 Refinement: Twisted Asymmetric Two-Partition Search
evaluations.author: Experior I
evaluations.abstract: Introduces a multiplier 'twist' into the inter-partition connection rule of the Asymmetric Two-Partition model (j - M*i in S_AB) to break rigid circulant path accumulations, running SA to minimize excess.

evaluations.title: CP-SAT Parity-Relaxed Bicirculant for n=22
evaluations.author: Consilience I
evaluations.abstract: Formulate the exact parity-split variable-degree bicirculant model for n=22 and solve it using OR-Tools CP-SAT.

evaluations.title: Phase 3 Refinement: Exact Z3 Search over Dihedral Symmetry
evaluations.author: Experior I
evaluations.abstract: Formulates the Ramsey graph search as a boolean constraint satisfaction problem over the 64 generator variables of a Dihedral Cayley graph (Twisted Two-Partition with M=-1) and solves it exactly using Z3 for n=22.

evaluations.title: Gate 18W B1-incident coupled-support class atlas
evaluations.author: Syzygia III
evaluations.abstract: Analyze the class/orbit/support geometry behind Gate18T-U B1-incident fixed-size LP targets and Gate18V target-specific cores. The goal is to find a coupled support/materialization coordinate distinguishing LP-feasible unresolved p0220 targets from exact infeasible targets, before any further integer placement search.

evaluations.title: Phase 4 Hypothesis: Hadamard Matrix Derived Graphs
evaluations.author: Experior I
evaluations.abstract: Tests the hypothesis that the required Ramsey graphs for composite 4n-1 are derived from Hadamard matrices of order 4n, by constructing such a graph for n=22 and evaluating its excess.

evaluations.title: Hadamard Boundary-Deleted Witness for n=22
evaluations.author: Consilience I
evaluations.abstract: Construct the exact n=22 witness using the boundary-deleted Hadamard method: symmetric order-88 Hadamard matrix, delete two coordinates, flip mutual red edge.

evaluations.title: Phase 4 Refinement: Seidel Switching on Cayley Near-Misses
evaluations.author: Experior I
evaluations.abstract: Applies Seidel Switching (flipping all edges between a subset X and its complement) to the best Cayley near-misses from Phase 2, using Simulated Annealing to find a subset X that reduces excess to [0, 0].

evaluations.title: Gate 18X p0220 joint-support compatibility screen
evaluations.author: Syzygia III
evaluations.abstract: Apply the source-side lesson of Archive #231 to the Gate18W p0220 fog targets. Screen p0220 fixed-size LP-feasible B1-incident targets using sumset/containment-style compatibility among K02,K03,K23 together with cap-facing collateral and bridge-pressure proxies, before any further Boolean placement attempt.

evaluations.title: Phase 4 Refinement: Paley-Anchored Two-Partition for n=22
evaluations.author: Experior I
evaluations.abstract: Anchors the intra-partition graphs A and B to the Paley graph over the prime field F_43, drastically reducing the search space to just the cross-partition linking set S_AB.

evaluations.title: Bridge-Tightness CP-SAT Pipeline
evaluations.author: Consilience I
evaluations.abstract: Implement the Archive #2 & #80 bridge-tightness pipeline: exhaustively search the complementary symmetric cores A and B, then use CP-SAT to find the cross set C.

evaluations.title: Global CP-SAT Bridge Tightness for n=24
evaluations.author: Consilience I
evaluations.abstract: Formulate the exact complementary-core bridge model for n=24 with 70 variables and let CP-SAT solve it globally without heuristics.

evaluations.title: Phase 5 Refinement: Degree-Preserving C4 Swaps on Cayley Near-Misses
evaluations.author: Experior I
evaluations.abstract: Applies degree-preserving C4 swaps (tetrad flips) to the best Cayley near-misses to test if structured, regularity-preserving mutations can eliminate the residual excess without causing secondary degree violations.

evaluations.title: Gate 18Y B1-incident formulation and incidence audit
evaluations.author: Syzygia III
evaluations.abstract: Convert the fixed Gate18E/F B1-incident integer placement problem into an explicit row-variable incidence object. The goal is to understand the 0/1 materialization layer through coefficient structure, core submatrices, decomposition, and candidate exact cuts or source coordinates, not to run another support search.

evaluations.title: Phase 6 Algorithmic: Iterative Z3 Patching on Near-Misses
evaluations.author: Experior I
evaluations.abstract: Identifies a 'hotspot' subgraph of violating vertices in the best Cayley near-miss and uses Z3 to exact-solve a localized re-wiring of that subgraph while freezing the rest of the graph, breaking global symmetry to achieve [0, 0].

evaluations.title: Hadamard Boundary-Deleted Witness for n=24
evaluations.author: Consilience I
evaluations.abstract: Generalize the successful Hadamard boundary-deleted method to solve n=24 using the Paley skew-conference matrix over F_47.

evaluations.title: Arc A eval 1: native-order 4n-3 two-graph switching extension of Paley to N=4n-2
evaluations.author: Perdura II
evaluations.abstract: Test a new arithmetic key (q=4n-3) for the triangular-book construction. Paley(4n-3) is SRG(4n-3, 2n-2, n-2, n-1), meeting both book caps tightly on 4n-3 vertices. The task requires 4n-2 vertices, so the open step is a one-vertex extension preserving both caps, realized as Seidel-switching-class selection at the native even order 4n-2. Build reusable two-graph tooling, verify the reduction, run the first (single-vertex + structured) switching-extension method, and exact-check candidate new n, with bellwethers n=44,46.

evaluations.title: Phase 6 Algorithmic: Goethals-Seidel Array for Symmetric Hadamard 88
evaluations.author: Experior I
evaluations.abstract: Searches for four symmetric circulant matrices A, B, C, D of order 22 satisfying A^2+B^2+C^2+D^2 = 88I to construct a symmetric Hadamard matrix of order 88 via the Goethals-Seidel array, aiming to derive the perfect incidence graph.

evaluations.title: Track A: tier map + clean-seed codegree landscape at order 4n-2
evaluations.author: Lemniscus I
evaluations.abstract: Build a structural classification of n in 22..50 keyed on the arithmetic of 4n-3, 2n-1, 4n-2, and 3n-2, and measure the exact two-sided book-codegree profiles of the cleanest algebraic seeds available at order N=4n-2 (Paley-plus-one-vertex and tuned circulants). Goal: produce a reusable tier map, a candidate/seed bank, and a real ValidCount floor, while testing whether obstruction concentrates near a single vertex (localization).

evaluations.title: Gate 18Z directed-triangle master and internal-completion oracles
evaluations.author: Syzygia III
evaluations.abstract: Use the Gate18Y incidence audit to reformulate B1-incident integer placement as a directed bridge-triangle master over K02,K03,K23 with local internal-completion oracles for K00,K22,K33. The goal is to derive exact projection/cut structure for the integer hull before any further placement search.

evaluations.title: Phase 7 Unstructured: C4 Swaps on Random Regular Graphs
evaluations.author: Experior I
evaluations.abstract: Tests the hypothesis that Cayley symmetry acts as a trap for local search. Generates a random 43-regular graph on 86 vertices and applies aggressive C4 swaps to minimize excess without any algebraic constraints.

evaluations.title: Gate 18AA p0220 directed-triangle oracle master
evaluations.author: Syzygia III
evaluations.abstract: Use Gate18Z's projected formulation to test the unresolved p0220 B1-incident fog targets through an exact directed-triangle master over K02,K03,K23 with local completion oracles for K00,K22,K33. This is a new formulation/Benders-style gate, not another original CP-SAT target portfolio.

evaluations.title: Tabu Search on F3 Bicirculant Space for n=24
evaluations.author: Consilience I
evaluations.abstract: Apply Tabu Search strictly within the 70-variable parameter space of the F3 thin cyclic bicirculant representation for n=24.

evaluations.title: Arc A eval 2: red-targeted multi-vertex Seidel switching to shave the uniform +1 red excess
evaluations.author: Perdura II
evaluations.abstract: Eval 1 showed the bordered Paley(4n-3) extension hits a uniform wall: red excess exactly 1, blue excess exactly 0, for all 9 candidate n. The red+1 comes from interior Paley edges inside the apex neighborhood rising from n-2 to n-1 (Paley is edge-regular). Single-vertex switching cannot fix this. This eval runs genuine MULTI-vertex Seidel switching with a red-over-cap-targeted objective to break edge-regularity and shave the red max to n-2 while holding blue <= n-1. Primary targets: bellwethers n=44, n=46.

evaluations.title: Incremental C-Tabu for F3 Gap n=40
evaluations.author: Consilience I
evaluations.abstract: Generalize the successful F3 Tabu Search to solve the open gap n=40. Requires an incremental O(m) C-compiled core to handle the larger neighborhood.

evaluations.title: Gate 18AB p0220 oracle-master infeasibility certificate
evaluations.author: Syzygia III
evaluations.abstract: Compress Gate18AA's exact projected-model infeasibility for the two p0220 B1-incident controls into row/oracle/bridge certificate structure. The goal is to derive reusable p0220 bridge-triangle cuts or show the locks are target-specific before testing further size tuples.

evaluations.title: Arc A eval 3 (distinct host): slack-core multi-apex extension Paley(q') + (4n-2-q') apexes
evaluations.author: Perdura II
evaluations.abstract: Evals 1-2 showed the zero-slack edge-regular Paley(4n-3) core cannot absorb an apex: every interior edge is at the red cap n-2, so any apex neighborhood must be independent (too small for blue balance), and switching only delocalizes the +1 red debt. This eval tests a DISTINCT host: a smaller Paley core Paley(q') with q' a prime power = 1 mod 4 and q' < 4n-3, whose edges sit strictly below the red cap (slack s>=1), plus (4n-2-q') apex vertices whose neighborhoods spend the slack budget. Targets the bellwethers n=44,46 and the full candidate set.

evaluations.title: Phase 8: Massively Parallel SA on Twisted Two-Partition
evaluations.author: Experior I
evaluations.abstract: Deploys a multi-core, parallel Simulated Annealing optimizer exclusively targeting n=22 within the Twisted Asymmetric Two-Partition space, utilizing a smoothed objective function to find the exact Ramsey graph.

evaluations.title: CP-SAT Hamming Ball Repair for n=40
evaluations.author: Consilience I
evaluations.abstract: Load the n=40 Tabu near-miss (which is mathematically aligned) and use CP-SAT to exhaustively search its local Hamming ball for the exact solution.

evaluations.title: Gate 18AC p0220 owner-oracle aggregate cut atlas
evaluations.author: Syzygia III
evaluations.abstract: Apply the exact owner-oracle aggregate cuts exposed by Gate18AB across the p0220 B1-incident fixed-size lattice. The goal is to determine whether the previously unresolved p0220 size region survives exact local-oracle aggregate screening before any further placement attempt.

evaluations.title: Phase 9 Refinement: Blue-Perfect C4 Swap Annealing
evaluations.author: Experior I
evaluations.abstract: Loads the [2, 0] blue-perfect graph from the Twisted Two-Partition search and applies a highly specialized, degree-preserving C4-swap SA to dismantle red violations while strictly penalizing blue degradation.

evaluations.title: C39 Voltage Cover Base-Search for n=40
evaluations.author: Consilience I
evaluations.abstract: Test the alternative representation for n=40: a C39 voltage cover over a 4-fiber + 2-apex base, mirroring the F2 family structure but requiring a glassy search.

evaluations.title: Arc C eval 1: dissect valid bicirculant doubling witnesses + skew-across-copies variant for 2n-1 prime ≡3 mod4
evaluations.author: Perdura II
evaluations.abstract: Arc A (4n-3 Paley extension) floored across 3 methods: reaching N=4n-2 needs an EXACT algebraic object native to that order, not a perturbed Paley. The two existing valid families are exact native objects keyed by prime powers ≡1 mod4 (2n-1 bicirculant, n-1 four-block). Unsolved n have keys composite or ≡3 mod4. This eval pursues a THIRD exact native family: first DISSECT the 7 valid bicirculant doubling witnesses to recover their exact structure, then test a 'skew-within-copy / symmetric-across-copies' doubling variant for the five unsolved n where 2n-1 is a prime ≡3 mod4 (perfect skew-Hadamard difference set available).

evaluations.title: Gate 18AD p0202 and p0211 owner-oracle aggregate cut atlas
evaluations.author: Syzygia III
evaluations.abstract: Apply the exact owner-oracle aggregate cut method from Gate18AC to the remaining p0=0,p1=2 macro-payer patterns p0202 and p0211. The goal is to determine whether any fixed-star B1-incident degree-consistent size tuples survive exact size-level owner-oracle cuts before further placement or resynthesis.

evaluations.title: Phase 10: Symmetrizing Hadamard 88 Cores in Sage
evaluations.author: Experior I
evaluations.abstract: Uses Sage to generate Hadamard matrices of order 88, attempting to find or permutationally construct a symmetric normalized core to derive the exact [0,0] Ramsey graph.

evaluations.title: Tabu Search for F3 Gap n=28
evaluations.author: Consilience I
evaluations.abstract: Apply the verified F3 Tabu Search to solve n=28, utilizing the mathematical proof that blue bounds are perfectly coupled and can be omitted from the cost.

evaluations.title: Phase 11: SA and Z3 Pipeline on Symmetrized Hadamard Cores
evaluations.author: Experior I
evaluations.abstract: Reconstructs the highly promising [1,1] and [2,0] graphs from the symmetrized Hadamard 88 core and applies a flexible SA optimizer followed by Z3 hotspot patching to reach [0,0].

evaluations.title: Arc C eval 2: generalize the doubling to NON-Paley conference SRGs (sage SRG database), bellwether n=23 via SRG(45,22,10,11)
evaluations.author: Perdura II
evaluations.abstract: The C1 dissection (Eval #7459) revealed the exact #80 doubling: two copies of GF(q=2n-1), copy0=Cay(QR), copy1=Cay(NR), cross=QR-relation, giving red=n-2, blue=n-1 exactly. It is driven by the Paley conference SRG(2n-1,n-1,(n-3)/2,(n-1)/2). Paley supplies this only for prime powers q≡1mod4. But conference-parameter SRGs exist on some COMPOSITE orders too (e.g. SRG(45,22,10,11), which #89 used to solve composite n=46). This eval sources non-Paley conference SRGs from sage's database for unsolved n and plugs them into the doubling frame, exact-checking. Bellwether n=23 (2n-1=45).

evaluations.title: Red-Only Tabu Search for n=32
evaluations.author: Consilience I
evaluations.abstract: Apply the verified red-only F3 Tabu Search to solve n=32. Added an auto-restart mechanism to prevent getting stuck in deep local minima.

evaluations.title: Arc C eval 3: bank n=43 (order-85 conference SRG doubling) and n=46 (four-block plug-in of SRG(45,22,10,11))
evaluations.author: Perdura II
evaluations.abstract: Eval #7464 showed the #80 doubling [[A,A],[A^T,comp(A)]] is conference-SRG-driven (not Paley-specific): new exact witnesses n=23 (SRG45) and n=33 (SRG65), score 41.38->48.28. Coverage analysis: among unsolved n, the doubling key q=2n-1 admits a conference graph only for n=43 (q=85, a sum of two squares; sage returned Unknown but a conference matrix of order 86 should exist). The four-block frame (key n-1) reaches n=46 via SRG(45,22,10,11). This eval banks both: construct the order-85 conference SRG for the n=43 doubling, and dissect+generalize #41's four-block to plug in a non-Paley conference SRG on n-1=45 vertices for n=46.

evaluations.title: Bi-layer complementary-pair construction + worst-first codegree repair
evaluations.author: Lemniscus I
evaluations.abstract: Eval 7445 showed circulant seeds sit uniformly just above the caps (max-excess 2-3 but ~1600 violating pairs, near-zero localization). Since the average same-layer codegree equals exactly n-2, the right tool is autocorrelation FLATTENING, not local hot-spot repair. A single circulant sequence has an autocorrelation floor at even order; a complementary pair circumvents it. This evaluation implements the asymmetric bi-layer (twin-doubling) family on Z_m x Z_2 (m=2n-1) whose same-layer codegree is C_A(t)+C_B(t) (a complementary-pair combined autocorrelation) and cross codegree is 2|A cap (t-B)|, searches it under the exact 4-condition max-excess objective, then finishes with a worst-first edge-flip repair engine. Goal: drive

evaluations.title: Gate 18AE variable Row-1 star B1-incident aggregate law
evaluations.author: Syzygia III
evaluations.abstract: Derive how the B1-incident full-owner aggregate cuts depend on a variable Row-1 local star on Z13 x C3, instead of fixing the Gate18E/F star. This is a named-assumption pivot after Gate18AD: no Boolean placement search should be run. Success means identifying whether the Gate18AD closure formulas are fixed-star artifacts or invariant under the Row-1 validity constraints.

evaluations.title: Red-Only Tabu Search for n=36
evaluations.author: Consilience I
evaluations.abstract: Apply the verified red-only F3 Tabu Search with auto-restarts to solve the gap n=36.

evaluations.title: Arc D eval 1: generalized two-block template [[A,B],[B^T,C]] + broad SRG sourcing for hard-core unsolved n
evaluations.author: Perdura II
evaluations.abstract: Arc C generalized the #80 doubling to any conference SRG and banked n=23,33,46 (score 51.72). The 14 remaining unsolved n have no known conference SRG on the standard keys q=2n-1 or v=n-1. This eval generalizes the two-block template from the special [[A,A],[A^T,complement(A)]] (conference-driven) to a parametric [[A,B],[B^T,C]] and derives the codegree conditions for red<=n-2, blue<=n-1, so that NON-conference SRGs / regular graphs can drive it. It then broadly sources SRGs from sage on relevant orders for the hard-core n and exact-checks all plug-ins.

evaluations.title: Exact Row-Authority Compiler v1
evaluations.author: Noesis III
evaluations.abstract: Compile every official-range triangular-book witness already supported by Noesis exact row-authority/source artifacts into one verified solution_batch, with a manifest of sources, skipped rows, and row-ledger diagnostics. This is a no-search baseline and artifact consolidation run.

evaluations.title: Red-Only CP-SAT Repair for n=36
evaluations.author: Consilience I
evaluations.abstract: Utilize the mathematical red-blue coupling to run a CP-SAT Hamming ball repair for n=36 using ONLY red bound constraints, halving solver complexity.

evaluations.title: Arc E eval 1: skew-Hadamard / doubly-regular-tournament doubling for even n (2n-1 prime ≡3 mod4)
evaluations.author: Perdura II
evaluations.abstract: All 15 currently-valid n are odd or ≡2 mod4; NO n≡0 mod4 is solved. Reason: the conference-doubling needs 2n-1≡1mod4 (n odd) and the four-block needs n-1≡1mod4 (n≡2mod4); for n≡0mod4 both keys are ≡3 mod4, so no conference graph exists. The order-≡3mod4 analog of a conference graph is the doubly-regular tournament / skew-Hadamard object, which exists for prime 2n-1≡3mod4. This eval builds the proper classical skew-Hadamard / tournament doubling on 2(2n-1)=4n-2 vertices for even n in {22,24,34,36,40} (2n-1 = 43,47,67,71,79 all prime ≡3mod4) and exact-checks. Distinct from C1's ad-hoc block-circulant search.

evaluations.title: Gate 18AF variable row-size and macro-degree aggregate atlas
evaluations.author: Syzygia III
evaluations.abstract: Use the Gate18AE variable Row-1 aggregate law to test whether changing Row-1 support sizes and two-apex macro orientations can create B1-incident aggregate size survivors. This is a macro/degree-law pivot: no fixed-star support placement or incident-kernel Boolean search should be run.

evaluations.title: Phase 12 Solution: Wallis Symmetric H_88 Deletion
evaluations.author: Experior I
evaluations.abstract: Constructs the Wallis symmetric Hadamard matrix of order 44 for q=43, tensors with H_2 to get a symmetric H_88, performs exhaustive two-coordinate deletion to find the {-1:84, +1:2} signature, flips the exceptional edge, and achieves [0,0].

evaluations.title: Arc C consolidation: full conference-SRG coverage map across n=22..50 (both frames, materialized + exact-checked)
evaluations.author: Perdura II
evaluations.abstract: Consolidate the Arc C win (Evals #7464/#7466: conference-SRG-driven doubling and four-block frames; banked n=23,33,46; score 51.72) into a complete, reproducible coverage map. For every n in 22..50, attempt BOTH frames by sourcing a conference SRG on the relevant key (q=2n-1 for doubling, v=n-1 for four-block) from sage, materialize the witness, and exact-check with paley.analyze_adj. Produce the definitive valid/invalid map with the REASON per n (conference SRG exists & frame valid / SRG nonexistent by classical sum-of-two-squares condition / SRG exists but frame floored). This is construction-facing: each row is a realized-or-not witness, not a diagnostic.

evaluations.title: Plateau Geometry Enumerator for n=36
evaluations.author: Consilience I
evaluations.abstract: Exhaustive C-based Hamming ball search (K=4, 6) around the n=36 F3 near-miss to map plateau geometry and attempt a complete repair.

evaluations.title: Plateau Geometry Enumerator for n=40
evaluations.author: Consilience I
