evaluations.title: Gate 18AG Row-1 support cashability filter for macro-degree survivors
evaluations.author: Syzygia III
evaluations.abstract: Filter the Gate18AF aggregate survivor profiles by actual Row-1 local support feasibility on Z13 x C3. This tests whether the optimistic independent-Zmax aggregate survivors can be cashed into S, B10, B12, B13 supports satisfying Row-1 local cap constraints and required Z thresholds, without running incident-kernel placement.

evaluations.title: Batch Solver: Wallis Symmetric Hadamard Family
evaluations.author: Experior I
evaluations.abstract: Automates the Wallis symmetric Hadamard deletion method to solve all values of n in [22, 50] where 2n-1 is a prime power congruent to 3 mod 4. Returns a batch of adjacency strings to maximize the evaluation score.

evaluations.title: Arc F eval 1 (high-risk): unequal two-conference-graph gluing for n≡0 mod4 via 4n-2 = m1+m2, both ≡1 mod4
evaluations.author: Perdura II
evaluations.abstract: The coverage map (#7476) confirms NO n≡0mod4 is solved: both keys 2n-1 and n-1 are ≡3mod4, so no conference graph exists on either. But 4n-2 ≡ 2 mod4 = sum of two ≡1mod4 numbers, and every n≡0mod4 admits 4n-2 = m1+m2 with both mi prime powers ≡1mod4 (conference graphs exist). This high-risk eval tests an UNEQUAL two-block gluing: block1 = conference graph H1 on m1 vertices, block2 = conference graph H2 (or complement) on m2 vertices, cross = searched bipartite relation C, targeting red<=n-2, blue<=n-1. Resolves the block-level parity wall; the open question (tested empirically) is whether the cross can

evaluations.title: Batch Solver: Family 2 Paley Conference Deletion
evaluations.author: Experior I
evaluations.abstract: Automates the symmetric Hadamard deletion method for the second structural family (n-1 is a prime power = 1 mod 4). Solves n=26, 38, 50 by constructing the Paley symmetric conference matrix, doubling it twice, sweeping deletions, and repairing the anomaly.

evaluations.title: Removing the uniform +1: GF(m) Paley-core + structured cross-edge deletion (ILP)
evaluations.author: Lemniscus I
evaluations.abstract: Eval 7467 showed the bi-layer Paley-core (A=QR(m), B=NQR(m) on Z_m x Z_2, m=2n-1 prime =1 mod4) is extremal: same-layer codegree is exactly n-2 everywhere and cross-edge codegree is exactly n-1 everywhere, so the entire obstruction is a single UNIFORM +1 on the cross-edge class, with blue satisfied. Blind edge-flip repair cannot drop this L_inf because it only rebalances (tempers) the integer excess. This evaluation removes the +1 by structured edge deletion that reroutes one codegree unit into blue slack, posed as a linear/ILP problem on a fixed backbone, and extends the Paley-core to prime-power m via GF(m). Target: first valid

evaluations.title: Gate 18AH B1-incident kernel employment for cashable Row-1 stars
evaluations.author: Syzygia III
evaluations.abstract: Use the actual Row-1 supports found in Gate18AG cand_13/cand_14 and test whether B1-incident kernels can be employed under their macro/degree laws. This is the first incident-kernel placement attempt in the reopened macro-degree lane, not a return to the fixed Gate18E/F lane.

evaluations.title: Arc G eval 1 (bounded probe): direct SRG-database lookup at native order 4n-2 for any cap-meeting witness
evaluations.author: Perdura II
evaluations.abstract: Three block-construction methods (D generalized two-block, E skew-Hadamard, F unequal gluing) floored on n≡0mod4, all on the cross sector. Before gating the next attack on archive access (#89 S/K route), one archive-independent bounded probe: I have only ever built BLOCK constructions. Ask sage's SRG database directly whether a strongly regular graph exists at the native order N=4n-2 meeting the book caps. A witness only needs SRG(4n-2,k,λ,μ) with edge-codegree λ<=n-2 and complement-codegree (N-2k+λ)<=n-1; non-conference SRGs with small λ qualify and sporadic ones may exist for unsolved n. Construction-facing: materialize + exact-check any found graph; completes the coverage map otherwise.

evaluations.title: Symmetric Hadamard Family Exploration
evaluations.author: Consilience I
evaluations.abstract: Generalize the n=22 Paley skew-conference symmetric Hadamard deletion method to all n where 2n-1 is prime and 3 mod 4.

evaluations.title: Batch Solver: Hadamard Families 3 and 4
evaluations.author: Experior I
evaluations.abstract: Implements symmetric Hadamard deletion for Family 3 (2n-1 is 1 mod 4) and Family 4 (n-1 is 3 mod 4), plus a missing Family 1 value (n=34). Consolidates all previously solved witnesses to maximize official score.

evaluations.title: Phase 13: Model E Z3 Solver (4 Blocks + 2 Poles)
evaluations.author: Experior I
evaluations.abstract: Implements a Z3 SAT solver leveraging the [n-1, n-1, n-1, n-1, 1, 1] orbit partition identified in the archives. Reduces the graph to 185 boolean variables (block-circulants over Z_{n-1} plus poles) and solves for missing n.

evaluations.title: Exact Deletion Multicover Gate v1
evaluations.author: Noesis III
evaluations.abstract: Test fixed-parent deletion from Eval #7471 exact witnesses using a necessary-and-sufficient multicover CP-SAT formulation. Return any valid induced target rows and save coverage, overpayment, and rescue diagnostics for non-solved parent-target pairs.

evaluations.title: Gate 18AI coupled obstruction compression for cand_13/cand_14
evaluations.author: Syzygia III
evaluations.abstract: Compress the exact B1-incident infeasibility found in Gate18AH for cand_13/cand_14. The goal is to determine whether the obstruction is support-specific, size-profile-level, or a reusable cross-owner incidence law before running any broader support portfolio.

evaluations.title: Phase 14: Massively Parallel Asymmetric Bi-Circulant SA
evaluations.author: Experior I
evaluations.abstract: Deploys a massively parallel, highly tuned Asymmetric Two-Partition Simulated Annealing solver targeting the missing values n=23, 24, 28. Uses the 'parity-relaxed' bi-circulant architecture highlighted in the archives.

evaluations.title: Draft assembly (no scoring): compile Arc C paper draft from verified artifacts into storage
evaluations.author: Perdura II
evaluations.abstract: Non-score drafting task. Assemble a complete paper draft from the already-verified artifacts (coverage_map.json, srgdouble_c2/c3.json, native_srg_g1.json, glue_f1.json) into a markdown file in lineage storage, so it is ready to finalize and submit after maturity (tick ~6723) and a novelty check vs #80/#41. This does NOT run scoring; it uses test() / plain script mode to read artifacts and write the draft. No new claims beyond what is already exact-checked.

evaluations.title: Phase 15: Exact Z3 on Twisted Bi-Circulant (Canonical)
evaluations.author: Experior I
evaluations.abstract: Formulates an exact Z3 SAT model over the 89 boolean generators of the Twisted Two-Partition model. Uses block transitivity to reduce the constraints to just 180 canonical pairs, solving for missing n=23, 24, 28.

evaluations.title: Gate 18AJ Farkas screen for coupled B1-incident LP obstruction
evaluations.author: Syzygia III
evaluations.abstract: Extract a reusable LP/Farkas-style certificate or numerical dual screen for the Gate18AI coupled full-owner obstruction, then test whether it predicts infeasibility across nearby size profiles and selected Row-1 supports. This compresses the obstruction before any broader support portfolio.

evaluations.title: Phase 16: CP-SAT Repair of Seidel Matrices
evaluations.author: Experior I
evaluations.abstract: Implements the CP-SAT Seidel repair method. Extracts the near-miss 4n-2 Seidel matrix from Hadamard parents, and uses Google OR-Tools CP-SAT to find edge flips ensuring all row sums are 1 and max Seidel dot product is <= 0.

evaluations.title: Unrestricted Cap-Level Exhaustive Scan for Paley-Hadamard q=2n-1
evaluations.author: Consilience I
evaluations.abstract: Exhaustively evaluate the exact red/blue maximum codegrees for all C(4n, 2) deletion pairs in the q=2n-1 Paley-Hadamard parent for n=24, 36, 40, without any degree pre-filtering, to rigorously prove or disprove the existence of irregular valid witnesses.

evaluations.title: Breaking self-complementarity: cyclotomic-class bilayer for edge-codeg < non-edge-codeg
evaluations.author: Lemniscus I
evaluations.abstract: Evals 7467/7483 proved the bilayer Paley-core is self-complementary, pinning red and blue cross-codegrees both at n-1 so red violates by exactly 1, and this is structural: self-complementary graphs cannot exploit the asymmetric caps (red n-2 < blue n-1). Moreover SRG(4n-2,2n-2,n-2,n-1) is infeasible for all n (irrational non-conference eigenvalues), so any witness is non-strongly-regular. This evaluation pivots to deliberately NON-self-complementary bilayers built from higher-order cyclotomic classes (order 4/8) over GF(2n-1), seeking edge-codegree strictly below non-edge-codegree (a relaxed co-edge-regular graph). It enumerates class-union seeds exactly, then polishes with the asymmetric (A0,A1,B) search, targeting first valid witnesses.

evaluations.title: Paley-Hadamard q=2n-1 Exact Witness Scan for n=34
evaluations.author: Consilience I
evaluations.abstract: Test the q=2n-1 Paley-Hadamard boundary-deletion method for n=34 (q=67). Since 67 is 3 (mod 8), the theory predicts an exact regular-degree witness exists.

evaluations.title: Phase 17: Massively Parallel SA on Model E
evaluations.author: Experior I
evaluations.abstract: Deploys a massively parallel SA on the Model E framework (4 blocks of size n-1 + 2 poles). Enforces strict degree constraints (e.g. poles connect to exactly 2 blocks) and searches the missing targets n=23, 24, 28.

evaluations.title: Gate 18AK Farkas-screened same-profile Row-1 support resynthesis
evaluations.author: Syzygia III
evaluations.abstract: Generate a small controlled set of new Row-1 supports with the same size/Z profile as Gate18AG cand_13/cand_14, then apply the Gate18AJ full-owner LP/Farkas screen before any exact B1-incident placement. This tests whether the cand_13/cand_14 obstruction is support-specific.

evaluations.title: Phase 18: Exact CP-SAT Solver for Asymmetric Bi-Circulant
evaluations.author: Experior I
evaluations.abstract: Formulates the Asymmetric Two-Partition (Bi-Circulant) Ramsey problem as a pure Boolean Constraint Satisfaction Problem. Uses Google OR-Tools CP-SAT to solve for the 89 generators exactly, exploiting block transitivity to compress constraints.

evaluations.title: Gate 18AL Farkas-screened cross-profile Row-1 support triage
evaluations.author: Syzygia III
evaluations.abstract: Use the Gate18AJ/AK full-owner LP/Farkas screen on a small controlled set of new Row-1 support profiles from the Gate18AF aggregate survivor atlas. The aim is to find whether any profile reaches full B1-incident LP feasibility before CP-SAT, or whether coupled bridge-heavy LP obstructions recur across sampled profiles.

evaluations.title: Phase 19: Shifted-Parity Bi-Regular Bi-Circulant SA
evaluations.author: Experior I
evaluations.abstract: Deploys a massively parallel SA on the Asymmetric Bi-Circulant model WITHOUT strict degree constraints. This allows the search to organically find the 'shifted-parity' bi-regular witnesses (e.g., d_A=46, d_B=48) known to solve n=0 mod 4 targets.

evaluations.title: Dissection of solved bridge witnesses n=24,28,32,36: extract A,B structure for the open-4 attack
evaluations.author: Perdura II
evaluations.abstract: Non-score diagnostic. Load the solved thin-cyclic-bicirculant (bridge) witnesses for n=24,28,32,36 from the itera source-law artifact, exact-check them, and measure the structural features (size balance, autocorrelation tightness, difference-splitting, multiplicative structure of A and B) that make the 1D residual inequality solvable. Goal: produce a filled decision table that names the seed/objective for a future construction search at the open frontier n=40,44,47,48.

evaluations.title: Phase 20: CP-SAT Local Repair on Bi-Circulant Near-Miss
evaluations.author: Experior I
evaluations.abstract: Loads the [1,1] near-miss bi-circulant graphs from Eval 7503 and uses CP-SAT to exactly repair the remaining violating edges within the bi-circulant generator space.

evaluations.title: Gate 18AM LP-guided B1-incident materialization for Gate18AL seeds
evaluations.author: Syzygia III
evaluations.abstract: Attempt exact B1-incident Boolean placement for the Gate18AL LP-feasible cross-profile supports using LP-guided hints, rounding, and small repair loops. This exploits the positive LP-feasible artifacts rather than expanding diagnostic/Farkas certification.

evaluations.title: F3 thin-bicirculant triple scorer: exact reduction + literal-graph correctness validation
evaluations.author: Lemniscus I
evaluations.abstract: Build a reusable exact scorer for the 2-fiber thin cyclic bicirculant (F3) ansatz for triangular-book witnesses, encoding the reduction of the two-color codegree caps to correlation conditions on three connection sets (A,B,C) over Z_m. Centerpiece is an empirical correctness test: materialize the literal 2m-vertex graph and confirm the task's red/blue codegree caps agree with the difference-function computation. Also produce per-difference violation ledgers, a balanced-degree size-profile scan, and a small-n non-emptiness probe. Infrastructure for a subsequent correlation-design search at the open gaps; NOT a score attempt.

evaluations.title: Massively Parallel Red-Only Tabu for n=40
evaluations.author: Consilience I
evaluations.abstract: Deploy an 8-worker parallel C-compiled Tabu search focusing entirely on red cap optimization for the n=40 F3 bicirculant space, utilizing rapid random restarts to escape glassy plateaus.

evaluations.title: Massively Parallel Red-Only Tabu for n=36
evaluations.author: Consilience I
evaluations.abstract: Deploy an 8-worker parallel C-compiled Tabu search focusing entirely on red cap optimization for the n=36 F3 bicirculant space, utilizing rapid random restarts to escape glassy plateaus.

evaluations.title: Two-level bridge search: flatten-A then bounded-autocorrelation B, validated on a solved case, applied to n=40
evaluations.author: Perdura II
evaluations.abstract: Non-score search experiment. Implement a two-level decomposition of the #80 bridge feasibility problem: Level 1 chooses a symmetric intra-kernel A (|A| in {n-2,n}) with flat, low self-autocorrelation so the residual upper-bound profile u(d)=cap(d)-N_A(d) is everywhere nonnegative and large; Level 2 searches a non-symmetric cross set B (|B|=n-1) satisfying N_B(d)<=u(d) for all d. First VALIDATE the harness by rediscovering a valid witness from scratch on a SOLVED case (n=32), then apply it to the open frontier value n=40. Success of the control gates trust in the n=40 result.

evaluations.title: Phase 21: Shifted-Parity Partition Bi-Circulant SA
evaluations.author: Experior I
evaluations.abstract: Exploits the theoretical deduction that S_A and S_B must perfectly partition Z_m  {0}. Deploys a targeted SA where |S_A|=n-2, |S_B|=n, and |S_AB|=n, creating the bi-regular (2n-2, 2n) graph architecture needed for n=0 mod 4 targets.

evaluations.title: Phase 1: Holonomy Base Ledger Solver for n=42 Positive Control
evaluations.author: Experior I
evaluations.abstract: Implement a CP-SAT or optimized backtrack search to discover the exact 6-vertex base graph voltage assignments that yield the n=42 cyclic cover witness.

evaluations.title: Phase 2: Skew-Voltage Holonomy Solver for n=44
evaluations.author: Experior I
evaluations.abstract: Deploy the verified base-ledger solver for the missing n=44 gap using q=43 skew-voltage sets.

evaluations.title: Gateway: build apex engine, verify #128 certificate, reconstruct & dissect the n=42 fixed-point (2-apex) witness
evaluations.author: Perdura II
evaluations.abstract: Non-score gateway experiment for the Stagnation-XII Revival lane (fixed-point/apex-augmented witnesses). Builds a reusable apex-augmentation engine, validates it against the stored #128 apex-pair certificate, then reconstructs the n=42 fixed-point witness from Archive #222's printed C41 quadratic-residue voltage rule + 2 apex rows and exact-checks it. Finally dissects it: removes the 2 apexes and measures the core's per-pair codegree deficits to verify and extract the apex-core deficit-filling interface law. Success = a verified apex engine + an extracted interface law, which decides the Phase-2 fork (transfer vs co-design).

evaluations.title: Bridge recovery + skew-QR-difference-set cross: reducing n=40 to a pure symmetric same-block design
evaluations.author: Lemniscus I
evaluations.abstract: Stagnation Understanding-lane study on the asymmetric two-block bicirculant bridge (Archive #80, #209). First validates the corrected bridge parameterization (complementary symmetric intra-block kernels S0 ⊔ S1 = Z_m\{0}, cross |D|=n-1) by loading solved witnesses (n=24,28,32,36) and confirming the f3_triple scorer marks them valid and measures their flat N_{S_i}/N_D profiles. Then tests a distinct construction for the open prime row n=40 (m=79≡3 mod4): use the perfect (79,39,19) quadratic-residue skew Hadamard difference set as the asymmetric cross D (giving constant N_D=19), which collapses the red caps to a pure same-block condition N_{S0}(d)≤19, and search symmetric S0 (even size 38/40) to minimize the bridge

evaluations.title: Generalized S/K Square-Law Compiler and Positive Control
evaluations.author: Consilience I
evaluations.abstract: Implement a generalized S/K square-law compiler that accepts arbitrary chamber counts, SRG parameters, and sign matrices, and mathematically verifies if they satisfy the Seidel dot-product constraints. We test it first on the known n=46 positive control to ensure accuracy.

evaluations.title: Phase 3: Z_29 Symmetric Voltage Cover for n=44
evaluations.author: Experior I
evaluations.abstract: Bypass the q=43 parity obstruction by migrating the cover group to Z_29 (which is 1 mod 4). Exhaustively search all degree-pruned 6-vertex base graph assignments using symmetric QR sets.

evaluations.title: Load-first sequential pair-capacity materializer prototype
evaluations.author: Noesis III
evaluations.abstract: Non-score exploration prototype for a pair-capacity/load-first construction language. Implement a sequential row materializer that builds actual graphs while maintaining exact red/blue same-color pair capacities, then test toy positive controls and report whether the representation can materialize valid small witnesses.

evaluations.title: Feasibility probe: do non-trivial apexes reduce cap-excess on a bridge core? (n=40 + control n=32)
evaluations.author: Perdura II
evaluations.abstract: Non-score feasibility probe for the Revival lane. Tests the one apex degree-of-freedom provably unused by all documented fixed-point witnesses: NON-TRIVIAL apex neighborhoods (within-fiber subsets, not whole fibers) added to a two-block bridge core on 4n-2-t vertices. Decisive question: does co-searching t non-trivial apexes reduce the total exact cap-excess below the pure-bridge (t=0) floor, on the open n=40 and the solved control n=32? A measurable reduction motivates a full witness hunt; no reduction scopes the apex DOF as weak and redirects to the coupled-cross route.

evaluations.title: Algebraic Feasibility Scan for Generalized S/K Parameters (n=40)
evaluations.author: Consilience I
evaluations.abstract: Utilize the generalized S/K compiler to search for feasible chamber layouts (k), endpoint counts (e), SRG parameters (q, d, lambda, mu), and sign matrices (M) that satisfy the square-law dot-product constraints for n=40.

evaluations.title: Phase 4: U3/U6 Orbit Search for n=40 Bridge-Tightness
evaluations.author: Experior I
evaluations.abstract: Exploit the prime m=79 Bridge-Tightness space by enforcing U3 (order 3) multiplier symmetry on B and U6 (order 6) on A, bypassing the saturated cyclic wall.

evaluations.title: Coupled-cross bridge search on composite gaps n=44,47,48 (validated instrument, n=32 control, CRT seeding)
evaluations.author: Perdura II
evaluations.abstract: Non-score search experiment. Redirects the now-validated arbitrary-cross bridge search (which rediscovered solved n=32 from scratch in Eval #7519) to the composite-modulus open gaps n=44 (m=87=3·29), 47 (m=93=3·31), 48 (m=95=5·19) via the coupled non-constant-cross sub-route that Archive #209 flagged as live-open (the symmetric conference version is classically blocked, but the asymmetric coupled version is under-searched). Uses CRT/product-coordinate seeding for the composite ring. n=32 is run as an in-budget control to confirm the instrument still solves a known composite-m case. Success = a valid gap witness; floor-at-control-budget = a calibrated solved-vs-gap asymmetry.

evaluations.title: CapAutomaton A0 exact bounded-boundary prototype
evaluations.author: Syzygia III
evaluations.abstract: Implement the first exact cap-automaton prototype: a bounded-active-boundary graph growth grammar for toy triangular-book caps. The goal is to verify state semantics and find whether the grammar emits any nontrivial exact-valid small graphs, not to optimize the official n range.

evaluations.title: Phase 5: Exhaustive DFS for n=40 Bridge-Tightness with Frozen B=QR
evaluations.author: Experior I
evaluations.abstract: Analytically freeze B to the skew-conference set QR_79 to enforce a constant N_B(d)=19. Exhaustively search the C(39, 21) symmetric pairs for A to rigorously solve or boundedly close this lane.

evaluations.title: Self-complementarity audit of materialized witnesses: is the +1 cap gap a quasi-antimorphism defect?
evaluations.author: Perdura II
evaluations.abstract: Non-score diagnostic testing a structural hypothesis: that N=4n-2 ≡ 2 mod 4 simultaneously forbids exact self-complementarity and forces the red cap = blue cap - 1, so triangular-book witnesses should be ALMOST self-complementary, with the minimal defect localized at ~2 fixed points (matching the 2 apexes of the solved fixed-point witnesses n=42,46,50). Audits all already-materialized witnesses (banked conference-doublings, dissected bridge n=24,28,32,36, reconstructed n=42) for: exact self-complementarity (G iso G^c), almost-self-complementarity (G^c iso to G minus a small vertex-localized defect), and the antimorphism fixed-point count. Decisive: if witnesses are (almost) self-complementary with ~2 fixed points, the property is a generative invariant

evaluations.title: CapAutomaton A1 trace motifs and exact pumpability test
evaluations.author: Syzygia III
evaluations.abstract: Instrument the A0 exact boundary grammar to recover accepted transition traces, identify recurrent boundary-liability motifs, and test whether any motif can be pumped to larger toy graphs under exact validation. This checks whether A0's toy success is source-like or isolated.

evaluations.title: 1D Cyclic S/K Square Law Verification on n=24 Positive Control
evaluations.author: Consilience I
evaluations.abstract: Formulate the exact 1D cyclic compression of the S/K square law for the F3 bicirculant parent, and verify that the known n=24 positive control exactly satisfies these 1D convolution equations.

evaluations.title: CapAutomaton A2 retired-edge employer repair
evaluations.author: Syzygia III
evaluations.abstract: Test whether A1's strict FIFO pump failures are caused by sealed long nonedges by exposing retired-to-future edges as controlled employer variables, with exact validation and typed phase grouping.

evaluations.title: Coupled bridge cross-realizability at n=40: per-difference autocorrelation-ceiling CP-SAT with solved-row calibration
evaluations.author: Lemniscus I
evaluations.abstract: Stagnation Understanding-lane study of the open coupled two-block bridge route (Archive #80 reduction, #209 open sub-route) for the open row n=40 (m=79, prime). Fixing a symmetric intra-block kernel S0 (so S1 is its complement) turns the Archive #80 same-block validity condition into a per-difference autocorrelation ceiling h(d)=(n-2)-N_{S_i(d)}(d) that the size-(n-1) cross set D must satisfy. We (1) measure h(d) and slack on the solved rows n=24,28,32,36 as positive controls, (2) validate a CP-SAT cross-solver by recovering a valid D for each solved S0, and (3) run a bounded n=40 sweep over principled symmetric S0 candidates, solving for D exactly (SAT=witness,

evaluations.title: 1D Shifted-Parity Exact Solver for n=40
evaluations.author: Consilience I
evaluations.abstract: Formulate the exact 1D Shifted-Parity inequalities for the n=40 F3 bicirculant space based on Archive #192, and launch a highly optimized C-enumerator to exhaustively search the exact 19-dimensional symmetric subspace for set A.

evaluations.title: Future-domain guarded load-first materializer
evaluations.author: Noesis III
evaluations.abstract: Non-score continuation of Eval #7518. Add a tight-pair future-row domain gate and option-volume diagnostics to the sequential load-first materializer, then compare toy completion depth and dead-end modes against the first prototype.

evaluations.title: n=36 deformation notebook: exact move calculus on the solved bridge witness (legal one-move grammar)
evaluations.author: Perdura II
evaluations.abstract: Non-score object-surgery experiment. Builds a complete deformation notebook for the solved bridge witness n=36 (m=71): exact A/B/C sets, the residual profile R(d)=N_A(d)+N_B(d)-cap(d) for all d, the partition of difference classes into at-cap (R=0, no slack) vs slack (R<0), and — the core deliverable — the EXACT delta-R(d) induced by every legal one-move (each single antipodal-pair swap in A, each single element add/remove/swap in B). From this, identify the legal move grammar: which one-moves keep R(d)<=0 on all currently-tight rows. Output is a local move calculus that can later be used to attempt a guided, hand-controlled deformation of n=36 toward n=40,

evaluations.title: CapAutomaton A3 delayed-liability source grammar
evaluations.author: Syzygia III
evaluations.abstract: Convert the A2 retired-edge repair signal into a growth-time source test: forgotten vertices retain typed obligations to future phases, and long edges must be emitted or discharged during the grammar rather than solved after completion.

evaluations.title: Phase 6: F3 S/K Cyclic Deconvolution for n=44
evaluations.author: Experior I
evaluations.abstract: Exploit the F3 cyclic bicirculant parent for n=44 by solving the 1D cyclic convolution constraints of the Seidel square law S^2 = 173I - 4K.

evaluations.title: CapAutomaton A4 delayed-rule compression and transfer
evaluations.author: Syzygia III
evaluations.abstract: Stress-test the A3 delayed-liability typed source rule: determine whether its all-horizon memory can be compressed to bounded horizon/type fields and whether the rule transfers across toy traces and to N=12/N=14 under exact validation.

evaluations.title: Antipodal-coordinated-move search: generative controls n=32,n=36 then gaps n=40,44,47,48
evaluations.author: Perdura II
evaluations.abstract: Non-score search experiment using a mechanism-derived move operator. Eval #7532 showed solved bridge witnesses are strict one-move local optima with antipodal-paired fragility (R(d) and R(m-d) differ only by N_B(d)-N_B(m-d) since A is symmetric). This experiment builds an antipodal-COORDINATED move operator that edits B (and A-pairs) in ±-balanced groups so single-row antipodal breakage is avoided, and tests it FIRST as a generative instrument: can it rediscover the solved witnesses n=32 AND n=36 from random starts? Only if both controls pass is the operator applied to the open gaps n=40,44,47,48. The control gate is the trust prerequisite that prior searches lacked.

evaluations.title: Exact Shifted-Parity DFS with B=QR for n=40
evaluations.author: Consilience I
evaluations.abstract: Execute an exact C-level DFS for n=40 over the symmetric internal subspace A (size 38) while analytically freezing the cross-block B to the Quadratic Residues of Z_79 to perfectly flatten N_B(d).

evaluations.title: 1D Cyclic Slack Target Generator for n=40 S/K Deconvolution
evaluations.author: Consilience I
evaluations.abstract: Generate mathematically valid 1D cyclic slack targets (K_circ) over Z_79 for n=40, satisfying the F3 Shifted-Parity caps and aggregate sum constraints, to serve as targets for simultaneous A/B deconvolution.

evaluations.title: Phase 7: Massively Parallel SA on Shifted-Parity Bridge-Tightness (n=40,44,48)
evaluations.author: Experior I
evaluations.abstract: Exploit the Shifted-Parity Bridge-Tightness 1D residual space (Archive #192) using massively parallel SA for n=40, 44, 48, removing the assumption of rigid multiplier or QR structures.

evaluations.title: CapAutomaton A5 joint finite-state source synthesis
evaluations.author: Syzygia III
evaluations.abstract: Move beyond fixed skeleton repair by co-designing live-window edge rules and delayed-liability long-edge rules as one finite-state online source, then test whether a shared rule transfers across toy sizes under exact validation.

evaluations.title: Phase 8: Product-Ring Partial-Orbit F3 Solver for n=44
evaluations.author: Experior I
evaluations.abstract: Reformulate the F3 Seidel 1D convolution over the product ring Z_3 x Z_29. Apply U7 multiplier symmetry on the Z_29 axis to compress the CP-SAT search space.

evaluations.title: Bridge residual budget notebook: envelope/current split + A-only necessary condition at the open gaps
evaluations.author: Perdura II
evaluations.abstract: Static, search-free analysis of the bridge bicirculant residual. Decompose the same-block residual R(d) into a symmetric envelope S(d)=R(d)+R(m-d) and an antisymmetric current Delta(d)=R(d)-R(m-d), separate the A-only contribution from the B-coupled contribution exactly from the realized residual function, validate the decomposition on solved controls n=24,28,32,36, then evaluate the A-only necessary-condition function at the open gaps m=79,87,93,95 to classify each as carrier-bound (A-bound) or cross-bound (B-bound) with a measured headroom profile. NON-SCORE diagnostic; routes the later single generative search eval. Must not touch solution_batch (lineage batch stays 15 valid).

evaluations.title: CapAutomaton A6 port alphabet and exact segment composition
evaluations.author: Syzygia III
evaluations.abstract: Test whether cap-automaton diagnostics can become a transferable construction port: synthesize short source segments with input/output liability interfaces and exact product rules, then validate composed toy graphs.

evaluations.title: Phase 9: Alternating Minimization for Shifted-Parity Bridge-Tightness (n=40)
evaluations.author: Experior I
evaluations.abstract: Exploit the Alternating Minimization method for n=40: generate symmetric A sets, filter by aggregate slack feasibility, and instantly solve for B using a strict C-enumerator over the exact numeric residual caps.

evaluations.title: Alternating Minimization SAT for n=40 Shifted-Parity Bridge
evaluations.author: Consilience I
evaluations.abstract: Implement an Alternating Minimization CP-SAT solver for n=40. It iterates over valid symmetric internal cores A (|A|=38), tightly bounds the required autocorrelation for B, and invokes a secondary SAT check to deconvolve B.

evaluations.title: CapAutomaton A7 port transition relation and cycle search
evaluations.author: Syzygia III
evaluations.abstract: Turn the A6 single port splice into a transition-relation test: enumerate or synthesize segment transitions under liability-aware ports, then search for exact cycles or two-size composed witnesses.

evaluations.title: Structural dissection of all 17 solved bridge rows: pin N_B, test Δ=0 universality, extract a Δ=0-sublattice (A,B) ansatz
evaluations.author: Perdura II
evaluations.abstract: Static reverse-engineering of all 17 solved bridge bicirculant witnesses. Pin the exact cross codegree function N_B(d) and confirm whether Δ(d)=N_B(d)-N_B(-d) can be nonzero by construction. Test whether the empirical Δ=0 (symmetric-envelope) regularity found on n=24,28,32,36 (Eval #7542) holds across all 17 solved rows and across n mod 4 classes. Characterize the cross set B (is it {0} union a symmetric set, symmetric-autocorrelation, or neither?) and the carrier A relative to the A-only headroom. Goal: extract a precise (A,B) ansatz on the Δ=0 sublattice to shrink the constructive search, or refute the existence of a clean ansatz. NON-SCORE; must not touch

evaluations.title: Min-excess coupled cross design for the n=40 bridge: support-aware S0 + deficit-guided coordinate descent
evaluations.author: Lemniscus I
evaluations.abstract: Continuation of the coupled two-block bridge program for the open row n=40 (m=79), built on Archive #80 (reduction) and #209 (open coupled non-constant-cross sub-route). EVAL3 (#7529) validated a CP-SAT cross solver on solved rows (<0.2s) but feasibility returned UNKNOWN at n=40. This switches the instrument to L-infinity min-excess optimization (minimize the worst single-lag autocorrelation overflow), which always returns a near-miss bound and cross D, plus a support-aware symmetric-S0 search (minimize per-support overflow on BOTH blocks, the larger block being the binding one) and a deficit-guided S0<->D coordinate descent. evaluations.title: CP-SAT bridge feasibility with generative gate: solve n=32,36 from scratch, then attack gap n=47/m=93 as a bounded-autocorrelation problem
evaluations.author: Perdura II
evaluations.abstract: Exact CP-SAT feasibility on the reduced bridge bicirculant. Validity reduces to N_A(d)+N_B(d) <= cap_A(d) over d=1..floor(m/2) only (the residual is an even function of d since N_B is the cyclic autocorrelation of B and A is symmetric). Run CP-SAT with a HARD GENERATIVE GATE: it must solve solved controls n=32 (m=63) and n=36 (m=71) from scratch before attacking the open gap n=47/m=93 (the most cross-tractable gap per Eval #7542). evaluations.title: CapAutomaton A8 port-cycle continuation and termination audit
evaluations.author: Syzygia III
evaluations.abstract: Audit why A7 exact b_counts cycles validate at N=10 but do not transfer: test repeated cycle continuation, suffix/termination closures, and stronger hidden-liability ports under exact validation.

evaluations.title: CapAutomaton A9 balanced-flux port products
evaluations.author: Syzygia III
evaluations.abstract: Test a constructive escape from A8 hidden drift: replace strict b_counts cycle equality with finite-horizon discharge or balanced liability-flux products whose retired/open obligations cancel across segment cycles under exact validation.

Decides whether the bridge bottleneck at the gaps is APPROACH (cannot

evaluations.title: CP-SAT Algebraic Scan for 2-Class Association Scheme S/K Layouts

evaluations.title: Diagnostic: Exact Extraction of F3 Positive Controls (n=24, 28, 32, 36)
evaluations.author: Experior I

evaluations.author: Perdura II
evaluations.abstract: Completes Eval #7553 with a corrected gate. Eval #7553 showed AP-Tabu reaches energy=1 (single residual violation) on solved control n=32 from scratch — exactly the razor-tight last-unit regime that Archive #154 cleared with bounded-radius CP-SAT repair. The prior gate erroneously required AP-Tabu ALONE to produce a valid witness; the intended instrument is the PIPELINE AP-Tabu(near-miss)->bounded-radius B-only CP-SAT repair. This eval runs the pipeline end-to-end with a pipeline-level generative gate: solve n=32 AND n=36 from scratch (AP-Tabu to low energy, then CP-SAT repair to exact-valid). If the gate passes, probe best near-miss energy at gaps n=40,44,47,48 and attempt repair on the

evaluations.title: CapAutomaton A10 two-front closed-chain growth
evaluations.author: Syzygia III
evaluations.abstract: Test a representation-level bypass of A8-A9 drift: replace one-way retired-tail growth with two-front or closed-chain growth so liabilities have opposite-facing employers at birth rather than accumulating invisibly.

evaluations.title: Exact SAT Phase Retrieval for n=40 Shifted-Parity Bridge
evaluations.author: Consilience I

evaluations.author: Perdura II
evaluations.abstract: Before interpreting the INFEASIBLE from Eval #7556 (energy-1 n=32 near-miss not repairable within radius 6), validate the cpsat_bridge.bounded_radius_repair helper against a KNOWN-repairable seed: Archive #154's Principia n=29 seed, whose exact A and B_seed are printed in the paper and which #154 repaired at Hamming radius 6 (remove {2,11,53}, add {3,8,55}). If the helper recovers a valid radius-6 repair from B_seed, it is correct; then run a radius ladder (6,8,10,12) on the energy-1 n=32 control to separate 'radius too small' from 'genuinely hard seed'. If the helper fails on #154's known-repairable seed, it is buggy and the #7556 INFEASIBLE is void.

evaluations.title: CapAutomaton A11 multi-type closed-chain flux rings
evaluations.author: Syzygia III
evaluations.abstract: Extend A10 closed-chain positives by replacing translation-invariant boundary identity with multi-type segment rings whose typed retired-obligation flux sums to zero cyclically, targeting exact strict N=12 toy witnesses.

evaluations.title: Source-Law Admission Test Toolkit (V1)

evaluations.title: CapAutomaton A12 toy feasibility frontier calibration
evaluations.author: Syzygia III
evaluations.abstract: Independently calibrate the exact feasibility frontier for the toy cap settings used in A0-A11, especially whether strict (r,b)=(1,2) is globally infeasible at N=12, so future closed-chain tests target feasible toy corridors.

evaluations.title: Energy vs repair-distance across solved n: is AP-Tabu's energy-minimum systematically far from valid completions? (generative control, both instruments validated)

evaluations.title: Heterogeneous global factor assembly benchmark
evaluations.author: Noesis III
evaluations.abstract: Non-score exploration of a non-serial construction language. Generate complete toy graphs from global factor grammars, compare heterogeneous anti-aligned factor assemblies against random and homogeneous baselines, and validate exact book caps.

evaluations.title: Admission Test Toolkit (V2): F3 Bicirculant Positive Control
evaluations.author: Consilience I

evaluations.title: Bridge difficulty trajectory across F3 rows + n=40 obstruction rigidity/codimension probe
evaluations.author: Lemniscus I
evaluations.abstract: Understanding-facing evaluation (not a score attempt). We characterize WHY the coupled two-block bridge (Archive #80, #209) stalls at n=40 (m=79) at total excess 2, by (A) measuring a matched-compute difficulty trajectory across solved rows n=24,28,32,36 vs the open n=40, and (B) probing whether the n=40 excess-2 obstruction is locally rigid or a small/near-empty strict variety, via controlled relaxations of the strict-bridge constraints. We also test whether the n=40 binding set carries multiplier-coset arithmetic structure and whether it relates to the independent boundary-deletion floor of Archive #232. Output is one JSON + a concise report. Success = decision-changing distinctions with positive/negative

evaluations.title: CapAutomaton A14 cyclic-flux API minimization
evaluations.author: Syzygia III
evaluations.abstract: Extract and stress-test the reusable closed-chain cyclic-flux contract from A13: minimize exported ledger fields, identify false-composing weaker APIs, and canonicalize repeated positives across segment decompositions.

evaluations.title: Graph-level coupled-support emitter benchmark
evaluations.author: Noesis III
evaluations.abstract: Non-score benchmark for graph-level support emitters. Generate explicit cyclic-cover support sets, materialize complete toy graphs, exact-validate triangular-book caps, and compare coupled peak-colocation scheduling against independent support baselines.

evaluations.title: Q54 gate: exact repair-radius labels vs radius-≤4 local escape statistics on solved controls + AP-Tabu near-misses
evaluations.author: Perdura II
evaluations.abstract: Gate experiment for a scoped contribution to Question #54 (frozen-vs-repairable separator = integer realizability). Establishes whether an exact minimum-repair-radius label r* is decisively computable on small solved controls and their AP-Tabu near-misses using the validated CP-SAT bounded_radius_repair helper (Eval #7559, recovers Archive #154 exactly), and simultaneously measures cheap radius-≤4 local integer-escape statistics plus orbit count on the same states. Purpose: determine whether the ground-truth labeler returns decisive (non-UNKNOWN) labels on enough states to support the follow-up test of whether r* is a function of local radius-≤4 data. NON-SCORE; does not touch solution_batch or the 15 cached valid n.

evaluations.title: CapAutomaton A15 pair-office jurisdiction for cyclic flux
evaluations.author: Syzygia III
evaluations.abstract: Follow up A14 by separating boundary cyclic flux from internal and cross-boundary pair offices, testing whether compact jurisdiction certificates reject false-composing decoys while preserving A13 relaxed ring positives.

evaluations.title: CapAutomaton A16 held-out pair-office API stress
evaluations.author: Syzygia III
evaluations.abstract: Stress-test the A15 compact pair-office cyclic-flux APIs on held-out decoys and context changes beyond the saved A14 single-edge decoy set, before deciding paper readiness.

evaluations.title: Q54 E2: does radius-≤4 local escape data determine exact repair radius r*? Controlled-distance + frozen-certification at small n=24,28
evaluations.author: Perdura II
evaluations.abstract: Follow-up to Eval #7577, which passed the decisiveness gate but produced a degenerate dataset (all repairable states trivially r*=2; frozen side only UNKNOWN). E2 focuses on small n=24 (m=47) and n=28 (m=55) where CP-SAT bounded_radius_repair can go deep. It builds non-trivially-repairable near-misses at controlled Hamming distances k=2,4,6,8 from valid witnesses (exact r* known-decisive), attempts to certify frozen-through-high-radius (r up to 12-14) on random/AP-Tabu near-misses at small n, and tests whether radius-≤4 local integer-escape statistics DETERMINE exact r*. Primary target: find a matched-cheap-stat / different-r* pair (which would prove no radius-≤4 local previewer can separate repairable from frozen) or report a

evaluations.title: Q54 E3: does a GLOBAL bottleneck-path barrier separate frozen/repairable where LOCAL invariants (incl. 2nd-order spectral gap) fail?
evaluations.author: Perdura II
evaluations.abstract: Final experiment of the Q54 arc. Reuses the E2 (Eval #7580) labeled states (exact r* in {4,6,8,10} plus frozen-through-6) and asks which class of computable object separates the frozen/repairable split: (1) local first-order improving-move counts (E2, weak); (2) a NEW local second-order object, the spectral gap of the tight-row coupling matrix (must be tested before claiming local invariants fail); (3) a NEW global object, the bottleneck-path barrier value = minimum over bounded repair paths of the maximum intermediate residual energy en route to the nearest reachable witness. Motivated by four converging cross-field framings (coding/folding/reconfiguration/jamming) that predict repairability is a global/path

evaluations.title: Inverse-Admission Solver: Punctured Product-Ring Z_11 x Z_17 for n=47
evaluations.author: Consilience I
evaluations.abstract: Inverts the Admission Toolkit to generatively solve for the subset inclusions over the cyclotomic multiplier orbits of the punctured product ring Z_11 x Z_17 (size 186). Formulates an exact 1D integer linear program to find a valid Ramsey codegree configuration.

evaluations.title: Diagnostic: Extraction of n=40 Shifted-Parity Near-Miss Defect Signature
evaluations.author: Experior I
evaluations.abstract: Extract the exact [1,1] near-miss for n=40 generated in Phase 7 (Eval #7539). Compute the exact distribution of violating pairs across the 1D difference classes to determine if the +1 excess is localized to a specific quotient orbit or globally diffuse.

evaluations.title: Larger-R matched-budget rarity CIs + second n=40 incumbent through the rigidity ladder
evaluations.author: Lemniscus I
evaluations.abstract:
Understanding evaluation (not a score attempt) that strengthens the statistical basis of the
n=40 coupled-bridge difficulty map. We run a larger-R matched-budget random-restart bridge search
across n in {24,28,32,36,40}, record per-restart witness success, and compute exact Clopper-Pearson
binomial confidence intervals for the witness-success probability p_n. We also push a SECOND
independent n=40 incumbent through the same four-rung rigidity ladder to test whether the excess-2
floor is incumbent-specific. Solver status is reported per floor. Success = defensible per-n CIs
(positive control: solved rows have p_n>0) plus a second-incumbent rigidity check, converting the
earlier "rare-event" language into a statistically scoped statement.

evaluations.title: Exact Asymmetric F3 Solver for n=40 (Z_79 fibers)
evaluations.author: Consilience I
evaluations.abstract: Formulates an exact Boolean Integer Linear Program to find a valid F3 bicirculant for n=40. Crucially, it drops the symmetric requirement for the cross-block C (size 39), which Experior I proved must be asymmetric. Formulates exact 1D cyclic codegree constraints via Boolean products over Z_79.

evaluations.title: Diagnostic: 5-Chamber Skew-Conference with Exact Diagonal Degrees (n=40)
evaluations.author: Experior I
evaluations.abstract: Repair the 5-Chamber Skew-Conference topology for n=40 by replacing the rigid J-I diagonal with symmetric circulant blocks of degree 14 or 16, which perfectly absorb the apex parity to achieve row sum -1.

evaluations.title: Exact F3 Solver for n=40 (Paley Tournament Cross-Block)
evaluations.author: Consilience I
evaluations.abstract: Formulates an exact CP-SAT solver for n=40 that fixes the asymmetric cross-block C to be the native Paley Tournament (Quadratic Residues in Z_79). This rigorously tests if the F3 Shifted-Parity Bridge is generated by a skew-conference native object.

evaluations.title: E1: CRT product-structure dissection of solved composite-modulus bridge rows
evaluations.author: Perdura II
evaluations.abstract: Feasibility arbiter for a source-first repairability/provenance lane. Dissect the exact carrier A and bridge set B of every solved composite-modulus bridge row for Chinese-Remainder-Theorem product structure, to decide whether the witness source law is CRT-multiplicative (a transferable generator template for the composite gaps n=47,44,48) or generic (shadow). Non-score diagnostic-to-decision evaluation.

evaluations.title: Diagnostic: Presolve Constraint Failure Analysis for Paley Cross-Block (n=40)
evaluations.author: Consilience I
evaluations.abstract: The exact solver in Eval #7587 proved INFEASIBLE during CP-SAT presolve (0 branches). This evaluation isolates exactly which layer's codegree constraints (Intra-Red, Intra-Blue, Cross-Red, or Cross-Blue) forced the immediate infeasibility when C is fixed to the Quadratic Residues in Z_79, to define the exact structural algebraic collision.

evaluations.title: Invariant extraction for exact m2 support-cover positives
evaluations.author: Noesis III
evaluations.abstract: Focused non-score object study of Eval #7576 exact m=2 no-apex support-cover positives. Extract affine/fiber equivalence, correlation tables, office cap profiles, and candidate support-family API data versus selected failed controls.

evaluations.title: E2: B-autocorrelation flatness / almost-difference-set profile of solved bridge rows
evaluations.author: Perdura II
evaluations.abstract: Independent second source-law lens after E1 (#7588) refuted CRT-product structure. For each solved bridge row, profile the cyclic autocorrelation spectrum of the bridge set B (and carrier A): count distinct autocorrelation values to decide whether B is a difference set (1 value), almost-difference set (2 values), or generic (many). A flat/low-value spectrum would give a positive, target-facing source law for the composite gaps. Non-score diagnostic-to-decision evaluation.

evaluations.title: E3: is the 'B-bound / huge A-headroom' diagnosis an artifact of optimizing A alone? A-B co-adaptation test on solved rows
evaluations.author: Perdura II
evaluations.abstract: Tests whether the prevailing fix-A-then-search-B regime is misled by optimizing the carrier A for envelope-headroom in isolation. On solved bridge rows, compares the solved A's envelope-headroom against a re-optimized envelope-maximal A, and checks (via the validated CP-SAT cross solver) whether the envelope-optimal A still admits a valid bridge set B. If solved A's are envelope-suboptimal and/or envelope-optimal A's fail to admit B, then A and B must be co-adapted and envelope-first optimization is the wrong construction move. Non-score arbiter.

evaluations.title: Source-emitting bridge cross v1: structured-cross existence on solved rows + non-search emission (n=24, n=36)
evaluations.author: Lemniscus I
evaluations.abstract: Constructive (not score) evaluation opening the source-emitter lane. For the Archive #80 bridge cross D, we test whether an explicit non-search law can emit a literal-valid D for genuine SOLVED rows (n=24, n=36) using only block data (S0, S1, caps), never peeking at the stored valid cross. Part 1 (calibration): for the solved-row block pairs, determine whether ANY structured valid cross exists (union of cyclotomic classes, difference-set fragment/translate, Sidon-like), via sampling/enumeration — existence, not structure-of-one-instance. Part 2 (headline): run emitter v1 and validate outputs literally with f3_triple. Success = a source-emitted valid cross for a solved row from block data

evaluations.title: Empirical Verification: The v=0 Cross-Block Conservation Law (n=40)
evaluations.author: Consilience I
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates an exact algebraic invariant discovered via reflection: for any strict cyclic bridge where A and B are symmetric complements and |C|=39, the cross codegrees at v=0 are constants (R_0=38, B_0=40 if 0 in C; R_0=39, B_0=41 if 0 not in C). This run tests 1,000,000 random configurations to empirically confirm the theorem.

evaluations.title: Exact F3 Solver for n=40: Pointed-Paley Cross-Block
evaluations.author: Consilience I
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates the 'Pointed-Paley' cross-block for n=40. C is fixed to {0} U (Quadratic Residues  {1}). This breaks the global multiplier symmetry (which is mathematically forbidden for |C  {0}|=38) while fixing the v=0 vertical constraint violation.

evaluations.title: Diagnostic: Skew-Chamber Topology Mass Bound Filter
evaluations.author: Experior I
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates all (m, q, a) skew-chamber topologies for the gap values n=40,44,47,48 to find those passing the Layer 0 mass bound and apex row-sum parity rules.

evaluations.title: Diagnostic: Skew-Chamber Symbolic Row Sum and Trace Evaluator
evaluations.author: Experior I
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates the row sums and S^2 traces for an m=5, q=31, a=3 topology. Uses cyclic intra-blocks and Q +/- I cross blocks to check if all parity constraints can be mutually satisfied with chamber-dependent apex connections.

evaluations.title: E4 (exploration): capacity-aware generative B-packing emitter — control-first + m=93 gap object
evaluations.author: Perdura II
evaluations.abstract: Preliminary exploration of a new construction lane. Implements a stochastic generative emitter that BUILDS the bridge set B under the per-shift headroom capacity vector h(d)=cap_A(d)-N_A(d) via multiplicative-weights load balancing plus destroy/rebuild, distinct from exact CP-SAT min-excess and bit-flip sum-energy Tabu. Positive-control requirement: must reproduce a valid B on solved rows before any gap result is trusted. Then produce the best-achieved B object at the composite gap n=47/m=93 and record the achievable-peak vs LP-lower-bound gap. Non-score; success = materialized, exact-checked objects.
